overview: The State Mini Cluster Development Scheme is a component of the Haryana Enterprises & Employment Policy-2020, aimed at supporting the development of industrial clusters in the state. It focuses on fostering entrepreneurship, enhancing MSME competitiveness, and promoting balanced regional development through cluster-based interventions. The scheme provides financial and infrastructural support to MSMEs for technology upgradation, market access, and common facility creation.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; entrepreneurs; startups
eligibility: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) engaged in manufacturing or services, particularly those located in industrially backward districts (Category D blocks) or participating in cluster development initiatives under the Haryana Enterprise Promotion Policy 2015. Enterprises must be registered under the MSMED Act, 2006 and comply with the policy framework for cluster development, technology upgradation, and market linkage enhancement.
benefits: Financial assistance for setting up Common Facility Centres (CFCs), technology upgradation, market access enhancement, credit linkage support, infrastructure development, skill development, entrepreneurship promotion, and institutional strengthening. Includes subsidies for plant and machinery, testing labs, raw material banks, design centres, and training facilities within clusters.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support in the form of subsidies for cluster development interventions, including up to 70% grant for setting up Common Facility Centres (CFCs) in MSME clusters, with a maximum ceiling of INR 10 crore per CFC. Additional support includes interest subsidies, credit guarantee coverage, and infrastructure grants as per the Haryana Enterprise Promotion Policy 2015 guidelines, disbursed through nodal agencies like the Directorate of MSME and Haryana Enterprises Promotion Centre (HEPC).
application_process: 1. Identify and form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) or consortium of MSMEs in a defined cluster. 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) outlining cluster interventions, technology needs, market linkages, and financial requirements. 3. Submit the DPR to the Directorate of MSME, Haryana or Haryana Enterprises Promotion Centre (HEPC) for appraisal. 4. Obtain approval from the State Level Steering Committee under HEEP 2020. 5. Execute the project upon sanction and submit utilization reports for fund release in stages. 6. Undergo monitoring and evaluation by the implementing agency for compliance and impact assessment.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Directorate of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Haryana

overview: The Critical Infrastructure Development Scheme under the Enterprises Promotion Policy 2015 aims to support the development of essential industrial infrastructure such as roads, water supply, drainage, and power supply in industrial areas to facilitate industrial growth and attract investment in Haryana. It is designed to improve the basic infrastructure in industrial estates and parks to make them investment-ready and support the establishment and expansion of industries.
target_beneficiaries: industries; MSME; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Industries and enterprises setting up or expanding in Haryana State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (HSIIDC) developed industrial estates, parks, and areas are eligible for the scheme. The scheme applies to units in industrially backward blocks (Category D) as per block categorization under HEEP 2020, where special incentives are provided to hasten industrial development.
benefits: The scheme provides financial assistance for the development of critical infrastructure including internal roads, water supply, sewerage/drainage, and power supply in industrial areas. It supports the creation of investment-ready industrial plots by ensuring basic infrastructure is in place, thereby reducing the initial setup cost for industries and promoting industrial dispersal across the state.
financial_support: Under the Enterprises Promotion Policy 2015, the Critical Infrastructure Development Scheme offers capital subsidy for infrastructure development in industrial estates. The financial support is provided as a subsidy to cover a portion of the cost of developing internal infrastructure such as roads, water supply, drainage, and power supply in HSIIDC-developed areas, with specific quantum and rates defined in the scheme guidelines.
application_process: 1. Identify the industrial estate or area where the unit is to be set up or expanded. 2. Verify eligibility based on location in HSIIDC-developed area and block categorization (especially Category D for backward areas). 3. Submit application through the HSIIDC or Department of Industries & Commerce, Haryana. 4. Provide project details including land allotment, infrastructure requirements, and cost estimates. 5. Await verification and approval by the competent authority. 6. Upon approval, receive subsidy disbursement as per scheme guidelines after infrastructure development is completed and verified.
deadlines: As per scheme notifications and HSIIDC circulars; typically tied to industrial plot allotment schedules or annual budget cycles
implementing_agency: Haryana State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (HSIIDC)

overview: The Industrial Infrastructure Development Scheme under the Haryana Enterprises & Employment Policy-2020 aims to develop robust industrial infrastructure by providing developed land and facilities for industrial ventures. It focuses on creating Industrial Model Townships (IMTs), Industrial Estates, and Theme Parks to support industrial growth and attract investment. The scheme is part of the state's strategy to enhance ease of doing business and promote balanced regional development through infrastructure-led geographical dispersal of industries.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; entrepreneurs; industrial units
eligibility: Eligibility is tied to the Haryana Enterprises & Employment Policy-2020 and applies to industrial units seeking to set up ventures in the state. Specific eligibility criteria for the Industrial Infrastructure Development Scheme are not detailed in the evidence, but beneficiaries are expected to comply with land allotment procedures, pollution control norms, and other clearances as advised by the Department of Industries & Commerce, Haryana.
benefits: Benefits include provision of developed land for industrial ventures, availability of world-class infrastructure leading to lower operating costs, support for attracting indigenous and foreign investments, facilitation of clearances from related government departments (Commercial Taxes, Labour, Town & Country Planning, Pollution Control Board), and promotion of ease of starting businesses through policy framework and advisory services.
financial_support: The scheme provides developed land and infrastructure support, but specific financial support quantum, type (e.g., subsidy, grant), or mechanism is not detailed in the evidence. Financial aspects are implied through infrastructure development and land provision rather than direct monetary disbursement.
application_process: 1. Approach the Department of Industries & Commerce, Haryana for advice on land availability and procedure for allotment. 2. Obtain guidance on conversion of land use and required clearances from departments such as Commercial Taxes, Labour, Town & Country Planning, and Pollution Control Board. 3. Avail incentives and concessions available to the industry. 4. Facilitate coordination with related government departments for regulatory clearances and enforcement. 5. Proceed with setting up of industries on developed land provided under the scheme.
implementing_agency: Department of Industries & Commerce, Haryana
contact_details: 0172-2714010 (Department of Industries & Commerce, Haryana), ipcharyana@yahoo.com, help[dot]hryindustries[at]gmail[dot]com

overview: The Haryana State Start-ups Scheme is a flagship initiative of the Government of Haryana under the Department of Industries and Commerce, aimed at fostering innovation, entrepreneurship, and job creation by providing a comprehensive framework of fiscal and non-fiscal incentives to startups and incubators. It supports the creation of a vibrant startup ecosystem through financial assistance, regulatory simplifications, mentorship, incubation, and access to funding and networking opportunities. The scheme is aligned with the Haryana State Startup Policy 2022 and targets DPIIT-recognized startups operating within or through government-supported infrastructure in Haryana.
target_beneficiaries: startups; incubators; women entrepreneurs
eligibility: Company Age: Period of existence and operations should not exceed 10 years from the Date of Incorporation. Company Type: Incorporated as a Private Limited Company, Registered Partnership Firm, or Limited Liability Partnership. Annual Turnover: Should not exceed ₹100 crores for any financial year since incorporation. Original Entity: Should not have been formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business. Innovative & Scalable: Must work towards development or improvement of a product, process, or service with a scalable business model and high potential for wealth and employment creation. Category 1 Startups: Must be DPIIT-registered and have a registered office in Haryana. Category 2 Startups: Must be DPIIT-registered, have a registered office outside Haryana, but operate through government-owned or supported operational incubators located in Haryana.
benefits: Fiscal benefits include: Seed Grant up to INR 10 Lakh per startup; Lease Rental Subsidy (30% for general startups, 45% for women-led startups, max INR 5 Lakh for 1 year); Patent Cost Reimbursement (100% of actual expenses, max INR 25 Lakh); Reimbursement for Cloud Storage (75% of expenses, max INR 2.5 Lakh per annum for 5 years); Reimbursement for Acceleration Programs (up to INR 2.5 Lakh per year); Reimbursement of Net SGST (50% for 7 years, capped at 100% of Fixed Capital Investment). Non-monetary benefits: Relaxation in Public Procurement Norms, Subsidized Incubation Space, Access to Events/Workshops/Startup-Specific Programs, Mentorship, Networking with investors and industry experts, Access to funding and investment opportunities, Guidance from industry experts, and Simplified regulatory framework.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through multiple schemes: Seed Grant of up to INR 10 Lakh per startup for idea validation, prototype development, proof of concept, and initial activities; Lease Rental Subsidy of 30% (45% for women-led startups) of lease rental, max INR 5 Lakh for 1 year; Patent Cost Reimbursement of 100% of actual expenses (filing, consultancy, search, maintenance, publishing fees) up to INR 25 Lakh for domestic and international patents; Reimbursement for Cloud Storage at 75% of expenses, max INR 2.5 Lakh per annum for 5 years on Haryana-based Data Centres; Reimbursement for Acceleration Programs up to INR 2.5 Lakh per year; and Reimbursement of Net SGST at 50% for 7 years, capped at 100% of Fixed Capital Investment. All financial assistance is disbursed upon submission of required documents and approval by the Evaluation & Approval Committee.
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 10 Lakh
application_process: 1. Register on the Startup Haryana portal at https://startupharyana.gov.in. 2. Log in using email/password, Gmail, or Startup India login details. 3. Select 'Startup' as the registration type. 4. Ensure DPIIT recognition is obtained prior to application (if not, get recognized via DPIIT first). 5. Complete the 4-step application form: (a) Details of the entity (Startup Details, Authorized Representative Details, Incubation Details, Upload Documents), (b) Details of Directors/Designated Partners, (c) Details of Business, (d) Preview and Final Submit. 6. Upload all required documents (file size ≤ 2 MB). 7. Accept terms and conditions and submit the application. 8. Application is processed within 30 days if no deficiencies; if deficiencies are found, applicant has 10 days to resubmit. 9. Upon approval, download the registration certificate from 'My Applications' section.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department of Industries and Commerce, Government of Haryana
contact_details: Helpline Number: +91 172-467-1337 | Mon - Fri (10:00 AM - 06:00 PM)

scheme_name: Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivar Utthan Yojana (MMAPUY)
overview: Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivar Utthan Yojana (MMAPUY) is an umbrella mission launched in July 2021 by the Government of Haryana to identify economically disadvantaged families and provide a tailored package of welfare measures from various schemes to uplift them. The scheme aims to eradicate poverty by raising income levels through targeted interventions like skill development, job placements, financial aid, and entrepreneurial support. It seeks to ensure sustainable livelihoods and a dignified quality of life for underprivileged families, with an initial economic threshold of Rs. 1 lakh per annum and a subsequent target of Rs. 1.80 lakh per annum.
target_beneficiaries: economically disadvantaged families; poorest of the poor families
eligibility: Poorest of the poor families are identified in the State of Haryana, and a package of measures from various welfare schemes (skill development, wage employment, self-employment etc.) is tailored for each family to ensure their economic upliftment.
benefits: Through targeted interventions like skill development, job placements, financial aid, and entrepreneurial support, the program seeks to provide sustainable livelihoods and ensure a dignified quality of life for underprivileged families. The initiative is dedicated to fostering equitable growth and reducing income disparities across the state.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial aid as part of a tailored package of measures from various welfare schemes, though specific quantum, type, and mechanism are not detailed in the evidence.
application_process: The evidence does not provide a numbered step-by-step application procedure for MMAPUY.
implementing_agency: Department of Information Technology Electronics & Communication, Haryana

overview: The PADMA Scheme (Programme to Accelerate Development for MSME Advancement) is a five-year block-level economic transformation policy notified by the Haryana Government on August 17, 2023, aiming to develop MSME industrial clusters across all 143 blocks of the state's 22 districts. It focuses on creating enabling infrastructure, knowledge creation, awareness generation, and handholding support to accelerate entrepreneurship, strengthen industrial infrastructure, and generate sustainable employment at the grassroots level. The scheme includes multiple sub-schemes such as Capital Investment Subsidy, Cluster Infrastructure Development, Designing & Branding, Entrepreneurship Acceleration, and Interest Subsidy, each targeting specific aspects of MSME development.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; micro enterprises; small enterprises; startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST; Self-Help Groups
eligibility: The micro and small enterprises inside/outside the approved PADMA cluster shall be eligible under the scheme. The MSEs shall also comply with the following conditions: The unit should have filed Udyam Registration Certificate (URC) and Haryana Udhyam Memorandum (HUM). The unit should be in commercial production. The unit should be in regular production at the time of disbursement and the subsidy shall not be released to closed unit. The unit shall remain in regular production for a period of 05 years from date of commercial production. The unit should be engaged in manufacturing/processing of the approved product category of that cluster. The unit shall have to use the PADMA logo on the product manufactured. The land for the project shall be arranged by the promoter either by purchase or on registered lease deed of at least 10 years. The unit availing incentive under this scheme will not be eligible to obtain incentives under any capital subsidy/similar scheme of other policies of the State Government. The CLU/NOC/Industrial License as applicable obtained by IA for the said PADMA cluster, will be applicable.
benefits: Financial assistance includes capital investment subsidy (up to 30% of eligible investment, max Rs. 30 lakh for women/SC/SHG units and Rs. 25 lakh for others inside PADMA cluster; half for outside), interest subsidy (reimbursement of interest @6% p.a. or actual rate, max Rs. 20 lakh/year inside and Rs. 10 lakh/year outside), entrepreneurship acceleration grant (Rs. 20 lakh inside and Rs. 10 lakh outside per startup for proof of concept), and designing/branding/marketing support (50% reimbursement, max Rs. 10 lakh/year inside and Rs. 5 lakh/year outside). Non-financial benefits include access to Common Facility Centres (CFCs), Business Development Centres (BDCs), plug-and-play facilities, skill development, market linkages, credit facilitation, mentorship, and strategic linkages with BDS providers and OEMs.
financial_support: Financial support varies by sub-scheme: Under PADMA Capital Investment Subsidy Scheme, 30% subsidy on eligible capital investment (max Rs. 30 lakh for women/SC/SHG units, Rs. 25 lakh for others) inside PADMA cluster; half for units outside. Under PADMA Interest Subsidy Scheme, reimbursement of interest @6% p.a. or actual rate paid, whichever is less, up to Rs. 20 lakh per financial year inside and Rs. 10 lakh outside. Under PADMA Entrepreneurship Acceleration Scheme, financial assistance of Rs. 20 lakh for startups inside and Rs. 10 lakh outside per innovative idea for proof of concept. Under PADMA Designing, Branding, Marketing & Exports Promotion Scheme, 50% reimbursement of expenses, max Rs. 10 lakh/year inside and Rs. 5 lakh/year outside. Under PADMA Cluster Infrastructure Development Scheme (PCIDS), 50% to 85% financial assistance, max Rs. 35 Crore for up to 50 acres and Rs. 45 Crore for more than 50 acres, based on block category (B: 50%, C: 75%, D: 85%).
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 30 lakh for women/SC/SHG owned micro and small units inside PADMA cluster; Rs. 25 lakh for other units inside; Rs. 15 lakh for women/SC/SHG and Rs. 12.50 lakh for others outside PADMA cluster
application_process: 1. Apply on the prescribed form (Annexure-I) for the respective sub-scheme (e.g., Capital Investment Subsidy, Interest Subsidy, etc.) along with required documents. 2. Submit the application to the Director General, Directorate of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Haryana, via the web portal within the stipulated time (e.g., 03 months from start of commercial production or date of scheme notification, whichever is later). 3. The application is scrutinized by the Joint Director/Deputy Director, District MSME Centre. 4. Deficiencies, if any, are communicated in writing within 07 days, with 10 days to rectify. 5. If deficiencies are not rectified, the claim is recommended for rejection. 6. The Competent Authority (Head of Department, Directorate of MSME, Haryana) sanctions the assistance after compliance of formalities. 7. For certain schemes like Cluster Infrastructure Development, progress reports and utilization certificates are required at each tranche of disbursement.
deadlines: The scheme shall commence with effect from the date of re-notification of PADMA policy i.e., 17.08.2023 and shall remain in operation for a period of 5 years up to 16.08.2028 or till the validity of the PADMA policy. Applicants shall have to apply on the prescribed form along with complete documents within 03 months from the start of commercial production or from the date of notification of the scheme or from the date of re-notification of PADMA policy, whichever is later.
implementing_agency: Directorate of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Haryana (Department of Industries & Commerce, Haryana)

overview: The HUM Registration scheme is a state-level initiative by the Government of Haryana aimed at registering and recognizing entities under the Haryana Udyami Mitra (HUM) program. It serves as a formal enrollment mechanism for beneficiaries to access various state government schemes, subsidies, and support services. The registration enables individuals and enterprises to be part of Haryana's entrepreneurial and MSME development ecosystem.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; entrepreneurs; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST
eligibility: Eligibility criteria for HUM Registration include individuals, startups, MSMEs, and enterprises based in Haryana, particularly those engaged in entrepreneurial activities, manufacturing, services, or agri-allied sectors. Priority may be given to women entrepreneurs, SC/ST categories, and persons with disabilities as per state government directives.
benefits: Registered beneficiaries gain access to state government schemes, subsidies, financial assistance, skill development programs, market linkages, and priority in government procurement. They also receive updates on new initiatives, eligibility for incubation support, and facilitation in obtaining clearances and approvals.
financial_support: Financial support varies depending on the specific scheme linked to HUM Registration, such as seed funding, interest subsidies, or capital grants under programs like Startup Haryana or MSME incentives. The registration itself does not provide direct financial aid but enables eligibility for such support.
application_process: 1. Visit the official Haryana government portal or designated HUM registration platform. 2. Click on the HUM Registration or Udyami Mitra enrollment link. 3. Fill in the online application form with personal, business, and enterprise details. 4. Upload required documents such as identity proof, address proof, business registration, and PAN. 5. Submit the application and await verification by the concerned authority. 6. Upon approval, receive a unique HUM registration number and certificate.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department of Industries and Commerce, Government of Haryana

overview: The SIDBI SMILE Scheme is a financial assistance program designed to support MSMEs and startups by providing access to credit and other financial products. It aims to facilitate affordable financing for micro-entrepreneurs and enterprises to promote livelihood and business growth. The scheme operates through partner institutions and digital platforms to ensure seamless credit delivery and documentation. It focuses on inclusive growth, with special emphasis on women entrepreneurs and socially backward sections.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST
eligibility: The scheme targets informal micro-entrepreneurs/ micro-enterprises (IMEs) for livelihood enterprise promotion. It is implemented through Partner Institutions including Financial Intermediaries (BC/ MFI/ SHPI/ NBFC/ FinTech’s, etc.) and Non-Financial Intermediaries (Corporates, Aggregators, etc.). The scheme is operational in PAN India, covering 30 States/UTs as of December 2023. More than 85% of beneficiaries are women entrepreneurs, and more than 70% belong to socially backward sections.
benefits: The scheme provides door step assistance through Partner Institutions for credit processes including collection of application information, digital documentation, and collections. It ensures faster credit delivery via seamless digital integration between OPI and SIDBI and through the Prayaas App/ portal. It supports access to affordable credit for livelihood and enterprise promotion, with special focus on women entrepreneurs and socially backward sections. Over 2,94,000 beneficiaries have been assisted under the scheme as of December 2023.
financial_support: The scheme facilitates access to affordable credit through Partner Institutions, with SIDBI providing refinance and credit facilitation. It does not directly lend but enables credit delivery via partner networks. Financial support is channelled through Partner Institutions who assist in loan processing, documentation, and disbursement. The scheme emphasizes quick and paperless sanction processes through digital platforms like the Prayaas App.
application_process: 1. Approach a registered Partner Institution (Financial Intermediary or Non-Financial Intermediary) empanelled with SIDBI under the Prayaas Scheme. 2. Submit application details including business information and KYC documents at the Partner Institution level. 3. Partner Institution assists in collection of application information, digital documentation, and verification. 4. Application is processed through seamless digital integration between the Partner Institution and SIDBI. 5. Credit sanction and disbursement are coordinated between the Partner Institution and SIDBI based on eligibility and credit assessment. 6. Utilize the Prayaas App/ portal for tracking and managing the loan lifecycle where available.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

scheme_name: CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for MSEs)
overview: CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises) is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India and Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) to facilitate collateral-free credit to Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) by providing guarantee cover to eligible Member Lending Institutions (MLIs). It does not provide direct financial assistance but guarantees loans extended by MLIs to MSEs, thereby enhancing access to institutional credit for unserved and underserved entrepreneurs. Over the past 25 years, CGTMSE has approved 1.15 crore guarantees worth ₹9.34 lakh crore, with 276 MLIs registered under CGS-I and CGS-II as of March 31, 2025.
target_beneficiaries: Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs); new generation entrepreneurs; unserved and underserved MSEs
eligibility: Eligible borrowers include new and existing Micro and Small Enterprises engaged in manufacturing or service activity (excluding Agriculture, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Liability Group (JLG)). Borrowers must obtain IT PAN (mandatory for loans above ₹5 lakh) and Udyam Registration Number. Credit facilities can be extended by multiple institutions up to ₹10 crore per borrower, subject to individual MLI ceilings. Eligible Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) include Scheduled Commercial Banks (PSU, Private, Foreign), selected Regional Rural Banks, state financial corporations, NBFCs, Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Scheduled Urban Co-operative Banks, Microfinance Institutions (MFIs), SIDBI, NSIC, and NEDFi, subject to RBI and GOI guidelines.
benefits: CGTMSE provides guarantee cover for collateral-free and third-party guarantee-free credit facilities extended by MLIs to MSEs. It enables access to institutional finance without requiring collateral or third-party guarantees. Special benefits include reduced guarantee fee (minimum 0.37% p.a.), increased guarantee coverage ceiling to ₹10 crore, and special provisions for women entrepreneurs. The guarantee does not involve direct financial assistance, loan disbursement, or subsidy by CGTMSE.
financial_support: CGTMSE does not provide any financial assistance, loans, credit facilities, or subsidies. It only provides guarantee cover for credit facilities extended by eligible Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) such as Banks, RRBs, and select financial institutions. The guarantee is issued upon receipt of applicable guarantee fee by the MLI after loan sanction/disbursement. The quantum of guarantee is tied to the loan amount sanctioned by the MLI, with a maximum coverage of ₹10 crore per borrower.
application_process: 1. Approach a Member Lending Institution (MLI) registered with CGTMSE for an MSE loan (Term Loan or Working Capital). 2. The MLI processes the loan application and sanctions/disburses the loan based on internal credit appraisal. 3. After loan sanction/disbursement, the MLI lodges an application for guarantee coverage with CGTMSE. 4. CGTMSE approves the application and issues the guarantee cover to the MLI upon receipt of the applicable guarantee fee.
deadlines: Rolling basis — MLIs can apply for guarantee cover anytime during the loan tenure, provided the credit facility was not restructured or remained in SMA2 status in the last 1 year from application date.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India and Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
contact_details: Toll Free No.: 1800222659 | Contact Nos.: (022): 6722 1553, 6753 1313, 6722 1483 | Email for registration queries: registration@cgtmse.in

overview: The NSIC Raw Material Assistance Scheme aims to help MSMEs by financing the purchase of raw materials (both indigenous and imported) through credit support, enabling them to focus on manufacturing quality products. It facilitates procurement with credit up to 180 days, allowing MSMEs to benefit from bulk purchase raw materials at bulk supplier rates and avail cash discounts. The scheme requires security in the form of a Bank Guarantee from approved banks and involves a process of application, appraisal, unit inspection, sanction of limit, agreement signing, and disbursement of assistance.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Any Manufacturing/Service MSME having Udyam Registration Certificate can apply for the assistance under the Scheme.
benefits: Materials facilitated under bulk supplies arrangements are provided at bulk supplier’s rate by eliminating the middlemen. Discounts received under bulk supplies arrangements are shared with MSMEs, enabling them to reduce cost of purchase of materials. Availability of raw material on credit enables MSMEs to execute orders in hand. The scheme also provides credit support for raw material procurement against Bank Guarantee with a maximum assistance of up to 95% of the BG value.
financial_support: The scheme provides credit support for raw material procurement against Bank Guarantee. The maximum assistance is provided up to 95% of the BG value. The rate of interest varies based on SME rating and unit type (Micro or Small & Medium). For assistance availed on or after 01.07.2025, the effective rate of interest per annum is: For Micro units: (i) SME 1 rating: 8.75%, (ii) SME 2 rating: 9.25%, (iii) Other units: 9.75%. For Small & Medium units: (i) SME 1 rating: 9.25%, (ii) SME 2 rating: 9.75%, (iii) Other units: 10.25%. Penal charge on delayed payment beyond 180 days is 1.25% per quarter. Processing fee is 1.0% p.a. on new sanctions for both Micro and Small & Medium units, and 0.5% p.a. on renewal for Micro units and 1.0% p.a. for Small & Medium units.
application_process: 1. Download the application form from NSIC’s website or obtain it from the nearest branch office. 2. Fill the application form with required details. 3. Submit the duly filled application form along with prescribed documents to the nearest NSIC branch office. 4. Preliminary appraisal and unit inspection are carried out by NSIC. 5. Sanction of limit to the unit is granted. 6. Agreement is signed between NSIC and the unit. 7. Assistance is disbursed to the unit.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. (NSIC)

overview: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) is a scheme launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on April 8, 2015 for providing loans up to 10 lakh (20 lakh for those entrepreneurs who have availed and successfully repaid previous loans under the 'Tarun' category) to the non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises. These loans are classified as MUDRA loans under PMMY and are given by Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, MFIs and NBFCs. The borrower can approach any of the lending institutions mentioned above or can apply online through the portal www.udyamimitra.in. Under the aegis of PMMY, MUDRA has created four products namely 'Shishu', 'Kishor', 'Tarun' and 'TarunPlus' to signify the stage of growth / development and funding needs of the beneficiary micro unit / entrepreneur and also provide a reference point for the next phase of graduation / growth.
target_beneficiaries: non-corporate; non-farm; small/micro enterprises; SC/ST; OBC; women entrepreneurs
eligibility: Any Indian Citizen who has a business plan for a non-farm income generating activity such as manufacturing, processing, trading or service sector whose credit need is up to 20 lakh can approach either a Bank, MFI or NBFC for availing of MUDRA loans under PMMY. The usual terms and conditions of the lending agency may have to be followed for availing of loans under PMMY. The lending rates are as per the RBI guidelines issued in this regard from time to time.
benefits: MUDRA loans are extended for a variety of purposes which result in income generation and employment creation. The loans are extended mainly for: Business loan for Vendors, Traders, Shopkeepers and other Service Sector activities; Working capital loan through MUDRA Cards; Equipment Finance for Micro Units; Transport Vehicle loans for commercial use only; Loans for agri-allied non-farm income generating activities, e.g. pisciculture, bee keeping, poultry farming, etc.; Tractors, tillers as well as two wheelers used for commercial purposes only; Community, Social & Personal Service Activities; Food Products Sector Activities; Textile Products Sector / Activity; Business loans for Traders and Shopkeepers; Equipment Finance Scheme for Micro Units; Activities allied to agriculture. MUDRA Card is a debit card issued against the MUDRA loan account, for working capital portion of the loan. The borrower can make use of MUDRA Card in multiple drawals and credits, so as to manage the working capital limit in cost-efficient manner and keep the interest burden minimum. MUDRA Card also helps in digitalization of MUDRA transactions and creating credit history for the borrower. MUDRA Card can be operated across the country for withdrawal of cash from any ATM / micro ATM and also make payment through any 'Point of Sale' machines.
financial_support: MUDRA is a refinancing Institution. MUDRA does not lend directly to the micro entrepreneurs / individuals. Mudra loans under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) can be availed of from nearby branch office of a bank, NBFC, MFIs etc. Borrowers can also now file online application for MUDRA loans on Udyamimitra portal (www.udyamimitra.in). The refinance is available for term loan and working capital loan up to an amount of 20 lakh per unit. The eligible Banks/NBFCs/MFIs, who comply with the requirements as notified, can avail refinance from MUDRA for the loans given by them for eligible MUDRA compliant activities under Shishu, Kishore, Tarun and Tarun Plus categories. In order to encourage women entrepreneurs, the financing Banks/NBFCs/MFIs may consider extending additional facilities, including interest reduction on their loan.
application_process: 1. Approach any of the lending institutions mentioned above (Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, MFIs and NBFCs). 2. Alternatively, apply online through the portal www.udyamimitra.in. 3. Submit the loan application along with required documents. 4. Await approval and disbursement from the lending institution.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd. (MUDRA)

overview: The NSIC Marketing Support Scheme, known as the Marketing Facilitation Scheme (MFS), supports Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) in marketing their goods and services through consortium-based tender participation and facilitation services. It enables MSEs to participate in government procurement by acting as a facilitator between buyers and suppliers, recommending the L1 bidder and charging a facilitation fee. The scheme is designed to enhance market access and competitiveness for MSEs, particularly those registered under the Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS).
target_beneficiaries: Micro & Small Enterprises (MSEs); units registered under SPRS
eligibility: The scheme covers only Micro & Small Enterprises registered with NSIC under its Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS). It also covers MSEs who apply for SPRS registration along with all required documents and whose factory is inspected before empanelment under MFS. Units engaging in trading activities without value addition, packing, or branding are not eligible.
benefits: NSIC offers facilitation services to Central Governments & their Departments, PSUs, State/UT Governments & their Departments, Local bodies, and Public/reputed Private Sector Companies. NSIC’s role is limited to recommending the L1 bidder (lowest bidder) to the buyer, who then awards the contract. NSIC receives facilitation charges in phases: 50% upon first milestone (acceptance of award), 25% at second milestone (total execution), and 25% upon final milestone (receipt of payment). NSIC charges 5% (inclusive of GST) of the award value as facilitation fee/commission. Units owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs are exempted from the enlistment fee. There is no fee for formation or renewal of consortia, but enlistment fee applies during participation in any enquiry by consortia members.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Instead, it offers non-financial facilitation services including tender marketing, consortium formation, and recommendation of L1 bidders. Financial transactions occur between the buyer and the MSE supplier, with NSIC charging a facilitation fee of 5% of the award value, payable in milestones. No credit, loan, or subsidy is extended by NSIC under this scheme.
application_process: 1. Submit application form in prescribed format (Annexures – A) duly signed by authorized signatory (Proprietor/Partner(s)/Director(s)). 2. Include required documents as mentioned in the application form. 3. Apply for enlistment under the Tender Marketing Scheme. 4. Ensure factory inspection is completed before empanelment. 5. Pay applicable annual fee based on SPRS monetary limit: Rs. 1000+GST (up to Rs.100 lacs), Rs. 2500+GST (Rs.100-500 lacs), Rs. 5000+GST (above Rs.500 lacs). 6. SC/ST-owned units are exempt from enlistment fee. 7. Await empanelment approval from NSIC. 8. Upon empanelment, participate in tender facilitation process as per scheme guidelines.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. (NSIC)

overview: The SIDBI Direct Credit Scheme provides direct lending products to MSMEs through various loan offerings such as project funding, machinery loans, working capital, and green finance. These schemes aim to fill credit gaps in the MSME sector by offering customized, innovative, and scalable financial solutions. The scheme supports MSMEs in expansion, modernization, technology upgradation, and sustainable growth through collateral-free or secured lending options with quick sanctions and competitive interest rates.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Eligibility varies by product but generally includes MSME units in operation for a minimum period (e.g., 2 years for project funding, 3 years for machinery loan), mandatory Udyam & GST registration, no defaults to banks/FIs, audited accounts, and cash profit in recent financial years. Specific products may require additional criteria such as validated defence orders, GST returns, ITRs, bank statements, and CIBIL scores.
benefits: Benefits include quick sanction (in 48 hours for some products), digital and paperless processing, competitive interest rates, collateral-free options (e.g., GST Sahay), up to 100% financing with security (e.g., machinery loan), flexible repayment tenures, moratorium periods, end-to-end digital processes, and support for women entrepreneurs and socially backward sections. Additional benefits include access to subsidized rates, ECS interest credit, nomination facility, and higher rates for senior citizens in fixed deposit schemes.
financial_support: Financial support includes term loans for project funding up to Rs. 50 crore (80% of project cost), machinery loans up to Rs. 3 crore (up to 100% financing with 25% FD security), working capital loans, and green finance loans. Repayment tenures range from 30 to 60 days (Gig Flexi) to up to 7 years (project funding) with moratoriums up to 2 years. Interest rates are MCLR-linked and attractive. Some schemes offer invoice-based financing up to Rs. 50 lakh (GST Sahay) or Rs. 2 lakh (FPS Sahay, JAKs). Venture debt financing offers Rs. 10-15 crore with 3-year tenure. Seed funding through incubators provides equity investment. Direct lending aims to fill credit gaps through innovative products scalable via credit delivery ecosystem.
application_process: 1. Identify the suitable loan product (e.g., Project Loan, Machinery Loan, Working Capital, Green Finance). 2. Check eligibility criteria specific to the product. 3. Apply online via the SIDBI portal or through referral partners. 4. Complete registration and KYC process. 5. Submit required documents (e.g., GST returns, ITRs, bank statements, Udyam registration, project details). 6. Undergo sanction and acceptance of loan terms. 7. Execute digital documents and NACH mandate. 8. Receive disbursement directly to bank account. 9. Repay principal along with applicable interest on due date.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

overview: Equipment Finance for MSMEs (SIDBI) is a loan scheme designed to support micro, small, and medium enterprises in acquiring machinery and equipment for business expansion, modernization, or technology upgradation. It provides financial assistance for the purchase of plant and machinery, fixed assets, and other capital goods essential for operational efficiency and growth. The scheme targets existing MSME units with a proven track record and aims to enhance productivity and competitiveness through accessible credit.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSME units in operation for at least three years. Mandatory Udyam & GST registration. No defaults to Bank/FIs. Cash profit in last audited financial results.
benefits: Quick sanction of machinery loan through automated platform using GST returns, ITRs, Bank Statement and CIBIL score. Loan amount up to Rs. 3 Crore with immediate in-principle offer. Upto 100% financing with 25% security in the form of fixed deposit. Processing fees of 0.50% plus applicable GST. MCLR Linked attractive rate of Interest. Repayment upto 60 months.
financial_support: Loan amount up to Rs. 3 Crore with immediate in-principle offer. Upto 100% financing with 25% security in the form of fixed deposit. Processing fees of 0.50% plus applicable GST. MCLR Linked attractive rate of Interest. Repayment upto 60 months.
application_process: 1. Apply Now through the SIDBI portal 2. Submit GST returns, ITRs, Bank Statement and CIBIL score 3. Complete registration and KYC 4. Receive sanction and acceptance of loan limit 5. Execute digital documents and NACH mandate 6. Receive disbursement
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

overview: The Mahila Udyam Nidhi Scheme (SIDBI) is a financial assistance program designed to support women entrepreneurs in establishing or expanding their micro and small enterprises. It provides term loans and working capital assistance to promote self-employment and income generation among women. The scheme aims to enhance access to credit for women who face barriers in obtaining conventional financing. It is implemented by SIDBI as part of its commitment to inclusive financial development.
target_beneficiaries: women entrepreneurs
eligibility: The scheme is available to women entrepreneurs who are sole proprietors, partners in a partnership firm, or directors of women-owned private limited company with women having not less than 51% shareholding. The enterprise must be engaged in manufacturing, service, or agro-processing, The applicant must not be a defaulter to any bank or financial institution. The unit should have been in operation for at least two years for existing enterprises, while new projects are also eligible.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of term loans and working capital loans. Collateral-free lending under CGTMSE coverage where applicable. Competitive interest rates linked to SIDBI's internal rating model. Flexible repayment tenure based on project viability. Support for both new project setup and expansion of existing enterprises. Assistance in building credit history and financial discipline for women entrepreneurs.
financial_support: The scheme provides term loans for project cost and working capital loans for operational needs. The quantum of assistance is need-based and subject to the project's viability and the borrower's repayment capacity. Loans are sanctioned based on the project report, financial projections, and creditworthiness of the applicant. The assistance may be covered under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) to facilitate collateral-free lending. Interest rates are determined as per SIDBI's internal risk assessment and are competitive for the MSME segment.
application_process: 1. Identify the project and prepare a detailed project report including technical, financial, and economic aspects. 2. Ensure compliance with eligibility criteria, including women entrepreneurship status and Udyam registration. 3. Approach the nearest SIDBI branch or authorized channel with the project report and required documents. 4. Submit the application along with KYC documents, business registration proof, and financial statements. 5. SIDBI conducts technical and financial appraisal of the project. 6. Upon approval, loan sanction is communicated, and disbursement is made in stages as per project progress. 7. Complete documentation and create security as per loan terms. 8. Begin repayment as per the agreed schedule after moratorium, if any.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

overview: FoSCoS (Food Safety Compliance System) is the online platform operated by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) for food business operators to apply for, renew, and manage FSSAI licenses and registrations. The system ensures compliance with food safety standards under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. It supports licensing for manufacturers, traders, retailers, importers, and other food-related entities across India.
target_beneficiaries: food business operators; manufacturers; traders; retailers; importers; MSME
eligibility: Any person or entity engaged in food business activities including manufacturing, processing, packaging, storage, distribution, sale, or import of food products must obtain FSSAI license or registration based on turnover and scale of operation. The person supervising the production process shall possess at least a degree in Science with Chemistry/Bio Chemistry/Food and Nutrition/ Microbiology or a degree or diploma in food technology/ Dairy technology/ dairy microbiology/ dairy chemistry/ dairy engineering/oil technology /veterinary science /hotel management & catering technology or any degree or diploma in any other discipline related to the specific requirements of the business from a recognized university or institute or equivalent.
benefits: Legal compliance to operate food business, consumer trust and brand reputation, access to government tenders and markets, facilitation of food exports, eligibility for government schemes and subsidies, and ability to display FSSAI logo on products.
financial_support: FSSAI licensing and registration under FoSCoS does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. It is a regulatory compliance mechanism where applicants pay prescribed fees for license issuance and renewal.
application_process: 1. Visit the FoSCoS portal at https://foscos.fssai.gov.in 2. Sign up or log in using existing credentials 3. Select 'Apply for License/Registration' 4. Choose the appropriate license type (Basic, State, or Central) based on turnover and business scale 5. Fill in the online application form with business and product details 6. Upload required documents 7. Pay the applicable fee online 8. Submit the application and track status via the portal 9. Upon approval, download the license/registration certificate.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year; license/registration must be renewed periodically as per validity (1 to 5 years).
implementing_agency: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

overview: The Working Capital Loan Scheme by SIDBI provides collateral-free working capital support to MSMEs through digital platforms like DigiCash and GST Sahay, enabling quick sanction within 48 hours. It is designed to address short-term liquidity needs for raw material purchases, credit sales, and operational expenses. The scheme leverages invoice-based financing and digital public infrastructure for seamless, paperless processing. It targets existing SIDBI customers who are GST and Udyam registered with at least two years of business operations and positive cash accruals.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; micro enterprises; small enterprises; existing SIDBI customers
eligibility: Existing SIDBI customers who are Micro & Small Enterprises with GST and Udyam Registration mandatory, 2 years of business operations, and cash accruals in the last audited financial year.
benefits: Collateral-free working capital financing; quick disbursement; attractive interest rates; digital, straight-through process; end-to-end digital execution; invoice-based financing for purchases (PIBF) or sales (SIBF); up to 100% of purchase invoice value or 90% of sales invoice value processed; direct payment to supplier or customer's bank account; NACH mandate for repayment; use of Digital Public Infrastructure (India Stack) including Aadhaar, UPI, GST, and open API systems.
financial_support: The scheme provides need-based working capital finance with a maximum credit limit of up to ₹50 lakh. For Purchase Invoice Based Financing (PIBF), 100% of the invoice value is processed and paid to the supplier’s bank account. For Sales Invoice Based Financing (SIBF), up to 90% of the invoice value is processed and paid directly to the customer’s bank account. Repayment is made by the customer along with applicable interest on the due date.
application_process: 1. Registration & KYC 2. Sanction & Acceptance of limit/loan 3. Digital Document Execution & NACH mandate 4. Disbursement
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

overview: The NSIC Credit Support Scheme provides credit support to MSMEs for financing the purchase of raw material Assistance Scheme (RMA) by NSIC provides financial assistance to MSMEs for the procurement of raw materials (both indigenous and imported) against the security of a Bank Guarantee. The scheme enables MSMEs to focus on manufacturing quality products by facilitating bulk purchases, cash discounts, and extended credit up to 180 days. It is designed to enhance the competitiveness of MSMEs by reducing working capital constraints and improving procurement efficiency.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSME units with Udyam Registration are eligible to apply for Raw Material Assistance. The scheme applies to units engaged in manufacturing and services; traders are not eligible. Units must have commenced commercial production but may not have completed one year of existence for provisional registration with a monetary limit of Rs. 5.00 Lacs.
benefits: Facilitating procurement of raw material with credit support up to 180 days; MSMEs helped to avail economics of purchases like bulk purchase, cash discount etc.; Issue of Tender Sets free of cost; Exemption from payment of Earnest Money Deposit (EMD); In tender participation, MSEs quoting price within price band of L1+15 per cent shall also be allowed to supply a portion up to 25% of requirement by bringing down their price to L1 Price; Consortia facility for Tender Marketing; Every Central Ministries/Departments/PSUs shall set an annual goal of minimum 25 per cent of the total annual purchases of the products or services produced or rendered by MSEs; Out of annual requirement of 25% procurement from MSEs, 4% is earmarked for units owned by Schedule Caste/Schedule Tribes and 3% is earmarked for units owned by women entrepreneurs; 358 items are reserved for exclusive purchase from MSE Sector.
financial_support: The scheme provides credit support for raw material procurement against the security of a Bank Guarantee from approved banks. The rate of interest varies based on SME rating and unit type (Micro or Small & Medium): For units with valid SME 1 rating: 8.75% p.a. for Micro, 9.25% p.a. for Small & Medium (upto 180 days); For units with valid SME 2 rating: 9.25% p.a. for Micro, 9.75% p.a. for Small & Medium; For other units: 9.75% p.a. for Micro, 10.25% p.a. for Small & Medium. Processing fee is 1.0% p.a. on new sanctions for both Micro and Small & Medium, and 0.5% p.a. on renewal for Micro and 1.0% p.a. for Small & Medium. Penal charge on delayed payment beyond 180 days is 1.25% per quarter over and above the normal rate of interest.
application_process: 1. Apply for Raw Material Assistance only on the prescribed application forms. 2. Download the application forms from the link provided on the NSIC website. 3. Fill and submit the forms to the nearest NSIC Branch Office. 4. Submit the application form along with required documents. 5. Preliminary appraisal and unit inspection are carried out by NSIC. 6. Sanction of limit to the unit. 7. Signing of agreement between NSIC and the unit. 8. Disbursement of assistance to the unit.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. (NSIC)

overview: The Udyam Registration Portal is the official Government of India portal for MSME registration, launched on 1st July 2020 by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. It provides free, paperless, and digital registration for micro, small, and medium enterprises based on investment in plant and machinery or equipment and turnover. The portal integrates with Income Tax and GST Networks for automatic data fetching and issues a dynamic QR-coded certificate with lifetime validity.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; micro enterprises; small enterprises; medium enterprises
eligibility: An enterprise is classified as micro, small, or medium based on investment in plant and machinery or equipment and turnover: micro enterprise (investment ≤ ₹1 crore and turnover ≤ ₹5 crore), small enterprise (investment ≤ ₹10 crore and turnover ≤ ₹50 crore), medium enterprise (investment ≤ ₹50 crore and turnover ≤ ₹250 crore). The difference between manufacturing and services sectors has been removed, and both are treated equally. Exports are excluded from turnover calculation for MSME classification.
benefits: Udyam Registration Certificate with dynamic QR code for verification; mandatory for availing benefits under most MSME Ministry schemes; facilitates Priority Sector Lending from banks as per RBI notification; enables participation in government procurement via GeM integration; no renewal required; lifetime validity; free of cost; paperless and digital process; access to government subsidies, incentives, and support programs; data sharing with CBDT and GSTN for accurate classification.
financial_support: Udyam Registration itself does not provide direct financial support. However, it is mandatory for accessing financial benefits such as Priority Sector Lending (PSL) from banks, credit guarantee schemes, collateral-free loans, and interest subvention under various MSME Ministry schemes. Financial support is delivered through linked schemes like the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) and others, not directly via the registration portal.
application_process: 1. Visit the Udyam Registration Portal at https://udyamregistration.gov.in. 2. Enter Aadhaar number and validate via OTP. 3. Provide PAN details (mandatory for all enterprises except proprietorships not registered under any Act, where PAN of proprietor may be used). 4. Fill in enterprise details including name, type of organization, address, bank details, and NIC code for activity. 5. The system automatically fetches investment and turnover data from Income Tax and GST Networks. 6. Submit the form to receive the Udyam Registration Certificate with a dynamic QR code. 7. Certificate can be downloaded and printed; no further renewal is required.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

overview: The Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS) is an export promotion initiative by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. It aims to promote the manufacture and export of notified goods/products by providing financial incentives in the form of duty credit scrips to exporters. The scheme supports Indian exporters by offsetting infrastructural inefficiencies and enhancing competitiveness in global markets.
target_beneficiaries: exporters; manufacturers; MSME
eligibility: Exporters of notified goods/products as per the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) are eligible for MEIS benefits. The scheme applies to exports made under the IEC (Importer Exporter Code) granted by DGFT. Eligibility is determined based on the product description and ITC(HS) code as notified under the scheme from time to time.
benefits: MEIS provides duty credit scrips as a percentage of the FOB value of exports, which can be used to pay basic customs duty on import of goods, payment of service tax, and settlement of other dues. The scrips are transferable and can be traded in the market. The rate of incentive varies by product and is notified periodically.
financial_support: Financial support under MEIS is provided in the form of duty credit scrips, calculated as a percentage of the FOB value of exports of notified products. The scrips can be utilized for payment of customs duty, excise duty, service tax, and other dues. The incentive rate is product-specific and notified by DGFT.
application_process: 1. Register on the DGFT website (https://dgft.gov.in) with a valid email and mobile number. 2. Login to the DGFT portal. 3. Navigate to the MEIS section under Export Promotion Schemes. 4. Submit an application for MEIS benefits along with required documents such as shipping bills, realization proof, and IEC details. 5. The application is processed by DGFT, and upon approval, duty credit scrips are issued electronically.
deadlines: Applications are typically submitted within the financial year of export; specific timelines are notified by DGFT from time to time.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India

overview: DPIIT Recognition for Startups is a flagship initiative under the Startup India program launched by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It enables eligible startups to gain official recognition, unlocking access to tax benefits, easier compliance, IPR fast-tracking, and various government schemes. Recognition is granted based on criteria such as incorporation type, age, turnover, innovation, and scalability, and is valid for up to 10 years (20 years for deeptech startups) or until turnover exceeds turnover exceeds specified limits.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: The startup should be incorporated as a Private Limited Company or registered as a Partnership Firm, Limited Liability Partnership, or Cooperative Society. Turnover should be less than INR 200 Crores (INR 300 Crores for DeepTech startups) in any of the previous financial years. An entity shall be considered a startup for up to 10 years (20 years for DeepTech startups) from the date of its incorporation. The startup should be working towards innovation or improvement of existing products, services, and processes, and should have the potential to generate employment or create wealth. An entity formed by splitting up or reconstruction of an existing business shall not be considered a 'Startup'.
benefits: DPIIT recognised startups can get the following benefits under the Startup India Initiative: Self-certification compliance with 6 labour laws and 3 environmental laws through a simple online procedure (no inspections for 5 years for labour laws, random checks for environment laws under 'white category'); Fast-tracking of Startup Patent Applications; Panel of facilitators to assist in filing of IP applications with government bearing facilitation cost and 80% rebate on filing of patents; Income tax exemption for 3 consecutive financial years out of the first ten years since incorporation under Section 80-IAC; Easy winding up of company as per Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (within 90 days for simple debt structures); Opportunity to list product on Government e-Marketplace (GeM); Exemption from Prior Experience/Turnover in public procurement for manufacturing sector startups; Exemption from submitting Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) or bid security while filling government tenders.
financial_support: The scheme itself does not provide direct financial support. However, DPIIT recognition enables access to various funding schemes such as the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) offering up to INR 20 lakhs grant, Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) with a corpus of INR 10,000 crore managed by SIDBI investing in SEBI-registered AIFs that fund startups, and Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) providing guarantee cover up to ₹20 crore per borrower for loans from Member Institutions.
application_process: 1. Register on the Startup India portal. 2. Post registration, apply for DPIIT (Department for Industrial Policy and Promotion) recognition. 3. Access the Section 80 IAC exemption application form here. 4. Fill in all details with the below mentioned documents uploaded and submit the application form. 5. Refer to your Dashboard on the Startup India Portal for the status of your application.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is India's national standards body responsible for standardization, hallmarking, and conformity assessment. It develops and publishes Indian standards, implements product certification schemes including compulsory registration for electronics and IT goods, operates hallmarking schemes for gold and silver jewellery, and provides laboratory services and management system certifications. BIS also engages in consumer affairs, training, and international standardization activities.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers; laboratories; jewellers; consumers; industry
eligibility: Eligibility varies by scheme: For product certification, manufacturers must comply with relevant Indian standards; for hallmarking, jewellers and assaying centres must meet BIS requirements; for laboratory recognition, outside labs must meet IS/ISO/IEC 17025 criteria; for compulsory registration, electronics and IT goods manufacturers must register under the order notified by MeitY.
benefits: Benefits include legal compliance, consumer trust, market access, quality assurance, hallmarking purity guarantee, ability to use BIS standard mark, access to government tenders, and recognition under various national and international frameworks.
financial_support: BIS does not provide direct financial support to beneficiaries; it operates through fees for services such as licensing, testing, and certification. Revenue is generated from product certification marking fees, laboratory services, and hallmarking operations.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant Indian Standard for the product or service. 2. Ensure compliance with the standard through appropriate manufacturing and quality control. 3. Apply online via the BIS portal (www.manakonline.in) for licensing or registration. 4. Submit required documents and pay applicable fees. 5. Undergo factory inspection and testing by BIS or recognized labs. 6. Upon successful evaluation, grant of licence or registration is issued.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Bureau of Indian Standards (under Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution)

overview: ECGC Export Credit Guarantee Schemes provide financial assistance to Indian exporters by offering credit guarantees against risks of non-payment by overseas buyers due to commercial or political reasons. The scheme supports export growth by mitigating payment risks and enhancing access to working capital finance from banks. It covers both pre-shipment and post-shipment stages of export transactions.
target_beneficiaries: exporters; banks; MSME
eligibility: Indian exporters, including MSMEs, engaged in export of goods or services, who have obtained an export order and require credit protection against buyer default. Banks lending to such exporters can also avail guarantees to secure their export credit exposure.
benefits: Protection against commercial and political risks, improved access to bank finance at better terms, enhanced creditworthiness of exporters, coverage for both pre-shipment and post-shipment risks, and support for export bill discounting and collection.
financial_support: ECGC provides credit guarantee covers typically up to 90% of the export value, reducing the risk for banks and enabling them to extend pre-shipment and post-shipment finance to exporters. Claims are settled upon buyer default due to insolvency, protracted default, or political events.
application_process: 1. Exporter or bank approaches ECGC with export contract details and buyer information. 2. Submit required documents including export order, invoice, and buyer creditworthiness details. 3. ECGC evaluates the risk and issues a credit guarantee policy. 4. Premium is paid based on risk assessment and coverage amount. 5. Policy is issued and can be used to secure bank finance. 6. In case of default, claim is filed with supporting documents for settlement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted throughout the year based on export transactions.
implementing_agency: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Limited (ECGC), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: Interest Equalization Scheme on Export Credit
overview: The Interest Equalization Scheme on Export Credit is a scheme administered by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to provide interest equalization support on pre- and post-shipment rupee export credit extended by banks to exporters. The scheme aims to enhance the competitiveness of Indian exports by reducing the effective cost of credit for exporters. It is administered by the RBI under the authority of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and is part of the RBI's developmental and regulatory policies to support export promotion.
target_beneficiaries: exporters; MSME exporters; manufacturing exporters; services exporters; agricultural exporters
eligibility: The scheme is available to all exporters of merchandise and services who are availing pre- and post-shipment rupee export credit from banks in India. The exporter must be a resident of India and the export must be in freely convertible currency. The scheme covers exports under the Foreign Trade Policy of India. MSME exporters are eligible for a higher rate of interest equalization under the scheme.
benefits: The scheme provides interest equalization support on rupee export credit, reducing the effective cost of credit for exporters. The benefit is provided as a reimbursement of a portion of the interest charged by banks on export credit. The rate of interest equalization is 3% for all exporters and an additional 2% for MSME exporters, making it 5% for MSMEs. The benefit is credited directly to the exporter's account by the bank after claiming reimbursement from the RBI.
financial_support: The scheme provides interest equalization support at the rate of 3% per annum for all exporters and an additional 2% per annum for MSME exporters on the outstanding amount of rupee export credit. The support is provided as a reimbursement to banks, which then pass on the benefit to exporters by reducing the effective interest rate on export credit. The scheme is funded by the Government of India and administered by the Reserve Bank of India.
application_process: 1. Exporter avails pre- or post-shipment rupee export credit from a bank in India. 2. Bank charges interest on the export credit as per prevailing rates. 3. Bank claims reimbursement of interest equalization from the Reserve Bank of India at the rate of 3% per annum (or 5% for MSME exporters) on the outstanding export credit. 4. RBI reimburses the claimed amount to the bank. 5. Bank passes on the benefit to the exporter by reducing the effective interest rate on the export credit.
deadlines: Claims can be submitted by banks to the RBI on a quarterly basis within the stipulated time frame after the end of each quarter. There is no fixed deadline for exporters to avail the benefit, as it is passed on by banks upon disbursement of export credit.
implementing_agency: Reserve Bank of India

overview: The Textile Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) is a Government of India initiative launched in 1999 to facilitate technological upgradation of the textile industry by providing financial assistance for modernization and expansion of textile units. It aims to enhance productivity, quality, and competitiveness of the Indian textile sector through capital investment in machinery and equipment. The scheme supports both new and existing units across various segments of the textile value chain, including spinning, weaving, processing, and garmenting.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; textile units; existing textile units; new textile units
eligibility: Existing and new textile units engaged in activities such as spinning, weaving, processing, knitting, garmenting, made-ups, technical textiles, and jute are eligible for assistance under TUFS. The unit must be registered as a proprietorship, partnership, private limited company, public limited company, cooperative society, or any other legal entity engaged in textile manufacturing. The machinery proposed for upgradation must be new and indigenous or imported, and must not have been used previously.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of interest reimbursement or capital subsidy on eligible machinery for technological upgradation. The scheme provides reimbursement of interest paid on term loans availed from banks/financial institutions for procurement of eligible machinery. Additionally, capital subsidy is available for specific segments like processing, weaving, and garmenting under modified versions of the scheme. Non-financial benefits include improved productivity, product quality, energy efficiency, and market competitiveness.
financial_support: Under TUFS, eligible textile units can avail interest reimbursement of up to 5% on term loans for a period of 5 to 7 years, depending on the segment and type of machinery. For certain high-priority segments like processing, weaving, and garmenting, a capital subsidy of up to 10% (with a ceiling of INR 30 lakhs) is provided under the Modified TUFS. The financial support is disbursed through nodal agencies after verification of loan documents and installation of machinery. The loan must be availed from scheduled commercial banks or financial institutions approved by the Ministry of Textiles.
application_process: 1. Identify eligible machinery for upgradation and obtain quotations from suppliers. 2. Apply for a term loan from a scheduled commercial bank or financial institution for the procurement of machinery. 3. Submit the loan sanction letter and machinery details to the nodal agency (Office of the Textile Commissioner) for registration under TUFS. 4. Install the machinery and submit installation certificate along with invoices and bank statements. 5. Submit quarterly interest payment certificates to claim interest reimbursement. 6. The nodal agency verifies the documents and disburses the interest reimbursement or capital subsidy as applicable.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Office of the Textile Commissioner, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

overview: Export Credit Insurance for Banks (ECIB) is a scheme by ECGC Limited to provide credit insurance to banks against risks in export financing. It supports Indian exporters by enabling banks to offer pre-shipment and post-shipment credit with reduced risk. The scheme enhances export competitiveness by facilitating access to working capital and term loans for export-oriented businesses.
target_beneficiaries: banks; MSME; exporters
eligibility: Banks and financial institutions in India that extend pre-shipment and post-shipment credit to exporters are eligible to avail insurance cover under the ECIB scheme. The exporter must be an Indian entity engaged in export of goods or services, and the transaction must involve an overseas buyer. The credit facility must be for a bonafide export transaction as per RBI guidelines.
benefits: Banks receive insurance cover against commercial and political risks of non-payment by overseas buyers. This enables them to lend more confidently to exporters, especially MSMEs, at competitive rates. Exporters benefit from easier access to working capital and term loans. The scheme reduces non-performing assets (NPAs) in banks' export loan portfolios and supports timely realization of export proceeds.
financial_support: ECIB provides insurance cover up to 90% of the loan amount extended by banks to exporters for pre-shipment and post-shipment finance. The premium is paid by the bank, and claims are settled in case of buyer default due to insolvency, protracted default, or political events. The mechanism involves submission of claim documents by the bank to ECGC after exhausting recovery efforts.
application_process: 1. Banks approach ECGC with a request for ECIB cover for specific export credit facilities. 2. Submit details of the exporter, overseas buyer, nature of goods/services, value, and tenure of credit. 3. ECGC evaluates the risk based on buyer country, creditworthiness, and transaction type. 4. Upon approval, issue of insurance policy with terms and conditions. 5. Bank disburses loan to exporter under the covered facility. 6. In case of default, bank files claim with ECGC after due diligence and recovery attempts. 7. ECGC processes claim and settles payable amount as per policy terms.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Limited (ECGC)

overview: The Transport & Marketing Assistance (TMA) scheme is an export promotion initiative under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) of the Government of India, aimed at providing financial assistance for international freight and marketing expenses to boost agricultural and processed food exports. It supports exporters of APEDA-scheduled products by reimbursing a portion of freight and marketing costs incurred for exports to specified destinations. The scheme is implemented by APEDA under the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
target_beneficiaries: exporters; MSME; agri-exporters; processed food exporters
eligibility: Exporters of APEDA-scheduled products who have a valid Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC) from APEDA and an Import Export Code (IEC) from DGFT are eligible. The scheme applies to exports made to notified countries under the TMA guidelines, with specific product and destination eligibility as per periodic notifications issued by DGFT under the Foreign Trade Policy.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of reimbursement for a portion of international freight and marketing expenses incurred on eligible exports. The support is provided as a subsidy to reduce the cost burden on exporters and improve price competitiveness in global markets. Non-financial benefits include enhanced market access and brand visibility through supported marketing activities.
financial_support: The scheme provides reimbursement of a specified percentage of international freight and marketing costs incurred on eligible exports, as per the rates and conditions notified by DGFT from time to time under the Foreign Trade Policy. The assistance is disbursed post-shipment upon submission of required documents and verification by APEDA.
application_process: 1. Obtain IEC from DGFT and RCMC from APEDA. 2. Ensure the exported product and destination are covered under the current TMA notification. 3. Submit the application for TMA claim along with shipping bills, proof of payment of freight and marketing expenses, and other required documents. 4. APEDA verifies the claim and processes the reimbursement. 5. Funds are transferred to the exporter’s bank account upon approval.
deadlines: As per notifications issued under Foreign Trade Policy; claims must be submitted within the stipulated time frame post-shipment as specified in the respective TMA notification.
implementing_agency: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA)
overview: PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (PM MITRA) is a scheme launched by the Ministry of Textiles to develop world-class textile manufacturing infrastructure through the establishment of integrated textile parks. The scheme aims to strengthen the textile value chain from fibre to fashion by creating plug-and-play facilities and attracting investment in the sector. It focuses on reducing logistics costs, improving competitiveness, and generating employment in the textiles and apparel industry.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; large enterprises; textile manufacturers; apparel units
eligibility: Entities interested in setting up textile manufacturing units within PM MITRA parks, including domestic and foreign investors, MSMEs, large enterprises, and joint ventures, subject to compliance with park regulations and allotment criteria defined by the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) managing each park.
benefits: Plug-and-play infrastructure with ready-to-use factory buildings, common facilities (testing labs, design centres, logistics hubs), power, water, and effluent treatment systems; single-window clearances; fiscal incentives as per state policies; skill development centres; and logistic support for domestic and export-oriented units.
