financial_support: The scheme provides capital subsidy support for the development of PM MITRA parks through equity contribution by the Government of India in the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) set up for each park, with a total committed financial outlay of INR 4,445 crore for seven parks over a period of five years.
application_process: 1. Identify the PM MITRA park of interest based on location and sector focus. 2. Contact the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) responsible for the park’s development and allotment. 3. Submit an expression of interest or application for land/unit allotment as per the SPV’s guidelines. 4. Undergo evaluation based on investment commitment, employment generation, and value addition. 5. Upon approval, execute lease agreement and proceed with unit setup.
deadlines: Rolling basis — subject to availability of land/units in the respective PM MITRA parks.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

overview: The SAMPADA Scheme (Food Processing), now known as Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana as Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY), is an umbrella Central sector scheme approved by the Government of India on 03.05.2017 with a total allocation of Rs. 6000 crore for the implementation period 2016-2020, later extended till 31.03.2026 with an additional allocation of Rs. 4600 crore. It aims to create modern infrastructure with efficient supply chain management from farm gate to retail outlet, boost food processing sector growth, provide better returns to farmers, double farmers' income, create employment opportunities in rural areas, reduce agricultural wastage, increase processing levels, and enhance exports of processed foods. The scheme comprises seven component schemes including Mega Food Parks, Integrated Cold Chain, Agro-Processing Clusters, Creation of Backward and Forward Linkages, Creation/Expansion of Food Processing & Preservation Capacities, Food Safety and Quality Assurance Infrastructure, and Human Resources and Institutions.
target_beneficiaries: entrepreneurs; MSME; agri-startups; farmers; food processing units; SC/ST Category; NER Region
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component scheme. For the Research & Development in Processed Food Sector: All Universities, IITs, Central/State Government Institutions, Government funded Organizations, R&D laboratories and CSIR recognized R&D units in private sector. For other sub-schemes like Mega Food Parks, Cold Chain, Agro-Processing Clusters, etc., eligibility typically includes entrepreneurs, MSMEs, FPOs, SHGs, producer cooperatives, and entities involved in food processing, with specific criteria detailed in individual scheme guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid for setting up infrastructure projects in food processing sector; technical and financial support for agro-processing clusters, cold chain, food testing laboratories, backward and forward linkages, and food processing unit expansion; support for skill development, research and development, promotional activities, and operational guidelines; access to subsidized credit through special funds; and facilitation of project approval via Program Management Agencies (PMAs) and Project Approval Committees.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as grants-in-aid for infrastructure projects in the food processing sector under various component schemes. The pattern of release of funds involves two instalments: 50% upon submission of acceptance letter and compliance documents, and the remaining 50% upon submission of utilization certificate and proof of expenditure. Funds are released through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) via the EAT module. The scheme leverages investment of Rs. 11,095.93 crore, with a total government allocation of Rs. 10,600 crore (initial Rs. 6000 crore + extension Rs. 4600 crore).
application_process: 1. Visit the respective scheme portal (e.g., PMKSY, Mega Food Park, Cold Chain, etc.) based on the component of interest. 2. Check for active Expressions of Interest (EoI) or notifications inviting proposals. 3. Download guidelines and application forms from the 'Download Guidelines' or 'Download Circulars' section. 4. Prepare the proposal as per the scheme guidelines, including project report, eligibility documents, and financial details. 5. Submit the application online through the designated portal or via email to the concerned division. 6. Await scrutiny by the Technical Committee and Project Approval Committee. 7. Upon approval, receive approval letter and proceed with fund release in instalments as per the Pattern of Release of Funds.
deadlines: Varies by component scheme and EoI notifications; many are time-bound with extensions (e.g., EOI dated 04.10.2023 extended upto 15.12.2023 for several schemes). Specific deadlines are announced in individual notifications. No universal rolling basis; applicants must check current EoIs on the ministry website.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI)

overview: The Powertex India Scheme is a comprehensive initiative launched by the Ministry of Textiles to support the growth and modernization of the powerloom sector in India. It aims to enhance the competitiveness of powerloom units through technology upgradation, skill development, market promotion, and infrastructure support. The scheme focuses on improving productivity, quality, and value realization for powerloom weavers and entrepreneurs across the country.
target_beneficiaries: powerloom units; MSME; weavers; entrepreneurs in the textile sector
eligibility: Powerloom units, cooperative societies, self-help groups, NGOs, and entrepreneurs engaged in powerloom activities are eligible to apply. The units must be registered and operational, with preference given to those located in identified powerloom clusters and those adopting modern, energy-efficient looms.
benefits: Financial subsidies for technology upgradation, skill development training, market development assistance, infrastructure support for common facility centers, interest subsidy on loans, and support for product design and diversification. The scheme also provides assistance for obtaining quality certifications and participating in national and international trade fairs.
financial_support: Under the scheme, financial support is provided in the form of capital subsidy ranging from 15% to 50% of the project cost for technology upgradation, depending on the type of machinery and location. Interest subsidy of up to 6% is available on term loans for eligible units. Additional support includes 100% reimbursement for skill training costs and 75% subsidy for market promotion activities.
application_process: 1. Identify the need for upgradation or support under the scheme components. 2. Prepare a detailed project report including cost estimates and benefits. 3. Register on the official Powertex India portal or through the designated implementing agency. 4. Submit the application along with required documents. 5. Application is scrutinized by the technical committee. 6. Upon approval, submit proof of installation and expenditure. 7. Subsidy is disbursed after verification and validation of the bank account of the beneficiary.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

overview: The Integrated Wool Development Programme (IWDP) is a centrally sponsored scheme under the Ministry of Textiles aimed at the holistic development of the wool sector in India. It focuses on improving productivity, quality, and value addition across the wool value chain, from sheep rearing to finished products. The programme supports activities such as breed improvement, processing, marketing, and skill development to enhance the competitiveness of Indian wool and wool products in domestic and international markets.
target_beneficiaries: sheep rearers; artisans; weavers; small entrepreneurs; self-help groups; NGOs; state wool development boards
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include individual sheep rearers, self-help groups, cooperatives, NGOs, state wool development boards, and entrepreneurs engaged in wool rearing, processing, marketing, or value addition activities. Preference is given to beneficiaries from economically weaker sections, women, SC/ST communities, and residents of hilly and backward areas where wool production is traditionally practiced.
benefits: Beneficiaries receive financial assistance in the form of subsidies for breed improvement (e.g., import of elite rams), establishment of processing units, skill development training, marketing support, and setting up of common facility centres. Additional support includes technical guidance, access to improved breeding stock, and assistance for participation in national and international exhibitions to promote wool products.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as a subsidy ranging from 50% to 80% of the project cost, depending on the beneficiary category and activity type. For general beneficiaries, the subsidy is 50%, while for SC/ST, women, and beneficiaries from hilly and backward areas, it can go up to 80%. The subsidy is disbursed through implementing agencies after verification of project completion and submission of required documents.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant component of the IWDP under which the activity falls (e.g., breed improvement, processing, marketing). 2. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, budget, implementation plan, and expected outcomes. 3. Submit the proposal to the State Wool Development Board or the designated implementing agency in the state. 4. The proposal is reviewed by the State Level Committee for technical and financial feasibility. 5. Upon approval, the implementing agency sanctions the subsidy amount. 6. The beneficiary implements the project as per the approved plan. 7. After completion, the beneficiary submits utilization certificates, bills, and completion report. 8. The subsidy is released after verification of documents and field inspection by the implementing agency.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and approval by the State Level Committee.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

overview: Operation Greens is a scheme announced in the Union Budget 2018-19 with an outlay of Rs.500 crore to promote Farmer Producers Organizations (FPOs), agri-logistics, processing facilities and professional management for the development of Tomato, Onion and Potato and later expanded to 2018. The scheme has two components: (I) Long Term Intervention-Integrated Value Chain Development Projects and (II) Short-Term Interventions. It aims to stabilize supply and prices of TOP crops and reduce post-harvest losses.
target_beneficiaries: Farmer Producers Organizations (FPOs); agri-logistics; processing facilities
eligibility: The scheme is implemented for development of Tomato, Onion and Potato (TOP) value chain since November 2018. The scheme has two components namely (I) Long Term Intervention-Integrated Value Chain Development Projects and (II) Short-Term Interventions.
benefits: Promotion of Farmer Producers Organizations (FPOs), agri-logistics, processing facilities and professional management. Stabilization of supply and prices of TOP crops. Reduction of post-harvest losses.
financial_support: The scheme was announced with an outlay of Rs.500 crore in the Union Budget 2018-19 to promote Farmer Producers Organizations (FPOs), agri-logistics, processing facilities and professional management.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Food Processing Industries

overview: The Cold Chain Infrastructure Scheme is a component of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) aimed at developing integrated cold chain and value addition infrastructure to reduce post-harvest losses, enhance processing levels, and boost exports of perishable products. It supports the setting up of multi-product food irradiation units and cold chain projects across India. The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid for infrastructure development in the food processing sector.
target_beneficiaries: entrepreneurs; MSME; agri-startups; SC/ST; NER Region
eligibility: Prospective entrepreneurs, including those from SC/ST Category and NER Region, are eligible to apply under various Sub-Schemes of PMKSY. Eligibility also extends to units proposed under the Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure scheme. Applications are invited through Expression of Interest (EoI) for setting up of multi-product food irradiation units and cold chain projects. Specific eligibility criteria for R&D and other sub-schemes may apply as per respective guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid for setting up infrastructure projects in the food processing sector. Support includes pattern of assistance for project implementation, release of funds in instalments, and technical guidance. The scheme facilitates access to cold chain infrastructure, value addition facilities, and irradiation units. It also enables beneficiaries to leverage investment, improve market linkages, and enhance product shelf life and safety.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as grants-in-aid for infrastructure projects under the Food Processing Sector. The release of funds follows a two-installment pattern: 50% upon compliance with initial conditions (including acceptance letter, land documents, and term loan details), and the remaining 50% upon submission of utilization certificate and verification of expenditure. Funds are released through the PFMS EAT module. The scheme also outlines requirements for bank accounts, surety bonds, and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Submit Expression of Interest (EoI) for setting up of multi-product food irradiation units or cold chain projects under the scheme. 2. Await pre-bid meeting notices and participate in clarification sessions. 3. Respond to RFPs for engagement of Programme Management Agency (PMA) if applicable. 4. Submit detailed proposals through the designated portal/link. 5. Undergo evaluation by Technical Committee and Project Approval Committee. 6. Receive approval from Inter-Ministerial Approval Committee (IMAC). 7. Fulfill compliance requirements including land documents, bank account details, and surety bond. 8. Receive first instalment of grant (50%) upon submission of acceptance letter and compliance. 9. Submit utilization certificate and expenditure details for second instalment (50%).
deadlines: Rolling basis — EoIs and proposals are invited periodically with specific closing dates (e.g., EoI dated 27.05.2025 for irradiation units closing 28.02.2026; EoI dated 20.05.2026 for irradiation units).
implementing_agency: Ministry of Food Processing Industries

overview: The Modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC 2.0) scheme is a government initiative under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at strengthening India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem by developing world-class infrastructure and common facilities in electronics manufacturing clusters. The scheme supports the creation of plug-and-play infrastructure, common facility centers, and other enabling infrastructure to attract investments in electronics manufacturing. It aims to enhance India's competitiveness in global electronics value chains and promote domestic value addition.
target_beneficiaries: electronics manufacturers; MSME; startups; electronics manufacturing clusters
eligibility: State Governments, Union Territory Administrations, and their agencies/organizations are eligible to apply for setting up Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMCs) under the scheme. Private entities can also participate as Special Purpose VGF (Viability Gap Funding) scheme. Private sector entities can participate through Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) in partnership with State Governments/UT Administrations. The scheme supports Greenfield and Brownfield projects for electronics manufacturing, including semiconductor and display fabrication units.
benefits: Financial support in the form of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) up to 50% of the project cost for Greenfield EMCs and 75% for Brownfield EMCs, with a ceiling of INR 500 crore per 100 acres of land. Additional support includes infrastructure development such as roads, water supply, power supply, effluent treatment plants, and common facility centers like testing labs, design centers, and skill development centers. The scheme also provides support for land acquisition, site development, and enabling infrastructure to create plug-and-play facilities for electronics manufacturers.
financial_support: The scheme provides Viability Gap Funding (VGF) as a capital subsidy: up to 50% of project cost for Greenfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMCs) and up to 75% for Brownfield EMCs, with a maximum ceiling of INR 500 crore per 100 acres of land. The financial support is disbursed in milestones linked to project milestones such as land acquisition, site development, and infrastructure creation. The funding is intended to cover infrastructure development including roads, water, power, effluent treatment, and common facility centers like testing labs, design centers, and skill development centers.
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 500 crore per 100 acres of land
application_process: 1. State Government/UT Administration or its agency identifies land and prepares a Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Electronics Manufacturing Cluster (EMC). 2. The proposal is submitted to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) through the State Government/UT Administration. 3. MeitY appraises the proposal through an Expert Committee or Project Appraisal Committee. 4. Upon approval, an In-Principle Approval (IPA) is issued. 5. The State Government/UT Administration acquires the land and begins site development. 6. Detailed Project Report (DPR) is submitted for final approval. 7. Upon final approval, the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) is released in milestones linked to project progress. 8. The State Government/UT Administration or its agency implements the project and develops the infrastructure. 9. The developed infrastructure is made available to electronics manufacturers on a plug-and-play basis.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and appraisal cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: Samarth (Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector) is a flagship skill development scheme approved in continuation to the Integrated Skill Development Scheme for the 12th FYP, Cabinet Committee of Economic Affairs. The scheme aims to provide demand-driven, placement-oriented skilling programmes to incentivize industry efforts in creating jobs in the organized textile and related sectors, promote skilling and skill up-gradation in traditional sectors, and provide sustainable livelihood through wage or self-employment across the country. It targets training 10 lakh persons over three years (2017-20) with an estimated budget of 1300 crore, later extended to train 3 lakh persons with an additional outlay of 495 crore for 2024-25 and 2025-26.
target_beneficiaries: unemployed youth; persons from all sections of society; marginalized social groups; beneficiaries in 115 aspirational districts
eligibility: The scheme invites participation of Textiles Industry/Associations registered under Central or State Government/Chambers of Commerce of Central or State Government. Implementing Agencies include Textile Industry, Institutions/Organization of the Ministry of Textiles/State Governments having training infrastructure and placement tie-ups with textile industry, and Reputed training institutions/NGOs/Societies/Trusts/Organizations/Companies/Start Ups/Entrepreneurs active in textile sector having placement tie-ups with textile industry. For self-employment, concessional credit under Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana will be provided for beneficiaries. Preference given to marginalized social groups and 115 aspirational districts.
benefits: Demand-driven, placement oriented NSQF compliant skilling programmes; placement linked skilling with mandatory wage employment (70% in organized sector, 50% in traditional sector); post-placement tracking for one year; third party assessment and certification; Aadhaar enabled biometric attendance system with minimum 80% attendance; CCTV recording for entire training programme and assessment process; training by certified trainers having ToT certification by RSA/SSCs; robust MIS and real-time scheme information publicized; call centre (Helpline) for feedback; mobile app for stakeholders; preference for marginalized social groups and 115 aspirational districts; public grievance redressal with designated officer; internal complaints committee under Sexual Harassment Act; funding as per MSDE norms; common branding as per MSDE guidelines; concessional credit under Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana for self-employment.
financial_support: Funds are released linked to physical progress updated on the MIS. The release of funds will be linked to physical progress updated on the MIS. For self-employment, concessional credit under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana will be provided for beneficiaries. Funding as per common norms of MSDE.
application_process: 1. Register for Empanelment under 'Samarth' (SCBTS) by clicking on Register for Empanelment under 'Samarth' (SCBTS) for new Registration. 2. Enter Organization Name, Address details, Phone, Email id (must be unique), and Captcha. 3. Click on Register button to register empanelment; verification link sent to registered mail id. 4. Click on verification link (highlighted with blue colour) for verification of registered mail id. 5. Click on Go to home page button to redirect to Home page. 6. Click on Login Here button to redirect to Login page. 7. Enter Valid Login Credential (Email id and password), enter captcha, then click on login button.
deadlines: Please upload action plan (project wise) in MIS till 29-01-2024 under tab 'Notice'.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
contact_details: Address: Ministry of Textiles Udyog Bhawan New Delhi-110011 Ph:+91-011-23062445 Email : samarth-mot[at]gov[dot]in

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components (SPECS)
overview: The Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) is a financial incentive scheme launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to promote domestic manufacturing of electronic components and semiconductors. It aims to reduce import dependency and strengthen India's position in the global electronics value chain by providing financial support to eligible applicants setting up new manufacturing units or expanding existing ones.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; manufacturing units
eligibility: Eligible applicants include companies registered in India under the Companies Act, 2013 or earlier, or Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs) registered under the LLP Act, 2008, engaged in the manufacturing of notified electronic components. The applicant must have a minimum net worth as specified in the scheme guidelines and must not have availed benefits under any other central or state government scheme for the same investment. The manufacturing unit must be located in India and commence commercial production within the stipulated time frame.
benefits: Financial incentive in the form of reimbursement of capital expenditure incurred on plant, machinery, equipment, and associated utilities for setting up a new manufacturing unit or expansion of an existing unit. The incentive is provided as a percentage of the capital expenditure, subject to a ceiling per unit of investment. Non-financial benefits include facilitation of clearances, technical support, and promotion of domestic value addition in the electronics supply chain.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support as a subsidy ranging from 25% to 50% of the capital expenditure on plant, machinery, equipment, and associated utilities, depending on the category of electronic component. The subsidy is disbursed in installments linked to the achievement of milestones such as commencement of commercial production and verification of capital expenditure. The total outlay of the scheme is INR 3,280 crore.
application_process: 1. Applicants must register on the National Single Window System (NSWS) portal. 2.0 the application form along with detailed project report, incorporation documents, board resolution, and details of proposed investment. 3. The application is scrutinized by the Project Management Agency (PMA) appointed by MeitY. 4. Upon approval, a Letter of Approval is issued. 5. After commencement of commercial production, the applicant submits claims for reimbursement with supporting documents such as chartered accountant certificates, bank statements, and invoices. 6. Claims are verified by the PMA and subsidy is disbursed to the applicant's bank account.
deadlines: The scheme was open for applications from 1st April 20 to 2023. No further applications are being accepted as the scheme has reached its financial closure.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) is a central government scheme launched to incentivize employers for generating new employment by paying the employer's contribution to the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) and Employees' State Insurance (ESI) for new employees. The scheme aims to encourage job creation in the formal sector, particularly benefiting first-time employees and supporting workforce formalization. It was operational from 2016 to 2019 and has since been subsumed into other initiatives like the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rozgar Yojana (ABRY).
target_beneficiaries: employers; new employees; formal sector workers
eligibility: Employers who have registered new employees with EPFO and/or ESIC on or after 1 April 2016, with a Universal Account Number (UAN) assigned to the employee, and who have not previously benefited from similar schemes for the same employee. The employee must be drawing a monthly wage of less than INR 15,000.
benefits: The government pays the employer's full contribution (12% towards EPF and ESI) for a period of three years for new employees earning less than INR 15,000 per month. This reduces the employer's cost of hiring and encourages formal employment generation.
financial_support: Under PMRPY, the Government of India pays the employer's contribution of 12% towards the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) and Employees' State Insurance (ESI) for new employees for a duration of three years from the date of registration. The support is provided directly to EPFO and ESIC on behalf of the employer.
application_process: 1. Employer registers new employees with EPFO and/or ESIC and obtains their Universal Account Number (UAN). 2. Employer ensures the employee's monthly wage is below INR 15,000. 3. Employer submits the details of such new employees through the EPFO employer portal. 4. EPFO verifies the eligibility and processes the government's share of EPF and ESI contributions. 5. The government remits the employer's contribution directly to EPFO and ESIC accounts.
deadlines: Scheme was applicable for employees registered up to 31 March 2019; benefits provided for three years from date of registration. No longer accepting new registrations.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India

scheme_name: ESDM – Electronic System Design and Manufacturing Scheme
overview: The ESDM – Electronic System Design and Manufacturing Scheme is a Government of India initiative under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at promoting domestic manufacturing and value addition in the electronics system design and manufacturing sector. The scheme aims to enhance India's capabilities in electronics manufacturing, reduce import dependence, and promote innovation and investment in the ESDM sector. It supports the development of electronic systems and components through incentives, infrastructure support, and policy interventions to strengthen the domestic electronics manufacturing ecosystem.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; manufacturing units; electronics manufacturers
eligibility: The scheme is open to Indian companies, including MSMEs, startups, and large enterprises, engaged in or planning to engage in electronic system design and manufacturing activities. Applicants must be registered entities in India with a valid GSTIN and must propose projects involving value addition in electronics manufacturing, such as design, development, prototyping, testing, and manufacturing of electronic systems and components. Preference may be given to projects involving semiconductor design, semiconductor fabrication, electronic components, and high-value electronics manufacturing.
benefits: The scheme provides financial incentives in the form of subsidies or incentives on capital expenditure, interest subsidies on loans, reimbursement of certain expenses related to technology acquisition, skill development, and quality certification. It also offers support for setting up manufacturing units, access to common facility centers, assistance in obtaining certifications, and facilitation of technology transfer and collaboration with R&D institutions. Additionally, it supports market development, export promotion, and participation in international exhibitions and trade fairs.
financial_support: Financial support under the ESDM scheme includes capital subsidies, interest subsidies, and reimbursement of certain expenses. The exact quantum and mechanism of support vary based on the specific component of the scheme and the nature of the project. Support is typically provided as a percentage of eligible project cost, subject to upper limits, and is disbursed through designated nodal agencies upon verification of milestones and expenditure.
application_process:
1. Visit the official MeitY website or the designated portal for the ESDM scheme.
2. Register and create an account on the portal.
3. Fill out the online application form with details of the proposed project, including project report, financials, and implementation plan.
4. Upload required documents such as company registration, GSTIN, project report, bank details, and other relevant certificates.
5. Submit the application and await scrutiny by the nodal agency.
6. Upon preliminary approval, submit detailed project report and financial closure documents.
7. Upon final approval, enter into an agreement with the implementing agency and fulfill compliance requirements.
8. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates for disbursement of funds in installments.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: The Cent Kalyani Scheme is a loan product offered by Central Bank of India specifically designed to support women entrepreneurs in establishing or expanding their business ventures. It provides financial assistance through term loans to eligible women entrepreneurs for various business purposes including working capital, asset creation, and business expansion. The scheme aims to promote women's entrepreneurship and economic empowerment by offering accessible credit facilities with favorable terms.
target_beneficiaries: women entrepreneurs
eligibility: Women entrepreneurs who are Indian nationals, aged 18 years and above, with KYC-compliant accounts with Central Bank of India. The scheme is applicable to women engaged in manufacturing, service, trading, or agricultural activities. Applicants must have a viable business project and demonstrate repayment capacity. Existing Central Bank of India customers with satisfactory account conduct are preferred.
benefits: Financial support through term loans for business purposes, no collateral requirement for loans up to a certain limit (as per CGTMSE coverage), competitive interest rates, flexible repayment tenure, and support for various business activities including working capital, asset creation, and business expansion. The scheme also offers guidance and support through the bank's MSME and women entrepreneur cell.
financial_support: The scheme provides term loans to women entrepreneurs with loan quantum determined based on project viability and repayment capacity. While specific loan limits are not detailed in the evidence, the scheme operates under the bank's general lending policies for MSMEs. Loans may be covered under CGTMSE for collateral-free lending up to specified limits. Interest rates are linked to external benchmarks like MCLR/RBLR with applicable spreads.
application_process: 1. Visit the nearest Central Bank of India branch or access the bank's online portal. 2. Inquire about the Cent Kalyani Scheme for women entrepreneurs. 3. Obtain and fill the loan application form. 4. Submit the application along with required documents including KYC, business plan, and financial projections. 5. Bank officials will verify documents and assess project viability. 6. Upon approval, loan sanction letter will be issued. 7. Complete legal formalities and disbursement will be made as per agreed terms.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Central Bank of India
contact_details: Toll Free Number - 1800 30 30 - for all | Toll Free Number - 18002031911 - Exclusively for Pensioner

scheme_name: Stree Shakti Package for Women Entrepreneurs
overview: The Stree Shakti Package for Women Entrepreneurs is a scheme by the State Bank of India (SBI) aimed at supporting women entrepreneurs by providing financial assistance and other benefits to promote women entrepreneurship in India. The scheme offers financial support in the form of loans and other benefits to help women start and expand their businesses.
target_beneficiaries: women entrepreneurs
eligibility: The scheme is available to women entrepreneurs who are Indian citizens, aged 18 years and above, and engaged in or planning to start a business venture. Applicants must have a viable business project and meet the bank's creditworthiness criteria. The scheme is applicable to individual women entrepreneurs, partnership firms, private limited companies, and cooperative societies where women hold a majority stake.
benefits: The scheme offers concessional interest rates, reduced margin requirements, relaxed collateral norms, and extended repayment periods. It also provides access to SBI's digital banking platforms like YONO for easy application and tracking. Additional benefits include waiver of certain processing fees and access to financial literacy and business development support through SBI's initiatives.
financial_support: The scheme provides term loans and working capital finance to women entrepreneurs. The loan amount varies based on the project viability and creditworthiness of the applicant. Interest rates are concessional compared to standard SBI rates, and margin requirements are relaxed. Loans are disbursed through SBI branches or digital channels like YONO app after due diligence and approval.
application_process: 1. Visit the nearest SBI branch or log in to the YONO SBI app. 2. Inquire about the Stree Shakti Package for Women Entrepreneurs. 3. Submit the loan application form along with required documents. 4. Undergo credit appraisal and project viability assessment by the bank. 5. Upon approval, complete documentation and accept the loan offer. 6. Loan amount is disbursed to the designated bank account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: State Bank of India

overview: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to reduce poverty and vulnerability of urban poor households by enabling access to gainful self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities. It aims to build strong grassroots-level institutions of the poor, provide shelter to the urban homeless, support urban street vendors, and promote financial inclusion and skill development. The mission operates through a three-tier structure at national, state, and city levels, with implementation led by Urban Local Bodies (ULBs).
target_beneficiaries: urban poor; urban homeless; street vendors; women; SC/ST; minorities; differently-abled persons; Self Help Groups (SHGs); micro entrepreneurs
eligibility: The primary target of DAY-NULM is the urban poor, including the urban homeless. As an interim measure, the target is the urban population identified as below poverty line by States/UTs. Coverage may be broadened to include families of disadvantaged groups like SCs, STs, women, minorities, disabled, etc., subject to a maximum of 25 percent of the urban poor population. Under DAY-NULM, Self Help Groups (SHGs) of urban poor will be formed, with at least 70% of members being urban poor to qualify for funding support. SHGs may consist of 10 to 20 members, and in hilly/tribal areas or for differently-abled persons, smaller groups with a minimum of 5 members may be formed. Normally, women SHGs will be formed, but male SHGs of handicapped persons are allowed. For the Self-Employment Programme (SEP), the percentage of women beneficiaries shall not be less than 30 percent, SCs and STs must be benefited at least to the extent of their proportion in the urban poor population, and a special provision of 3 percent reservation is made for the differently-abled. At least 15 percent of physical and financial targets under SEP shall be earmarked for minority communities.
benefits: DAY-NULM provides financial and non-financial benefits including: formation and strengthening of Self Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations; access to skill training through Employment through Skills Training and Placement (EST&P); financial assistance for self-employment ventures via the Self-Employment Programme (SEP) with interest subsidy on bank loans; support for urban street vendors through survey, identity cards, city street vending plans, infrastructure improvement, training, financial inclusion, and access to credit; provision of permanent shelters with basic infrastructure for the urban homeless; convergence with entitlements like social security pensions, PDS, ICDS, bank accounts, identity proof, school admission, and healthcare; financial inclusion through opening of bank accounts, financial literacy, and affordable insurance; revolving fund support to SHGs and federations; establishment of City Livelihood Centres (CLCs); training and capacity building for community institutions; and support for innovative and special projects. Under SEP, interest subsidy is provided on bank loans for individual and group enterprises, with no collateral required for loans up to Rs. 10 lakhs, and project costs capped at Rs. 2 lakhs for individual enterprises and Rs. 10 lakhs for group enterprises. Credit guarantee cover is available through CGTMSE. For SHG bank linkage, interest subsidy is provided on timely repayment. Under PMFME convergence, seed capital of Rs. 40,000 per SHG member is provided for working capital and purchase of small tools, with loan tenure of 18-36 months and interest not exceeding 6% per annum.
financial_support: Financial support under DAY-NULM is delivered through multiple components. Under the Self-Employment Programme (SEP), interest subsidy is provided on bank loans for individual and group enterprises, where the difference between 7% per annum and the prevailing rate of interest is reimbursed to banks for timely repayment. No collateral is required for loans up to Rs. 10 lakhs, with project costs capped at Rs. 2 lakhs for individual enterprises and Rs. 10 lakhs for group enterprises. Credit guarantee cover is available through the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE). Under the SHG Bank Linkage sub-component, interest subsidy is provided on loans to Self Help Groups (SHGs) for timely repayment. Under the convergence with PMFME scheme, seed capital assistance of Rs. 40,000 per SHG member is provided for working capital and purchase of small tools, structured as a loan from the Area Level Federation (ALF) or City Level Federation (CLF) to SHG members, with interest not exceeding 6% per annum, of which 3% is retained by the SHG for loan management, and the loan is repayable over 18-36 months. The Revolving Fund Support provides financial assistance to SHGs and their federations for income-generating activities. Funding for City Livelihood Centres (CLCs) is provided for establishment and operation. The scheme also supports training and skill development through EST&P, with cost norms for training providers. Financial inclusion is promoted through opening of bank accounts, financial literacy, and access to affordable insurance. The Innovative & Special Projects (I&SP) component utilizes up to 5% of total central funds for time-bound innovative approaches. The Capacity Building and Training (CB&T) component supports Mission Management Units at national, state, and city levels, with expenditure not exceeding 12% of total allocation. Funds are released through a structured mechanism involving State Nodal Agencies (SNAs), State Urban Livelihoods Missions (SULMs), and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), with utilization tracked via PFMS and NULM MIS.
application_process: 1. Identify prospective beneficiaries from the urban poor through Community Organisers (COs) and ULB professionals. 2. Community structures like Self Help Groups (SHGs) and Area Level Federations (ALFs) may refer beneficiaries for financial assistance. 3. Beneficiaries may directly approach ULB or its representatives, or banks may identify and send cases to ULB. 4. Submit an application of intent on plain paper with basic details: Name, Age, Contact details, Address, Aadhaar (if any), loan amount required, bank account number (if available), type of enterprise/activity, and category. 5. ULB enters details in a register or MIS and generates a waiting list with a unique registration number for tracking. 6. ULB conducts awareness campaigns through mass media, IEC, local newspapers, and City Livelihood Centres (CLCs). 7. ULB calls beneficiaries in waiting list order to complete documentation including Loan Application Form (LAF), activity details, identity proof, address proof, and bank account details. 8. SULM may develop a standardized LAF in consultation with State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC) convenor bank. 9. Completed applications are sent to the ULB-level Task Force for scrutiny. 10. Task Force calls prospective beneficiaries for an interview before recommending or rejecting the application or requesting additional information. 11. Recommended cases are forwarded by ULB to concerned banks for processing within 15 days. 12. Banks send periodic reports to ULB on application status; if MIS is used, banks may update status online in addition to manual reports. 13. For SEP-G (Group Enterprises), minimum 5 members with at least 70% from urban poor families are required, and no more than one person from the same family should be included in the group. 14. For SEP-I (Individual Enterprises), applicant must be at least 18 years of age. 15. For SHG Bank Linkage, SHGs must have at least 70% urban poor members and follow group norms. 16. For EST&P, candidates undergo skill gap analysis, curriculum design aligned with NSQF, and training of minimum 200 hours for fresh entrants or 16 hours for reskilling. 17. For PMFME convergence seed capital, SHG members engaged in micro food processing with at least one year experience apply via hard copy forms (Form I & II) facilitated by ROs/COs/CRPs, including enterprise details, product category, turnover, bank passbook, FSSAI/GST certificates if available, and photograph of enterprise. 18. Applications are scrutinized by SHG in meetings, forwarded to ULB for approval and digitization in NULM MIS. 19. ULB uploads approved applications to NULM MIS portal after Aadhaar authentication and mobile number validation. 20. SULM recommends applications to State Nodal Agency (SNA) for approval. 21. SNA approves and sanctions amount, which is transferred to SULM’s bank account. 22. SULM transfers funds to concerned federation’s (ALF/CLF) bank account within 10 days. 23. ALF/CLF disburses seed capital to individual SHG members’ bank accounts or to enterprise bank account for group/activity groups. 24. Beneficiaries utilize funds within one month’s interest-free lock-in period for procurement and installation. 25. ULBs collect fund utilization details through ROs/COs/CRPs and enter data via ULB login. 26. EMI repayment is supported by ROs/COs/CRPs, with ALF recovering EMI through SHGs and forwarding monthly reports to ULB. 27. For EST&P, candidates are mobilized, allotted to training centres, and training is conducted with attendance tracking. 28. Post-training, candidates are forwarded to Certifying Agency (CA) for assessment, and placement details are recorded. 29. For City Livelihood Centres (CLCs), ULB prepares Detailed Implementation Plan (DIP) after survey, ensures land ownership, relocation plan if any, infrastructure details, beneficiary list, and safety concerns. 30. DIP is submitted to SLAC for approval, and funds are released in installments contingent on beneficiary list submission. 31. For Shelter for Urban Homeless (SUH), ULB or other agencies operate shelters with minimum staff: one full-time manager and three caregivers (one per 8-hour shift), with at least one woman caregiver for women inmates. 32. For street vendor components, ULB conducts survey, issues identity cards, prepares city street vending plan, improves infrastructure, provides training (1-2 days with stipend not less than minimum wage), promotes financial inclusion, facilitates access to credit, and links to social security schemes. 33. All components require monitoring and evaluation through MIS, monthly progress reports, and quarterly performance tracking.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India

overview: The STPI Software Technology Park Incentives scheme is a 100% export-oriented initiative under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at promoting the development and export of computer software and electronics hardware. It integrates the concepts of Export Oriented Units (EOUs), Export Processing Zones (EPZs), and Science/Technology Parks to provide single-point clearance and operational support to member units. The scheme enables duty-free imports, tax benefits, and repatriation of profits, fostering India's position as a global IT exporter.
target_beneficiaries: software exporters; electronics hardware exporters; IT/ITES units; startups; MSMEs
eligibility: Units engaged in the development and export of computer software (under STP Scheme) or electronics hardware (under EHTP Scheme) using communication links or physical media. The unit must be 100% export-oriented. Jurisdictional STPI authorities can clear projects costing less than Rs.100 million with Indian investment. 100% foreign equity is permitted. Units may be set up anywhere in India.
benefits: Single window clearance for approvals; duty-free import of hardware and software; permission to import second-hand capital goods; re-export of capital goods allowed; simplified minimum export performance norms (Positive Net Foreign Exchange Earnings); domestic sales in DTA permitted with GST refund on capital goods; free repatriation of capital, know-how fees, royalties, dividends after income tax payment; donation of computers to educational/charitable institutions after two years without duty; 100% depreciation on computers and peripherals over five years.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants. Financial benefits are indirect, including duty savings on imports, GST refunds on capital goods purchased in DTA, and tax advantages through profit repatriation and depreciation claims. No direct fund disbursement or loan mechanism is described in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Apply for online registration via the STPI portal. 2. Submit project details for clearance by jurisdictional STPI authorities. 3. Obtain approval under single window clearance system. 4. Commence operations as a 100% export-oriented unit. 5. Avail benefits such as duty-free imports and tax incentives.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India

scheme_name: National Backward Classes Finance & Dev Corporation (NBCFDC)
overview: The National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation (NBCFDC) is a Government of India Undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, established to promote economic and developmental activities for the benefit of Backward Classes. It provides concessional financial assistance through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) and Banks for income-generating activities, skill development, and self-employment ventures. The corporation offers various loan schemes including Individual Loan Scheme, Group Loan Scheme, and education loans, targeting OBC members with annual family income up to Rs. 5.00 Lakh.
target_beneficiaries: Backward Classes; OBC; SC/ST; Minorities; Person with Disabilities (PwD); Self Help Groups (SHGs)
eligibility: Members of Backward Classes as notified by Central/State Govt. from time to time. Applicant's annual family income should be upto Rs.5.00 Lakh. For Group Loan Scheme, at least 60% members of SHG must belong to Backward Classes, with other members from weaker sections including SC/ST/Minorities/PwD. For skill training under PM DAKSH, eligibility is based on OBC/EBC status and income criteria.
benefits: Concessional financial assistance through loans for income-generating activities, skill development training under PM DAKSH, marketing support for artisans via national/international platforms (IITF, Surajkund Mela, Delhi Haat), awareness camps for beneficiary mobilization, and grants-in-aid to Channel Partners for infrastructure strengthening under PLGIA scheme. Loans are disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to bank accounts.
financial_support: NBCFDC provides loans covering 85-90% of project cost through Channel Partners, with beneficiary contributing 10-15%. Under Individual Loan Scheme: max Rs.25.00 Lakh per beneficiary (85% NBCFDC, 15% Channel Partner/Beneficiary). Under Group Loan Scheme: max Rs.25.00 Lakh per SHG (90% NBCFDC, 10% Channel Partner/NBFC-MFI). Education loans up to Rs.25.00 Lakh available. Rate of interest: 4-8% p.a. for NBCFDC to Channel Partner, 7-16% p.a. for Channel Partner to Beneficiary, with repayment periods of 3-7 years (10 years for education loans). Timely payment rebate of 1% per annum equally shared between Channel Partners and Beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Prospective eligible beneficiaries should apply on prescribed form (available with Channel Partners) to District Office of Channel Partners where they reside. 2. Applicant should clearly mention felt needs, choice of vocation, and training requirements in the application form. 3. Applicant must fulfil eligibility criteria (belong to Backward Class and have annual family income upto Rs. 3.00 lakh). 4. Submit documents as proof such as Caste and Income Certificate issued by Competent Authority (Tehsildar/Sub Divisional Magistrate/District Collector). 5. Self-certified annual family income certificate duly endorsed by gazetted officers of State Government or Branch Manager of the Bank giving the loan is admissible. 6. Eligible persons can apply online at the registration portal on NBCFDC website; requests are forwarded to concerned Channel Partners (SCAs/Banks) with intimation to the applicant.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation (NBCFDC), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

scheme_name: PMEGP via Khadi & Village Industries Commission
overview: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is a credit-linked subsidy scheme implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) to generate employment opportunities through the establishment of micro-enterprises in rural and urban areas. It provides financial assistance in the form of bank loans and government subsidies to individuals, self-help groups, and institutions for setting up new ventures. The scheme aims to promote sustainable livelihoods and reduce unemployment by supporting traditional and innovative village industries.
target_beneficiaries: individuals; self-help groups; institutions; MSME; rural entrepreneurs
eligibility: Any individual above 18 years of age is eligible. For setting up of project costing above Rs. 10 lakh in the manufacturing sector and above Rs. 5 lakh in the business/service sector, the beneficiary should possess at least VIII standard pass educational qualification. Self Help Groups (including those belonging to BPL provided that they have not availed benefits under any other Scheme) are also eligible. Institutions registered under Societies Registration Act, 1860; Production Co-operative Societies, and Charitable Trusts are also eligible.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of bank loan (term loan and working capital) and government subsidy. Subsidy rate is 25% for general category beneficiaries in rural areas, 15% in urban areas; 35% for special category (SC/ST/OBC/Minorities/Women, ex-servicemen, physically handicapped, NER, Hill and Border areas) in rural areas, and 25% in urban areas. Maximum project cost admissible under manufacturing sector is Rs. 50 lakh and under business/service sector is Rs. 20 lakh. The scheme promotes self-employment and entrepreneurship through training, mentorship, and post-establishment support.
financial_support: Beneficiaries receive a composite loan comprising of bank loan (90% to 95% of project cost) and government subsidy (5% to 10% of project cost). The government subsidy is credited to the beneficiary's bank account after loan disbursement and is locked for 3 years. The remaining project cost (5% to 10%) is contributed by the beneficiary as margin money. Maximum loan amount varies based on project cost and beneficiary category, with subsidy directly reducing the effective financial burden.
application_process: 1. Visit the official PMEGP portal at https://kviconline.gov.in 2. Register as a new beneficiary on the portal 3. Fill in the online application form with personal, project, and financial details 4. Upload required documents including educational certificates, project report, and identification proofs 5. Submit the application online 6. Application is forwarded to the concerned District Industries Centre (DIC) or KVIC office for verification 7. Upon verification, the application is sent to the selected bank for loan sanction 8. After bank approval, the loan is disbursed and government subsidy is credited to the beneficiary's account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

scheme_name: Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS)
overview: The Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS) is a Central Sector Scheme launched in January 2007 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, aimed at rehabilitating manual scavengers and their dependents by providing them with alternative livelihood opportunities through skill development and financial assistance for self-employment ventures. The scheme focuses on identifying and surveying manual scavengers, providing them with training, and facilitating access to loans and subsidies for setting up sustainable self-employment units. It operates through a network of State Channelising Agencies (SCAs) of the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), which is the nodal agency for implementation. The scheme has been revised and strengthened over time, with the latest revision effective from 2021-22 to enhance outreach and effectiveness.
target_beneficiaries: manual scavengers; dependents of manual scavengers; safai karamcharis
eligibility: The scheme covers manual scavengers as defined under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013, and their dependents. Eligible individuals include those who have been engaged in manual scavenging, identified through surveys conducted by State Governments or ULBs, and are willing to undergo training and take up self-employment ventures. Beneficiaries must be Indian citizens and preferably belong to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, or Other Backward Classes, though the primary criterion is engagement in manual scavenging.
benefits: Beneficiaries receive skill development training in various trades suitable for self-employment, financial assistance in the form of loans from NSKFDC through State Channelising Agencies (SCAs) at concessional interest rates, and a subsidy component to reduce the financial burden. The scheme also provides backward and forward linkages, including marketing support and handholding during the initial phase of enterprise setup. Additional support may include assistance for raw materials, machinery, and working capital, depending on the project cost and viability.
financial_support: Under SRMS, financial assistance is provided as a term loan up to a maximum of INR 15 lakhs per beneficiary for setting up self-employment units. The loan is extended at a concessional interest rate of 4% per annum. A subsidy of up to 50% of the project cost, subject to a maximum of INR 5 lakhs, is provided based on the beneficiary's category and project viability. The remaining amount is to be financed through the loan. The funds are disbursed through the State Channelising Agencies (SCAs) of NSKFDC after appraisal and approval of the project proposal.
application_process: 1. Identification of manual scavengers through surveys conducted by State Governments or Urban Local Bodies (ULBs). 2. Motivation and counseling of identified beneficiaries to opt for rehabilitation under SRMS. 3. Selection of suitable self-employment venture based on skills, local market demand, and training undergone. 4. Submission of project proposal to the concerned State Channelising Agency (SCA) of NSKFDC. 5. Appraisal of the project by the SCA for technical feasibility, financial viability, and beneficiary capacity. 6. Sanction of loan and subsidy components by the SCA upon approval. 7. Disbursement of funds in stages as per project progress. 8. Monitoring and handholding support provided by SCA/NSKFDC during implementation and initial operation.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and identification of beneficiaries.
implementing_agency: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India

overview: Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme approved on 13.04.2022 for implementation from 01.04.2022 to 31.03.2026, co-terminus with the XV Finance Commission period. The scheme focuses on re-imagining Panchayati Raj Institutions as vibrant centers of local self-governance and economic growth, with special emphasis on localization of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) at the grassroots level through a thematic approach and collaborative efforts of Central Ministries and State line departments. It ensures basic orientation training for Elected Representatives (ERs) of Panchayats within 6 months of election and refresher training within 2 years, with a funding pattern of 60:40 (Central:State) for general states, 90:10 for NE Hilly States and UT of J&K, and 100% Central share for other UTs.
target_beneficiaries: Panchayati Raj Institutions; Elected Representatives (ERs) of Panchayats; State Governments; Union Territories
eligibility: The scheme is implemented by State Governments and Union Territories. The funding pattern for State components is in the ratio of 60:40 (Central:State) respectively, except for NE Hilly States and UT of J & K where the Central and State Share is in the ratio of 90:10. For other UTs, the Central share is 100%. The scheme covers all Panchayati Raj Institutions across the country, including Gram Panchayats, Block Panchayats, and District Panchayats.
benefits: Capacity building and training of Panchayati Raj Institution representatives; construction and repair of Panchayat Bhawans; provision of computers to Gram Panchayats; organization of exposure visits; implementation of schemes and initiatives related to SDGs, economic and innovative projects, vibrant Gram Sabha, and Panchayat Awards; training through State Institutes of Rural Development (SIRDs); and overall strengthening of local self-governance infrastructure and human resource capacity.
financial_support: The scheme operates as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with financial support provided to States and Union Territories based on the funding pattern: 60:40 (Central:State) for general states, 90:10 for NE Hilly States and UT of J & K, and 100% Central share for other UTs. Funds are released for activities such as training of Elected Representatives, infrastructure development (Panchayat Bhawans), computerization, and other capacity-building initiatives under the RGSA framework.
application_process: States and Union Territories are required to submit Annual Action Plans (AAPs) through the MIS portal for approval. The process involves: 1. Preparation of State Annual Action Plan (AAP) by the State Government/UT Administration. 2. Submission of AAP via the MIS portal on the RGSA website. 3. Review and approval of AAP by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj. 4. Release of funds based on approved AAP and utilization certificates. 5. Implementation of activities at the district, block, and gram panchayat levels. 6. Monitoring and reporting of progress through the MIS portal. 7. Submission of Utilization Certificates and progress reports for subsequent fund releases.
deadlines: Annual Action Plans (AAPs) are to be submitted for each financial year. The scheme is implemented from 01.04.2022 to 31.03.2026. Specific submission deadlines for AAPs are communicated annually by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India
contact_details: Email ID : mis-rgsa[at]gov[dot]in | Helpdesk : 011-24305284 | Address : Ministry of Panchayati Raj Government of India 11th Floor, J.P. Building, Kasturba Gandhi Marg, Connaught Place, New Delhi - 110001

overview: ULIP – Unified Logistics Interface Platform is an integrated platform for stakeholders to enhance efficiency, utilize technology, and reduce the cost of logistics in India. It provides API-based data exchange between government and private entities involved in the Indian logistics ecosystem. The platform integrates systems from various ministries and departments to enable end-to-end visibility, optimal transportation usage, and simplified compliance processes. ULIP supports data-driven logistics policies and national programs like PM GatiShakti.
target_beneficiaries: transporters; manufacturers; service providers; government departments
eligibility: Stakeholders involved in the Indian logistics ecosystem including transporters, manufacturers, service providers, and government departments can access ULIP by signing in or registering on the portal.
benefits: Simplified compliance and onboarding through digital verification of vehicle documents and paperless driver onboarding; reduced empty miles and optimized routing via smart route selection and idle truck detection; cost-effective tracking and insights using FASTag-based tracking; real-time visibility of fuel and EV stations for efficient route planning; secured cargo movement through real-time detection of fraudulent or unauthorized cargo; unified multimodal visibility of rail, road, and air freight; sustainability insights from emissions data; third-party transporter validation via automated verification of statutory documents; process digitization through E-way Bill and ICEGATE API integration; real-time container tracking; simplified and paperless documentation; support for policy making, compliance enforcement, and movement tracking.
financial_support: No financial support is mentioned in the evidence. ULIP is a technology platform for data exchange and does not provide grants, loans, subsidies, or direct financial assistance to entities.
application_process: 1. Visit the ULIP portal at https://goulip.in/ 2. Click on SIGN IN or REGISTER to create an account 3. After registration, log in to access the platform 4. Request for APIs through the DATA REQUEST PLATFORM 5. Download API documents and SOP process flow by clicking the download icon 6. Customize APIs with ULIP platform as needed 7. Integrate and use the APIs for logistics operations and data exchange
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Access is available year-round after registration.
implementing_agency: National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) Logistics Data Services Ltd.

overview: DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Rural Development to reduce rural poverty by promoting diversified and gainful self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities. It focuses on organizing rural poor women into Self Help Groups (SHGs) and federations, building their capacities, and enabling access to financial and livelihood resources. The scheme aims to achieve universal social mobilization, financial inclusion, and sustainable livelihoods for rural households living below the poverty line.
target_beneficiaries: rural poor; women; Self Help Groups (SHGs); village organisations; rural youth
geographic_scope: Pan-India (rural areas across all states and union territories)
eligibility: Rural households living below the poverty line (BPL), with special focus on women, SC/ST, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups. Eligibility is determined through participatory identification of poor (PIP) at the village level, validated by Gram Sabha. All rural poor are eligible for mobilization into SHGs, with priority given to the poorest and most marginalized.
benefits: Financial inclusion through bank linkage and access to revolving fund and community investment fund; capacity building and skill training; livelihood support for farm and non-farm activities; market linkages and value chain development; social inclusion and empowerment; convergence with other government schemes; access to insurance and risk mitigation instruments; support for rural enterprises and producer groups.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through Revolving Fund (RF) and Community Investment Fund (CIF) to SHGs and their federations. RF is a one-time grant of up to INR 10,000–15,000 per SHG for strengthening group corpus. CIF is provided as a grant to village organisations for on-lending to SHGs for livelihood investments. Interest subvention is also available on loans to SHGs for livelihoods. Support is also provided for skill training, infrastructure, and enterprise development under various sub-components.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 15,000 per Self Help Group (SHG) as Revolving Fund
application_process: 1. Mobilization of rural poor into Self Help Groups (SHGs) through village-level outreach. 2. Formation and training of SHGs on group dynamics, savings, and inter-loaning. 3. Validation of SHGs by Village Organisation and Gram Sabha. 4. Opening of bank account and initiation of regular savings. 5. Application for Revolving Fund (RF) through Village Organisation. 6. Sanction and disbursement of RF by Block Level Federation. 7. Utilization of RF for internal lending and income-generating activities. 8. Eligibility for Community Investment Fund (CIF) based on group performance and grading. 9. Access to CIF for livelihood investments through village organisation.
deadlines: Rolling basis — SHG formation and RF/CIF applications are accepted throughout the year based on village-level readiness and validation.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India

overview: The National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC) is a Government of India undertaking under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, incorporated on 30th September 1994 as a not-for-profit company under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013. It functions as a National Level Apex Body to provide concessional finance to notified minority communities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains) for self-employment and income generation activities, with preference given to artisans and women. NMDFC implements its schemes through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) and offers various loan schemes including Term Loan, Education Loan, Virasat (for artisans), and Micro Finance, along with promotional and fellowship schemes.
target_beneficiaries: minorities; artisans; women
eligibility: Beneficiaries must belong to notified minority communities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains as per National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, with Jains added in January 2014). Annual family income eligibility: Credit Line-1 for income up to ₹3.00 lakhs per annum; Credit Line-2 for income up to ₹8.00 lakhs per annum (enhanced from November 2020 using 'Creamy Layer' criterion). Preference is given to artisans and women. For education loans, applicants must pursue job-oriented technical/vocational courses. For Virasat scheme, beneficiaries must be craftspersons. For MANF, candidates must have cleared UGC-NET or Joint CSIR-UGC NET and belong to minority communities.
benefits: Concessional interest rates on loans: Term Loan (Credit Line-1: 6% p.a., Credit Line-2: 8% p.a. with 2% rebate for women); Education Loan (Credit Line-1: 3% p.a., Credit Line-2: 8% p.a. with 3% rebate for women); Micro Finance (Credit Line-1: 7% p.a., Credit Line-2: 10% p.a. with 2% rebate for women); Virasat (Credit Line-1: 5% p.a., Credit Line-2: 6% p.a. for men, 5% for women). Loan tenures: Term Loan and Education Loan up to 5 years, Micro Finance and Virasat up to 3-5 years. Moratorium period: 6 months for Term Loan, Education Loan, and Virasat; 3 months for Micro Finance. Additional benefits include marketing assistance through exhibitions, grant for promotional schemes (90% NMDFC, 10% SCA), and fellowships with stipend, HRA, contingency, and escorts/reader assistance for disabled candidates.
financial_support: NMDFC provides concessional loans through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs). Under Term Loan scheme: up to ₹20.00 lakhs for Credit Line-1 and ₹30.00 lakhs for Credit Line-2. Education Loan: up to ₹20.00 lakhs for domestic courses and ₹30.00 lakhs for foreign courses under both credit lines. Virasat scheme: up to ₹10.00 lakhs under both credit lines. Micro Finance: up to ₹1.00 lakh per SHG member under Credit Line-1 and ₹1.50 lakh under Credit Line-2. Interest rates vary by scheme and beneficiary gender, with rebates for women. Repayment periods range from 3 to 5 years with moratorium periods of 3-6 months. Loans are disbursed via SCAs after submission of required documents including self-attested income, residence, religious certificates, and project reports.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant scheme (Term Loan, Education Loan, Virasat, Micro Finance, etc.) based on eligibility and purpose. 2. Check annual family income to determine Credit Line-1 (up to ₹3.00 lakhs) or Credit Line-2 (up to ₹8.00 lakhs). 3. Approach the State Channelizing Agency (SCA) nominated by your State Government. 4. Prepare required documents: self-attested income certificate, residence proof (with AADHAAR/Ration Card/Voter ID/Passport/Phone/Electricity Bill), religious certificate (if loan > ₹1 lakh), and brief project report. 5. For loans exceeding ₹1 lakh, arrange security: self-guarantee & post-dated cheques (up to ₹1 lakh); guarantee of one Govt./PSU/Bank employee or income tax payer & post-dated cheques (₹1-5 lakhs); guarantee of two Govt./PSU/Bank employees or two income tax payers/public representatives or collateral (₹5-10 lakhs). 6. Submit application form and documents to the SCA. 7. SCA verifies documents and forwards approved proposals to NMDFC for sanction. 8. Upon approval, loan is disbursed by SCA to beneficiary. 9. Repay loan as per agreed schedule (typically 3-5 years) after moratorium period.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC)
