scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor Loan)
overview: Pradhan Mantri SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor Loan) is a special micro-credit facility launched to provide affordable working capital loans to street vendors affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The scheme offers collateral-free loans with interest subsidies and digital transaction incentives to promote financial inclusion and livelihood security. It aims to support urban street vendors in resuming and expanding their vending activities through easy access to credit.
target_beneficiaries: street vendors
eligibility: Street vendors who have been covered in the Urban Local Body (ULB) survey and possess a Certificate of Vending (CoV) or Identity card, or those who have not been issued CoV/ID but are listed in the survey, or vendors who started vending after the survey and can provide a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) or declare receipt of one-time assistance during COVID lockdown or membership in a vending/hawkers association, or vendors from peri-urban/rural areas vending within ULB limits with similar documentation.
benefits: Collateral-free working capital loans, interest subsidy of 7% per annum on timely repayment, monthly cashback incentives for digital transactions, access to PM SVANidhi Credit Card for second tranche repaid vendors, vendor mobility facility to update ULB details on migration, and access to digital literacy and awareness campaigns under 'Main Bhi Digital'.
financial_support: The scheme provides term loans in three tranches: first loan up to ₹10,000, second loan up to ₹20,000, and third loan up to ₹50,000. Loans are disbursed through participating lending institutions with an interest subsidy of 7% per annum credited to the borrower's account on timely repayment. Additionally, monthly cashback incentives are provided for digital transactions undertaken using the loan amount.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to ₹50,000 for the third tranche loan
application_process: 1. Check eligibility based on vendor category and survey status. 2. Ensure mobile number is linked to Aadhaar for e-KYC validation. 3. Keep required documents ready such as Certificate of Vending, Identity card, Survey Reference Number (SRN), or Letter of Recommendation (LoR). 4. Apply online via the PM SVANidhi portal or through a Common Service Centre (CSC). 5. Complete e-KYC/Aadhaar validation during application. 6. Submit application and await digital approval from lending institution.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

overview: The National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM), also known as Aajeevika, is a flagship poverty alleviation program of the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India. It aims to reduce poverty by enabling poor households to access gainful self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities through the mobilization of rural poor into Self Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations. The mission focuses on building strong institutional platforms of the poor, enhancing livelihoods through skill development, access to credit, and market linkages, and promoting social inclusion and empowerment, particularly of women and marginalized groups.
target_beneficiaries: rural poor; women; SC/ST; marginalized communities; Self Help Groups (SHGs); rural youth
eligibility: The program targets rural poor households, particularly those identified through the Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011. Eligibility is based on poverty and social vulnerability criteria, with priority given to women, SC/ST, persons with disabilities, and other marginalized groups. Participation is voluntary and facilitated through community mobilization by trained resource persons. Self Help Groups (SHGs) are formed by 10-20 members from similar socio-economic backgrounds, who agree to save regularly and mutually contribute to a common fund.
benefits: Benefits include access to revolving fund and community investment fund support, skill training for wage and self-employment, placement assistance, interest subvention on bank loans, subsidies for livelihood activities, infrastructure support for producer groups, market linkages, convergence with other government programs, and social mobilization for empowerment. Non-financial benefits include capacity building, leadership development, access to information and entitlements, and collective bargaining power through SHG federations.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through a combination of grants and loans. The Revolving Fund (RF) of up to INR 10,000–50,000 per SHG is provided as a grant to strengthen group corpus. The Community Investment Fund (CIF) is provided as a grant to SHG federations for onward lending to members as loans. Interest subvention is available on bank loans up to INR 3 lakh at 4% per annum for women SHGs. Additional support includes livelihood loans, enterprise development funds, and credit linkage with banks under the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme.
application_process: 1. Identify rural poor households through SECC 2011 or participatory identification of poor (PIP). 2. Mobilize and form Self Help Groups (SHGs) of 10–20 members with facilitator support. 3. Train SHGs in group management, savings, and internal lending. 4. Open a joint bank account and begin regular savings. 5. Apply for Revolving Fund (RF) through the SHG federation after 3–6 months of functioning. 6. Upon RF utilization, apply for Community Investment Fund (CIF) via the federation for livelihood investments. 7. Access skill training and placement under Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) or Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs). 8. Link with banks for credit under SHG-Bank Linkage Programme with interest subvention. 9. Participate in producer collectives and market linkages for value chain development.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year based on household mobilization and SHG readiness.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India

overview: The Logistics Efficiency Enhancement Programme (LEEP) is a scheme under the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, aimed at improving logistics efficiency and reducing logistics costs in India. It focuses on enhancing trade facilitation, streamlining customs procedures, and supporting infrastructure development to boost exports and integrate Indian businesses into global value chains. The programme supports MSMEs, startups, and other stakeholders through policy interventions, digital initiatives, and capacity building.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; exporters; importers; logistics service providers
eligibility: The scheme is open to MSMEs, startups, exporters, importers, logistics service providers, and other stakeholders engaged in trade and logistics activities in India. Eligibility is based on active engagement in international trade, compliance with relevant regulations, and potential to benefit from logistics efficiency improvements. Specific eligibility criteria may vary based on sub-components of the programme and are determined by the Department of Commerce.
benefits: Benefits include reduced logistics costs, improved supply chain efficiency, enhanced market access, faster customs clearance, access to digital trade platforms (e.g., TIA Portal), capacity building and training opportunities, policy support for trade facilitation, and integration into global value chains. The scheme also supports MSMEs and startups through export readiness programmes, trade-related information access, and linkages with international SME ecosystems.
financial_support: LEEP does not provide direct financial support such as grants or loans. Instead, it offers non-financial support through policy interventions, regulatory reforms, digital infrastructure (e.g., Trade Intelligence & Analytics Portal), trade facilitation initiatives, and capacity building programmes. Financial support, if any, is channelled through allied schemes like the Interest Equalisation Scheme (IES) or Market Access Initiative (MAI), which are referenced in the Department of Commerce’s export promotion efforts.
application_process: 1. Identify eligibility under LEEP or allied Department of Commerce schemes. 2. Access relevant portals such as the Trade Intelligence & Analytics (TIA) portal or Department of Commerce website. 3. Register on the designated platform for trade facilitation services. 4. Submit required documents for verification and onboarding. 5. Avail benefits such as digital compliance tools, training programmes, or policy guidance. 6. Monitor updates and participate in stakeholder consultations as announced by the Department of Commerce.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
contact_details: Email: recruitment-e2@gov.in | Helpline: Not specified in evidence

overview: The Sagarmala Programme is a flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at promoting port-led development through the harnessing of India's 7,500 km long coastline, 14,500 km of potentially navigable waterways and strategic location on key international maritime trade routes. It seeks to reduce logistics costs for both domestic and EXIM cargo, enhance port infrastructure, and promote industrialization and coastal community development. The programme integrates the development of ports, industrial clusters, hinterland connectivity, and coastal shipping to drive economic growth and job creation.
target_beneficiaries: ports; shipping companies; logistics providers; industrial units; coastal communities; state governments
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component and project under Sagarmala. Generally, proposals are invited from state governments, maritime boards, port trusts, central public sector enterprises, and private sector entities through competitive bidding or public-private partnership (PPP) modes. Projects must align with the National Perspective Plan (NPP) under Sagarmala and contribute to port-led development.
benefits: Benefits include reduced logistics costs, improved port efficiency and capacity, enhanced hinterland connectivity, promotion of coastal shipping and inland waterways, development of industrial clusters and manufacturing zones, job creation in port and coastal areas, skill development for local communities, and increased exports and economic growth through port-led development.
financial_support: Financial support under Sagarmala is provided through various mechanisms including budgetary allocations from the Government of India, extra-budgetary resources, private investment via PPP, institutional financing from banks and financial institutions, and viability gap funding (VGF) where applicable. The programme leverages convergence with other central and state schemes, and financial support is extended based on project appraisal and approval under the institutional framework of Sagarmala.
application_process: 1. Identification of project ideas aligned with Sagarmala objectives and National Perspective Plan (NPP). 2. Preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) by the project proponent. 3. Submission of proposal to the concerned nodal agency (e.g., Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, State Government, or Port Trust). 4. Appraisal of the project by the Sagarmala Coordination and Steering Committee (SCSC) or relevant technical committee. 5. Approval by the Empowered Committee under Sagarmala. 6. Implementation of the project through EPC contracts or PPP mode. 7. Monitoring and evaluation by the Sagarmala Secretariat and concerned ministries.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year based on budget availability and project readiness.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

overview: AMRUT 2.0 (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation 2.0) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) to provide universal coverage of water supply and sewerage/septage management in all statutory towns across India. The mission aims to make cities water-secure and improve the quality of life through sustainable urban infrastructure development, with a focus on sewage treatment, reuse of treated wastewater, and rejuvenation of water bodies.
target_beneficiaries: Urban Local Bodies (ULBs); State Governments; Cantonment Boards
eligibility: All statutory towns as per Census 2011, including cantonment boards, are eligible under AMRUT 2.0. The scheme covers 500 cities and towns with a population of over 1 lakh, along with all state/UT capitals and cities/towns situated on the banks of major rivers, irrespective of population.
benefits: Financial assistance for water supply, sewerage, septage management, water body rejuvenation, and park development; capacity building and reforms implementation; incentive for water reuse and non-revenue water reduction; technical support for project preparation and monitoring; promotion of public-private partnerships in urban infrastructure.
financial_support: The scheme provides central funding in the form of grants to States/UTs based on an equitable formula. The central government bears 50% of the project cost for cities with population up to 10 lakhs, one-third for cities with population above 10 lakhs, and 90% for North Eastern and Himalayan States. The remaining cost is borne by the State/ULB. Funds are released in installments linked to project progress and reform implementation.
application_process: 1. States/UTs submit State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) for approval by the Apex Committee under MoHUA. 2. Upon approval, projects are formulated by Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) or Parastatal agencies. 3. Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) are prepared and submitted for technical sanction. 4. Works are tendered and awarded as per financial rules. 5. Projects are executed and monitored through geo-tagging and third-party inspection. 6. Utilization certificates and progress reports are submitted for subsequent fund releases.
deadlines: Annual planning cycle — States/UTs submit SAAPs yearly for approval; project implementation timelines vary as per DPR approval.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

overview: The National Water Mission (NWM) aims to conserve water, minimize wastage, and ensure equitable distribution through sustainable development strategies. It runs campaigns like Jal Shakti Abhiyan to engage stakeholders in water management and focuses on integrated water resource development. The mission is implemented by the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
target_beneficiaries: general public; state governments; local communities
eligibility: The evidence does not specify explicit eligibility criteria for beneficiaries or entities to participate in the National Water Mission.
benefits: The National Water Mission promotes water conservation, reduces wastage, ensures equitable distribution, and supports sustainable water management practices through awareness campaigns and stakeholder engagement.
financial_support: The evidence does not provide details on financial support mechanisms, quantum, or allocation under the National Water Mission.
application_process: The evidence does not describe a numbered step-by-step application process for the National Water Mission.
deadlines: The evidence does not mention any application deadlines or submission windows for the National Water Mission.
implementing_agency: Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation

overview: Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) is a flagship program of the Government of India aimed at providing safe and adequate drinking water through individual household tap connections to all rural households by 2024, with an extension approved up to December 2028 under JJM 2.0. The mission emphasizes community participation, source sustainability, greywater management, and information, education, and communication (IEC) as key components. It aims to create a 'Jan Andolan' for water, making it everyone's priority, and ensures functionality of tap connections through regular monitoring and community ownership.
target_beneficiaries: rural households; schools; anganwadi centres; gram panchayat buildings; health centres; wellness centres; community buildings
eligibility: States and Union Territories (UTs) are eligible to receive financial assistance under Jal Jeevan Mission for planning, implementing, and managing rural water supply schemes. The mission supports States/UTs in creating water supply infrastructure so that every rural household has a Functional Tap Connection (FHTC) by 2024 (extended to 2028 under JJM 2.0) and in developing robust institutions focused on service delivery and financial sustainability.
benefits: Benefits include provision of safe and adequate drinking water at the household level, improvement in living standards, reduction in water-borne diseases, empowerment of communities (especially women) through participation in planning and management, creation of sustainable water supply infrastructure, promotion of water conservation and greywater management, capacity building of stakeholders, and digital monitoring of water service delivery. The mission also facilitates convergence with other programs and financial assistance to States/UTs for implementation.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided to States/UTs as grants-in-aid based on fund allocation criteria including rural population (30% weight), rural SC and ST population (10%), special category states (30%), habitations affected by chemical contaminants (10%), and balance household connections to be provided (20%). Up to 2% of annual allocation is earmarked for National Mission-level activities (including NCDWSQ, PMU, IEC, capacity building, M&E, R&D), 0.5% for JE-AES states, 10% for NE States, and funds for NWQSM as per state requirements. The balance is allocated to non-NE states/UTs. Fund sharing follows the pattern of erstwhile NRDWP components subsumed under JJM.
application_process: States/UTs must submit proposals through the Institutional Mechanism involving State Water and Sanitation Mission (SWSM) and District Water and Sanitation Mission (DWSM). Proposals are appraised and approved by the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM) under the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation. Funds are released in installments based on utilization certificates and progress reports. The process includes preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), community contribution planning, and convergence with other schemes. Implementation is monitored via the JJM-Management Information System (MIS).
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted and processed throughout the year based on fund availability and approval cycles.
implementing_agency: Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti

overview: DigiLocker is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Electronics & IT (MeitY) under the Digital India programme. It provides a secure cloud-based platform for storage, sharing, and verification of digital documents and certificates. DigiLocker aims at 'Digital Empowerment' of citizens by providing access to authentic digital documents to their digital document wallet, with issued documents deemed legally at par with original physical documents under Rule 9A of the IT (Preservation and Retention of Information by Intermediaries providing Digital Locker facilities) Rules, 2016.
target_beneficiaries: citizens
eligibility: To access the DigiLocker platform, users must register using a valid Indian mobile number, Driving License, PAN or Aadhaar. Registration may require verification via an OTP. Users are using Aadhaar voluntarily.
benefits: For Citizens: Access Anytime, Anywhere; Legally Valid, Widely Trusted Digital documents; Effortless Sharing with explicit consent; Accelerate Services for jobs, government benefits, banking, healthcare, and education. For Agencies: Reduced Administrative Overhead; Digital Transformation through trusted issued documents; Secure Document Gateway for exchange between issuer and requester; Real Time Verification enabling government agencies to verify data directly from issuers with user consent.
financial_support: No fees shall be charged by NeGD for access to issued documents through DigiLocker. The platform is provided free of cost to users for core services.
application_process: 1. Register yourself using a valid Indian mobile number, Driving License, PAN or Aadhaar. 2. Verify yourself via OTP or other verification method. 3. Fetch your documents from linked issuers. 4. Share your documents with consent. 5. Become a DigiLocker Partner Organization by registering as an Issuer or Requester.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics & IT (MeitY), Government of India
contact_details: Email: support@digilocker.gov.in | Address: National e-Governance Division (NeGD), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, New Delhi, India

overview: The e-RUPI scheme is a digital payment solution launched by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) to enable contactless, cashless transactions through a QR code or SMS-based string. It is designed as a pre-paid, purpose-specific voucher system that ensures targeted delivery of benefits without the need for a bank account, digital wallet, or app. The scheme supports financial inclusion by allowing beneficiaries to redeem services at mapped merchant locations using a unique e-RUPI code.
target_beneficiaries: general public; beneficiaries of government welfare schemes
eligibility: Beneficiaries identified by government or corporate sponsors for specific welfare or promotional schemes; no bank account, smartphone, or internet required to receive or use e-RUPI.
benefits: Contactless redemption via QR code or SMS; no need for bank account, digital wallet, or app; ensures purpose-specific usage; real-time tracking by sponsors; zero transaction cost to beneficiary; supports offline redemption at mapped merchant locations.
financial_support: e-RUPI is a pre-paid voucher system where the sponsoring entity (government or corporate) loads funds onto the voucher; the beneficiary receives no direct cash but can redeem the voucher for specified goods or services at designated merchants; the financial value is determined by the sponsor and transferred to the merchant upon successful redemption.
application_process: 1. Government or corporate sponsor approaches NPCI or its authorized partner to issue e-RUPI vouchers. 2. Sponsor provides beneficiary details (name, mobile number) and purpose/amount of voucher. 3. NPCI generates a unique e-RUPI QR code or SMS string. 4. Sponsor distributes the e-RUPI to beneficiary via SMS or messaging platform. 5. Beneficiary shows the QR code or shares the SMS string at merchant point-of-sale. 6. Merchant validates the e-RUPI through their acquiring bank or PSP. 7. Upon validation, merchant provides the service/goods and settles the amount with NPCI.
deadlines: Rolling basis — issued as per sponsor requirement
implementing_agency: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)

overview: IndiaStack Initiatives is a collection of open APIs and digital public goods that aim to unlock the economic primitives of identity, data, and payments at population scale. It is a vision for financial and social inclusion, serving as national plumbing for the Internet Age. Inspired by open-source software and interoperability, IndiaStack enables people and businesses to access services like Aadhaar-based identity verification, digital signatures, UPI payments, and consent-based data sharing through DEPA.
target_beneficiaries: individuals; businesses; startups; MSMEs; fintechs; financial institutions
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component: Aadhaar-based services (e-auth, e-KYC) are available to banks, licensed NBFCs, telecom companies, and government bodies; other entities may use QR code scans, e-Aadhaar, or offline XML. For eSign ASP onboarding, eligible entities include Central/State Government ministries, authorities under Central/State Act, not-for-profit organizations of national importance, banks/financial/telecom companies, or any legal entity registered in India meeting criteria such as incorporation under Companies Act 1956 and no blacklisting by government bodies.
benefits: Non-financial benefits include secure digital identity verification, legally valid digital signatures, access to digitally signed documents via DigiLocker, consent-based data sharing, and open network participation. Financial benefits include reduced KYC costs (from ~$23 to ~$0.15), real-time low-cost payments via UPI, and access to credit and financial products through verified data trails.
financial_support: IndiaStack does not provide direct financial support such as grants or loans. It enables financial inclusion and access to credit through indirect mechanisms like UPI for real-time payments, Account Aggregators for consent-based data sharing, and e-KYC reducing verification costs for financial institutions.
application_process: For eSign ASP onboarding: 1. Submit application form to ESP. 2. Submit supporting documents for KYC. 3. Accept terms of eSign service. 4. Submit Digital Signature Certificate (public key). 5. Integrate API in testing/preproduction environment. 6. Conduct audit and submit report. 7. Obtain readiness confirmation and Go-Live approval. 8. Obtain production access certificate. For general use: developers can access APIs via sandbox environments provided by intermediaries like Digio, Karza, Signzy, or OnGrid.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Multiple agencies: Unique ID Authority of India (UIDAI) for Aadhaar, Ministry of Communications and Information Technology for eSign, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology for Digilocker, National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) for UPI, RBI for Account Aggregator framework
contact_details: Email: annaroy@nic.in (for DEPA comments as per NITI Aayog document), volunteer with iSPIRT at ispirt.in

overview: Bharatmala Pariyojana is a flagship infrastructure initiative by the Government of India aimed at improving road connectivity across the country, particularly in border areas, coastal regions, and economic corridors. It focuses on developing National Highways, strategic roads, and interconnecting routes to enhance regional integration and support economic growth. The scheme is implemented by agencies like NHIDCL under the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, with projects spanning multiple states and union territories.
target_beneficiaries: general public; industries; transport sector; border communities
eligibility: The scheme is implemented by government agencies and public sector undertakings like NHIDCL under the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways. Projects are sanctioned based on technical feasibility, strategic importance, and alignment with national infrastructure priorities. Eligibility for funding and execution is determined by the government through appraisal and approval processes.
benefits: Improved road connectivity leading to reduced logistics costs and travel time; enhanced access to remote and underdeveloped regions; boost to trade, commerce, and industrial activity; better access to healthcare, education, and markets; strengthened national security through border road development; employment generation during construction and maintenance; promotion of regional integration and economic corridors.
financial_support: Financial support for Bharatmala Pariyojana is provided through central government budgetary allocations, market borrowings, and private investment via public-private partnerships (PPP). NHIDCL executes projects using government funding and has accessed external financing from institutions like the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) for specific high-speed corridor projects.
application_process: 1. Project identification and feasibility studies conducted by NHIDCL or other implementing agencies. 2. Preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) including technical, economic, and environmental assessments. 3. Submission of DPRs to the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways for appraisal and approval. 4. Sanction of projects based on priority and availability of funds. 5. Tendering process for selection of contractors through competitive bidding. 6. Award of contracts and commencement of civil works. 7. Monitoring and supervision during construction. 8. Commissioning and handover for operation and maintenance.
deadlines: Rolling basis — projects are sanctioned and implemented based on annual planning and budget cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, Government of India
contact_details: Email: cvo[dot]nhidcl-morth[at]gov[dot]in | Chief Vigilance Officer: Ashish Nath

overview: Section 80IAC of the Income Tax Act provides a tax exemption to eligible startups for three consecutive assessment years out of their first ten years from incorporation. The scheme aims to promote innovation and entrepreneurship by reducing the tax burden on startups during their early growth phase. To qualify, startups must obtain recognition from the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and secure approval from the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB). The exemption applies to 100% of profits and gains from eligible business activities.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: The startup must be a private limited company or a limited liability partnership (LLP) registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008. It must have been incorporated on or after 1st April 2016. The turnover of the startup must not exceed INR 100 crore in any of the financial years since incorporation. The startup must be working towards innovation, development or improvement of products or processes or services, or if it is a scalable business model with a high potential of employment generation or wealth creation. The startup must obtain DPIIT recognition and subsequently secure approval from the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) set up by DPIIT.
benefits: 100% tax exemption on profits and gains derived from eligible business for three consecutive assessment years out of the first ten years from incorporation. The exemption is available at the option of the assessee for any three assessment years out of the ten years. This benefit reduces the effective tax liability to zero for the selected years, thereby improving cash flow and retained earnings for reinvestment.
financial_support: The scheme provides a direct financial benefit in the form of tax savings, where eligible startups can claim exemption from paying income tax on their profits for up to three years. The quantum of support is equivalent to the tax amount that would have been payable on the profits from eligible business during the exempted years, calculated at the applicable corporate tax rate. There is no upper monetary cap on the exemption amount, as it is based on actual profits.
application_process: 1. Incorporate the business as a Private Limited Company or LLP. 2. Obtain DPIIT recognition by registering on the Startup India portal (https://www.startupindia.gov.in) and submitting the recognition application. 3. After receiving DPIIT recognition, apply for approval from the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) via Form 1 of the Income Tax Rules. 4. Submit Form 1 along with required documents to the IMB through the designated channel. 5. Upon IMB approval, claim the tax exemption under Section 80IAC while filing the income tax return for the relevant assessment year(s).
deadlines: Applications for IMB approval can be made at any time; there is no fixed deadline. However, the tax exemption must be claimed in the income tax return for the relevant assessment year within the time allowed under the Income Tax Act.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: ONDC (Open Network for Digital Commerce) is an initiative of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, incorporated as a Section 8 company in December 2021. It aims to democratize digital commerce in India by enabling an open, interoperable network that connects buyers and sellers across platforms, thereby increasing e-retail penetration from 4.3% to its maximum potential. ONDC empowers MSMEs, startups, women entrepreneurs, and small businesses by providing equal opportunities to compete with large market players and access nationwide markets through a unified protocol.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; women entrepreneurs; small businesses; farmers; SC/ST-led enterprises
eligibility: Any business in India, regardless of size, location, or digital proficiency, can join ONDC as a Buyer Network Participant, Seller Network Participant, Technology Service Provider, or Gateway, provided they can deliver high-quality service aligned with their chosen role on the network. There is no restriction based on turnover, years of incorporation, or entity type; eligibility is based on the ability to fulfill role-specific requirements such as integrating with ONDC APIs, digitizing catalogs, or providing buyer/seller applications.
benefits: Sellers gain equal opportunity to compete with large market players and become discoverable online. Buyers enjoy a seamless shopping experience from a wide assortment of products across categories in a single checkout experience. Tech companies achieve rapid adoption and scale in go-to-market efforts. FinTechs can provide credit and financing solutions to all entities engaged in e-commerce. Participants benefit from increased visibility, access to wider markets, reduced commissions compared to traditional platforms, and support for growth through network effects. Women-led businesses gain access to broader digital marketplaces and increased visibility across buyer apps. The network enables structured discovery, sustainable execution, and helps brands scale responsibly with flexibility and long-term sustainability.
financial_support: ONDC does not provide direct financial support to participants. However, the Ministry of MSME has launched the MSME Trade Enablement and Marketing (TEAM) Initiative in partnership with ONDC, with a budget of ₹277.35 crore over three years, to onboard 5 lakh Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs), including 50% women-led businesses, by providing training, financial incentives, and support for catalogue creation, operations, and account management through Seller Network Participants. Additionally, ONDC has introduced fully digital, paperless loans available in just 6 minutes, integrated with 9 buyer applications (Lending Service Providers) and 3 lenders, enhancing accessibility and efficiency in credit services.
application_process: 1. Sign up on the ONDC Portal and create a profile. 2. Explore introductory resources and attend community webinars. 3. Select your role (Buyer Network Participant, Seller Network Participant, Technology Service Provider, or Gateway) and domain via the portal. 4. Integrate with ONDC APIs and test your solution in Staging, Pre-Production, and Production environments. 5. Qualify the requirements and Go-Live on the ONDC network.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
contact_details: Email: team@ondc.org | Address: Open Network For Digital Commerce (ONDC) 2nd Floor & 3rd Floor, 7/6, August Kranti Marg, Siri Fort Institutional Area, Near Siri Fort Auditorium, New Delhi - 110049

overview: MSME SAMADHAAN (MSME Delayed Payment Portal) is an online platform launched by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises to facilitate the resolution of delayed payment disputes faced by micro and small enterprises (MSEs) when dealing with central ministries, departments, central public sector enterprises (CPSEs), and state governments. The portal enables MSEs to file applications for the recovery of delayed payments along with applicable compound interest under the MSMED Act, 2006. It serves as a monitoring and redressal mechanism to ensure timely payments to MSEs as mandated by law.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Any micro or small enterprise (MSE) that has supplied goods or services to a central ministry, department, central public sector enterprise (CPSE), or state government and is facing delayed payment beyond the agreed period or 45 days (as per MSMED Act, 2006) can file an application on the portal. The enterprise must have a valid Udyam Registration Number.
benefits: The portal provides a structured online mechanism for filing delayed payment claims, facilitates the possibility of receiving compound interest on delayed amounts due date Act, 2006, and enables tracking of the case status. It reduces the need for litigation by providing a government-backed facilitative forum for dispute resolution.
financial_support: The portal does not provide direct financial support but facilitates the recovery of the principal amount due along with compound interest as mandated under Section 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006. The interest is calculated at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India.
application_process: 1. Visit the MSME SAMADHAAN portal at https://samadhaan.msme.gov.in 2. Click on 'File Application' or 'Register Grievance' 3. Enter Udyam Registration Number and validate the enterprise 4. Fill in the details of the buyer (central ministry/department/CPSE/state government), invoice details, amount due, and date of supply 5. Upload supporting documents such as invoices, delivery challans, and correspondence 6. Submit the application and note the application number for tracking 7. Monitor the status of the application through the portal using the application number
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be filed at any time as delayed payment issues arise
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

overview: The Account Aggregator (AA) framework is an RBI-approved initiative under India's Digital Public Infrastructure that enables secure, consent-driven sharing of financial data between Financial Information Providers (FIPs) and Financial Information Users (FIUs) via Account Aggregators (AAs). It empowers individuals and businesses to access financial services like loans, insurance, and wealth management by providing real-time, verified financial data with explicit user consent. The framework promotes financial inclusion, reduces operational friction, and supports innovation across lending, investments, insurance, and personal finance sectors. Sahamati acts as the industry body driving adoption, setting standards, and enabling interoperability within the AA ecosystem.
target_beneficiaries: individuals; businesses; MSMEs; lenders; insurers; wealth managers; stockbrokers; financial institutions
eligibility: Any registered and regulated entity under RBI, PFRDA, SEBI, IRDAI, or Department of Revenue (GSTN) can participate in the AA ecosystem.
benefits: The Account Aggregator framework enables secure, consent-based sharing of financial data, eliminating the need for physical document collection or sharing login credentials. It accelerates credit decisions, reduces operational friction, and expands access to affordable credit, especially for first-time and underserved borrowers. In lending, it improves underwriting accuracy and reduces fraud. In insurance, it enables faster policy issuance, better risk pricing, and improved persistency. In wealth management, it provides holistic financial insights and personalized advisory services. For individuals, it offers a unified, real-time view of finances across accounts, supporting better financial decision-making. The framework ensures data encryption, user-controlled consent management, and prevents data misuse or storage by AAs. It supports interoperability through standardized APIs and certification frameworks, and enables monitoring of government schemes, employee compliance, and counterparty risks. Participants benefit from access to Sahamati’s technical services, Central Registry, dispute resolution, and collaborative governance forums.
financial_support: The Account Aggregator framework does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies to entities. It is a technological and regulatory infrastructure enabling consent-driven data exchange. Financial benefits accrue indirectly through improved access to credit, reduced processing costs, and enhanced service delivery for participating institutions (FIPs, FIUs, AAs). There is no fund corpus or per-entity financial allocation under the framework itself. Revenue models for participants are based on their respective business models (e.g., AAs may charge transaction fees, FIPs/FIUs gain efficiency). Sahamati generates revenue through membership fees from Regulated Entities (REs), categorized by asset size or revenue tiers.
application_process: 1. Get registered and regulated by at least one Financial Service Regulator (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA). 2. Implement the required module (FIP, FIU, or AA) using RBI-defined API specifications published by ReBIT. 3. Test the module in RBI-approved Account Aggregator Sandboxes. 4. Enrol the module in the UAT-Central Registry for testing in the development environment. 5. Obtain certification from a Sahamati-empanelled auditor for adherence to ReBIT Technical Standards. 6. Get details publicised in the Central Registry upon going live. 7. Launch services with customers. 8. For Regulated Entity (RE) membership in Sahamati: submit valid registration certificate, executed Membership Terms, authorization document, and proof of certification; pay applicable annual fee based on entity category.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in collaboration with Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI), and Financial Stability Development Council (FSDC)
contact_details: Email: memberservices@sahamati.org.in | For certification: certifier@sahamati.org.in | For Fair Use: fairuse@sahamati.org.in | For SaaNS access: memberservices@sahamati.org.in | For RE membership: membership@sahamati.org.in

overview: The ISRO Start-up Policy & Technology Transfer initiative aims to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in the space sector by enabling startups to access ISRO's expertise, facilities, and technologies. It supports the development of space-related products and services through collaboration, mentorship, and technology licensing from ISRO centres. The policy encourages startups to contribute to India's space economy by leveraging ISRO's intellectual property and infrastructure.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups registered in India working on space technologies, applications, or allied sectors that can benefit from ISRO's expertise, facilities, or intellectual property are eligible to apply under the ISRO Start-up Policy.
benefits: Access to ISRO facilities for testing and validation, mentorship from ISRO scientists, guidance on technology development, opportunities for technology transfer and licensing of ISRO-developed technologies, and support in navigating regulatory and technical requirements for space activities.
financial_support: The policy does not specify direct financial grants or funding; support is primarily in-kind through access to facilities, expertise, and technology transfer. Any financial aspects would be negotiated case-by-case based on the nature of collaboration or technology licensing agreements.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant ISRO centre or unit based on the technology or domain of interest. 2. Submit a proposal detailing the startup's technology, objectives, and proposed collaboration with ISRO. 3. Proposal is reviewed by the ISRO centre for technical feasibility and alignment with policy goals. 4. If approved, discussions are held to define the scope of collaboration, including access to facilities, mentorship, or technology transfer. 5. A formal agreement (MoU or similar) is executed outlining terms of engagement, IP rights, and responsibilities.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Department of Space, Government of India

overview: MSME SAMBANDH is a public procurement portal launched by the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises to facilitate government procurement from MSMEs. It enables central and state government ministries, departments, and public sector undertakings to publish tenders and procurement opportunities specifically for MSMEs. The portal aims to enhance market access, promote transparency, and increase participation of MSMEs in government procurement processes.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSMEs with valid Udyam Registration are eligible to participate in procurement opportunities published on the SAMBANDH portal. The portal is accessible to all registered MSMEs across manufacturing and service sectors.
benefits: MSMEs gain access to government procurement opportunities, increased visibility for their products/services, transparent bidding processes, and potential for assured orders from government buyers. The portal reduces information asymmetry and search costs for MSMEs seeking government contracts.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support. It facilitates access to government procurement contracts where financial benefits accrue through successful bid awards and contract execution.
application_process: 1. MSMEs must first obtain Udyam Registration via https://udyamregistration.gov.in 2. Visit the SAMBANDH portal at https://msme.gov.in/sambandh 3. Browse available government tenders and procurement opportunities 4. Select relevant tenders based on business category and location 5. Download tender documents and review eligibility criteria 6. Prepare and submit bids as per tender specifications 7. Track application status through the portal 8. Upon award, execute contract as per terms
deadlines: Tender-specific deadlines apply; the portal hosts ongoing procurement opportunities with varying submission dates.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises

scheme_name: Angel Tax Exemption for DPIIT Startups
overview: The Angel Tax Exemption for DPIIT Startups provides income tax exemption under Section 80-IAC of the Income Tax Act for eligible startups recognized by DPIIT. It allows startups to avail a tax holiday for three consecutive financial years out of their first ten years since incorporation. The scheme aims to reduce early-stage financial pressure on startups and encourage investment by exempting profits and gains from taxation.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: The entity should be a DPIIT recognised startup. Only Private Limited Companies or Limited Liability Partnerships are eligible for tax exemption under Section 80IAC. The startup should have been incorporated after 1st April, 2016. The startup must be engaged in innovation, development, or improvement of products, processes, or services or a scalable business model with high potential for employment generation or wealth creation. The turnover should not exceed INR 200 crore in any financial year since incorporation (INR 300 crore for DeepTech startups). The entity should not have been formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business.
benefits: DPIIT recognised startups can avail 100% tax exemption on profits and gains for three consecutive financial years out of the first ten years since incorporation. Additional benefits include self-certification under labour and environmental laws, fast-track patent examination with 80% rebate on filing fees, easier public procurement norms, and easy winding up of company under Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
financial_support: The scheme provides tax exemption on profits and gains from eligible businesses. There is no direct financial disbursement; the benefit is in the form of tax savings on eligible income. The exemption is available for any 3 consecutive tax years within the first 10 years from incorporation.
application_process: 1. Register on the Startup India portal. 2. Apply for DPIIT recognition via the National Single Window System (NSWS). 3. After obtaining DPIIT recognition, access the Section 80 IAC exemption application form on the Startup India portal. 4. Fill in all required details and upload the necessary documents. 5. Submit the application form for review. 6. Track application status via the dashboard on the Startup India Portal.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: Startup IP Protection – Fast Track Patent Examination
overview: The Startup IP Protection – Fast Track Patent Examination scheme is designed to expedite the patent examination process for startups in India. It enables eligible startups to avail of accelerated examination of their patent applications, reducing the time taken for grant. The scheme is part of the broader Intellectual Property Protection (SIPP) initiative under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups recognized by DPIIT are eligible to avail of the fast track patent examination facility under the Startup Intellectual Property Protection (SIPP) scheme. The applicant must be a DPIIT-recognized startup and must submit Form 28 (Declaration for Startups) along with the patent application.
benefits: Expedited examination of patent applications, leading to faster grant of patents. Startups also benefit from an 80% rebate on official fees for patents, designs, and trademarks under the SIPP scheme. The facility helps in early protection of innovations, which is crucial for attracting investment and commercialization.
financial_support: The scheme provides an 80% rebate on official fees for patent filing, examination, and related procedures for DPIIT-recognized startups. There is no direct grant or loan; the support is in the form of fee reduction. The exact quantum depends on the number of claims, pages, and other factors as per the First Schedule of the Patents Rules.
application_process: 1. Obtain DPIIT recognition as a startup via the Startup India portal. 2. Prepare the patent application with Form 1 (Application for Grant of Patent) and Form 2 (Provisional/Complete Specification). 3. Fill and submit Form 28 (Declaration for Startups) to avail of startup benefits. 4. File the application online through the IP India e-filing portal or physically at the appropriate patent office. 5. Pay the prescribed fees (with 80% rebate applicable for startups). 6. Request expedited examination by filing Form 18A (Request for Expedited Examination). 7. Track application status via the IP India portal. 8. Respond to examination reports (FER) within the prescribed time. 9. Upon compliance, the patent proceeds to grant and publication.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: The DRDO CEPTAM Scheme is a recruitment initiative by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) aimed at hiring personnel for technical and administrative posts such as Senior Technical Assistant-B (STA-B) and Technician-A. It is part of DRDO's efforts to strengthen its workforce in research, development, and support functions across its laboratories and establishments. The scheme is advertised periodically, with the latest notification being CEPTAM-11 for STA-B and Technician-A positions.
target_beneficiaries: job seekers; technical staff; administrative staff
eligibility: Candidates must meet the educational qualifications, age limits, and other criteria specified for each post (e.g., STA-B and Technician-A) as detailed in the official advertisement. Eligibility varies by post and includes educational qualifications, age, and sometimes experience or specific technical skills.
benefits: Selected candidates receive a regular government job in DRDO with pay scale as per 7th CPC, allowances, job security, and opportunities for career growth in defence research and development. Benefits include medical facilities, leave entitlements, and other central government employee perks.
financial_support: The scheme offers a fixed monthly salary as per the pay matrix for the respective post (e.g., STA-B and Technician-A) under the 7th Central Pay Commission, along with dearness allowance, house rent allowance, and other applicable allowances. Exact figures are specified in the official recruitment notification.
application_process: 1. Check the official DRDO website for the latest CEPTAM advertisement (e.g., CEPTAM-11). 2. Read the eligibility criteria, post details, and instructions carefully. 3. Apply online through the designated portal as specified in the advertisement. 4. Upload required documents such as educational certificates, age proof, and category certificate (if applicable). 5. Submit the application before the last date. 6. Appear for the written examination/skill test as per the schedule. 7. Wait for result declaration and further selection process.
deadlines: As per the specific CEPTAM notification (e.g., CEPTAM-11 had a last date for application as mentioned in the advertisement; exact date not provided in evidence)
implementing_agency: Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), Ministry of Defence, Government of India
contact_details: Email: Not explicitly provided in evidence for CEPTAM scheme; general DRDO contact: director.desidoc@gov.in (from newsletter)

overview: The Design Registration Facilitation for Startups scheme under the Intellectual Property India portal supports startups in securing design protection by providing guidance on the design application workflow, eligibility criteria, fee structures, and procedural steps. It aims to simplify the design registration process for innovative startups through e-filing services, facilitator support, and clear documentation requirements.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups, as defined under the Startup India initiative, are eligible to apply for design registration. The applicant must be a recognized startup by DPIIT, incorporated as a private limited company, registered partnership, or limited liability partnership, with turnover less than INR 100 Crore and not older than 10 years from incorporation.
benefits: Startups benefit from facilitation in design registration, access to IP Mitras (facilitators) under the SIPP scheme, guidance on design application workflow, clarity on fee structures for natural persons/startups/small entities, and support through e-filing services. The scheme enables startups to secure legal protection for their designs, enhancing market competitiveness and innovation valuation.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or subsidies. However, startups benefit from reduced official fees for design applications as per the First Schedule of the Designs Rules, 2001, where natural persons, startups, or small entities pay lower fees compared to other applicants. Fee details are available in the 'Forms and Official Fees' section for designs.
application_process: 1. Check design availability by searching existing registered designs on the official website. 2. Assess novelty and identify the correct Locarno class-subclass. 3. Choose the goods/articles class and confirm eligibility and application category. 4. Decide applicant type (Individual/Startup/MSME/Others), understand applicable official fee, provide applicant details, design representation, and Power of Attorney (if applicable). 5. Prepare required information and documents, choose application type. 6. File new application (Form 1) via e-Filing portal: login, upload documents, pay prescribed fee. 7. Track application status online. 8. Respond to examination objections if required. 9. Application published in Design Journal upon acceptance.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year with no fixed deadline.
implementing_agency: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
contact_details: Email: cgoffice[at]gov[dot]in | Phone: 011-28034302 (Director, Administration and Establishment) | Helpdesk: Available via IP India portal

scheme_name: PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission
overview: The PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched to strengthen public health infrastructure and pandemic preparedness across India. It aims to develop critical care hospital blocks, expand diagnostic services, and enhance surveillance and research capabilities at national, state, and district levels. The mission focuses on building resilient health systems through investments in both urban and rural health facilities.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; union territories; public health facilities
eligibility: State Governments and Union Territories are eligible to receive financial assistance under the scheme. Funds are allocated based on population, disease burden, and health infrastructure gaps. Implementation is carried out through State Health Societies and designated nodal agencies.
benefits: Financial support for construction and equipping of critical care blocks, diagnostic laboratories, block public health units, and integrated public health labs. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, training programs, and monitoring support from central agencies. The scheme enhances access to quality healthcare services, especially in underserved and rural areas.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-in-aid to States and UTs for infrastructure development. Funding is released in installments based on utilization of previous installments and submission of utilization certificates. The central government bears 60% of the cost for most components, while 90% is provided for North Eastern and Himalayan States, and 100% for Union Territories.
application_process: 1. State Governments/UTs submit project proposals to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. 2. Proposals are appraised by the Expenditure Finance Committee or Standing Finance Committee. 3. Upon approval, administrative sanction is issued. 4. Funds are released in installments as per the agreed schedule. 5. States/UTs implement the projects through designated agencies. 6. Utilization certificates and progress reports are submitted for subsequent fund releases.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year based on annual budget allocations and planning cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

overview: The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) is a Government of India initiative under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) to promote apprenticeship training and provide financial support to establishments engaging apprentices. It aims to bridge the skill gap by offering stipend support to apprentices and incentivizing industries to participate in skill development. NAPS operates through a digital portal for registration, contract management, and reimbursement processes, targeting youth and establishments across India.
target_beneficiaries: youth; establishments; MSME; industries
eligibility: Establishments covered under the Apprentices Act, 1961 are eligible to engage apprentices and claim reimbursement under NAPS. Candidates must meet the educational and age criteria specified for the designated or optional trade they are applying for. Establishments must have a valid registration on the apprenticeship portal and comply with contract signing, advisor verification, and payroll creation timelines as per portal guidelines.
benefits: Financial reimbursement of stipend paid to apprentices (up to prescribed limits), facilitation of apprenticeship contracts through a digital portal, access to a wide range of training courses across sectors, support for Basic Training Providers (BTPs), and integration with schemes like PMKVY and NCVT for auto-population of candidate data. Non-financial benefits include skill development, improved employability, and industry-institute linkage.
financial_support: Under NAPS, the government reimburses 25% of the prescribed stipend subject to a maximum of Rs. 1,500 per month per apprentice for a maximum period of 500 hours of basic training. Reimbursement is processed through the apprenticeship portal after contract approval by the Apprenticeship Advisor and verification of stipend payment by the establishment. The stipend for apprentices is paid by the establishment, and the government provides partial reimbursement as per the scheme norms.
application_process: 1. Establishments register on the apprenticeshipindia.org portal. 2. Candidates register as apprentices on the portal. 3. Establishment selects a candidate and issues a contract through the portal. 4. Candidate signs the contract within 7 days of issuance. 5. The signed contract is routed to the Apprenticeship Advisor for verification/approval within 30 days. 6. Upon approval, stipend payroll is created and establishment pays the apprentice. 7. Establishment submits reimbursement claim through the portal for government share of stipend. 8. Claims are processed and funds transferred to the establishment's registered bank account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)
contact_details: Email: vs.arvind@nic.in | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

overview: Defence India Startup Challenge (DISC) is a sub-scheme under the Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) initiative, launched by the Ministry of Defence in partnership with Atal Innovation Mission. It aims to support startups, MSMEs, and individual innovators in creating prototypes and commercializing products/solutions relevant to national defence and security. The challenge provides grant funding and additional support such as access to defence testing facilities, mentorship, and accelerator programs through iDEX partners.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSMEs; individual innovators
eligibility: Startups, as defined and recognized by Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. Any Indian company incorporated under the Companies Act 1956/2013, primarily a Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as defined in the MSME Act, 2006. Individual Innovators are also encouraged to apply (research & academic institutions can also use this category).
benefits: Grant funding up to ₹1.5 crores, access to defence testing facilities and experts for product/technology development, entry to accelerator programs run by iDEX partners for mentorship in technology and business development, and support in prototyping, pilot implementation, and market assessment.
financial_support: Selected applications are funded up to ₹1.5 crores in the form of grant/equity/debt/other relevant structures, disbursed in tranches based on milestones decided by a high-powered selection committee. The grant is provided under the SPARK (Support for Prototype and Research Kickstart in Defence) framework.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to ₹1.5 crores
application_process: 1. Register on the iDEX website and login using credentials. 2. Complete the application form providing full details of a Single Point of Contact, Entity Details (for Startups/MSMEs), and Proposal Details including problem statement selection, funding level, technical and financial details, patents/research papers, and tentative business plan. 3. Upload required documents. 4. Submit the application. 5. Applications are screened by a duly constituted high-powered committee of defence and technology experts. 6. Shortlisted applications undergo evaluation by the High Powered Screening Committee (HPSC) on parameters including relevance, comprehensiveness, innovation, feasibility, capability, and viability. 7. Final winners are declared based on HPSC recommendations.
deadlines: Rolling basis — specific challenge deadlines vary (e.g., DISC 12 Re Open: Last Date - 30 Sep, 2026 11:59 PM; Open Challenge: Last Date - 04 May, 2026 5:00 PM)
implementing_agency: Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO)

overview: Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India in April 2018 under the Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, to foster innovation and technology development in defence and aerospace by engaging startups, MSMEs, individual innovators, R&D institutes, and academia. It provides grants, funding, and other support to carry out R&D with potential for future adoption in Indian defence and aerospace needs. iDEX operates through the Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO), a Section 8 company formed by HAL and BEL, and runs challenges such as Defence India Startup Challenge (DISC), Open Challenge, and ADITI to support prototype development and commercialization.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSMEs; individual innovators; R&D institutes; academia
eligibility: Startups as defined and recognized by Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India; any Indian company incorporated under the Companies Act 1956/2013, primarily a Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) as defined in the MSME Act, 2006; individual innovators are also encouraged to apply (research & academic institutions can use this category to apply).
benefits: Grants/funding, mentorship, access to defence testing facilities and experts, entry to accelerator programs run by iDEX partners, support in technology and business development, and facilitation of scale-up, indigenization, and integration in manufacturing facilities for successfully piloted technologies.
financial_support: Applicants showing capability, intent, and promise to be able to produce functional prototypes or to productize existing technologies will be awarded maximum grants of up to Rs. 1.5 crores per applicant, strictly on a milestone basis and starting, in the form of grant/equity/debt/other relevant structures, strictly on a milestone basis. The exact amount and mode of each grant shall be decided by a high-powered committee based on the application, as per the prevailing scheme. In special cases, if deemed necessary by the high-powered committee, the funding amount may be increased beyond the prescribed limit, on a case by case basis.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 1.5 crores per applicant
application_process: 1. Provide full details of a Single Point of Contact for the applying entity – these are the full contact details of a single person who will act as the point of contact between iDEX and the applicant. 2. Provide Entity Details – these are the details of the Startup/MSME applying (Individual Innovators do not have to fill these). 3. Provide Proposal Details – these are the details of the proposal in response to the iDEX Challenge problem statements/focus areas. Applicants must select the problem statement they are addressing, what level of funding they want and give technical and financial details of their proposal. This will include mentioning relevant patents and research papers by the applicant, if any as well as a tentative business plan. 4. Submit the application online via the iDEX portal. 5. Applications will be screened by a duly constituted high-powered committee of defence and technology experts for screening and selection of applications for the iDEX Challenge.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO), Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, Government of India
