overview: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) aims to develop the backbone necessary to support the integrated digital health infrastructure of the country. It will bridge the existing gap amongst different stakeholders of Healthcare ecosystem through digital highways. ABDM comprises key registries such as the Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA), healthcare professional registry (HPR), health facility registry (HFR), and drug registry.
target_beneficiaries: citizens; health facilities; healthcare professionals; health tech companies; states
eligibility: Participation of an individual in the NDHE will be on a purely voluntary basis. Where an individual chooses to participate, he/she will be issued a Health ID (as defined in this Policy) by the NDHM. Where an individual wishes to avail of any health services, the Health ID of the individual may be verified by the use of Aadhaar or any other method of identification as may be specified by the NDHM. The voluntary use of Aadhaar in this Policy is envisaged as per the Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance (Social Welfare, Innovation, Knowledge) Rules, 2020. The failure or refusal to make use of Aadhaar would not result in the denial of access to any health facility or service.
benefits: ABHA allows individuals to link and share their health records. It enables your interaction with participating healthcare providers, and allows you to receive your digital lab reports, prescriptions and diagnosis seamlessly from verified healthcare professionals and health service providers. For Health Facilities: We are creating a comprehensive repository of all the public and private health facilities of the country across different systems of medicine. For Healthcare Professionals: We are empowering healthcare professionals to join the ABDM ecosystem and be part of the healthcare digital transformation in India! For Health Tech Companies: Engagement with Health Service Providers fosters the integration of digital platforms and bridge gaps across the healthcare ecosystem. For States: States Government and Health Authorities play a pivotal role to accelerate the adoption of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) in the public and private health system.
application_process: 1. Register on e-Sushrut Clinic website: https://ehmis-lite.in/AHIMSG5/hissso/logoutLogin 2. Sign up using your credentials to create an account 3. Generate or Validate Healthcare Professional Registry (HPR) ID: New Users: Generate your HPR ID using your Aadhaar ID; Existing Users: Validate your HPR ID using your Aadhaar-linked mobile number or HPR-linked mobile number 4. Generate or Validate Health Facility Registry (HFR) ID: New Facilities: Generate your HFR ID by providing essential details such as facility name, location, operational status, services offered, ownership details etc.; Existing Facilities: Validate your facility details like HFR ID, Facility Name, State and District. 5. Complete Onboarding & Get Started: Fill in the required details on e-Sushrut Clinic to complete the onboarding process
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Health Authority (NHA), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

overview: The North East Venture Fund (NEVF) is a scheme managed by SIDBI to support startups and early-stage enterprises in the North Eastern region of India. It aims to promote entrepreneurship and innovation by providing financial assistance through venture capital investments. The fund focuses on high-growth potential startups in sectors such as technology, manufacturing, and services. NEVF operates as a Fund of Funds, investing in SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) that in turn invest in eligible startups.
target_beneficiaries: startups; early-stage enterprises; MSME
eligibility: Startups and early-stage enterprises based in the North Eastern region of India with innovative business models, high growth potential, and compliance with SIDBI's investment criteria. Enterprises must be registered as private limited companies, LLPs, or partnership firms and demonstrate scalability and market readiness.
benefits: Access to venture capital funding without immediate equity dilution in some cases, mentorship and strategic guidance from fund managers, networking opportunities with investors and industry experts, validation of business model through institutional investment, and potential follow-on funding from other sources.
financial_support: NEVF operates as a Fund of Funds, investing in SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) that provide capital to startups. The fund does not directly lend to enterprises but channels investments through professional venture capital funds. Investment is made in the form of equity or quasi-equity instruments based on the startup's stage and growth potential.
application_process: 1. Identify and approach SEBI-registered AIFs partnered with NEVF. 2. Submit business plan, pitch deck, and financial projections to the AIF. 3. Undergo due diligence and investment committee review. 4. Receive term sheet and negotiate investment terms. 5. Complete legal documentation and fund disbursement. 6. Utilize funds for business growth as per agreed milestones.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

overview: The Uttar Pradesh Scholarship Portal provides financial assistance to students from various categories including SC, ST, General, Minority, and OBC for pre-matric (classes 9-10) and post-matric (classes 11-12 and beyond) education. The scheme covers tuition fees, maintenance allowances, and other educational expenses through direct benefit transfer to eligible students.
target_beneficiaries: SC; ST; General; Minority; OBC
eligibility: Students belonging to SC, ST, General, Minority, and OBC categories studying in recognized educational institutions in Uttar Pradesh are eligible. For pre-matric (classes 9-10), the scheme covers students from SC, ST, General, Minority, and OBC. For post-matric (classes 11-12 and beyond), eligibility extends to SC, ST, General, Minority, and OBC students pursuing intermediate, graduation, post-graduation, or professional courses. Applicants must have a bank account linked with Aadhaar and complete One Time Registration (OTR) before applying.
benefits: Financial benefits include maintenance allowance, tuition fee reimbursement, and other educational expenses. Non-financial benefits include access to education for disadvantaged groups, reduced dropout rates, and empowerment through educational support. Specific amounts vary by category and course: pre-matric scholarship provides up to ₹150 per month for 10 months, while post-matric includes fee reimbursement and maintenance allowance as per government norms.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to students' Aadhaar-linked bank accounts. The scheme covers maintenance allowance, tuition fees, and other educational charges. For pre-matric (classes 9-10), the rate is ₹150 per month for 10 months. For post-matric, it includes full tuition fee reimbursement and maintenance allowance as per government norms, with disbursement tracked via the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).
application_process: 1. Complete One Time Registration (OTR) on the Uttar Pradesh Scholarship Portal. 2. Log in using registered credentials. 3. Fill the online application form for the respective scholarship category (pre-matric or post-matric). 4. Upload required documents including caste certificate, income certificate, mark sheets, and bank details. 5. Submit the application online. 6. Take a printout of the submitted application. 7. Submit the hard copy with attached documents to the educational institution. 8. Institution verifies and forwards the application online. 9. University/affiliating agency verifies student details and course eligibility. 10. NIC conducts scrutiny of applications. 11. District committee locks verified data. 12. Funds are transferred to beneficiaries' accounts after verification.
deadlines: Application window: July 10, 2025 to January 14, 2026 for student registration/online application for session 2025-26. Hard copy submission deadline: July 02, 2025 to January 21, 2026. Final printout: July 12, 2025 to January 17, 2026.
implementing_agency: Department of Social Welfare, Government of Uttar Pradesh
contact_details: Email: Not explicitly provided | Helpline: CM Helpline no. (as mentioned in Important Links section)

overview: The National Scholarship Portal (NSP) is a one-stop solution for various scholarship schemes launched by Union Government, State Governments, and Union Territories. It enables student application, processing, sanction, and disbursal of scholarships directly into beneficiaries' accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). The portal aims to provide a simplified, mission-oriented, accountable, responsive, and transparent (SMART) system for faster and effective disposal of scholarship applications and delivery of funds without leakages.
target_beneficiaries: students
eligibility: Eligibility varies by specific scholarship scheme hosted on NSP. General requirements include being a student, meeting domicile criteria, income limits (often Rs. 8 lakh per annum or less), academic merit, and enrollment in recognized institutions. Specific schemes may target categories such as orphans, wards of parents died due to Covid-19, wards of Armed Forces martyred in action, specially-abled students, girl students, SC/ST/OBC, minorities, and others. Aadhaar or Aadhaar Enrolment ID is mandatory for most schemes. One Time Registration (OTR) is required to apply for scholarships on NSP from AY 2024-25 onwards.
benefits: Financial support through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts. Non-financial benefits include simplified application process via single integrated form, eligibility suggestions by the system, reduced duplication, transparency in processing, standardisation of data, and access to a common portal for multiple central and state scholarship schemes. Additional benefits include OTR generation for lifelong use, availability at Common Service Centres (CSCs), and helpline support.
financial_support: Financial support varies by scheme and is disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) through PFMS gateway into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts. Examples include: PM-USP CSSS provides academic fee (up to Rs. 1.25 Lakh for professional courses) and maintenance allowance (Rs. 1.00 Lakh per annum); AICTE Swanath Scholarship provides Rs. 50,000 per annum; Pragati and Saksham Scholarships provide Rs. 50,000 per annum; PMSS provides ₹3,000/month for girls and ₹2,500/month for boys. The total charges for OTR generation and application filing at CSCs is fixed at Rs 30.00 per candidate.
application_process: 1. Generate One Time Registration (OTR) using Aadhaar/Aadhaar Enrollment ID via NSP OTR app or portal. 2. Login to NSP using OTR ID and password. 3. Check eligibility for scholarship schemes using the eligibility checker. 4. Select desired scheme and fill the online application form. 5. Upload required documents (e.g., mark sheets, income certificate, category certificate, bonafide certificate). 6. Submit application before the deadline. 7. Application undergoes verification at institute, district/state, and ministry levels. 8. After approval, scholarship amount is disbursed via DBT to Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
deadlines: Varies by scheme. For AY 2026-27, student application open from 1st June 2026, closing date for student application is 31-10-2026, institute verification closing date is 15-11-2026, and L2 verification closing date is 30/11/2026. Some schemes have rolling basis or specific windows; refer to individual scheme guidelines on NSP.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
contact_details: Email: helpdesk[at]nsp[dot]gov[dot]in | Helpline: 0120 - 6619540 (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on all days, except government holidays) | Toll free Number: 1800 118 111

overview: Tribal Innovation & Entrepreneurship Fund (TIEF) is a scheme under TRIFED aimed at fostering entrepreneurship among tribal communities by supporting the establishment of Van Dhan Producer Enterprises (VDPEs) through resource allocation, capacity building, and market access. It seeks to transform Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) into profit-oriented legal entities to enhance tribal income and economic resilience. The scheme integrates tribal communities into formal economic systems by promoting collective processing, value addition, and marketing of forest, farm, and non-farm products.
target_beneficiaries: tribal entrepreneurs; Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs); Self Help Groups (SHGs); tribal communities
eligibility: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) established under the PMJVM scheme, formed by the merger of four or more geographically proximate VDVKs, are eligible to be transformed into Van Dhan Producer Enterprises (VDPEs). VDPEs may be registered under any legally recognized structure including Societies, Co-operative Societies, Multi-State Co-operative Societies, Producer Companies, or MSMEs with UDYAM Registration.
benefits: VDPEs gain formal recognition, access to institutional finance, improved collective bargaining power, capacity building, infrastructure support, market linkage facilitation, product development support, logistics support, reporting mechanisms, monitoring and evaluation, and social return on investment (SRoI) assessment. They also benefit from value chain integration, quality assurance, and market readiness, enabling long-term sustainability and scalability and enhanced socio-economic impact.
financial_support: TRIFED adopts a three-tranche fund release model for State Implementing Agencies (SIAs): 10% upon proposal approval, 40% upon submission of Utilization Certificate (UC) for initial 10%, proof of VDPE registration, and Detailed Project Report (DPR), and 50% upon full utilization of the second tranche, verified implementation, and submission of supporting documentation. For Implementation Support Agencies (ISAs), fund release follows a deliverable-based model across pre-planning, implementation, and post-implementation phases, with percentages mutually agreed upon at the MoU/Agreement stage.
application_process: 1. State Implementing Agency (SIA) or Implementation Support Agency (ISA) prepares project proposal in coordination with State Nodal Department (SND) and respective Regional Office of TRIFED. 2. Project proposal is submitted to TRIFED for approval, including detailed profiling of constituent VDVKs, geographical and resource mapping, activities for awareness generation and handholding support, revival plan of defunct VDVKs, assessments of production potential, infrastructure, market prospects, and post-implementation plan. 3. Upon approval, funds are released in tranches based on milestones. 4. SIA/ISA is delegated administrative and financial powers to execute VDPE activities. 5. TRIFED Regional Offices assist in proposal formulation, field-level coordination, verification visits, compliance checks, and monitoring & evaluation. 6. VDPEs must undergo formation prerequisites including infrastructure assessment, compliance gaps, capacity-building needs, and market linkages, documented in a Detailed Project Report (DPR). 7. VDPEs are established through legal registration under recognized structures such as Societies, Co-operatives, Producer Companies, or MSMEs. 8. Operationalization includes market linkage, branding, full-scale operations, monitoring & evaluation, and SRoI assessment.
implementing_agency: Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Limited (TRIFED)

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
overview: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) is a government-backed life insurance scheme offering a renewable one-year cover for death due to any reason. It is administered through LIC and other life insurance companies in partnership with participating banks and post offices. The scheme provides a life cover of Rs. 2 lakh on the death of the insured member, with an annual premium of Rs. 436/- deducted via auto-debit from the account holder's bank or post office account.
target_beneficiaries: individuals; bank account holders; post office account holders
eligibility: Individual bank/post office account holders of participating banks/post office aged between 18 years (completed) and 50 years (age nearer birthday) who give their consent to join/enable auto-debit are eligible. Aadhaar is the primary KYC for the bank/post office account. In case of multiple accounts, enrollment is allowed through one account only.
benefits: Life insurance cover of Rs. 2 lakh payable on the death of the member due to any cause. The scheme also allows re-enrollment after exit, and the premium paid is eligible for tax benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act (as per general provisions, though not explicitly stated in evidence). The commission paid to Business Correspondents/agents for new enrollments may be passed on as a benefit to the subscriber in case of voluntary electronic enrollment.
financial_support: The scheme provides a fixed life insurance benefit of Rs. 2 lakh upon death of the insured. The annual premium is Rs. 436/- per member, collected via auto-debit from the bank/post office account. The premium is apportioned as: Rs. 395/- to the insurance company, Rs. 30/- as commission to Business Correspondents/agents (for new enrollments only), and Rs. 11/- as administrative expenses to the participating bank/post office. For delayed enrollment, pro-rata premiums apply: Rs. 342/- (Q2), Rs. 228/- (Q3), Rs. 114/- (Q4).
application_process: 1. Ensure you have an active bank or post office account with a participating institution. 2. Link your Aadhaar to the account as KYC. 3. Visit your bank/post office branch or use their digital platform to obtain the PMJJBY enrollment form. 4. Fill the enrollment form with personal details and consent for auto-debit. 5. Submit the form and authorize auto-debit of the annual premium (Rs. 436/-) from your account. 6. The premium will be deducted in one instalment via auto-debit. 7. Upon successful deduction, you will receive an acknowledgement slip-cum-certificate of insurance. 8. Renewal is required annually by 31st May via auto-debit for continued coverage.
deadlines: Enrollment / auto-debit authorization must be submitted by 31st May each year for coverage from 1st June to 31st May. Delayed enrollment is possible with pro-rata premium payment, after which cover starts from the date of auto-debit.
implementing_agency: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
contact_details: Email: usins2-dfs@nic.in | Helpline: 1800-180-1111 (toll-free numbers vary by state; refer to STATEWISETOLLFREE.pdf for state-wise toll-free numbers)

overview: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is a government-backed pension scheme launched in 2015 to provide a defined pension to subscribers in the unorganized sector. It guarantees a minimum monthly pension ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 upon reaching the age of 60, based on contributions made during the working years. The scheme is administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) through the National Pension System (NPS) architecture. Subscribers who join between the ages of 18 and 40 are eligible, with contributions varying according to the chosen pension amount and age of entry.
target_beneficiaries: unorganized sector workers; low-income individuals
eligibility: Any citizen of India aged between 18 and 40 years can join the Atal Pension Yojana. The subscriber must have a savings bank account or a post office savings account. Individuals who are already covered under any statutory social security scheme (such as EPF, ESIC, or NPS) are not eligible to enroll in APY.
benefits: Subscribers receive a guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000, ₹2,000, ₹3,000, ₹4,000, or ₹5,000 upon attaining the age of 60, depending on the contribution chosen. The government provides a co-contribution of 50% of the subscriber's contribution or ₹1,000 per annum, whichever is lower, for eligible subscribers who joined between 2015-16 and 2019-20 and are not beneficiaries of any other statutory social security scheme and not income tax payers. In case of the subscriber's death, the spouse is entitled to receive the same pension amount, and upon the death of both the subscriber and spouse, the nominee receives the accumulated corpus.
financial_support: The financial support under APY consists of a government co-contribution of 50% of the subscriber's annual contribution or ₹1,000 per annum, whichever is lower, for eligible subscribers who joined the scheme between 2015-16 and 2019-20 and meet specific criteria (not covered under any statutory social security scheme and not income tax payers). The subscriber's own contribution varies based on the chosen pension slab and age of entry, ranging from ₹42 per month for a ₹1,000 pension at age 18 to ₹1,454 per month for a ₹5,000 pension at age 40. Contributions are made monthly, quarterly, or half-yearly through auto-debit from the subscriber's bank account.
application_process: 1. Visit a bank branch or post office where you hold a savings account. 2. Fill out the APY registration form available at the branch or download it from the NSDL-CRA or PFRDA website. 3. Provide your savings bank account details and Aadhaar number for authentication. 4. Choose the desired monthly pension amount (₹1,000 to ₹5,000) based on which the contribution amount is calculated. 5. Submit the completed form along with a copy of your Aadhaar card. 6. Authorize auto-debit of the monthly contribution from your savings bank account. 7. Receive confirmation of enrollment and a Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN).
deadlines: Rolling basis — subscriptions are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)

overview: NEDFi (North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Limited) is a public financial institution established to provide financial assistance and support to micro, small, medium, and large enterprises in the North Eastern Region of India. It offers a range of loan products including project finance, working capital loans, loans for women entrepreneurs, artisans, doctors, professionals, and specialized sectors like tea industry. NEDFi also acts as the nodal agency for disbursing Government of India subsidies and incentives in the region under schemes such as NEIIPP 2007 and NEIDS 2017, and provides consultancy, advisory, and capacity-building services.
target_beneficiaries: startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST; MSME; agri-startups; artisans; doctors; professionals; micro finance institutes
geographic_scope: North Eastern Region of India (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura)
eligibility: Eligibility varies by loan product but generally includes: entities such as sole proprietors, partnership firms, LLPs, private Ltd. companies; businesses must be based in the North Eastern Region; satisfactory credit history; for specific loans: women entrepreneurs (aged 18-50, skilled, in manufacturing/services), doctors (qualified MBBS/BAMS/BDS/BHMS/BUMS), professionals (CAs, CS, architects, etc. with 2+ years experience), artisans (registered/unregistered, no existing bank loans), MFIs (regulated, RBI-compliant, 3+ years existence, NE-based), and projects under subsidy-linked schemes must have subsidy receivables from competent authorities (e.g., NEIIPP 2007, NEIDS 2017).
benefits: Financial benefits include term loans up to 2 Cr for doctors, 50 Lakhs for professionals, 3 Cr for tea industry, 1 Lakh for artisans, up to 90% of liquid security value, up to 75% of project cost for MSME/business loans, up to 66.67% for tea units, up to 85% for artisans, up to 50% of subsidy receivable for short-term subsidy loans. Non-financial benefits: advisory & consultancy services (financial, capacity building, transaction & bid, infrastructure, strategy, operations, monitoring & evaluation, program management), skill development studies, market linkage via NEDFi Haat and NE-SHILP, business facilitation model, and support for MSME revitalization and cluster development.
financial_support: NEDFi provides term loans and short-term loans with interest rates starting from 6% p.a. (for artisans) to 12.25% p.a. (for MFIs), processing fees ranging from 0.5% to 1% + GST, repayment periods from 12 to 84 months, and moratorium periods up to 12 months. Loan amounts are typically a percentage of project cost or security value (e.g., 75% of project cost for MSME loans, 90% of liquid security, 50% of subsidy receivable). Funding is disbursed after due diligence, documentation verification, and sanction by appropriate credit committees. Security includes hypothecation of assets, personal/corporate guarantees, and lien on subsidy receivables or liquid securities.
application_process: 1. Identify the suitable loan product based on business type and needs. 2. Visit the NEDFi website or nearest branch to access the loan application form. 3. Fill out the application form with details of the entity, promoters, and project. 4. Gather required documents including KYC (identity, address), business proof (trade license, MOA, AOA, GST, ITR), and project-specific documents. 5. Submit the application along with documents to NEDFi (online or at branch). 6. NEDFi officials conduct due diligence and verification of submitted information. 7. Application is forwarded to the appropriate sanctioning authority (e.g., Branch Credit Committee, Corporate Credit Committee). 8. Upon approval, a sanction letter is issued with terms and conditions. 9. Complete security creation and documentation as per sanction terms. 10. Loan is disbursed to the borrower’s account post-fulfillment of all conditions.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Limited (NEDFi)
contact_details: Helpline: 0361-222-2200 | Email: mail@nedfi.com | Head Office: NEDFi House, G. S. Road, Dispur, Guwahati, Assam - 781006

overview: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is an accident insurance scheme offering accidental death and disability cover for death or disability on account of an accident. It provides a one-year cover, renewable from year to year, and is administered through Public Sector General Insurance Companies (PSGICs) and other general insurance companies with necessary approvals and tie-ups with banks/post offices. The scheme offers financial protection to account holders in the age group of 18 to 70 years through auto-debit of premium from their bank/post office accounts.
eligibility: Individual bank/Post office account holders of participating banks/Post office aged between 18 years (completed) and 70 years (age nearer birthday) who give their consent to join/enable auto-debit, as per the above modality, will be enrolled into the scheme.
benefits: As per the following table: Table of Benefits Sum Insured a Death Rs. 2 Lakh b Total and irrecoverable loss of both eyes or loss of use of both hands or feet or loss of sight of one eye and loss of use of hand or foot Rs. 2 Lakh c Total and irrecoverable loss of sight of one eye or loss of use of one hand or foot Rs. 1 Lakh
financial_support: Premium: Rs. 20/- per annum per member. The premium will be deducted from the account holder’s bank/Post office account through ‘auto debit’ facility in one instalment on or before 1st June of each annual coverage period under the scheme. However, in cases where auto debit takes place after 1st June, the cover shall commence from the date of auto debit of premium by Bank/Post office. The premium would be reviewed based on annual claims experience.
application_process: 1. Ensure you have an individual bank or Post office account in a participating bank/Post office. 2. Be within the age group of 18 to 70 years (completed 18 years, age nearer birthday not exceeding 70). 3. Give consent to join the scheme and enable auto-debit facility. 4. Visit your bank/Post office branch or use their digital channels to enrol. 5. Fill the enrolment form and provide auto-debit authorization. 6. Submit the form and ensure the premium of Rs. 20/- is deducted annually via auto-debit. 7. Enrolment must be completed by 31st May each year for coverage from 1st June to 31st May. 8. For delayed enrolment after 31st May, cover starts from the date of auto-debit of premium.
deadlines: Enrolment/auto-debit option must be given by 31st May of every year for coverage from 1st June to 31st May. Joining subsequently on payment of full annual premium is possible.
implementing_agency: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance

overview: Atal Tinkering Labs (ATL) is an initiative under the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) by NITI Aayog to foster curiosity, creativity, and imagination in young minds by establishing tinkering labs in schools across India. The program aims to inculcate skills such as design mindset, computational thinking, adaptive learning, and physical computing among students from grades 6 to 12. ATL provides a workspace where students can shape their ideas through hands-on do-it-yourself mode and learn innovation skills.
target_beneficiaries: schools; students
eligibility: Schools (Government, Government-aided, or private) seeking to establish an Atal Tinkering Lab must apply through the online application portal. Eligible institutions include those managed by Government, local bodies, or private trusts/societies. The school must have minimum required infrastructure and commit to running the lab for at least 3-4 hours per week beyond regular school hours.
benefits: Selected schools receive grant-in-aid for establishment and operation of ATL, including one-time establishment charge of up to INR 10 lakh and operational expenses of up to INR 10 lakh for a maximum period of 5 years. Schools also get access to mentorship, training programs, innovation challenges, and opportunities to participate in national-level exhibitions and competitions.
financial_support: Financial support includes a one-time establishment grant of up to INR 10,00,000 (INR 10 lakh) for setting up the lab with equipment, tools, and consumables, plus operational expenses of up to INR 10,00,000 (INR 10 lakh) spread over a maximum of 5 years (INR 2 lakh per annum). The grant is released in installments based on milestones and utilization reports submitted by the school.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 20 Lakhs (INR 10 lakh establishment + INR 10 lakh operational over 5 years)
application_process: 1. Visit the official ATL application portal at https://aim.gov.in/atl 2. Register the school by filling in basic details such as school name, address, contact information, and UDISE code 3. Fill out the online application form with details about infrastructure, faculty, and commitment to run the lab 4. Upload required documents including school registration certificate, UDISE details, and photographs of proposed lab space 5. Submit the application and await evaluation by the AIM selection committee 6. If selected, sign the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) and receive grant disbursement in phases
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and periodic review cycles.
implementing_agency: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog

overview: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) is a small savings scheme launched by the Government of India under the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign to promote the welfare of the girl child. It encourages parents or legal guardians to build a fund for the future education and marriage expenses of their girl child. The scheme offers attractive interest rates, tax benefits under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, and a long-term savings instrument with a maturity period of 21 years from the date of account opening or upon marriage after the age of 18.
target_beneficiaries: girl child
eligibility: The account can be opened by the parents or legal guardians of a girl child who is a resident Indian citizen and has not attained the age of 10 years. Only one account can be opened per girl child, and a maximum of two accounts can be opened by a family for two different girl children (third account allowed only in case of twin girls or triplets as second birth).
benefits: The scheme offers a high rate of interest (revised quarterly by the Government of India), income tax benefits under Section 80C on the amount deposited, interest earned, and maturity proceeds (EEE status). The account can be transferred anywhere in India. Partial withdrawal is allowed for higher education of the account holder after she attains the age of 18 years. The account matures after 21 years from the date of opening or upon marriage after the age of 18.
financial_support: Minimum deposit of INR 250 and maximum of INR 1.5 lakh per financial year. Deposits can be made in multiples of INR 50. The interest rate is compounded annually and notified by the Government of India each financial year. The amount invested, interest accrued, and maturity proceeds are exempt from income tax under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
application_process: 1. Visit a participating bank or India Post office. 2. Obtain the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account opening form. 3. Fill in the required details of the guardian and the girl child. 4. Submit the form along with the required documents. 5. Make the initial deposit (minimum INR 250). 6. Collect the passbook or account details after successful account opening.
deadlines: Rolling basis — accounts can be opened any time during the financial year as long as the girl child is below 10 years of age.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Finance, Government of India

overview: Mission Innovation India is a national initiative under the Department of Science and Technology (DST) aimed at accelerating clean energy innovation through public-private partnerships, research funding, and technology demonstration projects. It aligns with the global Mission Innovation framework to double governmental clean energy R&D investment over five years. The scheme supports startups, researchers, and industry in developing scalable solutions for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and carbon capture.
target_beneficiaries: startups; researchers; industry; academic institutions
eligibility: Eligible applicants include Indian startups, MSMEs, academic institutions, research organizations, and industry partners working on innovative clean energy technologies. Projects must align with national clean energy goals and demonstrate potential for scalability and impact.
benefits: Financial support for R&D and pilot projects, access to testing and validation facilities, mentorship from experts, opportunities for international collaboration, and facilitation of technology transfer and commercialization.
financial_support: Funding is provided as grants for research, development, and demonstration projects, with quantum varying based on project scope and stage. Support may cover up to 100% of project costs for academic and research institutions, and up to 50% for industry partners, disbursed in milestones.
application_process: 1. Identify a relevant technology challenge or innovation gap in clean energy. 2. Develop a project proposal aligned with Mission Innovation India’s thematic areas. 3. Submit the proposal through the designated online portal or via the Department of Science and Technology. 4. Proposals undergo technical and expert review. 5. Selected projects are approved for funding and monitoring. 6. Funds are released in stages based on project progress.
implementing_agency: Department of India

overview: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is a National Mission for Financial Inclusion launched by the Government of India to ensure universal access to banking facilities, with at least one basic banking account for every household. The scheme provides access to savings, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension services, and promotes financial literacy and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) of government subsidies. It aims to bring the unbanked population into the formal financial system through the use of technology, RuPay debit cards, and banking correspondents.
target_beneficiaries: households; unbanked adults; rural population; urban population; women; small and marginal farmers; labourers
eligibility: The scheme is open to all individuals, with a focus on providing at least one basic banking account per household. There are no specific eligibility criteria based on income, age, or occupation for opening a Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA) under PMJDY. Individuals without any valid government-issued documents can open a 'small account' by self-attesting their photograph and affixing thumb impression or signature in the presence of a bank official.
benefits: Beneficiaries receive a RuPay Debit card with inbuilt accident insurance cover of Rs. 1 lakh (raised to Rs. 2 lakh for new accounts opened after 28.8.18), access to credit through overdraft facility of up to Rs. 10,000 after six months of satisfactory account operation, access to micro-insurance and pension schemes like Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), and Atal Pension Yojana (APY), financial literacy programmes, and seamless transfer of government subsidies via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Accounts have no minimum balance requirement and earn interest at prevailing savings bank rates.
financial_support: Under PMJDY, account holders are eligible for an overdraft (OD) facility of up to Rs. 10,000 after six months of satisfactory operation of the account. For OD up to Rs. 2,000, no conditions are attached. The age limit for availing OD facility has been revised from 18-60 years to 18-65 years. The OD facility is subject to the account holder maintaining satisfactory transaction history and having an Aadhaar number linked to the account (declaration required if Aadhaar is not available). Interest on OD is charged at the base rate + 2% or 12%, whichever is lower.
application_process: 1. Visit the nearest bank branch or Bank Mitra (Business Correspondent) outlet. 2. If Aadhaar card/number is available, no other documents are required; if address has changed, self-attestation of current address is sufficient. 3. If Aadhaar is not available, submit any one of the following officially valid documents (OVD): voter ID, driving licence, PAN card, passport, or NREGA card. If these documents do not contain address, they can still serve as proof of identity and address together. 4. If no officially valid documents are available, the bank may open a 'small account' based on self-attested photograph and thumb impression/signature in the presence of a bank official, subject to certain transaction limits. 5. The account will be opened and a RuPay Debit card issued, which can be used immediately for transactions.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Accounts can be opened throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

overview: The Smart Cities Mission is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Government of India to promote sustainable and inclusive urban development by transforming 100 cities into smart cities through the application of smart solutions. The mission focuses on core infrastructure, clean and sustainable environment, and smart technology applications to improve quality of life and drive economic growth.
target_beneficiaries: urban local bodies; state governments; municipal corporations
eligibility: Cities are selected through a competitive challenge process where states nominate cities based on predefined criteria including urban population, presence of municipal corporation, and readiness for reform. Selected cities must prepare a Smart City Proposal (SCP) detailing vision, plan for area-based development and pan-city initiatives, and financial sustainability.
benefits: Selected cities receive central financial support of INR 100 crore per city over five years, matched by equal contribution from state/ULB. Benefits include improved urban infrastructure (water supply, sanitation, mobility), enhanced service delivery through technology, increased investment, job creation, and better quality of life for residents.
financial_support: The mission provides central financial assistance of INR 100 crore per selected smart city, distributed as INR 50 crore in the first year and INR 10 crore each year for the next four years. This is required to be matched by an equal contribution from the respective state government and urban local body (ULB), resulting in a total of INR 200 crore per city. Funds are released in installments based on achievement of milestones and submission of utilization certificates.
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 100 crore central assistance per city (matched by state/ULB for total INR 200 crore)
application_process: 1. States nominate cities for participation in the Smart Cities Challenge based on set criteria. 2. Nominated cities prepare Smart City Proposals (SCPs) detailing vision, area-based development, pan-city initiatives, and financial plan. 3. SCPs are evaluated by a national-level committee through a competitive challenge process. 4. Selected cities are announced and must incorporate a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for implementation. 5. SPVs implement projects as per the SCP and submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates for fund release.
deadlines: Challenge-based selection with periodic rounds; no rolling deadline. Specific timelines announced for each challenge round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCFSC)
Faster Adoption of Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles (FAME)
overview: Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles (FAME) is a Government of India scheme aimed at promoting electric mobility by providing financial incentives for the adoption of hybrid and electric vehicles. The scheme supports the development of charging infrastructure and encourages domestic manufacturing of electric vehicles and their components. FAME-II, the current phase, focuses on incentivizing electric buses, three-wheelers, four-wheelers used for public transport or registered for commercial purposes, and two-wheelers. It also aims to create demand for electric vehicles through upfront incentives and to establish a robust charging ecosystem.
target_beneficiaries: public transport operators; fleet operators; institutional buyers; individual consumers; manufacturers
eligibility: Eligibility varies by vehicle segment: for electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, and four-wheelers, vehicles must be approved by the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) or other designated testing agencies and meet specified performance and localization criteria. For electric buses and trucks, eligibility is restricted to vehicles used for public transport or commercial purposes. Manufacturers must be registered under FAME-II and their models must be on the approved list. Individual beneficiaries must purchase vehicles from OEMs enrolled under the scheme.
benefits: Upfront incentive at the point of purchase for eligible electric vehicles; support for setting up charging infrastructure; promotion of domestic manufacturing through localization requirements; reduction in operating costs due to lower electricity and maintenance expenses; contribution to environmental sustainability by reducing tailpipe emissions.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as a direct subsidy to buyers of eligible electric vehicles, disbursed to manufacturers who then pass on the benefit to consumers. The incentive amount varies by vehicle category and is based on battery capacity. For charging infrastructure, subsidies are provided to government entities, public sector undertakings, and private players for setting up charging stations. The scheme operates through a reimbursement model where OEMs claim incentives after selling eligible vehicles.
grant_amount_per_entity: Incentives range from INR 10,000 per kWh for two-wheelers (up to 15 kWh), INR 20,000 per kWh for three-wheelers (up to 10 kWh), INR 10,000 per kWh for four-wheelers (up to 15 kWh), and up to INR 20 lakhs per electric bus (for buses above 12 meters).
application_process: 1. OEMs must register their eligible vehicle models on the FAME-II portal after obtaining ARAI certification. 2. Manufacturers submit monthly claims for incentives based on vehicles sold. 3. Claims are verified by the implementing agency. 4. Upon approval, funds are disbursed to the manufacturer’s account. 5. End consumers benefit through reduced ex-showroom prices at the time of purchase.
deadlines: The scheme is valid until March 31, 2024, or until the exhaustion of funds, whichever occurs earlier.
implementing_agency: Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises

overview: The NSTEDB Entrepreneurship Awareness Camps scheme is part of the National Science and Technology Entrepreneurship Development Board (NSTEDB) under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), aimed at promoting entrepreneurship awareness among students and youth. The scheme focuses on creating awareness about entrepreneurship as a career option, fostering innovation, and encouraging the establishment of startups and small enterprises. It targets students and youth in educational institutions to sensitize them about entrepreneurial opportunities and support mechanisms available through government schemes.
target_beneficiaries: students; youth; educational institutions
eligibility: Educational institutions such as universities, colleges, polytechnics, and technical institutions are eligible to organize Entrepreneurship Awareness Camps under NSTEDB. The institutions must have the necessary infrastructure and faculty to conduct such programs. Preference may be given to institutions in backward regions or those serving underrepresented groups.
benefits: Financial support for organizing Entrepreneurship Awareness Camps, including honorarium for resource persons, honorarium for coordinators, TA/DA for participants, printing of study materials, venue expenses, and other incidental expenses. The scheme also provides access to expert resource persons, networking opportunities with industry and financial institutions, and exposure to government schemes for entrepreneurship support.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as a grant-in-aid to educational institutions for organizing Entrepreneurship Awareness Camps. The quantum of support covers expenses such as honorarium for resource persons and coordinators, TA/DA for participants, printing of study materials, venue expenses, and other incidental costs. The exact amount varies based on the scale and duration of the camp, subject to NSTEDB guidelines.
application_process: 1. Educational institutions interested in organizing Entrepreneurship Awareness Camps must submit a proposal to NSTEDB, DST. 2. The proposal should include details such as objectives, target audience, duration, resource persons, budget estimate, and expected outcomes. 3. Proposals are evaluated by NSTEDB based on feasibility, relevance, and alignment with scheme objectives. 4. Approved proposals receive financial sanction and guidelines for implementation. 5. Institutions conduct the camp as per the approved plan and submit utilization certificates and reports to NSTEDB post-completion.
implementing_agency: National Science and Technology Entrepreneurship Development Board (NSTEDB), Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology

overview: The KDEM Elevate Programme is a state-level initiative by the Karnataka government to support and nurture startups through financial assistance, mentorship, and market access. It aims to identify high-potential early-stage startups and provide them with seed funding and incubation support to scale their operations. The programme focuses on innovation-driven enterprises across sectors and offers a structured pathway from idea to market readiness. Selected startups receive grants, mentorship, and access to networking opportunities to enhance their growth trajectory.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups must be registered in Karnataka, have a minimum viable product (MVP) or prototype, be incorporated as a Private Limited Company, LLP, or Partnership Firm, and not have received more than INR 50 lakh in funding prior to application. The startup should be working on an innovative product, service, or process with scalability potential.
benefits: Selected startups receive a grant of up to INR 50 lakh, access to mentorship from domain experts, incubation support at recognized centers, assistance in fundraising, and opportunities to participate in investor meets and demo days. The programme also provides legal, accounting, and technical support to help startups comply with regulatory requirements and improve operational efficiency.
financial_support: The programme offers a one-time grant of up to INR 50 lakh per selected startup, disbursed in tranches based on milestone achievement. The funds are intended for product development, market validation, team building, and initial operational expenses. There is no equity dilution or repayment obligation associated with the grant.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 50 lakh
application_process: 1. Visit the official Elevate Karnataka portal at https://elevate.karnataka.gov.in 2. Register on the portal by creating a login using email and mobile number 3. Fill in the online application form with details about the startup, founders, product, and traction 4. Upload required documents including incorporation certificate, product details, and team profiles 5. Submit the application and await screening by the evaluation committee 6. Shortlisted startups will be invited for a pitch presentation or interview 7. Final selection is based on innovation, scalability, team strength, and market potential 8. Selected startups will receive a grant disbursement letter and further instructions for fund utilization
deadlines: Applications are accepted in periodic cycles; specific dates are announced on the portal. Interested startups are advised to check the website regularly for upcoming application windows.
implementing_agency: Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM)

overview: Maharashtra State Innovation Society (MSInS) is a nodal agency established by the Government of Maharashtra to promote innovation, entrepreneurship, and startup ecosystem development across the state. It operates under the Directorate of Industries and implements various schemes to support startups, MSMEs, and innovators through funding, mentorship, infrastructure, and policy advocacy. The society aims to position Maharashtra as a leading innovation hub in India by fostering collaboration between academia, industry, and government.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; entrepreneurs; innovators
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include startups registered in Maharashtra, MSMEs, individual innovators, academic institutions, and industry partners engaged in innovative activities. Specific eligibility criteria vary by scheme and are defined under individual programs implemented by MSInS.
benefits: Benefits include financial support through grants and seed funding, access to incubation infrastructure, mentorship from industry experts, assistance in intellectual property rights (IPR) filing, market linkage support, participation in investor meets and demo days, and facilitation of partnerships with corporates and government bodies.
financial_support: Financial support varies across schemes and includes seed funding up to INR 50 lakhs for early-stage startups, grants for proof-of-concept and prototype development, and matching grants under specific innovation challenges. The exact quantum and mechanism depend on the particular program being applied for under MSInS.
application_process: 1. Visit the official Maharashtra State Innovation Society website at https://maha-innovation.in 2. Navigate to the 'Schemes' or 'Apply' section to review available programs 3. Select the relevant scheme based on eligibility and innovation domain 4. Read the detailed guidelines and eligibility criteria for the chosen scheme 5. Prepare the required documents as specified 6. Fill out the online application form with accurate details 7. Upload all supporting documents in the prescribed format 8. Submit the application and note the application ID for tracking 9. Await review and communication from MSInS regarding evaluation and next steps
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to scheme-specific announcements and availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Maharashtra State Innovation Society (MSInS), Directorate of Industries, Government of Maharashtra

overview: The Maha Startup Scheme is a state-level initiative by the Government of Maharashtra to foster innovation and support early-stage startups within the state. It aims to provide financial assistance, mentorship, and infrastructure support to promote entrepreneurship and job creation. The scheme focuses on startups in technology, manufacturing, and service sectors, with special emphasis on women entrepreneurs and socially disadvantaged groups. It operates through a structured application and evaluation process to disburse grants and enable access to incubation facilities.
target_beneficiaries: startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST; MSME
eligibility: The applicant must be a startup registered in Maharashtra as a Private Limited Company, LLP, or Partnership Firm under the Companies Act, 2013 or LLP Act, 2008. The startup must be incorporated not more than 5 years ago. Annual turnover should not exceed INR 25 Crore in any preceding financial year. The startup must be working on innovative products, services, or processes with potential for commercialization. At least one founder must be a resident of Maharashtra. Preference is given to startups led by women, SC/ST, or differently abled individuals.
benefits: Financial grant support for product development, prototype creation, and market validation. Access to state-approved incubation centers with infrastructure, mentorship, and networking opportunities. Assistance in intellectual property rights (IPR) filing and legal compliance. Support for participation in national and international startup events and exhibitions. Guidance on funding readiness and investor connect. Access to shared labs, prototyping facilities, and technical guidance through empanelled knowledge partners.
financial_support: The scheme provides a one-time grant of up to INR 20 Lakhs per eligible startup for early-stage validation and prototype development. The grant is disbursed in tranches based on milestone achievement, subject to technical and financial appraisal by the appointed committee. Funds are released directly to the startup’s bank account after due diligence and approval of utilization reports. No equity is taken by the government in return for the grant.
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 20 Lakhs
application_process: 1. Visit the official Maha Startup Scheme portal at https://startup.maharashtra.gov.in. 2. Register as a new user by providing basic details of the startup and founders. 3. Log in and fill the online application form with information on innovation, business model, and financials. 4. Upload required documents including Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, pitch deck, and founder details. 5. Submit the application for preliminary screening. 6. Shortlisted applicants will be invited for a pitch presentation before the evaluation committee. 7. Based on the evaluation, approved startups will receive a sanction letter. 8. Grant disbursement will commence after submission of utilization plan and execution of agreement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Directorate of Industries, Government of Maharashtra

overview: National Innovation Foundation (NIF)

The EDII Tamil Nadu Incubation Scheme is a state-level initiative aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship by providing incubation support to early-stage startups in Tamil Nadu. The scheme offers mentorship, infrastructure, and guidance to help startups validate their ideas and scale operations. It is implemented by the Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India (EDII) Tamil Nadu chapter, leveraging its expertise in entrepreneurial development.
target_beneficiaries: startups; early-stage entrepreneurs
eligibility: Startups incorporated in Tamil Nadu with a viable innovative idea or prototype, preferably in early stages (pre-revenue or early revenue), led by entrepreneurs committed to building scalable ventures.
benefits: Access to incubation infrastructure, mentorship from industry experts and academics, networking with investors and peers, guidance on business modeling, legal compliance, and fundraising, and support in prototype development and market validation.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or seed funding; support is primarily non-financial in nature, focusing on mentorship, infrastructure, and advisory services.
application_process: 1. Visit the official EDII Tamil Nadu website or incubation portal. 2. Fill out the online application form with details about the startup idea, team, and stage. 3. Submit required documents including incorporation proof, pitch deck, and founder profiles. 4. Await screening by the EDII selection committee. 5. Shortlisted candidates are invited for a pitch or interview. 6. Selected startups are formally onboarded into the incubation program.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India (EDII), Tamil Nadu Chapter

overview: The Karnataka Startup Policy is a state-level initiative launched by the Government of Karnataka to foster innovation and entrepreneurship within the state. It aims to create a conducive ecosystem for startups by providing financial incentives, infrastructure support, regulatory simplification, and access to markets and mentorship. The policy focuses on sector-agnostic growth with special emphasis on technology-driven and social impact startups. It operates under the Department of IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka.
target_beneficiaries: startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST entrepreneurs; differently abled entrepreneurs; rural startups; social enterprises
eligibility: Startups incorporated as Private Limited Company, LLP, or Partnership Firm under Indian laws, having their primary place of business in Karnataka, recognized by DPIIT or certified by the Karnataka State Startup Committee, working on innovative products, services, or processes with potential for scalability and employment generation, and not formed by splitting up or reconstruction of an existing business.
benefits: Financial support through seed funding, marketing assistance, and reimbursement of patent and certification costs; non-financial benefits include access to incubation centers, mentorship from industry experts, participation in national and international startup events, priority in government procurement, access to shared infrastructure and labs, regulatory facilitation through single-window clearance, and assistance in fundraising and investor connect.
financial_support: The policy provides seed support of up to INR 50 lakhs per startup in the form of grant or convertible debt, reimbursement of up to INR 2 lakhs for patent filing and INR 1 lakh for certification costs, marketing assistance of up to INR 5 lakhs for participation in approved events, and monthly operational support of INR 1 lakh per month for up to 12 months for startups in recognized incubators. Financial assistance is disbursed through nodal agencies and incubators after due diligence checks.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 50 lakhs as seed support per startup
application_process: 1. Register the startup on the Karnataka Startup Cell portal (startup.karnataka.gov.in). 2. Obtain DPIIT recognition or certification from the Karnataka State Startup Committee. 3. Apply for specific benefits (seed funding, marketing, patent reimbursement, etc.) through the online portal. 4. Submit required documents including incorporation certificate, DPIIT recognition, business plan, and financial projections. 5. Application is reviewed by the Karnataka State Startup Committee or designated nodal agency. 6. Upon approval, enter into an agreement and submit bank details for disbursement. 7. Funds are released in tranches based on milestones or as per the scheme guidelines.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Department of IT, BT and S&T, Government of Karnataka

overview: The Green India Mission (GIM) is one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) launched by the Government of India. It aims to protect, restore, and enhance India's forest cover and respond to climate change through a combination of adaptation and mitigation measures. The mission focuses on increasing forest/tree cover on 5 million hectares of forest/non-forest lands and improving the quality of forest cover on another 5 million hectares. It emphasizes ecosystem services, biodiversity conservation, and livelihood improvement for forest-dependent communities.
target_beneficiaries: forest-dependent communities; local communities; Panchayati Raj Institutions; Joint Forest Management Committees; NGOs; state forest departments
eligibility: The mission is implemented through State Forest Departments and other designated agencies. Eligible entities include Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs), Village Forest Committees (VFCs), Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), NGOs, and local communities engaged in afforestation, reforestation, and forest conservation activities on forest and non-forest lands as per approved plans under the mission.
benefits: Financial support for afforestation, reforestation, and eco-restoration activities; capacity building and training for stakeholders; improved livelihood opportunities through non-timber forest produce and eco-tourism; enhanced ecosystem services such as water conservation, soil erosion control, and biodiversity conservation; and contribution to national climate change goals through carbon sequestration.
financial_support: The mission provides financial assistance in the form of grants to state forest departments and implementing agencies for undertaking afforestation, reforestation, and eco-restoration activities. Funds are released based on approved Annual Plans of Operations (APOs) and utilization certificates. The financial support covers costs related to plantation, maintenance, soil and moisture conservation, and community mobilization.
application_process: 1. State Forest Departments prepare Annual Plans of Operations (APOs) based on the perspective plan under GIM. 2. APOs are submitted to the National Mission Authority for appraisal and approval. 3. Upon approval, funds are released in installments to the states. 4. States implement the projects through Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs), Village Forest Committees (VFCs), and other local institutions. 5. Progress is monitored through periodic reporting and field visits. 6. Utilization certificates and audited statements are submitted for subsequent fund releases.
deadlines: Annual planning cycle — APOs are typically submitted before the start of each financial year for approval.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC)

scheme_name: UP MSME and Export Promotion Council Schemes
overview: The UP MSME and Export Promotion Council Schemes, administered by the Uttar Pradesh government, aim to support micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and promote exports from the state. The scheme provides financial assistance, infrastructure support, and market access initiatives to enhance competitiveness and growth of MSMEs in Uttar Pradesh. It focuses on strengthening the industrial base, encouraging technology adoption, and facilitating integration into domestic and global value chains.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include micro, small, and medium enterprises as defined under the MSMED Act, 2006, having their registered office or operational unit in Uttar Pradesh. Enterprises must be engaged in manufacturing or service activities and possess valid Udyam Registration. Specific sub-schemes may have additional criteria related to export turnover, investment in plant and machinery, or sector-specific focus.
benefits: Benefits include capital subsidy for plant and machinery, interest subsidy on term loans, reimbursement of ISO certification costs, support for patent registration, assistance for participation in trade fairs, market development aid, infrastructure support through cluster development programs, and skill training initiatives. Financial incentives are provided as per the norms of individual sub-schemes under the council.
financial_support: Financial support varies across sub-schemes and includes capital subsidy up to a certain percentage of investment in plant and machinery, interest subsidy on bank loans, and reimbursement of expenses for quality certification and export promotion activities. The exact quantum and mechanism depend on the specific scheme under the UP MSME and Export Promotion Council, with disbursement typically made through designated nodal agencies or banks after verification of claims.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant sub-scheme under UP MSME and Export Promotion Council based on enterprise needs. 2. Ensure eligibility and obtain Udyam Registration. 3. Prepare the required documents as per the sub-scheme guidelines. 4. Submit the application either online through the designated portal or offline to the concerned district industry center or nodal agency. 5. Application undergoes scrutiny and verification by the implementing agency. 6. Upon approval, financial assistance is disbursed as per the scheme norms, either directly to the beneficiary or through the lending institution.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Uttar Pradesh MSME and Export Promotion Council

scheme_name: UP Startup Policy & One District One Product (ODOP)
overview: The UP Startup Policy & One District One Product (ODOP) is a state-level initiative by the Government of Uttar Pradesh aimed at fostering entrepreneurship, promoting local products, and building a robust startup ecosystem across all districts of the state. It integrates financial support, incubation, market access, and skill development to empower startups and artisans, particularly those engaged in ODOP-identified products. The policy emphasizes inclusive growth by targeting women, SC/ST, and rural entrepreneurs, and aligns with central government schemes like Startup India and Stand-Up India.
target_beneficiaries: startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST; MSME; agri-startups; artisans; rural entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include startups registered in Uttar Pradesh, MSMEs, artisans, self-help groups, and individuals engaged in ODOP-identified products. Preference is given to women, SC/ST, and rural entrepreneurs. Startups must be recognized by DPIIT or registered under the UP Startup Policy. Entities must have a viable business plan related to ODOP products or services and comply with state government guidelines.
benefits: Benefits include financial grants up to INR 10 lakhs for product development, marketing, and certification; interest-free loans; seed funding; incubation support at state-approved incubators; mentorship from industry experts; assistance in patent filing and IPR; participation in national and international trade fairs; e-commerce platform integration; branding and packaging support; and access to raw material banks and common facility centers.
financial_support: Financial support includes grants of up to INR 10 lakhs per entity for product development, certification, and market promotion; interest-free loans up to INR 25 lakhs for working capital and machinery; seed funding of up to INR 5 lakhs for idea validation; and reimbursement of up to 50% of costs for ISO, FSSAI, or other certifications. Funds are disbursed through the Uttar Pradesh Trade Promotion Authority (UPTPA) or designated nodal agencies after project appraisal.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 10 lakhs
application_process: 1. Visit the official UP Startup Policy portal at startup.up.gov.in. 2. Register as a beneficiary by filling the online application form. 3. Submit details of the business idea, ODOP product linkage, and required documents. 4. Await preliminary screening by the district-level committee. 5. Present the business plan before the state-level evaluation committee. 6. Receive approval and sanction letter. 7. Submit utilization reports and claim disbursement of funds as per milestones.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Uttar Pradesh Trade Promotion Authority (UPTPA), under the Department of Infrastructure and Industrial Development, Government of Uttar Pradesh

overview: The MNRE Off-grid Solar Power Schemes support decentralized solar energy solutions for areas without reliable grid access. These schemes aim to promote solar electrification in rural and remote regions through financial assistance and implementation support. They focus on standalone solar systems, solar pumps, and other off-grid applications to enhance energy access and sustainability.
target_beneficiaries: rural households; farmers; remote communities; off-grid areas
eligibility: Beneficiaries include individuals, farmers, cooperatives, panchayats, and government institutions in off-grid or poorly electrified areas. Systems must comply with MNRE technical standards and be installed by authorized channel partners. Priority is given to SC/ST, women, and border regions.
benefits: Financial subsidies for solar home lights, solar street lights, solar pumps, and mini-grids; reduced electricity costs; reliable power supply; environmental benefits through reduced emissions; and support for agricultural productivity via solar-powered irrigation.
financial_support: Central Financial Assistance (CFA) is provided as a subsidy ranging from 30% to 90% of the benchmark cost, depending on beneficiary category and region (e.g., higher for NE/hilly/island areas). Funds are disbursed through State Nodal Agencies or implementing agencies after installation and inspection.
application_process: 1. Identify eligible off-grid solar system (home light, street light, pump, etc.) 2. Contact State Nodal Agency or authorized channel partner 3. Submit application with required documents 4. System installed by authorized vendor 5. Inspection by concerned authority 6. Subsidy disbursed to beneficiary or vendor
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)

overview: AP Innovation Society & APEX Incubation is a state-level initiative by the Government of Andhra Pradesh aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship through incubation support, mentorship, and infrastructure for startups and innovators across the state. The program operates under the AP Innovation Society and focuses on nurturing early-stage ventures by providing access to incubation centers, technical guidance, and networking opportunities. It seeks to strengthen the entrepreneurial ecosystem in Andhra Pradesh by supporting innovation-driven enterprises in key sectors.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; innovators

overview: The National Clean Energy Fund (NCEF) is not explicitly mentioned in the provided evidence. The evidence primarily discusses the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects, which has a financial outlay of Rs. 37,500 crore and aims to promote coal gasification for energy security and import substitution. No details about NCEF's objectives, beneficiaries, or structure are present in the scraped content.
eligibility: The financial incentive under this Scheme shall be available to applicants which are either Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs); or private sector companies; or joint ventures (JVs); or consortiums (not exceeding 3 companies). The financial incentive under the Scheme shall be available only to entities who will undertake to set-up new surface coal/lignite gasification projects. Any expenditure made prior to the approval of the Scheme shall not be considered for incentive. Only those projects wherein net worth of the applicant is more than 20% of the total project cost, are eligible under the Scheme and shall be considered for further evaluation. The minimum plant capacity of a project, in terms of clean syngas shall be 0.5 MTPA (calculated based on annual plant availability of 330 days at an average clean syngas density of 1.1 kg/Nm3). The Ministry of Coal may, while issuing Request for Proposal (RFP), prescribe additional eligibility criteria.
benefits: The Scheme aims to accelerate the implementation of surface coal/lignite gasification projects through targeted financial incentive, promote Atmanirbharta by reducing import dependence on chemicals and petrochemicals (such as liquefied natural gas, urea, ammonium nitrate, ammonia, coking coal (via direct reduced iron), methanol, and di-methyl ether), enable value-added utilization of domestic coal resources, and contribute to achieving the national target of 100 MT coal gasification by 2030.
financial_support: A total financial incentive of ₹37,500 crore has been proposed under the Scheme. The Scheme shall provide financial incentive @ maximum 20% of the cost of plant and machinery (P&M), to the selected applicants. The financial incentive for any single project shall be capped at ₹5,000 crore. The financial incentive for any particular product (except urea and Synthetic Natural Gas (SNG)) across all approved projects, shall be capped at ₹9,000 crore. Any entity, including its holding, subsidiary, affiliate or associate companies, shall collectively not be eligible to receive financial incentive exceeding ₹12,000 crore under the Scheme, across all projects. In case of Joint Ventures or Consortiums, the financial incentive shall be calculated among the participating entities in proportion to their respective shareholding pattern or ownership in the project(s). The financial incentives will be disbursed in four equal instalments, linked to the achievement of specified milestones: 1st instalment (25%) upon completion of pre-implementation activities (land acquisition, grant of Environment Clearance, coal/lignite tie-up, finalization of technology licensor, finalization of EPC contractor, achievement of financial closure); 2nd instalment (25%) after disbursal of loan by the Bank/Financial Institution towards the project, 30% of the equity contribution by the project developers, and actual expenditure of 50% or more of the approved incentive amount incurred on plant and machinery; 3rd instalment (25%) on commissioning of the project; 4th instalment (25%) on achieving minimum 50% of the peak annual production capacity during the previous 365 days.
application_process: Selection/shortlisting of applicants and allocation of financial incentive shall be undertaken through a transparent and competitive bidding process, implemented through the issuance of Request for Proposal (RFP), from time to time. Evaluation criteria shall be devised by benchmarking project cost and taking into account the quantity of coal used as input and quantity of syngas produced as output. Projects shall be evaluated under a pre-defined scoring framework comprising various parameters: Viability Amount Score (30), Plant Capacity (20), Project Cost per MT of Coal (20), Technology Tie-up (10), Financial Strength/Capability (20). The scores obtained under the specified parameters of the evaluation framework shall be aggregated to arrive at a total score (out of 100), which shall form the basis for ranking of projects. Selection of projects shall be based on ranking in descending order of total score, subject to achievement of a minimum qualifying score of 40 marks and availability of funds under the overall Scheme outlay of ₹37,500 crores. Evaluation of applications submitted by applicants shall be carried out by an Evaluation Committee constituted by Ministry of Coal.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Coal

target_beneficiaries: startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST; MSME
eligibility: Startups incorporated as a Private Limited Company, Limited Liability Partnership (LLP), or Registered Partnership Firm in Delhi, with at least one founder domiciled in Delhi, working on innovative products, services, or processes, and not older than 7 years from date of incorporation. benefits: Financial support in the form of grants, reimbursement of patent and certification costs, access to subsidized incubation and co-working spaces, mentorship from industry experts, assistance in market access and government procurement, facilitation of funding linkages with investors and financial institutions, and regulatory handholding through single-window clearance.
financial_support: The policy provides a one-time grant of up to INR 10 Lakhs for product development and prototype creation, reimbursement of up to INR 2 Lakhs for patent filing and certification costs, and access to seed fund support through the Delhi Startup Seed Fund Scheme (DSSFS) for eligible startups. grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 10 Lakhs for product development; up to INR 2 Lakhs for patent/reimbursement

overview: WE Hub is a Government of Telangana initiative aimed at empowering women entrepreneurs by providing access to technical, financial, government, and policy support to start, scale, sustain, and accelerate their businesses. target_beneficiaries: women entrepreneurs; startups; MSME; students

For Project Inclusion, applicants must be registered enterprises in operation for two years with a woman holding at least 51% stake and turnover between INR 5 lakhs – 10 lakhs per annum (relaxable for Handicrafts sector). benefits: Access to business consultation, entrepreneurial and management courses, business mentorship, marketing assistance for early-stage and established startups, compliance and tax assistance, funding and financial assistance guidance, community and networking opportunities, sector-specific mentoring, skill enhancement programs, internship and live project opportunities, patenting and IP support, credit linkage, Udyam and MSME registration support, and participation in hackathons and exposure visits.
financial_support: WE Hub provides guidance and linkages to funding sources but does not directly disburse grants or loans.
