application_process: 1. Identify the suitable program based on business stage (e.g., WE Reach for pre-incubation, Project Inclusion for incubation, WE Leads for acceleration). 2. Check eligibility criteria specific to the program (e.g., geographic, turnover, stakeholding requirements). 3. Prepare required documents including business registration, PAN, pitch deck, and stakeholder details. 4. Apply via the designated email address for the program (e.g., fo-sie-wehub@telangana.gov.in for SIE programs, pm-wehub@telangana.gov.in for Project Ujaagar). 5. Await confirmation and further instructions from the WE Hub team regarding selection and onboarding.

scheme_name: iCreate – International Centre for Entrepreneurship and Technology

It operates as a public-private partnership to foster next-generation entrepreneurship by supporting tech-based startups through incubation, mentorship, funding, and market access. iCreate provides end-to-end support from idea to scale-up, including prototype development, seed funding, and accelerator programs, with a focus on sectors like EV, agritech, healthtech, and renewable energy.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; students; MSME; agri-startups; women entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligibility varies by program: For Spark-up Idea Fund, any student or team from any discipline and college can apply if the idea is implementable, commercially viable, and new or a better alternative. application_process: 1. Identify the relevant program (e.g., Spark-up Idea Fund, NIDHI-SSS, iCreate Pro-Fund Gateway, iCreate Idea Catalyst). 2. Attend final pitch or evaluation session (e.g., 16 Aug for Spark-up Idea Fund). 7. Receive final result and begin onboarding (e.g., 20 Aug for Spark-up Idea Fund). 8. Sign NDA and start working from iCreate Campus (e.g., 26 Aug for Spark-up Idea Fund).

target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; innovators

scheme_name: Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF)
overview: The Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) was established by the Government of India in 2018 to promote sustainable growth of the fisheries sector. With an allocation of over ₹7,500 crore, the fund provides long-term finance at concessional rates for the creation and modernization of fisheries and aquaculture infrastructure. As of 2024, FIDF has sanctioned 132 projects worth ₹5,794.09 crore, strengthening essential infrastructure such as fishing harbours, processing plants, cold storage, and fish seed farms.
target_beneficiaries: fishers; fish farmers; stakeholders in fisheries sector; entrepreneurs; cooperatives
eligibility: The Nucleus Breeding Centres and Broodstock Multiplication Centres shall be established for increasing production and productivity of the coastal aquaculture sector in India by any existing producers of specific pathogen free broodstock as well those involved in domestication and breeding programmes of any potential candidate species for coastal aquaculture either from India or from overseas either independently or through a joint venture with the local partner from the India. An applicant organization possesses in the requisite experience and capabilities required for establishment and operation of Nucleus Breeding Centres or Broodstock Multiplication Centres may apply in Form-F-1 either individually (as sole organisation) or as lead partner of a consortium of organisations (as lead partner) as per the extant rules, regulations and procedure in force. The Applicants shall individually or collectively possess the following technical capacity and experience, namely: (i) have successfully designed and operated a Nucleus Breeding Centres or Broodstock Multiplication Centres for Litopenaeus vannamei or any such other fish or shrimp species which has developed and maintained a minimum of 5 generations; and (ii) have successfully developed and managed a minimum of 50 families of Litopenaeus vannamei or any such other fish or shrimp species, through its own research and development activities, in the last ten years. The applicants must have been engaged in the establishment and operation of at least one Nucleus Breeding Centres or Broodstock Multiplication Centres assignment within the last five years preceding the date of application and submit details thereof.
benefits: FIDF provides long-term finance at concessional rates for the creation and modernization of fisheries and aquaculture infrastructure. It offers interest subvention up to 3% per annum for all Eligible Entities (EEs) for development of identified fisheries-based infrastructure facilities including establishment of Nucleus Breeding Centres (NBCs). The fund provides a 25% credit guarantee facility to projects of entrepreneurs, individual farmers and cooperatives approved under FIDF during the extended period of 3 years from 2023-24 to 2025-26 from the existing credit guarantee fund of Infrastructure Development Fund of Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Lending rate of interest is not lower than 5% per annum for all EEs for development of identified fisheries based infrastructure facilities. Repayment period is 12 years with moratorium of 2 years for repayment of principle amount.
financial_support: FIDF provides long-term finance at concessional rates for the creation and modernization of fisheries and aquaculture infrastructure. Interest subvention: Up to 3% per annum for all EEs for development of identified fisheries-based infrastructure facilities including establishment of Nucleus Breeding Centres (NBCs). Lending Rate of Interest: Not lower than 5% per annum for all EEs for development of identified fisheries based infrastructure facilities. Repayment period: 12 years with moratorium of 2 years for re-payment of principle amount. FIDF provides 25% credit guarantee facility to the projects of entrepreneurs, individual farmers and cooperatives to be approved under FIDF during the extended period of 3 years from 2023-24 to 2025-26 from the existing credit guarantee fund of Infrastructure Development Fund of Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
application_process: 1. Submit Expression of Interest (EOI) for establishing Nucleus Breeding Centres (NBCs) or Broodstock Multiplication Centres (BMCs) as per Form-F-1. 2. Provide company background, qualifications, methodology, technology details, and disease-free certification. 3. Shortlisted proponents must provide a 60-minute presentation covering background and experience, presence in India and seed supply chain, available germplasm, conceptual plans, layout, site selection, selective breeding strategies, biosecurity measures, technological advantages, projected economic benefits, and training plans. 4. Project Screening Committee (PSC) evaluates and recommends potential applicants. 5. Prior permission is granted by the Central Government in the Department of Fisheries based on recommendations of the Project Screening Committee within ninety days from the date of receipt of application.
deadlines: This is a rolling EOI. Sealed envelope marked to the below address, containing the proposal with all relevant documents may be submitted mentioning 'Expression of Interest for establishing Nucleus Breeding Centres (NBC) for L. vannamei in India on the top of the envelope.

scheme_name: Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU)
overview: Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) is a Central Sector Scheme administered by NCGTC that provides guarantee coverage for loans up to Rs.10 lakh sanctioned by Banks, NBFCs, MFIs, or other financial intermediaries to eligible micro units. It also covers overdraft loan amounts of Rs.10,000 sanctioned under PMJDY accounts. The scheme aims to facilitate collateral-free credit access for micro enterprises by sharing lending risk with financial institutions.
target_beneficiaries: micro units
eligibility: Eligible micro units seeking loans from Banks / NBFCs / MFIs / other financial intermediaries engaged in providing credit facilities. Overdraft loan amount of Rs.10,000 sanctioned under PMJDY accounts shall also be eligible to be covered under Credit Guarantee Fund.
benefits: Collateral-free loan access for micro units, guarantee coverage reducing lending risk for financial institutions, inclusion of PMJDY overdraft loans up to Rs.10,000, enhanced credit accessibility for underserved micro enterprises.
financial_support: The scheme provides guarantee coverage for loans up to the specified limit of Rs.10 Lakh sanctioned by Banks / NBFCs / MFIs / other financial intermediaries. Further, overdraft loan amount of Rs.10,000 sanctioned under PMJDY accounts is also eligible for coverage under the Credit Guarantee Fund.
application_process: 1. Eligible Lending Institutions (ELIs) must register with NCGTC by submitting a signed and stamped undertaking along with Board Resolution. 2. Upon successful registration, login credentials are created for the ELI on NCGTC’s portal. 3. The ELI can then apply for guarantee cover on loans extended to eligible micro units via the NCGTC portal. 4. Guarantee fee is payable monthly by the 7th day of each month for the outstanding loan amount.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Ltd (NCGTC)

overview: The Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) is a Government of India initiative launched to provide liquidity support to businesses adversely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and other crises such as the West Asia conflict. It offers 100% guarantee coverage to Banks and NBFCs on credit extended to Business Enterprises/MSMEs based on their loan outstanding as of February 29, 2020, subject to defined criteria, to meet additional term loan or working capital requirements. The scheme has evolved through multiple versions, with ECLGS 5.0 launched in May 2026 as a targeted response to the West Asia crisis. It is administered by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Ltd (NCGTC), a wholly owned entity of the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; Business Enterprises
eligibility: The scheme provides 100% guarantee coverage to Banks & NBFCs on credit extended to Business Enterprises/MSMEs on their loan outstanding as on February 29, 2020, subject to defined criteria. Eligible borrowers include Business Enterprises and MSMEs seeking additional term loan or working capital support. Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) must register with NCGTC by submitting an undertaking on stamp paper and a board resolution to avail guarantee cover under the scheme.
benefits: 100% guarantee coverage on eligible loans extended by Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) to eligible borrowers; collateral-free lending facilitated for businesses; support for business continuity and stability during periods of distress; access to working capital and term loans without requiring additional collateral; backstop for lenders to extend credit to stressed sectors with reduced risk perception.
financial_support: The scheme provides 100% guarantee coverage to Banks and NBFCs on credit extended to eligible borrowers (Business Enterprises/MSMEs) based on their loan outstanding as of February 29, 2020. The guarantee covers additional term loans or working capital loans extended by MLIs to meet liquidity needs arising from pandemic-induced distress or other crises like the West Asia situation. The financial support is channeled through banks and NBFCs, with NCGTC bearing the default risk up to the guaranteed amount.
application_process: 1. Eligible Lending Institutions (ELIs) must register with NCGTC as a Member Lending Institution (MLI) by submitting a signed and stamped undertaking on stamp paper of requisite value (to be stamped as an Agreement under the local Stamp Act) along with a copy of Board Resolution. 2. Submit the undertaking and documents to the Registered Office of NCGTC in Mumbai. 3. Upon successful registration, login credentials are created for the MLI on the NCGTC portal. 4. The MLI can then apply for guarantee cover on loans extended by it to eligible borrowers through the NCGTC portal. 5. After disbursement of the loan to the borrower, the MLI must submit a claim for guarantee cover to NCGTC. 6. Guarantee fee is payable by the MLI to the Trust by the 7th day of each month for the outstanding loan amount on the closing day of the previous month.
deadlines: ECLGS 5.0 was launched in May 2026; specific end date not mentioned in evidence. Earlier versions had end dates (e.g., ECLGS 1.0-4.0 loans to be sanctioned by 30.09.2021 and disbursed by 31.12.2021). Current operational status should be verified via official channels.

overview: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM) is a nodal agency of the Government of Kerala for entrepreneurship development and incubation activities in Kerala, India. It provides a comprehensive ecosystem of support including funding schemes, incubation, acceleration, mentorship, market access, and investor connections to nurture startups from idea to scale-up stages. KSUM aims to foster innovation, promote inclusive entrepreneurship, and strengthen Kerala's position as a leading startup destination through structured programs and strategic partnerships.
target_beneficiaries: startups; women entrepreneurs; student innovators; SC/ST; MSME; agri-startups; transgender-led startups
eligibility: Eligibility varies by scheme but generally requires startup incorporation in Kerala as a Private Limited Company, LLP, or OPC with active MCA status, DPIIT recognition, and a valid KSUM Unique ID. Specific criteria include: Idea Grant – startups at ideation, designing, or PoC stage; Productization Grant – startups in product development stage with innovative technology product; Market Acceleration Grant – startups in early revenue stage; Scale-up Grant – startups with ₹10 lakhs revenue in last 6 months or ₹30 lakhs external equity; Women/Transgender Productization Grant – women/transgender founders holding ≥51% shareholding; Seed Fund – LLP or Pvt. Ltd with active KSUM Unique ID and DIPP registration; NIDHI Seed Support – DPIIT-recognized startup with ≥3 months association in incubator, ≥51% Indian promoter shareholding; Innovation Grant – innovator based in/out of Kerala, company incorporation and KSUM Unique ID mandatory for disbursement; Women Soft Loan – registered company in Kerala as LLP or Pvt. Ltd, active KSUM Unique ID, DIPP registration, innovative product/technology, no pending dues, CIBIL score >750 preferred.
benefits: KSUM offers financial and non-financial benefits including: Idea Grant (up to ₹3 lakhs), Productization Grant (up to ₹7 lakhs), Women/Transgender Productization Grant (up to ₹12 lakhs), Market Acceleration Grant (up to ₹10 lakhs), Scale-up Grant (up to ₹15 lakhs), Innovation Grant (up to ₹15 lakhs for startups, ₹20 lakhs for women startups), Seed Fund (loan up to ₹15 lakhs), Women Soft Loan (up to ₹15 lakhs), NIDHI Seed Support (₹25 lakhs to ₹1 Crore), R&D Grant (up to ₹30 lakhs), Patent Reimbursement (₹2 lakhs national, ₹10 lakhs international), Technology Transfer Scheme (up to ₹10 lakhs), incubation and acceleration programs, mentorship from industry experts, access to world-class infrastructure (Integrated Startup Complex, Super Fablab, Digital Hub, Emerging Tech Hub, Startup Pod, Freedom Square), coworking spaces (LEAP Centres), market expansion initiatives, investor connect programs (Investor Café, Pitch Days, VC 101 Bootcamp), investor education (Ignite), Fund of Funds for capital deployment into SEBI-registered AIFs, Creative Economy Fund, government as marketplace for procurement, and international exposure programs.
financial_support: Financial support includes grants, loans, and equity-linked instruments. Grants range from ₹2 lakhs (Student Idea Grant) to ₹30 lakhs (R&D Grant). Loans include Seed Fund (up to ₹15 lakhs at 6% simple interest with 12-month moratorium and 36-month repayment), Women Soft Loan (up to ₹15 lakhs at 6% simple interest repayable in 1 year or project completion), and Scale-up Seed Fund (collateral-free debt or CCD/CCPS up to ₹25 lakhs at 6% simple interest with 12-month moratorium and 36-month repayment). The Fund of Funds deploys capital as a Limited Partner in SEBI-registered AIFs that invest in Kerala-based startups. The Innovation Grant provides up to ₹15 lakhs for startups and ₹20 lakhs for women startups. Specific grants: Idea Grant (₹3 lakhs), Productization Grant (₹7 lakhs), Market Acceleration Grant (₹10 lakhs), Scale-up Grant (₹15 lakhs), Women/Transgender Productization Grant (₹12 lakhs), NIDHI Prayas Grant (₹10 lakhs), NIDHI Seed Support (₹25 lakhs–1 Crore), R&D Grant (₹30 lakhs).
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to ₹30 lakhs for R&D Grant
application_process: 1. Visit the KSUM website at https://startupmission.kerala.gov.in 2. Navigate to the 'Schemes' section and select the relevant scheme 3. Download the guideline document for detailed eligibility and process 4. Check for open application calls published on the website, social media, and print media 5. Submit application online through the KSUM portal during the application window 6. Fill the application form and upload required documents (incorporation, PAN, KSUM Unique ID, bank details, fund utilization plan, etc.) 7. Application scrutiny by KSUM officials 8. Shortlisting based on eligibility and proposal merit 9. Pitch presentation before the Expert Committee 10. Evaluation based on team, product innovation, marketing, financials, and fund utilization plan 11. Approval by CEO/Chairman, KSUM 12. Agreement execution with KSUM 13. Fund disbursement in milestone-based tranches (typically 50% first tranche, balance after progress review and utilization certificate)
deadlines: Rolling basis — application windows are announced periodically through KSUM’s website, social media, and print media. Specific schemes like Innovation Grant are conducted under 'Kerala Innovation Drive’YY’ annually or as per demand. EOIs and tenders have fixed closing dates (e.g., EOI for Startup Space Allotment: 22 June 2026 at 5:00 PM; Tender for AutoCAD: 13 July 2026 at 5:00 PM).
implementing_agency: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), nodal agency of the Government of Kerala for entrepreneurship development and incubation activities

overview: The Blue Revolution – Neela Kranti scheme, launched in 2015-16 and running until 2019-20, was a centrally sponsored initiative by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India, with a central outlay of ₹3,000 crore that helped mobilize a total investment of ₹5,000 crore. It laid the foundation for integrated fisheries development by focusing on increasing fish production and productivity through technological upgradation, expansion of aquaculture, and development of fisheries infrastructure. The scheme aimed to enhance the socio-economic conditions of fishers and fish farmers while promoting sustainable and responsible utilization of fisheries resources.
target_beneficiaries: fishers; fish farmers; coastal communities; entrepreneurs; MSME
eligibility: The scheme was open to State Governments, Union Territories, fisheries cooperatives, fish farmers, entrepreneurs, and other stakeholders involved in fisheries and aquaculture activities. Beneficiaries had to submit project proposals through the respective State Fisheries Departments for approval and funding under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme framework. Specific eligibility criteria varied by component but generally required adherence to scheme guidelines, technical feasibility, and financial viability of proposed projects.
benefits: The scheme provided financial assistance for the development of fisheries infrastructure, including fishing harbours, fish landing centres, aquaculture farms, hatcheries, and post-harvest facilities. It supported technological upgradation, capacity building, and training for fishers and entrepreneurs. It facilitated access to credit and subsidies for inputs such as seed, feed, and equipment. The scheme also promoted market linkages, value addition, and export-oriented activities. Additionally, it contributed to employment generation, livelihood diversification, and improved socio-economic conditions for coastal and inland fishing communities.
financial_support: The Blue Revolution Scheme had a central outlay of ₹3,000 crore, which helped mobilize a total investment of ₹5,000 crore. Financial support was provided as a subsidy through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) mechanism, where the Government of India provided grant-in-aid to State Governments and Union Territories for implementing approved projects. The funding pattern typically followed a 60:40 ratio (Central:State) for general States and 90:10 for Himalayan and North-Eastern States, with 100% central funding for Union Territories. Funds were released in installments based on project progress and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Identify the project component under Blue Revolution Scheme (e.g., aquaculture development, infrastructure, post-harvest). 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) as per scheme guidelines. 3. Submit the DPR to the respective State Fisheries Department. 4. State Fisheries Department forwards the proposal to the Department of Fisheries, Government of India for appraisal and approval. 5. Upon approval, obtain sanction letter and proceed with project implementation. 6. Utilize funds as per approved plan and submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates. 7. Claim reimbursement or receive funds in installments based on milestone achievement.
deadlines: The scheme operated from 2015-16 to 2019-20. Applications were accepted during the scheme period based on annual budget allocations and State-level proposals. There was no fixed rolling deadline; submissions were invited periodically as per scheme guidelines and fund availability.
implementing_agency: Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India

overview: The Duty Drawback Scheme is a customs duty refund mechanism under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) that reimburses exporters for duties paid on imported inputs used in the manufacture of export goods. It aims to enhance the competitiveness of Indian exports by neutralizing the incidence of taxes and duties on inputs used in export production. The scheme operates under the Customs Act, 1962 and is administered by CBIC to promote export-oriented industrialization and reduce the cost burden on exporters.
target_beneficiaries: exporters; manufacturers; MSME
eligibility: Exporters who have paid customs duty on imported inputs or central excise duty on indigenous inputs used in the manufacture of goods that are subsequently exported are eligible for duty drawback. The claim must be filed within the prescribed time limit from the date of export, and the exporter must maintain proper records of import, usage in production, and export.
benefits: Financial reimbursement of customs and central excise duties paid on inputs used in export production; neutralization of tax burden on exports; improved price competitiveness in international markets; encouragement of value addition and import substitution in export-oriented sectors; compliance with WTO principles by not constituting a subsidy but a tax remission.
financial_support: The scheme provides refund of customs duty paid on imported inputs and central excise duty paid on indigenous inputs used in the manufacture of export goods. The drawback rate is fixed as a percentage of the FOB value of exports or as a fixed amount per unit, based on the input-output norms notified by CBIC. Refunds are credited directly to the exporter's bank account via electronic transfer after verification of shipping bills and other documentation.
application_process: 1. Determine eligibility based on import of inputs and subsequent export of finished goods. 2. Maintain records of bills of entry, warehouse documents, production records, and shipping bills. 3. File drawback claim electronically through the ICEGATE portal along with shipping bill and proof of export. 4. Submit supporting documents such as bills of entry, bank realization certificate, and consent letter if applicable. 5. Claim is processed by the jurisdictional Customs Office after verification of documents and adherence to time limits. 6. Upon approval, drawback amount is credited to the exporter's bank account.
deadlines: Claims must be filed within 12 months from the date of let export of the goods, as per Section 75 of the Customs Act, 1962.
implementing_agency: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

overview: The Bill Discounting Scheme by NSIC provides financial assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) engaged in manufacturing or service activities by discounting bills arising from genuine trade transactions with reputed buyers such as Public Limited Companies, Government Departments, and Private Limited Companies. The scheme facilitates working capital financing against the security of Bank Guarantee, with bills having a maximum usance period of 180 days. It excludes traders and focuses on enabling MSMEs to improve cash flow and manage receivables efficiently.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises engaged in manufacturing / service activities (Traders will be excluded). The Unit must mandatorily have Udyam Registration. The scheme covers discounting of bills arising out of genuine trade transactions i.e. supplies made by MSMEs to reputed Public Limited Companies / State and Central Govt. Departments / Undertakings / Private Limited Companies (not traders), engaged in manufacturing / service activities.
benefits: Facilitates procurement of Raw Material with credit support up to 180 days. MSMEs helped to avail Economics of Purchases like bulk purchase, cash discount etc. The scheme provides financial assistance against Bank Guarantee security. Processing fees are applicable: 1.00% p.a. for Micro and Small & Medium on new sanctions, 0.50% p.a. for Micro and 1.00% p.a. for Small & Medium on renewal. Concessional discounting rates are available for units with valid SME 1 or SME 2 ratings, subject to timely repayment.
financial_support: The Scheme will cover discounting of bills arising out of genuine trade transactions i.e. supplies made by Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to reputed Public Limited Companies / State and Central Govt. Departments / Undertakings / Private Limited Companies (not traders), engaged in manufacturing / service activities. Bills (Bill of exchange) drawn by MSMEs for the supplies made by them and duly accepted by the Purchaser will be discounted against security of Bank Guarantee to be provided either by the Buyer or Seller, in favour of NSIC. Annual limits can be fixed for such units by obtaining information as per the prescribed application form. The maximum usance period of the bills (Bill of Exchange) shall not exceed 180 days. Security: Bank guarantees issued by approved banks equivalent to the value of assistance. Personal guarantee of proprietor, partners of firms and Directors of the company.
application_process: 1. The Entrepreneurs are required to apply for Bill Discounting only on the prescribed application forms. 2. The application forms downloaded from the link given below may be filled and can be submitted to the nearest Branch Office. 3. The blank forms are also available free of charge from the Branch offices. 4. Duly filled application form is to be submitted along with the Application. 5. Preliminary appraisal and Unit inspection is carried out by NSIC. 6. Sanction of Limit to the Unit. 7. Signing of agreement between NSIC and Unit. 8. Disbursement of assistance to the unit.
implementing_agency: National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. (NSIC)

scheme_name: Jan Samarth Portal – Unified Credit Scheme Portal
overview: JanSamarth Portal is a national digital platform launched by the Government of India that links 16 central government credit-linked schemes across 8 loan categories, enabling beneficiaries to check eligibility, apply online, and receive digital approval from over 250+ participating lenders. The portal integrates with UIDAI, CBDT, NSDL, LGD, and NeSL to automate verification and streamline lending processes. Its core objective is to promote inclusive growth by connecting applicants with suitable government benefits through smart analytics and end-to-end digital processing.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST; farmers; agri-startups; street vendors; self-help groups; micro enterprises; handloom weavers; rural poor
eligibility: Eligibility varies by scheme; applicants must first check eligibility under their required loan category on the portal. General requirements include being an Indian resident, having a valid Aadhaar, PAN, and bank account, and meeting scheme-specific criteria such as DPIIT recognition for startups, Udyam registration for micro enterprises, or income limits for housing loans. Each scheme has its own eligibility norms as defined by the respective nodal ministry.
benefits: Benefits include digital eligibility checking, online application, auto-filling of details via smart analytics, digital approval from lenders, real-time application tracking, access to 250+ lenders, collateral-free loans under certain schemes, interest subvention, credit guarantee coverage, margin money support, and no payment required from applicants to the portal. Specific benefits vary by scheme (e.g., interest subsidy under DAY-NRLM, margin money under PMEGP, credit guarantee under CGSS for startups).
financial_support: Financial support varies by scheme and includes term loans, working capital, cash credit, overdraft, and composite loans. Quantum ranges from ₹10,000 (PM SVANidhi) to ₹1,500 crore (ECLGS for airlines). Support is delivered through participating banks and financial institutions, with credit guarantee coverage provided by NCGTC under schemes like CGSS, CGFMU, and CGTMSE. Interest rates are bank-determined but often capped, with subventions available under specific schemes (e.g., 3% under AIF, 7% under DAY-NRLM).
application_process: 1. Visit the JanSamarth portal and select your loan category. 2. Check eligibility by answering a few simple questions. 3. If eligible, proceed to apply online. 4. Provide basic details and upload required documents. 5. The portal’s smart analytics will auto-fill required details. 6. View offers from 250+ lenders and select a bank. 7. Receive digital approval from the selected bank. 8. Track application status in real time via the portal.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, Government of India
contact_details: Customer support: Customer[dot]support[at]jansamarth[dot]in | 079690-76111 | Bank support: Bank[dot]support[at]jansamarth[dot]in | 079690-76123

scheme_name: SIDBI Make in India Soft Loan Fund (SMILE)
overview: SIDBI Make in India Soft Loan Fund for Enterprises (SMILE) is a soft loan scheme by the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) aimed at providing financial assistance to MSMEs and service enterprises for setting up new projects, expansion, modernization, diversification, technology upgradation, and rehabilitation of sick units. The scheme supports both manufacturing and service sectors, with a focus on promoting Make in India initiatives by facilitating access to affordable credit for capital investment and operational needs.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; service enterprises; manufacturing units; service sector units; sick units undergoing rehabilitation
eligibility: The scheme is open to MSMEs and service enterprises engaged in manufacturing or service activities. Eligible entities include sole proprietorships, partnerships, cooperative societies, private and public limited companies in the micro and small sector. Units undertaking new projects, expansion, modernization, diversification, technology upgradation, or rehabilitation of sick units are eligible. Priority may be given to women entrepreneurs and units adopting state-of-the-art technology.
benefits: The scheme provides soft loans with favorable terms including concessional interest rates, extended repayment tenors, and flexible repayment options. It supports capital expenditure for plant and machinery, technical know-how, and other project-related expenses. The loan is designed to reduce the financial burden on enterprises undertaking long gestation projects and promotes technology upgradation and modernization. Additional benefits may include collateral relaxation and simplified documentation for eligible borrowers.
financial_support: SMILE provides soft loans for project financing, covering expenses related to plant and machinery, technical know-how, and other project components. The loan amount is need-based and subject to the project cost and borrower's repayment capacity. Repayment tenure is structured to align with project cash flows, often including a moratorium period. Interest rates are concessional compared to market rates, and the loan may be covered under credit guarantee schemes like CGTMSE to reduce collateral requirements.
application_process: 1. Identify the project requirement and prepare a detailed project report including project cost, means of financing, and projected financials. 2. Approach the nearest SIDBI branch or office with the project proposal and required documents. 3. Submit the loan application along with the project report and supporting documents. 4. SIDBI officials will conduct due diligence, including technical and financial appraisal of the project. 5. Upon approval, a sanction letter is issued outlining the loan amount, interest rate, repayment schedule, and other terms. 6. Complete documentation and execution of loan agreement. 7. Disbursement of loan amount in stages as per project progress and submission of utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on fund availability and project viability.
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
contact_details: Toll Free Number: 180-022-6753 | Phone: +91 86930 33333 | Email: Available via SIDBI's online enquiry form at https://sidbi.in/online-enquiry

overview: The RBI Regulatory Sandbox for Fintech is a framework that allows fintech innovators to test their products and services in a controlled environment with regulatory relaxations. It aims to foster innovation in the financial sector while ensuring consumer protection and systemic stability. The sandbox enables live testing of innovative financial technologies under RBI supervision.
target_beneficiaries: fintech startups; financial technology companies
eligibility: Entities must be incorporated in India and have a net worth of at least INR 25 lakh as per the last audited balance sheet. They must demonstrate a genuine need for testing in the sandbox and have a clear exit strategy. The product or service must be innovative and not already widely available in the market.
benefits: Regulatory relaxations specific to the tested product/service, access to RBI guidance during the testing period, permission to test with real customers in a controlled environment, and potential pathway to broader regulatory approval upon successful completion.
financial_support: The RBI Regulatory Sandbox does not provide direct financial support, grants, or funding to participants. Support is limited to regulatory facilitation and guidance during the testing phase.
application_process: 1. Submit an application through the RBI's designated portal with details of the innovative product/service. 2. RBI evaluates the application for eligibility and innovativeness. 3. If approved, enter into a sandbox agreement outlining the scope, duration, and regulatory relaxations. 4. Conduct live testing under RBI supervision. 5. Submit a final report on outcomes and learnings. 6. RBI assesses results and provides feedback on next steps.
deadlines: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis; there are no fixed deadlines.
implementing_agency: Reserve Bank of India

overview: The Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Scheme is a Government of India initiative aimed at promoting exports, attracting foreign investment, and generating employment through the establishment of SEZs across the country. It provides a duty-free enclave for export-oriented units with streamlined regulatory and tax incentives. The scheme supports both manufacturing and services sectors and is governed by the SEZ Act, 2005 and SEZ Rules, 2006.
target_beneficiaries: developers; co-developers; units; manufacturers; service providers
eligibility: Any person, including a company, partnership, proprietorship, or cooperative society, can make an application for setting up an SEZ or for developing infrastructure facilities in an SEZ. The applicant must be a resident or non-resident as per FEMA regulations and must comply with the SEZ Act, 2005 and SEZ Rules, 2006.
benefits: Units in SEZs are entitled to duty-free import/domestic procurement of goods for development, operation, and maintenance; exemption from central and state taxes and levies as approved by the Board of Approval; exemption from minimum alternate tax under Section 115JB of the Income Tax Act; external commercial borrowing up to USD 500 million per year without maturity restriction; single window clearance for approvals; exemption from industrial licensing; and exemption from service tax.
financial_support: The SEZ Scheme does not provide direct financial grants or subsidies. Instead, it offers fiscal incentives such as tax exemptions, duty concessions, and procedural simplifications. Financial benefits are indirect and accrue through reduced operational and capital costs due to tax and duty exemptions.
application_process: 1. Submit an application in the prescribed format (Form-A) to the concerned State Government or directly to the Board of Approval (BoA). 2. The State Government forwards its recommendations within 45 days. 3. The application is reviewed by the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC). 4. The Board of Approval (BoA) takes a final decision within 45 days of receiving the State Government's recommendation. 5. Upon approval, a Letter of Approval (LoA) is issued. 6. After obtaining LoA, the developer must execute a lease deed and develop the SEZ within the stipulated time.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: The SEBI Innovation Sandbox is a regulatory framework designed to allow fintech startups and innovators to test new products, services, or business models in a controlled environment under SEBI supervision. It aims to foster innovation in the securities market while ensuring investor protection and market integrity. Participants can experiment with relaxed regulatory requirements for a limited period, subject to oversight and reporting obligations.
target_beneficiaries: startups; fintech companies; innovators
eligibility: Entities must be incorporated in India, have a minimum net worth as specified by SEBI, and propose an innovative product, service, or business model related to securities markets. The innovation must address a genuine market need and include safeguards for investor protection and risk management.
benefits: Access to a regulated testing environment with relaxed compliance requirements, guidance from SEBI officials, potential pathway to full regulatory authorization, and enhanced credibility through SEBI association. Non-financial benefits include regulatory mentorship and market access opportunities.
financial_support: The SEBI Innovation Sandbox does not provide direct financial support, grants, or funding to participants. It offers regulatory relief and facilitation rather than monetary assistance.
application_process: 1. Submit an application detailing the innovative product, service, or business model to be tested. 2. Include information on the technology, target users, risk mitigation measures, and investor protection mechanisms. 3. SEBI reviews the application for eligibility and potential risks. 4. If approved, enter into a sandbox agreement outlining the scope, duration, and conditions of testing. 5. Conduct the test under SEBI supervision with periodic reporting. 6. Submit a final report on outcomes and lessons learned.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

overview: The Advance Authorization Scheme allows duty-free import of inputs that are physically incorporated in an export product, enabling exporters to import raw materials, intermediates, components, consumables, parts, and accessories without payment of basic customs duty, additional customs duty, anti-dumping duty, safeguard duty, or social welfare surcharge, subject to fulfilling export obligations within a specified time frame.
target_beneficiaries: exporters; manufacturers; merchant exporters
eligibility: Any manufacturer exporter or merchant exporter tied to a supporting manufacturer is eligible to apply for Advance Authorization. The applicant must have a valid Importer Exporter Code (IEC) and must be engaged in the manufacture and export of goods. The scheme is applicable to exports under the Foreign Trade Policy, 2023.
benefits: Duty-free import of inputs (basic customs duty, additional customs duty, anti-dumping duty, safeguard duty, social welfare surcharge exempted), no requirement to pay duty on inputs if export obligation is fulfilled, ability to import inputs without upfront cash outflow for duties, flexibility in sourcing inputs globally, and validity of authorization for 12 months from date of issue.
financial_support: The scheme provides duty exemption on imported inputs, which constitutes indirect financial support by reducing the cost of production. There is no direct cash subsidy or grant; the benefit is in the form of foregone customs duties on inputs that are physically incorporated into the export product and for which the export obligation is fulfilled.
application_process: 1. Register on the DGFT website with a valid IEC. 2. Log in to the DGFT portal and navigate to the Advance Authorisation module. 3. Fill out the online application form with details of the export product, inputs required, and export obligation. 4. Upload required documents including PAN, IEC, GST certificate, and details of the export order or self-declaration of export capability. 5. Submit the application and pay the applicable application fee online. 6. Await scrutiny and approval by the concerned Regional Authority. 7. Upon approval, the Advance Authorization is issued electronically. 8. Import inputs as per the authorization. 9. Fulfill the export obligation within the validity period. 10. Apply for redemption of the authorization after export realization.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Foreign Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: The Export Oriented Unit (EOU) Scheme is a policy initiative under India's Foreign Trade Policy that allows units to undertake export-oriented production with benefits such as duty-free import of capital goods, raw materials, and consumables, as well as exemptions from central excise duty and service tax. The scheme aims to boost exports by providing fiscal incentives and simplifying procedural requirements for units committed to exporting their entire production. EOUs are permitted to sell up to 50% of their output in the Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) under certain conditions, subject to payment of applicable duties.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers; exporters; MSME; large enterprises
eligibility: Units undertaking to export their entire production of goods and services (except permissible sales in DTA) are eligible under the EOU Scheme. The unit must be engaged in manufacturing, services, software development, agriculture, aquaculture, animal husbandry, floriculture, horticulture, pisciculture, poultry, sericulture, viticulture, or mining. The unit must achieve a positive net foreign exchange earnings cumulatively over a period of five years from the commencement of production. The unit must not be engaged in any activity listed in the negative list of exports as per the Foreign Trade Policy.
benefits: EOUs are entitled to duty-free import of capital goods, raw materials, components, consumables, spares, and packaging materials required for the manufacture of goods for export. They are exempt from paying central excise duty on goods manufactured and service tax on services utilized in the production process. EOUs can procure goods from bonded warehouses and export promotion capital goods (EPCG) scheme holders without payment of duties. They are allowed to sell up to 50% of their annual production in the Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) on payment of applicable duties. EOUs can also avail of refunds of duties and taxes paid on inputs used in the manufacture of exported goods under the duty drawback scheme.
financial_support: The EOU Scheme does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants. Instead, it offers fiscal incentives through exemptions and concessions: duty-free import of inputs, exemption from central excise and service tax, and eligibility for duty drawback on exported goods. The financial benefit is indirect, arising from reduced input costs and tax liabilities, thereby improving the competitiveness and profitability of export-oriented units.
application_process: 1. Submit an application in the prescribed format (Form F) to the Development Commissioner of the concerned Export Processing Zone (EPZ) or the Unit Approval Committee (UAC) under the Department of Commerce. 2. Provide details of the proposed project, including investment, employment, export projections, and foreign exchange earnings. 3. Submit supporting documents such as certificate of incorporation, project report, partnership deed, and bank solvency certificate. 4. Obtain approval from the Unit Approval Committee (UAC) or the Development Commissioner. 5. Execute a Legal Undertaking (LUT) or bond with customs authorities for adherence to export obligations. 6. Upon approval, commence operations and begin availing benefits under the scheme.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: ECGC MSME Export Scheme is a government initiative by the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, designed to support Indian exporters, particularly MSMEs, by providing financial assistance for export-related claims arising from buyer defaults or political disruptions. The scheme operates under the RELIEF (Resilience and Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) program, offering timely support to exporters facing payment delays or non-payment by overseas buyers due to insolvency, bankruptcy, or geopolitical disturbances. It enables exporters to file claims for compensation through a standardized process, with ECGC acting as the insurer of last resort for export credit risks.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; exporters
eligibility: Indian exporters, particularly MSMEs, who have suffered losses due to non-payment by overseas buyers on account of buyer insolvency, bankruptcy, or geopolitical disruptions in regions such as West Asia, and who hold valid export credit insurance policies issued by ECGC are eligible to file claims under the RELIEF scheme.
benefits: Financial compensation for export losses due to buyer default, quick claim settlement process, access to ECGC’s digital portal for claim submission and tracking, support under the government-backed RELIEF initiative, and assistance in recovering dues from insolvent or defaulting overseas buyers.
financial_support: ECGC provides financial support by settling export insurance claims arising from buyer default, insolvency, or geopolitical risks. Claim amounts are determined based on the insured value of the export transaction and the extent of loss suffered. Payments are made directly to the exporter’s bank account after verification and approval, as evidenced by multiple claim settlements ranging from ₹13.5 lakh to over ₹10.72 crore in the provided evidence.
application_process: 1. Visit the ECGC website and navigate to the RELIEF scheme section. 2. Click on the ‘Standard Operating Procedure for filing claims under RELIEF Components I, II and III’ link. 3. Download the claim form and required documents checklist. 4. Fill out the claim form with details of the export transaction, buyer default, and loss amount. 5. Attach supporting documents such as invoice, shipping bill, proof of non-payment, and buyer insolvency proof. 6. Submit the completed application via the ECGC client portal or designated email. 7. Await verification and processing by ECGC officials. 8. Upon approval, the claim amount is disbursed to the exporter’s account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — claims can be submitted as and when buyer default occurs, subject to policy terms and RELIEF scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
contact_details: Email: Not explicitly stated in evidence-based on evidence | Helpline: Not explicitly evidence-based

overview: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is a flagship crop insurance scheme launched by the Government of India in Kharif 2016 to provide affordable and comprehensive crop insurance coverage to farmers against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages. The scheme aims to stabilize farmers' income, encourage adoption of modern agricultural practices, ensure credit flow to the agriculture sector, and promote innovation in insurance products. It operates on an 'Area Approach' basis and is implemented through a multi-agency framework involving insurance companies, financial institutions, and government bodies under the overall guidance of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
target_beneficiaries: farmers
eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in a notified area during the season who have insurable interest in the crop are eligible. Compulsory coverage applies to farmers in the notified area who possess a Crop Loan account/KCC account (Loanee Farmers) to whom credit limit is sanctioned/renewed for the notified crop during the crop season, and such other farmers whom the Government may decide to include from time to time. Voluntary coverage may be obtained by all farmers not covered in the compulsory component, including Crop KCC/Crop Loan Account holders whose credit limit is not renewed.
benefits: Financial support for crop loss/damage due to unforeseen events, income stabilization to ensure continuance in farming, encouragement to adopt innovative and modern agricultural practices, ensured flow of credit to the agriculture sector contributing to food security and crop diversification, protection from production risks, and promotion of innovation & research in insurance and allied products. The scheme also provides on-account payment of claims up to 25% of likely claims if expected yield during the season is likely to be less than 50% of normal yield, and claim amount is credited electronically to the individual insured bank account.
financial_support: The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged under PMFBY by the Implementing Agency (IA). The rate of Insurance Charges payable by the farmer is as follows: 2.0% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less for Kharif foodgrain and oilseeds crops; 1.5% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less for Rabi foodgrain and oilseeds crops; and 5% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less for Annual Commercial/Annual Horticultural crops. The difference between the premium rate and the rate of insurance charges payable by farmers is treated as the Rate of Normal Premium Subsidy, which is shared equally by the Centre and State. For loanee farmers, insurance charges payable by farmers are financed by the loan disbursing office of the Bank and treated as an additional component to the Scale of Finance for obtaining loan.
application_process: 1. Visit the PMFBY portal at https://pmfby.gov.in and click on 'Farmer Corner' then 'Enroll Now' to apply for crop insurance. 2. Use the Insurance Premium Calculator to know the insurance premium before applying. 3. After enrollment, use the Application Status feature to check your application status on every step. 4. For grievances or to report crop loss, call the Krishi Rakshak Portal & Helpline (KRPH) at 14447. 5. Use the Policy ID to check policy status via the Application Status feature. 6. Access digital tools like Farmer App, WhatsApp Chatbot, AIDE App, CCE App, CLAP App, and WINDS App for application, management, and grievance redressal.
deadlines: Cut-off date for receipt of Proposals of farmers (loanee & non-loanee) is 31st July for Kharif and 31st December for Rabi. Cut-off date for receipt of Declarations of Loanee farmers covered on compulsory basis & non-loanee farmers covered on voluntary basis from Bank branches to Respective Nodal Offices is within 15 working days for loanee farmers and seven working days for non-loanee farmers after cut-off date. Cut-off date for receipt of Declarations of farmers covered on Voluntary basis from designated Insurance Agent(s) to Insurance Companies is within two working days after receiving declaration/premium.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India
contact_details: Email: muktanand[dot]ias08[at]nic[dot]in | Telephone / landline: 23382444 | WhatsApp ChatBot: 7065514447 | Krishi Rakshak Portal & Helpline (KRPH): 14447

scheme_name: Interest Subvention Scheme for MSMEs on Post Shipment Credit
overview: The Interest Subvention Scheme for MSMEs on Post Shipment Credit provides financial assistance to MSME exporters by offering interest subvention on post-shipment credit availed from banks. The scheme aims to enhance export competitiveness by reducing the cost of credit for MSMEs engaged in export activities. It supports MSMEs in managing working capital requirements post-shipment and encourages timely realization of export proceeds. The scheme is implemented through the Ministry of MSME and is designed to improve liquidity and sustainability of export-oriented MSME units.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSME exporters with valid Udyam Registration (UR) Certificate who have availed post-shipment credit from scheduled commercial banks or other eligible financial institutions for export of goods or services. The export proceeds must be realized within the stipulated time period as per RBI guidelines. The beneficiary must be a valid MSME as per MSMED Act, 2006 and must have a valid Udyam Registration Certificate.
benefits: Interest subvention on post-shipment credit availed by MSME exporters, reducing the effective cost of credit. The scheme provides financial relief by subsidizing the interest burden on post-shipment loans, thereby improving liquidity and supporting working capital needs. It encourages timely realization of export proceeds and enhances competitiveness in international markets. The benefit is provided as a reimbursement or direct subsidy on the interest paid by the MSME exporter on post-shipment credit.
financial_support: The scheme provides interest subvention on post-shipment credit availed by MSME exporters. The quantum of support is the difference between the actual interest rate charged by the lending institution and a benchmark rate (typically linked to repo rate or LIBOR plus spread), subject to a cap. The exact quantum and mechanism (reimbursement or direct credit) are not specified in the provided evidence. The support is disbursed through the lending institution or directly to the beneficiary MSME upon submission of required documents and proof of interest payment and export realization.
application_process: 1. Avail post-shipment credit from a scheduled commercial bank or eligible financial institution for export of goods/services. 2. Ensure realization of export proceeds within the stipulated time as per RBI guidelines. 3. Pay the interest on the post-shipment credit to the lending institution. 4. Submit application for interest subvention along with required documents to the nodal agency or designated portal. 5. Submit proof of export realization, interest payment certificate, Udyam Registration Certificate, and IEC code. 6. Await verification and approval from the implementing agency. 7. Receive interest subvention amount as per scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

overview: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Government of India to provide income support to all landholding farmer families in the country. The scheme aims to supplement the financial needs of farmers for procuring agricultural inputs and domestic needs, ensuring proper crop health and yields. Under the scheme, eligible beneficiaries receive a direct payment of Rs. 6000 per year in three equal installments of Rs. 2000 each, transferred directly into their Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts.
target_beneficiaries: landholding farmer families; Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs); all farmer families irrespective of landholding size
eligibility: All landholding farmer families having cultivable land in their names are eligible to get benefit under the scheme. The landholder farmer's family is defined as 'a family comprising of husband, wife and minor children who collectively own cultivable land as per land records of the concerned State/UT'. However, certain categories are excluded: Institutional land holders; farmer families with members holding constitutional posts, serving/retired government employees (excluding Multi Tasking Staff/Class IV/Group D), superannuated/retired pensioners with monthly pension of Rs. 10,000 or more, income tax payees in the last assessment year, and professionals like doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, and architects registered with professional bodies.
benefits: Financial benefit of Rs. 6000 per annum per family payable in three equal installments of Rs. 2000 each every four months; direct transfer of funds into beneficiaries' bank accounts via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism; no duplication of payments; benefit allowed in cases of land transfer due to succession after the cut-off date; provision for proportionate benefit in case of land transfer between 01.12.2018 and 31.01.2019; facility for farmers to check beneficiary status through portal, SMS, or Panchayat displays; grievance redressal mechanism via District Level Grievance Redressal Monitoring Committees.
financial_support: Under the Scheme, a direct payment of Rs. 6000 per year is transferred in three equal installments of Rs. 2000 each every four months into the Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of eligible landholding Small and Marginal Farmer (SMF) families. The first installment for the period 01.12.2018 to 31.03.2019 was transferred immediately on identification of beneficiaries. The entire financial liability towards transfer of benefit is borne by the Government of India. Funds are released via PFMS through State Notional Account (similar to MNREGS) to beneficiaries' bank accounts, with Aadhaar Payment Bridge used where available, and alternate verification for first installment in certain States/UTs.
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 6000 per annum per family
application_process: 1. States/UTs identify eligible beneficiary landholding farmer families using land records. 2. Prepare database capturing Name, Age, Gender, Category (SC/ST), Aadhaar Number (or Enrollment Number with alternate documents in Assam, Meghalaya, J&K), Bank Account Number, IFSC Code, and Mobile Number (optional). 3. Ensure no duplication of payments and speedy reconciliation for wrong/incomplete bank details. 4. Upload certified beneficiary lists on PM-Kisan portal in batches/phases. 5. State Nodal Officers authenticate and upload data on the portal. 6. Data undergoes multi-level verification by NIC, PFMS, and banks. 7. State Nodal Officers sign Request For Transfer (RFT) containing beneficiary count and total amount. 8. PFMS issues Fund Transfer Order (FTO) based on RFT. 9. Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare issues sanction order. 10. Amount transferred to beneficiaries' bank accounts via accredited and sponsoring banks using PFMS portal, managed by NPCI.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round based on State/UT submission of beneficiary lists.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare (DAC&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare

overview: The National Beekeeping & Honey Mission (NBHM) is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, implemented through the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NACFED). It aims to promote holistic growth of the beekeeping sector for income and employment generation, particularly for small and marginal farmers, tribals, and women. The mission focuses on scientific beekeeping, honey production, processing, value addition, and market linkage through integrated interventions.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; beekeepers; self-help groups; farmer producer organizations; tribal communities; women
eligibility: Individual farmers, beekeepers, self-help groups (SHGs), joint liability groups (JLGs), farmer producer organizations (FPOs), cooperatives, and tribal communities engaged in or willing to take up beekeeping activities are eligible. Preference is given to small and marginal farmers, SC/ST, and women beneficiaries.
benefits: Financial assistance for setting up beekeeping colonies, procurement of equipment (hives, extractors, processing units), training and capacity building, infrastructure support for honey processing and storage, market development support, branding and packaging assistance, quality certification support, and technical guidance on scientific beekeeping practices.
financial_support: The scheme provides subsidy-based financial assistance: up to 50% subsidy for general category beneficiaries and up to 90% subsidy for SC/ST, women, and beneficiaries in North Eastern and Himalayan states for beekeeping colonies, equipment, and processing units. Assistance is provided through NACFED as the nodal agency via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode.
application_process: 1. Identify the nearest NACFED office or designated implementing agency in the state. 2. 2. Submit application form along with required documents. 3. Application is scrutinized by the district-level committee. 4. Upon approval, financial assistance is sanctioned. 5. Beneficiary procures approved items from empaneled suppliers. 6. Submit bills and vouchers for reimbursement. 7. Subsidy amount is transferred directly to beneficiary's bank account via DBT.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NACFED)

scheme_name: Formation and Promotion of FPOs Scheme

overview: The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) is a centrally sponsored scheme under the Department of Agriculture & Cooperation, Ministry of Agriculture, Government of India, launched to enhance agricultural productivity, sustainability, and climate resilience, particularly in rainfed areas. It promotes integrated farming systems, resource conservation, soil health management, water use efficiency, and climate change adaptation through four major components: Rainfed Area Development (RAD), On Farm Water Management (OFWM), Soil Health Management (SHM), and Climate Change and Sustainable Agriculture: Monitoring, Modeling and Networking (CCSAMMN). The mission converges with other schemes like MGNREGS, IWMP, RKVY, and NFSM to leverage resources and ensure integrated development.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; agri-entrepreneurs; rural households; small farmers; state governments; implementing agencies
eligibility: The scheme is implemented through State Governments and their subordinate offices/institutions. Eligible implementing agencies include State Departments of Agriculture, State Agricultural Universities (SAUs), Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) Centres, and reputed NGOs engaged by State Governments for cluster/village development plans in areas with limited government infrastructure. Beneficiaries are primarily farmers, especially small and marginal farmers in rainfed areas, who participate through State-level implementation structures.
benefits: Financial assistance for adopting sustainable agricultural practices including integrated farming systems, water conservation technologies (farm ponds, efficient irrigation), soil health management (soil testing, nutrient management, reclamation of problem soils), agroforestry, and climate-resilient farming. Non-financial benefits include capacity building, training, exposure visits, knowledge sharing, access to soil health cards, demonstration of agroforestry models, and convergence with other central and state schemes for livelihood diversification and environmental protection.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as grants-in-aid to State Governments based on Annual Action Plans (AAPs), following a 60:40 funding pattern between Centre and State for general states, 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly states, and 100% central funding for Union Territories and National Level Agencies. Funds are released in installments upon submission of Utilization Certificates and progress reports. The mission leverages convergence with schemes like MGNREGS, IWMP, RKVY, and NFSM for supplementary support.
application_process: 1. State Governments prepare Annual Action Plans (AAPs) based on fund availability and past performance. 2. AAPs are submitted to the Government of India for approval by the Project Sanctioning Committee. 3. Funds are released in installments to States upon receipt of Utilization Certificates and detailed progress reports. 4. States implement components through district and village-level agencies. 5. Beneficiaries (farmers) access benefits via State-level implementing departments/agencies. 6. Monitoring and evaluation are conducted quarterly by technical personnel and reported to the National Advisory Committee.
deadlines: Annual Action Plan (AAP) submission is required yearly; funds are released based on AAP approval and utilization of previous funds. Revalidation of unspent funds is permitted subject to conditions.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Cooperation, Ministry of Agriculture, Government of India

overview: PM Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) is an umbrella scheme launched by the Government of India to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for their produce. It comprises three components: Price Support Scheme (PSS), Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS), and Pilot of Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme (PPPS). The scheme aims to protect farmers from distress sales and ensure minimum support prices (MSP) are realized through direct procurement or compensation mechanisms.
target_beneficiaries: farmers
eligibility: All farmers selling notified agricultural commodities under the scheme are eligible. The scheme applies to crops covered under MSP as declared by the Government of India from time to time. Farmers must sell their produce through authorized agencies or registered private traders under the PPPS component to avail benefits.
benefits: Farmers receive MSP for their produce under PSS via direct procurement by Central/State agencies. Under PDPS, farmers get direct payment of the difference between MSP and actual selling/modal price. Under PPPS, private players procure at MSP and are compensated with service charges. Benefits include assured income, reduced post-harvest losses, and timely payments.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through direct procurement at MSP (PSS), direct payment of price deficiency (PDPS), and service charges to private players (PPPS). The Central Government bears the financial liability as per norms. Funds are released to nodal agencies for procurement and payments. The exact quantum varies based on market prices, production, and MSP declarations.
application_process: 1. Farmer sells notified crop to authorized procurement agency (PSS) or registered private trader (PPPS). 2. For PDPS, farmer registers sale and submits claim for price difference. 3. State/UT nodal agency verifies sale and MSP eligibility. 4. Payment is made directly to farmer’s bank account via DBT. 5. Private traders under PPPS submit procurement bills for service charge reimbursement.
deadlines: Based on harvest season and market arrival of notified crops; varies by state and commodity
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

scheme_name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) – Organic Farming
overview: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) – Organic Farming is a sub-scheme under the National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) aimed at promoting organic farming through cluster-based approaches and Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) certification. It supports farmers in adopting organic practices, improving soil health, and accessing domestic and export markets for organic produce. The scheme emphasizes capacity building, input support, market linkage, and certification assistance to ensure sustainable agricultural livelihoods.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; farmer groups; self-help groups; producers
eligibility: Farmer groups, self-help groups, producers, and other collectives engaged in agriculture and willing to adopt organic farming practices under the Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India) are eligible. Individual farmers can also benefit through group participation. Preference is given to small and marginal farmers, women farmers, and those from SC/ST communities.
benefits: Financial assistance for organic input production, certification, labeling, packaging, and marketing; capacity building and training on organic practices; exposure visits; handholding support for certification; market linkage development; and access to organic premium markets. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, quality assurance, and institutional support for PGS certification.
financial_support: Under PKVY, financial assistance is provided to farmer groups at the rate of Rs. 50,000 per hectare for a period of three years, out of which 62% (Rs. 31,000) is given as incentive for organic conversion, input production, labeling, packaging, transportation, and marketing, and the remaining 38% (Rs. 19,000) is allocated for mobilization, capacity building, training, exposure visits, documentation, and certification expenses. The support is released in installments based on progress and verification.
application_process: 1. Form a farmer group or self-help group with minimum 5 members practicing or willing to adopt organic farming. 2. Register the group with the concerned State Nodal Agency or Regional Council under PGS-India. 3. Submit application along with required documents including group details, farm history, and pledge. 4. Undergo verification and approval by the Regional Council. 5. Upon approval, receive user ID and password to upload data on the PGS-India portal. 6. Begin organic farming practices and maintain records for peer review and certification. 7. After completion of conversion period, apply for PGS certification through the group.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

overview: The Software Technology Park (STP) Scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme for the development and export of computer software, including export of professional services using communication links or physical media. It integrates the government concept of 100% Export Oriented Units (EOU) and Export Processing Zones (EPZ) with the concept of Science Parks/Technology Parks. The scheme provides single-point contact services for member units to conduct export operations at a pace commensurate with international practices.
target_beneficiaries: software exporters; IT/ITES companies; computer software developers
eligibility: Any entity engaged in the development and export of computer software, including professional services via communication links or physical media, can set up an STP unit anywhere in India. Jurisdictional STPI authorities can clear projects costing less than Rs.100 million with Indian Investment. 100% foreign equity is permitted.
benefits: Single window clearance system; permission to set up STP units anywhere in India; duty-free import of hardware and software; permission to import second-hand capital goods; re-export of capital goods allowed; simplified minimum export performance norms (Positive Net Foreign Exchange Earnings); use of computer systems for commercial training permissible if no terminals outside STP premises; sales in Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) allowed with GST refund on capital goods purchased from DTA; free repatriation of capital invested by foreign entrepreneurs, know-how fees, royalty, dividend after payment of Income Taxes; donation of computers and peripherals to recognized non-commercial educational institutions, charitable hospitals, public libraries, funded R&D establishments, or Govt. of India/State/UT after two years without duty payment; 100% depreciation on computers and computer peripherals over five years.
financial_support: The STP Scheme does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Instead, it offers fiscal benefits including duty-free imports, GST refunds on capital goods purchased from DTA, and 100% depreciation on computers and peripherals over five years. There is no mention of a fund corpus, grant amount per entity, or direct financial disbursement to beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Apply for registration under the STP Scheme through STPI. 2. Obtain Letter of Permission from jurisdictional STPI authorities (within 10 days). 3. Submit Legal Undertaking-cum-endorsement of Capital Goods (CG) (within 3 days). 4. Receive Green Card (within 2 days). 5. For online registration, click 'For Online Registration Click Here' on the STP Scheme page.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
contact_details: Email: sachin[at]stpi[dot]in (Chief Finance Officer, STPI HQ) | Phone: +91-11-24628081

scheme_name: Interest Subvention Scheme for Short Term Credit to Farmers

overview: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, to mobilize a medium- to long-term debt financing facility for investment in viable post-harvest management infrastructure and farming assets. It provides financial support through interest subvention and credit guarantee to eligible beneficiaries including farmers, FPOs, agri-entrepreneurs, startups, and others. The scheme aims to improve agriculture infrastructure, reduce post-harvest losses, enhance farmer income, and strengthen the agricultural value chain across India.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; FPOs; agri-entrepreneurs; startups; PACS; SHGs; JLGs; multipurpose cooperative societies; marketing cooperative societies; state agencies; agricultural produce market committees; national and state federations of cooperatives; federations of FPOs; federations of SHGs; central/state agency or local body sponsored PPP projects
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Marketing Cooperative Societies, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Self Help Groups (SHGs), Farmers, Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), Multipurpose Cooperative Societies, Agri-entrepreneurs, Startups, Central/State agency or Local Body sponsored Public Private Partnership Projects, State Agencies, Agricultural Produce Market Committees (Mandis), National & State Federations of Cooperatives, Federations of FPOs, and Federations of Self Help Groups (SHGs).
benefits: Financial benefits include interest subvention of 3% per annum up to a limit of ₹2 crore for a maximum period of 7 years, and credit guarantee coverage for loans up to ₹2 crore under the CGTMSE scheme with the government paying the fee. Non-financial benefits include convergence with various Central and State Government schemes (MIDH, PMFME, SMAM, GOBAR-Dhan, PMKSY, AMI, PACS as MSC, RKVY, PMEGP, PM-KUSUM), online single window facility in collaboration with participating lending institutions, and Project Management Unit (PMU) support for handholding in project preparation.
financial_support: The financing facility provides loans up to ₹2 crore per project per location, with interest subvention of 3% per annum capped at ₹2 crore per project, available for a maximum period of 7 years. Credit guarantee coverage is available for loans up to ₹2 crore under the CGTMSE scheme, with the government bearing the fee. For loans exceeding ₹2 crore, interest subvention is limited to ₹2 crore. The scheme has a total size of ₹1 lakh crore, and repayment period covers a maximum of 7 years including a moratorium period of up to 2 years.
application_process: 1. Visit the AIF portal at https://agriinfra.dac.gov.in 2. Register as a beneficiary through the Beneficiary Registration section 3. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) using the template provided 4. Approach a participating lending institution (Commercial Banks, Cooperative Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, NCDC, NBFCs etc.) with the DPR 5. The lending institution processes the loan application under the AIF scheme 6. Upon sanction, the loan is disbursed by the lending institution 7. Interest subvention and credit guarantee claims are submitted through the AIF portal
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

overview: The Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanisation (SMAM) is a Government of India initiative under the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, aimed at increasing agricultural productivity through farm mechanization. It provides subsidies to farmers, entrepreneurs, societies/SHGs/FPOs, and manufacturers for procuring agricultural machinery and establishing Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs).
