The scheme operates via a Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) portal where subsidies are transferred electronically to beneficiaries' bank accounts after verification.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; entrepreneurs; societies/shg/fpo; manufacturers; dealers
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include individual farmers, entrepreneurs, societies/SHGs/FPOs, and manufacturers who register on the agrimachinery.nic.in portal. Farmers must provide Aadhaar number, land records, bank details, and identity proof. For CHC projects, additional requirements include agriculture graduate certificate, domicile, and date of birth proof. Manufacturers must register with GST certificate and product test reports. Dealers must be registered through manufacturers. All applicants must select correct state, district, block, and village during registration, and furnish accurate details to avoid debarment during physical verification.
benefits: Financial benefits include central and state government subsidies for purchasing agricultural machinery and establishing CHCs, transferred via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to bank accounts. Non-financial benefits include access to performance-tested machinery, technical support through FMTTIs, training of candidates by FMTTIs, availability of a multi-lingual mobile app (FARMS) for CHC operations, SMS alerts at key stages (registration, dealer selection, bill submission, verification, disbursement), and facilitation of machinery hire/sale through the platform. The system ensures transparency through online application tracking, beneficiary reports, and physical verification by government officers.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as a shared subsidy between the Centre and State governments. The Centre releases funds to State Governments, which then allocate category-wise and district-wise targets. Subsidy amounts are calculated based on the final negotiated price of machinery, with centre and state/top-up limits applying. For CHC projects involving loans over ₹25 lakh, bank loan documents must be uploaded. Payment is processed via RTGS/NEFT after physical verification and approval by government officers. The subsidy is disbursed directly to the beneficiary's bank account (farmer or dealer, as selected during bill upload).
application_process: 1. Visit https://agrimachinery.nic.in and click on 'Registration' from the navigation bar. 2. Select beneficiary type: Farmer, Entrepreneur, Society/SHG/FPO, or Manufacturer. 3. Enter required details: For Farmer – Aadhaar/mobile/name, state, district, block, village, land area, address, pincode, bank details, and identity proof; for Entrepreneur/Society – GSTN/PAN, contact details, address; for Manufacturer – GST certificate, product details, test report, bank details. 4. Accept terms and conditions and submit to receive User ID and password (sent via SMS). 5. Login to the portal using credentials. 6. For machinery purchase: Select implement, check availability, add application, generate PIN, select dealer, negotiate price, upload bill and joint photographs. 7. For CHC project: Apply for CHC establishment, upload project details (agriculture graduate, domicile, DOB certificate), await government officer approval, print permit, upload implement bill and loan documents (if applicable). 8. After physical verification by government officer, subsidy is approved and payment file generated for disbursement. 9. Track application status via Application Tracking system using reference number.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year as per state-specific timelines and Annual Action Plan (Demand) submission to M&T Division.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
contact_details: Email: support-agrimech@gov.in | Helpline: 011-23604908, 8076258719 (Technical Support) | C.R. Lohi (Dy. Commissioner): cr[dot]lohi[at]nic[dot]in 011-23389019 | Sh.V.N.Kale (Add. Commissioner): vn[dot]kale[at]gov[dot]in 011-233387200

scheme_name: Kisan Credit Card for Fisheries & Animal Husbandry
overview: The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme was introduced by the Government of India in 1998 to provide timely and affordable credit support to farmers, including fishers and livestock farmers. It enables cultivators, livestock farmers, and fishers to access short-term loans for crop production, allied activities, and household requirements. Under KCC, farmers are issued a credit card linked to their bank account, which allows them to withdraw funds as needed. The scheme has been extended to fisheries and animal husbandry sectors to support fishers and fish farmers with working capital for fisheries-related activities.
target_beneficiaries: fishers; fish farmers; livestock farmers; cultivators
eligibility: Cultivators, livestock farmers, and fishers engaged in agricultural and allied activities are eligible for the Kisan Credit Card scheme. The scheme is available to farmers who require credit for crop production, fisheries, animal husbandry, and household needs.
benefits: The Kisan Credit Card provides timely and affordable credit support, enables access to short-term loans for crop production, allied activities, and household requirements, and offers a credit card linked to the bank account for flexible withdrawal of funds as needed.
financial_support: Under Kisan Credit Card, farmers are issued a credit card linked to their bank account, which allows them to access short-term loans for crop production, allied activities, and household requirements. The card enables flexible withdrawal of funds as needed for fisheries and animal husbandry activities.
application_process: 1. Approach a bank offering Kisan Credit Card facility. 2. Submit application form along with required documents. 3. Bank verifies eligibility and land/crop/fisheries/animal husbandry details. 4. Upon approval, KCC is issued linked to the bank account. 5. Cardholder can withdraw funds as needed for approved purposes.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying

overview: The Aquaculture Development Scheme (MPEDA) is a central sector scheme aimed at promoting sustainable aquaculture practices, supporting value addition, and enhancing export competitiveness of marine products. It provides financial and technical assistance to aquaculture farmers and exporters for infrastructure development, technology adoption, and capacity building. The scheme focuses on species diversification, better management practices, and market promotion to increase India's share in global seafood trade.
target_beneficiaries: aquaculture farmers; exporters; MSME; fisheries cooperatives
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include aquaculture farmers, exporters, fisheries cooperatives, and MSMEs engaged in marine products sector. Applicants must be registered with MPEDA or its affiliated societies like NaCSA and RGCA. Priority is given to small-scale and marginal farmers, particularly those adopting cluster-based farming and Better Management Practices (BMPs). Exporters seeking support for value addition, cold storage, or processing infrastructure must demonstrate export potential and compliance with quality standards.
benefits: Financial support for infrastructure development, technology upgradation, and value addition units. Technical assistance through training programs, capacity building, and access to Better Management Practices (BMPs). Support for species diversification via RGCA and NaCSA. Assistance in obtaining export facilitation certificates and quality certifications. Access to institutional finance and insurance linkages. Market promotion through participation in international fairs and buyer-seller meets. Subsidized testing and certification services through MPEDA laboratories.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as a subsidy for eligible components such as cold storage, processing machinery, hatchery development, and farm infrastructure. The support is disbursed through NaCSA and RGCA after verification of project proposals and utilization certificates. The scheme operates on a demand-driven basis with budgetary support allocated annually. Assistance is provided based on the scope of the project, with higher support for value addition and technology adoption initiatives.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant component of the scheme (value addition, infrastructure, training, etc.). 2. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, budget, and expected outcomes. 3. Submit the proposal through the respective Regional/Sub-Regional Office of MPEDA or via NaCSA/RGCA for aquaculture-specific interventions. 4. Upload required documents such as registration certificates, project reports, and financial statements. 5. Await technical and financial appraisal by MPEDA officials. 6. Upon approval, receive sanction letter and proceed with implementation. 7. Submit utilization certificates and progress reports for fund release.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to budget availability.
implementing_agency: Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India

overview: The National Horticulture Mission (NHM) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 2005-06 to promote holistic growth of the horticulture sector through regionally differentiated strategies. It aims to enhance horticultural production, improve nutritional security, and provide income support to farm households. The mission focuses on increasing productivity, promoting post-harvest management, and developing market infrastructure for horticultural crops.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; self-help groups; farmer producer organizations; entrepreneurs; NGOs; cooperatives
eligibility: The scheme is open to farmers, self-help groups, farmer producer organizations, entrepreneurs, NGOs, cooperatives, and other entities engaged in horticulture activities. Beneficiaries must be involved in cultivation, processing, marketing, or post-harvest management of horticultural crops. Specific eligibility may vary by component and state-level implementation guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance for setting up nurseries, tissue culture units, vegetable seed production, and floriculture units. Support for protected cultivation (polyhouses, shade nets), organic farming, vermicompost production, and mushroom cultivation. Assistance for beekeeping, post-harvest management (pack houses, cold storage, ripening chambers), and market infrastructure (wholesale markets, rural primary markets). Training, demonstration, and exposure visits for farmers and technicians.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as back-ended subsidies ranging from 40% to 50% of the project cost, with higher assistance (up to 50%) for SC/ST, small, marginal, and women farmers. Subsidy is released in installments based on verification of field-level progress. The assistance is credit-linked and routed through nodal banks or implementing agencies.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant component under NHM for which assistance is sought. 2. Prepare a project proposal as per the guidelines of the component. 3. Submit the application to the State Horticulture Mission (SHM) or District Horticulture Office. 4. Application is scrutinized by the technical committee at the SHM/District Office. 5. Upon approval, administrative sanction is issued. 6. Beneficiary initiates the project and submits progress reports. 7. Subsidy is released in installments after verification of field progress.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year as per State Horticulture Mission notifications.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

overview: Agri Export Zones (AEZ) is a scheme aimed at promoting agricultural exports by creating a cluster-based industries, value addition, and infrastructure development in the agriculture sector. The scheme focuses on integrating the entire value chain from production to export, providing support for post-harvest management, processing, and marketing of agricultural products. It encourages private sector participation and public-private partnerships to develop export-oriented agri-based industries. The initiative seeks to boost India's share in global agricultural trade by improving quality, reducing wastage, and enhancing competitiveness of agri-exports.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; agro-processors; exporters; MSME; farmer producer companies
eligibility: Eligibility under the Agri Export Zones (AEZ) scheme includes farmers, farmer producer companies, agro-processing units, exporters, and other stakeholders engaged in the production, processing, and export of agricultural products. Applicants must be engaged in activities related to scheduled products under APEDA and must demonstrate export potential or existing export activity. The scheme encourages cluster-based participation where multiple stakeholders in a geographic region collaborate to develop an export-oriented agri-value chain. Registration with APEDA as an exporter (RCMC) is typically required for availing benefits under the scheme.
benefits: Benefits under the Agri Export Zones (AEZ) scheme include financial assistance for setting up infrastructure such as packhouses, processing units, cold storage, and testing laboratories. Support is provided for quality certification, branding, and market development activities. The scheme facilitates access to export promotion initiatives, participation in international trade fairs, and buyer-seller meets. It also supports technology upgradation, skill development, and training for stakeholders in the agri-export value chain. Additionally, AEZs may receive assistance for logistics, packaging, and compliance with international sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) standards.
financial_support: Financial support under the Agri Export Zones (AEZ) scheme is provided as a subsidy for infrastructure development, quality upgradation, and market promotion activities. The support is typically extended through APEDA's Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS), where eligible entities can receive grants for setting up packhouses, processing units, cold chains, and testing facilities. The quantum of support varies based on the nature of the project, with specific ceilings for different components such as infrastructure, certification, and market development. Funds are disbursed in installments based on project milestones and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Identify the agri-product and geographic cluster for export potential. 2. Form a consortium of farmers, processors, exporters, and other stakeholders. 3. Develop a detailed project report (DPR) outlining infrastructure, value addition, and export plan. 4. Apply for registration with APEDA to obtain RCMC (Registration-cum-Membership Certificate). 5. Submit the DPR and application through the APEDA portal or designated channel for evaluation. 6. Upon approval, enter into an agreement with APEDA for financial and technical support. 7. Implement the project as per the approved plan and submit periodic progress reports. 8. Claim financial assistance upon submission of utilization certificates and completion of milestones.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA)

scheme_name: National Scheme on Welfare of Fishermen
overview: The National Scheme on Welfare of Fishermen is a centrally sponsored scheme under the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, aimed at providing financial assistance and welfare measures to fishermen and fish farmers. It supports livelihood enhancement, social security, and infrastructure development for the fisheries sector. The scheme is implemented across India and targets traditional and small-scale fishers.
target_beneficiaries: fishermen; fish farmers; traditional fishers; small-scale fishers
eligibility: Traditional and small-scale fishermen, fish farmers, and members of fisher communities engaged in capture fisheries, aquaculture, or allied activities, who are citizens of India and belong to economically weaker sections, as identified by State Governments/UTs based on socio-economic criteria.
benefits: Financial assistance for housing, sanitation, drinking water, community assets, and livelihood support; access to accident insurance and health coverage; support for formation of fisher cooperatives and self-help groups; skill development and training programs; and subsidies for fisheries-related equipment and infrastructure.
financial_support: The scheme provides central share of the Department of Fisheries provides financial assistance to State Governments/UTs for implementation of welfare activities for fishermen, with central share released as grants-in-aid based on approved project proposals and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. State Governments/UTs submit project proposals for fisher welfare activities to the Department of Fisheries. 2. Proposals are appraised by the Department for technical and financial feasibility. 3. Approved projects are sanctioned with central share allocation. 4. Funds are released in installments based on utilization certificates and progress reports. 5. States implement the schemes through designated agencies and monitor outcomes.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per budget cycle and scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying

overview: The National Food Security and Nutrition Mission (NFSNM) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in October 2007 to increase production of rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals, commercial crops, and nutri-cereals through area expansion, productivity enhancement, and sustainable practices. It aims to restore soil fertility, enhance farm-level economy, improve seed replacement rates, and strengthen seed sector infrastructure. The mission has been continued under Krishonnati Yojana till 31.03.2026 and comprises seven components: NFSNM-Rice, NFSNM-Wheat, NFSNM-Pulses, NFSNM-Coarse Cereals (Maize & Barley), NFSNM-Sub Mission on Nutri Cereals (Shree Anna), NFSNM-Commercial Crops, and NFSNM-Seed Components.
target_beneficiaries: farmers
eligibility: Farmers cultivating rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals (maize & barley), commercial crops (cotton, jute, sugarcane), and nutri-cereals (shree anna) in identified districts of the country are eligible for benefits under the mission. The mission prioritizes districts with low productivity yet high potential, especially focusing on food-grain crops cultivated in rain-fed regions.
benefits: Benefits include demonstrations, need-based inputs (seed, INM & IPM), cropping system trainings, flexi interventions, seed hubs, strategic adaptive research support, exposure visits to international organizations, assistance for seed transportation, fostering seeds of new varieties, creation & modernization of seed infrastructure, boosting seed production of traditional varieties, strengthening seed production infrastructure in potato, seed processing and storage units at gram panchayat level, strengthening seed quality control components, national seed reserve, and assistance for boosting seed production in private sector. Financial assistance is provided through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) by the States.
financial_support: Funds are released to States/UTs based on Annual Action Plans approved by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) as per extant guidelines of DA&FW, MoA&FW and Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance. The mechanism of fund flow follows the prevailing guidelines of the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, Government of India. Financial assistance is provided through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) by the States.
application_process: 1. Prepare Annual Action Plan aligned with the Mission’s goals and objectives. 2. Execute the Approved Action Plan using funds provided by Government of India, along with matching State Share. 3. Maintain designated scheme accounts through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). 4. Release of Central Share to States shall be in accordance with prevailing guidelines of the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, Government of India. 5. States/UTs should adopt the fund flow mechanism as communicated by the Government of India and ensure that the accounts thus maintained are audited annually by the Designated Authority/Agency of the State/UT.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

overview: The MSME Competitive (LEAN) Scheme is a Government of India initiative aimed at enhancing the competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) through the implementation of Lean Manufacturing practices. The scheme focuses on reducing waste, improving productivity, and increasing operational efficiency in manufacturing units. It provides financial and technical support to MSMEs for adopting Lean tools and techniques, thereby enabling them to compete effectively in domestic and global markets.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: The scheme is open to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) engaged in manufacturing activities, as defined under the MSMED Act, 2006. The unit must be operational and have a valid Udyam Registration. Priority is given to units willing to implement Lean Manufacturing practices and commit to the required handholding and implementation period.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of subsidy for implementation of Lean Manufacturing tools, access to expert consultants and trainers, handholding support during implementation, improved productivity and reduced operational costs, enhanced quality and delivery performance, better inventory management, and increased competitiveness in national and international markets.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support up to 80% of the project cost for implementation of Lean Manufacturing practices, with a maximum ceiling of INR 40 lakhs per MSME unit. The remaining 20% of the cost is to be borne by the beneficiary unit. The support is released in installments based on achievement of milestones as verified by the implementing agency.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 40 lakhs per MSME unit
application_process: 1. Register on the official LEAN scheme portal at lean.msme.gov.in 2. Submit online application with details of the MSME unit and Udyam Registration 3. Upload required documents including project proposal and bank details 4. Application is screened by the implementing agency for eligibility 5. Eligible units are selected for implementation 6. A Lean consultant is assigned to conduct initial assessment 7. Detailed project report (DPR) is prepared and submitted 8. Upon approval, implementation of Lean tools begins 9. Progress is monitored and verified 10. Subsidy is disbursed in installments based on milestone completion
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME)

overview: The Digital MSME Scheme aims to promote the adoption of digital technologies among Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to enhance their competitiveness, productivity, and market reach. It supports MSMEs in integrating digital tools such as cloud computing, AI, IoT, and digital marketing into their operations. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME) and focuses on enabling digital transformation across various sectors. It encourages MSMEs to leverage technology for innovation, scalability, and sustainability.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: The scheme is open to all Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) registered under the MSME Act, 2006, including manufacturing and service enterprises. Enterprises must have a valid Udyam Registration Certificate. There are no restrictions based on sector, location, or ownership profile, as long as the enterprise meets the MSME classification criteria.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of subsidy for adopting digital technologies; access to digital infrastructure and services; improved operational efficiency and productivity; enhanced market reach through e-commerce and digital marketing; better data management and analytics capabilities; support for innovation and technology upgradation; reduced operational costs through automation.
financial_support: The scheme provides a subsidy of up to 50% of the project cost for adopting digital technologies, with a maximum ceiling of INR 10 Lakhs per MSME. The subsidy is disbursed after successful implementation and verification of the digital solution. The remaining 50% of the cost is to be borne by the beneficiary enterprise.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 10 Lakhs
application_process: 1. Register on the Udyam portal and obtain Udyam Registration Certificate. 2. Identify the digital technology solution to be adopted (e.g., cloud, AI, IoT, digital marketing). 3. Select a certified vendor or service provider from the empanelled list. 4. Submit the project proposal along with cost estimates through the Digital MSME portal. 5. Obtain approval from the designated authority. 6. Implement the digital solution with the vendor. 7. Submit completion report and invoices for verification. 8. Receive subsidy disbursement directly into the bank account after validation.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME)

scheme_name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)
overview: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the holistic growth of the horticulture sector covering fruits, vegetables, root & tuber crops, mushrooms, spices, flowers, aromatic plants, coconut, cashew, cocoa and bamboo. It promotes holistic growth through area-based, regionally differentiated strategies including research, technology promotion, extension, post-harvest management, processing and marketing. The scheme encourages aggregation of farmers into farmer groups like FIGs/FPOs and FPCs to bring economy of scale and scope, enhances horticulture production, augments farmers' income, strengthens nutritional security, improves productivity through quality germplasm, planting material and water use efficiency via Micro Irrigation, and supports skill development and employment generation for rural youth in horticulture and post-harvest management, especially in the cold chain sector.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; farmer groups; FIGs/FPOs; FPCs; rural youth
eligibility: Farmers / beneficiaries should contact the Horticulture Officer of concerned district for availing benefits and assistance under the scheme. The scheme is implemented by State Horticulture Missions (SHM) in selected districts of 18 States and 6 Union Territories for NHM, and in North Eastern States and Himalayan States for HMNEH. National Horticulture Board (NHB), Coconut Development Board (CDB), Central Institute for Horticulture (CIH), Nagaland and National
benefits: Promote holistic growth of horticulture sector, including bamboo and coconut through area based regionally differentiated strategies, which includes research, technology promotion, extension, post harvest management, processing and marketing, in consonance with comparative advantage of each State/region and its diverse Encourage aggregation of farmers into farmer groups like FIGs/FPOs and FPCs to bring economy of scale and scope. Enhance horticulture production, augment farmers, income and strengthen nutritional security. Improve productivity by way of quality germplasm, planting material and water use efficiency through Micro Irrigation. Support skill development and create employment generation opportunities for rural youth in horticulture and post harvest management, especially in the cold chain sector.
financial_support: While Government of India (GOI) contributes 85% of total outlay for developmental programmes in all the states except the states in North East and Himalayas, 15% share is contributed by State Governments. In the case of North Eastern States and Himalayan States, GOI contribution is 100%. Similarly, for development of bamboo and programmes of National Horticulture Board (NHB), Coconut Development Board (CDB), Central Institute for Horticulture (CIH), Nagaland and the National Level Agencies (NLA), GOI contribution will be 100%.
application_process: Village Level Farmers can submit necessary data swiftly and easily via online forms instead of going to government offices. Block Level In the approval process, farmers data is verified to ensure it fits the criteria for the programs to which it qualifies. District Level The District Horticulture Officer makes a decision regarding the approval of the block horticulture project. State Level The project will be forwarded to the state-level agricultural or horticultural department. Ministry If the project meets the necessary criteria, it may receive approval at the ministry level.
implementing_agency: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

overview: The Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) scheme is a World Bank-assisted initiative under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME) aimed at strengthening MSME performance through improved access to finance, market linkages, technology upgradation, and institutional support. It focuses on enhancing competitiveness, resilience, and sustainability of MSMEs across India, particularly in the post-pandemic recovery phase. The scheme supports both existing and new MSMEs through financial and non-financial interventions delivered via state-level implementation units.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Existing MSMEs registered under Udyam or EM-II, including manufacturing and services enterprises, that are operational and have a valid GSTIN. The scheme also supports prospective MSMEs through handholding and pre-investment support. Priority is given to MSMEs in manufacturing, agro-processing, and services sectors, with special focus on women entrepreneurs, SC/ST owners, and enterprises in aspirational districts.
benefits: Financial support through credit guarantees, interest subvention, and grants for technology upgradation; non-financial benefits include market development assistance, access to e-commerce platforms, participation in national and international exhibitions, skill development programs, mentoring, and handholding support for formalization and growth. The scheme also facilitates access to incubation, acceleration, and business development services.
financial_support: Under RAMP, financial support is provided through a combination of interest subvention on bank loans, credit guarantee coverage under CGTMSE, and grants for technology adoption and quality certification. The interest subvention is available at 2% per annum for a period of up to 2 years on term loans for technology upgradation. Grants of up to INR 10 lakhs are provided for ISO certification, patent registration, and digital transformation. Credit guarantee coverage extends up to INR 2 crores per borrower under the CGTMSE scheme.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 10 lakhs for technology upgradation and quality certification
application_process: 1. Register on the Udyam portal if not already registered. 2. Approach a participating bank or financial institution for loan application. 3. Submit project proposal detailing the purpose of fund utilization (e.g., technology upgradation, market development). 4. Bank forwards the proposal to the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) or designated nodal agency for approval. 5. Upon approval, loan is disbursed with applicable interest subvention. 6. For grant components, apply through the state implementation agency with required documents and project report. 7. Utilize funds as per approved plan and submit utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to fund availability
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME)

scheme_name: Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) for Informal Sector
overview: The Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) is an initiative by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, designed to facilitate the online registration of Informal Micro Enterprises (IMEs) through an Assist Process. It enables Designated Agencies (DAs) such as banks, NBFCs, and MFIs to share data of their IME customers to generate Udyam Registration Numbers (URN) and Udyam Assist Certificates (UAC). The platform aims to formalise informal enterprises outside the GST ecosystem and integrate them into digital and financial systems.
target_beneficiaries: Informal Micro Enterprises (IMEs); micro enterprises outside GST ecosystem
eligibility: Informal Micro Enterprises (IMEs) that are not registered on the Udyam Registration Portal (URP) and are outside the GST ecosystem. Registration is facilitated through Designated Agencies (DAs) such as Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs), Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs), Non Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), etc., which share customer data with consent. IMEs cannot register directly; they must approach a DA for assistance.
benefits: Udyam Registration Number (URN) enables classification of bank loans under Priority Sector Lending (PSL) as per RBI guidelines, encouraging higher credit flow. It facilitates issuance of merchant QR codes for digital payments. URN acts as a passport for access to digital systems in governance, financial services, and marketplaces. Registered IMEs receive Udyam Assist Certificate (UAC). Data generated supports policy interventions. Access to knowledge and skills development is also provided.
financial_support: The Udyam Assist Platform does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. It is a registration and facilitation platform that enables access to financial services (e.g., bank loans) by providing Udyam Registration Number (URN), which helps in classifying loans under Priority Sector Lending (PSL). Financial support, if any, comes through linked schemes or lending institutions, not directly from UAP.
application_process: 1. Designated Agencies (DAs) such as banks, NBFCs, MFIs must register on the Udyam Assist Platform (www.udyamassist.gov.in) by submitting a Letter of Authorisation designating a Nodal Officer. 2. NBFCs and NBFC-MFIs must additionally submit their RBI registration certificate. 3. MFIs not classified as NBFCs must submit a letter of confirmation from their Self-Regulatory Organisation (SRO). 4. DAs must accept the Terms and Conditions of the platform. 5. Upon approval by the Implementing Agency (SIDBI), DAs receive login credentials. 6. The DA’s Nodal Officer can add up to 5 sub-users for platform access. 7. Registered DAs upload data of their Informal Micro Enterprise (IME) customers via SFTP, smart EXCELs, or other approved protocols. 8. The Udyam Assist Platform processes the data, conducts validations, and generates Udyam Registration Number (URN) and Udyam Assist Certificate (UAC). 9. The URN and UAC are made available to the DA, which then informs the IME via SMS/Email. 10. IMEs can download the UAC from the portal (www.udyamassist.gov.in) after validation.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

overview: The National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) is a flagship initiative launched by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, to position India as a global leader in technical textiles. It aims to enhance domestic manufacturing, promote innovation, increase exports, and develop skilled human resources in the technical textiles sector. The mission focuses on research and development, market development, export promotion, and skill development across various sub-segments of technical textiles.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers; research institutions; startups; MSME; entrepreneurs; skill development trainees
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include Indian companies, startups, MSMEs, research institutions, universities, and industry associations engaged in technical textiles manufacturing, research, innovation, or skill development activities. Specific eligibility varies by component and is defined under each sub-mission.
benefits: Benefits include financial support for R&D projects, market development assistance, export promotion incentives, skill development training, infrastructure support for common facility centers, and recognition for innovation. The mission also facilitates technology transfer, industry-academia collaboration, and access to testing and certification facilities.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through grants-in-aid, subsidies, and equity participation depending on the component. Support includes up to 50% of project cost for R&D, 25-50% for market development, and 100% government funding for infrastructure in certain cases. Funds are disbursed through implementing agencies after project approval and milestone-based verification.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant component of NTTM (R&D, market development, export promotion, etc.) 2. Prepare project proposal as per guidelines 3. Submit application through the designated nodal agency or online portal 4. Application undergoes technical and financial appraisal 5. Approved projects are sanctioned and funds released in installments 6. Progress monitored through periodic reports and site visits 7. Final submission and utilization certificate required for closure
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and approval cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

scheme_name: Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP)
overview: The Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP) is a Government of India initiative aimed at enhancing productivity, infrastructure development, common facility centers, market access, and technology upgradation for MSE clusters. It provides integrated support through cluster development to strengthen competitiveness and ensure sustainable growth of micro and small enterprises. The scheme focuses on creating common facility centers, improving infrastructure, and facilitating technology adoption within clusters.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; micro enterprises; small enterprises
eligibility: Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) engaged in viable economic activities, forming clusters or willing to form clusters for mutual benefit, with focus on sectors having potential for growth and employment generation. The scheme supports both new and existing clusters of MSEs across manufacturing and service sectors.
benefits: Financial assistance for setting up Common Facility Centers (CFCs), infrastructure development (roads, water, power, drainage), technology upgradation, capacity building, skill development, market development assistance, and support for obtaining quality certifications. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, project formulation support, monitoring and evaluation, and handholding for cluster formation and sustainability.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-in-aid for soft interventions (diagnostic studies, capacity building, skill training, market development) and hard interventions (setting up Common Facility Centers, infrastructure development). Financial support is provided as grant-in-aid with varying percentages based on the intervention type and cluster characteristics, typically ranging from 30% to 90% of project cost, with higher support for special category clusters (SC/ST, women, NER, hilly areas).
application_process: 1. Identify and form a cluster of micro and small enterprises with common economic interests. 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) outlining cluster profile, proposed interventions, expected outcomes, and budget. 3. Submit the DPR along with required documents to the nodal agency (Office of Development Commissioner, MSME) or State-level implementing agencies. 4. Project appraisal and approval by the Steering Committee. 5. Release of funds in installments based on project milestones and utilization certificates. 6. Implementation of approved interventions by the cluster Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV). 7. Monitoring, evaluation, and submission of progress reports.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and appraisal cycles.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

overview: The Amended Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (ATUFS) is a credit-linked subsidy scheme launched by the Ministry of Textiles to promote technology upgradation in the textile industry. It aims to enhance productivity, quality, and global competitiveness of textile units by providing financial assistance for the adoption of indigenous, state-of-the-art, and energy-efficient technology. The scheme supports both new and existing textile units across various segments including spinning, weaving, processing, garmenting, technical textiles, and jute.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; textile units; existing and new textile enterprises
eligibility: Existing and new textile units engaged in activities such as spinning, weaving, processing, garmenting, technical textiles, and jute are eligible. The unit must be registered under the Companies Act, 1956/2013, or any other relevant statute, and must have a valid Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) or Udyam Registration. The project must involve technology upgradation through indigenous, state-of-the-art, and energy-efficient machinery as per the approved list under ATUFS.
benefits: The scheme provides a credit-linked subsidy at the rate of 15% (10% for garmenting and technical textiles segments) on the capital investment made in eligible machinery, subject to a ceiling of INR 30 crores per unit. The subsidy is disbursed through lending institutions after verification of installation and commissioning of approved machinery. Additional benefits include improved operational efficiency, reduced energy consumption, and enhanced product quality.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as a credit-linked subsidy where the government reimburses 15% (10% for garmenting and technical textiles) of the qualifying capital investment in approved machinery to the lending institution, which then passes on the benefit to the beneficiary unit. The maximum subsidy per unit is capped at INR 30 crores. The subsidy is released in installments based on verification of machinery installation and commissioning by the Project Management Agency (PMA).
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 30 crores
application_process: 1. Identify eligible machinery from the approved list under ATUFS. 2. Submit a project proposal to a lending institution (bank or financial institution) along with required documents. 3. The lending institution appraises the project and sanctions the loan. 4. Submit the sanctioned loan details and documents to the Project Management Agency (PMA) for registration. 5. After installation and commissioning of machinery, submit verification documents to the PMA. 6. PMA verifies the claim and recommends subsidy release. 7. The subsidy is released by the Ministry of Textiles to the lending institution, which credits the beneficiary’s account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

overview: The Scheme for Integrated Textile Parks (SITP) is a Government of India initiative under the Ministry of Textiles aimed at developing world-class infrastructure facilities for textile units through public-private partnerships. It supports the establishment of integrated textile parks with plug-and-play facilities to enhance productivity, global competitiveness, and attract investment in the textiles sector. The scheme focuses on creating synergies by co-locating various stages of textile production within a single park.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; private entrepreneurs; industry associations; state governments
eligibility: Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) formed by industry associations, private entrepreneurs, or state government agencies with minimum 10 acres of land, clear title, and commitment to develop the park with at least 50% area allotted to textile units. The SPV must contribute at least 25% of the project cost as equity and ensure that no individual unit occupies more than 25% of the developed area.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grant-in-aid for infrastructure development, common facilities like power, water, effluent treatment, roads, and security. Enables economies of scale, shared services, reduced logistics costs, and access to plug-and-play infrastructure for textile units. Promotes cluster-based development and enhances export competitiveness.
financial_support: Government of India provides grant-in-aid up to 40% of the project cost, with a ceiling of INR 40 crore per textile park. For projects in hilly, tribal, or difficult areas, the grant is up to 90% of project cost with a ceiling of INR 60 crore. The remaining cost is to be borne by the SPV through equity contribution and term loans from financial institutions.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 40 crore per textile park (INR 60 crore for hilly/tribal/difficult areas)
application_process: 1. Formation of Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) by eligible entities 2. Identification and acquisition of land (minimum 10 acres) with clear title 3. Preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) including layout plan, financials, and implementation schedule 4. Submission of application along with DPR to the Office of the Textile Commissioner 5. Appraisal by the Project Appraisal Committee (PAC) 6. Approval by the Inter-Ministerial Steering Committee 7. Signing of Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) between SPV and Government of India 8. Implementation of the park in phases as per approved DPR 9. Submission of utilization certificates and progress reports 10. Release of grant-in-aid in installments based on verification of milestones
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds
implementing_agency: Office of the Textile Commissioner, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

overview: The Horticulture Cluster Development Programme (CDP) is a central sector scheme by the National Horticulture Board (NHB) under the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India. It aims to leverage geographical specialization of horticulture clusters to make them globally competitive by facilitating economies of scale in production and post-harvest activities, better price realization, and empowerment of the farming community through increased competitiveness across the value chain. The programme supports the development of Multi-Commodity High Value Clusters and Peri-urban Vegetable Clusters through a challenge mode selection process where applicants identify and demonstrate feasibility of proposed clusters. Total investment under the programme is INR 10,000 Crore (equivalent to $1.3 Billion).
target_beneficiaries: Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs/FPCs); Cooperatives/Societies; Partnership Firms; Companies
eligibility: Implementing Agency (IA) must be a legal entity excluding proprietorships or natural persons, including Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs/FPCs), Cooperatives/Societies, Partnership Firms, Companies, or combination thereof. The applicant entity must demonstrate a net worth at least equivalent to the equity contribution of the IA proposed in the project, contribute a minimum of 20% of the IA’s Cost Component as equity, possess substantial and relevant experience in agricultural or horticultural input supply, production, aggregation, trading, food processing, exporting, retailing, or logistics provision, have an annual turnover at least equal to the total project cost, secure a term loan from RBI Approved Scheduled Commercial Bank or Financial Institution constituting at least 20% of the IA’s Cost Component, provide a detailed Appraisal Note from the Bank/FI sanctioning the term loan, ensure the farmer component is minimum 40% of the total project cost, and maintain a clean financial record with no defaults on debt obligations over the past three years and no classification as non-performing assets by any lender.
benefits: Financial assistance under the Programme for project execution, support for achieving financial closure, facilitation in obtaining statutory approvals and clearances, assistance in receiving and utilizing financial assistance transparently and judiciously, support in maintaining proper books of accounts, dovetailing and integrating initiatives of other ministries and departments for holistic cluster development, coordination with State Horticulture Mission (SHM) for timely implementation, adherence to Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) guidelines and Ministry of Finance procurement manuals, provision of technical guidance on package of practices and good agriculture practices (GAPs) to farmers, promotion of crop diversification as a performance indicator, and mandatorily ensuring adoption of GAP component of MIDH (especially for reduction in use of pesticide) by farmers in the cluster.
financial_support: The Cluster Development Programme (CDP) has a total investment of $1.3 Billion (INR 10000 Cr). Financial assistance is provided to selected Implementing Agencies (IAs) for project execution. The IA must contribute a minimum of 20% of the IA’s Cost Component as equity and secure a term loan from RBI Approved Scheduled Commercial Bank or Financial Institution constituting at least 20% of the IA’s Cost Component. The farmer component shall be minimum 40% of the total project cost. Financial assistance is released in a transparent and judicious manner adhering to principles of accountability and fiscal responsibility.
application_process: 1. Submit concept note in response to EoI (Expression of Interest) 2. Responsiveness check and technical evaluation of concept notes 3. Shortlisted applicants invited to submit detailed business plan/ DPR 4. Six weeks provided for preparation and submission of DPR/ Business case 5. Post evaluation of the business case/ DPR, projects awarded to IA and Contract signed between NHB and IA
deadlines: Last date for submission of application is 31st July 2026 (6:00 PM, Friday). Pre-bid meeting held in hybrid mode on 13th July 2026, (11:00 AM Monday). Last date for submission of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) by shortlisted applicants initially communicated as 10.04.2026, has been extended to 17th April 2026 (06:00 PM).
implementing_agency: National Horticulture Board (NHB), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
contact_details: Email: clusters.nhb@gov.in | md@nhb.gov.in | dmd.nhb@gov.in | Help Desk: 0124-2343414 | Toll-Free Helpline No. (1800 180 1404) | Helpdesk (0124-2343414)

scheme_name: Champions Portal for MSME Grievance Resolution
overview: The Champions Portal for MSME Grievance Resolution is a technology-driven platform launched by the Ministry of MSME to help MSMEs resolve grievances related to finance, raw materials, labor, regulatory permissions, and other issues, particularly in the context of the Covid-19 situation. It aims to capture new opportunities, identify and encourage potential MSMEs, and provide handholding and support through a unified system. The portal integrates with other grievance redressal systems like CPGRAMS and uses AI, machine learning, and data analytics to reduce human intervention and delay.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and other related stakeholders can voice their issues and grievances through the portal.
benefits: The portal provides facilities to MSMEs and other related stakeholders to voice their issues and grievances and get resolution and way forward; extensive use of AI, Machine learning and Data analytics to avoid and reduce human intervention, delay and duplication; seamless integration with other grievance related portals of GOI like CPGRAMS and other portals of the MSME Ministry; auto-generated unique ID numbers for different types of grievances (GR, CP, CO, IN, VI); timely resolution with matters not remaining unattended for more than three days and not inconclusive after seven days; access to Champion Control Rooms (Central and State Level) for monitoring and resolving issues; and support for MSMEs to avail benefits of Government schemes and access various inputs and requirements.
financial_support: The Champions Portal does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. It is a grievance redressal and handholding platform focused on non-financial support like issue resolution, guidance, and facilitation of access to government schemes.
application_process: 1. Visit the Champions Portal at https://champions.gov.in 2. Register or log in to the portal 3. Submit grievances related to finance, raw materials, labor, regulatory permissions, or other issues 4. Receive an auto-generated unique ID (starting with GR for general grievances, CP for CPGRAMS-fetched, CO for collaborative ideas, IN for administrative interventions, VI for VIP references) 5. The issue is automatically segregated subject-wise and officer-wise and transferred to concerned officials under the MSME Ministry 6. Concerned officers deal with the issue with promptness, sensitivity, and seriousness 7. If unresolved, the matter can be escalated to the Champion Control Room (CCR) for further intervention 8. The Secretary MSME reviews the functioning and holds fortnightly sessions with applicants whose grievances are not settled.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Grievances can be submitted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

overview: The National Horticulture Board (NHB) implements the Cluster Development Programme (CDP) to leverage geographical specialization of horticulture clusters and make them globally competitive. The scheme aims to facilitate suitable economies of scale in production and post-harvest activities, improve price realization, and empower farming communities by enhancing income through increased competitiveness across the value chain. It operates in challenge mode where interested parties identify clusters, demonstrate feasibility, and submit proposals for development of existing or induced clusters. The programme supports multi-commodity high-value clusters and peri-urban vegetable clusters under revised CDP guidelines.
target_beneficiaries: Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs/FPCs); Cooperatives/Societies; Partnership Firms; Companies
eligibility: Implementing Agency (IA) must be a legal entity excluding proprietorships or natural persons, including Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs/FPCs), Cooperatives/Societies, Partnership Firms, Companies, or combination thereof. The applicant must demonstrate net worth at least equivalent to the equity contribution of the IA proposed in the project, contribute a minimum of 20% of the IA’s Cost Component as equity, possess substantial and relevant experience in agricultural or horticultural input supply, production, aggregation, trading, food processing, exporting, retailing, or logistics provision, have an annual turnover at least equal to the total cost of the project, secure a term loan from RBI Approved Scheduled Commercial Bank or Financial Institution constituting at least 20% of the IA’s Cost Component, provide a detailed Appraisal Note from the Bank/FI, ensure the farmer component is minimum 40% of the total project cost, and maintain a clean financial record with no defaults on debt obligations or non-performing asset classification over the past three years.
benefits: Financial assistance under the Programme for project execution, support for achieving financial closure, facilitation in obtaining statutory approvals and clearances, guidance on utilization of funds in a transparent and judicious manner, support for maintaining proper books of accounts, dovetailing with other ministries and departments for holistic cluster development, coordination with State Horticulture Mission (SHM) for timely implementation, adherence to Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) guidelines and Ministry of Finance procurement manuals, and provision of technical guidance on package of practices and good agriculture practices (GAPs) to producers in the cluster.
financial_support: The applicant must provide a financing plan clearly identifying sources of funds and indicating equity: debt split for the IA component of project cost. The farmer component shall be minimum 40% of the total project cost. The IA must secure a term loan from RBI Approved Scheduled Commercial Bank or Financial Institution that constitutes at least 20% of the IA’s Cost Component, confirmed by relevant banking institutions and documented appropriately. The applicant entity must contribute a minimum of 20% of the IA’s Cost Component as equity in the proposed project.
application_process: 1. Submit concept note in response to Expression of Interest (EoI) via online portal at https://cdp.nhb.gov.in. 2. Await responsiveness check and technical evaluation of concept notes received on or before the cut-off date. 3. If shortlisted, submit detailed business plan/ Detailed Project Report (DPR) within six weeks. 4. Post evaluation of the business case/DPR, projects will be awarded to the IA and contract will be signed between NHB and IA. 5. No deadline date extensions will be provided for DPR submission.
deadlines: Last date for submission of application is 31st July 2026 (6:00 PM, Friday). Last date for submission of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) by shortlisted applicants is 17th April 2026 (06:00 PM).
implementing_agency: National Horticulture Board (NHB), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

overview: The Handloom Weavers Comprehensive Welfare Scheme (HWCWS) is a component of the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) aimed at ensuring the welfare of handloom workers through provision of life and financial support to indigent handloom awardees. It is implemented by the Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms under the Ministry of Textiles. The scheme targets handloom weavers and their families, particularly those from disadvantaged sections of society, to provide social security and improve their livelihoods.
target_beneficiaries: handloom weavers; women; SC/ST; transgender; allied workers
eligibility: Handloom weavers and allied workers engaged in pre-loom (winding, warping, dyeing etc.) and post-loom activities (finishing, calendaring etc.), including Self Help Groups, producer companies, and other handloom agencies, particularly those belonging to disadvantaged sections of society such as SC, ST, women, transgender, and differently-abled individuals.
benefits: Life and accidental insurance cover under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana and Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, scholarships for school and higher education for wards of weavers, financial support to indigent handloom awardees, easy access to raw material at subsidized prices, enhanced capabilities including social security, better healthcare, life insurance, work sheds, and easy credit flow at low interest rate.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through life and accidental insurance coverage, scholarships for education of wards, and direct financial assistance to indigent handloom awardees. The scheme operates under the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) and is implemented via State Directorates of Handlooms and Textiles, Weavers' Service Centres, and other eligible handloom agencies. Funds are released in installments based on utilization certificates and project progress.
application_process: 1. State Directorate of Handlooms and Textiles submits project proposals to the Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms (O/o DC HL). 2. Proposals are scrutinized and approved by O/o DC HL based on recommendations from State Level Project Committees (SLPC). 3. Funds are released in two equal installments: 50% of GoI share as advance, and the second installment upon receipt of Utilization Certificate (UC) for at least 70% of the first installment. 4. Implementation is carried out by State Directorates, Weavers' Service Centres, National/State Level Handloom Organizations, Apex/Primary Handloom Weavers’ Co-operative Societies, Self Help Groups, and Producers’ Companies. 5. Monitoring and evaluation are conducted by State Implementation Monitoring & Review Committee (SIMRC) and National Implementation Monitoring & Review Committee (NIMRC).
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per State Directorate timelines.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles
contact_details: Email: wscguw@gmail.com (example from WSC Guwahati) | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

overview: The Workshed Scheme for Handloom Weavers provides financial assistance for the construction of individual and common worksheds to improve productivity and working conditions for handloom weavers. It is a component of the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) and aims to support weavers by providing infrastructure that enhances their earning potential and reduces drudgery. The scheme targets individual worksheds for BPL/SC/ST/Women/differently-abled weavers and common worksheds for groups of weavers, with funding patterns varying based on beneficiary category.
target_beneficiaries: handloom weavers; BPL; SC/ST; Women; differently-abled; Self Help Groups; Producers' Companies
eligibility: Individual Worksheds for BPL/SC/ST/Women/differently-abled are funded 100% by GoI. For others, Individual worksheds are funded in the ratio 75:25 by GoI:Beneficiary. Common Workshed is funded in the ratio 90:10 by GoI:Beneficiary. Solar Lighting System for Common Workshed is funded in the ratio 90:10 by GoI:Beneficiary. Implementing agencies include Central/State Government Organizations, National/State Level Handloom Organizations, Apex/Primary Handloom Weavers’ Co-operative Societies, Self Help Groups, and Producers’ Companies.
benefits: Financial assistance for construction of worksheds, improved productivity and working conditions, reduced drudgery, enhanced earning potential, infrastructure support for skill upgradation, access to concessional credit under Weaver MUDRA Scheme, marketing assistance, and integration with tourism through Craft Handloom Villages.
financial_support: Under the Small Cluster Development Programme (SCDP) of NHDP, need-based financial assistance is provided up to Rs. 2.00 crore (GoI share) per cluster for groups having up to 500 handloom workers. For individual worksheds: BPL/SC/ST/Women/differently-abled – 100% GoI share; Others – 75% GoI: 25% beneficiary. For common worksheds: 90% GoI: 10% beneficiary. For Solar Lighting System for Common Workshed: 90% GoI: 10% beneficiary. Funds are released in two equal installments: 50% of GoI share as advance, and the second installment on receipt of Utilization Certificate for at least 70% of the first installment.
application_process: 1. State Directorate submits proposals along with SLPC recommendations. 2. Proposals recommended by State Directorate are scrutinized and approved by O/o DC (HL). 3. If State Directorate does not forward cluster proposal within two months, WSC concerned submits directly to O/o DC (HL) with intimation to State Directorate. 4. If WSCs, IIHTs, or National Level Organizations are implementing agencies, they submit proposal directly to O/o DC (HL) under intimation to State Directorate. 5. Required documents include: Minutes of SLPC, Baseline Survey (Annexure A1), Diagnostic Study and Action Plan (Annexure A2), Profile of IA (Annexure A3), Profit & Loss Account and Balance Sheet for last two years (if applicable), NGO registration documents (if applicable), list of weavers for individual interventions (Annexure A7(I)), land details for common workshed, and solar lighting system details.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles

scheme_name: Yarn Supply Scheme for Handloom Weavers
overview: The Yarn Supply Scheme for Handloom Weavers is a component of the Raw Material Supply Scheme (RMSS) under the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP). It aims to provide subsidized yarn to handloom weavers through a structured supply mechanism involving yarn depots and warehouses. The scheme supports weavers by ensuring easy access to raw materials at subsidized prices, thereby reducing input costs and improving productivity.
target_beneficiaries: handloom weavers
eligibility: Handloom weavers, handloom agencies, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Producer Companies, and other eligible handloom entities as recommended by the State Government and approved by the Development Commissioner (Handlooms).
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of transport subsidy and price subsidy on yarn supply. Non-financial benefits include assured supply of quality yarn through a network of yarn depots and warehouses, reduced drudgery in procuring raw materials, and improved productivity and income for weavers.
financial_support: Under the Raw Material Supply Scheme, financial assistance is provided via transport subsidy and price subsidy on yarn. As per the Physical and Financial achievements as on 31.03.2024, a total of 9139.88 lakh kg of yarn was supplied under Transport Subsidy & Price Subsidy, benefitting 5.38 lakh handloom weavers. The supply mechanism involves 511 yarn depots and 46 warehouses functioning across the country.
application_process: 1. Handloom weavers or agencies approach the nearest Weavers' Service Centre (WSC) or State Directorate of Handlooms. 2. Submit application along with required documents. 3. Application is forwarded to the concerned authority for verification and approval. 4. Upon approval, yarn is supplied through designated yarn depots at subsidized rates. 5. Utilization Certificate (UC) may be required for continued support.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles
contact_details: Email: wscguw@gmail.com (example from WSC Guwahati); Helpline numbers available via Weavers' Service Centres; Central office: Dr. M. Beena, Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Udyog Bhawan, New Delhi

overview: The National SC/ST Hub (NSSH) is a central sector scheme launched by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India in October 2016, aimed at enhancing the capacity of SC/ST entrepreneurs and promoting an 'entrepreneurship culture' among the SC/ST population. It empowers SC/ST entrepreneurs to participate in public procurement and fulfill the mandated target of 4% procurement from SC/ST enterprises under the Public Procurement Policy. The scheme is implemented by the National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) and includes various sub-schemes such as Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS), Capacity Building Training Programs, Special Marketing Assistance Scheme (SMAS), and multiple reimbursement schemes for bank loan processing, testing fees, export promotion council membership, and more.
target_beneficiaries: SC/ST; MSME; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Sole Proprietorships, Partnerships, Co-operative societies, Private and Public limited companies owned by SC/ST Entrepreneurs of MSE sector engaged in the manufacturing and service activities are eligible for seeking assistance. It is mandatory to have a valid Udyam Registration for availing the subsidy under SCLCSS. For capacity building training programs, candidates belonging to SC/ST community and above 18 years of age on the date of commencement of training are eligible. For reimbursement schemes, SC/ST MSEs must have availed the relevant service (e.g., bank loan processing fee, testing fee, etc.) and submit required documents including Udyam Registration, PAN card, caste certificate, and proof of payment.
benefits: Benefits include reimbursement of bank loan processing charges (80% or up to Rs. 1,00,000, whichever is less), reimbursement of bank guarantee charges (80% or up to Rs. 1,00,000, whichever is less), reimbursement of testing fees (80% or up to Rs. 1,00,000, whichever is lower), reimbursement of export promotion council membership fees (80% or up to Rs. 20,000, whichever is less), reimbursement of course fees from top 50 NIRF-rated management institutions (90% or up to Rs. 1,00,000, whichever is lower), reimbursement of membership fees in government promoted e-commerce portals (80% or up to Rs. 25,000, whichever is less), reimbursement under Single Point Registration Scheme (100% subsidy with nominal fee of Rs. 100), capacity building training programs, special marketing assistance for domestic and international exhibitions, vendor development programs, and workshops/seminars/awareness campaigns with specified financial limits.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through various reimbursement schemes and subsidies. Under SCLCSS, a 25% subsidy is provided for procurement of plant and machinery/equipment through institutional credit, with an overall ceiling of Rs. 25 lakhs. Reimbursement schemes offer 80% or up to specified limits (e.g., Rs. 1,00,000 for bank loan processing, testing fees, bank guarantee charges; Rs. 20,000 for export promotion council membership; Rs. 25,000 for e-commerce portal membership; 90% or up to Rs. 1,00,000 for training course fees). Funds are released through the PFMS portal to the beneficiary's bank account after submission of claims and required documentation.
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 25 Lakh
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant sub-scheme (e.g., SCLCSS, reimbursement schemes, capacity building). 2. Ensure eligibility (SC/ST ownership, Udyam Registration, etc.). 3. Gather required documents (Udyam Registration, PAN card, caste certificate, proof of payment, bank statements, etc.). 4. Submit application either online via the NSSH website or through the concerned nodal agency (e.g., bank for SCLCSS, NSIC/NSSH office for reimbursements). 5. For reimbursement schemes, submit claim with supporting documents to the implementing agency (NSIC/NSSH) through PFMS. 6. Await verification and disbursement of funds to the beneficiary's bank account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — claims can be submitted throughout the year; for SCLCSS, timeline for acceptance is one year from the reference date (date of release/disbursement of last installment of term loan).
implementing_agency: National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), a public-sector undertaking under the administrative control of the Ministry of MSME
