overview: MeitY Startup Hub (MSH) is an initiative by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to support and nurture technology startups in India. It provides a platform for startups to access mentorship, funding, infrastructure, and market linkages. The hub focuses on fostering innovation in emerging technologies such as AI, IoT, blockchain, and electronics system design.
target_beneficiaries: startups; technology startups; electronics and IT startups
eligibility: Technology-based startups incorporated in India, working in areas such as electronics, IT, AI, IoT, blockchain, and other emerging technologies, with a focus on innovation and scalability.
benefits: Access to incubation facilities, mentorship from industry experts, networking opportunities, investor connect, prototype development support, testing and certification support, and guidance on regulatory compliance.
financial_support: MeitY Startup Hub provides support in accessing government grants, seed funding, and connections to venture capital and angel investors, though direct quantum of financial support is not specified in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Visit the MeitY Startup Hub official website at https://msh.meity.gov.in 2. Review eligibility criteria and program details 3. Submit an online application through the portal 4. Provide required documents including business plan, incorporation details, and technology focus 5. Await review by the selection committee 6. If selected, complete onboarding formalities to access incubation support.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

scheme_name: MUDRA Loan for Weavers (Weaver MUDRA Scheme)
overview: The MUDRA Loan for Weavers (Weaver MUDRA Scheme) is part of the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY), which provides loans up to ₹20 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises, including weavers. Launched on April 8, 2015, PMMY aims to fund the unfunded by extending credit through last-mile financiers such as banks, NBFCs, and MFIs. The scheme supports income-generating activities in manufacturing, processing, trading, services, and agri-allied sectors, with special focus on weaker sections including SC/ST/OBC and women entrepreneurs.
target_beneficiaries: weavers; micro enterprises; small businesses; SC/ST; OBC; women entrepreneurs; non-corporate entities
eligibility: Any Indian Citizen who has a business plan for a non-farm income generating activity such as manufacturing, processing, trading or service sector whose credit need is up to 20 lakh can approach either a Bank, MFI or NBFC for availing of MUDRA loans under PMMY. The usual terms and conditions of the lending agency may have to be followed for availing of loans under PMMY. The lending rates are as per the RBI guidelines issued in this regard from time to time.
benefits: MUDRA loans are extended for a variety of purposes which result in income generation and employment creation. The loans are extended mainly for: Business loan for Vendors, Traders, Shopkeepers and other Service Sector activities; Working capital loan through MUDRA Cards; Equipment Finance for Micro Units; Transport Vehicle loans for commercial use only; Loans for agri-allied non-farm income generating activities, e.g. pisciculture, bee keeping, poultry farming, etc.; Tractors, tillers as well as two wheelers used for commercial purposes only. MUDRA Card is a debit card issued against the MUDRA loan account, for working capital portion of the loan. The borrower can make use of MUDRA Card in multiple drawals and credits, so as to manage the working capital limit in cost-efficient manner and keep the interest burden minimum. MUDRA Card also helps in digitalization of MUDRA transactions and creating credit history for the borrower. MUDRA Card can be operated across the country for withdrawal of cash from any ATM / micro ATM and also make payment through any 'Point of Sale' machines.
financial_support: MUDRA is a refinancing Institution. MUDRA does not lend directly to the micro entrepreneurs / individuals. Mudra loans under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) can be availed of from nearby branch office of a bank, NBFC, MFIs etc. Borrowers can also now file online application for MUDRA loans on Udyamimitra portal (www.udyamimitra.in). Under the aegis of PMMY, MUDRA has created four products namely 'Shishu', 'Kishor', 'Tarun' and 'TarunPlus' to signify the stage of growth / development and funding needs of the beneficiary micro unit / entrepreneur and also provide a reference point for the next phase of graduation / growth. Shishu: covering loans upto 50,000/-; Kishor: covering loans above 50,000/- and upto 5 lakh; Tarun: covering loans above 5 lakh and upto 10 lakh; TarunPlus: covering loans above 10 lakh and upto 20 lakh. The refinance is available for term loan and working capital loan up to an amount of 20 lakh per unit. The eligible Banks/NBFCs/MFIs, who comply with the requirements as notified, can avail refinance from MUDRA for the loans given by them for eligible MUDRA compliant activities under Shishu, Kishore, Tarun and Tarun Plus categories.
application_process: 1. Approach any of the lending institutions mentioned above (Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, MFIs and NBFCs) or apply online through this portal www.udyamimitra.in. 2. File online application for MUDRA loans on Udyamimitra portal (www.udyamimitra.in). 3. Ensure the loan proposal is for a non-farm income generating activity such as manufacturing, processing, trading or service sector as well as agri-allied activities. 4. Ensure credit need is up to 20 lakh. 5. Follow the usual terms and conditions of the lending agency. 6. Avail the loan from the selected lending institution.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd. (MUDRA)

overview: The Cyber Security Centre of Excellence (CCoE) is an initiative under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at strengthening India's cybersecurity ecosystem through research, innovation, and collaboration. It focuses on developing indigenous cybersecurity solutions, building capacity, and fostering partnerships between government, industry, and academia. The CCoE serves as a hub for advancing cybersecurity technologies and practices to protect critical information infrastructure.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; academic institutions; research organizations
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include Indian startups, MSMEs, academic institutions, and research organizations working in the cybersecurity domain. Entities must be registered in India and demonstrate capability or potential in cybersecurity innovation, research, or solution development. Specific eligibility may vary based on the nature of engagement (e.g., incubation, collaboration, or funding support).
benefits: Benefits include access to cybersecurity infrastructure, mentorship from experts, funding support for prototype development, opportunities for technology transfer, collaboration with government and defense sectors, participation in cybersecurity drills and exercises, access to testing and certification facilities, and guidance on regulatory compliance and standards.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through grants, seed funding, or subsidies for prototype development, proof-of-concept, and scaling of cybersecurity innovations. The exact quantum and mechanism depend on the specific program or call for proposals under CCoE, with support typically disbursed in milestones based on project progress.
application_process: 1. Visit the official CCoE portal or MeitY website for announcements. 2. Check eligibility criteria for the specific program or call for proposals. 3. Prepare required documents including project proposal, company/incorporation details, and technical specifications. 4. Submit application through the designated online portal or email as specified in the announcement. 5. Applications are reviewed by an expert committee. 6. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for presentations or interviews. 7. Successful applicants receive approval and further instructions for fund disbursement or collaboration.
deadlines: Rolling basis — specific calls for proposals may have defined deadlines announced periodically.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: The IndiaAI Compute Initiative is a pillar of the IndiaAI Mission focused on building a scalable AI ecosystem with 10,000+ GPUs via public-private partnerships, offering AI services and resources to democratize computing access and support AI innovation across sectors.
target_beneficiaries: startups; researchers; enterprises; academic institutions
eligibility: Eligibility criteria are not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence for the IndiaAI Compute Initiative.
benefits: Benefits include access to scalable AI computing infrastructure (10,000+ GPUs), AI services and resources, support for indigenous AI model development, and facilitation of industry collaboration and innovation in the AI ecosystem.
financial_support: Financial support mechanisms are not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence for the IndiaAI Compute Initiative.
application_process: Application process details are not explicitly provided in the evidence for the IndiaAI Compute Initiative.
implementing_agency: IndiaAI Mission under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

scheme_name: Raw Material Supply Scheme (RMSS) for Handlooms
overview: The Raw Material Supply Scheme (RMSS) for Handlooms is a central sector scheme implemented by the Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms under the Ministry of Textiles. It aims to ensure easy access to raw materials at subsidized prices for handloom weavers by providing yarn through a network of yarn depots and warehouses. The scheme operates via a Yarn Passbook system and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism to supply yarn at subsidized rates, thereby reducing input costs and improving productivity and earnings of handloom weavers.
target_beneficiaries: handloom weavers; handloom agencies; self-help groups; producer companies; co-operative societies
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include handloom weavers, self-help groups, producer companies, primary handloom weavers’ cooperative societies, and other handloom agencies engaged in handloom production and recommended by State Directorates of Handlooms and Textiles and approved by the Development Commissioner (Handlooms).
benefits: Financial benefits include price subsidy and transport subsidy on yarn supplied under the scheme. Non-financial benefits include assured availability of yarn through a network of 511 yarn depots and 46 warehouses, streamlined supply via Yarn Passbook and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), and reduced drudgery in procuring raw materials. The scheme has supplied 9139.88 lakh kg of yarn and benefited 5.38 lakh handloom weavers as per achievements reported.
financial_support: Financial support is provided in the form of price subsidy and transport subsidy on yarn supplied to eligible handloom agencies and weavers. The subsidy is disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the bank accounts of beneficiaries. The scheme operates via a Yarn Passbook system where entitlements are tracked and yarn is supplied through authorized depots. Funds are released to implementing agencies based on verified utilization and submission of Utilization Certificates (UCs).
application_process: 1. Eligible handloom agencies or weavers apply through the State Directorate of Handlooms and Textiles. 2. The State Directorate forwards the proposal to the Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms (DCHL) for approval. 3. Upon approval, the agency is enrolled in the Yarn Passbook system. 4. Yarn is supplied through authorized yarn depots at subsidized rates. 5. Subsidy amount is transferred directly to the beneficiary’s bank account via DBT. 6. Utilization Certificate (UC) must be submitted for further fund releases.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year as per State Directorate recommendations and DCHL approval cycles.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles
contact_details: Email: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

overview: The National Green Hydrogen Mission is a flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at making India a global hub for the production, utilization, and export of green hydrogen and its derivatives. Launched under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), the mission seeks to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, decarbonize key sectors such as transportation, industry, and power, and achieve energy independence by 2047. It focuses on scaling up green hydrogen production through electrolyser manufacturing, demand creation, and pilot projects in end-use sectors.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers; industries; research institutions; startups; MSME
eligibility: Eligible entities include companies registered in India under the Companies Act, 2013 or earlier, central/public sector undertakings, state government entities, joint ventures, and consortiums. For the Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) programme, eligibility is open to manufacturers of electrolysers and producers of green hydrogen who meet technical and financial criteria as specified in the scheme guidelines issued by MNRE and SECI.
benefits: Financial incentives for setting up green hydrogen production and electrolyser manufacturing facilities; support for pilot projects in end-use sectors such as mobility, shipping, and steel; funding for research and development; facilitation of land and statutory clearances; creation of green hydrogen hubs; and support for development of export infrastructure and international partnerships.
financial_support: Under the SIGHT programme, financial incentives are provided in the form of direct subsidies for electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production. The incentive for electrolyser manufacturing is up to INR 4,440 per kW for a period of 5 years, and for green hydrogen production, it is up to INR 50 per kg for a period of 3 years, subject to annual caps. Funds are disbursed through the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) as the implementing agency.
grant_amount_per_entity: Incentive for electrolyser manufacturing: up to INR 4,440 per kW; for green hydrogen production: up to INR 50 per kg
application_process: 1. Eligible entities must register on the National Green Hydrogen Mission portal managed by SECI. 2. Submit an online application under the SIGHT programme for either electrolyser manufacturing or green hydrogen production. 3. Provide required documents including company incorporation details, technical specifications, financial statements, and land/clearance proofs. 4. Applications are evaluated by SECI based on technical and financial criteria. 5. Selected applicants receive a Letter of Award (LoA) and must sign an agreement with SECI. 6. After commissioning of the facility, incentives are disbursed based on verified performance.
deadlines: Applications are invited periodically through notifications issued by SECI; specific windows are announced in scheme guidelines. Not rolling basis.
implementing_agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), implemented through Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI)
contact_details: Email: nghm@seci.gov.in | Helpline: Not specified in evidence

overview: BharatNet is a flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at providing broadband connectivity to all Gram Panchayats (approximately 2.5 lakh) across the country. It seeks to bridge the digital divide by creating a robust, scalable, and affordable broadband infrastructure in rural and remote areas. The project is implemented in phases and leverages optical fibre technology to enable high-speed internet access for e-governance, education, health, and other socio-economic applications.
target_beneficiaries: rural populations; gram panchayats; government institutions; citizens in remote areas
eligibility: The scheme targets Gram Panchayats as the primary unit for connectivity. Implementation is carried out by Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL), a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) under the Department of Telecommunications. State governments and local bodies facilitate right-of-way and infrastructure sharing. Central and state funding is utilised based on a defined cost-sharing model.
benefits: High-speed broadband connectivity enabling access to digital services such as telemedicine, online education, e-agriculture, and digital banking. Supports implementation of government-to-citizen (G2C) and government-to-government (G2G) services. Enhances socio-economic development in rural areas by reducing information asymmetry and enabling digital entrepreneurship.
financial_support: The project is funded through a combination of government budgetary support, universal service obligation fund (USOF), and contributions from state governments. Financial assistance is provided in the form of subsidies for laying optical fibre, setting up network infrastructure, and operational sustainability. Funds are disbursed to BBNL and implementing agencies based on milestone achievement.
application_process: 1. Identification of Gram Panchayats for inclusion in the BharatNet project. 2. Submission of proposals by state governments or implementing agencies to the Department of Telecommunications. 3. Technical and financial appraisal of the project by BBNL and DoT. 4. Approval of the project and allocation of funds. 5. Execution of civil works, laying of optical fibre, and installation of equipment. 6. Testing, commissioning, and handover of network infrastructure. 7. Monitoring and maintenance for service continuity.
deadlines: Rolling basis — projects are sanctioned based on annual budget allocations and implementation readiness.
implementing_agency: Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL), under the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications

overview: The National Supercomputing Mission (NSM) is a joint initiative by the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at achieving self-reliance in supercomputing and enhancing India's capabilities in high-performance computing (HPC). The mission involves installing supercomputers across academic and R&D institutions, integrating them via the National Knowledge Network (NKN), and developing HPC-aware human resources. NSM supports research in diverse domains such as weather prediction, climate modeling, disaster management, computational biology, and AI through indigenous supercomputing systems like PARAM Shakti and PARAM Rudra.
target_beneficiaries: academic institutions; R&D labs; scientific community; researchers; students
eligibility: Academic and R&D institutions as well as key user departments/ministries participate by using NSM facilities to develop applications of national relevance. Access is provided through the National Knowledge Network (NKN).
benefits: Access to high-performance computing systems (e.g., PARAM Shakti, PARAM Rudra) for research in AI, quantum phenomena, turbulence simulations, catalyst design, flood prediction, urban modeling, and more. Enables high-impact publications, training of students, development of indigenous HPC software and hardware, and collaboration with agencies like IMD and municipal corporations for decision support systems.
financial_support: The Mission is implemented and steered jointly by the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) at an estimated cost of Rs. 4500 crore over a period of seven years.
application_process: 1. Identify research problem of national relevance requiring HPC resources. 2. Affiliate with an academic or R&D institution participating in NSM. 3. Submit proposal through institutional channels for access to NSM supercomputing facilities. 4. Proposal reviewed for scientific merit and alignment with NSM objectives. 5. Upon approval, allocate computing time on systems like PARAM Shakti or PARAM Rudra. 6. Utilize allocated resources for simulations, modeling, and analysis. 7. Submit outcomes and publications as part of mission deliverables.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year based on availability and review cycles.
implementing_agency: Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: The Semicon India Programme is a comprehensive initiative launched by the Government of India to develop a sustainable semiconductor and display manufacturing ecosystem in the country. It aims to position India as a global hub for electronics manufacturing and design through financial incentives, infrastructure development, and capacity building across the semiconductor value chain. The programme encompasses multiple schemes including the Scheme for Setting up of Semiconductor Fabs in India, Scheme for Setting up of Display Fabs in India, Scheme for Setting up of Compound Semiconductors/Silicon Photonics/Sensors Fab (including ATMP/OSAT) in India, and the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme.
target_beneficiaries: semiconductor manufacturers; display manufacturers; compound semiconductor/silicon photonics/sensors manufacturers; ATMP/OSAT units; design companies; startups; MSME
eligibility: Eligibility varies by specific scheme under Semicon India Programme. For semiconductor fabs: companies must propose to set up semiconductor wafer fabrication facilities in India. For display fabs: companies must propose to set up display panel fabrication facilities. For compound semiconductors/silicon photonics/sensors/ATMP/OSAT: entities must propose to set up respective facilities. For Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme: domestic companies, startups and MSMEs engaged in semiconductor design (including ICs, chipsets, SoCs, systems & IP cores) and semiconductor design linked deployment (including semiconductor design for use in IoT devices, automotive, aerospace, defense, communication, industrial automation, medical devices, etc.) are eligible. Applicants must be registered under Companies Act 2013 or earlier, or as a partnership firm or LLP, and must have necessary technical and financial capability to implement the project.
benefits: Financial incentives include fiscal support of up to 50% of project cost for setting up semiconductor and display fabs, and up to 30% of capital expenditure for compound semiconductors/silicon photonics/sensors and ATMP/OSAT facilities. Under the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme, incentives include: Product Design Linked Incentive (up to 50% of eligible expenditure, capped at ₹15 Crore per application), Deployment Linked Incentive (up to 6% of net sales turnover over 5 years), and Facility Linked Incentive (up to 30% of capital expenditure for design infrastructure). Additional benefits include infrastructure support, technology collaboration opportunities, access to semiconductor fab facilities for prototyping, and facilitation of partnerships with global semiconductor companies.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as fiscal incentives in the form of capital expenditure support. For semiconductor fabs and display fabs: up to 50% of the project cost. For compound semiconductors, silicon photonics, sensors, and ATMP/OSAT facilities: up to 30% of capital expenditure. Under the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme: Product Design Linked Incentive provides up to 50% of eligible expenditure (capped at ₹15 Crore per application), Deployment Linked Incentive provides up to 6% of net sales turnover over 5 years, and Facility Linked Incentive provides up to 30% of capital expenditure for setting up design infrastructure. The incentives are disbursed as reimbursement against verified expenditure or as periodic payouts based on achievement of milestones.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to 50% of project cost for semiconductor/display fabs (capped based on approval); up to ₹15 Crore per application under Product Design Linked Incentive (DLI Scheme)
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant scheme under Semicon India Programme based on the proposed activity (semiconductor fab, display fab, compound semiconductor/silicon photonics/sensor/ATMP/OSAT facility, or semiconductor design). 2. Prepare detailed project report including technical feasibility, financial viability, land acquisition plan, water and power requirements, environmental clearance status, and employment generation details. 3. Submit application online through the designated portal of the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM). 4. Application undergoes preliminary scrutiny for completeness and eligibility. 5. Technical evaluation by expert committee constituted by ISM. 6. Financial appraisal and due diligence. 7. Recommendation for approval by Inter-Ministerial Committee. 8. Final approval by the Union Cabinet or designated authority. 9. Signing of Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) or agreement with India Semiconductor Mission. 10. Disbursement of incentives in tranches based on achievement of project milestones and verification of expenditure.
deadlines: Applications are accepted periodically as per notification windows announced by India Semiconductor Mission; specific opening and closing dates are notified for each scheme under Semicon India Programme
implementing_agency: India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: The National Quantum Mission is a flagship initiative under the Electronics & IT category launched by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India. It aims to advance research, development, and innovation in quantum technologies, including quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing, and quantum metrology. The mission seeks to strengthen India's capabilities in strategic quantum technologies and promote technological self-reliance in alignment with the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision.
target_beneficiaries: startups; research institutions; academia; industry players
eligibility: The scheme is open to industry players, startups, research institutions, and academia engaged in quantum technology development. Eligible entities must be engaged in developing R&D-intensive quantum technologies at Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) 4 and above. Startups as defined by DPIIT Notification G.S.R. 127(E) dated 19 February 2019 are eligible. Entities must be legal entities such as companies registered under the Companies Act 2013, partnerships under the Indian Partnership Act 1932, or limited liability partnerships under the Limited Liability Partnership Act 2008.
benefits: Financial support through long-term loans at low or nil interest rates, equity infusion especially for startups, and contributions to the Deep-Tech Fund of Funds. Non-financial benefits include access to specialized infrastructure, mentorship, collaboration opportunities with research organizations, and facilitation of technology transfer. The scheme also supports patent filing, commercialization, and scaling of quantum innovations through second-level fund managers.
financial_support: The mission operates under the Research, Development, and Innovation (RDI) Scheme with a total outlay of ₹1 lakh crore. Modes of financing include long-term loans at low or nil interest rates and equity infusion, particularly for startups. Grants and short-term loans are not supported. Financing can cover up to 50% of assessed project cost for transformative R&D projects at TRLs 4 and above, with exceptions possible via the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS). Funds are channeled through Second-Level Fund Managers (SLFMs) such as Alternate Investment Funds (AIFs), Development Finance Institutions (DFIs), NBFCs, or Focused Research Organizations (FROs).
application_process: 1. Interested Second Level Fund Managers (SLFMs) express interest by contacting Dr Jyoti Sharma, Head, RDI Cell at sharma[dot]jyoti[at]nic[dot]in. 2. Existing NBFCs planning to establish AIFs are encouraged to contact DST for potential participation. 3. Industry stakeholders seeking funding must not submit proposals directly to DST. 4. All disbursements are routed exclusively through designated SLFMs via separate advertisement. 5. For more details, visit https://rdifund.anrf.gov.in/. 6. Applications are evaluated based on project viability, innovation, and alignment with strategic technology goals.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology
contact_details: Email: sharma[dot]jyoti[at]nic[dot]in | Phone: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

scheme_name: Solar Parks & Ultra Mega Solar Power Projects
overview: Solar Parks & Ultra Mega Solar Power Projects is a scheme launched by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) on 12-12-2014 to support the development of solar parks and ultra mega solar power projects across India. The scheme aims to facilitate large-scale solar power generation by providing developed land with necessary infrastructure such as transmission systems, water access, road connectivity, and communication networks. It targets the establishment of at least 25 solar parks with a cumulative capacity exceeding 20,000 MW within five years starting from 2014-15. SECI acts as an implementing agency for this scheme, facilitating grant disbursement and project monitoring.
target_beneficiaries: State Governments; Union Territories; Implementing Agencies designated by State Governments
eligibility: All States and Union Territories are eligible to benefit under the scheme. The implementing agency for developing and maintaining the solar park is chosen by the State Government. The scheme allows for solar parks of 500 MW and above, with smaller parks considered in Himalayan and other hilly states where contiguous land is difficult to acquire or in states with acute shortage of non-agricultural land.
benefits: The scheme provides developed land with all necessary clearances, transmission systems, water access, road connectivity, and communication networks. It facilitates access to Central Financial Assistance (CFA) for solar park development. Implementing agencies receive grants for preparing Detailed Project Reports (DPR) and for project costs including grid-connectivity. The scheme accelerates solar power project installation by reducing land acquisition and infrastructure development timelines. It enables states to meet solar renewable purchase obligations and supports India’s renewable energy targets under the National Solar Mission.
financial_support: The implementing agency is sanctioned a grant of up to Rs. 25 Lakh per park for preparing the Detailed Project Report (DPR). Subsequently, the implementing agency may apply to SECI for a grant of up to Rs. 20 lakhs per MW or 30% of the project cost (including grid-connectivity cost), whichever is lower. The approved grant is released by SECI as per milestones prescribed in the scheme. As of 31st December 2014, a grant of Rs. 141.50 Crore has been released to SECI by the Ministry for this scheme.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 25 Lakh per park for DPR and up to Rs. 20 lakhs/MW or 30% of project cost (including grid-connectivity), whichever is lower
application_process: 1. State Government designates an implementing agency for the solar park. 2. The implementing agency prepares the Detailed Project Report (DPR) and applies for a grant of up to Rs. 25 Lakh from SECI for DPR preparation. 3. Upon DPR approval, the implementing agency applies to SECI for the main project grant of up to Rs. 20 lakhs/MW or 30% of the project cost (including grid-connectivity), whichever is lower. 4. SECI appraises the application and sanctions the grant. 5. Grant is released by SECI in installments linked to project milestones. 6. SECI monitors the project progress and ensures compliance with scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI)

scheme_name: UJALA Scheme – Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs

overview: The Small Hydro Power Programme (SHP) under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) supports the development of small hydro projects (up to 25 MW capacity) to enhance renewable energy capacity in India. The scheme provides Central Financial Assistance (CFA) for project implementation, including survey and investigation, and aims to promote clean energy generation in remote and hilly areas. It is implemented in coordination with State Nodal Agencies and focuses on grid-connected and off-grid applications.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; private developers; public sector undertakings; cooperative societies
eligibility: Eligible entities include State Governments, State Power Utilities, Public Sector Undertakings, private developers, and cooperative societies. Projects must have a capacity of up to 25 MW and be technically feasible as per CEA guidelines. Preference is given to projects in hilly and remote areas. The implementing agency must submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR) and obtain necessary clearances.
benefits: Financial support through Central Financial Assistance (CFA) for survey, investigation, and project implementation. Technical guidance from MNRE and its institutes. Facilitation of clearances and approvals. Promotion of renewable energy in underserved regions. Contribution to national renewable energy targets and reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.
financial_support: Central Financial Assistance (CFA) is provided at 90% of the project cost for survey and investigation (up to ₹10 lakh per project) and up to ₹5 crore per MW for project implementation, subject to a ceiling of ₹20 crore per project. For special category states (North Eastern and Himalayan states), CFA is enhanced to 100% for survey and investigation and up to ₹7 crore per MW for implementation. Funds are released in instalments based on project milestones.
application_process: 1. Identify a potential small hydro site and prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) as per CEA guidelines. 2. Obtain necessary clearances from concerned authorities (e.g., forest, environment, irrigation). 3. Submit the DPR along with application to the State Nodal Agency (SNA). 4. SNA forwards the proposal to MNRE for appraisal. 5. MNRE appraises the proposal through the Project Appraisal Committee (PAC). 6. Upon approval, administrative sanction is issued by MNRE. 7. Funds are released in instalments based on project progress and submission of utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)

overview: PM-WANI (WiFi Access Network Interface) is a scheme launched by the Department of Telecommunications under the Ministry of Communications to provide public Wi-Fi services through Public Data Offices (PDOs) and PDO aggregators, aiming to expand broadband access across India by enabling last-mile connectivity via Wi-Fi hotspots. The scheme promotes interoperability and ease of access for users through a centralized registry and authentication system, encouraging the proliferation of Wi-Fi networks in public spaces.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; entrepreneurs; small businesses
eligibility: Any entity, including startups, MSMEs, entrepreneurs, or small businesses, can apply to become a Public Data Office (PDO) or PDO aggregator under PM-WANI, provided they comply with the technical and operational guidelines issued by the Department of Telecommunications, including registration on the designated portal and adherence to security and service quality standards.
benefits: PM-WANI enables easy setup and operation of Wi-Fi hotspots without requiring individual licensing for each access point, provides a centralized authentication and billing system through PDO aggregators, offers revenue-sharing opportunities for PDO owners, promotes digital inclusion by expanding internet access in underserved areas, and supports the growth of a distributed Wi-Fi ecosystem across India.
financial_support: PM-WANI does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants to entities; instead, it enables revenue generation through user fees collected at Public Data Offices (PDOs), with PDO aggregators facilitating billing, settlement, and reimbursement processes. Financial returns depend on user uptake and service usage, with no guaranteed or fixed financial support from the government.
application_process: 1. Visit the PM-WANI portal on the Department of Telecommunications website. 2. Register as a Public Data Office (PDO) or PDO aggregator by providing entity details. 3. Submit required documents including proof of identity, address, and business registration. 4. Await verification and approval from the designated authority. 5. Upon approval, deploy Wi-Fi access points and integrate with the PM-WANI ecosystem for authentication and service delivery.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications

overview: The National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy aims to promote large grid-connected wind-solar PV hybrid systems for optimal and efficient utilization of transmission infrastructure and land, reducing the variability in renewable power generation and achieving better grid stability. It encourages new hybrid projects as well as hybridization of existing wind or solar projects. The policy provides a framework for promoting hybrid projects through various fiscal and financial incentives, and outlines the methodology for determining the tariff for hybrid projects.
target_beneficiaries: power producers; renewable energy developers; independent power producers (IPPs); state utilities
eligibility: The policy applies to all wind and solar power projects, including existing projects seeking hybridization and new hybrid projects. Projects must be grid-connected and comply with the technical standards and grid connectivity norms as specified by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA). The hybridization must ensure optimal utilization of infrastructure and must not exceed the sanctioned capacity at the point of interconnection.
benefits: Benefits include optimal utilization of transmission infrastructure and land, reduced variability in power output leading to better grid stability, extended hours of power generation, and eligibility for various fiscal and financial incentives available for wind and solar power projects under existing schemes. Hybrid projects can avail of benefits such as accelerated depreciation, concessional customs duty exemption, and priority sector lending, as per the provisions of the respective wind and solar policies.
financial_support: The policy does not provide direct financial subsidies but enables access a dedicated fund but allows hybrid projects to avail of financial benefits under existing wind and solar schemes, such as generation-based incentives (GBI), accelerated depreciation, and concessional finance through institutions like IREDA. The quantum of support depends on the specific scheme under which the project is availing benefits.
application_process: 1. Project developers must submit a detailed project report (DPR) to the Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI) or the respective state nodal agency. 2. The DPR must include details of wind and solar components, hybridization methodology, single point of grid connection, and compliance with CEA technical standards. 3. SECI or the state nodal agency evaluates the proposal for technical feasibility and grid impact. 4. Upon approval, the project is registered and proceeds to implementation. 5. After commissioning, the project can apply for applicable incentives under wind and solar policies through the respective implementing agencies.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
contact_details: Email: info@mnre.gov.in | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

overview: Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to correct regional imbalances in the availability of affordable and reliable tertiary healthcare services and to augment facilities for quality medical education in the country. The scheme involves setting up new AIIMS-like institutions and upgrading existing government medical colleges and institutions.
target_beneficiaries: general public; medical students; healthcare professionals
eligibility: The scheme is implemented through the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Eligibility for benefits under PMSSY is generally for patients seeking treatment at the upgraded or newly established institutions, and for medical education opportunities at these facilities. Specific eligibility criteria for admission to courses or treatment are determined by the respective institutions.
benefits: Benefits include access to affordable tertiary healthcare services, improved medical education infrastructure, increased availability of specialist doctors, and enhanced healthcare delivery in underserved regions through the establishment of new AIIMS and upgradation of medical colleges.
financial_support: The scheme provides central financial assistance for the capital cost of setting up new AIIMS and for the upgradation of existing government medical colleges. The funding mechanism involves central government grants to the implementing agencies for civil works, medical equipment, and other infrastructure development.
application_process: As PMSSY involves infrastructure development and service delivery through established institutions, there is no direct application process for beneficiaries to access the scheme. Benefits are availed by seeking treatment or admission at the respective AIIMS or upgraded medical colleges under their normal admission and treatment procedures.
deadlines: Not applicable — benefits are accessed through ongoing hospital services and academic admissions at the respective institutions.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

overview: The Offshore Wind Energy Policy is a government initiative aimed at promoting the development of offshore wind energy projects in India. It seeks to harness the country's offshore wind potential to contribute to renewable energy targets and reduce dependence on fossil fuels. The policy includes provisions for viability gap funding and other incentives to attract investment in offshore wind projects.
target_beneficiaries: project developers; investors; energy companies
eligibility: Project developers and investors interested in setting up offshore wind energy projects in India are eligible to apply under the policy. Specific eligibility criteria may include technical and financial capability, compliance with regulatory norms, and adherence to environmental and safety standards as outlined in the scheme guidelines.
benefits: The policy offers financial support through mechanisms such as Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to make offshore wind projects economically viable. It also provides regulatory facilitation, single-window clearances, and support for grid connectivity and infrastructure development. Additionally, it encourages domestic manufacturing and job creation in the renewable energy sector.
financial_support: Under the Offshore Wind Energy Policy, financial support is provided via the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for 1,000 MW of offshore wind energy projects. The exact quantum and disbursement mechanism are defined in the scheme guidelines, with funding aimed at bridging the gap between project costs and revenue to ensure financial viability.
application_process: The application process involves submitting proposals through the designated portal or agency as specified in response to calls for proposals under the policy. Applicants must comply with technical, financial, and environmental requirements, and undergo evaluation for sanction of financial assistance. Specific steps are outlined in the scheme documents and related notifications.
implementing_agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)

overview: The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) Scheme is a flagship initiative of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) under the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE, targeting energy-intensive industries through mechanism where energy consumption norms and excess energy savings are converted into tradable Energy Savings Certificates (ESCerts). The scheme operates in cycles of three years each, with targets assigned to Designated Consumers (DCs) from notified sectors such as aluminum, cement, iron & steel, thermal power plants, etc., and has been implemented across multiple cycles since its inception.
target_beneficiaries: Designated Consumers; energy intensive industries
eligibility: Industrial units from notified energy intensive sectors (Aluminum, Cement, Chlor-Alkali, Fertilizer, Iron & Steel, Paper & Pulp, Railways, Thermal Power and Textile) that meet the threshold level of annual energy consumption as specified in the notifications issued under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, and are designated as Designated Consumers (DCs) by the Central Government.
benefits: Financial benefits through trading of Energy Savings Certificates (ESCerts) on power exchanges; recognition for achieving energy efficiency targets; contribution to national energy savings and reduction in GHG emissions; facilitation of investment in energy efficient technologies and processes; access to technical guidance and user manuals developed by BEE for effective implementation.
financial_support: The PAT scheme does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants. Instead, it operates as a market-based mechanism where Designated Consumers (DCs) that achieve energy savings beyond their targets are issued Energy Savings Certificates (ESCerts), which can be traded on power exchanges, thereby providing a financial incentive. Investments in energy efficiency measures are made by the DCs themselves, and the scheme has mobilized significant private sector investment, as evidenced by reports indicating DCs made investments of approximately INR 43,721 Crores in PAT Cycle II to achieve energy savings.
application_process: 1. Identification of energy intensive sectors and notification of threshold levels for designation as Designated Consumers (DCs). 2. Notification of energy consumption norms and targets for each PAT cycle by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE). 3. Designated Consumers (DCs) implement energy efficiency measures to meet or exceed their specific energy consumption (SEC) reduction targets. 4. Monitoring and verification of energy savings achieved by DCs through accredited energy auditors. 5. Issuance of Energy Savings Certificates (ESCerts) to DCs achieving excess savings beyond targets. 6. Trading of ESCerts on power exchanges (such as Indian Energy Exchange) by DCs that have surplus certificates, and purchase by DCs needing to meet their targets.
deadlines: Based on PAT cycle notifications; each cycle spans three years with specific target year and verification periods as per official notifications (e.g., PAT Cycle VII notified in October 2021 for period 2022-23 to 2024-25).
implementing_agency: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, Government of India

overview: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) aims to develop the backbone necessary to support the integrated digital health infrastructure of the country by bridging the existing gap amongst different stakeholders of the healthcare ecosystem through digital highways. It enables citizens to generate a unique health identifier called Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) to access and share health records digitally. The mission includes components such as ABHA Number, Health Facility Registry, Healthcare Professionals Registry, Unified Health Interface, and National Health Claims Exchange.
target_beneficiaries: citizens; health facilities; healthcare professionals; health tech companies; states
eligibility: Citizens or individuals can generate a unique health identifier called the Ayushman Bharat Health Account or ABHA. Health facilities (public and private) across all systems of medicine can register on the Health Facility Registry. Healthcare professionals (doctors, nurses, paramedics, allied health workers) across all systems of medicine can register on the Healthcare Professionals Registry. Health tech companies can engage with ABDM to integrate and validate software systems with ABDM APIs. State governments and health authorities can adopt ABDM to improve healthcare services.
benefits: Citizens can access and share health records digitally, receive digital lab reports, prescriptions, and diagnosis seamlessly from verified healthcare providers. Health facilities get connected to India's digital health ecosystem. Healthcare professionals get connected to India's digital health ecosystem. Health tech companies benefit from increasing market demand for ABDM-compliant HMIS, increased credibility for ABDM-certified products, and improved ease of doing business. States improve healthcare planning and management, formulate data-driven policies, and enhance healthcare availability, accessibility, and quality for citizens.
financial_support: The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission does not provide direct financial support to beneficiaries. It is a digital infrastructure initiative focused on creating registries, enabling interoperability, and providing digital health services. Financial aspects are not detailed in the evidence; the mission operates through government funding and partnerships without specifying grants, loans, or subsidies to end users.
application_process: 1. For citizens: Visit https://abha.abdm.gov.in/register to generate an ABHA number. 2. For health facilities: Visit https://facility.abdm.gov.in/ to register on the Health Facility Registry. 3. For healthcare professionals: Visit https://hpr.abdm.gov.in/en to register on the Healthcare Professionals Registry. 4. For health tech companies: Integrate and validate software systems with ABDM APIs via the ABDM Sandbox at https://sandbox.abdm.gov.in/. 5. For states: Refer to https://abdm.gov.in/resources/for-states for strategic overview and technical guidelines, and check adoption status at https://dashboard.abdm.gov.in/abdm/. 6. For e-Sushrut Clinic registration: Visit https://ehmis-lite.in/AHIMSG5/hissso/logoutLogin, generate or validate HPR ID, generate or validate HFR ID, and complete onboarding.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: National Health Authority (NHA), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
contact_details: Email: abdm[at]nha[dot]gov[dot]in | Toll-free-number: 1800-11-4477 | Contact Address: 9th Floor, Tower-I, Jeevan Bharati Building, Connaught Place, New Delhi - 110 001

overview: The Medical Devices Park Scheme aims to provide world-class infrastructure and common facilities for the manufacturing of medical devices in India. It seeks to reduce import dependence, promote domestic manufacturing, and create an ecosystem for innovation and export in the medical devices sector. The scheme supports the development of medical device parks with plug-and-play facilities, testing labs, and other shared infrastructure to attract investment and boost the industry.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers; MSME; startups; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligible entities include companies, consortiums, or special purpose vehicles (SPVs) registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or any other relevant law, engaged in or planning to engage in the manufacturing of medical devices. The implementing agency will evaluate proposals based on technical feasibility, financial viability, and potential for employment generation and export promotion.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grant-in-aid for creation of common infrastructure facilities such as roads, water supply, power distribution, effluent treatment, and testing labs. Non-financial benefits include facilitation of clearances, single-window approval, and access to shared testing and certification facilities. The scheme also provides plug-and-play infrastructure to reduce setup time and cost for manufacturers.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-in-aid up to 70% of the project cost for setting up common infrastructure facilities in medical device parks, with a maximum ceiling of INR 100 crore per park. The remaining 30% of the project cost is to be borne by the implementing entity. Funds are disbursed in installments based on achievement of predefined milestones.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 100 crore per medical device park
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed project report (DPR) along with the application form to the implementing agency. 2. The DPR must include details on land availability, project layout, proposed facilities, financial plan, and employment generation. 3. Applications are evaluated by a technical committee appointed by the Department of Pharmaceuticals Department of Pharmaceuticals. 4. Shortlisted proposals undergo site verification and due diligence. 5. Upon approval, a formal sanction letter is issued. 6. Funds are released in stages based on milestone completion verified by the agency.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers

overview: The Bulk Drug Parks Scheme aims to develop world-class infrastructure for bulk drug manufacturing in India by establishing dedicated parks with common facilities. It seeks to reduce manufacturing costs, enhance competitiveness, and ensure a steady supply of critical drugs. The scheme supports the creation of integrated infrastructure including common effluent treatment plants, solvent recovery systems, and logistics hubs. It is designed to promote self-reliance in pharmaceutical manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports.
target_beneficiaries: bulk drug manufacturers; pharmaceutical companies; MSME; large enterprises
eligibility: Entities eligible for setting up Bulk Drug Parks include State Government agencies, Government-owned corporations, joint ventures with equity participation from State Governments, and private sector companies selected through a transparent bidding process. The implementing agency will be a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) formed by the State Government or its nominee.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grant-in-aid for common infrastructure facilities. Non-financial benefits include plug-and-play infrastructure, common effluent treatment plants, solvent recovery systems, steam and power supply, water supply, logistics support, and safety and security services. The scheme enables economies of scale and reduces capital expenditure for individual units.
financial_support: The Government of India provides grant-in-aid limited to 70% of the project cost for common infrastructure facilities, with a maximum of INR 1000 Crore per Bulk Drug Park. For Himachal Pradesh and other hill states, the grant is increased to 90% of the project cost. The remaining 30% (or 10% for hill states) is to be contributed by the State Government and the SPV.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 1000 Crore per Bulk Drug Park
application_process: 1. State Governments submit proposals for setting up Bulk Drug Parks to the Department of Pharmaceuticals. 2. Proposals are evaluated based on predefined criteria including land availability, water and power connectivity, environmental clearance status, and industrial ecosystem. 3. Selected proposals are accorded 'In-Principle' approval. 4. After obtaining necessary statutory clearances, the State Governments form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV). 5. The SPV submits a Detailed Project Report (DPR) for final approval. 6. Upon approval, funds are released in installments based on progress milestones. 7. The SPV undertakes implementation of common infrastructure facilities. 8. Facilities are made operational and allotted to bulk drug manufacturers on lease or ownership basis.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per notifications issued by the Department of Pharmaceuticals.
implementing_agency: Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers

overview: The Standards & Labelling Programme (BEE) is a flagship initiative of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) under the Ministry of Power, Government of India. It aims to provide consumers with an informed choice about energy-saving and cost-saving potential of appliances through star labeling. The programme covers a wide range of appliances and equipment, promoting energy efficiency by enabling comparison and encouraging the adoption of energy-efficient products in the market.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers; consumers; retailers
eligibility: Manufacturers can file their applications online for star labelling of appliances under the S&L programme. The list of BEE approved models is available in the public domain through linkage of the S & L application with the website of BEE.
benefits: Star Labels on an appliance enable a Consumer to know the performance of an appliance, eventually helping a Consumer to make informed decisions on cost and energy saving potential at the time of purchase. With the adoption of Unique QR code on every appliance under the S & L scheme, BEE wants to ensure the authenticity of the labels used in the market, so that misuse of Star Labels can be obviated by empowering the Consumer to retrieve and verify the technical specifications displayed on the star label affixed on an appliance with ease from registered appliance database of BEE using a phone by scanning or a text message. Manufacturers would be mandated to affix QR codes for every appliance bearing a BEE star label. Moreover, the adoption of QR Code eco-system should portray a relevant picture of the Indian Appliance Market scenario, by tracking the sales in different categories of appliances at various stages in respective supply chains with the help of QR Codes. Further, it is expected that this QR Code based eco-system shall enable manufacturers/ distributors/ retailers, log the sale of appliances with the help of existing BEE star label mobile app directly in the BEE database. BEE aims to deploy QR Code as a fail-proof way to adopt and implement anti counterfeit of BEE labels and to capture appliance sales. Mobile App: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) has developed a mobile application for Standards and Labeling (S & L) program for consumers. The app is linked with S & L database of BEE, thus it provides a platform to receive real-time feedback from consumers and other stakeholders. The data in the app is updated daily. Currently, consumers rely on energy efficiency information that is presented on star label. Mobile application will allow consumers to instantly compare personalized energy savings across all products of a specific class and thus enabling consumers to choose more efficient products that are available in the market. The app can be downloaded on android and iOS (BEE Star Label). BEE also published advertisement in national newspapers to promote the usage of the app and is using the app as an awareness and outreach medium under the S & L program as well as guide to consumers for purchasing decision.
financial_support: The promotional role of BEE includes giving financial assistance to institutions for promoting efficient use of energy and its conservation. However, specific financial support details for the Standards & Labelling Programme are not explicitly mentioned in the provided evidence.
application_process: 1. Manufacturers can file their applications online. 2. Easy tracking of applications filed by manufacturers. 3. Reports can be downloaded easily. 4. Minimizes paperwork. 5. The list of BEE approved models is available in the public domain through linkage of the S & L application with the website of BEE. 6. More effective communication between manufacturers and BEE. 7. Analysis of energy savings and generation of reports thereof. 8. Integration of SMS gateways and Payment gateways for smoother operations.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, Govt. of India
contact_details: Please contact BEE help desk at helpdesk[at]beenet[dot]in and 011-26766700, for any issues.

scheme_name: National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE)
overview: The National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE) is one of the eight national missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC). Its primary objective is to develop regulations and policies that strengthen the market for energy efficiency through self-regulation and market principles, including capacity building and financing. NMEEE includes flagship programmes such as Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT), Standards & Labelling, and initiatives for SMEs, buildings, transport, and agriculture.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; industries; designated consumers; state designated agencies; energy service companies
eligibility: Eligibility varies by sub-scheme under NMEEE. For the Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme, energy intensive units from sectors such as Aluminum, Cement, Chlor-Alkali, Fertilizer, Iron & Steel, Paper & Pulp, Railways, Thermal Power and Textile are notified as Designated Consumers based on specific energy consumption norms. For SME programmes, eligibility is based on MSME classification as per MSME Act. For Standards & Labelling, manufacturers of appliances and equipment can apply for star rating certification.
benefits: Benefits include energy savings, reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, cost savings, issuance of tradable Energy Savings Certificates (ESCerts) under PAT, access to financing for energy efficiency projects, technical support and capacity building, star labelling for appliances promoting consumer awareness, and implementation support for Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC) in commercial buildings.
financial_support: Financial support under NMEEE includes innovative financing mechanisms for energy efficiency projects, such as the BEE-WB-SIDBI-GEF project for MSMEs, and leveraging multi-lateral and bi-lateral support. The PAT scheme allows trading of Energy Savings Certificates (ESCerts) on power exchanges, creating a market-based financial incentive. Financial assistance is also provided to institutions for promoting efficient use of energy and its conservation.
application_process: Application processes vary by sub-scheme. For PAT, designated consumers are notified by the Central Government based on energy consumption norms and must comply with notified norms, rules and regulations. For Standards & Labelling, manufacturers can file applications online through the BEE web portal for star labelling of appliances. For SME programmes, interested entities can apply through designated channels as per specific programme guidelines. For ECBC, implementation is at state and local level through integration in municipal bye-laws.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, Government of India

overview: The National Ayush Mission (NAM) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Ayush to promote AYUSH systems of healthcare through cost-effective services, strengthen educational systems, ensure availability of quality raw materials, and sustainably manage medicinal plants. It aims to improve access to AYUSH services, particularly in vulnerable and underserved areas, by upgrading AYUSH hospitals and dispensaries, co-locating AYUSH facilities at primary health centres, and supporting cultivation and conservation of medicinal plants.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; ayush institutions; farmers; medicinal plant growers; ayush practitioners
eligibility: State Governments and Union Territories are eligible to avail financial assistance under the National Ayush Mission. The scheme supports AYUSH institutions, farmers engaged in medicinal plant cultivation, and organizations involved in the conservation and sustainable management of medicinal plants. Eligibility is based on state-specific project proposals submitted through State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) approved by the Ministry of Ayush.
benefits: Financial assistance for upgrading AYUSH hospitals and dispensaries, setting up integrated AYUSH hospitals, co-locating AYUSH facilities at PHCs/CHCs/DHs, establishing AYUSH wellness centres, supporting cultivation and conservation of medicinal plants, strengthening AYUSH educational institutions, and promoting AYUSH research and development. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, quality standards for AYUSH drugs, and support for insurance coverage of AYUSH treatments through benchmark rates.
financial_support: The National Ayush Mission provides grant-in-aid to State Governments and Union Territories based on approved State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs). Funding covers infrastructure development, procurement of equipment, supply of medicines, human resource engagement, and program management. The financial support is released in installments subject to utilization certificates and progress reports. The scheme operates as a centrally sponsored scheme with cost-sharing between the Centre and States (typically 60:40 for most states and 90:10 for Northeastern and Himalayan states).
application_process: 1. State Governments/UTs prepare State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) based on local needs and scheme guidelines. 2. SAAPs are submitted to the Ministry of Ayush for appraisal and approval. 3. Upon approval, funds are released in installments to the State Nodal Agency. 4. States implement projects through designated implementing agencies. 5. Progress is monitored through quarterly reports, utilization certificates, and field visits. 6. Subsequent releases are contingent on satisfactory utilization of previous installments.
deadlines: Annual cycle — SAAPs are typically submitted before the start of each financial year for approval.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

scheme_name: PM SHRI Schools (PM Schools for Rising India)
overview: PM SHRI Schools (PM Schools for Rising India) is a centrally sponsored scheme by the Government of India aimed at developing more than 14,500 schools managed by Central Government, State/UT Governments, local bodies, KVS, and NVS. The initiative seeks to provide a safe, stimulating, and inclusive learning environment with quality infrastructure and resources, aligned with the National Education Policy 2020. It targets over 20 lakh students as direct beneficiaries and aims to scale up learnings to other schools nationwide. The scheme is implemented over a five-year period from 2022-23 to 2026-27.
target_beneficiaries: students
eligibility: Schools managed by Central Government, State/UT Government, local bodies including Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS) and Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (NVS) are eligible to be developed under the PM SHRI Schools scheme.
benefits: Students benefit from a safe and stimulating learning environment, wide range of learning experiences, good physical infrastructure, and appropriate resources conducive to learning. The scheme aims to nurture students to become engaged, productive, and contributing citizens for building an equitable, inclusive, and plural society as envisaged by the National Education Policy 2020. It also promotes understanding of various dimensions of quality in school education to inform policy, practice, and implementation, with learnings scaled up to other schools.
financial_support: As a centrally sponsored scheme, financial support is provided by the Government of India for the development and upgradation of PM SHRI Schools, though specific quantum, type, and mechanism details are not explicitly stated in the evidence.
application_process: The application process is not detailed in the provided evidence. Information regarding application steps for schools to join the PM SHRI Schools scheme is not available on the reviewed pages.

scheme_name: IMPRINT India (Impacting Research Innovation and Technology)
overview: IMPRINT India (Impacting Research Innovation and Technology) is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Defence aimed at addressing major engineering and technology challenges relevant to national development through collaborative research between premier academic institutions and user agencies. The scheme focuses on translating research into usable technologies and products by funding high-impact, interdisciplinary projects in identified thematic areas.
target_beneficiaries: academic institutions; researchers; scientists; faculty members; user agencies
eligibility: The scheme invites project proposals from faculty members and researchers of premier academic institutions such as IITs, IISc, NITs, IISERs, and other centrally funded technical institutions. Proposals must be submitted in collaboration with identified user agencies (e.g., Defence Research and Development Organisation, Indian Space Research Organisation, Ministry of Railways, etc.) that define the problem statement and commit to potential adoption of the developed technology.
benefits: Financial support for research and development projects, access to user agency problem statements and domain expertise, opportunity for technology transfer and product development, enhanced visibility and impact of academic research, potential for commercialization and strategic deployment of outcomes, and facilitation of industry-academia-government collaboration.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-based financial support to selected research projects, with funding typically covering manpower, equipment, consumables, travel, and contingency costs. The quantum of support varies per project based on scope and duration, and is disbursed in installments tied to project milestones and deliverables as agreed upon with the user agency.
application_process: 1. Identify a relevant challenge area under the IMPRINT India thematic domains. 2. Form a consortium with academic partners and a user agency that defines the problem statement. 3. Develop a detailed project proposal including objectives, methodology, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 4. Submit the proposal through the designated portal or nodal agency (currently IIT Madras acts as the coordinating hub). 5. Proposals undergo technical review by expert committees. 6. Selected projects are approved for funding and implementation begins upon sanction.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per announcements from the coordinating agency.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Education, Government of India (in collaboration with Ministry of Defence and other user agencies)

overview: The National Tele Mental Health Programme (Tele-MANAS) is a comprehensive mental health care service launched by the Government of India to provide universal access to equitable, accessible, affordable and quality mental health care through 24x7 tele-mental health services. It operates as a digital component of the National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) across all Indian States and UTs, offering toll-free helpline services, video consultations, e-prescriptions, and linkages to in-person services. The programme aims to scale up mental health service reach, extend services to vulnerable and hard-to-reach populations, and provide integrated medical and psychosocial interventions.
target_beneficiaries: general public; individuals with mental health issues; vulnerable groups; hard-to-reach populations
eligibility: Any individual with mental health issues can reach out to Tele MANAS services for help. Family members of persons with mental health issues can reach out for help. Grass-root health care providers/community health providers i.e., Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), and community volunteers from the community can reach out to Tele MANAS on behalf of an individual or individuals in that community with mental health issues.
benefits: Tele MANAS provides 24/7 on-demand toll-free helpline service (14416 or 1-800 891 4416), access to mental health resources via mobile app (available on Google Play and App Store), telephone-based counselling, psychotherapy, psychiatric consultations, referral services, emergency support, video consultations with e-prescription facility, and support for parents and caretakers of children with developmental disorders. Services are available in 20 Indian languages and include screening for psychiatric disorders such as depression, anxiety, psychosis, dementia, addiction, and more.
financial_support: The service is provided free of cost to users. There is no financial support or direct monetary benefit provided to beneficiaries under this programme as it is a fully government-funded public health service.
application_process: 1. Dial the toll-free number 14416 or 1-800 891 4416 to access the Tele MANAS helpline. 2. The call will be an IVRS-based audio call with timely auto-call back. 3. A trained counsellor will attend the call and assess the level of care required. 4. If needed, the counsellor will provide care within their capabilities or refer the caller to a mental health specialist. 5. For specialist care, a video consultation can be initiated with consent, and a link will be sent via SMS to join the call. 6. If medication is needed, psychiatrists can issue e-prescriptions. 7. For urgent in-person intervention, the caller will be referred to the nearest in-person service or an audio-visual consultation arranged via eSanjeevani.
deadlines: 24x7 service — available round the clock, throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)

overview: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) is a campaign launched by the Department of Pharmaceuticals in association with Central Pharma Public Sector Undertakings to provide quality generic medicines at affordable prices through dedicated outlets called Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras. The scheme aims to reduce healthcare expenditure, popularize generic medicines, ensure menstrual health accessibility, and generate self-employment opportunities. As of March 2026, more than 19,000 Kendras are functional across India, offering a product basket of 2100 drugs and 300 surgical items.
target_beneficiaries: individual entrepreneurs; proprietors; partnerships; charitable institutes/hospitals; NGOs/trusts/societies; government/nominated agencies
eligibility: Individual applicants must hold a D. Pharma / B. Pharma degree or employ degree holders and provide proof at application or final approval. Entrepreneurs, pharmacists, trusts, societies, and charitable organizations must employ B.Pharma/D.Pharma degree holders and provide proof. In government hospital premises, reputed NGOs/charitable organizations are preferred, though individuals are also eligible. Applicants must own or hire space (minimum 120 sq. ft.) with proper lease agreement, secure a registered pharmacist, submit financial capacity documents (ITR, bank statements, PAN/Aadhar), obtain a drug license in the Kendra's name, and adhere to distance policy (minimum 1 km between Kendras, no restriction within 500m of hospitals with 100+ beds or medical college-associated hospitals).
benefits: Operating margin of 20% on MRP (excluding taxes) of each drug; normal incentive of 20% of monthly purchases from PMBI, capped at Rs. 20,000 per month (disbursed 50:50 based on purchase and stocking mandate); special one-time incentive of Rs. 2.00 lakhs (Rs. 1.50 lakh for furniture/fixtures, Rs. 0.50 lakh for computer/internet/printer/scanner) for women entrepreneurs, Divyang, SC/ST, ex-servicemen, and those in aspirational districts (NITI Aayog-notified), Himalayan, Island, or North-Eastern territories; exemption from Rs. 5,000 application fee for eligible categories; access to PMBI's supply chain for WHO-GMP certified, NABL-tested generic medicines; authorization to sell allied medical products not supplied by PMBI; use of PMBI's software for billing and inventory; training and support via POS system and helpline.
financial_support: Financial support includes a 20% operating margin on MRP (excluding taxes) of each drug sold. Normal incentive is 20% of monthly purchases from PMBI, subject to a monthly ceiling of Rs. 20,000, disbursed on a 50:50 basis: 50% based on actual purchase (up to Rs. 10,000) and 50% based on stocking mandate (maintaining 180-200 medicines for full payment). Special one-time incentive of Rs. 2.00 lakhs is provided for eligible categories (women entrepreneurs, Divyang, SC/ST, ex-servicemen, aspirational districts, Himalayan, Island, North-Eastern states), comprising Rs. 1.50 lakh for furniture/fixtures and Rs. 0.50 lakh for computer/internet/printer/scanner, reimbursed against original bills within 90 days of opening, restricted to actual expenditure. A non-refundable application fee of Rs. 5,000 is required, except for exempted categories upon proof of eligibility.
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 2.00 lakhs (one-time special incentive for eligible categories)
application_process: 1. Visit https://janaushadhi.gov.in and click on 'APPLY FOR KENDRA' tab. 2. Click 'REGISTER NOW' and fill applicant details including mobile number and email ID. 3. Upon successful registration, receive email with unique USER ID and PASSWORD for portal login. 4. Login using USER ID/PASSWORD or via registered mobile/email using 'Get OTP' option. 5. Fill application form: enter basic and proposed Kendra details, adhere to distance policy, upload required documents in PDF (each <5 MB). 6. For location tagging, drag and drop location icon within blue circle to exact address/shop/building. 7. Pay application fee of Rs. 5,000/- via online payment gateway (exempt for eligible categories with category proof). 8. After submission, confirmation sent to registered email; check status online via portal or call helpline 18001808080.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI)
