The Pradhan Mantri Research Fellows (PMRF) Scheme is a flagship initiative by the Ministry of Education (MoE) to support PhD scholars in Science and Engineering with attractive fellowships and research grants. It aims to attract top talent into doctoral research, build outstanding research ecosystems, and focus on innovative and challenging research problems. The scheme was announced in the Budget 2018-19 and is implemented through the National Coordinating Institute (NCI) and National Coordination Committee (NCC).
target_beneficiaries: PhD scholars in Science and Engineering
eligibility: Candidates can apply through Direct Entry or Lateral Entry channels. For Direct Entry: (a) completed or pursuing final year of 4/5-year undergraduate or 5-year integrated M.Tech./2-year M.Sc./5-year UG-PG dual degree in Science and Technology from IISc/IITs/NITs/IISERs/IIEST and centrally funded IIITs with CGPA/CPI ≥ 8.0, OR (b) same from any other recognized Institute/University with CGPA ≥ 8 and GATE score ≥ 650 or UGC/CSIR JRF rank ≤ 100 or NBHM fellowship, OR (c) qualified GATE and pursuing/completed M.Tech./MS by research at a PMRF granting institute with CGPA/CPI ≥ 8.0 and minimum four courses at time of application. Further, must be selected for Ph.D. at a PMRF granting institute. For Lateral Entry: currently pursuing Ph.D. at a PMRF granting institute, completed at most 12 months (if joined with Master’s) or 24 months (if joined with Bachelor’s) in PhD programme, completed at least four full-semester courses with aggregate CGPA ≥ 8.5, and strong recommendation from the host institute.
benefits: Attractive monthly fellowship (Year 1: ₹70,000; Year 2: ₹70,000; Year 3: ₹75,000; Year 4: ₹80,000; Year 5: ₹80,000), annual research grant of ₹2 lakhs per year (up to ₹10 lakhs for five years), mandatory TAship duty (teaching ~1 hour/week in non-PMRF institutes), annual review process, and certification upon completion.
financial_support: Fellowship is paid monthly as per the pay matrix: ₹70,000 in Year 1, ₹70,000 in Year 2, ₹75,000 in Year 3, ₹80,000 in Year 4, and ₹80,000 in Year 5. Each fellow is eligible for a research grant of ₹2 lakhs per year, totaling up to ₹10 lakhs over five years. The research grant can be carried forward but must be spent before thesis submission or PMRF tenure end, whichever is earlier, and any unspent amount must be refunded. Fellowship and research grant are paid until the date of Final Viva Voce or end of PMRF tenure, whichever is earlier, with no retrospective payments for thesis submissions on or after November 1, 2022.
grant_amount_per_entity: ₹10 lakhs (total research grant over five years)
application_process: 1. Get nominated by the PMRF granting institute after meeting eligibility criteria. 2. Receive a link to the PMRF portal to submit application. 3. Submit academic background, transcripts, research experience/internship, CV, research proposal/statement of purpose, list of publications, and details of recommenders. 4. Await evaluation by a National Panel for each broad area. 5. Final selection by the National Coordination Committee (NCC) based on ranks and seat allocation.
deadlines: Application windows vary: for December 2024 annual review, submission was 01st Nov 2024 to 07th Nov 2024; for May 2025 review, submission was 08-May-2025 to 14-May-2025 (with extension to 20-May-2025 for 1 scholar). Specific cycles have defined timelines; otherwise, admissions occur twice a year (May and December cycles).

scheme_name: SWAYAM PRABHA DTH Channels for Education
overview: SWAYAM PRABHA is a group of 40 DTH channels devoted to telecasting high-quality educational programmes on a 24x7 basis using the GSAT-15 satellite. It aims to reach the unreached segment of India, particularly in rural, tribal, and remote locations, by providing free educational content from leading institutions like IITs, UGC, CEC, IGNOU, and others. The content is repeated multiple times a day to allow flexible viewing, and the service is available through DD Free Dish and Dish TV.
target_beneficiaries: students; learners; rural populations; tribal populations; remote area residents
eligibility: There are no eligibility criteria for viewing SWAYAM PRABHA channels; the service is free and open to all students, learners, and the general public across India.
benefits: Free access to 24x7 educational DTH channels with high-quality content from premier institutions; flexible viewing schedule with fresh content repeated 5 times daily; availability on DD Free Dish and Dish TV; accessibility via JIO TV mobile application; no fees for viewing; support for school education, higher education, and competitive exam preparation; content available in Hindi, English, and regional languages.
financial_support: The SWAYAM PRABHA scheme does not provide direct financial support to beneficiaries; it is a free educational broadcasting service funded by the Government of India.
application_process: No application is required to access SWAYAM PRABHA channels. Users can view the channels by installing DD Free Dish and configuring the set-top box with the specified parameters, or through the JIO TV application.
deadlines: Not applicable — service is available continuously on a 24x7 basis.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Education, Government of India
contact_details: Email: swayamprabha@inflibnet.ac.in | Helpline: +91 79-23268279 (Available Monday to Friday from 10:00 AM to 05:30 PM)

overview: SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) is a Government of India initiative providing free online courses from school to post-graduation level, hosted by top institutions like IITs, IIMs, and central universities. It aims to achieve access, equity, and quality in education by bridging the digital divide and offering courses in 11 Indian languages. Learners can access video lectures, reading materials, self-assessment tests, and discussion forums at no cost, with optional proctored exams for certification available at a nominal fee.
target_beneficiaries: students; faculty; lifelong learners; out-of-school students; working professionals
eligibility: There is no specific eligibility or age criterion for joining any online course on SWAYAM. Anyone in the world can register for a course. Faculty may recommend basic knowledge for better comprehension, but no formal prerequisites are mandated.
benefits: Free access to courses from top Indian institutions; self-paced learning anytime, anywhere; opportunity to earn certifications from recognized universities (nominal fee for exam); possibility to transfer credits to academic records per UGC and AICTE frameworks; access to discussion forums for doubt clearance; availability of courses in 11 Indian languages; industry-relevant skill courses for employability; blended learning ecosystem with optional in-person interaction; faculty development programmes for teacher upskilling.
financial_support: All courses on SWAYAM are available free of cost to learners. No tuition or enrollment fee is charged. However, learners seeking certification must pay a nominal fee for the in-person, proctored exam: Rs. 1000 per course for NPTEL offerings and Rs. 750 per course for IIMB offerings. Exam fees are the only financial cost involved.
application_process: 1. Visit the SWAYAM portal at https://swayam.gov.in 2. Click on 'Register as Student' 3. Provide essential information: Name and Email ID 4. Optionally sign up using Google or Microsoft login 5. Verify account via email notification from support@swayam.gov.in 6. Browse or search for courses by category, keyword, or university 7. Select a suitable course and click to enroll 8. Access course content immediately after enrollment 9. For certification, register for the proctored exam when announced 10. Pay the exam fee (if applicable) and appear at the designated centre on the specified date.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Courses have specific enrollment windows (e.g., enrollment ends 31 Aug, 2026 for many courses), but learners can enroll in self-paced courses anytime. Exam registration has end dates (e.g., 14 Aug, 2026 for many July 2026 semester courses).
implementing_agency: Ministry of Education, Government of India
contact_details: Email: support@swayam.gov.in | Helpline: Not explicitly stated in evidence for general SWAYAM support; however, NTA helpline for exams is +91-11-40759000

scheme_name: DSIR Recognition for In-house R&D Units
overview: The Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) operates a scheme for granting recognition and registration to in-house R&D units established by corporate industry. The scheme aims to benchmark industrial R&D, provide eligibility for fiscal incentives, and facilitate access to R&D funding from other government departments. Recognition is granted to units engaged in innovative R&D activities related to the firm's line of business, excluding routine activities like market research or quality control.
target_beneficiaries: corporate industry; in-house R&D units
eligibility: The applicant should be a company registered under the Companies Act, 1956 or 2013. The company shall be eligible for consideration only after the completion of three financial years after formation. The applicant should have regular source of income at least during the last two years to sustain the business. Companies seeking recognition should be engaged in manufacture or production or rendering technical services. Companies fully engaged in contract research are eligible if independent infrastructure is available for research activities. Those engaged in research only at present but with plans to start manufacture later may be considered if there is potential. The R&D unit(s) should not be located in residential areas but should operate in premises authorized by relevant Central/State Government. Independent infrastructure for research activities and adequate technically qualified manpower should be available (minimum area for R&D activities should be at least 1000 Sq. ft.). At the time of application, the R&D unit(s) should be functional and have well-defined, time-bound R&D programmes leading to development of innovative products and/or technology.
benefits: Recognized in-house R&D units are eligible for fiscal incentives for research and development implemented through DSIR (wherever applicable). They also become eligible to receive funds for R&D from other government departments and agencies such as Department of Science and Technology (DST), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Department of Electronics and Information Technology (DeitY), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF), Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI), Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), and Technology Development Board (TDB), where DSIR recognition is a requirement.
financial_support: The scheme itself does not provide direct financial support but enables access to financial support for R&D from other government departments and agencies. DSIR recognition is a prerequisite for accessing such funds.
application_process: 1. Companies interested in applying for DSIR in-house R&D recognition need not submit hard copy. 2. Submit a covering letter, completely filled-in application form (signed by Managing Director or any Director on Board) along with requisite Annexures in PDF format (single attachment less than 20 MB). 3. For Fresh Recognition, submit the signed PDF application to the email: rdi-fresh@gov.in. 4. For Renewal of Recognition, submit the signed PDF application to the email: rdi-renewal@gov.in. 5. Applications can be submitted throughout the year. 6. No hard copy of the application needs to be submitted; only soft copy is processed.
deadlines: Applications can be submitted throughout the year. No fixed deadline.
implementing_agency: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India

For additional information: Dr (Ms) Sarika Madan, Scientist – E, Phone: 26960629, 26590534, Email: sarika[dot]madan[at]nic[dot]in

scheme_name: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT 1.0)
overview: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT 1.0) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) to provide basic infrastructure services such as water supply, sewerage, septage management, storm water drainage, green spaces, and non-motorized urban transport in 500 selected cities across India. The mission aims to ensure that every household has access to a tap with assured water supply and a sewerage connection, thereby improving the quality of life in urban areas, particularly for the poor and disadvantaged.
target_beneficiaries: urban local bodies; municipal corporations; state governments; urban poor
eligibility: The scheme covers 500 cities selected based on criteria including: all cities and towns with a population of over one lakh with notified Municipalities, including Cantonment Boards; all capital cities of States/Union Territories; cities classified as Heritage Cities by MoHUA under the HRIDAY scheme; and cities located on the stem of major rivers (between 5-50 km). Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) of these selected cities are eligible to receive central assistance under AMRUT 1.0.
benefits: Financial assistance from the Government of India for infrastructure projects in water supply, sewerage and septage management, storm water drainage, green spaces and parks, and non-motorized urban transport. The mission promotes convergence with other schemes like Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban), Housing for All (Urban), and Smart Cities Mission. It also encourages public-private partnerships (PPPs) and aims to improve service delivery and urban governance through institutional reforms and capacity building of ULBs.
financial_support: AMRUT 1.0 had a total central outlay of INR 50,000 crore for the period 2015-16 to 2019-20, with funding shared between the Centre and States in a ratio of 90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan States, 80:20 for other States, and 50:50 for Union Territories. Central Assistance is provided as grant-in-aid to States/UTs based on project proposals submitted in State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs), which are appraised and approved by the Apex Committee chaired by the Secretary, MoHUA.
application_process: 1. States/UTs prepare State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) detailing project proposals for water supply, sewerage, drainage, green spaces, and non-motorized transport. 2. SAAPs are submitted to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) for appraisal. 3. The Apex Committee under MoHUA reviews and approves the SAAPs. 4. Upon approval, central funds are released to States/UTs in installments based on utilization certificates and progress reports. 5. States/UTs further disburse funds to Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) for project implementation. 6. ULBs execute projects through tendering and project management, with monitoring by State and Central authorities.
deadlines: AMRUT 1.0 was implemented from 2015-16 to 2019-20. The scheme has been subsumed into AMRUT 2.0, which was launched in 2021. No new applications are being accepted under AMRUT 1.0.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India

overview: The Atmanirbhar Bharat Defence Production Policy is a strategic initiative by the Ministry of Defence to enhance self-reliance in defence manufacturing. It aims to reduce import dependence, promote indigenous design and development, and strengthen the domestic defence industrial base through policy reforms, financial incentives, and streamlined procurement procedures. The policy encourages private sector participation, MSMEs, and startups in defence production and supports innovation via indigenisation and research & development initiatives.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; private sector
eligibility: Eligible entities include Indian companies, startups, MSMEs, and private sector organisations engaged in defence manufacturing, design, development, or supply of defence equipment, systems, or services. Preference is given to entities contributing to indigenisation, technology absorption, and Make in India initiatives under the Atmanirbhar Bharat framework.
benefits: Benefits include preferential treatment in defence procurement, simplified procedures for vendor registration, access to defence testing and evaluation facilities, support for technology transfer and joint ventures, facilitation of exports, and participation in defence exhibitions and seminars. Financial incentives may be available through linked schemes such as the Defence Production and Export Promotion Policy (DPEPP).
financial_support: Financial support is provided through linked government schemes such as the Defence Production and Export Promotion Policy (DPEPP), which offers financial incentives for eligible defence manufacturers. The policy enables access to government procurement opportunities and facilitates partnerships with defence PSUs and ordnance factories for technology development and production.
application_process: 1. Identify defence production opportunities through the Ministry of Defence or defence PSUs. 2. Register as a vendor on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) or defence-specific procurement portals. 3. Submit Expression of Interest (EOI) or tender response for defence contracts. 4. Undergo technical evaluation and quality assurance processes. 5. Upon selection, enter into contract for supply, development, or production of defence equipment. 6. Avail benefits under linked schemes like DPEPP for financial incentives.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on defence procurement cycles and tender notifications.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Defence

overview: Global Initiative of Academic Networks (GIAN) is a Government of India program in Higher Education aimed at tapping the talent pool of scientists and entrepreneurs internationally to encourage their engagement with Indian higher education institutes, augment academic resources, accelerate quality reform, and elevate India's scientific and technological capacity to global excellence. It facilitates short to semester-long courses by foreign faculty in Indian institutions, promoting international academic collaboration and knowledge exchange.
eligibility: All Government (State or Central) higher education Institutions / University which are in top 200 in NIRF overall rankings and having at least NAAC ‘A’ grade (3.0 and above).
benefits: International faculty engagement, knowledge exchange, collaborative research opportunities, course development, pedagogic innovation, global exposure for students and faculty, access to international expertise, creation of digital repository for future viewing via National Digital Library, potential for MOOC creation, honorarium and travel support for foreign faculty, honorarium for host faculty and local coordinator, video recording and webcasting facilities, online feedback mechanism.
financial_support: A lump-sum amount of up to US$ 8000 for 12 to 14 hours of contact and up to US$ 12000 for 20 to 28 hours of contact can be paid to foreign experts covering travel and honorarium. Local hospitality is arranged by the Host Institute. The National Coordinator can spend Rs 1.0 crore for portal development and initial activities. Each Group Coordinator can spend Rs 50 lakhs from Plan grant for group activities. Funding for courses by Institutes is partially supported through Plan/Non-Plan Funds, TEQIP, UGC, AICTE, DST, DSIR, sponsorships, industry/foundations, participant fees, and other sources.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to US$ 8000 for short duration courses (12-14 hours) and up to US$ 12000 for longer duration courses (20-28 hours) for foreign faculty honorarium and travel.
application_process: 1. Institute confirms eligibility (top 200 NIRF, NAAC A grade). 2. Competent authority appoints a local coordinator for GIAN. 3. Institute sends formal request letter from VC/Director, NAAC ‘A’ grade certificate, proof of NIRF ranking in top 200, and formal office order for local coordinator appointment (with name, email, mobile) to National Coordinator at IIT Kharagpur via email/speed post. 4. After document verification, Institute is added to GIAN program and login created for local coordinator. 5. Local coordinator logs into GIAN portal, edits profile, circulates proposal template to faculty. 6. Local coordinator invites course coordinators to submit proposals via portal. 7. Course coordinator uploads proposal in PDF format and submits. 8. Local coordinator scrutinizes proposal and foreign faculty consent form, then forwards to GIAN office by clicking ‘Accept’. 9. Proposal sent for document verification; if in order, forwarded to Chairman of appropriate sectional committee for review. 10. Status updates until approval by Apex body (GIAN Implementation Committee). 11. Upon approval, local coordinator receives mail to upload final brochure and course dates. 12. Local coordinator coordinates with course coordinator to upload brochure and finalize dates. 13. Official signed sanction letter with fund details sent to Institute. 14. Fund allocated released via PFMS after brochure upload. 15. During course, local coordinator monitors via portal, ensures participant feedback submission. 16. After course, local coordinator submits course completion report and fund utilization certificate to IIT Kharagpur within 15 days.
deadlines: Proposals may be submitted throughout the year. Three months required for review to final approval. Preferably, six months lead time from date of holding the course.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Education (formerly Ministry of Human Resource Development)
contact_details: Official Query Email: gian [at] iitkgp [dot] ac [dot] in | Phone: +91-3222-282288 | Profile Updating, Courses Registration & Participant Login Portal Email: gian [at] iitkgp [dot] ac [dot] in

overview: Swadesh Darshan Scheme 2.0 is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, aimed at developing theme-based tourist circuits across the country. It focuses on integrated development of tourism infrastructure, promoting sustainable and responsible tourism, and enhancing visitor experience through planned interventions. The scheme supports the creation of world-class tourism destinations by improving connectivity, facilities, and services at identified circuits.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; union territory administrations
eligibility: State Governments and Union Territory Administrations are eligible to submit project proposals under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme 2.0. Projects must be aligned with the identified thematic circuits and adhere to the scheme guidelines, including norms for sustainable tourism, environmental clearances, and land availability.
benefits: Financial assistance for development of tourism infrastructure such as wayside amenities, tourist centers, accommodation, eco-lodges, sound & light shows, pathways, landscaping, illumination, and signage. Non-financial benefits include technical support from the Ministry of Tourism, convergence with other central and state schemes, and promotion of identified circuits through marketing and branding initiatives.
financial_support: The scheme provides central financial assistance (CFA) to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations for the development of tourism infrastructure in identified circuits. The funding pattern is 60:40 for general category states (Centre:State), 90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan states, and 100% central funding for Union Territories. The assistance is released in installments based on physical and financial progress of the project.
application_process: 1. State Governments/UT Administrations identify potential tourist circuits based on thematic themes. 2. Prepare Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) as per scheme guidelines. 3. Submit proposals to the Ministry of Tourism along with required documents. 4. Proposals are appraised by the Project Appraisal Committee (PAC). 5. Upon approval, sanction letters are issued. 6. Funds are released in installments subject to utilization-linked manner. 7. Projects are monitored through site visits and progress reports.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India

scheme_name: HRIDAY – Heritage City Development and Augmentation Yojana
overview: HRI Day India is a website providing online banking help and financial guides for various Indian banks. It offers step-by-step instructions for banking tasks such as activating debit cards, checking account balances, downloading statements, and managing online banking services. The site covers multiple banks including SBI, IOB, Canara Bank, PNB, and others, with guides on net banking, mobile apps, and account-related procedures.
target_beneficiaries: bank customers; individuals; retail users
eligibility: Anyone with a bank account at the covered Indian banks who needs assistance with online banking services, statement downloads, or account management can use the guides provided on the website.
benefits: Users get access to step-by-step guides for various banking services including balance checks, debit card activation, statement downloads, password recovery, and online banking registration. The guides are designed to be user-friendly and reduce confusion in managing bank accounts through digital channels.
financial_support: The website does not provide any financial support, grants, loans, or subsidies. It is an informational platform offering only guidance and tutorials for banking services.
application_process: 1. Visit the HRI Day India website at https://hridayindia.in 2. Use the search or filter options to find guides for your specific bank and service need 3. Select the relevant article (e.g., 'How to Download IOB Statement Online', 'How to Download IOB Statement Online') 4. Follow the step-by-step instructions provided in the guide 5. Complete the required actions such as entering credentials, downloading apps, or visiting bank websites as directed
deadlines: Rolling basis — guides are available year-round with no fixed deadlines for access
implementing_agency: HRI Day India (Editorial Team)

overview: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to reduce poverty and vulnerability of urban poor households by enabling access to self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities. It aims to build strong grassroots-level institutions of the poor, provide shelter for the urban homeless, support street vendors, and promote financial inclusion and skill development. The mission operates through a three-tier structure at national, state, and city levels, with implementation led by Urban Local Bodies (ULBs).
target_beneficiaries: urban poor; urban homeless; street vendors; SCs; STs; women; minorities; differently-abled persons
eligibility: The primary target of DAY-NULM is the urban poor, including the urban homeless. As an interim measure, the target is the urban population identified as below poverty line by States/UTs. Coverage may be broadened to include families of disadvantaged groups like SCs, STs, women, minorities, disabled, etc., subject to a maximum of 25 percent of the urban poor population. For Self-Employment Programme (SEP), no minimum educational qualification is required, but training must be provided if special skills are needed for the enterprise. For group enterprises under SEP, the group must have a minimum of 3 members (amended) with at least 70% from urban poor families, and no more than one person from the same family should be included. For Employment through Skills Training & Placement (EST&P), eligibility varies by training type: fresh entrants require minimum 200 hours, reskilling requires 16 hours, and formal recognition requires bridge courses if needed.
benefits: Benefits include access to skill training for market-based jobs and self-employment, interest subsidy on bank loans for individual and group enterprises (difference between 7% and prevailing rate), revolving fund support to Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations, financial inclusion through basic savings accounts and credit linkage, shelter for urban homeless with basic infrastructure, identity cards and social security linkages for street vendors, training and stipend for street vendors, and support for innovative and special projects. Non-financial benefits include capacity building, institution formation, bank linkage, training of community organisers, and convergence with other government schemes for entitlements like food, healthcare, education, and housing.
financial_support: Financial support under DAY-NULM includes interest subsidy on bank loans for individual micro-enterprises (project cost up to Rs. 2 lakhs) and group enterprises (project cost up to Rs. 10 lakhs), where the subsidy covers the difference between 7% per annum and the prevailing interest rate, subject to timely repayment. For Self-Help Groups, revolving fund support is provided. Under convergence with PMFME, seed capital of Rs. 40,000 per SHG member is available for working capital and small tools, repayable as a loan from SHG federations at interest not exceeding 6% per annum. Credit-linked subsidy of 35% of project cost, up to Rs. 10 lakh, is available for food processing enterprises. Funding for City Livelihood Centres (CLCs) and shelters is also provided. The overall expenditure on Capacity Building and Training (CB&T) is capped at 12% of total allocation.
application_process: 1. Identify prospective beneficiaries through Community Organisers (COs) or ULB officials from urban poor households. 2. Submit application of intent with basic details (name, age, contact, address, Aadhaar, loan required, bank account, enterprise type) to ULB. 3. ULB enters details into a register or MIS and issues acknowledgement with unique registration number. 4. ULB screens applications and forwards recommended cases to Task Force at ULB level. 5. Task Force scrutinises applications, conducts interviews, and recommends or rejects based on viability. 6. Recommended cases are sent to concerned banks for processing within 15 days. 7. Banks process loans and submit periodic reports to ULB on application status. 8. For interest subsidy, banks submit quarterly claims to ULB after loan disbursement; ULB verifies and releases subsidy (difference between 7% and prevailing rate) to banks. 9. For SEP-G (group enterprises), similar process applies with group entry form and verification of group strength and urban poor membership. 10. For SHG bank linkage, SHGs apply through ULB, and subsidy is released on timely repayment. 11. For innovative projects, proposals are submitted to State/UT Government or SULM, screened by National Mission Directorate, and approved by Project Approval Committee (PAC).
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India

overview: The National Mineral Exploration Trust (NMET) Grants scheme is established under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 2015 to promote regional and detailed mineral exploration across India. It provides financial assistance in the form of grants to state governments and other entities for conducting mineral exploration activities. The scheme aims to augment mineral resources through systematic exploration and reduce dependence on imports.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; public sector undertakings; joint venture companies; private entities
eligibility: State Governments, Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), Joint Venture Companies, and other entities engaged in mineral exploration activities are eligible to apply for NMET grants. Proposals must be for exploration of minerals specified in the First Schedule of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 2015, and must follow the guidelines issued by NMET from time to time.
benefits: Financial support for conducting mineral exploration including reconnaissance, prospecting, and general exploration. Benefits include funding for geophysical surveys, geochemical sampling, drilling, and related exploration activities. The scheme enables access to unexplored or under-explored mineral blocks and supports capacity building in exploration technologies.
financial_support: NMET provides grants covering up to 50% of the total project cost for exploration activities, with the remaining 50% to be borne by the applicant. The grant is disbursed in installments based on project milestones and submission of utilization certificates and progress reports as per NMET guidelines.
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed project proposal for mineral exploration to the NMET Secretariat. 2. The proposal must include objectives, methodology, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 3. Proposals are reviewed by the Technical Committee constituted by NMET. 4. Upon approval, a sanction letter is issued specifying the grant amount and terms. 5. Funds are released in stages based on progress reports and utilization certificates. 6. Final report and audit report must be submitted upon project completion.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per NMET notifications
implementing_agency: National Mineral Exploration Trust (NMET), under the Ministry of Mines, Government of India

overview: National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICP) is India's most ambitious infrastructure programme aiming to develop futuristic industrial cities in India which can compete with the best manufacturing and investment destinations in the world. The programme aims to create employment opportunities and economic growth leading to overall socio-economic development. It involves the development of 11 industrial corridors with 32 projects in 4 phases, including greenfield industrial smart cities and logistics hubs.
target_beneficiaries: industries; investors; manufacturing units; MSME; state governments
eligibility: State Governments, Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs), Private Developers, or joint ventures thereof can submit applications under the BHAVYA Scheme for development of industrial parks. The sponsoring agency must ensure 90% encumbrance-free land is in possession at the time of application submission. Land area requirements: minimum 100 acres contiguous land in non-hilly states, 25 acres in hilly states, northeast region, union territories, and states with population less than 1 crore. Non-contiguous parcels (not exceeding 2) within 2 km radius with minimum 100 acres each may be considered. Up to 20 industrial parks may have development area between 500 to 1000 acres, with funding capped at 1000 acres for larger parks developed in phases.
benefits: Plug-and-play infrastructure with 24-hour power supply, potable and recycled water, effluent treatment plants, multi-modal connectivity, gas pipelines, integrated city planning, and robust telecom networks. Benefits include single-window clearance, E-land management, anchor investor discounts, flexible payment plans, and incentives from Union and State Governments. The cities offer world-class infrastructure, seamless connectivity via NH-16, Krishnapatnam Port, and Tirupati Airport, and are designed for sustainability and inclusivity. They attract investments, support job creation, encourage MSME growth, and integrate smart solutions for efficient operations and improved living standards. Only green and clean businesses are permitted, prohibiting red or pollutive industries. NICDC cities feature an underground power network system for industrial use with seven underground integrated services per plot. ICT-based infrastructure optimizes utility and resource use, reducing environmental impact and enhancing livability. SCADA system monitors and controls infrastructure for reliable power and other services.
financial_support: Financial assistance under the BHAVYA Scheme is provided by the Central Government through NICDIT in the form of equity, in tranches linked to achievement of predefined milestones. The equity participation of NICDIT in any SPV shall not exceed 50% of the paid-up equity capital. For SPVs formed between NICDIT and the State Government/State Nodal Agency (without private participation), the shareholding pattern shall not be altered. In cases where private developer participates as an anchor investor, they may be permitted to allot to themselves up to 25% of the developed land within the industrial park, with the remaining 75% allotted to other industries/units transparently and non-discriminatorily. The SPV shall be permitted to set aside up to 5% of the gross allotment premium into a dedicated O&M Corpus Fund for operational deficit during the first five years post-completion.
application_process: 1. Application shall be submitted by the sponsoring agency/authority in prescribed format through the designated portal. 2. A separate application shall be submitted for development of each industrial park. 3. Each application shall be accompanied by a Detailed Project Report (DPR) prepared in accordance with the indicative template provided at Annexure II. 4. In case the State Government is the sponsoring authority, the application shall be submitted after due consideration and with clear recommendation of the State Level Committee (SLC). 5. In case a Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) is the sponsoring agency, the application shall be submitted with the approval of the Board of CPSE and in compliance with applicable instructions of the Government of India. 6. Applications under this scheme will be received and processed through an online portal developed and managed by Project Management Agency (PMA). 7. The portal shall be opened for submission of applications for a specified period following due public notice. 8. Applications meeting the mandatory eligibility criteria will be taken up for evaluation and scoring in accordance with the prescribed evaluation criteria. 9. The highest-ranking applications scoring above the benchmark threshold shall be shortlisted and their DPR shall be examined and evaluated for further consideration and approval. 10. An appraisal report in respect of shortlisted applications will be prepared by PMA and presented before the NLSC for approval.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry

scheme_name: Viability Gap Funding (VGF) for PPP Projects
overview: The Viability Gap Funding (VGF) Scheme is a flagship initiative of the Government of India under the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) that provides financial assistance to financially unviable but socially/economically desirable Public Private Partnership (PPP) projects. Launched to address infrastructure deficits, the scheme supports PPPs by bridging the gap between project costs and expected revenues, thereby attracting private investment in infrastructure and social sectors. The revamped scheme, launched in 2020, has a total outlay of Rs. 8,100 crores till 2024-25 and includes enhanced support for social sector projects such as health, education, water supply, wastewater treatment, and solid waste management.
target_beneficiaries: PPP project sponsors; state governments; central ministries; statutory entities; private sector entities
eligibility: PPP projects must be sponsored by Central Government Ministries, Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs), statutory authorities, or other entities under their administrative control. Projects must be in infrastructure sectors including social sectors like health, education, water supply, wastewater treatment, and solid waste management. Social sector projects under Sub Scheme-1 must have at least 100% Operational Cost recovery, while Sub Scheme-2 projects (demonstration/pilot) must have at least 50% Operational Cost recovery. The project must be a PPP structure and undergo appraisal by the Public Private Partnership Appraisal Committee (PPPAC).
benefits: Financial support in the form of viability gap funding grants to cover project costs. For economic sector projects: up to 40% of Capex as VGF grant. For social sector projects: up to 80% of Capex and up to 50% of Opex for 5 years after Commercial Operation Date (CoD). Sub Scheme-1 (social sectors): Central Government provides up to 30% of Capex, with State Government/Sponsoring Central Ministry/Statutory Entity providing additional support up to 30% of Capex. Sub Scheme-2 (demonstration/pilot social sectors): Central Government provides up to 40% of Capex and up to 25% of Opex for first five years of commercial operations, with State Government/Sponsoring Central Ministry/Statutory Entity providing additional support up to 40% of Capex and up to 25% of Opex. The scheme facilitates private investment, reduces financial burden on project sponsors, and increases bankability of PPP projects.
financial_support: The revamped VGF scheme launched in 2020 has a total outlay of Rs. 8,100 crores till 2024-25. Economic sector projects may receive up to 40% of Capex as VGF grant. Social sector projects may receive up to 80% of Capex and up to 50% of Opex for 5 years after CoD. Sub Scheme-1: Central Government provides up to 30% of Capex, with potential additional 30% from State Government/Sponsoring Central Ministry/Statutory Entity. Sub Scheme-2: Central Government provides up to 40% of Capex and up to 25% of Opex for first five years, with potential additional 40% Capex and 25% Opex from State Government/Sponsoring Central Ministry/Statutory Entity. Post-revamp, Rs. 470.46 Cr have been disbursed under the VGF Scheme. Overall, till date, 67 projects with total project cost of Rs. 45,802 crores have received final approval with VGF of Rs. 7,682 crores approved and disbursal of Rs. 4,847 Crore completed.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to 80% of Capex for social sector projects and up to 40% of Capex for economic sector projects, with additional support possible from state/central entities as per sub-scheme
application_process: 1. Project Sponsoring Authority (PSA) identifies the PPP project and prepares feasibility studies, project agreements, etc. with expert assistance. 2. PSA submits proposal to the Public Private Partnership Appraisal Committee (PPPAC) Secretariat in the specified format (six copies, hard and soft) along with pre-feasibility/feasibility report and term-sheet of proposed project agreements. 3. PPPAC Secretariat circulates documents to all members and convenes a meeting within three weeks to consider the proposal for 'in principle' approval. 4. Planning Commission appraises the project and forwards its Appraisal Note to PPPAC Secretariat; other involved ministries/departments forward written comments within stipulated time. 5. PPPAC Secretariat forwards all comments to PSA for written response. 6. PSA submits concession agreement, supporting agreements/documents, PPPAC Memo, and project report for consideration by PPPAC. 7. PPPAC evaluates the Appraisal Note, comments, and PSA's response, and either recommends approval (with or without modifications) or requests necessary changes for further consideration. 8. Once cleared by PPPAC, the project is put up to the competent authority (same as for PIB approval) for final approval. 9. After final approval, financial bids are invited. 10. Post-award, claims for VGF disbursement are submitted based on project milestones and verification.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round as per the appraisal and approval procedure of PPPAC.
implementing_agency: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
contact_details: Email: secy-dea@nic.in | Phone: 011-23092254 (as per induction material for Economic Advisor, Admin, BC&SF, C&C - generic DEA contact)

overview: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Ministry of Education, launched to address the declining child sex ratio and promote the education and empowerment of the girl child. The scheme focuses on preventing gender-biased sex-selective elimination, ensuring survival and protection of the girl child, and promoting her education and participation. It operates through a multi-sectoral approach involving awareness campaigns, enforcement of PC&PNDT Act, and incentivizing girl child education.
target_beneficiaries: girl child; families with girl child; communities in low child sex ratio districts
eligibility: The scheme targets families and communities in districts identified with low Child Sex Ratio (CSR) as per Census data. There is no individual beneficiary registration; benefits are delivered through district-level interventions and awareness campaigns. Eligibility for specific incentives under BBBP-linked schemes (like Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana) is governed by those respective schemes.
benefits: Non-financial benefits include awareness campaigns, community mobilization, training of functionaries, and monitoring of CSR. Financial benefits are delivered through linked schemes such as Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY), which offers tax-free interest and tax deduction under Section 80C. BBBP also facilitates convergence with other schemes for scholarships, bicycles, toilets, and financial incentives for girl child education.
financial_support: BBBP itself does not provide direct financial transfers to beneficiaries. Financial support is channeled through convergent schemes like Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY), where guardians can open accounts for girl children with a minimum deposit of INR 250 and maximum of INR 1.5 lakh per financial year, earning interest rate fixed by the government (currently 8.2% per annum, compounded annually). The scheme also supports state-level incentives for girl child education under the BBBP framework.
application_process: 1. Identify the district-level BBBP implementation unit (usually under District Magistrate or Women and Child Development Officer). 2. Awareness and mobilization activities are conducted at the community level through Anganwadi workers, ASHA, and school teachers. 3. For financial benefits under linked schemes (e.g., Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana), visit a authorized bank or post office with the girl child’s birth certificate and parent/guardian ID proof. 4. Open SSY account and deposit funds as per rules. 5. Monitor progress through district-level BBBP task force meetings and periodic reviews.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline for account opening under linked schemes like Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana. BBBP activities are ongoing throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India

overview: The One Stop Centre Scheme (Sakhi) is a centrally sponsored scheme under the Ministry of Women and Child Development aimed at providing integrated support and assistance to women affected by violence, both in private and public spaces, under one roof. It facilitates immediate emergency response, medical, legal, psychological, and counselling support to survivors of gender-based violence. The scheme operates through One Stop Centres (OSCs) set up across the country to ensure access to essential services for women in distress.
target_beneficiaries: women affected by violence; survivors of gender-based violence; women in distress
eligibility: Any woman affected by violence, including domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, or any other form of gender-based violence, irrespective of age, class, caste, education, marital status, race, or culture, is eligible to access services at the One Stop Centre. The scheme also extends support to girls below 18 years of age in cases of sexual assault.
benefits: Services provided include emergency medical aid, police assistance (FIR filing, NCR recording), legal aid and counselling, psycho-social counselling, temporary shelter for up to 5 days, video conferencing facility for court proceedings, and referral linkages to other services such as skill training, employment, and long-term rehabilitation. All services are provided free of cost.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support for the setting up and functioning of One Stop Centres through a centrally sponsored model. The Government of India bears 100% of the cost for the non-recurring and recurring components. Financial assistance is provided to State Governments/UT Administrations for construction, renovation, equipment, manpower, and operational expenses as per approved norms.
application_process: 1. Women affected by violence can directly walk into the nearest One Stop Centre or be referred by any individual or organization. 2. Upon arrival, the centre provides immediate medical, legal, and psychological first aid. 3. A case is registered and a needs assessment is conducted. 4. Based on assessment, coordinated with police, hospitals, legal services, and shelter homes as required. 5. Follow-up and tracking of the case is ensured for timely resolution and rehabilitation.
deadlines: Services are available 24x7, 365 days a year on a walk-in basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Women and Child Development
contact_details: Helpline: 181 (Women Helpline integrated with OSC in many states)

overview: The Support to Training and Employment Programme (STEP) is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development to provide skills that enhance employability and entrepreneurship among women aged 16 years and above across India. The scheme focuses on traditional sectors such as agriculture, horticulture, food processing, handlooms, handicrafts, textile and embroidery, zari work, sericulture, fisheries, and allied sectors, aiming to empower women through skill development and self-employment opportunities.
target_beneficiaries: women
eligibility: Women aged 16 years and above across India are eligible to benefit from the scheme. The implementing agencies include Institutions/Organisations set up as Autonomous Bodies under Ministries/Departments of Government of India, State Governments/UT Administrations, Voluntary Organisations, Non-Governmental Organisations, Co-operatives, and other similar entities engaged in training and employment generation for women.
benefits: The scheme provides skill training in traditional sectors to enhance employability and entrepreneurship among women, enabling them to become self-employed or start their own enterprises. It supports capacity building and income generation through training and market linkages in identified traditional sectors.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance to implementing agencies for setting up training infrastructure, procurement of equipment, raw materials, honorarium to trainers, and other recurring and non-recurring expenses related to training programs. The quantum of support is project-based and sanctioned by the Ministry of Women and Child Development based on detailed project reports submitted by implementing agencies.
application_process: 1. Identify a project proposal aligned with STEP objectives in traditional sectors. 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) including objectives, beneficiary details, training modules, budget, and sustainability plan. 3. Submit the DPR to the Ministry of Women and Child Development for appraisal and approval. 4. Upon approval, enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Ministry. 5. Implement the training program as per the approved DPR. 6. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates of accounts to the Ministry. 7. Undergo monitoring and evaluation by the Ministry or its designated agencies.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Women and Child Development

overview: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) is a maternity benefit scheme under the Ministry of Women and Child Development, launched pan India with effect from 01.01.2017. It provides financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers to improve health and nutrition for mother and child, and to compensate for wage loss. The scheme was initially for the first child only, but from 01.04.2022, benefits are also provided for the second child if it is a girl.
target_beneficiaries: pregnant women; lactating mothers; women belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged sections; SC/ST; disabled women; BPL ration card holders; PMJAY beneficiaries; E-shram card holders; Kisan Samman Nidhi beneficiaries; MGNREGA job card holders; women with net family income less than ₹8 lakh per annum; pregnant and lactating AWWs/AWHs/ASHAs; women holding ration card under NFSA 2013
geographic_scope: Pan-India (except Telangana and Odisha, which have their own maternity benefit schemes)
eligibility: The scheme aims to cover women belonging to socially, economically disadvantaged, and marginalized sections of society. Any of the following eligibility criteria is required to avail the benefit of PMMVY: Women belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes; Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan); Women holder of BPL ration Card; Women Beneficiaries under Pradhan Mantri Jan Aarogya Yojana (PMJAY) under Ayushman Bharat; Women holding E-shram card; Women farmers who are beneficiaries under Kisan Samman Nidhi; Women holding MGNREGA Job Card; Women whose net family income is less than ₹8 Lakh per annum; Pregnant and Lactating AWWs/ AWHs/ ASHAs; Women holding Ration Card under NFSA Act 2013; Any other category as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
benefits: Financial assistance of Rs 5000/- for the first child in two instalments (₹3000/- after Ante-Natal Check-up and ₹2000/- after childbirth and 14 weeks of universal immunization); Rs. 6000/- for the second child (if girl child) in a single instalment after childbirth and completion of universal immunization within 14 weeks; eligibility for Janani Suraksha Yojana (Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Scheme) after institutional delivery; direct benefit transfer to Aadhaar-linked bank/post office account; self-registration provision across the country; mobile app for registration; field functionaries (AWW/ASHA) can fill applications online for beneficiaries in their jurisdiction.
financial_support: The PMMVY benefit of Rs 5000/- is given for the first child in two instalments (first instalment of ₹3000/- after Ante-Natal Check-up (ANC) and second instalment of ₹2000/- after the childbirth and 14 weeks of universal immunization). Rs. 6000/- is given for the second child (if girl child) in a single instalment after the childbirth and completion of universal immunization within 14 weeks. After filling of online application form and approval of block level officer, the fund will be directly credited to the Aadhaar based bank account of the beneficiary through Direct Beneficiary Transfer (DBT).
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs 5000/- for first child; Rs 6000/- for second child (if girl child)
application_process: 1. Visit the nearest Anganwadi worker/ASHA worker or access the PMMVY portal at https://pmmvy.wcd.gov.in. 2. Fill the online application form (self-registration or through AWW/ASHA). 3. Upload required documents including Aadhaar card, Aadhaar-mapped bank/post office account details, mobile number, eligibility proof, MCP/RCHI card, LMP date, ANC date, child birth certificate, and child immunization details. 4. Submit the application. 5. Await approval from block level officer. 6. Upon approval, funds are disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the Aadhaar-linked bank/post office account.
deadlines: A beneficiary is eligible to register in the PMMVY portal till 270 days from childbirth.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Women and Child Development
contact_details: Email Id: pmmvy-mwcd@gov.in | For Helpline: 1515 (from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm)

overview: Mission Shakti is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development to strengthen interventions for women safety, security, and empowerment. It integrates the erstwhile schemes of Umbrella Scheme for Protection and Development of Women and aims to address issues affecting women through a life-cycle continuum approach. The scheme focuses on convergence, capacity building, and strengthening institutional mechanisms at national, state, and district levels.
target_beneficiaries: women; girl children; adolescent girls; pregnant and lactating mothers; elderly women
eligibility: The scheme targets all women and girls in India, with special focus on vulnerable and marginalized groups including those affected by violence, belonging to SC/ST/OBC communities, residing in rural and tribal areas, and economically weaker sections. Implementation is carried out through State Governments and UT Administrations based on need assessment and gap analysis.
benefits: Benefits include financial assistance for setting up One Stop Centres (OSCs), Women Helplines (WHLs), and Sakhi Niwas (working women's hostels); support for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) activities; capacity building and training of stakeholders; awareness generation campaigns; and strengthening of existing institutions like Swadhar Grehs and Ujjwala Homes. Non-financial benefits include improved access to justice, counselling, medical aid, legal assistance, and temporary shelter for women in distress.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as a centrally sponsored scheme with cost-sharing between the Centre and States. For North Eastern and Himalayan States, the funding ratio is 90:10 (Centre:State); for all other States, it is 60:40; and for Union Territories without Legislature, it is 100% central funding. Funds are released based on annual plans and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. State Governments/UT Administrations prepare Annual Action Plans based on gap analysis and needs assessment. 2. Plans are submitted to the Ministry of Women and Child Development for appraisal. 3. Ministry appraises and approves the plans. 4. Funds are released in instalments based on utilization of previous grants and submission of required documents. 5. States/UTs implement the scheme components through designated nodal agencies. 6. Monitoring and evaluation are conducted through periodic reviews and third-party audits.
deadlines: Annual cycle — Action Plans to be submitted by States/UTs each financial year, typically before the start of the fiscal year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Women and Child Development

overview: The Homestay Scheme for Rural Tourism is a sub-scheme under Swadesh Darshan 2.0, aimed at developing homestays in tribal areas to promote responsible tourism and enhance livelihood opportunities for tribal communities. It provides funding support for the development and renovation of tribal homestays and village community requirements, creating community-based responsible tourism through cultural exchange between tourists and indigenous people. The scheme is implemented under the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PMJUGA) and targets the development of 1000 homestays in tribal areas.
target_beneficiaries: tribal households; tribal communities; rural entrepreneurs
eligibility: The State Government / UT Administrations shall be required to identify suitable tribal village(s) and tribal beneficiary(ies) in the tribal areas for construction/renovation of homestays. This shall be done in consultation with the local community. State Government / UT Administration shall give priority to establish Home stays in the Dharti Aaba villages. However the same can be established in nearby suitable tribal villages after exhausting this possibility, with the intention that the Dharti Aaba villages will also be benefitted under ripple effect. Further, under the secondary impact, tribals from Dharti Aaba villages can also be trained and involved to provide services including hospitality, guides, cultural shows etc. Selection of villages should be done with the objective to provide awareness for Livelihood while preserving and celebrating culture of tribal communities. Similarly, the State Governments/UTAs shall identify required interventions for the village community where homestays are proposed for funding to enhance tourism potential of the identified village and the same may be included in the project proposal.
benefits: Funding support for development & renovation of Tribal Homestays and village community requirements. Creation of community-based responsible tourism in tribal villages through cultural exchange between tourists and indigenous people. Authentic tribal rural experience for tourists. Encouragement for states/UTs to provide further assistance required to uplift the livelihood of the local community. Opportunity for tribal households to generate alternate livelihood through homestay operations. Capacity building and training for tribal beneficiaries in hospitality, guiding, and cultural shows. Integration of feedback mechanism on promotional websites/platforms. Periodic data collection on revenue generation, occupancy, and feedback received.
financial_support: The Government of India will provide 100% of the funds for the identified components of the project. The central funding under the scheme shall be routed through the Implementing Agency designated by the State/UT. The Implementing Agency will also be responsible to disburse funds to individual beneficiaries / village communities in a well-defined and transparent manner. The funds would be released to the Implementing Agency of the concerned States/UTs after in-principle approval of the projects by the Ministry of Tourism. States/UTs will submit one project to the Ministry of Tourism under this scheme which may include proposal for cluster(s) of villages comprising of five-six (5-6) villages in a cluster and 5-10 homestays in each village. A maximum of Rs. 5 crores may be provided to each State/UT. For exceptional projects, the Ministry of Tourism (MoT) may propose a higher allocation upto Rs. 2 crore to the best performing States/UTs. The decision of MoT on the amount to be approved for the project shall be final. Higher allocation would be considered only in those cases where States have been able to exhaust the upper ceiling (of Rs. 5.00 Crore) and post recommendation of Mission Directorate and Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee. The funding under the scheme cannot be utilized for land acquisition, resettlement and rehabilitation, relocation, dredging/development of bunds of a water body (man-made & natural both) etc.
application_process: 1. States/UTs shall identify suitable tribal villages with tourism potential and tribal beneficiaries for homestay development in consultation with local community. 2. States/UTs shall prioritize Dharti Aaba villages for homestay establishment. 3. States/UTs shall identify required interventions for village community to enhance tourism potential. 4. States/UTs shall prepare project proposal as per the Model Template (Annexure-I) including preference to female homestay owners, model homestay design according to local vernacular architecture, marketing plan, convergence with central and state schemes, development of community space, and capacity building plan. 5. States/UTs shall submit the project proposal on the portal (sd2.tourism.gov.in) with covering letter of State/UT Tourism Secretary as per timeline communicated by Ministry of Tourism. 6. In case of any issues related to proposal submission on the portal, States/UTs may submit the proposal on email id swadesh.darshan@gov.in and inform the same to the Ministry. 7. Proposals meeting guidelines shall be placed before Mission Directorate (MD) for review and recommendation to Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC). 8. CSMC after due examination will grant approval to the project and further, the project will be sanctioned by the Ministry of Tourism. 9. State Government has to implement the project as per approved project proposal and scheme guidelines. 10. In case of any revisions in the project, approval of CSMC will be obtained.
deadlines: As per timeline communicated by the Ministry of Tourism from time to time
implementing_agency: State Government / UT Administrations (to designate Implementing Agency)

overview: The Hunar Se Rozgar Tak (HSRT) Scheme is a skill development initiative by the Ministry of Tourism aimed at providing hospitality training to youth from economically weaker sections to enhance employability in the tourism sector. It offers short-term courses in various hospitality trades such as Multi Cuisine Cook, Food & Beverage Service Steward, Room Attendant, Front Office Associate, and others, aligned with the National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF). The scheme focuses on wage and self-employment outcomes, with stipends, certification, and placement support provided to trainees.
target_beneficiaries: youth; economically weaker sections; unemployed persons; persons seeking skill development in hospitality
eligibility: The scheme targets persons with not much means and in need to acquire skills facilitative to employment. For fresh entrants to the job market, training duration must be minimum 200 hours (including practical and/or on-the-job training). For re-skilling or skill up-gradation of persons already engaged in an occupation, training programmes must have a minimum duration of 16 hours or more of trainings including practical and/or on-the-job training. Persons who have acquired skill through informal, non-formal or experiential training in any vocational trade or craft are eligible if formal recognition and certification of such skill is obtained after imparting bridge courses.
benefits: Trainees receive a stipend (e.g., Rs.1,000/- for certain courses under Entrepreneurship Programme, or Rs.300/- per day under Tourism Awareness Programme), certification upon successful completion with minimum 80% attendance, placement tracking for one year, support for self-employment via loans/licenses, and third-party assessment and certification. The scheme also provides training of trainers, curriculum, equipment, raw material, and trainer salaries as part of the funding norms.
financial_support: Funding norms are based on trade/job role classification. For example, under the Entrepreneurship Programme (EP), the total cost per trainee is Rs.11,340/-, comprising training fee (Rs.5,000), course material (Rs.500), certification fee (Rs.1,000), apron (Rs.300), lunch (Rs.3,000), stipend (Rs.1,000), and administrative expenses (5% of total cost, Rs.540). Funds are released to implementing agencies in instalments based on outcomes achieved outcomes, with 10% released upon tracking 90% of candidates in a batch (or Rs.5,000 per candidate, whichever is less).
application_process: 1. Identify eligible trainees meeting attendance and eligibility criteria. 2. Enroll trainees in NSQF-approved hospitality courses under HSRT. 3. Conduct training with minimum 6 hours daily for five/six days a week. 4. Maintain attendance records and ensure minimum 80% attendance for eligibility to appear in final assessment. 5. Conduct internal and external assessment by independent examiners. 6. Award certification to successful trainees. 7. Track trainees for one year post-certification for career progression and retention. 8. Submit utilization reports and progress reports to the Ministry of Tourism. 9. Ensure Aadhaar and bank account linkage for stipend transfer via PFMS. 10. Upload video clippings on 10th and concluding day of training to the Programme Monitoring Unit (Skill Development) at pmuhsrt@gmail.com.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted quarterly (upto 31st March, 30th June, 30th September, and 31st December every year) for empanelment of training providers; training batches are conducted as per institutional capacity and prior permission from the Ministry.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
contact_details: Email: pmuhsrt@gmail.com (Programme Monitoring Unit - Skill Development)

scheme_name: Geological Survey of India (GSI) Startup Mineral Exploration
overview: The Geological Survey of India (GSI) is a world-class organization providing expertise and disseminating geoscientific information for sustainable socio-economic development. It undertakes projects related to critical minerals, resource augmentation in the National Mineral Inventory, and mineral blocks handed over for auction. GSI focuses on the strategic evolution of mineral exploration and undertakes various projects related to mineral exploration and mining projects.
implementing_agency: Geological Survey of India (GSI)

overview: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) is a central sector scheme aimed at providing quality education to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students in remote areas through the establishment and management of residential schools from Class VI to XII. The scheme focuses on holistic development, including academic excellence, preservation of tribal culture and heritage, and overall personality development of tribal children. EMRS schools are designed to be at par with Navodaya Vidyalayas in terms of infrastructure and academic standards.
target_beneficiaries: Scheduled Tribe (ST) students
eligibility: The scheme targets Scheduled Tribe students studying in classes VI to XII. Admission is primarily based on merit and availability of seats, with priority given to students from Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), displaced families, and those affected by left-wing extremism. Schools are set up in blocks with 50% or more ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons.
benefits: Free education, lodging, boarding, school uniforms, textbooks, stationery, and medical care. Students receive holistic development through co-curricular activities, sports, life skills training, and exposure to tribal culture and traditions. The schools follow CBSE curriculum and aim for all-round development of tribal children.
financial_support: The scheme provides 100% financial assistance from the Government of India for both recurring and non-recurring expenses. The central government bears the full cost of setting up and operating EMRS, including infrastructure development, staff salaries, student maintenance, and educational resources. Funding is released directly to the implementing agency, the National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS), which manages the schools.
application_process: 1. State governments or UT administrations identify suitable locations for EMRS based on tribal population density. 2. Proposals for new schools are submitted to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs through the state government. 3. 3. The Ministry appraises the proposal based on norms and availability of funds. 4. Upon approval, funds are sanctioned to NESTS for construction and operation. 5. Admissions are conducted annually through a selection process based on merit and eligibility criteria. 6. Selected students are enrolled in the respective EMRS for classes VI to XII.
deadlines: Admissions are conducted annually, typically before the start of the academic session. Exact dates vary by state and are notified by the respective EMRS or state tribal welfare department.
implementing_agency: National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS), under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India

overview: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas in May 2016 to provide deposit-free LPG connections to women from poor households. The scheme aims to replace traditional cooking fuels with clean cooking fuel (LPG) to improve health and reduce environmental degradation. As of July 2026, over 10.56 crore LPG connections have been released under the scheme, including extensions like Ujjwala 2.0 and additional allocations. The scheme provides financial assistance for security deposit, regulator, hose, installation charges, and includes free first refill and stove.
target_beneficiaries: women; poor households; SC/ST; PMAY(Gramin); Most Backward Classes; Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY); Tea and Ex-Tea Garden tribes; Forest Dwellers; People residing in Islands and River Islands; SECC Households; Migrant households
eligibility: The applicant must be a woman who has attained 18 years of age. There should be no other LPG connection from any Oil Marketing Company (OMC) within the same household. The adult woman must belong to a poor household based on submission of a deprivation declaration (as per prescribed format). Eligible categories include SC Households, ST Households, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin), Most Backward Classes, Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY), Tea and Ex-Tea Garden tribes, Forest Dwellers, People residing in Islands and River Islands, SECC Households (AHL TIN), and Poor Household as per 14-point declaration.
benefits: Cash assistance for PMUY connections is provided by Government of India - Rs. 1600 (for a connection 14.2kg cylinder/ Rs. 1150 for a 5 kg cylinder). The cash assistance covers: Security Deposit of Cylinder – Rs. 1250 for 14.2 kg cylinder/ Rs. 800 for 5 kg cylinder, Pressure Regulator – Rs. 150, LPG Hose – Rs. 100, Domestic Gas Consumer Card – Rs. 25, Inspection/Installation/Demonstration charges – Rs. 75. Additionally, all PMUY beneficiaries are provided with first LPG refill and stove (hotplate) both free of cost along with their deposit-free connection by the Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).
financial_support: Cash assistance for PMUY connections is provided by Government of India - Rs. 1600 (for a connection 14.2kg cylinder/ Rs. 1150 for a 5 kg cylinder). The cash assistance covers: Security Deposit of Cylinder – Rs. 1250 for 14.2 kg cylinder/ Rs. 800 for 5 kg cylinder, Pressure Regulator – Rs. 150, LPG Hose – Rs. 100, Domestic Gas Consumer Card – Rs. 25, Inspection/Installation/Demonstration charges – Rs. 75. Additionally, all PMUY beneficiaries are provided with first LPG refill and stove (hotplate) both free of cost along with their deposit-free connection by the Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 1600 (for a connection 14.2kg cylinder/ Rs. 1150 for a 5 kg cylinder)
application_process: 1. Applicants can apply online through the application form available at https://pmuy.gov.in or visit the nearest CSC Centre for assistance in submitting the application. 2. There is no fee for self-submission. However, a charge of ₹20 will be applicable if the application is submitted through CSC Centres. 3. Offline applicants can directly submit the application at preferably nearest LPG distributorship of OMCs. 4. Required documents include KYC form, Aadhaar copy, proof of address, ration card or state government document certifying family composition, bank account details, and deprivation declaration. 5. For migrant applicants, self-declaration as per Annexure I for PoA and family composition is sufficient. 6. After submission, the application is verified by the LPG distributor and connection is released upon successful verification.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MOPNG)
