The Medical & Wellness Tourism Policy is a scheme under the Ministry of Tourism aimed at promoting India as a destination for medical and wellness tourism. It seeks to leverage India's traditional healthcare systems and modern medical facilities to attract international patients. The policy focuses on infrastructure development, service quality enhancement, and global marketing of medical and wellness tourism offerings.
target_beneficiaries: tourism service providers; state governments; union territory administrations
eligibility: The Tourism Service Providers must be approved by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, or by the concerned State / Union Territory Tourism Department. The approved Tourism Service Providers showing minimum FEE of Rs. 1.00 crore – Rs. 2.00 crore in any one of the preceding two (2) years i.e. 2018-19 or 2019-20, the number of tours may be limited to maximum of two (02) in one financial year. The approved Tourism Service Providers showing minimum FEE of Rs. 2.00 crore and above in any one of the preceding two (2) years i.e. 2018-19 or 2019-20, the number of tours may be limited to maximum of three (03) in one financial year. Tourism Departments of State Governments / UT Administrations are also eligible to avail benefits under the Scheme. However, the above eligibility conditions are NOT applicable to them.
benefits: Financial support for Study Tours, participation in travel shows / exhibitions/ Road Shows (organized by the Ministry of Tourism) in the overseas markets would be extended as per following details, subject to an overall ceiling of Rs. 3.50 Lakh per case / tour: Economy class air fare for travel between India to another country and from there to a group of countries by air / rail at 90%; Cost of built up / furnished stall, electricity and water charges, participation fee, etc., at travel fair / exhibitions held overseas at 90%; Lodging expenses on overseas tour Max. 5 nights with an upper ceiling of room rate at Rs. 10,000/- per night. Financial support for participation in travel shows / exhibitions / in the overseas markets would be extended for Tourism Departments of State Governments / UT Administrations as per following details: Cost of built up / furnished stall, electricity and water charges, participation fee, etc., at travel fair / exhibitions held overseas with an overall ceiling of Rs. 3.50 Lakh. Financial support would be extended for Online Promotion of tourism destinations and products, tour packages in the overseas markets, including content creation / production of digital promotional brochures / leaflets etc. @ 50% of the total cost with an upper ceiling of Rs. 1.00 lakh/- once in a financial year, subject to actuals.
financial_support: Financial support for Study Tours, participation in travel shows / exhibitions/ Road Shows (organized by the Ministry of Tourism) in the overseas markets would be extended as per following details, subject to an overall ceiling of Rs. 3.50 Lakh per case / tour: Economy class air fare for travel between India to another country and from there to a group of countries by air / rail at 90%; Cost of built up / furnished stall, electricity and water charges, participation fee, etc., at travel fair / exhibitions held overseas at 90%; Lodging expenses on overseas tour Max. 5 nights with an upper ceiling of room rate at Rs. 10,000/- per night. Financial support for participation in travel shows / exhibitions / in the overseas markets would be extended for Tourism Departments of State Governments / UT Administrations as per following details: Cost of built up / furnished stall, electricity and water charges, participation fee, etc., at travel fair / exhibitions held overseas with an overall ceiling of Rs. 3.50 Lakh. Financial support would be extended for Online Promotion of tourism destinations and products, tour packages in the overseas markets, including content creation / production of digital promotional brochures / leaflets etc. @ 50% of the total cost with an upper ceiling of Rs. 1.00 lakh/- once in a financial year, subject to actuals.
application_process: 1. The eligible TSP/SG/UT shall obtain Prior Approval of the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, before undertaking tour overseas. 2. The application as at Annexure -I for Prior Approval, shall be submitted to the Assistant Director General (Overseas Marketing), Government of India, Ministry of Tourism, on e-mail: mda-tourism@gov.in at least 21 days in advance prior to undertaking tour. 3. Prior Approval shall be granted subject to receipt of application complete in all respect. 4. After undertaking the tourism promotional activity/tour abroad for which Prior Approval had been accorded by the Ministry of Tourism, the Tourism Service Provider / State Govt./ UT Administration will submit the application for re -imbursement/claim, in the prescribed / applicable formats placed at Annexures – II, III & IV to the Assistant Director General (Overseas Marketing), Ministry of Tourism, Govt. of India, Transport Bhawan, 1, Parliament Street, New Delhi 110 001 on email mda-tourism@nic.in positively within a period of 45 days of completion of the activity. 5. Submission of claims in physical form will not be accepted. All documents submitted should be in pdf format only.
deadlines: Financial support under the Scheme would be subject to availability of budget during the year under the MDA Scheme.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Tourism

overview: The Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) Industry Linkage scheme, managed by the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL), aims to enhance logistics efficiency by connecting industrial hubs to the Dedicated Freight Corridors. It facilitates seamless freight movement, reduces transit time and cost, and supports industrial growth through improved rail connectivity. The scheme focuses on developing last-mile connectivity and industrial nodes along the DFC network.
target_beneficiaries: industries; manufacturing units; logistics providers; MSME
eligibility: Industries, manufacturing units, and logistics providers located near or planning to locate along the Dedicated Freight Corridor network are eligible to apply for linkage development. Entities must have valid industrial registration and comply with DFCCIL's technical and safety standards for siding connections.
benefits: Financial assistance for siding construction, priority path allocation on DFC, reduced freight charges, assured wagon availability, end-to-end logistics solution, reduced carbon footprint, and improved supply chain reliability.
financial_support: DFCCIL provides financial support for the construction of private sidings connecting industries to the DFC network, typically covering a portion of the capital cost based on traffic volume and commitment. The support is disbursed in milestones linked to construction progress and operational readiness.
application_process: 1. Identify the nearest DFC alignment and conduct feasibility study for siding connection. 2. Submit a formal application to DFCCIL with project details, land documents, and traffic projections. 3. Obtain in-principle approval from DFCCIL after technical evaluation. 4. Sign a Licensing Agreement for siding construction and maintenance. 5. Construct the siding as per DFCCIL specifications under supervision. 6. Complete safety inspection and commissioning. 7. Begin operations and avail linkage benefits.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to technical feasibility and network capacity.
implementing_agency: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL)

scheme_name: LEEP – Logistics Ease Across Different States
overview: LEEP – Logistics Ease Across Different States is a government initiative aimed at improving logistics efficiency and reducing costs across Indian states by identifying bottlenecks, streamlining procedures, and enhancing infrastructure coordination. The scheme focuses on creating a unified logistics ecosystem through policy reforms, digital integration, and stakeholder collaboration to boost trade competitiveness.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; logistics providers; state governments; industry stakeholders
eligibility: The scheme involves participation from state governments, logistics service providers, industry associations, and other stakeholders engaged in logistics and supply chain operations across India.
benefits: Improved logistics efficiency, reduced transit times and costs, enhanced supply chain reliability, better infrastructure utilization, data-driven policy insights, and increased competitiveness for businesses engaged in inter-state and international trade.
financial_support: LEEP does not provide direct financial support to entities; it is a policy and coordination framework focused on systemic improvements through governance, infrastructure planning, and regulatory harmonization.
application_process: LEEP does not have a traditional application process for beneficiaries; it operates through intergovernmental coordination, data collection from states, stakeholder consultations, and periodic assessment of logistics performance via the LEEP index.
deadlines: Rolling basis — assessments and updates are conducted periodically as part of ongoing logistics performance monitoring.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: TRIFED Schemes for Tribal Enterprises aim to promote tribal entrepreneurship by transforming Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) into Van Dhan Producer Enterprises (VDPEs) through capacity building, market access, and financial support. The schemes focus on value addition of Minor Forest Produce (MFP), sustainable livelihood generation, and integration of tribal communities into formal economic systems. TRIFED acts as the nodal agency under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, implementing initiatives like Van Dhan Yojana, PTP-NER, and Tech for Tribals to enhance tribal income and economic resilience.
target_beneficiaries: tribal entrepreneurs; tribal gatherers; self-help groups; MSME
eligibility: Tribal individuals, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs), and tribal producer groups engaged in Minor Forest Produce (MFP) collection, value addition, and marketing under the Van Dhan Yojana or Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Vikas Yojana (PMVDY) are eligible. VDPEs require federation of four or more geographically proximate VDVKs, with relaxation possible based on feasibility and justification reviewed by TRIFED.
benefits: Benefits include capacity building and training programs (e.g., Tech for Tribal with 120 sessions), market access through TRIBES India retail outlets and exhibitions, financial support for equipment and infrastructure, brand development under 'Tribes India', access to e-commerce platforms, participation in national and international fairs, skill upgradation, and institutional support for legal registration and governance of Van Dhan Producer Enterprises (VDPEs).
financial_support: Financial support is provided through a three-tranche fund release model: 10% upon proposal approval for initiation activities, 40% upon submission of Utilization Certificate and Detailed Project Report for capacity building and infrastructure setup, and 50% upon full utilization of the second tranche and verified implementation. For Implementation Support Agencies (ISAs), funding is deliverable-based across pre-planning, implementation, and post-implementation phases. Van Dhan Kendras have been sanctioned Rs. 15 lakhs each, with Rs. 1 lakh per SHG of 20 members for training, equipment, and activities. Under MSP for MFP, Rs. 5 lakhs is advised to be released to VDVKs to make them primary procurement agencies.
application_process: 1. State Implementing Agency (SIA) or Implementation Support Agency (ISA) prepares project proposal in coordination with State Nodal Department (SND) and TRIFED Regional Office (RO). 2. Submit proposal to TRIFED for approval. 3. Upon approval, receive first tranche (10% for SIA, 10–20% for ISA) to initiate activities like staff deployment and awareness generation. 4. Submit Utilization Certificate (UC) and Detailed Project Report (DPR) for second tranche (40% for SIA, 30–40% for ISA) to fund capacity building, infrastructure setup, and revival of defunct VDVKs. 5. Achieve full utilization of second tranche, undergo verification, and submit supporting documents for final tranche (50% for SIA, remaining balance for ISA) to support market linkage, operationalization, and monitoring & evaluation. 6. TRIFED conducts periodic physical verifications, audits, and performance evaluations throughout the lifecycle.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Limited (TRIFED)
contact_details: Email: info@tribesindia.com | Phone: 91(11)71600410, 71600420 | Address: NSIC, MDBP Building, Ground Floor, Core 07-12, Okhla Phase-III, Okhla Industrial Estate, New Delhi–110020

overview: The Punjab Startup and Entrepreneurship Policy is a state-level initiative launched by the Government of Punjab to foster innovation, support early-stage startups, and build a vibrant entrepreneurial ecosystem across the state. It aims to provide financial, infrastructural, and regulatory support to startups in key sectors such as IT, agro-processing, manufacturing, and biotechnology. The policy emphasizes ease of doing business, access to funding, and collaboration between industry, academia, and government.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; MSME
eligibility: Startups incorporated as Private Limited Company, LLP, or Partnership Firm under relevant Indian laws, with headquarters or significant operations in Punjab, working on innovative products, services, or processes, and recognized by the Department of Industries, Government of Punjab, or an approved incubator.
benefits: Financial support through seed funding and grants, access to state-funded incubators and co-working spaces, mentorship from industry experts, fast-track approvals and single-window clearance, assistance in intellectual property rights (IPR) filing, participation in state-organized startup events and exhibitions, and facilitation of linkages with investors and markets.
financial_support: The policy provides for the creation of a Punjab Startup Fund with a corpus to be contributed by the state government and financial institutions, offering seed funding of up to INR 25 Lakhs per startup in the form of grants or convertible equity, along with reimbursement of up to 50% of costs incurred on patent filing, subject to a maximum of INR 2 Lakhs per startup.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 25 Lakhs
application_process: 1. Register the startup with the Department of Industries, Government of Punjab, or an approved incubator. 2. Submit the incorporation documents, business plan, and details of innovation. 3. Apply for recognition as an eligible startup under the policy. 4. Submit application for financial support along with required documents such as project report, cost estimates, and bank details. 5. Application is reviewed by the designated committee. 6. Upon approval, financial support is disbursed in stages based on milestones. 7. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department of Industries, Government of Punjab

scheme_name: Mechanism for Marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP)
overview: The Mechanism for Marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP) through Minimum Support Price (MSP) & Development of Value Chain for MFP is a central sector scheme launched by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, to ensure fair and remunerative prices for tribal MFP gatherers by institutionalizing the value chain through training, sustainable collection, procurement, value addition, infrastructure, and marketing. Implemented by TRIFED as the nodal agency, the scheme aims to empower tribal communities by enhancing their income and livelihoods through sustainable harvesting, skill upgradation, and market linkages, with a focus on women's financial empowerment and convergence with other development partners.
target_beneficiaries: tribal MFP gatherers; Self Help Groups (SHGs); Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs); tribal artisans; forest dwellers
eligibility: The Scheme covers 50 non-nationalized MFPs (Annexure 1) and includes all states and union territories of India. The scheme is designed to be implemented through State and District level functionaries. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs as the Nodal Ministry will be the Central Apex Committee and responsible for policy, oversight and obtaining and providing budgetary resources for the Scheme. TRIFED will function as the technical support unit for MoTA and will coordinate the implementation and flow of funds of the Scheme through the designated State and other agencies including District Implementing Units through an Executive Committee setup within TRIFED. The Minimum Support Price will be recommended by the Pricing Cell setup in TRIFED. The State Government would identify the State Nodal Department and other agencies including the District Implementing Units. The State Nodal Department will coordinate the flow of funds and.
benefits: The Scheme provides direct benefits to the tribal by institutionalizing various avenues in the value chain of MFP such as training, sustainable collection, procurement, value addition, infrastructure, marketing etc. It ensures training on sustainable harvesting with primary level value addition, skill upgradation and processing. The 'Van Dhan Vikas Karyakram' adds to the income and livelihoods for tribals by harnessing the wealth of forests. The programme aims to tap into traditional knowledge & skill sets of tribals to convert the tribal wisdom into a viable economic activity. The Scheme has strong linkage to women’s financial empowerment. MFP collection and value addition activity is also undertaken by women MFP gatherers. The Scheme ensures fair and remunerative price s to the tribals. It provides fair deal to tribals by offering Minimum Support Price to the tribal MFP gatherers for forest produces collected by them. It also pro visions to bridge the last mile connectivity between the tribals and markets through activation of Haat bazars by strengthening of grassroots infrastructure for MFP procurement, storage, transportation, marketing etc. Besides specific thrust is being given under the Scheme on training and skill upgradation of the tribal artisans in a systematic manner by introducing value addition and marketing through tribal groups and clusters.
financial_support: The Fund Flow Mechanism involves the Ministry of Tribal Affairs as the Nodal Ministry being the Central Apex Committee responsible for policy, oversight and obtaining and providing budgetary resources for the Scheme. TRIFED functions as the technical support unit for MoTA and coordinates the implementation and flow of funds of the Scheme through the designated State and other agencies including District Implementing Units through an Executive Committee setup within TRIFED. The Minimum Support Price is recommended by the Pricing Cell setup in TRIFED. The announcement of MSP is done by MoTA. The State Government identifies the State Nodal Department and other agencies including the District Implementing Units. The State Nodal Department coordinates the flow of funds and.
implementing_agency: Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Limited (TRIFED)

overview: The MedTech Regulatory Sandbox (CDSCO) is a framework designed to support innovation in medical technology by providing a controlled environment for testing and validating new medical devices, diagnostics, and digital health solutions under regulatory supervision. It aims to accelerate the development and market entry of innovative MedTech products while ensuring safety, efficacy, and compliance with Indian regulatory standards. The sandbox facilitates collaboration between startups, innovators, and regulatory authorities to streamline approval processes and reduce time-to-market for emerging healthcare technologies.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; innovators; medical device manufacturers
eligibility: Eligible applicants include Indian startups, MSMEs, and innovators developing medical devices, in-vitro diagnostics, digital health solutions, or other MedTech products. The applicant must be a legally registered entity in India, possess a clear innovation or technological solution with potential for healthcare impact, and demonstrate readiness for prototype testing or clinical validation. Preference may be given to solutions addressing unmet medical needs or aligned with national health programs.
benefits: Participants receive regulatory guidance and hand-holding from CDSCO experts, access to accelerated review pathways, waiver or relaxation of certain procedural requirements during the sandbox phase, opportunity to test products in real-world or simulated environments, support for clinical trial design and approval, facilitation of connections with testing labs and hospitals, and assistance in preparing documentation for final market authorization. Non-financial benefits include mentorship, technical support, and networking with regulators and industry experts.
financial_support: The MedTech Regulatory Sandbox does not provide direct financial grants or funding to participants. Support is primarily non-financial in nature, focusing on regulatory facilitation, technical guidance, and access to infrastructure and expertise. Any financial aspects related to product development, testing, or clinical trials must be borne by the applicant or sourced through external funding mechanisms.
application_process: 1. Submit an online application through the designated CDSCO portal detailing the innovation, intended use, and development stage. 2. Provide supporting documents including product description, technical specifications, preclinical data (if any), and team credentials. 3. Undergo initial screening by CDSCO to assess eligibility and sandbox suitability. 4. If shortlisted, present the proposal to the sandbox evaluation committee for review. 5. Upon acceptance, sign a memorandum of understanding outlining the scope, duration, and responsibilities. 6. Begin sandbox activities including product testing, data generation, and regulatory interactions as per the agreed plan. 7. Submit periodic progress reports and final outcomes for evaluation. 8. Receive feedback and recommendations for next steps toward regulatory approval or commercialization.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on availability and evaluation cycles.
implementing_agency: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India

overview: Invest Punjab – Business First Portal is a state-level initiative by the Punjab Bureau of Investment Promotion (Invest Punjab) that serves as a single point of contact for investors seeking to set up businesses in Punjab. It provides state-level regulatory clearances, approvals for fiscal incentives, and facilitates the entire investment lifecycle from proposal to implementation. The portal operates under the 'Business First' philosophy, aiming to reduce compliance burden, ensure time-bound digital approvals, and foster a conducive environment for growth, innovation, and employment generation.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; entrepreneurs; investors; industries
eligibility: Investors looking to set up a business in Punjab, including domestic and international investors, startups, MSMEs, and industries seeking state-level regulatory clearances and fiscal incentives through the Invest Punjab portal.
benefits: Unified regulator for 40+ state-level approvals across 12+ departments, dedicated relationship manager, time-bound and digital approvals, power at affordable rates, peaceful labour relations, one-stop clearance system, attractive incentives, robust infrastructure, skilled human capital, and facilitation of fiscal incentives and regulatory approvals via the Business First Portal.
financial_support: Invest Punjab does not directly provide financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Instead, it facilitates access to fiscal incentives and regulatory approvals through the state government, and supports investors in availing benefits from central and state schemes, including partnerships with SIDBI for MSME development.
application_process: 1. Visit the Invest Punjab Business First Portal at https://investpunjab.gov.in 2. Complete investor registration and login 3. Submit the Online Common Application Form (CAF) for regulatory clearances 4. Apply online for fiscal incentives 5. Receive digital regulatory approvals and make e-payments through the Unified Regulator system 6. Access dedicated helpdesk for assistance 7. Utilize aftercare services for continuous industry engagement
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Punjab Bureau of Investment Promotion (Invest Punjab), Government of Punjab

scheme_name: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation Fast Track
overview: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) Fast Track scheme is designed to expedite regulatory processes for pharmaceutical products, including drugs, biologics, and medical devices, by streamlining approvals, reducing timelines, and enhancing transparency in the evaluation and licensing procedures. It aims to facilitate faster market access for innovative and essential medical products while maintaining stringent safety, efficacy, and quality standards. The scheme leverages digital platforms like the SUGAM portal for online submissions and integrates with national regulatory frameworks to ensure uniformity and accountability across central and state drug control organizations.
target_beneficiaries: pharmaceutical companies; biologics manufacturers; medical device firms; importers; exporters; startups; MSME
eligibility: Eligibility applies to manufacturers, importers, exporters, and authorized agents of drugs, biologics, medical devices, and cosmetics seeking registration, import licensing, or market authorization in India. Applicants must comply with the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and Rules 1945, including submission of required documentation via the SUGAM portal, adherence to Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Good Distribution Practices (GDP), and provision of valid wholesale/manufacturing licenses, product details, stability data, and undertakings as specified in CDSCO guidelines. Startups and MSMEs may avail relaxations in experience and turnover criteria under relevant government policies.
benefits: Faster processing of registration certificates, import licenses, and market authorizations; reduced timelines for scrutiny and approval via digital SUGAM portal; enhanced transparency through online tracking and status updates; facilitation of export-oriented permissions and no-objection certificates; support for innovation via accelerated pathways for biologics and medical devices; alignment with international regulatory standards; access to guidance documents, public notices, and stakeholder consultation mechanisms; and integration with national pharmacovigilance and quality control systems.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Instead, it offers procedural and regulatory benefits including fee-based services (e.g., application fees for registration and import licensing), with costs borne by applicants. Financial transactions are processed via TR-6 challans for fees deposited under relevant heads (e.g., '0210 - Medical and Public Health'). No corpus fund or per-entity financial allocation is specified under this fast track mechanism.
application_process: 1. Access the SUGAM portal at https://sugam.cdsco.in for online submission. 2. Determine the appropriate application form (e.g., Form 40 for Registration Certificate, Form 8/8A for Import License) based on the product type. 3. Prepare and upload required documents including covering letter, application form, power of attorney, TR-6 challan of fees paid, import permissions, wholesale/manufacturing licenses, authorization letters, product specifications, stability data, and labels. 4. Submit the application through the SUGAM portal. 5. Undergo technical review by Drugs Inspector, Assistant Drugs Inspector, Assistant Drugs Controller, Deputy Drugs Controller, and Joint Drugs Controller. 6. Respond to any queries raised during review. 7. Receive final approval or rejection from the Drug Controller General of India (for Registration Certificate) or Joint Drugs Controller (for Import License). 8. Upon approval, download the certificate or license from the portal.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round via the SUGAM portal with no fixed annual deadline.
implementing_agency: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

overview: The Multimodal Logistics Park (MMLP) Scheme is a government initiative aimed at developing integrated logistics infrastructure to enhance freight movement efficiency across India. It focuses on creating multimodal hubs that connect various transport modes such as road, rail, and waterways to reduce logistics costs and improve supply chain performance. The scheme is implemented by NHIDCL under the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and supports the Bharatmala Pariyojana and Act East Policy objectives. MMLPs are envisioned as key enablers for economic growth in strategic regions, particularly the North Eastern Region and border areas.
target_beneficiaries: logistics operators; transport agencies; industrial units; freight forwarders; MSMEs engaged in logistics
eligibility: Entities involved in logistics, transport, warehousing, or industrial operations seeking to establish or upgrade multimodal logistics parks in India, particularly in the North Eastern Region, border areas, and strategic corridors under Bharatmala Pariyojana, are eligible to participate or benefit from the scheme through collaboration with NHIDCL.
benefits: The MMLP Scheme offers benefits such as reduced logistics costs, improved supply chain efficiency, enhanced regional connectivity, better access to national and international markets, support for industrial development, job creation in logistics and allied sectors, and integration with digital platforms like INAMPRO, INFRACON, and ePACE for transparent operations. It also enables private sector participation through PPP models and facilitates access to funding from global institutions like ADB and JICA.
financial_support: Financial support under the MMLP Scheme is structured through public-private partnership (PPP) models, with funding sourced from government budgetary allocations, loans from financial institutions, and investments from global agencies such as the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). NHIDCL facilitates project structuring and implementation, leveraging its expertise in infrastructure development in challenging terrains.
application_process: 1. Identify a suitable location for the Multimodal Logistics Park (MMLP) in alignment with national logistics plans and regional connectivity goals. 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) including technical, financial, and environmental aspects. 3. Submit the proposal to NHIDCL or the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways for appraisal. 4. Obtain necessary clearances and approvals from relevant authorities. 5. Enter into a concession agreement or MoU with NHIDCL for project execution. 6. Proceed with land acquisition, design, and construction as per approved plans. 7. Commission the MMLP and initiate operations under the agreed operational framework.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Proposals are accepted and evaluated periodically based on fund availability and project readiness.
implementing_agency: National Highways & Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL), under the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, Government of India

overview: The West Bengal Startup Policy is a state-level initiative aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship within the state of West Bengal. It seeks to create a conducive ecosystem for startups by providing support in areas such as funding, mentorship, infrastructure, and regulatory ease. The policy focuses on promoting technology-driven and innovation-led enterprises across various sectors. It is implemented by the Department of MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; MSME
eligibility: Entities must be registered as a Private Limited Company, Limited Liability Partnership (LLP), or Partnership Firm under relevant Indian laws. The startup should be incorporated in West Bengal or have at least 50% of its operations based in the state. The entity must be working on innovative products, services, or processes with potential for scalability and employment generation. Preference may be given to startups led by women, SC/ST, or differently-abled entrepreneurs.
benefits: Registered startups under the policy may access seed funding, prototype development grants, and reimbursement of patent filing fees. They are eligible for subsidies on lease rental for incubation centers, priority in government procurement, and fast-track clearance for licenses and approvals. Additional benefits include mentorship from industry experts, access to investor networks, participation in startup fairs and roadshows, and support for international market access.
financial_support: Financial support includes seed funding of up to INR 25 lakhs for prototype development and product commercialization. Grants are also provided for intellectual property rights (IPR) protection, with reimbursement of up to INR 2 lakhs for domestic patent filing and INR 10 lakhs for international patent filing. Incubation support includes subsidy on seat rent in government-recognized incubators.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 25 lakhs for seed funding; up to INR 2 lakhs for domestic patent and INR 10 lakhs for international patent reimbursement
application_process: 1. Visit the official MSME West Bengal website or designated startup portal. 2. Register as a startup by providing basic entity and promoter details. 3. Fill out the online application form under the West Bengal Startup Policy. 4. Upload required documents including Certificate of Incorporation, business plan, and proof of innovation. 5. Submit the application for review by the designated committee. 6. Upon approval, receive acknowledgment and further instructions for benefit disbursement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year
implementing_agency: Department of MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal

overview: The Bengal Silicon Valley Startup Hub is a state-level initiative by the Government of West Bengal to foster innovation and entrepreneurship by providing infrastructure, mentorship, and support services to startups in the state. It aims to create a conducive ecosystem for technology-driven ventures through incubation, networking, and access to resources. The hub focuses on enabling early-stage startups to scale by offering shared facilities and expert guidance.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups registered in West Bengal with innovative ideas or technology-based solutions are eligible to apply for the Bengal Silicon Valley Startup Hub.
benefits: Access to incubation infrastructure, mentorship from industry experts, networking opportunities, shared office facilities, and support services to help startups grow and scale.
financial_support: The scheme provides non-financial support such as infrastructure and mentorship; direct financial support details are not specified in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Visit the official website of WBSIDCO. 2. Navigate to the Bengal Silicon Valley Startup Hub section. 3. Fill out the online application form with startup details. 4. Submit required documents including incorporation proof and project proposal. 5. Await review and approval from the implementing agency.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: West Bengal Small Industries Development Corporation Limited (WBSIDCO)

overview: The Assam Startup – Nidhi Program is a state-level initiative under the Assam Startup ecosystem designed to provide financial assistance to early-stage startups registered in Assam. It aims to support innovation and entrepreneurship by offering seed funding to eligible ventures. The program is managed through the Assam Startup portal and focuses on nurturing high-potential startups in their initial phases.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups must be registered in Assam and recognized by the Assam Startup portal. They should be in the early stage of development and demonstrate innovative potential. The startup must be a legal entity registered under the Companies Act, LLP Act, or as a partnership firm.
benefits: Financial support in the form of seed funding to cover initial operational and product development costs. Non-financial benefits include mentorship, networking opportunities, and access to incubation support through the Assam Startup ecosystem.
financial_support: The program provides seed funding to eligible startups as a grant. The exact quantum and disbursement mechanism are determined based on the startup's stage, needs, and evaluation by the selection committee. Funds are disbursed in tranches linked to milestones.
application_process: 1. Register the startup on the Assam Startup portal (assamstartup.com). 2. Ensure the startup profile is complete and up to date. 3. Apply for the Nidhi Program through the designated section on the portal. 4. Submit the required documents along with the application. 5. Await evaluation by the selection committee. 6. If approved, proceed with fund disbursement as per the agreed terms.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Assam Startup, under the Department of Industries and Commerce, Government of Assam

overview: The MP MSME Development Policy 2025 is a state-level initiative by the Government of Madhya Pradesh aimed at promoting the growth and competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) through financial assistance, infrastructure support, and policy incentives. It focuses on strengthening MSMEs by providing access to credit, technology, and market opportunities, while also encouraging rural entrepreneurship and employment generation. The policy includes provisions for land allotment, cluster development, and support for self-employment schemes, with implementation through the Department of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; women entrepreneurs; rural entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as defined under the MSMED Act, 2006, operating in Madhya Pradesh. The policy applies to new and existing MSMEs engaged in manufacturing, services, and agro-based activities. Specific schemes under the policy may have additional criteria such as investment limits, employment generation, and location-based preferences for rural or backward areas.
benefits: Benefits include financial assistance for industrial land allotment, support for cluster development, access to infrastructure and testing facilities, assistance under self-employment schemes, support for technology upgradation and quality certification, marketing assistance, and facilitation of credit linkage. The policy also provides incentives for women entrepreneurs, SC/ST beneficiaries, and units in backward areas, along with support for export promotion and participation in national/international events.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided through schemes like the MP MSME Promotion Scheme 2025 and MP MSME Incentive Scheme 2025, which include subsidies for land allotment, interest subvention, capital investment support, and reimbursement for quality certification and patent filing. Assistance is disbursed through a single-click mechanism via the department’s online portal, with funds transferred directly to eligible beneficiaries’ bank accounts after verification.

scheme_name: J&K New Industrial Development Scheme (J&K NIDS)
overview: The J&K New Industrial Development Scheme (J&K NIDS) is a state-level initiative launched by the Government of Jammu and Kashmir to promote industrial development, attract investment, and generate employment in the Union Territory. The scheme offers financial incentives and support to eligible industrial units for setting up new enterprises or expanding existing ones. It focuses on thrust sectors such as manufacturing, agro-processing, tourism-related industries, and services. The scheme aims to boost economic growth and industrialization in Jammu and Kashmir through structured fiscal and policy support.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; large industries; new industrial units; expanding units
eligibility: Eligible units include new industrial units setting up operations in Jammu and Kashmir and existing units undertaking substantial expansion. Units must be registered under the Factories Act, 1948 or as a company/LLP and engaged in manufacturing, agro-processing, mining, or services. The unit must commence commercial production within the stipulated time frame and adhere to environmental and labor norms. Preference is given to units in identified industrially backward blocks and those employing local workforce.
benefits: Financial incentives include capital investment subsidy, interest subsidy on term loans, GST reimbursement, power tariff concession, and employment generation subsidy. Additional benefits consist of stamp duty exemption, land cost subsidy, and subsidy on quality certification. The scheme also provides support for skill development, infrastructure development, and single-window clearance for faster approvals.
financial_support: Under J&K NIDS, eligible units can receive a capital investment subsidy of up to 30% of investment in plant and machinery, subject to a ceiling of INR 50 lakhs. Interest subsidy is provided at 6% per annum on term loans for a period of 5 years. GST reimbursement is available for a period of 5 years from the date of commencement of commercial production. Employment generation subsidy is offered at INR 15,000 per annum per employee for a period of 3 years for local domiciled workers. Power tariff concession is available at 50% for a period of 5 years.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 50 lakhs for capital investment subsidy
application_process: 1. Submit application online through the single-window portal of the Jammu and Kashmir Industries and Commerce Department. 2. Upload required documents including project report, incorporation certificates, land documents, and bank appraisal note. 3. Application is scrutinized by the District Industries Centre (DIC) for preliminary verification. 4. Forwarded to the Empowered Committee for evaluation and approval. 5. Upon approval, letter of intent is issued. 6. After commencement of commercial production, final disbursement of subsidies is made upon submission of proof of investment and production.
deadlines: Applications are accepted throughout the year on a rolling basis subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Jammu and Kashmir

overview: The Odisha MSME Development Policy, 2016 is a state-level initiative by the Government of Odisha to promote the growth and competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) through a comprehensive framework of enabling, supporting, and financial incentives. It aims to encourage new manufacturing capacity, provide a conducive ecosystem for MSMEs in potential sectors, maximize employment generation for youth, facilitate access to domestic and export markets, and make focused efforts for revival of sick enterprises and sustainable, inclusive growth. The policy integrates state and central government schemes, develops infrastructure like MSME parks and product-specific clusters, and offers financial support including capital investment subsidies, seed capital assistance, and trade mark assistance.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST
eligibility: Eligibility varies by incentive type. For Capital Investment Subsidy, new Micro & Small Enterprises are eligible @25% of capital investment in Plant & Machinery subject to an upper limit of Rs.1 crore; new Micro & Small Enterprises owned by SC, ST are eligible @33% subject to Rs.1.5 crore; new Micro & Small Enterprises owned by women are eligible @30% subject to Rs.1.25 crore. For Seed Capital Assistance, assistance up to Rs.10 lakh per unit is available for project report preparation and other pre-operative expenses. General eligibility requires enterprises to be registered under the MSME Act, have commenced fixed capital investment on or after the policy's effective date, and commence production within three years for MSMEs and five years for large industries from the date of starting fixed capital investment.
benefits: Benefits include Capital Investment Subsidy (up to Rs.1 crore for general enterprises, higher for SC/ST/women), Seed Capital Assistance (up to Rs.10 lakh), Project Report Subsidy (50% of cost, max Rs.25,000), Reimbursement of Audit Cost for Water Conservation (50% of cost, max Rs.10,000), Assistance for raising capital through SME Exchange (50% of listing expenses, max Rs.2 lakh), Trade Mark Assistance (50% of fees for domestic registration, max Rs.10,000; 50% for international, max Rs.50,000), Reimbursement of Training Expenditure (50% of cost, max Rs.5,000 per person), and Awards to MSME Enterprises/Entrepreneurs (cash prizes up to Rs.1 lakh). Non-financial benefits include infrastructure development via MSME parks, cluster development, credit flow facilitation, marketing assistance through MSME e-Bazaar portal, export promotion support, raw material supply through OSIC/NSIC, and technology up-gradation awareness.
financial_support: Financial support is delivered through various subsidies and assistances. Capital Investment Subsidy provides @25% of capital investment in Plant & Machinery for new Micro & Small Enterprises, subject to an upper limit of Rs.1 crore (higher limits for SC/ST/women enterprises). Seed Capital Assistance offers up to Rs.10 lakh per unit for project report preparation and pre-operative expenses. Project Report Subsidy covers 50% of cost, max Rs.25,000. Reimbursement of Audit Cost for Water Conservation provides 50% of cost, max Rs.10,000. Assistance for raising capital through SME Exchange covers 50% of listing expenses, max Rs.2 lakh. Trade Mark Assistance provides 50% of fees for domestic registration (max Rs.10,000) and international (max Rs.50,000). Reimbursement of Training Expenditure offers 50% of cost, max Rs.5,000 per person. Awards to MSME Enterprises/Entrepreneurs include cash prizes up to Rs.1 lakh. These are administered via an online mechanism for time-bound sanction and release of incentives.
application_process: 1. Enterprises must first register under the MSME Act and obtain Udyam Registration. 2. Identify the specific incentive scheme under the Odisha MSME Development Policy, 2016 (e.g., Capital Investment Subsidy, Seed Capital Assistance). 3. Prepare the required documents including project reports, quotations, bank sanction letters, and proof of investment. 4. Submit the application online through the MSME Department's designated portal or offline at the District Industries Centre (DIC) or Regional Industries Centre (RIC). 5. The application is scrutinized by the State Directorate Level Committee (SDLC) or relevant committee based on investment size. 6. Upon approval, the incentive is sanctioned and released through direct benefit transfer or reimbursement after verification of expenditure and installation.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year as per the Operational Guidelines and notifications issued from time to time.
implementing_agency: Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Department, Government of Odisha

overview: Odisha Startup Policy & iStart Odisha is a state-level initiative by the Government of Odisha to foster innovation, support startups, and build a robust entrepreneurial ecosystem through strategic partnerships, policy interventions, and financial incentives. The scheme provides recognition, funding, incubation support, and various benefits to startups operating in the state, with a focus on sectors like Agritech, IT, AI, Healthcare, Fintech, and Biotechnology. It aims to position Odisha among the top startup hubs in India by promoting innovation, skill development, and market access for startups.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST; MSME; agri-startups
eligibility: The registration by a startup entity for recognition can be done online by simply filling a Startup Registration Form and giving self-certification for the following set of documents: 1. Incorporation certificate of the entity (verified from MCA-21 portal). 2. Self-certification for Startup definition: The date of its incorporation/registration is not prior to 7 years (10 years for Biotechnology Startups). The entity’s annual turnover does not exceed Rs.25 Crore for any preceding financial year. If not registered in Odisha, the entity employs at least 50% of its total qualified workforce in Odisha. The entity is not an extension of the existing family business; or formed by splitting up or reconstruction of a business already in existence. 3. Self-Certification for Proof of innovation: DIPP Startup India recognition certificate; OR Startup has a patent filed in the entity name and published in the Journal by the India Patent Office in areas affiliated with the nature of business being promoted; OR Sanction Letter of funding/grant to the entity by Government of India or any State Government as part of any specified scheme to promote innovation; OR Letter of funding of not less than 20 percent in equity by any Incubation Fund/Angel Fund/Private Equity Fund/Accelerator/Angel Network duly registered with SEBI that endorses innovative nature of the business; OR If an entity does not possess any of the above mentioned four documents, it may submit a one page write-up/note explaining the innovative nature of its product. The applicant entity is encouraged to share its business plan along with the note on innovation.
benefits: Monthly allowance of Rs.20,000 (Rs.22,000/- if the startup Founder(s)/Co-Founder(s) are Women or transgender or from Social Categories such as SC/ST/SEBC/PH, with at least 50% equity), which may be provided for a period of one year if the startup fulfills any of the following conditions: total equity financing by SEBI registered AIF Category 1 & 2 fund or Angel Networks in the range of Rs. 5 Lakh to Rs. 1.00 Crore; or has a patent filed in the entity name and published in the Journal by the India Patent Office in areas affiliated with the nature of business being promoted; or has a sanction letter of funding/grant to the entity by Government of India or any State Government; or has a revenue run rate of Rs. 50 thousand to Rs. 10 Lakh per month over the last three months at least. Product Development and Marketing/Publicity assistance up to Rs. 15 lakh (Upto Rs.16 lakhs if the startup Founder(s)/Co-Founder(s) is Woman or transgender or from Social Categories such as SC/ST/SEBC/PH, with at least 50% equity), which may be given to a 'recognized' Startup entity for introduction of innovated product in the market if it fulfills any of the following conditions: total equity financing by SEBI registered AIF Category 1 & 2 fund or Angel Networks of at least Rs. 25 Lakh; or Sanction Letter of funding/grant to the entity by Government of India or any State Government of at least Rs. 5 Lakh; or the startup has got a revenue run rate of Rs. 2.5 Lakh per month over last six months at least. Need based assistance towards cost of raw material/components and other related equipments required for the innovative process for new product development/existing product improvement, provided only in case(s) where innovation is dependent on specific raw material/equipment and subject to approval by the Startup Council. Financial Support for event Participation: financial support to state recognized Startups for participating in reputed national and international events, where they are representing the state (support may include economy class air fare or 3 tier AC train fare for travel & free space in the stall, if set up by State Government). Subsidised Incubation: Recognised startups may avail subsidy benefit to the extent of 50% of monthly rental of the incubation space (subject to a maximum of Rs. 5000) for a period of maximum one year, if getting incubated at any of the incubators recognised by the Startup Odisha Initiative. Additional benefits to Women led Startups: Monthly allowance shall be Rs.22,000/-, if the startup Founder(s)/Co-Founder(s) are Women or transgender or from Social Categories such as SC/ST/SEBC/PH (with at least 50% equity). Up-to Rs.16 lakhs towards product development and marketing/publicity assistance, if the startup Founder(s)/Co-Founder(s) is Woman or transgender or from Social Categories such as SC/ST/SEBC/PH (with at least 50% equity). Benefits to Incubators: One-Time Capital Grant of 50% of the capital cost (excluding the cost of building) up to a maximum of Rs.1 crore, which may be given to an approved incubator to set up or scale up incubation facility. In case, a university recognised under the Central/State Act is able to raise funding for development of its incubation infrastructure, the Startup Council may consider providing a matching grant subject to an upper limit of Rs.5 crore on case-to-case basis. Such grant from the government shall only be used for development of incubation infrastructure including purchase of equipment for the incubation facility. Reimbursement of Utility Expense of Rs.1 lakh per year for a period of 3 years, which may be provided to an approved incubator for providing free internet, free electricity and free mentoring services to the incubatees. This benefit will not be available to virtual incubators. Performance capital grant of Rs.5 lakhs, which may be given to an approved incubator for its each successful Startup incubated at least for a minimum period of 3 months.
financial_support: The Fund of Funds Scheme with a target corpus of Rs 100 Crore will be disbursed over 5 years to support 5,000 Startups in the State. The scheme money is to be invested in selected funds with an agreement of minimum availability at 1:1 ratio to the state registered startups within 5 years. The scheme budget to be drawn from the treasury and shall be utilized as grants periodically. Similarly, the returns from these to be reinvested in strengthening the ecosystem. A high powered advisory committee led by developmental commissioner and principal secretaries of various departments like MSME, Finance, Skill Development etc. as members to monitor and take decisions periodically viz. Execution of the scheme, Eligibility guidelines, selection as well as exit from partner funds. Through this Scheme, Startup’s will be getting multiple collateral benefits, investment opportunities & also the employment avenue for youths shall be broadened by aiding the Enterprises.
application_process: 1. Register on startupodisha.gov.in 2. Fill Startup Registration Form with self-certification for incorporation, startup definition, and proof of innovation 3. Upload Incorporation certificate (verified from MCA-21 portal) 4. Submit and await approval by Nodal Agency within 2 weeks 5. Nodal Agency forwards to Startup Secretariat collates certified applications and presents to Task Force for consideration and final approval 6. Result published online and emailed to the concerned Startup entity 7. A startup applicant can reapply for startup recognition/financial assistance one more time after a gap of 3 months from the date of communication of rejection 8. Once recognized, apply online for monetary benefit by filling a standard form 9. Nodal Agency reviews monetary application and shares review with Startup Secretariat within next 2 weeks 10. Startup Secretariat collates applications, undertakes due diligence, presents to Task Force/Startup Council for consideration and final approval within next 2 weeks 11. Result published online and emailed to the concerned Startup entity 12. Once approved by the Task Force, Startup receives the monetary benefit(s) directly in the entity’s bank account
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: MSME Department, Government of Odisha

With annual turnover not exceeding INR 100 crore in any of the preceding financial years. 3. Incorporated as a Private Limited Company, a Registered Partnership Firm or a Limited Liability Partnership. 4. Should be working towards the innovation, development or improvement of a product, process or service and/or have a scalable business model. The entity should not have been formed by splitting up or reconstructing an already existing business.
benefits: Benefits include reimbursement for co-working spaces/incubators/accelerators (up to INR 6000 per seat for accelerators, INR 5000 for incubators, INR 3000 for co-working spaces, max 8 seats), salary reimbursement (50% of fresher salary up to INR 15,000/month per recruit, max 25 people for 3 years), lease rental subsidy (up to INR 20/- per sq ft per month for local startups in rented premises, cap INR 3 lakh/annum), internet/cloud/software reimbursement (up to INR 1 lakh/quarter for one year), seed capital grant (up to INR 10 lakh one-time), IPR reimbursement (up to 100% of costs, cap INR 2 lakh for national IP, INR 5 lakh for international IP), trademark reimbursement (50% of cost up to INR 25,000), R&D reimbursement (50% of expenses including PhD/Master salaries, cap INR 5 lakh/annum, salary cap INR 2 lakh), grant for incubation centers in educational institutes (up to INR 10 lakh capital, INR 3 lakh/year operational for 3 years), and skill development promotion scheme benefits for educational institutes.
financial_support: Financial support varies by scheme: Seed Capital Scheme offers a one-time grant of up to INR 10 lakh; Salary Reimbursement Scheme provides 50% of fresher salary capped at INR 15,000/month per recruit for up to 25 people over 3 years; Co-Working Spaces/Incubators/Accelerators Subsidy Scheme reimburses 50% of seat cost with caps of INR 3000 (co-working), INR 5000 (incubator), INR 6000 (accelerator) per seat, max 8 seats; IPR Reimbursement Scheme covers up to 100% of IP registration fees (INR 2 lakh national, INR 5 lakh international); Trademark Reimbursement Scheme reimburses 50% of trademark registration cost up to INR 25,000; R&D Reimbursement Scheme covers 50% of R&D expenses including PhD/Master salaries, capped at INR 5 lakh per annum with salary component not exceeding INR 2 lakh; Grant for Incubation Centers provides up to INR 10 lakh for capital expenses and INR 3 lakh per year for operational expenses over 3 years.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 10 lakh (Seed Capital Scheme), INR 25,000 (Trademark), INR 2 lakh (national IPR), INR 5 lakh (international IPR), INR 5 lakh per annum (R&D), INR 10 lakh capital + INR 3 lakh/year operational (Incubation Grant)
application_process: 1. Register on the Startup Goa portal (startup.goa.gov.in) to obtain a startup certificate from the Startup and IT Promotion Cell (SITPC). 2. Ensure eligibility as per the specific scheme (e.g., turnover < INR 100 crore, incorporated < 10 years, Private Limited Company/LLP/Partnership Firm). 3. Gather required documents (address proof, cancelled cheque, Aadhaar-linked bank accounts, etc., varying by scheme). 4. Apply for the specific incentive scheme via the Startup Goa portal or designated application link. 5. Submit application with documents for SPC due diligence and panel of experts review. 6. Await approval/rejection; if approved, request payment via the incentive application process. 7. Receive disbursement from the ITG (Disbursing Body) after approval.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department of Information Technology, Electronics and Communications (DITE&C), Government of Goa
contact_details: Email: spc-dit[dot]goa[at]gov[dot]in | Phone: 1800-233-5060 | Office Address: IT HUB, 2nd Floor, Altinho, Panaji - Goa, 403001

overview: The Space Technology Incubation Centre (S-TIC) – ISRO is a program initiated by the Indian Space Research Organisation to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in space technology. It aims to support startups and incubate ideas that contribute to the advancement of space applications and related technologies. The scheme provides a platform for nurturing early-stage ventures through mentorship, infrastructure, and technical guidance from ISRO experts.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Startups and entrepreneurs working on innovative ideas, technologies, or applications in the domain of space technology, including satellite technology, remote sensing, navigation, space applications, and allied fields, are eligible to apply for incubation support under S-TIC.
benefits: Selected startups receive access to ISRO's technical expertise, mentorship from scientists and engineers, infrastructure support, networking opportunities with industry and academia, and guidance on technology development, testing, and validation. The program also facilitates connections with potential investors and collaborators in the space ecosystem.
financial_support: The S-TIC program does not provide direct financial grants or funding to incubated startups. Support is primarily non-financial, focusing on technical mentorship, infrastructure access, and guidance from ISRO. Any financial support would need to be sourced externally by the startup.
application_process: 1. Interested startups must submit an application through the official ISRO S-TIC portal or designated incubation centre. 2. Applications are reviewed by a selection committee based on innovation, feasibility, and relevance to space technology. 3. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for presentations or interviews. 4. Selected startups are offered incubation support, including access to ISRO facilities and mentorship. 5. The incubation period is typically for a fixed duration, during which the startup works on developing its technology or solution under ISRO guidance.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year, subject to availability of incubation slots and review cycles.
implementing_agency: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)

scheme_name: National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS)
overview: The National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) is a mission-mode initiative under the Department of Science and Technology (DST) aimed at fostering innovation, research, and development in cyber-physical systems and related interdisciplinary domains. It seeks to strengthen India's capabilities in strategic technologies, promote technological self-reliance, and align with the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision by supporting academia, industry, startups, and research institutions in cutting-edge areas such as AI, robotics, quantum computing, and IoT. The mission encourages private sector participation and aims to build a robust ecosystem for innovation and entrepreneurship in deep tech sectors.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; research institutions; academia; industry players
eligibility: The scheme is open to industry players, startups, MSMEs, research institutions, academia, and other stakeholders engaged in research, development, and innovation in strategic technology areas such as energy security, climate action, deep technologies (quantum computing, robotics, space), AI applications in agriculture, health, education, biotechnology, biomanufacturing, synthetic biology, pharma, medical devices, and digital economy including digital agriculture. Entities must be engaged in developing RDI-intensive technology at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4 and above.
benefits: Financial support through long-term loans at low or nil interest rates, equity infusion (especially for startups), and contributions to the Deep-Tech Fund of Funds. Non-financial benefits include access to mentorship, infrastructure, collaboration networks, and support for scaling up innovations. The scheme also facilitates technology transfer, commercialization, and participation in national innovation ecosystems.
financial_support: The scheme operates with a total outlay of ₹1 lakh crore. Modes of financing include long-term loans at low or nil interest rates and equity infusion, particularly for startups. Grants and short-term loans are not supported. Financing can cover up to 50% of the assessed project cost for transformative R&D projects at Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) 4 and above, with exceptions possible upon approval by the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS). Disbursements are routed exclusively through designated Second-Level Fund Managers (SLFMs), which may include Alternate Investment Funds (AIFs), Development Finance Institutions (DFIs), NBFCs, or Focused Research Organizations (FROs) such as TDB, BIRAC, or IIT Research Parks.
application_process: 1. Interested Second Level Fund Managers (SLFMs) express interest by writing to Dr Jyoti Sharma, Head, RDI Cell at sharma[dot]jyoti[at]nic[dot]in. 2. Existing NBFCs planning to establish AIFs are encouraged to contact DST regarding potential participation. 3. Industry stakeholders seeking funding are advised not to send proposals directly to DST. 4. All disbursements will be routed exclusively through designated SLFMs via separate advertisement. 5. For more details, visit https://rdifund.anrf.gov.in/. 6. The fund flow from CFI to RDIF is based on half-yearly net requirements. 7. RDIF releases funds to SLFMs in a 'Just-In-Time' manner via the Treasury Single Account (TSA) system. 8. SLFMs prepare fund requirements based on repayment or exit proceeds and forward them to RDIF. 9. Upon receipt of demand, RDIF releases funds to the designated bank account of SLFM within a specified time frame.
implementing_agency: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology
contact_details: Email: sharma[dot]jyoti[at]nic[dot]in | Phone: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

The NASSCOM 10000 Startups Programme is a joint initiative by NASSCOM and the Government of India aimed at nurturing and scaling 10,000 technology startups across India. It provides end-to-end support including mentorship, funding access, infrastructure, and market linkages to early-stage startups. The programme focuses on fostering innovation in emerging technologies and building a sustainable startup ecosystem through incubation, acceleration, and industry connect.
target_beneficiaries: startups; technology startups; early-stage startups
eligibility: The programme is open to early-stage technology startups incorporated in India, working on innovative products or services in domains such as software, hardware, AI, IoT, fintech, healthtech, and other emerging technologies. Startups must have a scalable business model and be led by committed founders. There is no restriction on the year of incorporation, but preference is given to startups in the idea, prototype, or early revenue stage.
benefits: Selected startups receive mentorship from industry leaders, access to NASSCOM’s network of investors and corporates, incubation support, office infrastructure, technical and business workshops, pitch events, demo days, and opportunities for global market access. The programme also facilitates connections with potential customers, partners, and venture capital firms.
financial_support: While the NASSCOM 10000 Startups Programme does not directly provide grants or equity funding, it facilitates access to funding through its investor network, demo days, and pitch events. Startups are connected with angel investors, venture capital funds, and other funding sources. Financial support is indirect and based on successful investor engagement facilitated by the programme.
application_process: 1. Visit the official NASSCOM 10000 Startups website at https://10000startups.com 2. Click on the 'Apply' or 'Register' section 3. Fill out the online application form with details about the startup, founders, product/service, and traction 4. Submit the application along with required documents 5. Applications are reviewed by the NASSCOM selection committee 6. Shortlisted startups are contacted for interviews or pitch sessions 7. Final selection is based on innovation, scalability, team strength, and market potential 8. Selected startups are onboarded into the programme with access to mentorship, incubation, and investor connect opportunities.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year with periodic selection cycles.
implementing_agency: NASSCOM (National Association of Software and Service Companies)

overview: Startup India Innovation Week Challenge is a program under the Startup India initiative that invites startups to participate in innovation challenges and competitions to showcase their solutions, gain recognition, and access support such as mentorship, networking, and potential funding opportunities. It aims to foster innovation across sectors by connecting startups with industry experts, investors, and government bodies. The challenge is part of broader efforts to strengthen the startup ecosystem through structured programs and events.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups must be DPIIT recognised to participate in the Innovation Week Challenge. Eligibility for DPIIT recognition includes being incorporated as a Private Limited Company, LLP, or partnership firm, being within 10 years of incorporation (20 years for DeepTech), having turnover not exceeding INR 200 crore (INR 300 crore for DeepTech), and working towards innovation, development, or improvement of products/services with potential for wealth and employment generation.
benefits: Participants gain access to mentorship, networking opportunities with investors and industry leaders, potential cash prizes, handholding support, visibility through national platforms, and eligibility for further government schemes such as Seed Fund Scheme, Fund of Funds, and Credit Guarantee Scheme. Winners may also receive support for scaling and market access.
financial_support: Financial support varies by challenge and may include cash prizes (e.g., up to ₹10 lakhs in some programs like National Startup Awards), seed funding through linked schemes such as SISFS (up to ₹20 lakhs), or investment facilitation via Startup India Investor Connect. The Innovation Week Challenge itself may not provide direct grants but links startups to funding avenues.
application_process: 1. Register on the Startup India portal (startupindia.gov.in) 2. Obtain DPIIT recognition via the 'Get Recognised' section 3. Navigate to the Innovation Week Challenge or specific program page 4. Fill out the application form with startup details and innovation description 5. Upload required documents such as incorporation certificate, PAN, and pitch deck 6. Submit the application and await evaluation 7. If selected, participate in the challenge events and receive benefits
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round for various challenges under Startup India Programs.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: The IIT Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) at IIT Bombay provide incubation support to technology-based startups, offering infrastructure, mentorship, and networking opportunities to foster innovation and entrepreneurship. The program aims to convert research and ideas into viable entrepreneurial ventures through structured support systems.
target_beneficiaries: startups; technology-based entrepreneurs
eligibility: Technology-based startups and entrepreneurs seeking incubation support at IIT Bombay's Technology Business Incubator (TBI) are eligible to apply. Specific criteria may include innovation quotient, scalability, and alignment with IIT Bombay's focus areas.
benefits: Incubatees receive access to IIT Bombay's research infrastructure, mentorship from faculty and industry experts, networking opportunities, legal and IP support, seed funding assistance, and access to investor networks. The TBI also provides office space, laboratory facilities, and administrative support.
financial_support: The TBI facilitates access to seed funding, grants, and investment opportunities through its network of investors, venture capitalists, and government schemes. Specific financial support mechanisms include assistance in applying for government grants, angel investments, and venture capital funding, though direct quantum is not specified in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Visit the IIT Bombay TBI website or portal. 2. Review eligibility and program details. 3. Submit an online application with business plan, team details, and innovation description. 4. Undergo screening and evaluation by the TBI selection committee. 5. Attend interview or pitch session if shortlisted. 6. Receive incubation offer and complete onboarding formalities.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay

overview: NIT Innovation & Entrepreneurship Development Centre is a facility at NITK Surathkal aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship among students and faculty. It supports startup activities through mentoring, infrastructure, and industry linkages. The centre is part of NITK's broader efforts to promote research, innovation, and technology transfer.
target_beneficiaries: students; faculty; alumni; startups
eligibility: Open to students, faculty, and alumni of NITK Surathkal who are engaged in innovative projects or startup ideas. Specific eligibility may vary based on the program or grant being applied for under the centre's activities.
benefits: Access to incubation infrastructure, mentorship from faculty and industry experts, networking opportunities, support for patent filing and technology transfer, assistance in applying for government grants and funding schemes, and participation in entrepreneurship development programs.
financial_support: The centre facilitates access to various funding sources such as DST NIDHI Prayas Grant, CSR grants, and sponsored research projects. Financial support varies by program and is not standardized; examples include grants like Rs. 9.3 lakh under DST NIDHI Prayas for startups like Oxyheal Pvt. Ltd.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant program or grant under NIT Innovation & Entrepreneurship Development Centre. 2. Check eligibility criteria for the specific opportunity. 3. Prepare required documents such as project proposal, team details, and proof of concept. 4. Submit application through the designated portal or contact the centre directly. 5. Await review and potential interview or presentation. 6. Upon approval, receive mentorship, infrastructure, and/or financial support as per the scheme.
deadlines: Varies by program; some are rolling basis, others have specific dates as announced
implementing_agency: National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK), Surathkal

overview: Atal Bhujal Yojana (ABY) is a central sector scheme launched by the Government of India to improve groundwater management in water-stressed areas through community participation and sustainable practices. The scheme focuses on demand-side management, aquifer recharge, and strengthening institutional frameworks for groundwater governance. It aims to arrest the rate of decline of groundwater levels and improve water conservation practices in identified over-exploited and water-stressed areas.
target_beneficiaries: gram panchayats; water user associations; local communities; farmers
geographic_scope: Seven states: Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh
eligibility: The scheme is implemented in identified water-stressed areas of seven states: Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. Benefits are extended to gram panchayats, water user associations, and local communities in these areas who participate in groundwater management activities through community-led water security plans.
benefits: Financial and technical support for preparation and implementation of community-led Water Security Plans (WSPs), capacity building and training for stakeholders, support for IEC (Information, Education, and Communication) activities, technical assistance for groundwater monitoring and data management, and convergence with other schemes for integrated water resource management.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance as grants to implementing agencies for activities under the Water Security Plans. The funding pattern is 50% from the World Bank loan and 50% from central government assistance, with funds released based on achievement of disbursement-linked indicators (DLIs).
application_process: 1. Identification of water-stressed areas by the central and state governments. 2. Formation of Water User Associations (WUAs) and Gram Panchayat-level committees. 3. Preparation of Community-led Water Security Plans (WSPs) through participatory processes. 4. Submission of WSPs to the WSPs for approval by the State Level Scheme Sanctioning Committee (SLSSC). 5. Implementation of approved WSPs with financial and technical support from the scheme. 6. Monitoring and evaluation based on Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs).
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are invited periodically based on annual action plans
implementing_agency: Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti

scheme_name: Centre for Nano Science and Engineering (CeNSE) Grants
overview: The Centre for Nano Science and Engineering (CeNSE) at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) was established in 2010 to pursue interdisciplinary research in nanoscale systems, including nanoelectronics, MEMS/NEMS, microfluidics, nanomaterials, photonics, nano-biotechnology, solar cells, quantum and neuromorphic computing, sensors, and optoelectronics. It offers M.Tech and PhD programs, hosts state-of-the-art nanofabrication and characterization facilities, and runs the in-house technology business incubator INCeNSE, which currently incubates 6 start-ups with access to infrastructure, labs, and mentoring support. CeNSE maintains close industry interactions and supports national initiatives like the India Semiconductor Mission through specialized training programs and industry collaborations.
target_beneficiaries: startups; students; researchers; industry partners
