eligibility: For M.Tech in Semiconductor Technology: BE/BTech or equivalent in any discipline with GATE paper in EC, EE, ME, IN, XE-C, MT OR MSc or equivalent in Electronics or Physics with GATE paper in PH, IN, EC. For PhD: ME/MTech or equivalent in any discipline OR BE/BTech in Engineering with valid GATE score OR MSc in Science with valid GATE score OR qualification in national exams like INSPIRE, CSIR UGC NET for JRF, DBT JRF, UGC NET for JRF, or JEST. Selection is based on 100% GATE/CAM score for regular programs and interview performance post-shortlisting.
benefits: Access to 14,000 sq. ft. state-of-the-art nanofabrication and clean room facility (NNFC), comprehensive micro nano characterization facility (MNCF), Systems and Packaging Facility (S&PF), and in-house technology business incubator INCeNSE which incubates 6 start-ups with infrastructure, labs, and mentoring support. Students benefit from industrial interactions, cutting-edge R&D facilities, industry fellowships, internships, and placements. Faculty and researchers gain access to advanced equipment, collaborative projects, and national facility networks. Industry partners receive facility usage, consultancy, research projects, training, talent access, networking, and distinguished lectures via the Industry Affiliate Program.
financial_support: The MTech Fellowship Program for 2nd Year MTech students provides an enhanced fellowship of INR 24,800 per month for 12 months, support for attending conferences, and engagement with sponsors including opportunities for internships, placement, and career guidance. Eligibility is restricted to all 2nd Year MTech students of CeNSE. Applications are sent via email in July and selection completed before the first week of August by a CeNSE faculty committee with inputs from industry sponsors.
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 24,800 per month for 12 months (under MTech Fellowship Program)
application_process: 1. Visit the CeNSE website and navigate to the 'For Students' or 'How to apply' section. 2. Check eligibility for the desired program (M.Tech, PhD, M.Engg, Joint M.Tech, or Fellowship). 3. For M.Tech/PhD: Apply through the IISc admissions website during the July session (limited January session for PhD). 4. Candidates are shortlisted based on national exam scores (GATE/CAM) or qualification. 5. Shortlisted candidates must appear for an interview at CeNSE. 6. Final selection is based on interview performance and exam results, announced 2-3 weeks post-interview. 7. For Fellowships: Wait for the annual call (typically July), submit application via email, and undergo review by CeNSE faculty committee with industry sponsor inputs. 8. Selected candidates receive formal admission or fellowship offer.
deadlines: Admissions to M.Tech and PhD programs are typically offered for the July session, with a limited number of topic/field-specific admissions possible in the January session for PhD. The MTech Fellowship Program call is sent via email in July, with selection completed before the first week of August.
implementing_agency: Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore
contact_details: Email: iap.cense@iisc.ac.in (for Industry Affiliate Program), industry.cense@iisc.ac.in (for industry engagements), summerinterncense@gmail.com (for internship queries), workshop.cense@iisc.ac.in (for workshop queries)

scheme_name: IIM Ahmedabad CIIE.CO – Bharat Inclusion Initiative
overview: The Bharat Inclusion Initiative by IIM Ahmedabad CIIE.CO is a program aimed at supporting startups that serve underserved and low-income populations in India. It focuses on fostering innovation in sectors such as financial inclusion, agriculture, health, and livelihoods. The initiative provides incubation support, mentorship, and access to networks to help early-stage ventures scale their impact. It is part of CIIE.CO’s broader mission to promote inclusive entrepreneurship.
target_beneficiaries: startups; social enterprises; early-stage ventures
eligibility: Startups or early-stage ventures working on innovative products, services, or business models that address the needs of underserved and low-income populations in India, particularly in the areas of financial inclusion, agriculture, health, and livelihoods.
benefits: Incubation support, mentorship from industry experts and IIM Ahmedabad faculty, access to CIIE.CO’s investor and partner network, guidance on product-market fit and scaling, and opportunities for follow-on funding and pilot collaborations.
financial_support: The initiative does not provide direct grants or seed funding; instead, it focuses on non-financial support such as incubation, mentorship, and network access to help startups become investment-ready.
application_process: 1. Visit the CIIE.CO Bharat Inclusion Initiative webpage. 2. Review the eligibility criteria and program details. 3. Submit an online application through the designated portal. 4. Await screening and shortlisting by the selection committee. 5. Participate in interviews or pitch sessions if shortlisted. 6. Receive final selection decision and onboarding instructions.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: CIIE.CO (formerly known as Centre for Innovation Incubation and Entrepreneurship), IIM Ahmedabad

scheme_name: Light House Projects (LHP) for Affordable Housing
overview: Light House Projects (LHP) for Affordable Housing is a technology-driven initiative under the Global Housing Technology Challenge-India (GHTC-India) to construct six model housing projects across India using innovative, sustainable, and disaster-resilient technologies. The projects aim to demonstrate and deliver affordable, ready-to-live-in housing at scale, with each LHPs comprising approximately 1,000 houses. The initiative seeks to accelerate the adoption of cutting-edge construction technologies in the Indian affordable housing sector.
target_beneficiaries: economically weaker sections; low-income groups; urban poor
eligibility: The Light House Projects are implemented as model projects by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) through its implementing agencies. The end beneficiaries are individuals from Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Low Income Groups (LIG) as defined under PMAY-U, selected through the respective state/union territory level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committees (SMCs).
benefits: Beneficiaries receive affordable, ready-to-live-in housing units constructed using innovative, sustainable, and disaster-resilient technologies. The LHPs provide improved quality of life through better construction standards, energy efficiency, and resilience to natural hazards. The projects also serve as demonstration sites for mainstreaming new technologies in mass housing.
financial_support: The LHPs are funded under the Technology Sub-Mission of PMAY-U, with financial support coming from central assistance under PMAY-U and contributions from state governments. The per-unit cost varies by location and technology, but the central government provides fixed financial assistance per EWS/LIG house as per PMAY-U norms, supplemented by state and beneficiary shares.
application_process: Beneficiaries are identified and selected by the respective State/Union Territory Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committees (SMCs) under PMAY-U. There is no direct application portal for individual beneficiaries to apply for LHPs. Allotment is done through state-level procedures based on PMAY-U beneficiary criteria.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Gramin Phase II
overview: Swachh Bharat Mission – Gramin Phase II (SBM-G Phase II) is a flagship Government of India initiative launched post-2019 to sustain Open Defecation Free (ODF) status and achieve 'Sampoorn Swachhata' through comprehensive solid and liquid waste management in rural India. Building on Phase I’s success of constructing over 100 million individual household toilets and declaring 6 lakh villages ODF, Phase II focuses on waste-to-wealth initiatives, behavioral change, and infrastructure for long-term sanitation sustainability. The mission integrates multiple ministries, promotes innovative campaigns like Swachhata Green Leaf Rating and GOBARdhan, and aims to transform rural sanitation into a holistic, sustainable public health model.
target_beneficiaries: rural households; gram panchayats; villages; self-help groups; ngos; csr entities
eligibility: Rural households, Gram Panchayats, villages, self-help groups, NGOs, and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) entities including Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) are eligible to participate in or implement SBM-G Phase II activities such as construction of individual household latrines, community sanitary complexes, solid and liquid waste management systems, and GOBARdhan projects, subject to guidelines issued by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under Ministry of Jal Shakti.
benefits: Financial and non-financial benefits include sustained ODF status, improved health outcomes (reduction in diarrheal deaths), economic savings (INR 50,000 annually per household on health costs), environmental benefits (reduced groundwater contamination), enhanced safety and dignity for women (93% reported feeling safer), employment generation through waste management and GOBARdhan initiatives, production of organic manure and biogas, access to clean energy via Compressed Biogas (CBG), and recognition under Swachhata Green Leaf Rating system for hospitality and tourism units.
financial_support: The mission's current phase is supported by an investment of Rs.1.40 lakh crores, which integrates various governmental schemes to enhance sanitation infrastructure further. Financial assistance is provided for projects such as GOBARdhan, with up to Rs. 50 Lakh per district available for setting up model projects at community and cluster levels under SBM(G) Phase-II until 2024–25. Funds are channeled through central and state government mechanisms, including convergence with other ministries and utilization of CSR funds from CPSEs and corporate houses as per guidelines.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 50 Lakh per district for GOBARdhan model projects
application_process: 1. Identify eligible sanitation project (e.g., IHHL, CSC, SWM, LWM, GOBARdhan) as per SBM-G Phase II guidelines. 2. Gram Panchayat or implementing agency submits proposal through the Swachh Bharat Mission Gramin portal or to the District Water and Sanitation Committee. 3. Project is appraised by the Block/ District level officials for technical and financial feasibility. 4. Upon approval, funds are released in installments linked to physical progress. 5. Implementation is carried out by Gram Panchayat, SHG, NGO, or CSR partner. 6. Operation and maintenance plan is established, often with CPSEs/NGOs for 10 years. 7. Project is monitored via Swachh Survekshan Grameen and reported through MIS. 8. Upon completion, village is assessed for ODF Plus status (Aspiring, Rising, Model).
deadlines: Available until 2024–25 for GOBARdhan financial assistance; overall Phase II implementation ongoing until 2025
implementing_agency: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India
contact_details: Email: Not explicitly stated in evidence | Helpline: Not explicitly stated in evidence

scheme_name: Film Facilitation Office (FFO) – Single Window Clearance
overview: The Film Facilitation Office (FFO) – Single Window Clearance is a government initiative under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting that provides a single point of contact for filmmakers seeking permissions and clearances for shooting films in India. It streamlines the process of obtaining various no-objection certificates (NOCs) and approvals from central and state government agencies, thereby reducing delays and administrative burden for film production activities across the country.
target_beneficiaries: filmmakers; production houses; media and entertainment professionals
eligibility: Filmmakers, production houses, or any entity intending to shoot films in India that require permissions from central or state government authorities for locations, drone usage, road closures, or other regulatory clearances.
benefits: Single point of contact for all film shooting-related permissions; coordination with ministries and departments such as Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Civil Aviation, Archaeological Survey of India, and state governments; time-bound processing of applications; reduced procedural complexity; support for both Indian and foreign film productions.
financial_support: The Film Facilitation Office does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Its primary function is facilitative — offering clearance and coordination services without monetary disbursement to beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Visit the FFO portal at https://ffo.gov.in 2. Register as a user on the portal 3. Fill out the online application form for the required clearances 4. Upload necessary documents such as script, production details, location information, and identification proofs 5. Submit the application 6. FFO forwards the application to relevant concerned agencies 7. Track application status through the portal 8. Receive NOCs/clearances from respective agencies via FFO coordination.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year as per project requirements.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India

overview: SIDBI Startup Mitra – Incubation Portal is a platform under the Startup India initiative designed to support startups by providing access to incubation services, mentorship, and resources. It aims to nurture early-stage startups through structured incubation programs, connecting them with incubators, accelerators, and industry experts. The portal facilitates application to various incubation schemes and offers guidance on accessing government and private funding, regulatory support, and market linkages.
target_beneficiaries: startups; early-stage startups; technology-enabled startups
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startups with technology-enabled business ideas are eligible to apply for incubation support through the SIDBI Startup Mitra portal. Startups must be incorporated as a Private Limited Company, Registered Partnership Firm, Limited Liability Partnership, or Cooperative Society. The entity should be working towards innovation, development, or improvement of products, processes, or services, and have a scalable business model with high potential for wealth and employment generation. The startup should not have been formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business.
benefits: Access to incubation and acceleration programs, mentorship from industry experts, networking opportunities with investors and corporates, guidance on applying for government schemes such as Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS), Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS), and Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS), support for intellectual property protection, and assistance in market access and regulatory compliance.
financial_support: The SIDBI Startup Mitra portal does not directly provide financial support but facilitates access to financial schemes such as the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS), which offers grants up to INR 20 lakh, and the Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS), which contributes to SEBI-registered AIFs that invest in startups. It also connects startups to the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) for collateral-free debt funding.
application_process: 1. Visit the Startup India portal at https://www.startupindia.gov.in/ 2. Navigate to the Startup Mitra – Incubation Portal section 3. Register or log in to your Startup India profile 4. Complete the application form with details about your startup, including innovation, business model, and team 5. Upload required documents such as Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, and pitch deck 6. Submit the application for review 7. Await confirmation and further instructions from the incubation partner
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

overview: Swachh Bharat Mission – Urban 2.0 (SBM-U 2.0) is a flagship initiative of the Government of India launched on 1st October 2021 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) with the vision of achieving 'Garbage Free' status for all cities by 2026. The mission focuses on 100% scientific solid waste management, sustained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, and behavioral change through Jan Andolan. It aims to institutionalize 'swachh' behavior, contribute to SDG 2030, and drive urban transformation through infrastructure development, capacity building, digital innovations, and citizen engagement.
target_beneficiaries: urban local bodies; states; union territories; citizens
eligibility: SBM-U 2.0 is implemented by MoHUA through States/UTs in all statutory towns (as per Census 2011, and statutory towns added subsequent to that). The Government of India in partnership with States/UTs and ULBs is committed to make all cities 'Garbage Free' under SBM-Urban 2.0. ULBs must maintain complete and accurate data on the Swachhatam Portal, update contact details of representatives, and regularly submit monthly MIS. ULBs formed on or before 31st Dec’24 will be assessed in SS 2025-26; those formed after may be included on formal request to MoHUA from the respective State/UT.
benefits: Benefits include improved sanitation infrastructure, increased waste processing capacity, remediation of legacy dumpsites, enhanced access to sanitation facilities, behavioral change through citizen engagement, digital tools like Swachhata App and e-learning portal, recognition via Swachh Survekshan rankings and Garbage Free City Star ratings, ODF+/ODF++/Water+ certifications, and contribution to SDG 2030. Financial support is provided via central grants, State/UT shares, and beneficiary contributions, enabling ULBs to set up waste processing facilities, mechanized sweeping, and bioremediation projects.
financial_support: The outlay of SBM-U 1.0 was ₹62,009 crores, including GoI share of ₹14,623 crores and minimum State share of ₹4,874 crores, with balance funds generated through individual beneficiary contribution, PPP, and other sources. For SBM-U 2.0, funding follows a similar pattern: central grants, State/UT shares, and ULB contributions. Financial support is channeled through Capacity Building (CB) Funds allocated to States/UTs, which mentor and mentee cities under Swachh Shehar Jodi may utilize. States/UTs are encouraged to top up these funds. Additional funding mechanisms include viability gap funding, processing fees, and tariffs under PPP models for waste-to-energy, composting, and MRF projects, as detailed in model RFPs and concession agreements.
application_process: 1. ULBs must maintain complete and accurate data on the Swachhatam Portal. 2. ULBs must update contact details of their representatives on the Swachhatam Portal. 3. ULBs must regularly submit monthly Management Information System (MIS) data. 4. For star rating certification, ULBs fill Common City Profile on SBM Urban Portal. 5. Fill MIS on SBM Urban Portal. 6. Check self-assessment scores on SBM Urban Portal. 7. Apply for Star Rating as per eligibility on SBM Urban Portal. 8. Upload documents & declarations. 9. Undergo Third Party Verification through Desktop Assessment and Field Assessment. 10. Receive Final Star Rating Certification (Valid for 1 Year). 11. For Swachh Shehar Jodi, mentor and mentee cities finalize pairs by 5th September 2025, conduct As-Is Joint Assessment & Action Plan by end of September 2025, sign MOUs by October 2025, implement Action Plan for 100 days, and assess progress during Swachh Survekshan 2025-26.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications for star rating and project proposals are accepted year-round. Specific timelines exist for initiatives like Swachh Shehar Jodi (announcement 17th July 2025, city pair finalization by 5th September 2025, action plan by end September 2025, MOU signing October 2025, 100-day implementation, assessment during Swachh Survekshan 2025-26).
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

overview: The NFDC Production Grants scheme is part of the Development, Communication and Dissemination of Filmic Content (DCDFC) scheme by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, under which NFDC produces and co-produces feature films, children's films, and documentary films in various Indian languages. It encourages debutant filmmakers by undertaking 100% production of their first feature film, children's film, and documentary film, and supports co-production of good quality films in partnership with filmmakers from India and abroad. The scheme aims to foster excellence in cinema, promote cultural diversity, and preserve India's cinematic heritage.
target_beneficiaries: debutant filmmakers; filmmakers; content creators
eligibility: Under the DCDFC scheme, NFDC produces & co-produces films, children's films and documentaries under its extant guidelines for production, whereby it encourages debutant filmmakers by undertaking 100% production of their first Feature Film, Children’s Film and Documentary Film and Co-production of good quality films in partnership with filmmakers both from India and abroad.
benefits: 100% production support for debut feature films, children's films, and documentary films; co-production opportunities with Indian and international filmmakers; access to NFDC's production guidelines and expertise; participation in Film Bazaar and other NFDC initiatives for global exposure; preservation and promotion of India's cinematic heritage.
financial_support: NFDC provides 100% financial support for the production of debut feature films, children's films, and documentary films under the DCDFC scheme, and co-produces good quality films in partnership with filmmakers from India and abroad, with funding sourced from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting's Development, Communication and Dissemination of Filmic Content scheme.
grant_amount_per_entity: 100% production cost for debut feature films, children's films, and documentary films
application_process: 1. Apply through government-supported film festivals such as IFFI (Goa), Mumbai International Film Festival, Film Bazaar, etc. 2. Submit feature, documentary, animation projects, etc. for consideration. 3. NFDC evaluates submissions under the DCDFC scheme. 4. Selected projects receive 100% production support or co-production opportunities. 5. Follow NFDC's extant production guidelines for execution.
implementing_agency: National Film Development Corporation Limited (NFDC)

overview: The AVGC-XR Policy (Animation, VFX, Gaming, Comics) is a government initiative by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at promoting growth and innovation in the media and entertainment sector, specifically focusing on animation, visual effects, gaming, comics, and extended reality (XR) technologies. The policy seeks to strengthen India's position as a global hub for AVGC content creation by providing support through infrastructure, skill development, and industry collaboration.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; entrepreneurs; creative professionals; educational institutions
eligibility: The policy applies to Indian entities including startups, MSMEs, educational institutions, and creative industry professionals engaged in animation, VFX, gaming, comics, and extended reality (XR) activities. Specific eligibility criteria for individual components of the policy (such as grants, incubation, or infrastructure support) are defined in respective guidelines and notifications issued by MeitY or its authorized agencies.
benefits: Benefits under the AVGC-XR Policy include financial support for project development, access to shared infrastructure and technology facilities, skill development programs, mentorship and incubation support, assistance with market access and international collaboration, regulatory facilitation, and support for intellectual property rights management. The policy also promotes participation in global festivals, co-production opportunities, and access to funding mechanisms through government-backed funds.
financial_support: Financial support under the AVGC-XR Policy is delivered through various mechanisms including grants, seed funding, venture capital linkages, and subsidies for infrastructure and technology adoption. Specific quantum and disbursement details are outlined in individual scheme documents and guidelines issued by MeitY or its implementing agencies such as the Digital Entertainment and Gaming Hub (DEGH) or approved centres of excellence.
application_process: The application process varies depending on the specific component of the AVGC-XR Policy being accessed (e.g., grants, incubation, infrastructure support). Interested applicants are advised to refer to the official MeitY website or designated portals for scheme-specific guidelines, where detailed calls for proposals, eligibility criteria, and submission procedures are published. Applications are typically submitted online through designated government portals after registration and document upload.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India

overview: The National Centre for Textile Design (NCTD) is an autonomous body under the Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India. It functions as a premier institute for design development, training, and research in the textile and handicrafts sector. NCTD aims to enhance the competitiveness of Indian textiles through innovative design interventions, skill upgradation, and market linkage support. It serves designers, weavers, artisans, exporters, and textile industries by providing design services, forecasting trends, and promoting traditional and contemporary textile arts.
target_beneficiaries: designers; weavers; artisans; exporters; textile industries; handloom clusters; handicraft units
eligibility: Eligibility varies by programme; generally open to individual designers, weavers, artisans, self-help groups, cooperatives, NGOs, exporters, and textile/handicraft units seeking design support, training, or market linkage services from NCTD.
benefits: Access to professional design services, trend forecasting, prototype development, training in design software and traditional techniques, product development support, market linkage assistance, participation in design exhibitions and buyer-seller meets, and documentation of traditional designs.
financial_support: NCTD provides design and technical support services; financial support such as grants or subsidies is not directly provided by NCTD but may be facilitated through linkage with Ministry of Textiles schemes like NHDP, HSS, or CDP. Specific financial quantum or mechanism is not detailed in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Visit the NCTD website at https://nctd.gov.in 2. Explore available programmes such as design development, training, or trend services 3. Contact NCTD via email or phone to express interest 4. Submit required documents based on the specific programme 5. Await evaluation and approval from NCTD officials 6. Upon acceptance, avail the selected service or enrol in the training programme.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year depending on programme availability.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner for Handlooms, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

scheme_name: Design & Technical Upgradation Scheme for Handicrafts

overview: STPI Centres of Entrepreneurship (CoEs) are domain-specific specialized incubation facilities established by Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to support startups in emerging technologies. These CoEs provide infrastructure, mentoring, funding opportunities, networking, and technical support to nurture innovative startups in areas such as IoT, AI, FinTech, AR/VR, ESDM, and others. The initiative aligns with the Start-up India vision to build a vibrant startup ecosystem and position India as a 'Product Nation'.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Startups operating in emerging technology domains such as Internet of things (IoT), Block Chain, FinTech, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Augmented & Virtual Reality (AR/VR), ESDM, Data Science & Analytics, Medical Electronics & Healthcare, Gaming & Animation, Machine Learning, Cyber Security etc., are eligible for support at STPI Centres of Entrepreneurship (CoEs). Selection is based on pre-defined criteria including innovativeness, team strength, and business proposal soundness.
benefits: STPI CoEs provide Infrastructure (Hardware & Software labs), Knowledge & handholding, Funding & Investment opportunities, Mentoring & Networking to nurture innovative start-ups in emerging technologies. Additional benefits include access to domain-specific labs, mentoring from academia and industry, market connect with angel investors/VCs, and collaborative ecosystem support involving Government, Industry, Academia, and Investors.
financial_support: STPI CoEs facilitate funding and investment opportunities for startups through connections with angel investors, venture capitalists, and investment funding agencies. Specific financial support mechanisms such as seed funds or grants are managed under linked schemes like the Next Generation Incubation Scheme (NGIS), which provides seed funding of up to Rs. 25 Lakhs per startup.
application_process: 1. Submit proposals for incubation at STPI Centres of Entrepreneurship (CoEs). 2. Proposals are accepted based on pre-defined criteria. 3. Selected startups receive mentorship from eminent personalities from Academia and Industry. 4. Undergo evaluation of Proof of Concept (POC), product development, and market connect. 5. Interact with angel investors/VCs for funding opportunities. 6. Benefit from collaborative ecosystem involving Government, Industry, Academia, and Investors.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: The Marketing Support & Services for Handicrafts scheme aims to promote and market handicraft products through various initiatives such as participation in domestic and international exhibitions, organizing craft bazaars, and providing marketing assistance to artisans and handicraft exporters. It focuses on enhancing market access, brand building, and export promotion for the handicraft sector. The scheme supports individual artisans, self-help groups, NGOs, cooperatives, and private enterprises engaged in handicraft production.
target_beneficiaries: artisans; self-help groups; NGOs; cooperatives; private enterprises; handicraft exporters
eligibility: Individual artisans, self-help groups, NGOs, cooperatives, and private enterprises engaged in the production of handicrafts are eligible to apply for benefits under the Marketing Support & Services for Handicrafts scheme. Applicants must be involved in handicraft activities and possess valid registration or recognition as handicraft producers where applicable.
benefits: Financial assistance for participation in domestic and international exhibitions, craft bazaars, and trade fairs; reimbursement of stall rent, travel expenses, and publicity costs; support for market development activities; assistance in branding and product promotion; facilitation of buyer-seller meets; and support for e-commerce initiatives and digital marketing of handicraft products.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support in the form of subsidies for participation in exhibitions and fairs, including reimbursement of stall rent, travel expenses, and publicity costs up to certain limits. Assistance is also provided for organizing craft bazaars and marketing events, with funding shared between the implementing agency and the beneficiary. The exact quantum of support varies based on the nature of the event, location, and category of participant.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant marketing event or exhibition under the scheme. 2. Contact the designated implementing agency or regional office for application details. 3. Submit the application form along with required documents. 4. Await scrutiny and approval from the sanctioning committee. 5. Upon approval, participate in the event and submit expenditure claims. 6. Receive reimbursement of eligible expenses as per scheme norms.
deadlines: Based on event-specific schedules; applications are typically invited well in advance of exhibitions, craft bazaars, and trade fairs.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

overview: Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH) was established under Companies Act in the year 1986-87 and is a non-profit organisation, with an object to promote, support, protect, maintain and increase the export of handicrafts. It is an apex body of handicrafts exporters for promotion of exports of Handicrafts from country and projecting India's image abroad as a reliable supplier of high quality of handicrafts goods & services and ensured various measures keeping in view of observance of international standards and specification. The Council has created necessary infrastructure as well as marketing and information facilities, which are availed both by the members exporters and importers.
target_beneficiaries: handicrafts exporters; artisans; MSME
eligibility: Any person willing to venture into exports of handicrafts can become the member of the Council. Membership is a pre-condition for registration. Registration can be obtained as a 'Merchant Exporter' or 'Manufacturer Exporter' or Merchant-cum-Manufacturer Exporter as per documents submitted. A self certified copy of Import Export Code (IEC) is mandatory and needs to be enclosed with the application form. If the Company is a partnership firm it has to submit a Partnership Deed along with the Application Form. If the company is a private limited or a limited firm a photocopy of certificate of incorporation (Memorandum of Article of Association) and resolution deed regarding the signing authority has to be submitted. If an Export House applies for member ship it must furnish a copy of Export House Certificate. If a company is a manufacturer exporter must furnish MSME UAM or Udhyam & self declaration certifying what type of Handicrafts product manufacturing. A copy of GSTIN number is required.
benefits: Membership provides access to EPCH's infrastructure, marketing and information facilities. Members can participate in international trade fairs organised by EPCH in India and abroad. EPCH organizes seminars and workshops on training and presenting emerging trends to empower the handicraft community. EPCH provides support to the handicraft community and plays an active role in advancing the sector. EPCH's initiatives include the International Lace Trade Centre, Moradabad Resource Centre, Handicrafts Productivity Centre at Jaipur, Technology Upgradation Centre at Saharanpur, National Centre for Photo & Picture Framing Technology at Saharanpur and Jodhpur, Establishment of International Lace Trade Centre at Narasapur, and Aggressive International Marketing Project for the Development and Promotion of North Eastern Crafts.
financial_support: EPCH is a self-sustaining organisation where all promotional activities are self-financed. Membership fees are the primary source of revenue: Entrance fee in the year of enrolment - Rs. 2500/-, Annual Membership Fee - Rs. 5000/-, Total (during the year of Enrollment) - Rs 7500/- + GST 18% (Rs. 8850/-). Membership renewal fee is Rs. 5900/- (Rs 5000/- + GST 18%). Every year Membership Fee is due on 1st April and payment is to be made by 30th June.
application_process: 1. Apply for New Membership via EPCH website. 2. Pay entrance fee of Rs. 2500/- and annual membership fee of Rs. 5000/- (total Rs. 7500/- + 18% GST = Rs. 8850/-) during the year of enrollment. 3. Submit self certified copy of Import Export Code (IEC). 4. If partnership firm, submit Partnership Deed. 5. If private/limited company, submit photocopy of certificate of incorporation and resolution deed regarding signing authority. 6. If Export House, submit Export House Certificate. 7. If manufacturer exporter, furnish MSME UAM or Udhyam & self declaration certifying type of Handicrafts product manufacturing. 8. Submit copy of GSTIN number. 9. Avoid similar or duplicate names by checking EPCH website member directory. 10. Membership renewal fee of Rs. 5900/- (Rs 5000/- + GST 18%) is due every year by 30th June.
deadlines: Every year Membership Fee is due on 1st April and payment is to be made by 30th June.
implementing_agency: Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH)

overview: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Telecom & Networking Products aims to boost domestic manufacturing, increase exports, and reduce import dependency in the telecom sector. Launched by the Government of India, it provides financial incentives to eligible companies to encourage investment and innovation in telecom products and networking equipment.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; large enterprises
eligibility: Eligible companies must be engaged in manufacturing of telecom and networking products in India, meet minimum investment thresholds, and achieve incremental sales of covered products over a base year. Specific eligibility criteria include compliance with Make in India guidelines and meeting domestic value addition requirements.
benefits: Financial incentives based on incremental sales of covered products over a base year, tax benefits under relevant schemes, support for technology upgradation, and facilitation of access to global markets through enhanced manufacturing competitiveness.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial incentives as a percentage of incremental sales of eligible telecom and networking products manufactured in India, disbursed annually based on verified claims submitted by beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Register on the designated PLI portal 2. Submit application with details of manufacturing capacity and investment plan 3. Provide proof of compliance with eligibility criteria 4. Await evaluation and approval by the empowered committee 5. Sign agreement upon approval 6. Commence production and submit periodic reports 7. Claim incentives based on verified incremental sales
deadlines: Application window typically opens annually with specific deadlines notified via official communications; exact dates vary by year.
implementing_agency: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications

overview: The Digital Communications Innovation Square (DCIS) is a scheme under the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, aimed at fostering innovation and development in the telecom sector. It serves as a platform for startups, MSMEs, and innovators to test, validate, and scale their digital communication solutions. The initiative supports the broader goals of Atmanirbhar Bharat and India's 6G ambitions by promoting indigenous telecom technologies and reducing import dependency.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; innovators
eligibility: Startups, MSMEs, innovators, and entities engaged in telecom innovation, standardisation, or development of digital communication solutions are eligible to participate in DCIS. Preference may be given to entities working on 5G/6G technologies, indigenous solutions, and those aligned with national telecom priorities.
benefits: Access to testing infrastructure, mentorship from industry experts, networking opportunities with investors and telecom operators, visibility through government platforms, and support for scaling innovations. Financial support may be available through linked schemes such as TDIP or PLI, though DCIS primarily focuses on non-financial incubation and validation support.
financial_support: DCIS does not provide direct financial grants or loans. Financial support, if any, is channeled through allied schemes like the Technology Development & Investment Promotion (TDIP) Scheme or Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for telecom and networking products, which offer subsidies or incentives based on investment and sales performance.
application_process: 1. Visit the DCIS portal at https://dot.gov.in/dcis 2. Register as an innovator or startup 3. Submit a proposal detailing the telecom innovation, its objectives, and expected outcomes 4. Undergo technical evaluation by DoT experts 5. If selected, gain access to DCIS infrastructure for testing and validation 6. Receive mentorship and guidance for scaling the solution 7. Submit progress reports and outcomes for review
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted throughout the year
implementing_agency: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications

overview: The Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF) is a scheme under the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, Government of India, aimed at promoting research, development, and innovation in telecom technologies. It supports indigenous development of telecom equipment and solutions to reduce import dependence and strengthen India's position in global telecom standards. The fund encourages collaboration between industry, academia, and research institutions to advance 5G, 6G, and other emerging telecom technologies.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; academic institutions; research organizations
eligibility: Eligible applicants include Indian companies, startups, MSMEs, academic institutions, and research organizations engaged in telecom technology development. Applicants must be registered in India and demonstrate capability to develop and deploy telecom solutions. Preference is given to projects with clear commercialization potential and alignment with national telecom priorities such as 5G/6G, rural connectivity, and secure communications.
benefits: Financial support for R&D projects, access to testing and certification facilities, technical guidance from DoT experts, opportunities for field trials with telecom service providers, assistance in intellectual property rights (IPR) filing, and support for participation in international telecom standards forums. Successful projects may also gain recognition for inclusion in government procurement lists and access to pilot deployment opportunities.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-based financial support to eligible entities for telecom technology development projects. Funding covers costs related to research, prototyping, testing, and field trials. The quantum of support is determined based on project scope, technical merit, and commercialization potential, subject to availability of funds under the TTDF corpus.
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed project proposal outlining objectives, methodology, timeline, and budget. 2. Include technical specifications, expected outcomes, and plan for technology transfer or commercialization. 3. Provide details of the applicant organization, including registration, technical team, and past experience. 4. Attach supporting documents such as certificates of incorporation, audited financial statements, and letters of collaboration (if applicable). 5. Submit the application through the designated portal or as specified in the official notification. 6. Await evaluation by the expert committee constituted by the Department of Telecommunications. 7. If approved, sign the grant agreement and commence project execution. 8. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates as per scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, Government of India

overview: The 5G Use Case Labs & Testbeds Initiative is a program under the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, aimed at fostering innovation and development of 5G use cases through dedicated labs and testbeds. It supports startups, MSMEs, and other entities in testing and validating 5G applications across various sectors. The initiative provides infrastructure and technical support to accelerate 5G adoption and innovation in India.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; enterprises
eligibility: Startups, MSMEs, enterprises, and academic institutions working on 5G use cases are eligible to apply. Entities must be registered in India and demonstrate a clear 5G innovation proposal with potential for scalability and impact.
benefits: Access to 5G testbed infrastructure, technical mentorship, connectivity support, and validation facilities. Financial support may be provided for prototype development and testing. Participants gain exposure to industry experts and potential funding opportunities.
financial_support: Financial support includes grants for prototype development, testing, and validation activities. The exact quantum and mechanism are determined on a case-by-case basis based on the proposal and available budget under the initiative.
application_process: 1. Visit the official 5G initiative portal at https://dot.gov.in/5g 2. Review eligibility criteria and guidelines 3. Prepare a detailed proposal outlining the 5G use case, objectives, and expected outcomes 4. Submit the application through the designated portal 5. Await evaluation by the expert committee 6. If selected, sign an MoU and proceed with lab/testbed access 7. Develop and test the 5G solution 8. Submit final report and outcomes for review
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications

overview: The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, aimed at identifying and supporting potential medal prospects for the Olympic Games. It provides financial assistance for customized training, foreign exposure, equipment, and support staff to elite athletes. The scheme focuses on athletes who have demonstrated consistent performance and medal-winning potential in international competitions.
target_beneficiaries: elite athletes; Olympic medal prospects
eligibility: Athletes who have achieved top-8 finishes in World Championships/Olympics or top-3 finishes in Asian Games/Commonwealth Games in individual events, or medal-winning performance in team events, are considered for inclusion in the TOPS core group. Developmental athletes showing consistent improvement and potential may also be included in the TOPS development group.
benefits: Financial support for foreign training, international competition participation, equipment, sports science and medical support, hiring of foreign coaches and support staff, and a monthly out-of-pocket allowance. Athletes also receive personalized training plans and performance monitoring.
financial_support: The scheme provides customized financial assistance based on individual athlete needs, covering expenses for foreign training, competition exposure, equipment, support staff, and a monthly stipend. The quantum of support is determined by the TOPS Mission Directorate based on the athlete's requirements and performance potential.
application_process: 1. Identification of potential athletes by National Sports Federations (NSFs) and the Sports Authority of India (SAI). 2. Evaluation by the TOPS Mission Directorate based on performance benchmarks and potential. 3. Approval of inclusion in the TOPS core or development group. 4. Formulation of a customized annual training plan (ATP) for each athlete. 5. Disbursement of funds as per the approved ATP upon submission of utilization certificates and progress reports.
deadlines: Rolling basis — athletes can be considered for inclusion throughout the year based on performance and potential.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India

overview: The Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF), renamed as Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, is a Government of India initiative aimed at providing universal access to quality ICT services at affordable prices in rural and remote areas. It supports telecom service providers through subsidy mechanisms to bridge the digital divide by funding projects such as BharatNet, 4G saturation in uncovered villages, mobile tower installations in Left Wing Extremism-affected areas, and international bandwidth hiring. The fund is administered by the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, and is financed through the Universal Access Levy (UAL) on telecom operators' adjusted gross revenue.
target_beneficiaries: People of rural and remote areas; Underserved rural, remote and urban areas; Telecom service providers
eligibility: Telecom service providers undertaking projects in areas where ICT services are not available due to commercial non-viability, on account of sparse population, remoteness of areas, absence of supporting infrastructure, low income of inhabitants and insurgency, as determined by the Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) / Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN).
benefits: Subsidy support to incentivize telecom service providers to venture into commercially non-viable areas; funding for BharatNet, 4G saturation, mobile tower projects in LWE-affected areas, CTDP for NER, international bandwidth hiring, and Digital Satellite Phone Terminals; non-discriminatory access to telecommunication services; promotion of R&D in telecom technologies; support for pilot projects and consultancy services; encouragement of adoption of new telecom services.
financial_support: The Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) provides financial support through subsidy disbursements to implementing agencies such as BSNL, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited, Bharti Airtel Limited, and Bharti Hexacom Limited for various projects. Funds are sourced from the Universal Access Levy (UAL) collected from telecom operators. As per the fund status as of 31.03.2026, total UAL accretion is ₹201,690.52 crore, total disbursement is ₹95,138 crore, and the potentially available fund balance is ₹106,552.50 crore. Specific project allocations include: ₹7,330 crore for LWE Phase II (excluding taxes), ₹2,426 crore for LWE Phase I 4G upgradation, ₹17.15 crore for international bandwidth hiring to BSNL, ₹2028.80 crore for CTDP in Arunachal Pradesh and two districts of Assam, ₹726.65 crore for uncovered villages and national highways of Meghalaya, ₹686.71 crore for 502 uncovered villages in aspirational districts, ₹3,685 crore for 7,287 aspirational villages, and ₹26,316 crore for saturation of 4G mobile services in uncovered villages across the country.
implementing_agency: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications

overview: The National Sports Development Fund (NSDF) was established in 1998 under the Charitable Endowments Act, 1890, to mobilize resources from government and non-government sources for the promotion of sports and games in India. It aims to support excellence in sports by providing financial assistance to athletes, coaches, and sports institutions for training, equipment, and participation in national and international competitions. The fund operates under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and accepts contributions from various stakeholders including public sector undertakings and private entities.
target_beneficiaries: athletes; coaches; sports institutions
eligibility: Individual athletes, coaches, sports persons, and sports institutions recognized by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports or respective National Sports Federations are eligible to apply for assistance from the NSDF. Applications must be recommended by the concerned sports federation or state sports council.
benefits: Financial assistance for training, equipment, participation in national and international competitions, exposure trips, and sports science support. Non-financial benefits include facilitation of access to training facilities, coordination with sports authorities, and support for career development of athletes.
financial_support: The NSDF provides grants based on the merit of the case and availability of funds. The quantum of assistance varies depending on the sport, level of competition, and specific needs of the applicant. There is no fixed upper limit mentioned in the evidence, and disbursement is made after approval by the NSDF Council.
application_process: 1. Submit application through the respective National Sports Federation or State Sports Council. 2. Obtain recommendation from the federation/council. 3. Forward the application to the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. 4. Application is reviewed by the NSDF Council. 5. Upon approval, funds are disbursed to the beneficiary.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year as per the needs of athletes and institutions.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

scheme_name: Sports Authority of India (SAI) Training Grants
overview: The Sports Authority of India (SAI) Training Grants scheme provides financial assistance to athletes, coaches, and sports institutions for training, equipment, and competition participation. It aims to support the development of sporting talent across various disciplines and levels, from grassroots to elite. The scheme is implemented by SAI under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to enhance India's performance in national and international sports events.
target_beneficiaries: athletes; coaches; sports institutions
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include individual athletes, coaches, and sports institutions recognized by SAI or affiliated with National Sports Federations (NSFs). Athletes must be registered with SAI or recommended by NSFs. Coaches must possess recognized qualifications. Institutions must be SAI-accredited training centers or recognized sports academies.
benefits: Financial assistance for training expenses, sports equipment, competition travel, coaching fees, and stipends. Non-financial benefits include access to SAI facilities, expert coaching, sports science support, and exposure to national/international competitions.
financial_support: Grants are provided based on the athlete's level, sport discipline, and training requirements. The quantum of support varies and is determined by SAI's expert committees. Funds are disbursed directly to beneficiaries or institutions after approval of training plans and expenditure proposals.
application_process: 1. Identify the appropriate SAI training grant scheme based on athlete level and sport. 2. Obtain recommendation from the respective National Sports Federation (NSF) or SAI regional center. 3. Submit application along with required documents to the concerned SAI office. 4. Application is reviewed by SAI's expert committee. 5. Upon approval, sanction letter is issued. 6. Funds are released in installments as per the approved training plan and utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year based on training cycles and competition schedules.
implementing_agency: Sports Authority of India (SAI), Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

scheme_name: Ease of Doing Business – BizReform App
overview: The Ease of Doing Business – BizReform App is a digital platform launched by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) to streamline regulatory processes for businesses in India. It provides a single-window interface for accessing various government services, approvals, and clearances required to start and operate a business. The app aims to reduce compliance burden, enhance transparency, and improve the overall business environment by integrating central and state-level services. It supports entrepreneurs, startups, and MSMEs in navigating legal and regulatory requirements efficiently.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Any business entity, including startups, MSMEs, and entrepreneurs, seeking government approvals, registrations, or clearances can use the BizReform App to access services.
benefits: Single-window access to multiple government services; reduced procedural delays; digital submission and tracking of applications; integration with central and state portals; improved transparency in approval processes; time and cost savings for businesses.
financial_support: The BizReform App does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. It is a facilitation platform focused on regulatory ease and process efficiency.
application_process: 1. Download the BizReform App from the official portal or app stores. 2. Register using mobile number or email ID. 3. Create a business profile with entity details. 4. Select the required government service or clearance. 5. Fill in the application form and upload necessary documents. 6. Submit the application and track its status in real time. 7. Receive approvals or notifications digitally through the app.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Services are accessible year-round as per user requirement.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: Affordable Rental Housing Complexes (ARHCs) is a sub-scheme under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) launched by the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs to provide dignified affordable rental housing to urban migrants and poor from EWS/LIG categories near their workplaces. The scheme operates through two models: Model-1 involves converting existing government-funded vacant houses into ARHCs via Public-Private Partnership or public agencies, while Model-2 involves construction, operation, and maintenance of ARHCs by public/private entities on their own vacant land. Projects are to be operated for a minimum period of 25 years and aim to unlock vacant housing stock, promote investment in rental housing, and improve living conditions for urban migrants/poor.
target_beneficiaries: urban migrants; poor; EWS; LIG
eligibility: Beneficiaries for ARHCs are urban migrants/poor from EWS/LIG categories. Under Model-1, concessionaires are selected through transparent bidding process by States/UTs/ULBs for repairing, retrofitting, developing, operating, and transferring ARHCs. Under Model-2, public/private entities with their own vacant land can apply via Expression of Interest (EoI) to construct, operate, and maintain ARHCs. Entities must comply with NBC/State/Local Authority norms for dwelling units and dormitories, and projects must include at least 40 dwelling units or equivalent dormitory beds.
benefits: Incentives/benefits include: exemption of income tax and GST on profits from ARHC operations; concessional project finance at lower interest rates through Affordable Housing Fund (AHF) and Priority Sector Lending (PSL); 50% additional FAR/FSI free of cost; single window approval system for design/drawings and statutory approvals within 30 days; provision of trunk infrastructure (road, water, sanitation, electricity) at no additional cost; municipal services levied at par with residential projects; use permission changes if needed; and Technology Innovation Grant (TIG) for adopting innovative technologies.
financial_support: Financial support includes concessional loans from Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) under Affordable Housing Fund (AHF) and Priority Sector Lending (PSL) by commercial banks at lower interest rates. Viability Gap Funding (VGF) may be provided from central assistance released to States/UTs for JnNURM/RAY projects if needed. Technology Innovation Grant (TIG) of Rs. 1,00,000 per double bedroom unit, Rs. 60,000 per single bedroom unit, and Rs. 20,000 per dormitory bed is available for projects using identified innovative technologies. Under Model-1, concessionaires invest their own funds to make houses livable; under Model-2, entities bear the investment for construction on their vacant land.
application_process: 1. For Model-1: States/UTs/ULBs prepare inventory of government-funded vacant houses, customize and issue RFP based on model RFP from MoHUA, conduct pre-bid meeting, receive and evaluate technical and financial bids, select concessionaire, sign concession agreement. 2. For Model-2: MoHUA issues Expression of Interest (EoI); entities submit application with documents on ARHC website; concerned ULBs shortlist entities based on eligibility; shortlisted entities submit Detailed Project Report (DPR) to ULB for approval; upon approval, entities construct, operate, and maintain ARHCs on their vacant land for 25 years.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round through EoI for Model-2 and RFP notices for Model-1 as issued by States/UTs/ULBs.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

overview: The Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) is a collaborative initiative between the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology, and the Department of Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. It aims to prevent the misappropriation of India's traditional knowledge by providing access to patent examiners at international patent offices. The database contains transcribed and digitized traditional knowledge from ancient Indian texts in five international languages (English, French, German, Spanish, Japanese) to facilitate prior art searches.
target_beneficiaries: patent examiners; researchers; indigenous communities; government bodies
eligibility: TKDL is not a beneficiary-oriented scheme; it is a defensive database accessible to patent examiners under international agreements. Access is granted to patent offices that have signed access agreements with TKDL, including the European Patent Office (EPO), United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), Japan Patent Office (JPO), United Kingdom Intellectual Property Office (UKIPO), and Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO).
benefits: Prevents erroneous patent grants on traditional knowledge, provides prior art evidence to patent examiners, supports legal opposition and revocation of patents, enhances global awareness of India's traditional knowledge, and safeguards indigenous rights without financial compensation to individuals.
financial_support: TKDL does not provide direct financial support to individuals or entities. It is a knowledge repository initiative funded by the Government of India through CSIR and AYUSH for development, maintenance, and access management.
application_process: 1. Patent offices interested in accessing TKDL must negotiate and sign an access agreement with the TKDL Unit. 2. Upon agreement, access credentials are provided to authorized patent examiners. 3. Authorized users can search the TKDL database through the secure access portal. 4. Search results are used to assess novelty and inventive step in patent applications related to traditional knowledge.
deadlines: Rolling basis — access is granted upon execution of formal access agreements.
implementing_agency: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and Department of Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

overview: Khelo India – Sport Tech Fund is a component of the Khelo India National Programme for Development of Sports, aimed at reviving sports culture at the grassroots level by building a strong framework for all sports in India and establishing the nation as a sporting superpower. The programme includes verticals such as State Level Khelo India Centres, Annual Sports Competitions, Talent Search and Development, and support for sports academies, among others. It is implemented by multiple agencies including the Sports Authority of India, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, and Lakshmi Bai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE). The initiative provides financial assistance to talented athletes, infrastructure development, and opportunities for participation in national and international competitions.
target_beneficiaries: athletes; sportspersons; youth; women; persons with disabilities; rural and tribal communities; school-going children
eligibility: The Khelo India programme targets young athletes across various sports disciplines. Talented players identified in priority sports disciplines at various levels by the High-Powered Committee are provided annual financial assistance of INR 5 lakh per annum for 8 years. Support is extended to athletes participating in State Level Khelo India Centres, Annual Sports Competitions, Talent Search and Development, and other verticals under the scheme. Specific eligibility varies by vertical, including age, performance, and discipline-based criteria.
benefits: Benefits include annual financial assistance of INR 5 lakh per annum for 8 years for talented athletes, access to State Level Khelo India Centres, participation in Annual Sports Competitions (e.g., Khelo India Youth Games, University Games, Winter Games, Beach Games, Para Games), talent search and development programs, support for sports academies, promotion of sports for women and persons with disabilities, development of rural and indigenous games, physical fitness initiatives for school children, infrastructure development (play field creation/upgradation), and community coaching development through LNIPE.
financial_support: Under the Talent Search and Development vertical, talented players identified in priority sports disciplines are provided annual financial assistance of INR 5 lakh per annum for 8 years. Additional funding includes grants for State Level Khelo India Centres (e.g., ₹2 lakhs per discipline as annual recurring grant for SAI Extension centres converted to Khelo India Centres), viability gap funding for Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCE), and expenditure on lodging, boarding, education, competition exposure, sports training, and equipment incurred by the Government for athletes in supported centres.
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 5 lakh per annum for 8 years
application_process: 1. Athletes are identified through talent search and development programs conducted by the High-Powered Committee. 2. Selected athletes are notified via official induction notifications (e.g., Induction Notification of Khelo India Athletes - [discipline]). 3. Athletes must submit required documents for verification and inclusion in the Khelo India athlete database. 4. Upon approval, athletes receive annual financial assistance and access to training facilities. 5. Continued support is subject to performance review and retention protocols.
deadlines: Rolling basis — inductions and notifications are issued periodically throughout the year based on talent identification cycles.
implementing_agency: Sports Authority of India, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, Lakshmi Bai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE)

overview: Shram Suvidha Portal – Labour Compliance is a unified digital platform launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment to facilitate ease of compliance and ease of doing business under the new Labour Codes. It enables digitization of processes such as registration, licence, returns, inspection notices, and enforcement by agencies like EPFO, ESIC, DGMS, DGFASLI, and CLC. The portal supports self-certification for startups under labour laws and provides access to various labour codes, notifications, and user manuals.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; employers; contractors
eligibility: Every employer of any establishment which comes into existence after the commencement of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 and the Social Security Code, 2020 must apply for registration within 60 days in Form-I electronically through the Shram Suvidha Portal. Establishments already registered under other labour laws must update their registration details within six months from the date of commencement of these Rules.
benefits: Digitized processes for registration, licence, returns, inspection notices, and enforcement; self-certification facility for startups under labour laws; access to Labour Codes and rules; online submission of returns and generation of Labour Identification Number (LIN); risk-based inspection system; reduced compliance burden through harmonized returns and transparent enforcement.
financial_support: The portal does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. It is a compliance and registration platform facilitating ease of doing business under labour laws. Any financial aspects relate to fees for services like licence issuance or security deposits, which are borne by the user.
application_process: 1. Visit the Shram Suvidha Portal at https://shramsuvidha.gov.in. 2. Click on 'Sign up' to register as a user by providing name, email ID, mobile number, and captcha code. 3. Verify registration via the link sent to the registered email ID. 4. Set user ID and password after OTP verification. 5. Log in to the portal using OTP or user ID/password. 6. Navigate to the Registration module. 7. Select 'Apply for New/Existing/Offline Registration'. 8. Choose registration type (e.g., 'New Registration' or 'Existing with LIN'). 9. Fill Form-I with establishment details, proof of identity, PAN/TAN, address, and Inter-State migrant worker information. 10. Upload supporting documents. 11. Apply e-sign using Aadhaar-based OTP verification. 12. Submit the application. 13. Certificate of Registration (Form-III) is auto-generated and issued immediately upon successful submission.
deadlines: Registration must be completed within 60 days from the date of applicability of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 and the Social Security Code, 2020. Existing establishments must update registration within six months from the date of commencement of these Rules.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India

overview: The National IPR Policy 2016 Implementation Schemes, administered by the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM) under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, aim to strengthen India's intellectual property ecosystem through awareness, facilitation, and protection mechanisms. These schemes support innovators, startups, MSMEs, and creators across various IP domains including patents, designs, trademarks, geographical indications, and copyrights by providing procedural guidance, fee structures, examination facilities, and recognition frameworks.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; entrepreneurs; individual inventors; educational institutions
eligibility: Eligibility varies by IP type but generally includes natural persons, startups, small entities, educational institutions, and other legal entities applying for patents, designs, trademarks, geographical indications, or copyrights under the respective Acts and Rules, with specific fee concessions available for startups and small entities as per the First Schedule of the Patents Rules 2003 and analogous provisions in other IP statutes.
benefits: Benefits include legal protection of intellectual property, exclusive rights to exploit creations, facilitation through e-filing systems, access to examination and publication facilities, fee concessions for startups and small entities, certificate issuance, journal publication, and support for international applications via PCT and Madrid Protocol, along with awareness programs and training workshops conducted by RGNIIPM and other units under CGPDTM.
financial_support: Financial support is primarily through fee concessions rather than direct grants or loans. Startups and small entities receive reduced official fees for patent filings (e.g., 800 INR for natural persons/startups/small entities vs. 4000 INR for others under Form 1), with similar concessions across other IP types. No direct fund disbursement or loan mechanism is described in the evidence; support is procedural and cost-reduction based.
application_process: 1. Determine the type of IP protection required (patent, design, trademark, GI, copyright). 2. Confirm eligibility and applicable fee structure based on applicant category (natural person, startup, small entity, etc.). 3. Prepare required documents including forms, specifications, representations, and affidavits as per guidelines. 4. File application via the e-filing portal or physical submission with prescribed fees. 5. Track application status through the online portal. 6. Respond to examination reports or objections within stipulated time. 7. Attend hearings if scheduled. 8. Upon compliance, receive registration certificate and publication in the respective journal.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
