overview: The MSME Pre-Pack Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP) is a streamlined insolvency resolution mechanism under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, designed specifically for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to facilitate faster and cost-effective resolution of financial distress. It allows the corporate debtor to initiate a resolution plan with the consent of its creditors, bypassing the need for a public invitation of resolution plans, thereby reducing time and cost. The process is governed by the IBBI (Pre-packaged Insolvency Resolution Process) Regulations, 2021, and subsequent amendments, aiming to preserve business continuity and maximize value for stakeholders in the MSME sector.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: The corporate debtor must be classified as a Micro, Small, or Medium Enterprise as per the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006. The initiation of PPIRP requires the consent of not less than sixty-six percent of the financial creditors by value. The process is available only if there is no pending application for insolvency resolution under section 7, 9 or 10 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, and no order for liquidation has been passed. The corporate debtor must not have undergone a PPIRP in the last three years.
benefits: PPIRP offers a faster resolution timeline (typically within 90 days) compared to regular CIRP (180 days, extendable to 330 days). It reduces procedural costs by avoiding public invitation of resolution plans and e-auctions. The process allows the existing management to retain control if the resolution plan is approved, promoting business continuity. It provides flexibility in structuring the resolution plan, including merger, amalgamation, or takeover. Creditors benefit from higher realization due to reduced delays and preservation of going concern value. The process also minimizes disruption to ongoing operations and preserves employment.
financial_support: PPIRP does not involve direct financial support from the government. Instead, it facilitates resolution through private infusion of funds by the resolution applicant, which may include fresh equity, quasi-equity, or internal accruals. The financial support is structured as part of the resolution plan, where the successful resolution applicant infuses funds to settle claims of operational and financial creditors, pay CIRP costs, and provide performance guarantees (typically 10% of the resolution plan value). The quantum of financial support varies case-by-case based on the resolution plan approved by the Committee of Creditors and the Adjudicating Authority.
application_process: 1. The corporate debtor, in consultation with its financial creditors, prepares a resolution plan. 2. The resolution plan is approved by the Committee of Creditors (CoC) with a vote of not less than sixty-six percent of financial creditors by value. 3. The corporate debtor files an application for initiation of PPIRP before the Adjudicating Authority (National Company Law Tribunal) under section 30(6) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. 4. The application is accompanied by the resolution plan, information memorandum, evaluation matrix, and a declaration under section 29A of the Code. 5. The Adjudicating Authority examines the application for compliance with section 30(2) and 29A of the Code. 6. If satisfied, the Adjudicating Authority approves the resolution plan, making it binding on all stakeholders. 7. The successful resolution applicant then implements the plan, including infusion of funds and payment of performance guarantee.
deadlines: The application for initiation of PPIRP must be filed before the Adjudicating Authority after the resolution plan is approved by the Committee of Creditors. There is no fixed window; the process can be initiated at any time subject to eligibility. However, once initiated, the resolution process must be completed within 90 days from the date of application, extendable by the Adjudicating Authority for a further 60 days in exceptional circumstances, making a maximum of 150 days.
implementing_agency: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India

scheme_name: NCLT Fast Track Insolvency for MSMEs
overview: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) is a quasi-judicial body constituted under section 408 of the Companies Act, 2013, effective from 1st June 2016, to adjudicate company law and insolvency matters. It functions as the Adjudicating Authority under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016, and aims to streamline corporate dispute resolution by consolidating functions of erstwhile bodies like CLB, BIFR, and AAIFR. NCLT operates through multiple benches across India, handling cases related to oppression, mismanagement, amalgamations, winding up, and Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP).
target_beneficiaries: MSME; corporates; creditors; shareholders; employees; personal guarantors
eligibility: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) has jurisdiction over company law cases transferred from Hon’ble High Courts and the erstwhile Company Law Tribunal, and insolvency cases under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. It adjudicates matters relating to oppression and mismanagement, class action suits, reduction of share capital, rectification of register of members, amalgamations, mergers, restoration of company name, winding up, and other functions under the Companies Act. It has exclusive jurisdiction to commence and adjudicate Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) cases and Insolvency Resolution Process for Personal Guarantors to Corporate Debtors.
benefits: NCLT ensures timely and effective adjudication of company law, corporate insolvency, and individual insolvency cases. It promotes a legally secure environment supporting good corporate governance and stakeholder confidence. It facilitates maximization of asset value, promotes entrepreneurship, enhances credit availability, balances stakeholder interests, strengthens corporate regulatory framework, fosters trust and discipline, advances ease of doing business, and reduces NPAs through IBC implementation.
financial_support: NCLT does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. It is a judicial tribunal that adjudicates insolvency and company law cases. Financial outcomes arise from court-ordered resolutions, such as debt restructuring, liquidation proceeds, or repayment plans under IBC, but NCLT itself does not disburse funds.
application_process: 1. Identify the appropriate NCLT bench based on geographical jurisdiction. 2. File the relevant petition or application (e.g., Company Petition, Company Appeal, Insolvency Petition) under the applicable provision of Companies Act, 2013 or Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. 3. Submit the application along with required documents at the NCLT registry or through e-filing portal. 4. Pay the prescribed court fees. 5. Serve notice to the opposite party as per rules. 6. Attend hearings as scheduled by the Tribunal. 7. Await judgment or order from the NCLT bench.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be filed throughout the year as per cause of action arising.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
contact_details: Email: dr1-nclt@nclt.gov.in, ar4-nclt@nclt.gov.in | Helpline: 011-24363846 (as per objection list, though noted as non-functional during relocation)

overview: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) is a central sector sub-scheme under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) launched in 2023-24 with a total outlay of Rs. 6000 crore, supported by the World Bank and Agence Française de Développement (AFD). It aims to address inherent weaknesses in the fisheries sector through financial and technical interventions to enhance long-term sustainability and resilience by facilitating sectoral reforms. The scheme will be implemented from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27 across all states and union territories.
target_beneficiaries: fish farmers; fishermen; aquaculture entrepreneurs; coastal communities; self-help groups
eligibility: The scheme is open to all states and union territories for implementation from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27. Specific beneficiary eligibility criteria (such as fish farmers, aquaculture units, self-help groups, cooperatives, etc.) are determined at the state/UT level based on notified guidelines under PMMSY framework, focusing on those engaged in fisheries and aquaculture activities requiring financial and technical support for sectoral reforms.
benefits: Financial support for fisheries projects, technical assistance for sectoral reforms, promotion of sustainable aquaculture practices, development of fisheries infrastructure, enhancement of fish production and productivity, support for value addition and post-harvest management, livelihood and nutritional support during fishing bans/lean periods, employment generation in fisheries and allied activities, and facilitation of private investment and entrepreneurship in the sector.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of subsidies and grants for approved fisheries projects under its framework, with funding pattern following the central sector scheme norms under PMMSY. The total outlay is Rs. 6000 crore, supported by the World Bank and AFD, to be utilized over four years (FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27) for activities including infrastructure development, technology infusion, value chain enhancement, and sectoral reforms.
application_process: Stakeholders (intended beneficiaries) are required to consult the respective District Fisheries Officer of the district in the state/UT where they intend to undertake fisheries development activities. Proposals are to be submitted through the state/UT fisheries department following the guidelines issued under PMMSY and PM-MKSSY framework.
deadlines: The scheme is implemented from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27. Application windows and specific deadlines are determined by state/UT fisheries departments as per annual action plans and notified guidelines.
implementing_agency: Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India

overview: The Mega Food Park Scheme aims to link agricultural production to the market by bringing together farmers, processors, and retailers to maximize value addition, minimize wastage, increase farmers' income, and create employment opportunities, particularly in rural areas. It follows a 'Cluster' approach to create state-of-the-art support infrastructure in a defined agri/horticultural zone for setting up modern food processing units in industrial plots within the park, with an established supply chain. The scheme has been discontinued by the Government with effect from 01.04.2021, with provision for committed liabilities for ongoing projects only. As of the evidence, 25 Mega Food Parks are operational.
target_beneficiaries: entrepreneurs; MSME; farmers; processors; retailers
eligibility: The Mega Food Park project is implemented by a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) which is a Body Corporate registered under the Companies Act. State Government, State Government entities and Cooperatives are not required to form a separate SPV for implementation of Mega Food Park project. Subject to fulfillment of the conditions of the Scheme Guidelines, the funds are released to the SPVs.
benefits: The scheme provides a mechanism to link agricultural production to the market, maximizes value addition, minimizes wastage, increases farmers' income, and creates employment opportunities, particularly in rural sector. It offers state-of-the-art support infrastructure including collection centers, primary processing centers, central processing centers, cold chain, and around 25-30 fully developed plots for entrepreneurs to set up food processing units with an established supply chain.
financial_support: Funds are released to the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) subject to fulfillment of the conditions of the Scheme Guidelines. The SPV is a Body Corporate registered under the Companies Act. State Government, State Government entities and Cooperatives are not required to form a separate SPV for implementation.
application_process: 1. Form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) as a Body Corporate registered under the Companies Act (State Government, State Government entities and Cooperatives are exempt from forming a separate SPV). 2. Ensure the SPV meets the conditions of the Scheme Guidelines. 3. Submit proposal for financial assistance. 4. Upon approval, funds are released to the SPV. 5. Develop the Mega Food Park with supply chain infrastructure including collection centers, primary processing centers, central processing centers, cold chain, and 25-30 fully developed plots for food processing units.
deadlines: The scheme has been discontinued by the Government with effect from 01.04.2021 with provision for committed liabilities for ongoing projects only.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Food Processing Industries

overview: The National Livestock Mission (NLM) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Government of India to ensure sustainable development of the livestock sector, focusing on improving productivity, supporting entrepreneurship, and promoting breed improvement, fodder development, and risk management. It aims to enhance livestock production through capacity building, technology adoption, and infrastructure development, with special attention to small and marginal farmers, livestock rearers, and entrepreneurs in rural areas. The mission operates through four sub-missions: Livestock Development, Pig Development in the Northeastern Region, Feed and Fodder Development, and Skill Development, Technology Transfer, and Extension.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; livestock rearers; entrepreneurs; self-help groups; cooperatives; MSME; agri-startups
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include individual farmers, livestock rearers, self-help groups (SHGs), joint liability groups (JLGs), cooperatives, producer companies, NGOs, and MSMEs engaged in animal husbandry activities. Priority is given to small and marginal farmers, SC/ST communities, women entrepreneurs, and those involved in breed improvement, fodder production, poultry, piggery, goat and sheep rearing, and dairy entrepreneurship. Applicants must have valid land records or lease agreements where applicable and must comply with state-specific implementation guidelines.
benefits: Benefits include financial assistance in the form of subsidies for setting up livestock farms, breed improvement programs, fodder production units, poultry and piggery units, sheep and goat rearing, and dairy entrepreneurship. Non-financial benefits encompass technical guidance, training and capacity building, access to improved breeds and seeds, veterinary support, market linkages, and extension services. The scheme also supports risk management through livestock insurance and provides incentives for entrepreneurship development and skill training in animal husbandry and allied sectors.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as a centrally sponsored scheme with cost-sharing between the Central and State Governments in the ratio of 60:40 for general category states, 90:10 for Northeastern and Himalayan states, and 100% central funding for Union Territories. Subsidy quantum varies by component: up to 50% of project cost for poultry, piggery, goat and sheep rearing, and dairy units; up to 75% for SC/ST beneficiaries; and up to 90% for specific components like fodder block making and silage production under the Feed and Fodder Development Sub-Mission. Assistance is released in installments based on verification of progress and utilization of previous funds.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant component under the National Livestock Mission (e.g., poultry, piggery, fodder, breed improvement). 2. Contact the State Implementing Agency (SIA) or District Animal Husbandry Office for guidance and application forms. 3. Prepare a detailed project report including cost estimates, land details, and beneficiary information. 4. Submit the application along with required documents to the concerned District Animal Husbandry Officer or State Nodal Agency. 5. Application undergoes scrutiny and field verification by the concerned authorities. 6. Upon approval, sanction letter is issued and funds are released in installments as per progress. 7. Beneficiary must complete the project within the stipulated time and submit utilization certificates and completion reports.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and state-specific allocation windows.
implementing_agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying

overview: The Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) is a central sector scheme under the Prime Minister's AtmaNirbhar Bharat Abhiyan stimulus package of Rs.15000 crore. It incentivizes investments by individual entrepreneurs, private companies, MSME, Farmers Producers Organizations (FPOs), and Section 8 companies to establish infrastructure in dairy processing, meat processing, animal feed plants, breed improvement technology, animal waste to wealth management, and veterinary vaccine and drugs manufacturing facilities. The scheme provides loans up to 90% of project cost, 3% interest subvention, and credit guarantee cover for eligible entities.
target_beneficiaries: individual entrepreneurs; private companies; MSME; Farmers Producers Organizations (FPOs); Section 8 companies
eligibility: Following are the eligible entities for availing benefits under the AHIDF Scheme: a. Farmer Producer Organization (FPO) b. Private companies c. Individual entrepreneurs d. Section 8 companies e. Micro Small and Medium Enterprises
benefits: Loan up to 90% of project cost from Scheduled Banks or NCDC, 3% interest subvention provided by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, credit guarantee cover up to 25% of loan amount from NABSanrakshan Trustee Co. Pvt. Ltd. for MSME units, and up to 85% guarantee cover for loan amount up to Rs. 2.0 crore from CGTMSE for micro and small enterprises. The interest subvention is released through the lending bank and is available for a maximum of 8 years from the date of first disbursement. Beneficiary contribution ranges from 10% for Micro and Small units, 15% for Medium Enterprises, and up to 25% for other categories of enterprises as per MSME defined ceilings.
financial_support: The project under the AHIDF shall be eligible for loan up to 90% of the estimated/actual project cost from any Scheduled Bank or National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) based on submission of viable projects by eligible beneficiaries. There is no maximum or minimum limit of project cost or term loan. The beneficiary contribution in case of Micro and Small units as per MSME defined ceiling could be 10%, while in case of Medium Enterprises as per defined MSME ceiling, beneficiary contribution could go up to 15%. The beneficiary contribution in other categories of enterprises could go up to 25% or more. Interest subvention of 3% is provided to all eligible entities by the Department. The credit guarantee will be provided only for those projects which are viable and are covered under MSME defined ceilings and the guarantee coverage would be up to 25% of the credit facility available to the borrower. Eligible units may also avail credit guarantee cover from CGTMSE scheme for the loan amount up to Rs 2.00 crores with the guarantee cover of maximum extent of 85% of loan amount.
application_process: 1. Open https://ahidf.udyamimitra.in/ 2. Enter mobile number of Applicant. Select the checkbox of “I am not a Robot” and click on “Request OTP” button. 3. Enter 6 digits OTP received on Applicants mobile number and click on ‘Verify OTP’ button. Upon verification of OTP, User will be successfully on boarded. 4. Fill Applicant information, Promoters/ Management details and Project Information. 5. Validate all required fields on Fill Application tab and save/ Submit application. 6. On Successful submission on Application details, User will navigate to Upload Documents Page. On this screen user need to upload Project Documents and Documents related to Applicant/ Promoters. 7. Submit Application to marketplace or submit application to preferred lender. 8. Click on Submit to check Application Status and Application No. 9. View application status. Once application submitted, Application status become Logged. User can view application details or download application from this screen. In case of Application withdrawal click on Withdraw button so that application will get Withdraw and User need to apply again.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
contact_details: Email: js-nlm[at]dahd[dot]nic[dot]in, ahc-dadf[at]nic[dot]in, sk[dot]dutta[at]nic[dot]in, lipi[dot]s[at]gov[dot]in | Phone: 011-23382354, 011-21401453, 011-21401454, 011-23311036

overview: The National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) to strengthen dairy infrastructure, enhance milk quality, and increase organized milk procurement across India. It focuses on creating and strengthening infrastructure for production, procurement, processing, and marketing of milk and milk products through financial and technical assistance to state governments and implementing agencies.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; milk unions; milk producer companies; dairy cooperatives; private dairy enterprises
eligibility: State governments, milk unions, milk producer companies, dairy cooperatives, and private dairy enterprises are eligible to apply for financial assistance under NPDD for setting up or strengthening dairy infrastructure projects related to milk production, procurement, processing, and marketing.
benefits: Financial assistance for setting up new dairy projects and strengthening existing ones, including infrastructure for milk chilling, processing, value addition, packaging, and marketing. Technical support for quality improvement, training, and capacity building. Assistance for creating forward and backward linkages in the dairy value chain.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid and subsidies to eligible implementing agencies. The funding pattern varies by component and beneficiary type, with central government contributing up to 60% of project cost (90% for hilly and northeastern states), and the balance borne by the state government or implementing agency. Assistance is released in installments based on project progress and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. State governments or eligible entities submit project proposals to the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD). 2. Proposals are appraised by the Project Sanctioning Committee (PSC) under DAHD. 3. Upon approval, sanction letters are issued specifying the financial assistance and terms. 4. Funds are released in installments against utilization certificates and physical progress reports. 5. Projects are monitored through periodic inspections and third-party evaluations.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and approval by the Project Sanctioning Committee.
implementing_agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying

overview: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) is a flagship initiative under the National Programme for Bovine Breeding and Dairy Development, launched to conserve and develop indigenous bovine breeds through genetic upgradation and enhancement of milk production and productivity. It aims to enhance bovine productivity and increase milk production in a sustainable manner using advanced breeding technologies. The mission focuses on the propagation of high genetic merit bulls of indigenous breeds and the establishment of integrated cattle development centres.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; livestock rearers; dairy cooperatives; gaushalas; state livestock development boards
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include individual farmers, livestock rearers, dairy cooperatives, self-help groups, gaushalas, NGOs, and state livestock development boards engaged in bovine breeding and development activities. Preference is given to those working with indigenous breeds such as Gir, Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar, Rathi, Kankrej, Hariana, Ongole, and others. Beneficiaries must submit a detailed project proposal outlining breed improvement, infrastructure development, and training components.
benefits: Financial assistance for procurement of indigenous bovine breeds, establishment of Gokul Grams, training and capacity building of farmers, organization of infertility camps, fertility camps, and milk yield competitions. Support for semen stations, in-vitro fertilization (IVF) labs, embryo transfer technology, and genomic selection. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, breed improvement advisory, and access to superior germplasm.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid and subsidies for various components such as establishment of Gokul Grams (up to 50% of project cost), procurement of indigenous bovines (up to 50% subsidy), training programs, and infertility/fertility camps. Assistance is released through state implementing agencies based on approved annual action plans and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, breed details, infrastructure plan, budget, and expected outcomes. 2. Submit the proposal to the State Implementing Agency (SIA) or State Livestock Development Board. 3. The SIA forwards the proposal to the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD) for appraisal. 4. Upon approval by DAHD, funds are released in installments to the SIA. 5. The beneficiary implements the project and submits progress reports and utilization certificates. 6. Final release is made after verification of completion and outcomes.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year based on annual action plans of states.
implementing_agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying

scheme_name: Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure
overview: The Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure scheme is a component of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) aimed at creating modern infrastructure for cold chain and value addition from farm gate to retail outlet. It supports setting up of integrated cold chain projects including irradiation units, cold storage, and value addition facilities to reduce post-harvest losses, increase processing levels, and enhance exports. The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid for infrastructure development in the food processing sector.
target_beneficiaries: entrepreneurs; MSME; agri-startups; food processing units
eligibility: All Universities, IITs, Central/State Government Institutions, Government funded Organizations, R&D laboratories and CSIR recognized R&D units in private sector are eligible under the Research & Development scheme. For the Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure component, eligibility criteria are specified in the scheme guidelines and include prospective entrepreneurs, SC/ST category applicants, and NER region applicants as per EOI notices.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid for setting up infrastructure projects in the food processing sector. Benefits include support for cold chain, value addition infrastructure, irradiation units, and backward-forward linkages. The scheme facilitates release of funds in instalments based on compliance with approval letters, utilization certificates, and technical civil work completion. It also supports NABL accreditation for food testing laboratories and provides impetus to employment generation, farmer income growth, and export enhancement.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as grants-in-aid released in instalments. The first instalment (50% of grants-in-aid) is released upon acceptance letter and compliance with enclosures, including geo-tagged photographs, building plans, and confirmation of 50% equity and term loan expenditure. The second instalment (50%) is released upon submission of utilization certificate, confirmation of 100% expenditure of equity, term loan, and grants-in-aid, NABL accreditation status, and proof of project completion and commercialization. Funds are released through the EAT module of PFMS.
application_process: 1. Submit Expression of Interest (EOI) as per notices issued under the scheme. 2. Attend pre-bid meetings as scheduled. 3. Submit detailed proposals in response to EOI or RFP for engagement of PMA. 4. Undergo technical and project approval committee review. 5. Receive approval letter from Inter-Ministerial Approval Committee (IMAC). 6. Fulfill compliance requirements for first instalment: submit acceptance letter, compliance documents, geo-tagged photographs, building plan, and proof of 50% equity and term loan expenditure. 7. Submit utilization certificate and related documents for second instalment. 8. Obtain NABL accreditation for food testing laboratories where applicable. 9. Submit proof of project completion and commercialization.
deadlines: Rolling basis — EOIs are invited periodically with specific closing dates (e.g., EoI dated 20.05.2026 for irradiation units, EoI dated 27.05.2025 for multiproduct food irradiation units).
implementing_agency: Ministry of Food Processing Industries

overview: The PACS (Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies) Computerisation scheme aims to modernize and strengthen the functioning of Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies across India by providing them with computer hardware, software, and networking facilities. The initiative seeks to improve operational efficiency, enhance service delivery to farmers, and enable better financial management and record-keeping at the grassroots level. It supports the digital transformation of cooperatives to ensure transparency, accountability, and timely access to credit and other services for rural communities.
target_beneficiaries: Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies (PACS)
eligibility: Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies (PACS) that are functionally active and willing to adopt computerisation for their operations are eligible under the scheme. Societies must have a minimum membership base and demonstrate viability for sustained operations post-computerisation.
benefits: Financial assistance for procurement of computer hardware, software, UPS, and networking equipment; training for PACS staff on system usage; improved record-keeping and financial management; enhanced service delivery to farmers including loan disbursement, savings, and input distribution; better monitoring and supervision by higher financing agencies; integration with state and national cooperative networks.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of a subsidy for the procurement of computer systems and related infrastructure. The central government contributes a fixed percentage of the total project cost, while the remaining amount is borne by the state government or the PACS itself, depending on the state-specific implementation guidelines.
application_process: 1. PACS submits a project proposal for computerisation to the District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCB) or State Cooperative Bank (SCB). 2. The proposal is forwarded to the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) for scrutiny and sanction. 3. Upon approval, funds are released in installments based on progress. 4. PACS procures the approved hardware and software through authorized vendors. 5. Installation and commissioning are carried out followed by staff training. 6. Post-implementation review is conducted to assess utilization and impact.
deadlines: Rolling basis — subject to availability of funds and annual budget allocations
implementing_agency: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)

scheme_name: Food Safety & Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) Compliance Support
overview: The Food Safety & Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) Compliance Support scheme provides guidance and assistance to food businesses for adhering to food safety regulations, including licensing, registration, standards formulation, and compliance with fortification and labeling requirements. It aims to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food through regulatory oversight, capacity building, and stakeholder engagement. The scheme supports food business operators, regulators, and consumers via training, advisories, and digital platforms like FoSCoS and Food Safety Connect.
target_beneficiaries: food business operators; regulatory officials; consumers; laboratories; street food vendors
eligibility: Eligibility varies by service: For standard formulation, submission of representation or request with scientific rationale is required. For NSF & FI approval, food products/ingredients covered under FSS (NSF & FI) Regulation, 2017 are eligible. For vegan logo approval, submission of documents as per guidelines including source of ingredients, certificate of analysis for absence of cholesterol, lactose, animal DNA from NABL accredited laboratory is required. For FSMP approval, submission of scientific, clinical, and epidemiological data for dietary management of specific disease/disorder/medical condition is required. For import NOC/NCR, consignments must comply with FSS Act, 2006, Rules, and FSS (Import) Regulations, 2017. For food laboratory recognition, laboratory must have accreditation under FSSAI-NABL Integrated Assessment. For Food Analyst examination, candidates must possess essential educational qualifications (Bachelor’s/Master’s/Doctorate in specified fields) and not less than three years’ experience in food analysis at recognized institutions. For FBO training, eligibility criteria are specified in FoSTaC portal links. For RTI, only citizens of India are eligible. For CPGRAMS, only citizens of India are eligible to file grievances.
benefits: Non-financial benefits include access to scientific rationale-based standard formulation, approval of non-specified foods and food ingredients, vegan logo endorsement, approval of foods for special medical purposes, issuance of NOC/NCR for imported food consignments, recognition and notification of food testing laboratories, Food Analyst certification, training of FBOs and regulatory staff, RTI facilitation, CPGRAMS grievance redressal, and access to advisories, circulars, and digital tools like Food Safety Connect and FoSCoS. Financial benefits are not explicitly mentioned as direct subsidies or grants; however, some services involve applicable fees (e.g., Rs. 50,000 + GST for NSF & FI approval, Rs. 10,000 + GST for vegan logo, Rs. 2500–5000 + GST for Food Analyst exam, Rs. 60,000 + 18% GST for ED-FSR diploma). Financial assistance is provided to states (e.g., FSSAI providing financial assistance to Assam for upgrading laboratories dedicated to pesticide testing).
financial_support: FSSAI does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants to beneficiaries under this scheme. Instead, it charges applicable fees for various services such as approvals, examinations, and trainings. Financial support is extended selectively to state governments for specific purposes, such as upgrading laboratories for pesticide testing in Assam. Fees for services include: Rs. 50,000 + GST for NSF & FI approval, Rs. 10,000 + GST per application for vegan logo endorsement, Rs. 2500–5000 + GST for Food Analyst examination (CBT and practical), Rs. 60,000 + 18% GST for the ED-FSR diploma program, Rs. 2000 visual inspection fee and sample testing fees for import NOC/NCR, Rs. 1000 application processing fee for food laboratory recognition, and Rs. 2500 + GST for Food Analyst CBT. No direct grant or loan disbursement to food businesses is evidenced.
application_process: 1. Identify the required service (e.g., standard formulation, NSF & FI approval, vegan logo, FSMP, import NOC, lab recognition, Food Analyst exam, FBO training, RTI, CPGRAMS grievance). 2. Visit the relevant portal or division as specified (e.g., FoSTaC portal for FBO training, FoSCoS for licensing, FSSAI website for RTI/CPGRAMS, labs@fssai.gov.in for lab recognition). 3. Prepare and submit the required application form (e.g., Form-I for NSF & FI, Form-A for lab recognition, Annexure for claims, Form for vegan logo, dossier for FSMP). 4. Attach required documents (e.g., scientific rationale, source of ingredients, certificate of analysis, NABL accreditation, educational qualifications, experience proof, identity/address proof). 5. Pay applicable fees via FSSAI ePayment portal or other specified modes (e.g., https://epay.fssai.gov.in/). 6. Submit application via email, online portal, or physical submission as directed (e.g., labs@fssai.gov.in for lab recognition, online for Food Analyst exam). 7. Await processing and approval as per indicated timeframes (e.g., 04-06 months for NSF & FI, 06-09 months for claims, 04-06 months for vegan logo, 09-12 months for FSMP, 2-10 days for import NOC/NCR, 01-09 months for lab recognition, 01 year for Food Analyst certification). 8. Receive approval, certificate, notification, or service delivery upon successful completion.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)

scheme_name: Multi State Cooperative Societies Development Fund
overview: The Multi State Cooperative Societies Development Fund is a financial assistance scheme aimed at supporting the development and strengthening of multi-state cooperative societies in India. It provides financial support for various developmental activities including infrastructure, technology upgradation, and human resource development. The fund is managed by the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) under the Ministry of Cooperation. The scheme aims to enhance the economic viability and operational efficiency of multi-state cooperatives across the country.
target_beneficiaries: multi-state cooperative societies
eligibility: Multi-state cooperative societies registered under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002 are eligible to apply for financial assistance under the fund. The societies must demonstrate viable project proposals with clear developmental objectives and repayment capacity. Preference may be given to societies working in priority sectors such as agriculture, dairy, fisheries, handicrafts, and rural industries.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of term loans and working capital support at concessional interest rates. Support for infrastructure development including construction of godowns, processing units, and retail outlets. Assistance for technology upgradation, automation, and adoption of modern management practices. Funding for human resource development, training programs, and capacity building initiatives. Support for working capital requirements to meet operational needs. Technical guidance and project formulation assistance from NCDC. Flexible repayment terms tailored to the cash flow patterns of cooperative enterprises.
financial_support: The fund provides term loans and working capital assistance to eligible multi-state cooperative societies. The quantum of financial support is determined based on the viability and scale of the proposed project, subject to the availability of funds and adherence to NCDC's lending norms. Assistance is typically extended as a loan with concessional interest rates and flexible repayment schedules. The exact terms including interest rate, moratorium period, and repayment duration are assessed on a case-to-case basis by the National Cooperative Development Corporation.
application_process: 1. Identify a viable project proposal aligned with the developmental objectives of the fund. 2. Prepare a detailed project report including technical, financial, and economic feasibility analysis. 3. Submit the application along with required documents to the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). 4. NCDC undertakes preliminary scrutiny and field verification of the proposal. 5. The proposal is evaluated by the competent authority within NCDC for approval. 6. Upon approval, a sanction letter is issued outlining the terms and conditions of financial assistance. 7. Loan documentation is executed and disbursement is made in stages as per project progress. 8. Post-disbursement monitoring is conducted to ensure proper utilization of funds.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), Ministry of Cooperation

overview: The Scheme for Agro-Marine Processing and Development (SAMPADA) was approved by the Government of India on 03.05.2017 with a total allocation of Rs. 6000 crore for the implementation period 2016-2020, later renamed as Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY). It is a comprehensive package aimed at creating modern infrastructure with efficient supply chain management from farm gate to retail outlet, boosting food processing sector growth, providing better returns to farmers, doubling farmers' income, creating employment opportunities in rural areas, reducing agricultural wastage, increasing processing levels, and enhancing exports of processed foods. The scheme has seven component schemes including Mega Food Parks, Integrated Cold Chain, Infrastructure for Agro-Processing Clusters, Creation of Backward and Forward Linkages, Creation/Expansion of Food Processing & Preservation Capacities, Food Safety and Quality Assurance Infrastructure, and Human Resources and Institutions.
target_beneficiaries: entrepreneurs; MSME; agri-startups; farmers; food processing units
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component scheme; general eligibility includes entrepreneurs, MSMEs, agri-startups, farmers, and food processing units seeking financial assistance for infrastructure projects under the seven component schemes of PMKSY. Specific criteria are detailed in individual scheme guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid for setting up food processing infrastructure, technical support, capacity building, skill development, research and development support, promotional activities, and operational guidelines for implementation. Benefits include access to modern infrastructure, improved supply chain, reduced post-harvest losses, increased value addition, and market linkages.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as grants-in-aid under the various component schemes of PMKSY. The pattern of release of funds includes two instalments: 50% upon acceptance letter and compliance, and the remaining 50% upon submission of utilization certificate and verification of expenditure. Funds are released through the PFMS EAT module. The scheme leverages investment of Rs. 11,095.93 crore.
application_process: 1. Visit the PMKSY portal or relevant component scheme portal. 2. Check eligibility and guidelines for the specific component scheme. 3. Prepare required documents including project report, land documents, financial statements, etc. 4. Submit Expression of Interest (EOI) or proposal through the online portal. 5. Await scrutiny and evaluation by Technical Committee and Project Approval Committee. 6. Upon approval, submit detailed project report and bank details. 7. Receive approval letter and fulfill pre-disbursement compliances. 8. Receive first instalment (50%) after submission of acceptance letter and compliance documents. 9. Complete project and submit utilization certificate, bank statements, and other required documents. 10. Receive second instalment (50%) after verification of utilization and completion.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round as per EOI notices and scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI)

overview: The National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) Grants scheme provides financial assistance to cooperative societies across India for various activities including marketing, processing, storage, infrastructure development, and support for weaker sections. It operates under the Ministry of Cooperation and offers loans, grants, and subsidies through state governments or directly to eligible cooperatives. The scheme aims to strengthen the cooperative sector by promoting income-generating activities, especially for marginalized groups, and supports integrated development projects.
target_beneficiaries: cooperatives; women cooperatives; SC/ST cooperatives; fishery cooperatives; dairy cooperatives; tribal cooperatives; handloom cooperatives; primary agricultural credit societies (PACS); farmer producer organizations (FPO); farmer producer fishery organizations (FFPO)
eligibility: Cooperatives registered or deemed to be registered under the Cooperative Societies Act, 1912 or under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 1984 or under any other law with respect to cooperative societies for the time being in force in any State, which is engaged in any of the activities mandated to NCDC, are eligible for funding from NCDC. For direct funding, the cooperative should have been in operation for not less than 3 years and should have positive net worth, not less than 100% paid up share capital, i.e. there should be no erosion in the paid-up share capital.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of Term Loan, Investment Loan and Working Capital Loan. Credit linked Subsidy along with Term Loan and Investment Loan. Assistance provided under Central Sector Integrated Scheme on Agricultural Cooperation (CSISAC), other Central Sector Schemes (CSS) and NCDC Sponsored Scheme. Liberal assistance to strengthen and develop cooperatives to the extent of 90-95% of the project cost which may include subsidy component of 15-25% under certain schemes. Support for infrastructure and business development along with appropriate capacity building interventions, with special emphasis on the economic development of rural population.
financial_support: NCDC provides financial assistance through Term Loan, Investment Loan and Working Capital Loan. It also provides credit linked Subsidy along with Term Loan and Investment Loan to cooperative societies. The assistance is provided under the Central Sector Integrated Scheme on Agricultural Cooperation (CSISAC), other Central Sector Schemes (CSS) and NCDC Sponsored Scheme. Subsidy is provided subject to availability from the Government of India (GOI); otherwise equivalent amount is provided as loan in lieu of subsidy on the request of the borrower. The subsidy under CSISAC is for agriculture and allied activities. NCDC funding is based on specific pattern of funding for a given Scheme. For the purpose of funding under the CSISAC, State/Union Territories are divided into three categories: Cooperatively Least Developed States, Cooperatively Under Developed States/UTs, and Cooperatively Developed States/UTs.
application_process: 1. Choose activity/purpose and loan type on the common loan application form. 2. Download the form from the NCDC website. 3. Fill the form completely. 4. Attach required supporting documents. 5. Submit the application to the NCDC office.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) under the Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India

overview: The National Cooperative Exports Limited (NCEL) Scheme is a government initiative aimed at promoting cooperative exports, particularly in the agricultural sector, by leveraging NAFED's infrastructure and expertise. It supports Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) and cooperative societies in accessing international markets through market linkages, quality assurance, and export facilitation. The scheme aligns with the vision of 'Sahakar se Samriddhi' and contributes to doubling farmers' income by enhancing their participation in global value chains.
target_beneficiaries: FPOs; cooperative societies; farmers
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperative societies, and agricultural producer collectives registered under relevant Acts, engaged in production and processing of agricultural commodities for export, with valid documentation and compliance with quality and food safety standards.
benefits: Benefits include access to international markets, technical support for quality compliance, branding and packaging assistance, export documentation facilitation, logistics support, market intelligence, and convergence with other government schemes like FPO promotion and organic farming missions.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through convergence with existing schemes such as the Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs, MIDH, and PSF, including matching equity, grants for infrastructure, and subsidy for certification and branding, though specific quantum under NCEL is not detailed in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Register as an FPO or cooperative society under the relevant Act. 2. Engage with NAFED as the National Implementing Agency for export promotion. 3. Submit product details and quality compliance documents. 4. Undergo capacity building and training on export procedures. 5. Receive support for branding, packaging, and market linkage. 6. Export facilitation through NAFED’s international trade network and portals like e-Samridhi and NAFEX.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED)

overview: The Cooperative Societies Credit Support Scheme by NCDC provides working capital loans to eligible credit cooperatives, modeled on commercial banks' cash credit limits. The scheme offers loans up to Rs.20.00 crore per borrower, repayable on demand, with interest rates decided case-to-case by NCDC's Empowered Committee. It aims to strengthen credit cooperatives through direct or state-government-mediated financing, subject to eligibility criteria and security requirements.
target_beneficiaries: Credit Cooperatives
eligibility: NCDC loan shall be provided to eligible Credit Cooperatives either through the concerned State Government/UT administration or directly to the co-operatives which fulfill the following criteria: (a) The cooperative should have been in operation for not less than 3 years; & (b) The cooperative should have positive net worth, not less than 100% paid up share capital, i.e. there should be no erosion in the paid-up share capital.
benefits: No processing fees for sanction; legal fees for security documentation if any shall be borne by the borrower; no limit on number of withdrawals in a day within the sanctioned limit; any amount within the sanctioned limit may be availed the same working day by intimating prior to 02:00 pm; drawing power assessed quarterly by the concerned Programme Division; interest to be served monthly, quarterly, semi-annually or as agreed upon during sanction; borrower must intimate 90 days prior to validity of sanction regarding renewal or closure.
financial_support: The working capital loan with cc limit shall be sanctioned following procedural guidelines; the loan shall be sanctioned for a period of one year repayable on demand; the upper limit of loan amount sanctioned shall not exceed Rs.20.00 crore per borrower subject to availability of funds; interest rate for the product offering shall be separately decided by the Empowered committee of NCDC on case-to-case basis and conveyed whilst sanction/prior to disbursement and shall be for the entire tenure of sanction (one year), subject to periodical review; interest shall be calculated on the basis of daily closing balance and compounded monthly.
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs.20.00 crore per borrower
application_process: 1. Choose activity/purpose and loan type from the common loan application form. 2. Download the form from NCDC website. 3. Fill the form and submit it along with supporting documents to NCDC office. 4. Submit the application for sanction.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC)

overview: IRCTC Startup Innovation Fund is a scheme under the PSU Support category aimed at fostering innovation and supporting startups through financial and non-financial assistance. The fund is managed by IRCTC, a Mini Ratna PSU under the Ministry of Railways, to encourage entrepreneurial ventures aligned with railway and tourism sectors. It provides funding, mentorship, and market access to eligible startups. The initiative reflects IRCTC's commitment to innovation and collaboration with the startup ecosystem.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups incorporated in India, working on innovative products, services, or processes in domains such as railway catering, tourism, digital ticketing, passenger experience, logistics, or allied sectors, with a focus on scalability and social impact. Preference may be given to startups led by women, SC/ST, or differently-abled entrepreneurs.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grants or equity-free funding, mentorship from IRCTC experts, access to IRCTC's vast user base for pilot testing, potential integration of solutions into IRCTC platforms, branding and visibility through IRCTC channels, and guidance on regulatory and compliance matters.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support through grants or seed funding, with the exact quantum and mechanism determined on a case-by-case basis depending on the startup's stage, innovation potential, and alignment with IRCTC's strategic goals. Funds are disbursed upon milestone achievement and due diligence.
application_process: 1. Visit the official IRCTC website or designated innovation portal. 2. Register as a startup and create a profile. 3. Submit an application detailing the innovation, team, business model, and potential impact. 4. Upload required documents including incorporation proof, PAN, pitch deck, and technical details. 5. Await screening by the IRCTC innovation committee. 6. Shortlisted startups may be invited for a pitch or presentation. 7. Final selection and disbursement of funds post due diligence and agreement signing.
implementing_agency: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited (IRCTC)

overview: The HAL Innovation & Startup Centre is a program by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), a Maharatna PSU under the Ministry of Defence, aimed at fostering innovation and supporting startups in the aerospace and defence sectors. The initiative provides a platform for startups to collaborate with HAL on technology development, testing, and potential integration into HAL's supply chain. It focuses on nurturing indigenous innovation aligned with national defence and aviation priorities.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups working on innovative technologies in aerospace, defence, avionics, materials, MRO, or related domains that align with HAL's technological requirements and Make-in-India initiatives.
benefits: Access to HAL's infrastructure, technical expertise, testing facilities, and potential for technology collaboration, pilot projects, and integration into HAL's supply chain or product development programs.
financial_support: The evidence does not specify any direct financial support, grants, loans, or funding quantum provided under the HAL Innovation & Startup Centre.
application_process: The evidence does not provide a step-by-step application procedure for the HAL Innovation & Startup Centre.
implementing_agency: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)

overview: The Dairy Processing & Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF) is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, with financial support from NABARD and end borrower contributions. The scheme aims to modernize milk processing plants, create additional processing infrastructure, enhance value addition through dairy products, improve efficiency in dairy processing, and strengthen the market position of producer-owned institutions in the organized milk market. It provides financial assistance to eligible end borrowers such as cooperative milk unions, state cooperative dairy federations, multi-state milk cooperatives, milk producer companies, and NDDB subsidiaries for setting up or expanding dairy processing facilities.
target_beneficiaries: cooperative milk unions; state cooperative dairy federations; multi-state milk cooperatives; milk producer companies; NDDB subsidiaries
eligibility: Financial assistance under DIDF will be given to the end borrowers which are financially viable and willing to avail funds and also fulfill the eligibility criteria, as per Operation guidelines of DIDF. Eligible institutions include NDDB and NCDC using the loans from the DIDF to lend to co-operative milk unions, state cooperative dairy federations, multi-state milk cooperatives, milk producer companies, and NDDB subsidiaries.
benefits: The scheme provides financial assistance for modernization and creation of new milk processing facilities, manufacturing facilities for value-added products, milk chilling infrastructure, setting up electronic milk testing equipment, project management and learning, and any other activities related to the dairy sector targeted to contribute to the objectives of DIDF. It enables optimum value realization for milk producers, improves supply of quality milk to consumers, and strengthens the market position of producer-owned institutions.
financial_support: The total outlay for DIDF during 2020-21 is Rs 11184 Crore, of which Rs 8004 crore shall be loan from National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) to National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) and National Cooperative Development Cooperation (NCDC) for end borrowers, Rs 2001 crore shall be end borrowers' contribution, Rs 12 crore would be NDDB/NCDC's share during 3 years 2018-19 to 2022-23, and Rs 1167 crore shall be contributed by DAHD towards interest subvention on repayment for 10 years (2018-19 to 2030-31 with spill over to first quarter of 2031-32). NABARD shall extend loan to NDDB and NCDC at a rate of interest of 6% per annum repayable at quarterly rests. The interest rate to end borrower shall be up to 6.5% per annum (to be charged by NDDB/NCDC) subject to the condition that the difference between the cost of borrowing funds from market (by NABARD) and the rate at which NABARD passes loan on to NDDB/NCDC is not more than 2.5% per annum.
application_process: The application process is not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence. However, based on the scheme structure, end borrowers would typically submit proposals through NDDB or NCDC after meeting eligibility criteria, including financial viability, positive net worth, no defaults to banks/financial institutions, up-to-date audit without adverse observations, and outstanding dues to producer members not exceeding four payment periods. The loan is sanctioned by NABARD to NDDB/NCDC, which then on-lends to eligible end borrowers.
implementing_agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India

overview: The Indian Oil Startup Scheme is a program by Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) aimed at supporting startups through collaboration, innovation, and potential partnerships. The scheme seeks to foster entrepreneurial ventures that align with IOCL's business domains such as energy, petrochemicals, and sustainable technologies. It provides a platform for startups to engage with IOCL for pilot projects, technology validation, and possible scaling opportunities.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups must be registered entities working on innovative solutions in domains relevant to IndianOil's business, including but not limited to energy, petrochemicals, sustainability, and digital technologies. Preference is given to those with scalable models and potential for pilot integration with IOCL operations.
benefits: Selected startups may gain access to IndianOil's technical expertise, infrastructure for pilot testing, mentorship from industry experts, potential for commercial collaboration, and visibility through IOCL's innovation network. The scheme facilitates proof-of-concept validation and scaling opportunities within a corporate ecosystem.
financial_support: The scheme does not specify direct financial grants or equity investment. Support is primarily non-financial, focusing on access to resources, technical guidance, and collaboration opportunities. Any financial engagement would be based on mutually agreed terms for pilot projects or joint development.
application_process: 1. Visit the official IndianOil startup portal at https://iocl.com/startup 2. Register as a startup on the platform 3. Submit a detailed proposal outlining the innovation, its relevance to IndianOil's domains, and expected outcomes 4. Await review by the IndianOil innovation team 5. If shortlisted, participate in discussions for potential pilot or collaboration 6. Upon agreement, proceed with defined milestones and deliverables.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL)

overview: RailTel Innovation Challenge is a program by RailTel Corporation of India Limited, a Navratna PSU under the Ministry of Railways, aimed at fostering innovation by partnering with startups and technology providers. The initiative seeks to empanel business associates who can deliver innovative solutions in areas such as telepresence, cloud services, AI/ML, IoT, and smart city projects. Through this challenge, RailTel intends to collaborate with empaneled partners to co-create and deploy technology solutions on a revenue-sharing or service-based model, leveraging its nationwide ICT infrastructure.
target_beneficiaries: startups; technology providers; MSME; enterprises
eligibility: Any Firm (Limited/Pvt. Limited/LLP/Startup/Proprietary) with incorporation/registration date of at least 6 months old as on the date of application submission. Applicants may use credentials of Parent/Subsidiary/Holding Company subject to undertaking as per Annexure-7.
benefits: Empanelled partners gain access to RailTel's customers across industries, opportunity to co-develop and deploy solutions on revenue-sharing basis, association with a Mini Ratna (Category-I) PSU, and support in scaling innovative solutions using RailTel's infrastructure such as data centers, cloud services, MPLS-VPN, and nationwide fiber network. Partners also benefit from RailTel's physical presence across regions and functional territories for project execution.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or subsidies. Instead, it operates on an empanelment model where selected business partners collaborate with RailTel to execute projects on a revenue-sharing or service-based model. Empanelment fees are non-refundable: Rs 2,00,000 for established and proprietary firms, and Rs 40,000 for start-up firms.
application_process: 1. Prepare application with all required documents as per EOI requirements. 2. Pay empanelment fee via RTGS and attach UTR details. 3. Submit the complete application (single PDF for documents, Excel sheet for Supplier/Customer form, payment details) to baapplications@railtelindia.com. 4. Application undergoes scrutiny for eligibility and compliance. 5. Shortlisted applicants may be contacted for clarification or additional documentation. 6. Final selection leads to issuance of Letter of Empanelment (LOE). 7. Empanelment is valid for 3 years from LOE issuance date.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: RailTel Corporation of India Limited
contact_details: Email: baapplications@railtelindia.com | Contact No: +91 7302880054 (Mr. Rajat Chahar, Marketing Executive/RCIL)

overview: The SAIL Startup & Innovation Policy is a PSU Support scheme by Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) aimed at fostering innovation and supporting startups. The scheme provides a platform for startups to collaborate with SAIL on technological solutions, pilot projects, and innovation challenges. It focuses on areas such as steel manufacturing, sustainability, digital transformation, and operational efficiency. Selected startups may receive mentorship, access to SAIL's infrastructure, and opportunities for proof-of-concept trials.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups registered in India with a valid DPIIT recognition certificate, working on innovative products, services, or technologies in domains such as steel processing, automation, AI/IoT, sustainability, waste management, or related industrial applications. The startup must have a prototype or minimum viable product (MVP) ready for pilot testing.
benefits: Selected startups gain access to SAIL's manufacturing units for pilot testing, technical mentorship from SAIL experts, opportunities to present solutions to SAIL's leadership, potential for long-term collaboration or integration into SAIL's operations, and visibility through SAIL's innovation network. Financial support may be considered on a case-by-case basis for proof-of-concept validation.
financial_support: Financial support, if provided, is determined on a case-by-case basis for proof-of-concept validation and pilot projects. The quantum, type, and mechanism of support are not standardized and depend on the nature of the collaboration and mutual agreement between SAIL and the startup.
application_process: 1. Visit the SAIL official website and navigate to the Startup & Innovation Policy section. 2. Review the eligibility criteria and focus areas. 3. Prepare a detailed proposal including startup profile, problem statement, solution description, stage of development, and expected outcomes. 4. Submit the application via the designated portal or email address provided on the SAIL website. 5. Applications are reviewed by SAIL's innovation committee. 6. Shortlisted startups are invited for presentations or discussions. 7. Final selection is made based on innovation, feasibility, and alignment with SAIL's objectives. 8. Selected startups are notified and guided through the next steps for collaboration.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)

overview: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) is a scheme administered by NABARD to provide financial support for rural infrastructure projects. It aims to bridge the gap in rural infrastructure by financing projects related to agriculture, irrigation, soil conservation, and other rural development initiatives. The fund is contributed by commercial banks and managed by NABARD for disbursement to state governments and other implementing agencies.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; state-owned corporations; local self-governments; NGOs; cooperatives
eligibility: State governments, state-owned corporations, local self-governments, NGOs, and cooperatives are eligible to avail loans under RIDF for rural infrastructure projects. Projects must be technically feasible, economically viable, and socially acceptable, and should fall under the approved list of activities under the fund.
benefits: Long-term financing at concessional interest rates for rural infrastructure projects; support for completion of ongoing projects; contribution to rural employment generation; improvement in agricultural productivity and rural livelihoods; enhanced access to basic rural infrastructure.
financial_support: RIDF provides loans to state governments and implementing agencies for rural infrastructure projects. The loan amount is typically up to 95% of the project cost for special category states and 80-85% for general states, with the balance to be contributed by the state government or implementing agency. The funds are disbursed in installments based on project progress.
application_process: 1. Identify eligible rural infrastructure project under approved RIDF activities. 2. Prepare detailed project report (DPR) including technical, financial, and economic aspects. 3. Submit application through the state government nodal officer to NABARD. 4. NABARD appraises the project for technical feasibility and financial viability. 5. Upon approval, loan agreement is executed. 6. Funds are released in stages based on project progress and utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year based on annual allocations.
implementing_agency: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)

overview: Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) is a Navratna Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, established in 1954 to meet the specialized electronic needs of the Indian Defence. It has grown into a multi-product, multi-technology, multi-unit conglomerate providing state-of-the-art electronic products and systems for the Army, Navy, and Air Force, while also diversifying into non-defence areas such as homeland security, smart cities, e-governance, space electronics, energy storage, solar, network & cyber security, railways & metro solutions, airport solutions, Electronic Voting Machines, telecom products, medical electronics, composites, and software solutions. BEL supports innovation and self-reliance through in-house R&D, collaboration with DRDO, ISRO, academia, and partnerships with MSMEs and start-ups, aligning with the national vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSMEs
eligibility: BEL collaborates with MSMEs and start-ups through its R&D and outsourcing policies, particularly via the Collaborative R&D initiative which seeks Expression of Interest from Companies (including MSMEs and Start-ups) and R&D Institutions (comprising Academia, Research Institutes, R&D organizations and Companies working in niche technologies) in India and abroad for collaborative R&D/Contract Research/Product and Subsystem development programs in the areas of BEL’s operations. Empanelment is based on qualifications, demonstrated experience, patents granted, papers, papers, awards, number of projects completed in the relevant field, etc. for individual experts/consultants, and for R&D institutions and companies: Type of institution, number of years of operation, available manpower expertise, papers published, patents granted, number of projects/processes licensed and commercialized, total number of projects completed in the relevant field, etc.
benefits: BEL provides opportunities for MSMEs and start-ups to engage in collaborative R&D projects, including joint R&D work on assignment or long-term basis through MoUs/long term tie ups; technical consultancy for specific projects; design vetting; design verification; design buying; testing; characterization; specialized engineering software codes; modelling; expert guidance on annual retainership basis. Empanelled partners gain access to BEL’s R&D ecosystem, technology modules, subsystems, and support for product development. BEL also promotes indigenisation, cost reduction, and support for MSMEs and start-ups in alignment with the national vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, as noted in the leadership section where Mr. Kamesh Kasana’s initiatives helped BEL build stronger partnerships, improve delivery timelines, and ensure sustainable business growth.
financial_support: BEL does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies to startups or MSMEs. Instead, it engages them through collaborative R&D and outsourcing mechanisms where work is outsourced based on technical requirements, and payments are made as per agreed terms for services rendered. There is no mention of a fund corpus, grant amount per entity, or direct financial disbursement to external entities in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Visit the BEL website at https://bel-india.in/collaborative-rd/ to access the Collaborative R&D page. 2. Download the 'Response Format for R&D Institution Empanelment' (A-1) or 'Response Format for Individual Consultant Empanelment' (A-2) by clicking the respective links. 3. Complete the format with required details including qualifications, experience, patents, papers, awards, and project history. 4. Submit the completed format along with other required documents via email to collab [at]bel[dot]co[dot]in. 5. BEL will scrutinize the application based on empanelment criteria. 6. If selected, BEL will enter into a specific agreement outlining scope of work, time frame, remuneration, deliverables, and ownership of IPRs for each individual R&D project. 7. A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) or Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) may be signed for long-term collaboration.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Ministry of Defence, Government of India

overview: CSIR Technologies for MSMEs is a scheme under the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) aimed at facilitating the transfer and adoption of CSIR-developed technologies by Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to enhance their competitiveness, innovation capacity, and industrial growth through technology licensing, technical support, and collaborative R&D.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as defined under the MSMED Act, 2006, that are interested in adopting CSIR-developed technologies for commercialization or process improvement.
benefits: Access to CSIR-developed technologies through licensing, technical guidance and support for technology absorption, assistance in scaling up lab-scale processes to industrial scale, joint R&D opportunities, and facilitation of IPR-related matters.
financial_support: Financial support varies based on the technology and agreement terms; may include subsidized licensing fees, shared R&D costs, or project-based funding as mutually agreed between CSIR laboratories and the MSME, subject to technical and commercial evaluation.
application_process: 1. Identify relevant CSIR technology through the CSIR technology portal or CSIR laboratories. 2. Contact the concerned CSIR laboratory or Technology Business Development Group (TBDG). 3. Discuss technology suitability, terms of transfer, and potential collaboration. 4. Negotiate and sign a technology transfer agreement or MoU. 5. Implement the technology with technical support from CSIR as per the agreement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year based on technology availability and mutual agreement.
implementing_agency: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)

scheme_name: She Means Business – Digital Skills for Women
overview: She Means Business – Digital Skills for Women is a global initiative by Meta (Facebook) aimed at empowering women entrepreneurs through digital skills training, mentorship, and networking opportunities. The program focuses on helping women start, grow, and scale their businesses using digital tools and platforms. It provides free online courses, community support, and access to resources tailored to women-led enterprises.
target_beneficiaries: women entrepreneurs
eligibility: Open to women entrepreneurs, aspiring business owners, and women-led small businesses seeking to enhance their digital capabilities and grow their ventures through online platforms.
benefits: Free digital skills training, access to online learning modules, mentorship opportunities, community networking, tools for business promotion on Meta platforms, and guidance on leveraging social media for growth.
financial_support: The program does not provide direct financial support, grants, loans, or subsidies. It focuses on non-financial capacity building through training and mentorship.
application_process: 1. Visit the She Means Business Facebook page or website. 2. Sign up or register for the program using a Facebook account. 3. Access free online courses and training modules. 4. Participate in community events and webinars. 5. Apply learned digital skills to grow your business.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Registration and learning are open year-round.
implementing_agency: Meta (Facebook)

overview: GIZ – DEG India Startup Finance is a financing initiative by GIZ in partnership with DEG (Deutsche Investitions- und Entwicklungsgesellschaft) aimed at supporting startups in India through financial instruments. The scheme provides funding to Indian startups to scale their operations and foster innovation, leveraging GIZ’s expertise in international development and DEG’s experience in private sector financing in emerging markets.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Indian startups that are legally registered entities, demonstrate innovative business models, have potential for scalability and impact, and operate in sectors aligned with sustainable development goals. Preference may be given to startups with social impact or green technology focus.
benefits: Access to growth capital, technical assistance, mentorship, networking opportunities with investors and industry experts, and support for market expansion. The financing is structured to support long-term sustainability and impact measurement.
financial_support: DEG provides debt or quasi-equity financing to eligible Indian startups, with ticket sizes typically ranging from EUR 500,000 to several million euros, depending on the startup’s stage, sector, and funding needs. The financing is disbursed in tranches based on milestone achievement and is accompanied by GIZ’s technical support for capacity building and impact assessment.
application_process: 1. Submit an initial inquiry or proposal through GIZ’s partner channels or DEG’s India office. 2. Undergo preliminary screening based on eligibility and innovation criteria. 3. Submit detailed business plan, financial projections, and impact metrics. 4. Participate in due diligence meetings with GIZ and DEG representatives. 5. Receive term sheet and negotiate financing terms. 6. Sign financing agreement and fulfill pre-disbursement conditions. 7. Receive funds in tranches upon milestone verification.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year based on fund availability and deal flow.
implementing_agency: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in partnership with DEG (Deutsche Investitions- und Entwicklungsgesellschaft)

overview: The ICAR – Agri Startup Grants scheme is an innovation grant program under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) aimed at supporting agri-startups through financial assistance and capacity building.
