Submission includes technical and financial proposals along with required documents. 5. Bids are opened and evaluated as per the evaluation criteria. 6. The selected concessionaire is issued a Letter of Award (LOA). 7. The concessionaire signs the Concession Agreement with NHAI. 8. Financial closure is achieved within the stipulated period. 9. Construction begins as per the agreed schedule.
deadlines: As per bid-specific timelines mentioned in the tender notice
implementing_agency: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)

scheme_name: PM Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) Phase III
overview: PM Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) Phase III is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at consolidating 1,25,000 km of rural roads through upgradation of existing routes to connect habitations to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), Higher Secondary Schools, and Hospitals. The scheme focuses on improving rural connectivity and access to socio-economic services by upgrading existing rural roads to all-weather standards. It is implemented in a mission mode to ensure timely completion and quality execution.
target_beneficiaries: rural habitations; farmers; rural communities
eligibility: The scheme covers rural roads that are part of the Core Network and are required to be upgraded to provide connectivity to habitations with a population of 250+ (in general areas) and 100+ (in tribal, desert, hilly areas, and selected tribal and backward districts) as per Census 2011. Roads must be existing and part of the PMGSY Core Network to qualify for upgradation under Phase III.
benefits: Upgradation of rural roads to all-weather standards with proper drainage and safety features; improved access to markets, education, and healthcare; reduced travel time and vehicle operating costs; enhanced agricultural productivity and market access for farmers; increased rural employment opportunities; better connectivity for emergency services; and overall socio-economic development of rural areas.
financial_support: The scheme is funded through a 60:40 ratio between the Central Government and State Governments (90:10 for Northeastern and Himalayan states). The Central Share is provided as a subsidy to the States for execution of works. Funds are released in instalments based on physical progress verified through the Online Management, Monitoring and Accounting System (OMMAS).
application_process: States identify eligible roads from the Core Network and prepare Detailed Project Reports (DPRs). DPRs are submitted to the respective State Level Standing Committee for approval. Approved DPRs are then forwarded to the Ministry of Rural Development for sanction. Upon sanction, funds are released to the States in instalments. States then tender and execute the works through contracted agencies. Progress is monitored via OMMAS and field inspections.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year based on annual planning cycles and fund availability.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India

overview: The Indian Railways Station Redevelopment Programme (IRSRD) aims to modernize and upgrade railway stations across India through public-private partnerships, leveraging commercial development of station land and airspace to fund infrastructure improvements. The initiative focuses on enhancing passenger amenities, improving safety and accessibility, and transforming stations into world-class transit hubs while maintaining operational efficiency.
target_beneficiaries: passengers; railway users; local communities; private developers
eligibility: The programme invites private sector participation through competitive bidding for station redevelopment projects. Eligible bidders include companies, consortia, and special purpose vehicles (SPVs) with relevant experience in infrastructure development, real estate, urban planning, and construction. Participation is governed by transparent bidding processes managed by Indian Railways Station Development Corporation Limited (IRSDC).
benefits: Passengers benefit from upgraded facilities including waiting areas, sanitation, food courts, retail spaces, and improved circulation. Private developers gain long-term lease rights for commercial development of station premises and airspace. Indian Railways achieves infrastructure modernization without direct budgetary expenditure through land value capture mechanisms.
financial_support: The programme operates on a public-private partnership model where private developers invest in station redevelopment and recover costs through commercial development rights over a concession period. No direct government grants or subsidies are provided; funding is generated through monetization of station land and airspace via commercial real estate development.
application_process: 1. Monitor IRSDC website for tenders and requests for proposals (RFPs) for specific station redevelopment projects. 2. Review project details, eligibility criteria, and bidding documents published in tender notices. 3. Prepare technical and financial bids as per RFP requirements. 4. Submit bids through the designated e-procurement portal before the deadline. 5. Participate in bid opening and evaluation process. 6. If selected, enter into concession agreement with IRSDC and fulfill contractual obligations.
deadlines: Project-specific — varies per tender notice published on the IRSDC website
implementing_agency: Indian Railways Station Development Corporation Limited (IRSDC), a joint venture of Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) and IRCON International Limited

overview: The Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP) provides financial incentives to Indian shipyards for constructing vessels under shipbuilding contracts, with assistance released in stages tied to milestones such as keel laying, launching, delivery, and post-delivery. The policy aims to support the domestic shipbuilding industry, enhance global competitiveness, and promote indigenous manufacturing. It applies to all Indian shipyards and covers contracts signed between April 1, 2016, and March 31, 2026.
target_beneficiaries: Indian Shipyards
eligibility: All Indian shipyards are eligible. Vessels must be constructed and delivered within specified timelines: one or two vessels within four years from contract date; three or four vessels within six years; five or more vessels beyond six years if each subsequent vessel is delivered within one year of the preceding vessel. Specialized vessels follow similar timelines. Extensions of up to one year may be granted for contracts affected by Covid-19 or its variants.
benefits: Financial assistance is released in Indian Rupees in stages: 30% at keel laying (against security instrument), 40% on launching (against security instrument), 30% on delivery, and security instrument released upon final payment by ship owner. Assistance is computed as the product of the applicable rate of financial assistance and the lower of contract price or fair price, converted to INR. Actual payment received may replace contract price if lower.
financial_support: Financial assistance is granted as a monetary incentive based on the rate of financial assistance prevailing on the date of contract, applied to the lower of contract price or fair price (in INR). Payments are released in stages: 30% at keel laying, 40% on launching, 30% on delivery, with security instruments released post-final payment. If budget is unavailable, assistance is prioritized in the subsequent financial year.
application_process: 1. Apply for In-principle Approval as per Annexure-I. 2. Submit application for release of Financial Assistance as per Annexure-II-1 to II-4. 3. Competent Authority scrutinizes application; if deficiencies are found, applicant is given opportunity to rectify. 4. Upon satisfactory compliance, Financial Assistance is released. 5. Claims for stage payments can be submitted during construction based on progress, supported by documentary evidence.
deadlines: Applications for contracts signed between April 1, 2016, and March 31, 2026, are eligible. No rolling basis mentioned; tied to contract dates within validity period.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

overview: The Indian Railways Startup Policy (IRSDC) is a government initiative aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship within the Indian Railways ecosystem by supporting startups that develop solutions for railway operations, infrastructure, safety, and passenger experience. The policy encourages collaboration between Indian Railways and startups through structured engagement, pilot projects, and potential scaling of successful innovations. It seeks to modernize railway systems by leveraging agile, technology-driven solutions from the startup community.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups registered in India under the Companies Act, 2013, LLP Act, 2008, or as a partnership firm, working on innovative products, services, or processes relevant to Indian Railways domains such as rolling stock, infrastructure, signaling, safety, logistics, or passenger amenities.
benefits: Access to Indian Railways’ infrastructure and operational environment for piloting solutions, technical guidance from railway experts, potential for scaling successful pilots into long-term contracts, visibility through IRSDC platforms, and facilitation of regulatory and statutory approvals where required.
financial_support: The policy does not provide direct financial grants or funding to startups; instead, it facilitates non-financial support such as access to testbeds, pilot opportunities, and technical collaboration. Any financial engagement would be based on mutually agreed terms for pilot projects or contracts derived from successful evaluations.
application_process: 1. Visit the IRSDC portal at https://irsdc.gov.in 2. Register as a startup on the portal 3. Submit a detailed proposal outlining the innovation, its relevance to Indian Railways, and implementation plan 4. Proposal undergoes initial screening by IRSDC 5. Shortlisted startups are invited for presentation and evaluation 6. Selected startups enter the pilot phase with relevant railway units 7. Performance is monitored during the pilot 8. Based on outcomes, further collaboration or scaling is considered.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation Limited (IRSDC)

overview: The Coastal Shipping Incentive Scheme is a component of the Sagarmala Programme aimed at promoting coastal shipping as a fuel-efficient, economical, and environment-friendly mode of transport. It seeks to reduce logistics costs for EXIM and domestic trade by encouraging the use of coastal shipping and inland waterways. The scheme supports the development of dedicated coastal berths, bunkering facilities, and hinterland transport infrastructure to facilitate seamless coastal movement. It also promotes the introduction of green technologies like hybrid electric and hydrogen vessels to increase cargo movement on inland waterways.
target_beneficiaries: shipping companies; port operators; logistics providers; MSME
eligibility: Eligibility criteria are not explicitly mentioned in the provided evidence for the Coastal Shipping Incentive Scheme.
benefits: Benefits include reduced transportation costs (coastal shipping costs only Rs. 2.0-3.0 per ton-km by road vs Rs. 0.2-0.3 per ton-km by rail), environment-friendly transport, reduced dependence on fossil fuels, lower emissions in port waters, and support for green shipping initiatives such as the Green Tug Transition Programme (GTTP).
financial_support: Financial support details are not explicitly mentioned in the provided evidence for the Coastal Shipping Incentive Scheme.
application_process: Application process details are not explicitly mentioned in the provided evidence for the Coastal Shipping Incentive Scheme.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

overview: The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) has announced opportunities for startups and private entities to participate in Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) toll highway projects under Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models. These opportunities involve Design, Build, Finance, Operate, and Transfer (DBFOT) models for national highway projects, enabling private sector participation in infrastructure development through toll revenue collection.
target_beneficiaries: startups; private companies; PPP operators; infrastructure developers
eligibility: Private companies, consortia, or special purpose vehicles (SPVs) registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or relevant statutes, with demonstrated technical and financial capacity to undertake highway projects on DBFOT or BOT (Toll) basis, meeting pre-qualification criteria set by MoRTH or NHAI for specific projects.
benefits: Opportunity to develop and operate national highway projects on DBFOT/BOT (Toll) basis, earn revenue through toll collection over concession period, contribute to national infrastructure development, avail tax benefits and incentives under PPP frameworks, and gain long-term operational rights over developed assets.
financial_support: Financial support is not provided as a grant or subsidy; instead, private entities are responsible for financing the project through equity and debt. Revenue is generated through toll collection during the concession period, with financial closure required as part of the bid process.
application_process: 1. Identify upcoming BOT (Toll) highway projects announced by MoRTH or NHAI. 2. Check eligibility and pre-qualification criteria published in the project RFP. 3. Prepare and submit bid documents including technical and financial proposals. 4. Submit bid through the designated portal (e.g., NHAI e-tendering portal) before the deadline. 5. Participate in bid opening and evaluation process. 6. If selected, sign the concession agreement and achieve financial closure. 7. Proceed with land acquisition, clearances, and construction as per agreement.
deadlines: Project-specific; varies per tender. Bids must be submitted before the deadline specified in the individual project's Request for Proposal (RFP).
implementing_agency: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH), Government of India
contact_details: Email: planningmorth@gmail.com | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

overview: The Green Ship Building Incentive Scheme is part of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways' initiatives to promote sustainable shipbuilding in India. It aims to incentivize the construction of environmentally friendly vessels through financial assistance and policy support. The scheme aligns with national goals such as Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 to enhance green shipping and reduce carbon emissions in the maritime sector.
target_beneficiaries: shipyards; MSME; private sector
eligibility: Indian shipyards (including Central Public Sector, State Government, and private sector) constructing vessels eligible under the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS) or Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SbDS), with vessels meeting green shipbuilding criteria such as use of low-emission fuels, hybrid propulsion, or other environmentally sustainable technologies as defined in the scheme guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance for green shipbuilding projects, including subsidies for vessels built with green technologies; support for skill development and technology upgradation; promotion of indigenous manufacturing; enhancement of global competitiveness; and contribution to sustainable blue economy growth.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of subsidies or grants for green shipbuilding projects, with support channeled through the Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS) and Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SbDS), including capital assistance for eligible items and potential funding via Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL).
application_process: 1. Submit application online through the designated portal of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. 2. Provide Detailed Project Report (DPR) and supporting documents including proof of incorporation, audited financial statements, and statutory clearances. 3. Upload affidavit, indemnity bond, and business plan as per annexures. 4. Indicate project start and expected completion dates. 5. Await in-principle approval from the Implementing Agency (Directorate General of Shipping or Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited). 6. Upon approval, proceed with project implementation and submit claims for stage-linked disbursement.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Shipping (DGS) and Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL)

overview: The Steel Scrap Recycling Policy is a government initiative aimed at promoting the recycling of steel scrap to enhance resource efficiency, reduce dependence on raw material imports, and support sustainable steel production in India. It provides a framework for the collection, processing, and utilization of steel scrap in the steelmaking process, encouraging the use of secondary raw materials in electric arc furnaces and induction furnaces. The policy aligns with national goals of circular economy, waste utilization, and decarbonization of the steel sector by reducing carbon emissions associated with primary steel production.
target_beneficiaries: steel producers; MSME; recycling units; steel scrap processors
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include steel producers, MSMEs, recycling units, and scrap processors engaged in the collection, segregation, processing, and supply of steel scrap for use in electric arc furnaces, induction furnaces, and other steelmaking routes, as per guidelines issued by the Ministry of Steel under the Steel Scrap Recycling Policy.
benefits: The policy facilitates access to raw material security by promoting domestic steel scrap utilization, reduces production costs and energy consumption in steelmaking, supports compliance with environmental standards through waste utilization, encourages investment in scrap processing infrastructure, and enables participation in government procurement preferences for domestically produced steel with value addition. It also supports the Green Steel Initiative by lowering carbon emissions via scrap-based steel production routes.
financial_support: The Steel Scrap Recycling Policy does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants. Instead, it enables indirect financial benefits through cost savings in raw material procurement, energy efficiency in electric arc furnace operations, and eligibility under related schemes such as the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Specialty Steel and DMI&SP policy for government procurement preference. Financial support for related activities may be accessed through the Ministry of Steel’s R&D Scheme or PLI Scheme, which offer grants, incentives, or tax benefits as per their respective guidelines.
application_process: 1. Identify eligibility under the Steel Scrap Recycling Policy guidelines issued by the Ministry of Steel. 2. Ensure compliance with quality standards and processing norms for steel scrap as per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and Ministry notifications. 3. Register steel scrap processing or recycling units with relevant state pollution control boards and obtain necessary environmental clearances. 4. Maintain records of scrap collection, processing, and supply to steel plants for audit and verification. 5. Apply for recognition or benefits under linked schemes such as PLI, DMI&SP, or R&D Scheme via the respective portals (e.g., https://research.steel.gov.in/Applicant for R&D, https://www.pli.gov.in for PLI). 6. Submit required documents including mill test certificates, consignment details, and process descriptions. 7. Await verification and approval from the Ministry of Steel or designated agencies.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications and compliance are accepted year-round as per ongoing policy implementation.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Steel, Government of India
contact_details: Email: g.sarathyraja@gov.in | Tele No.: 23061064 (Shri G. Sarathy Raja, Deputy Secretary, Technical Division)

overview: The Private Train Operators Policy is a scheme under the Ministry of Railways that allows private entities to operate passenger trains on Indian Railways network. It aims to introduce competition, improve service quality, and enhance passenger experience through private sector participation in train operations. The policy enables private operators to run trains under specified terms and conditions, contributing to modernization and efficiency in rail services.
target_beneficiaries: private train operators; railway passengers
eligibility: Private entities meeting the criteria set by the Ministry of Railways, including financial capability, technical expertise, and compliance with safety and operational standards, are eligible to apply for operating private trains under the policy. Specific eligibility conditions are defined in the policy documents and tender notices issued by the Railway Board.
benefits: Private train operators benefit from the opportunity to operate trains on Indian Railways network, access to railway infrastructure, potential for revenue generation, and contribution to improved passenger services. Passengers benefit from enhanced service quality, modern amenities, increased train frequency, and competitive fares resulting from private participation.
financial_support: The policy does not involve direct financial support from the government to private operators. Instead, private operators are expected to bear the capital and operational costs of train operations, including procurement of rolling stock, maintenance, and staffing, while paying applicable charges to Indian Railways for use of infrastructure and services as per the agreed terms.
application_process: 1. Monitor tender notices issued by the Railway Board for private train operations. 2. Check eligibility criteria and requirements specified in the tender documents. 3. Prepare and submit the bid as per the instructions in the tender notice. 4. Submit required documents including financial statements, technical proposals, and compliance certificates. 5. Await evaluation and selection process by the Railway Board. 6. Sign the concession agreement upon selection. 7. Fulfill pre-operational requirements such as rolling stock procurement and safety certifications. 8. Commence operations as per the agreed schedule and terms.
deadlines: As per tender notices issued by the Railway Board
implementing_agency: Ministry of Railways, Railway Board

scheme_name: Rail Logistics Policy – Private Freight Terminal
overview: The Rail Logistics Policy – Private Freight Terminal is a policy initiative by the Ministry of Railways aimed at enhancing freight logistics efficiency by encouraging private sector participation in developing and operating freight terminals. It seeks to decongest existing railway infrastructure, improve first and last-mile connectivity, and boosts across the Indian Railways network.
target_beneficiaries: private operators; logistics companies; MSMEs; industries
eligibility: Private companies, consortiums, SPVs, or logistics providers registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or LLP Act, 2008, with net worth as per RBI guidelines, and capable of meeting technical and financial criteria for developing and operating private freight terminals on railway land or siding.
benefits: Access to railway land for terminal development on long-term lease, priority in path allocation for freight trains, customs clearance facilitation, single-window clearance through Indian Railways, potential for revenue sharing, and integration with Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs) and industrial corridors.
financial_support: No direct financial subsidy or grant is provided; support is in the form of land allocation on lease basis, regulatory facilitation, and operational privileges. Private entities bear the capital and operational costs of terminal development and management.
application_process: 1. Identify suitable railway siding or land for terminal development. 2. Submit a detailed project report (DPR) including technical, financial, and operational plans to the concerned Divisional Railway Manager (DRM). 3. Obtain in-principle approval from Railway Board after technical scrutiny. 4. Execute a Lease Agreement for land use. 5. Acquire necessary statutory clearances (environmental, local bodies, etc.). 6. Construct terminal infrastructure as per approved plans. 7. Commission operations and sign a Freight Terminal Agreement for traffic handling.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of land and technical feasibility.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Railways, Railway Board
contact_details: Email: cpio@rb.railnet.gov.in | Helpline: 139 (Rail Madad) | Public Grievance Portal: https://railmadad.indianrailways.gov.in/madad/final/home.jsp

scheme_name: National Steel Policy 2017 – MSME Cluster Support
overview: The National Steel Policy 2017 – MSME Cluster Support is a policy initiative under the Ministry of Steel aimed at boosting domestic steel production and supporting MSMEs in the steel sector. It focuses on enhancing production capacity, improving product quality, and meeting domestic demand to make India self-reliant in steel. The policy targets a crude steel production capacity of 300 million tonnes by 2030-31 and includes measures for raw material security, technological advancement, and sustainability.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: The policy provides policy support and guidance to private manufacturers, MSME steel producers, CPSEs, and encourages adequate capacity additions. Specific eligibility criteria for MSME cluster support under the National Steel Policy 2017 are not detailed in the provided evidence.
benefits: The policy supports self-sufficiency in steel production, development of globally competitive manufacturing capabilities, cost-efficient production and domestic availability of raw materials, facilitation of overseas raw material asset acquisition, and enhancement of domestic steel demand. It also promotes technological advancements, enhances steel quality, and contributes to economic growth.
financial_support: The National Steel Policy 2017 does not specify direct financial support mechanisms such as grants or loans for MSMEs. Financial assistance for R&D in the steel sector is provided under the 'Promotion of Research & Development in Iron & Steel Sector' scheme, which offers up to 50% funding for industrial/commercial organisations, 70% for academic institutions, and up to 40% for pilot/demonstration scale projects, with the budget allocated at around Rs 5-10 Crore per year.
application_process: The application process for MSME cluster support under the National Steel Policy 2017 is not detailed in the provided evidence. For the R&D scheme, applicants must submit proposals via the online portal (https://research.steel.gov.in/Applicant) or email (mosteel-rd@gov.in) in PDF format, following guidelines and formats provided in annexures.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed date for submission of R&D proposals under the Promotion of Research & Development in Iron & Steel Sector scheme.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Steel
contact_details: Email: mosteel-rd@gov.in | Tel: 011-26773364 (for R&D scheme queries)

scheme_name: Kisan Rail for Agri Produce Transport
overview: Kisan Rail for Agri Produce Transport is a scheme introduced by Indian Railways to facilitate the transportation of agricultural produce via dedicated freight trains, aiming to reduce post-harvest losses and improve farmers' income by ensuring timely and efficient movement of perishable goods across the country. The scheme leverages the existing rail network to connect farms with markets, supporting the agricultural supply chain.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; agri-produce transporters; MSME
eligibility: Farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives, agri-businesses, and other entities involved in the production and transportation of agricultural produce are eligible to utilize Kisan Rail services for transporting their goods.
benefits: Kisan Rail offers subsidized freight rates for agricultural commodities, ensures faster and safer transport of perishable goods, provides end-to-end logistics support including loading/unloading assistance, reduces dependency on road transport, minimizes post-harvest losses, and enables farmers to realize better prices by accessing distant markets in a timely manner.
financial_support: The scheme provides a subsidy of up to 50% on the freight charges for transporting fruits and vegetables via Kisan Rail, making it economically viable for small and marginal farmers to use rail logistics for their produce.
application_process: 1. Identify the agricultural produce to be transported and ensure it meets the eligibility criteria for Kisan Rail. 2. Contact the nearest railway freight office or authorized logistics partner. 3. Submit details of the consignment including origin, destination, quantity, and type of produce. 4. Complete the booking process through the Indian Railways freight portal or authorized agent. 5. Prepare the goods for loading as per railway guidelines. 6. Track the shipment using the railway consignment note. 7. Collect the delivered goods at the destination station upon arrival.
deadlines: Rolling basis — services are available throughout the year based on demand and operational feasibility.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Railways, Government of India
contact_details: Email: cpio@rb.railnet.gov.in | Helpline: 139 (for public grievances) | Phone: (011) 23303849

overview: The Plastic Parks Scheme aims to set up need-based Plastic Parks with common infrastructure facilities to promote investment, boost domestic manufacturing, and enhance competitiveness in the plastic industry. It provides financial assistance for developing common infrastructure in Plastic Parks, including internal roads, drainage, water supply, power distribution, and effluent treatment plants. The scheme supports the establishment of plastic processing units and ancillary industries within these parks to create employment and promote sustainable growth in the sector.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; industries; entrepreneurs
eligibility: State Governments or their agencies (including State Industrial Development Corporations) are eligible to apply for setting up Plastic Parks under the scheme. The implementing agency must be a Government of India undertaking or a State Government entity.
benefits: Financial assistance for development of common infrastructure facilities such as internal roads, drainage, water supply, power distribution, street lighting, and effluent treatment plants. The scheme enables plug-and-play facilities for plastic processing units, promotes cluster-based development, and supports sustainable industrial growth with shared infrastructure.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-in-aid up to 50% of the project cost for setting up common infrastructure facilities in Plastic Parks, with a maximum ceiling of INR 40 Crore per Plastic Park. The remaining 50% of the project cost is to be contributed by the State Government or the implementing agency.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 40 Crore per Plastic Park
application_process: 1. State Government or its agency identifies a suitable location for the Plastic Park. 2. Prepares a Detailed Project Report (DPR) including land details, infrastructure plan, and financials. 3. Submits the proposal to the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. 4. The proposal is appraised by a Technical Committee. 5. Upon approval, financial assistance is sanctioned and released in installments based on progress. 6. The implementing agency executes the project and utilizes the grant for common infrastructure development.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per the scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers

overview: The Ministry of Steel provides financial assistance through the Government funded scheme 'Promotion of Research and Development in the steel sector' to pursue R&D addressing technological issues faced by the sector and for indigenous development of processes/technologies. The thrust areas include development of new alternate processes & technologies to address challenges such as climate change (green steel production, H2 based steel production, CCUS etc.), waste utilization, and resource efficiency. The scheme supports R&D work at lab scale, bench scale, and scale-up to pilot/demonstration plants, with financial assistance varying by applicant type: up to 50% for industrial/commercial organisations, up to 70% for academic institutions and national/regional research laboratories, and up to 40% for pilot/demonstration scale projects with the balance met by industrial partners. Joint proposals with other laboratories/institutions/industry are encouraged, and individual innovators and start-ups in the steel sector are granted access to scheme-funded facilities and equipment.
target_beneficiaries: academic institutions; research laboratories; steel companies; MSMEs; individual innovators; start-ups
eligibility: R&D Project Proposals are invited from stakeholders viz. reputed Academic Institutions, Research Laboratories and Indian Steel Companies for pursuing R&D projects for the benefit of the Iron & Steel Sector in the country. The scheme was introduced in the year 2009-10, based on the recommendation of the Working Group for Iron & Steel Industry for the 11th Five Year Plan. Subsequently, the scheme has been continued further and the current approval is till March 2031. The Scheme is of continuous nature since the R&D projects being pursued under the scheme are of varying durations, usually 2-3 years duration and new projects are being approved every year. Further, R&D has very long gestation periods before any fruitful results can be achieved. Accordingly, the scheme needs to be continued further to provide uninterrupted support to the stakeholders on in carrying our R&D for the Iron & Steel sector.
benefits: Financial support for R&D projects, access to scheme-funded facilities and equipment (e.g., at NML and IIMT) for individual innovators and start-ups, provision for joint proposals with other laboratories/institutions/industry, and support for R&D work at lab scale, bench scale, and scale-up to pilot/demonstration plants. The scheme also encourages commercialization and technology development, with a heavy bias towards projects amenable to commercialization, technology development and immediate absorption by the industry.
financial_support: The budget allocated for the scheme is around Rs 5-10 Crore per year. Financial assistance is provided as follows: for Industrial/Commercial organisations pursuing R&D projects with Plan Fund, financial assistance of upto 50% of the total cost is permissible; for Academic Institutions & National/Regional Research Laboratories, financial assistance of upto 70% is permissible (preference given to R&D project having tie-up with user industry); for Pilot/Demonstration Scale R&D projects, financial contribution from Plan Fund will be limited to upto 40% & the balance to be met by the industrial partner; Financial assistance up to 100% for multidimensional team shall be under discretion of Secretary Steel on merit of the proposal. The Ministry shall create a categorized Pool of industrial partners, including MSMEs, aligned with key thrust areas. If a Principal Investigator (PI) cannot secure industry partnership, the Ministry will route the proposal to the relevant pool for review and potential funding/collaboration.
application_process: 1. Applicants are requested to go through guidelines, formats and terms & conditions given as Annexures before submitting the R&D Proposals. 2. R&D Proposals duly signed and forwarded by Head of the Institutions/Organisations/Companies should be uploaded to the Ministry of Steel R & D portal (https://research.steel.gov.in/Applicant) as well as sent in Pdf to mosteel-rd@gov.in. 3. For further queries, contact Technical Division, Ministry of Steel at Tel: 011-26773364. 4. Submission of R&D proposals is continuous and there is no last date for submission of the proposals (open ended).
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Steel
contact_details: Technical Division, Ministry of Steel, Tel: 011-26773364, e-mail: mosteel-rd@gov.in

overview: The Domestic Steel Procurement Preference Policy (DMI&SP) mandates that government procurement of iron and steel products with a minimum value addition of 15%-50% must prioritize domestically manufactured products. The policy applies to all ministries and government departments and their agencies under administrative control. It covers iron and steel products with an estimated value of ₹25 crore or more, with exemptions allowed when domestic production of a specific steel grade is unavailable or insufficient to meet project demand.
target_beneficiaries: domestic steel manufacturers; MSME steel producers; CPSEs
eligibility: Each ministry or government department and all agencies/institutions under their administrative control must comply with the DMI&SP policy notified by the Ministry of Steel. The policy applies to the supply of iron and steel products with a total estimated value of ₹25 crore or more. Exemptions are permitted where specific steel grades are not manufactured domestically or where project demand cannot be met from domestic sources.
benefits: Domestic steel manufacturers benefit from guaranteed procurement preference in government projects, which supports market access, demand creation, and capacity utilization. The policy encourages investment in domestic steel production, promotes self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat), and helps reduce import dependence. It also supports MSMEs and CPSEs by creating a level playing field in government procurement.
financial_support: The policy does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Instead, it creates market opportunities through procurement preference, which can lead to increased sales and revenue for eligible domestic steel manufacturers. Financial benefits are indirect and derived from enhanced order books and capacity utilization.
application_process:
1. Identify if the procurement falls under DMI&SP (iron and steel products with ≥15% value addition and estimated value ≥ ₹25 crore).
2. Check if domestic production of the required steel grade is available and sufficient to meet project demand.
3. If yes, give preference to domestically manufactured iron and steel products in the tender.
4. If domestic supply is inadequate or unavailable, apply for exemption as per policy provisions.
5. Submit procurement details through the respective ministry/department's procurement portal.
6. Maintain records of compliance for audit and monitoring purposes.
deadlines: Based on individual procurement cycles of ministries and departments; no centralized deadline.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Steel
contact_details: Email: gurpreet.gadhok@nic.in | Telephone: (011)-23063355 (Nodal Public Grievance Officer, Ministry of Steel)

scheme_name: PLI Scheme for White Goods (AC & LED)
overview: The PLI Scheme for White Goods (AC & LED) targets manufacturers of components/sub-assemblies of Air Conditioners & LED Lights and offers 4–6% incentive on incremental sales to boost localization, reduce imports, and build a domestic supply chain.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers of components/sub-assemblies of Air Conditioners & LED Lights
eligibility: Manufacturers of components/sub-assemblies of Air Conditioners & LED Lights are eligible under the PLI Scheme for White Goods.
benefits: The scheme offers 4–6% incentive on incremental sales to boost localization, reduce imports, and build a domestic supply chain.
financial_support: The scheme offers 4–6% incentive on incremental sales to boost localization, reduce imports, and build a domestic supply chain.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)

overview: The One Station One Product (OSOP) Scheme is an initiative by Indian Railways to promote local products and artisans by providing them a platform at railway stations to sell their goods. The scheme aims to enhance the livelihood of local communities, promote indigenous crafts, and improve passenger experience by offering region-specific products at stations. It supports the vision of 'Vocal for Local' and encourages entrepreneurship at the grassroots level.
target_beneficiaries: local artisans; self-help groups; MSME; women entrepreneurs; tribal communities
eligibility: Local artisans, self-help groups, cooperatives, NGOs, and MSMEs producing indigenous or region-specific products are eligible to participate in the OSOP scheme. Preference is given to products that reflect the cultural, culinary, or artisanal heritage of the station's locality.
benefits: Selected participants get allocated space at designated railway stations to display and sell their products. They benefit from increased visibility, direct access to a large passenger footfall, and opportunities for business growth. The scheme provides non-financial support such as training in packaging, branding, and customer service, along with facilitation for digital payments and marketing through Indian Railways' channels.
financial_support: The OSOP scheme does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants. Instead, it offers nominal or concessional licensing fees for stall allocation, with revenue sharing models where applicable. Indian Railways facilitates logistics and infrastructure support, but primary investment in product development and inventory is borne by the beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Identify the nodal officer or station manager at the respective railway station. 2. Submit a proposal detailing the product, its local significance, production capacity, and business plan. 3. Provide samples and documentation such as business registration, GST details, and product photographs. 4. Await evaluation by the station-level committee. 5. Upon approval, sign an agreement for space allocation and comply with operational guidelines. 6. Begin operations after receiving clearance from railway authorities.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on station availability and product suitability.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Railways, Government of India
contact_details: Email: railwayboard@indianrailways.gov.in | Helpline: 139 (Rail Madad) | Contact Us: https://indianrailways.gov.in/contactUs.html

scheme_name: Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Region (PCPIR)
overview: The Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Region (PCPIR) is a government initiative aimed at promoting investment in the chemicals and petrochemicals sector by developing integrated investment regions with world-class infrastructure. It seeks to create a conducive environment for manufacturing and export-oriented units through policy support, infrastructure development, and fiscal incentives. The scheme encourages public-private partnerships and aims to boost domestic value addition and employment generation in the sector.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturing units; investors; MSME; large industries
eligibility: Eligible entities include companies, consortia, or special purpose vehicles (SPVs) proposing to set up units in the chemicals, petrochemicals, and petroleum sectors within the designated PCPIR areas. The project must involve substantial investment and contribute to value addition and employment generation.
benefits: Benefits include fiscal incentives such as tax exemptions, customs duty concessions, and reimbursement of state taxes; infrastructure support like road, rail, port, and utility linkages; single-window clearance for approvals; and facilitation of land acquisition and statutory clearances through the SPV mechanism.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through viability gap funding (VGF) for infrastructure development, central government grants for master planning, and facilitation of access to loans from financial institutions. The scheme does not provide direct subsidies to units but enables cost reduction through infrastructure and policy support.
application_process: 1. State government submits an in-principle application to DPIIT in the prescribed format. 2. DPIIT examines the application and forwards it to the Commerce & Industry Minister for in-principle approval. 3. Upon in-principle approval, the state government submits a detailed application for final approval along with required documents. 4. The application is reviewed by a High-level Committee chaired by the Secretary, DPIIT. 5. Final approval is granted by the Commerce & Industry Minister. 6. The NIMZ is notified in the official gazette by DPIIT.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: The National Urban Innovation Stack (NUIS) is a digital infrastructure initiative designed to support urban innovation by providing a unified platform for data, services, and applications across Indian cities. It aims to enable seamless integration of urban systems, foster innovation in smart city solutions, and improve governance through technology-driven approaches. NUIS serves as a foundational layer for urban stakeholders including startups, municipal bodies, and technology developers to build and deploy scalable urban applications.
target_beneficiaries: startups; technology developers; municipal corporations; urban local bodies
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include startups, technology companies, urban local bodies, municipal corporations, and academic institutions working on urban innovation solutions that can integrate with the NUIS platform. Entities must demonstrate alignment with national urban development goals and possess the technical capability to build or deploy applications on the stack.
benefits: Access to standardized urban data sets and APIs, technical support for integration with NUIS, opportunities for pilot projects in smart cities, visibility through government urban innovation networks, and potential for scaling solutions across multiple cities. Financial support may be available through linked innovation funds or challenge grants administered via partner agencies.
financial_support: While NUIS primarily provides technical and platform-based support, financial assistance for eligible innovators may be accessed through associated urban innovation funds, challenge grants, or incubator programs linked to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs or Smart Cities Mission, subject to separate eligibility and application processes.
application_process: 1. Visit the NUIS portal at nuisnet.gov.in to understand platform capabilities and documentation. 2. Register your entity or solution on the portal if required for access. 3. Review API documentation, data sets, and integration guidelines available on the platform. 4. Develop or adapt your urban solution to be compatible with NUIS standards. 5. Submit your solution for validation or listing through the portal’s innovation submission interface. 6. Await review by the NUIS governance team for approval and potential inclusion in the urban innovation registry.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

scheme_name: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL) Overseas Mineral Support
overview: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL) is a joint venture company established by three Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) under the Ministry of Mines to ensure supply of critical and strategic minerals to the Indian domestic market. The company focuses on identifying, acquiring, developing, processing, and commercializing overseas mineral assets of strategic and commercial importance to India. KABIL aims to build a sustainable mineral resource base for the country through overseas investments and partnerships.
target_beneficiaries: Indian industries; manufacturing sector; strategic mineral users
eligibility: KABIL is a joint venture company formed by CPSEs under the Ministry of Mines. The scheme operates through KABIL as an implementing entity; direct beneficiary eligibility is not specified in the provided evidence as it focuses on corporate-level overseas mineral asset acquisition rather than individual or MSME-level support.
benefits: Secured supply chain for critical and strategic minerals, enhanced mineral security for India, access to overseas mineral assets, potential for value addition and downstream processing, reduced import dependence, and strengthened international partnerships in the mineral sector.
financial_support: KABIL functions as a joint venture company with equity participation from its promoter CPSEs. Financial support is structured through investments in overseas mineral asset acquisition, development, and commercialization activities. The specific quantum, type, and mechanism of financial support per entity or project are not detailed in the provided evidence.
application_process: The application process is not detailed in the provided evidence. KABIL undertakes identification, negotiation, and acquisition of overseas mineral assets through its corporate structure and joint venture mechanisms.
implementing_agency: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd (KABIL), a joint venture company of Central Public Sector Enterprises under the Ministry of Mines, Government of India

overview: The Critical Minerals Mission – Startup Support is a component of the Ministry of Mines' Science and Technology Programme, specifically under the Promotion of Research and Innovation in Startups and MSMEs in Mining, Mineral Processing, Metallurgy and Recycling Sector (S&T-PRISM). It aims to provide seed support to deserving startups and individual innovators in the critical minerals value chain, including exploration, extraction, processing, and recycling. The scheme is implemented through the release of funds to startups, MSMEs, and individual innovators to ensure timely availability of financial support for innovation in the critical minerals sector.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSMEs; individual innovators
eligibility: Startups, MSMEs, and individual innovators engaged in mining, mineral processing, metallurgy, and recycling sector, particularly those working on critical minerals and energy critical elements, are eligible for support under the S&T-PRISM programme of the Ministry of Mines.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grants for research and development projects, prototype development, technology validation, and market linkage. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, access to Ministry of Mines' scientific institutions, networking opportunities with industry and academia, and facilitation of collaborations for scaling innovations.
financial_support: Under the S&T-PRISM programme, funds are released to startups, MSMEs, and individual innovators to support research and innovation projects. The exact quantum and mechanism of financial support are determined based on project proposals and are subject to approval by the Ministry of Mines' expert committees.
application_process: 1. Submit project proposal under the S&T-PRISM programme of the Ministry of Mines. 2. Proposal is reviewed by expert committees for technical feasibility and innovation potential. 3. Shortlisted applicants are invited for presentation or interview. 4. Final selection is made based on evaluation criteria. 5. Approved projects receive grant sanction and fund release. 6. Progress is monitored through periodic reports and site visits.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round as per announcements under S&T-PRISM.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Mines, Government of India

overview: The Exploration Licence for Private Players is a scheme introduced under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2023, which empowers the Central Government to auction exploration licences for critical and deep-seated minerals. The scheme allows private sector participation in reconnaissance and prospecting operations for minerals listed in the new Seventh Schedule of the Act. Exploration licences are granted through a transparent, non-discretionary online auction process, with a validity of 5 years extendable by another 2 years.
target_beneficiaries: private companies; startups; MSME
eligibility: Comply with eligibility conditions specified in Section 5 of the MMDR Act: Indian National and Company Registered under Companies Act, 1956. Maximum area limit: One or more exploration licences covering a total area of more than 5000 Sq Km. Net worth requirement for Exploration Licence: Bidder should have net worth of more than or equal to Rs. 25 Crore.
benefits: Opportunity to undertake reconnaissance and prospecting for critical and deep-seated minerals; access to National Mineral Exploration Trust (NMET) funding for partial reimbursement of exploration expenses (up to 50% of direct costs with ceilings ranging from ₹1.50 Crore to ₹10.00 Crore depending on activity type); potential for higher reimbursement (up to 60%) if G2 blocks are handed over for auction and successfully auctioned within three years; seamless access to geo-scientific data via National Geoscience Data Repository (NGDR); 100% FDI allowed under automatic route.
financial_support: Scheme for partial reimbursement of exploration expenses from National Mineral Exploration Trust (NMET) for holders of Exploration Licence granted through auction: 50% of direct costs reimbursed for geological mapping and sampling (max ₹1.50 Crore), geophysical investigations (max ₹3.00 Crore), exploratory drilling (max ₹10.00 Crore), chemical and petrological analysis/mineral beneficiation (max ₹2.50 Crore), research collaboration/consultancy/advisory (max ₹1.50 Crore), and logistics (max ₹1.50 Crore, subject to ₹30 Lakhs per year). If EL holder hands over G2 block(s) for auction within three years and they are successfully auctioned, reimbursement increases to 60% of direct costs with increased ceilings.
application_process: 1. State/Central Government issues notice inviting tender to commence auction process and identify/demarcate area. 2. Submission of Technical Bids and Initial Price Offer (IPO) as percentage of value of mineral despatched. 3. Top 50% technically qualified bidders (TQB) or 5 whichever is higher proceed to Round II. 4. If TQBs < 3, auction process annulled. 5. Opening of IPO and live forward auction with minimum increment of 0.05%. 6. At least one Final Price Offer (FPO) required for successful auction. 7. Bidder submitting highest FPO declared as Preferred Bidder (PB). 8. If no qualified bidder submits FPO, auction annulled. 9. For second attempt, terms remain same as first annulled attempt.
deadlines: Auctions conducted as per notices issued by State/Central Government; no fixed rolling window specified in evidence.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Mines, Government of India
contact_details: Email: ngawards-mines@gov.in | Telefax: 011-23385329 (based on National Geoscience Awards contact, as no specific scheme contact provided)

overview: The Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) Policy is a framework under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 that allows private sector participation in mining operations through a contractual model where the MDO is responsible for developing and operating mines on behalf of the mineral concession holder. The policy aims to enhance efficiency, bring in technical expertise, and ensure optimal utilization of mineral resources by leveraging private sector capabilities in mine development and operations. It is designed to promote transparency, accountability, and sustainable mining practices while reducing the burden on government agencies for operational management.
target_beneficiaries: private sector companies; mine developers and operators; mineral concession holders
eligibility: The Mine Developer and Operator (MDO) must be a company registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or any other applicable law, with the technical and financial capability to undertake mine development and operations. The MDO must comply with the eligibility conditions specified under Section 5 of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, including being an Indian national or a company incorporated in India. The MDO must also meet the net worth requirements as per the Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2015, depending on the type of concession (mining lease, composite licence, or exploration licence) being operated.
benefits: The MDO model provides access to private sector expertise in mine planning, development, and operations, leading to improved efficiency, safety, and productivity. It ensures timely execution of mining projects, better resource utilization, and adherence to statutory and environmental norms. The mineral concession holder benefits from reduced operational burden, assured royalty payments, and compliance with legal obligations. The MDO earns revenue through pre-agreed fees or profit-sharing mechanisms as per the MDO agreement, ensuring returns on investment while promoting sustainable mining practices.
financial_support: Under the MDO Policy, financial arrangements are contractual and based on mutual agreement between the mineral concession holder and the MDO. Compensation to the MDO is typically structured as a fixed fee per tonne of mineral extracted, a percentage of the gross revenue, or a hybrid model, as defined in the MDO agreement. There is no direct government financial support or subsidy under this policy; all financial flows are between the concession holder and the MDO. The policy enables cost recovery and profit generation for the MDO based on operational performance and agreed terms.
application_process: 1. Identify a mineral concession holder seeking to engage an MDO for mine development and operations. 2. The mineral concession holder invites bids or enters into negotiations with eligible MDO entities. 3. The MDO submits a technical and financial proposal detailing its capability, work plan, and proposed financial terms. 4. The concession holder evaluates the proposal based on technical competence, experience, and financial viability. 5. Upon selection, a formal MDO agreement is executed outlining roles, responsibilities, financial terms, timelines, and performance metrics. 6. The MDO commences mine development activities, including land acquisition, clearances, infrastructure setup, and mining operations. 7. Regular monitoring and reporting are conducted by the concession holder or an appointed third party to ensure compliance with the agreement and regulatory requirements. 8. Payments to the MDO are made as per the agreed schedule, based on milestones achieved or mineral dispatch.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted as and when mineral concession holders invite bids or seek MDO engagement.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Mines, Government of India

overview: The Metro Rail Policy – Private Participation is a framework under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) that enables private sector involvement in metro rail projects through public-private partnerships (PPPs), equity participation, and financial structuring. It aims to leverage private investment for urban rail infrastructure while ensuring policy compliance, safety standards, and institutional oversight. The policy supports metro rail implementation across Indian cities by defining roles of central and state governments, special purpose vehicles (SPVs), and financing mechanisms including grants, loans, and subordinate debt.
target_beneficiaries: private sector entities; public-private partnerships (PPPs); special purpose vehicles (SPVs); urban local bodies (ULBs); state governments
eligibility: Eligible entities include central and state government-owned Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) in 50:50 joint ventures, private sector partners in PPP arrangements, and financial institutions providing loans. Applicants must comply with legal frameworks under The Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978, The Metro Railways (Operation & Maintenance) Act, 2002, and the Railways Act, 1989. Private participation requires adherence to MoHUA guidelines on standardization, indigenization, and corporate governance, with SPVs bound by central government policy directions.
benefits: Financial benefits include access to central assistance in the form of equity, subordinate debt, and grants; leveraging of market-based finance such as loans and bonds; and credit repayment guarantees. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance from MoHUA, safety certification by Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety, institutional support via High Powered Committees, and policy coordination for integrated urban transport planning. The policy also enables capacity building, technology adoption, and green transport initiatives like cycle sharing facilities at metro stations.
financial_support: Financial support is structured as catalytic central assistance (CA) to leverage larger market-based investments. For metro rail projects, central assistance is provided as equity and subordinate debt by the Government of India (GoI), typically up to 50% of project cost in joint ventures with state governments. External funding from bilateral/multilateral agencies may cover up to 60% of project cost. Central assistance is released in tranches linked to project milestones, with cost escalation due to price or exchange rate variations borne by the state government. GoI does not fund procurement of additional rolling stock beyond the sanctioned project cost.
application_process: 1. Identify metro rail project alignment and prepare Detailed Project Report (DPR). 2. Form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) as a 50:50 joint venture between Government of India and respective State Government. 3. Secure approvals from MoHUA, including legal compliance under Metro Railway Acts and safety certification. 4. Obtain sanction from the Union Cabinet detailing financing pattern, institutional arrangements, and conditions. 5. Sign tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between GoI, State Government, and SPV. 6. Arrange financing: central assistance (equity/subordinate debt), state contribution, and loans from bilateral/multilateral agencies. 7. Implement project under SPV with oversight from High Powered Committee chaired by Chief Secretary of State Government. 8. Ensure compliance with reforms such as Urban Transport Fund (UTF), fare revision mechanisms, and integrated ticketing. 9. Monitor progress via National Apex Committee (NAC) and State Level Technical Committee (SLTC). 10. Release central assistance in tranches (30%, 50%, 20%) based on physical and financial progress.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round based on project readiness and sanction timelines.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
contact_details: Email: mohua@nic.in | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

scheme_name: PM SVANidhi Plus (Micro Credit for Street Vendors)
overview: PM SVANidhi Plus (Micro Credit for Street Vendors) is a special micro-credit facility launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to provide collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors. The scheme aims to support urban street vendors affected by economic hardships, enabling them to resume livelihood activities through accessible credit. It offers loans in tranches with increasing amounts upon successful repayment, along with digital transaction incentives and credit card facilities for eligible beneficiaries.
target_beneficiaries: street vendors
geographic_scope: Pan-India (limited to notified States/UTs under Street Vendors Act, 2014)
eligibility: The scheme is available for beneficiaries belonging to only those States/UTs which have notified rules and scheme under Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014. Vendors are categorized into four groups based on survey coverage and documentation: (A) Vendors with Certificate of Vending or ID card from ULB/Town Vending Committee; (B) Vendors covered in ULB survey but without CoV/ID card; (C) Vendors left out of ULB-led survey or who started vending after survey completion, with subcategories based on Letter of Recommendation (LoR) or Covid assistance/association membership; (D) Peri-urban/rural area vendors vending in ULB geographical limits, similarly subdivided based on LoR or declaration of Covid assistance/association membership.
benefits: Collateral-free working capital loans in three tranches (₹10,000, ₹20,000, ₹50,000); PM SVANidhi Credit Card facility for second tranche repaid vendors; digital transaction cashback incentives; vendor mobility (ULB transfer) facility to update vending location; access to Udyam Assist for MSME registration; eligibility for PRAISE Awards (national and state level); ability to apply through Common Service Centres (CSCs); doorstep credit delivery via lending partners.
financial_support: The scheme provides micro-credit in three progressive tranches: first loan of up to ₹10,000, second loan of up to ₹20,000 upon timely repayment of first, and third loan of up to ₹50,000 upon repayment of second. Loans are disbursed through participating banks (including SBI, Bank of Baroda, Union Bank of India, PNB, Indian Bank) and administered via Urban Local Bodies. Total disbursed amount as per portal data is ₹1,39,25,036 (in thousands, i.e., ₹1,392.50 crores approximately). Interest subsidy of 7% per annum is credited to beneficiaries' accounts on a quarterly basis through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
application_process: 1. Check Eligibility: Understand the loan application requirements and determine your vendor category (A, B, C1, C2, D1, D2) based on survey status and documentation. 2. Apply Online: Ensure your mobile number is linked to your Aadhaar for e-KYC validation. 3. Get Digital Approval: Check your eligibility status as per scheme rules after submitting the application with required documents. Applicants can apply directly on the portal or through a Common Service Centre (CSC).
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

overview: The Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) is a centrally sponsored scheme under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) designed to catalyze market-based financing for urban infrastructure projects. It provides Central Assistance (CA) as catalytic support to leverage larger investments from bonds, bank loans, and public-private partnerships (PPPs). The fund supports projects across three verticals: 'Cities as Growth Hubs', 'Creative Redevelopment of Cities', and 'Water and Sanitation', with a focus on Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) infrastructure development as an admissible project type.
target_beneficiaries: Urban Local Bodies (ULBs); States; Union Territories (UTs)
eligibility: All States and UTs are eligible to participate in UCF with a specific focus on strengthening Tier II and Tier III cities. Eligible categories include: all cities with a projected 2025 population of 10 lakh or more; capital cities of State/UT not included in the first category; major industrial cities (Manufacturing & Services) with a projected 2025 population of 1,00,000 or more; and all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) in Hilly States/UTs, Northeastern States, and ULBs with population below 1,00,000 in other States/UTs. As per the guidelines, all ULBs are eligible to participate in UCF.
benefits: Central Assistance (CA) acts as catalytic support to leverage market-based financing from bonds, bank loans, and PPPs. The fund enables structured project implementation, timely execution, and financial viability of urban infrastructure projects. It supports capacity building at national, State/UT, and city levels through the Project Preparation and Capacity Building Fund (PPCBF). The Credit Repayment Guarantee Sub-Scheme (CRGSS) enhances creditworthiness and facilitates market borrowing. Projects must be designed as part of a comprehensive, integrated intervention with well-structured implementation plans to deliver large-scale transformative impact.
financial_support: The Urban Challenge Fund provides a total Central Assistance (CA) of ₹1,00,000 crore over the Mission period (FY 2025–26 to FY 2030–31, extendable by three years). The CA is structured as: ₹90,000 crore for the Project Fund, ₹5,000 crore for the Project Preparation and Capacity Building Fund (PPCBF), and ₹5,000 crore for the Credit Repayment Guarantee Sub-Scheme (CRGSS). The CA for projects is limited to 25 percent of the cost of bankable projects, with a stipulation that at least 50 percent of the project cost must be funded from bonds, bank loans, and PPPs. Fund release occurs in tranches: first tranche (30%), second tranche (50%), and third tranche (20%) based on physical and financial progress.
application_process: 1. States/UTs submit project proposals under the three UCF verticals: Cities as Growth Hubs, Creative Redevelopment of Cities, and Water and Sanitation (including TOD infrastructure development). 2. Proposals undergo appraisal at national level by the National Apex Committee (NAC) and National Project Management Unit. 3. Independent Review and Monitoring Agencies (IRMA) evaluate projects for technical and financial viability. 4. Upon approval, funds are released in tranches: 30% first tranche upon sanction, 50% second tranche after utilization of at least 70% of first tranche, and 20% third tranche after utilization of at least 70% of second tranche and 100% of first tranche. 5. State/UT level implementation involves State High Powered Steering Committee (SHPSC), State Level Technical Committee (SLTC), and ULB/Implementing Agency. 6. Project Development and Management Consultant (PDMC) or Project Preparation and Support Unit assists in planning and execution. 7. Monitoring occurs at national and state levels through NAC, NAC, IRMA, SHPSC, SLTC, and ULB.
deadlines: The Mission will be implemented from Financial Year (FY) 2025–26 to FY 2030–31, extendable by three years. Applications are accepted during the Mission period as per annual guidelines and fund allocation cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

overview: The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) is a reform-based and results-linked scheme launched by the Government of India to improve the operational efficiencies and financial sustainability of power distribution companies (DISCOMs) across the country. It aims to reduce Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses to pan-India levels of 12-15% by 2024-25 and eliminate the gap between average cost of supply and average revenue realized (ACS-ARR) by 2024-25. The scheme provides financial assistance to DISCOMs for prepaid smart metering, distribution infrastructure upgradation, and system strengthening works. It is implemented through a central sector scheme with funding support from the Government of India and participation from state governments and DISCOMs.
target_beneficiaries: power distribution companies (DISCOMs); state power departments; state governments
eligibility: All power distribution companies (DISCOMs) and power departments owned by state governments or union territories are eligible to participate in the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS). Participation is contingent upon signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of Power, Government of India, and agreeing to the scheme's reform milestones, financial discipline parameters, and performance benchmarks. State governments must provide necessary guarantees and commitments for loan repayment and subsidy disbursement as per the scheme guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of grants and loans for prepaid smart metering, distribution infrastructure upgradation, loss reduction works, and system strengthening. Support for installation of smart meters, feeder segregation, underground cabling, and IT/OT systems. Technical guidance and monitoring through a centralized project management framework. Incentives for achieving pre-defined performance targets related to loss reduction, billing efficiency, and revenue collection. Facilitation of convergence with other central and state government schemes for holistic development of the power distribution sector.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support through a combination of grant and loan components. For prepaid smart metering, a grant of up to 60% of the cost is provided, with the remaining 40% arranged by the DISCOM through loans or own funds. For distribution infrastructure works, including feeder segregation, system strengthening, and loss reduction, a grant of up to 50% of the project cost is available, with the balance to be arranged by the DISCOM. The financial assistance is disbursed in tranches linked to the achievement of project milestones and performance indicators verified by independent agencies. The overall funding pattern includes central government grant, state government contribution, and DISCOM's own equity or loan component.
application_process: 1. State government or DISCOM prepares a Detailed Project Report (DPR) for smart metering and distribution infrastructure works as per RDSS guidelines. 2. The DPR is submitted to the nodal agency designated by the Ministry of Power for technical appraisal. 3. Upon approval, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) is signed between the Ministry of Power, state government, and the DISCOM. 4. The project is sanctioned by the Inter-Ministerial Monitoring Committee (IMMC) based on the appraised DPR. 5. Funds are released in installments linked to physical progress and achievement of pre-defined milestones. 6. Third-party inspection agencies verify the quality and quantity of works before subsequent fund releases. 7. Performance is monitored against key indicators such as AT&C loss reduction, ACS-ARR gap, and metering coverage.
deadlines: Projects under RDSS are to be completed within a stipulated timeline, generally 24-30 months from the date of sanction, with the overall scheme target to achieve objectives by 2024-25. Fund utilization and performance assessment are subject to annual review and mid-term evaluation.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Power, Government of India

scheme_name: PM Surya Ghar Subsidy – Rooftop Solar
overview: The PM Surya Ghar Subsidy – Rooftop Solar scheme is a government initiative under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy to promote the installation of rooftop solar systems across India. It provides financial subsidies to residential consumers for adopting solar energy, aiming to reduce electricity costs and increase renewable energy usage. The scheme operates through a national portal that facilitates application, approval, and subsidy disbursement processes.
target_beneficiaries: residential consumers
eligibility: Residential consumers who own or have authority to install rooftop solar systems on their property are eligible. The beneficiary must be an individual household owner or resident welfare association applying for solar installation on a self-owned or occupied residence.
benefits: Financial subsidy on installation costs, reduced electricity bills through self-generation, potential income from excess power export via net metering, low maintenance and long lifespan of solar systems, contribution to carbon footprint reduction.
financial_support: The scheme provides a central financial subsidy directly credited to the beneficiary's bank account after installation and inspection. The subsidy amount varies based on system capacity and is disbursed through the implementing agency upon verification.
application_process: 1. Visit the national portal at https://pmsuryaghar.gov.in 2. Register as a beneficiary using mobile number and email 3. Log in and fill the application form with property and consumer details 4. Upload required documents including proof of ownership and identity 5. Select an empaneled vendor for solar installation 6. Submit the application for technical feasibility check 7. Upon approval, proceed with installation by the selected vendor 8. After installation, submit completion report and inspection request 9. Once inspected and approved, subsidy is disbursed to the beneficiary's bank account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to fund availability.
implementing_agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana Urban Special Window
overview: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana Urban Special Window is a scheme launched by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on April 8, 2015 for providing loans up to 10 lakh (20 lakh for those entrepreneurs who have availed and successfully repaid previous loans under the 'Tarun' category) to the non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises. These loans are classified as MUDRA loans under PMMY and are given by Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, MFIs and NBFCs. The borrower can approach any of the lending institutions mentioned above or can apply online through the portal www.udyamimitra.in. Under the aegis of PMMY, MUDRA has created four products namely 'Shishu', 'Kishor', 'Tarun' and 'TarunPlus' to signify the stage of growth / development and funding needs of the beneficiary micro unit / entrepreneur and also provide a reference point for the next phase of graduation / growth.
target_beneficiaries: non-corporate; non-farm; small/micro enterprises; entrepreneurs; MSME
eligibility: Any Indian Citizen who has a business plan for a non-farm income generating activity such as manufacturing, processing, trading or service sector whose credit need is up to 20 lakh can approach either a Bank, MFI or NBFC for availing of MUDRA loans under PMMY. The usual terms and conditions of the lending agency may have to be followed for availing of loans under PMMY. The lending rates are as per the RBI guidelines issued in this regard from time to time.
benefits: MUDRA loans are extended for a variety of purposes which result in income generation and employment creation. The loans are extended mainly for: Business loan for Vendors, Traders, Shopkeepers and other Service Sector activities; Working capital loan through MUDRA Cards; Equipment Finance for Micro Units; Transport Vehicle loans for commercial use only; Loans for agri-allied non-farm income generating activities, e.g. pisciculture, bee keeping, poultry farming, etc.; Tractors, tillers as well as two wheelers used for commercial purposes only. MUDRA Card is a debit card issued against the MUDRA loan account, for working capital portion of the loan.
