The borrower can make use of MUDRA Card in multiple drawals and credits, so as to manage the working capital limit in cost-efficient manner and keep the interest burden minimum. MUDRA Card also helps in digitalization of MUDRA transactions and creating credit history for the borrower. MUDRA Card can be operated across the country for withdrawal of cash from any ATM / micro ATM and also make payment through any 'Point of Sale' machines.
financial_support: MUDRA is a refinancing Institution. MUDRA does not lend directly to the micro entrepreneurs / individuals. Mudra loans under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) can be availed of from nearby branch office of a bank, NBFC, MFIs etc. Borrowers can also now file online application for MUDRA loans on Udyamimitra portal (www.udyamimitra.in). The refinance is available for term loan and working capital loan up to an amount of 20 lakh per unit. The eligible Banks/NBFCs/MFIs, who comply with the requirements as notified, can avail refinance from MUDRA for the loans given by them for eligible MUDRA compliant activities under Shishu, Kishore, Tarun and Tarun Plus categories.
application_process: 1. Approach any of the lending institutions mentioned above (Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, MFIs and NBFCs) or apply online through the portal www.udyamimitra.in. 2. File online application for MUDRA loans on Udyamimitra portal (www.udyamimitra.in). 3. Avail refinance support from MUDRA for the loans given by them for eligible MUDRA compliant activities under Shishu, Kishore, Tarun and Tarun Plus categories. 4. Utilize the loan for income generating activities such as manufacturing, processing, trading, service sector and agri-allied activities.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd. (MUDRA)

overview: The National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) is a contactless smart card initiative under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) that enables seamless travel across different modes of public transport (metro, bus, suburban railways) and facilitates retail payments. It aims to integrate urban transport systems by providing a unified, interoperable payment solution for commuters. The card supports offline transactions and is designed to promote digital inclusion and ease of mobility in urban areas.
target_beneficiaries: general public; commuters; urban residents
eligibility: The National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) is available to all residents and commuters in India who wish to use a unified contactless card for public transport and retail payments. There are no specific eligibility restrictions based on income, age, or occupation; the card is issued by authorized banks and transit agencies upon application and KYC compliance.
benefits: The NCMC enables contactless, seamless travel across metro, bus, and suburban rail systems; supports retail payments at participating merchants; allows offline transactions in low-connectivity areas; reduces the need for multiple cards or cash; promotes digital inclusion; integrates with the National Common Mobility Card ecosystem; and is backed by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for nationwide interoperability.
financial_support: The National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) does not involve direct financial subsidies or grants to users. Users bear the cost of obtaining the card (typically a nominal issuance fee) and load funds onto it for transit and retail transactions. The scheme operates on a user-funded model where financial transactions are processed through linked bank accounts or wallets, with no central financial assistance provided per entity.
application_process: 1. Visit an authorized bank or transit agency issuing NCMC. 2. Complete the application form with personal details. 3. Submit KYC documents (identity and address proof). 4. Pay the nominal card issuance fee (if applicable). 5. Load funds onto the card via cash, bank transfer, or UPI. 6. Start using the card for transit and retail payments at enabled terminals.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted year-round
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

benefits: De-dieselisation of farm sector and enhancing the income of farmers.

implementing_agency: This scheme is being implemented by the designated departments of the State Government.

overview: The PLI for Solar PV Modules is a Production Linked Incentive scheme aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing of high-efficiency solar photovoltaic modules in India. It supports the national goal of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel-based electricity generation capacity by 2030 and reducing reliance on imports. The scheme provides financial incentives based on incremental sales of domestically manufactured solar PV modules over a five-year period. It is part of broader efforts to strengthen India's solar manufacturing ecosystem under the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative.
target_beneficiaries: domestic manufacturers; solar PV module producers; MSME
eligibility: Domestic manufacturers of solar PV modules who are registered under the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) and meet the eligibility criteria as per the PLI scheme guidelines issued by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). Applicants must have a valid GSTIN, PAN, and be engaged in the manufacturing of solar PV modules in India.
benefits: Financial incentives on incremental sales of domestically manufactured solar PV modules over a five-year period, support for scaling up manufacturing capacity, enhancement of domestic value chain in solar energy, reduction in import bills, and strengthening of India's position in the global solar supply chain.
financial_support: The scheme provides a production-linked incentive based on incremental sales of high-efficiency solar PV modules manufactured in India. The incentive is disbursed annually over five years, calculated as a percentage of net sales revenue from eligible products, subject to a cap on total outlay. The total financial outlay for the scheme is INR 24,000 Crore.
application_process: 1. Eligible manufacturers must register on the ALMM portal. 2. Submit application for PLI scheme through the designated MNRE portal. 3. Provide details of manufacturing capacity, technology, and investment plans. 4. Submit required documents including incorporation certificates, GSTIN, PAN, and bank details. 5. Application is evaluated by the Project Appraisal Committee (PAC). 6. Upon approval, a Letter of Award (LoA) is issued. 7. Incentives are claimed annually based on verified incremental sales. 8. Submission of utilization certificates and audit reports is required for each claim.
deadlines: As per scheme guidelines; specific windows are announced by MNRE from time to time.
implementing_agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)

overview: The National Electricity Fund (NEF) is an interest subsidy scheme approved by the Government of India to promote capital investment in the distribution sector by providing interest subsidy linked with reform measures on loans taken by public and private power utilities for various capital works under distribution projects. The scheme aims to improve the quality, reliability, and affordability of power supply through a financially sustainable and operationally efficient distribution sector. It supports pre-paid smart metering, system metering, and distribution infrastructure works for loss reduction and modernization.
target_beneficiaries: public power utilities; private power utilities
eligibility: Public and private power utilities taking loans for various capital works under distribution projects are eligible for the National Electricity Fund (Interest Subsidy) Scheme, subject to meeting pre-qualifying criteria and achievement of basic minimum benchmarks by the DISCOM, evaluated on the basis of action plans.
benefits: The scheme provides interest subsidy on loans for distribution projects, supports pre-paid smart metering, system metering, and distribution infrastructure works for loss reduction and modernization, enables access to funds for improving operational efficiencies and financial sustainability of DISCOMs, and includes annual appraisal of DISCOM performance against predefined performance trajectories including AT&C losses, ACS-ARR gaps, infrastructure upgrade performance, consumer services, hours of supply, and corporate governance.
financial_support: The National Electricity Fund (NEF) provides interest subsidy on loans taken by public and private power utilities for various capital works under distribution projects. The financial assistance for distribution infrastructure works under the scheme is subject to meeting pre-qualifying criteria and achievement of basic minimum benchmarks by the DISCOM, evaluated on the basis of action plans. DISCOMs must score a minimum of 60% of marks and clear a minimum bar in respect to certain parameters to be eligible for funding against the scheme in that year.
implementing_agency: Government of India, Ministry of Power

overview: The Open Government Data (OGD) Platform India, accessible at data.gov.in, is a national initiative under the Digital India program to proactively publish government datasets in open, machine-readable formats for public use, innovation, and transparency. It serves as a centralized repository where ministries, departments, and state governments share non-sensitive data across sectors such as health, education, agriculture, and finance. The platform enables citizens, researchers, developers, and startups to access, visualize, and reuse government data for societal and economic benefit.
target_beneficiaries: startups; researchers; developers; citizens; MSME
eligibility: Any individual, organization, startup, researcher, or developer can access and use the datasets available on the OGD Platform (data.gov.in) without restriction, subject to the terms of the National Data Sharing and Accessibility Policy (NDSAP) and applicable licenses.
benefits: Free access to thousands of government datasets in machine-readable formats (CSV, JSON, XML, etc.), data visualization tools, APIs for developers, metadata cataloging, multilingual interface, and the ability to create, share, and reuse data-driven applications and insights for commercial or non-commercial purposes.
financial_support: The OGD Platform does not provide direct financial support to users. It is a free-to-use digital public infrastructure offering open data access at no cost. Any financial support for data-driven innovation would come through linked government schemes or grants accessed independently by users leveraging the platform.
application_process: 1. Visit the OGD Platform at https://data.gov.in 2. Browse or search for datasets using keywords, sectors, or tags 3. Select a dataset to view its metadata, preview, and download options 4. Click 'Download' to access the dataset in preferred format (CSV, JSON, XML, etc.) 5. Optionally, register for personalized features such as saving favorites or tracking updates 6. Developers can access APIs via the developer section for programmatic data retrieval.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Data is published and accessible continuously as it is released by government sources.
implementing_agency: National Informatics Centre (NIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

scheme_name: Electricity Amendment Act – Open Access for MSMEs
overview: The Electricity Amendment Act – Open Access for MSMEs is a policy initiative aimed at enabling Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to access electricity through open access mechanisms, allowing them to procure power directly from generators or traders rather than being restricted to local distribution companies. This scheme promotes competition, reduces electricity costs, and enhances energy choice for MSMEs by facilitating their participation in open access transactions under the Electricity Act, 2003. It supports the broader goal of making the power sector more efficient, transparent, and consumer-centric.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as defined under the MSME Development Act, 2006, seeking to procure electricity through open access under the Electricity Act, 2003, and meeting the technical and regulatory requirements set by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) or State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs) for open access consumers.
benefits: MSMEs can procure electricity directly from power generators or through open access, potentially reducing electricity costs through competitive pricing; access to renewable energy sources; improved power supply reliability; freedom to choose power suppliers; and enhanced operational flexibility in energy management.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants. Instead, it enables cost savings through market-based power procurement under open access, where MSMEs can negotiate power purchase agreements (PPAs) at competitive rates, avoiding high retail tariffs imposed by distribution companies.
application_process: 1. MSMEs must first confirm their eligibility as an open access consumer under the Electricity Act, 2003 and relevant CERC/SERC regulations. 2. They must apply for open access approval to the designated nodal agency (typically the State Transmission Utility or State Load Despatch Centre). 3. Submit required documents including MSME registration, proof of identity, address, and details of the proposed power procurement arrangement. 4. Upon approval, sign a Long-Term Access (LTA) or Medium-Term Open Access (MTOA) agreement with the transmission utility. 5. Coordinate with the chosen power generator/trader for scheduling and energy accounting. 6. Commence power draw under open access after meeting all technical and commercial conditions.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year as per the procedures of the respective State Transmission Utility or Load Despatch Centre.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Power, Government of India

scheme_name: e-Sanjeevani Telemedicine Platform for Health Startups
overview: eSanjeevani is India's National Telemedicine Service, providing accessible and affordable healthcare through a hub-and-spoke model connecting patients at Ayushman Bharat Health & Wellness Centres (spokes) with doctors and specialists at medical college hubs. It enables remote consultations via smartphones or at wellness centres, supporting Universal Health Coverage by bridging the digital health divide. The platform is ABDM compliant, integrates with Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA), and supports electronic health records, e-prescriptions, and SNOMED CT terminology.
target_beneficiaries: general public; patients in rural and remote areas; healthcare providers; Community Health Officers; Medical Officers
eligibility: Patients can access eSanjeevani by visiting the nearest Ayushman Bharat Health & Wellness Centre or using the platform via smartphone with internet connectivity. Healthcare providers (MBBS doctors, specialists, Medical Officers, Community Health Officers) can onboard as providers after training and registration through the NHM-supported hub-and-spoke model.
benefits: Affordable and accessible healthcare, remote consultations reducing travel burden, integration with ABHA for health record linkage, e-prescription functionality, support for SNOMED CT and DICOM standards, seamless integration with CPHC-IT application, SMS alerts, comprehensive dashboard for monitoring, and lifetime archival of health records via MyHealthRecord (PHRMS).
financial_support: The platform is implemented under the National Health Mission (NHM) with financial support from MoHFW to State Governments for infrastructure, training, and operational costs. Hubs are established at medical colleges with contractual MBBS doctors and daily-roster specialists. Spokes (HWCs) are upgraded with telemedicine infrastructure. Equipment such as Bluetooth-enabled diagnostic devices (approx. cost Rs. 1 lakh) may be deployed. Funding is provisioned through State proposals under NHM for HR, infrastructure, and application hosting (central or cloud-based).
application_process: 1. States/UTs conduct a gap analysis of existing infrastructure at HWCs under NHM or other schemes. 2. Prepare a proposal for telemedicine rollout including infrastructure, HR, and budget requirements. 3. Submit proposal to MoHFW under NHM for financial and technical support. 4. Upgrade HWCs (spokes) with required telemedicine infrastructure and train existing manpower (CHO, MPW, ASHA). 5. Establish HUBs at medical colleges or zonal levels with MBBS doctors (contractual) and specialists (daily roster). 6. Deploy the centrally hosted e-Sanjeevani application. 7. Integrate with ABHA, MyHealthRecord, and CPHC-IT application. 8. Launch services and monitor via district/state/centre-level dashboards.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted year-round under NHM; service access is available 24x7.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India
contact_details: Email: Not explicitly provided in evidence | Helpline: Not explicitly provided in evidence

overview: The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) provides Aadhaar-based authentication services that enable startups to verify identities digitally using Aadhaar e-KYC and authentication APIs. This service supports digital onboarding, reduces fraud, and enhances trust in digital transactions for startups operating in India. It is part of the broader Digital India initiative to promote secure and inclusive digital infrastructure.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups registered in India seeking to integrate Aadhaar-based authentication for customer onboarding or identity verification purposes.
benefits: Access to UIDAI's Aadhaar authentication and e-KYC APIs, secure and real-time identity verification, reduced operational costs for KYC compliance, enhanced customer trust, and support for regulatory compliance under various digital service frameworks.
financial_support: No direct financial support is provided; the service offers free access to authentication APIs subject to usage guidelines and compliance with UIDAI regulations.
application_process: 1. Visit the UIDAI developer portal at https://uidai.gov.in/section/developer-portal 2. Register as an Authentication User Agency (AUA) or Sub-AUA 3. Submit required documentation including legal entity proof and security compliance 4. Upon approval, obtain API access credentials 5. Integrate Aadhaar authentication APIs into your startup's platform 6. Begin conducting Aadhaar-based e-KYC and authentication transactions.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

overview: The Smart Metering Implementation (AMISP) scheme under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme focuses on deploying prepaid smart metering, system metering, and distribution infrastructure works to improve operational and financial stability of discoms/power departments (excluding private discoms). Financial assistance under the scheme is contingent on meeting pre-qualification norms and achieving minimum standards by discoms, with performance evaluated annually on parameters like AT&C losses, ACS-ARR gap, infrastructure upgradation, consumer services, and supply hours. The scheme aims to reduce pan-India AT&C losses to 12-15% and ACS-ARR gap to zero by 2024-25, while enabling consumer empowerment through prepayment smart metering in PPP mode and leveraging AI/OT data for energy accounting and decision-making on loss reduction, demand forecasting, ToD tariffs, renewable integration, and futuristic analysis.
target_beneficiaries: discoms; power departments
eligibility: Discoms/power departments (excluding private discoms) must achieve a minimum of 60% score on performance parameters and cross the minimum threshold to be eligible for funding under the scheme against that year's allocation. Performance is evaluated annually on pre-agreed parameters including AT&C losses, ACS-ARR gap, infrastructure upgradation performance, consumer services, supply hours, etc.
benefits: Financial assistance for prepaid smart metering, system metering, and distribution infrastructure works; consumer empowerment through prepayment smart metering in PPP mode; utilization of AI/OT equipment for analyzing data from smart meters and IT/OT systems to generate monthly energy accounting reports; informed decision-making on loss reduction, demand forecasting, time-of-day (ToD) tariffs, renewable energy (RE) integration, and futuristic analysis; convergence with PM-KUSUM for solarising agricultural feeders to supply daytime power to farmers.
financial_support: Financial assistance under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme is provided for prepaid smart metering, system metering, and distribution infrastructure works, subject to discoms meeting pre-qualification eligibility norms and achieving basic minimum standards. Assistance is based on performance evaluation against agreed parameters, with discoms needing to score at least 60% and clear minimum thresholds to qualify for funding in a given year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Power, Government of India

scheme_name: Tax Collected at Source (TCS) Exemption for Startups
overview: Tax Collected at Source (TCS) Exemption for Startups is a tax benefit under the Income Tax Act, 1961 that allows eligible startups to be exempt from TCS on certain specified transactions, reducing their compliance burden and improving cash flow during early growth stages.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups recognized by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Startup India initiative are eligible for TCS exemption on specified goods and services as per the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
benefits: Exemption from Tax Collected at Source (TCS) on specified transactions such as sale of overseas tour packages, foreign remittances, and sale of alcohol, thereby reducing upfront tax outflow and improving liquidity for eligible startups.
financial_support: The scheme provides indirect financial support by exempting eligible startups from paying TCS on certain specified transactions, thereby retaining more working capital that would otherwise be blocked as tax deducted at source.
application_process: 1. Obtain DPIIT recognition for the startup via the Startup India portal. 2. Ensure the startup is engaged in specified transactions attracting TCS. 3. Furnish Form 27EQ or relevant TCS exemption certificate to the collector of tax. 4. The collector shall not collect TCS if a valid exemption certificate is furnished. 5. Maintain documentation for audit and compliance purposes.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the financial year as and when TCS-liable transactions occur.
implementing_agency: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

overview: myScheme is a National Platform that aims to offer one-stop search and discovery of Government schemes from both Central and State/UT Governments. It provides an innovative, technology-based solution to discover scheme information based on citizen eligibility. The platform helps citizens find the right Government schemes for them and guides on how to apply, eliminating the need to visit multiple Government websites.
target_beneficiaries: citizens
eligibility: Eligibility Check You can check your eligibility for schemes using different criteria and personal attribute
benefits: The myScheme platform provides comprehensive information on each scheme, including eligibility criteria, benefits offered, application procedure, and the documents required to avail the scheme. It also features a dedicated Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) section to address common queries related to the scheme.
application_process: 1. Enter Details: Start by entering your basic details! 2. Search: Our search engine will find the relevant schemes! 3. Select & Apply: Select and apply for the best suited scheme
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National e-Governance Division (NeGD), with the Support of Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievance (DARPG) and in partnership with other Central and State Ministries/Departments

overview: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is a national public procurement portal that facilitates online procurement of goods and services for Central and State Government Ministries, Departments, Public Sector Units (PSUs), and affiliated entities. It aims to make public procurement transparent, efficient, and inclusive by providing a unified platform for buyers and sellers. GeM supports MSMEs, startups, and women entrepreneurs through dedicated sections and preferential treatment under public procurement policies.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST entrepreneurs; Self Help Groups; North East states and J&K sellers
eligibility: Sellers and service providers can register on GeM by providing required documents and completing the online registration process. There is no fee for registration. Specific eligibility for preferential treatment includes MSMEs (as per Udyam registration), startups (able to list products under Startup Runway 2.0), women entrepreneurs (under Womaniya initiative), and SC/ST entrepreneurs (under MSME SC/ST initiative). Sellers must comply with GeM's policies, including updating TReDS onboarding status in their profile and avoiding bid rigging or cartelisation.
benefits: Sellers get access to the National Public Procurement market with no registration fees. Benefits include special provisions for startups, MSMEs and Emporium products, a fully online paperless and contactless platform, access to GeM Seller ID for verification, ability to participate in bids and reverse auctions, online grievance redressal mechanism, seller-friendly dashboard for monitoring supplies and payments, and exemptions for North East and J&K sellers from ITR at bid participation. Buyers benefit from transparency, rich product listings, multiple procurement modes (Direct Purchase, L1, Bid/RA), integrated payment system, and real-time visibility of bids and prices.
financial_support: GeM does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. It facilitates access to government procurement opportunities where sellers can sell goods and services to government buyers. Financial transactions occur between buyers and sellers on the platform, with GeM providing an integrated payment system. GeM is linked with TReDS Exchanges to enable cheaper and quicker financing for MSMEs by sharing CPSE purchase data with financiers.
application_process: 1. Visit the GeM portal at https://gem.gov.in 2. Click on 'Sign Up' and select 'Seller' or 'Service Provider' 3. Fill in the registration form with required details 4. Upload required documents including PAN, bank account details, and business registration documents 5. Complete PFMS verification of bank account 6. Submit the application for verification 7. Upon approval, receive GeM Seller ID and login credentials 8. Log in to the seller dashboard to start offering products/services 9. Update TReDS onboarding status in profile (Profile -> TReDS) if applicable 10. Participate in bids, reverse auctions, or direct purchase opportunities
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Registration is open year-round.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
contact_details: Email: helpdesk-gem@gov.in | Helpline: 1800-419-3436 / 1800-102-3436 (9:00 am - 10:00 pm Mon to Sat)

overview: India Enterprise Architecture (InEA) is a framework under the Digital India initiative by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at establishing a standardized, interoperable, and secure enterprise architecture for government systems and digital services. It seeks to align IT investments with national goals, improve efficiency, and enable seamless data exchange across departments. The framework supports the design, development, and deployment of scalable and future-ready digital infrastructure in line with India’s digital transformation objectives.
target_beneficiaries: government departments; public sector undertakings; state governments; central ministries
eligibility: The framework is applicable to all central government ministries/departments, state governments, union territories, and their agencies undertaking IT system design, development, or modernization under Digital India and related initiatives.
benefits: InEA provides a structured approach to IT planning, promotes reuse of components, ensures compliance with national standards (such as e-Gov standards), enhances system reliability and security, facilitates cloud adoption, and supports long-term maintainability and scalability of government digital systems.
financial_support: InEA is a policy and technical framework; it does not involve direct financial support, grants, or subsidies to entities. Implementation is carried out through budgetary allocations of respective ministries/departments for their IT projects aligned with the framework.
application_process: As a framework, InEA does not have a traditional application process. Ministries and departments adopt its guidelines during the planning and design phases of IT projects. Adoption involves referencing InEA guidelines, aligning system architecture with its principles, and undergoing review by MeitY or designated technical committees for compliance.
deadlines: Rolling basis — adoption is ongoing as part of project planning cycles
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: Meity's Data Centre Policy is a strategic initiative under the Digital India programme aimed at establishing a robust ecosystem for data centres in India. The policy focuses on attracting investments, ensuring reliable power and connectivity, and promoting sustainable and secure data infrastructure. It seeks to position India as a global hub for data storage, processing, and cloud services by leveraging the country's growing digital demand and strategic location.
target_beneficiaries: data centre operators; investors; cloud service providers; telecom companies; MSMEs
eligibility: Eligible applicants include companies registered in India, including startups, MSMEs, and large enterprises, that propose to establish or expand data centre facilities. Projects must comply with MeitY guidelines, including minimum investment thresholds, land availability, power and connectivity readiness, and adherence to environmental and safety norms. Foreign direct investment (FDI) is permitted as per extant government policy.
benefits: Benefits include fiscal incentives such as capital subsidies, interest subvention, and tax exemptions; non-fiscal benefits like single-window clearance, facilitated land allocation, assured power supply through dedicated feeders, and priority in right-of-way for optical fibre connectivity. Additional support includes skill development programmes, access to government test beds, and collaboration opportunities with MeitY's R&D institutions.
financial_support: Financial support includes a one-time capital subsidy of up to 25% of the investment in plant and machinery, subject to a ceiling of INR 50 crore per project. Interest subvention on term loans for data centre projects is available at 6% per annum for a period of 5 years. Support is disbursed through designated nodal agencies upon verification of milestones and submission of required documentation.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 50 crore per project
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed project report (DPR) along with land details, power and connectivity plans, and environmental clearances. 2. Apply online through the MeitY Data Centre Policy portal or designated nodal agency website. 3. Undergo technical and financial appraisal by the empowered committee. 4. Receive in-principle approval based on eligibility and viability. 5. Sign memorandum of understanding (MoU) with MeitY or its agency. 6. Implement the project as per approved timelines. 7. Submit completion report and utilization certificate for disbursement of incentives.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to budget availability.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
contact_details: Email: ceo-dibd@digitalindia.gov.in | Helpline: Not specified in evidence

overview: The Startup GST Exemption & Composition Scheme is a tax benefit initiative under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) framework designed to reduce compliance burden and tax liability for eligible startups. It allows qualifying startups to opt for the GST Composition Scheme, which offers lower tax rates and simplified return filing. The scheme aims to support early-stage enterprises by providing tax relief and easing administrative requirements.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups with an aggregate annual turnover not exceeding INR 1.5 Crore in the preceding financial year are eligible to opt for the GST Composition Scheme. The scheme applies to suppliers of goods (and certain services as notified) who are registered under GST and opt to pay tax at a fixed percentage of turnover instead of normal GST rates.
benefits: Eligible startups benefit from reduced GST rates (1% for manufacturers and traders, 5% for restaurants), quarterly return filing (GSTR-4) instead of monthly, simplified compliance with minimal record-keeping, and lower tax outflow compared to regular GST rates. The scheme also eliminates the need to issue tax invoices and maintain detailed input tax credit records.
financial_support: Under the Composition Scheme, startups pay GST at a concessional rate of 1% (for manufacturers and traders) or 5% (for restaurants) on their turnover, instead of the standard GST rates. This results in direct tax savings, improving cash flow. There is no direct financial grant or subsidy; the benefit is in the form of reduced tax liability.
application_process: 1. Log in to the GST Portal (https://www.gst.gov.in) using valid credentials. 2. Navigate to Services > Registration > Application to Opt for Composition Scheme. 3. Fill in Form CMP-02 to opt in for the Composition Scheme. 4. Provide details such as business type, turnover, and declaration of eligibility. 5. Submit the application electronically. 6. Upon successful submission, an acknowledgment is generated. 7. The option is effective from the beginning of the financial year in which it is opted, subject to compliance with conditions.
deadlines: The option to opt for the Composition Scheme must be exercised before the commencement of the financial year for which it is sought, or within 30 days of obtaining GST registration. Once opted, it remains valid unless withdrawn or disqualified.
implementing_agency: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) under the guidance of the GST Council and Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)

overview: Self-Certification for Labour Laws (Startups) is a regulatory simplification initiative under the Startup India initiative that allows DPIIT-recognised startups to self-certify compliance with specified labour and environmental laws, reducing the need for routine inspections and lowering compliance burden. Startups can self-certify through the Startup India portal or mobile app, with no inspections conducted for a specified period unless a credible complaint is filed. The scheme aims to foster innovation by enabling startups to focus on core business activities rather than regulatory formalities.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: DPIIT recognised startups that are within 10 years from date of incorporation (20 years if deeptech recognized). To apply for DPIIT recognition, click “Get Recognised” below.
benefits: Startups shall be allowed to self-certify compliance with 6 labour laws and 3 environmental laws through a simple online procedure. In the case of labour laws, no inspections will be conducted for a period of 5 years. Startups may be inspected only on receipt of a credible and verifiable complaint of violation, filed in writing and approved by at least one level senior to the inspecting officer. In the case of environment laws, startups that fall under the ‘white category’ (as defined by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)) would be able to self-certify compliance, and only random checks would be carried out in such cases.
financial_support: No direct financial support is provided under this scheme; it is a regulatory simplification measure that reduces compliance costs and administrative burden.
application_process: 1. Register on the Startup India portal. 2. Log in to your dashboard. 3. Navigate to the 'Get Recognised' section. 4. Fill out the DPIIT recognition application form with business details. 5. Upload required documents including Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, and business description. 6. Submit the application for review. 7. Upon recognition, access the Shram Suvidha Portal of the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 8. Register at the Shram Suvidha Portal and log in. 9. Click the link 'Is Any of your Establishment a Startup'. 10. Follow the instructions to complete self-certification for labour laws.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: ESOP Tax Deferment for Startup Employees
overview: The ESOP Tax Deferment for Startup Employees scheme allows eligible startups to defer tax on Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs) and sweat equity shares, enabling employees to pay tax only upon sale of shares or exit from the company, thereby reducing early financial burden and promoting employee retention and wealth creation in startups.
target_beneficiaries: startup employees
eligibility: The employer must be a DPIIT-recognised startup under Section 140 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, incorporated on or after 1st April 2016 and before 1st April 2030, with turnover not exceeding ₹300 crore in the relevant tax year, and engaged in innovation, development, or improvement of products, processes, or services, or having a scalable business model with high potential for employment generation or wealth creation. The employee must receive ESOPs or sweat equity shares from such an eligible startup.
benefits: Tax deferment on ESOPs and sweat equity shares until the earlier of: expiry of 60 months from the end of the relevant tax year, sale of shares by the employee, or exit from the company. Employees are not required to pay tax at the time of exercising the option or receiving sweat equity shares, thereby improving cash flow and aligning tax liability with actual financial benefit realization.
financial_support: The scheme provides tax deferment, not direct financial support. The benefit lies in postponing tax liability on the perquisite value of ESOPs or sweat equity shares until a liquidity event (sale or exit), allowing employees to use the full value of their equity compensation without immediate tax outgo.
application_process: 1. Obtain DPIIT recognition for the startup via the Startup India portal or National Single Window System (NSWS). 2. Obtain certification from the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) for eligibility under Section 140 of the Income Tax Act, 2025. 3. Issue ESOPs or sweat equity shares to employees in compliance with company law and scheme guidelines. 4. Employees must declare the deferment claim in their income tax return at the time of filing, specifying the nature of the benefit and the deferment period. 5. Tax is assessed and payable only upon the occurrence of the trigger event: sale of shares, exit from the company, or expiry of the 60-month deferment period.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be made at any time during the startup's eligibility period.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: PM Kisan Maan Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) Pension for Farmers
overview: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY) is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme launched by the Government of India for old age protection and social security of Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs). It provides an assured monthly pension of Rs. 3000/- after attaining the age of 60 years, with matching contributions from the government. The scheme is administered through Common Service Centres (CSCs) and managed by Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) as the pension fund manager.
target_beneficiaries: Small and Marginal Farmers
eligibility: All Small and Marginal Farmers having cultivable landholding up to 2 hectares falling in the age group of 18 to 40 years, whose names appear in the land records of States/UTs as on 01.08.2019 are eligible. However, the following are ineligible: SMFs covered under any other statutory social security schemes such as National Pension Scheme (NPS), Employees’ State Insurance Corporation scheme, Employees’ Provident Fund Organization Scheme; farmers who have opted for Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan Yojana or Pradhan Mantri Vyapari Maandhan Yojana; institutional land holders; former and present holders of constitutional posts; former and present Ministers/State Ministers and former/present Members of Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha/State Legislative Assemblies/State Legislative Councils; former and present Mayors of Municipal Corporations and Chairpersons of District Panchayats; all serving or retired officers and employees of Central/State Government Ministries/Offices/Departments and their field units, Central or State PSEs and Attached offices/Autonomous Institutions under Government as well as regular employees of Local Bodies (excluding Multi Tasking Staff/Class IV/Group D employees); all persons who paid Income Tax in the last assessment year; and professionals like Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with professional bodies and carrying out profession by undertaking practice.
benefits: Assured pension of Rs. 3000/- per month after attaining the age of 60 years; family pension of 50% of the pension to the spouse upon death of the subscriber; pension continuation option for spouse in case of death before age 60; return of subscriber's contribution with interest (savings bank rate or actual fund earnings, whichever is higher) on exit before age 60 under specified conditions; transfer of corpus back to the fund after death of subscriber and spouse; no administrative cost to subscribers; nomination facility available; option to contribute via PM-KISAN benefits; pension card issued upon enrollment.
financial_support: The scheme is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme where subscribers make monthly contributions ranging between Rs 55 to Rs 200 per month based on entry age (18 to 40 years) till they attain the age of 60. The Government of India provides a matching contribution equal to the subscriber's monthly contribution. The total monthly contribution (subscriber + government) ranges from Rs 110 to Rs 400. Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) acts as the Pension Fund Manager responsible for pension pay-out and fund management.
application_process: Step 1: The Eligible SMFs desirous of joining the scheme shall visit nearest Common Service Centre (CSC). Step 2: Following are the prerequisites for the enrolment process: Aadhaar Card Savings Bank Account Number along with IFSC Code ( Bank Passbook or Cheque Leave/book or copy of bank statement as evidence of bank account ). Step 3: Initial contribution amount in cash will be made to the Village Level Entrepreneur (VLE). Step 4: The VLE will key-in the Aadhaar number, Name of subscriber and Date of birth as printed on aadhaar card for authentication. Step 5: The VLE will complete the online registration by filling up the details like Bank Account details, Mobile Number, Email Address, Spouse (if any) and Nominee details will be captured. Step 6: System will auto calculate monthly contribution payable according to age of the Subscriber. Step 7: Subscriber will pay the 1st subscription amount in cash to the VLE. Step 8: Enrolment cum Auto Debit mandate form will be printed and will be further signed by the subscriber. VLE will scan the same and upload it into the system. Step 9: A unique Kisan Pension Account Number (KPAN) will be generated and Kisan Card will be printed.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and Farmers Welfare

overview: The GST QRMP Scheme for MSMEs allows eligible small taxpayers to file GSTR-3B and GSTR-1 returns on a quarterly basis while paying taxes monthly. It is designed to reduce compliance burden for small businesses by simplifying return filing frequency. Taxpayers under this scheme must pay tax through Form PMT-06 for the first two months of each quarter and file returns only once per quarter. The scheme is optional and available to taxpayers with an aggregate annual turnover of up to INR 5 crores.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Taxpayers having an aggregate annual turnover of up to INR 5 crores in the preceding financial year are eligible to opt into the QRMP scheme. The scheme is optional and applies to all categories of registered taxpayers under GST, including MSMEs, who wish to file returns quarterly while paying tax monthly.
benefits: Quarterly filing of GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B returns reduces the frequency of return submission from monthly to quarterly. Taxpayers pay tax monthly using Form PMT-06, ensuring steady cash outflow compliance. The scheme reduces the administrative burden of frequent filings while maintaining regular tax payment discipline. It is particularly beneficial for small businesses seeking simpler compliance under GST.
financial_support: The QRMP scheme does not provide direct financial support, subsidies, or grants. Instead, it offers a procedural benefit by allowing eligible taxpayers to file returns quarterly while continuing to pay tax on a monthly basis through Form PMT-06. There is no fund allocation, grant amount, or loan component associated with this scheme.
application_process: 1. Log in to the GST portal at https://www.gst.gov.in. 2. Navigate to the 'Services' section. 3. Select 'Returns' > 'Quarterly Return Monthly Payment (QRMP)'. 4. Opt into the QRMP scheme for the desired quarter. 5. Confirm selection and save the choice. 6. For the first two months of the quarter, pay tax using Form PMT-06. 7. At the end of the quarter, file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B returns quarterly.
deadlines: Tax payment via PMT-06 is due monthly by the 25th of the following month. Quarterly returns (GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B) must be filed by the 22nd or 24th of the month following the quarter, depending on the taxpayer's category and state/UT. The option to opt into or opt out of the QRMP scheme must be exercised before the last day of the opening month of a quarter.
implementing_agency: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) under the oversight of the GST Council and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)

scheme_name: Three-Year Tax Holiday for DPIIT Startups (80IAC)
overview: The Three-Year Tax Holiday for DPIIT Startups (80IAC) provides eligible startups with a 100% income tax exemption for three consecutive financial years out of their first ten years of incorporation. This benefit is granted under Section 80-IAC of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and requires certification from the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) set up by DPIIT. The scheme aims to reduce the tax burden on early-stage startups to encourage innovation and entrepreneurship.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: To be eligible for deduction under section 80-IAC, an entity must be a startup certified by the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB), incorporated as a private limited company or a limited liability partnership (LLP) or a registered partnership firm, have been incorporated on or after 1st April, 2016 but before 1st April, 2025, and have an annual turnover not exceeding INR 100 crore in any of the financial years preceding the year in which deduction is claimed.
benefits: 100% deduction of profits and gains from eligible business for three consecutive assessment years out of ten years beginning from the year of incorporation. This results in complete income tax exemption for the selected three years. The benefit is available only after obtaining certification from the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) established by DPIIT.
financial_support: The scheme provides a tax holiday in the form of 100% income tax exemption on profits from eligible business for three consecutive years. There is no direct cash disbursement; the benefit is realized through reduced tax liability when filing income tax returns. The quantum of support depends on the startup's profits during the selected three-year block.
application_process: 1. Obtain DPIIT recognition for the startup via the Startup India portal. 2. Apply for certification from the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) through Form 1 of the Income-tax Rules, 1962. 3. Submit the application along with required documents such as Certificate of Incorporation, details of business, PAN, and audited financial statements. 4. Upon IMB approval, claim the deduction under section 80-IAC while filing the income tax return for the relevant assessment years.
deadlines: Applications for IMB certification can be made at any time; there is no fixed deadline. However, the tax benefit must be claimed in the income tax return for the relevant assessment year within the time allowed under section 139(1) of the Income-tax Act.
implementing_agency: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

overview: The Presumptive Taxation Scheme under Section 44AD of the Income-tax Act, 1961 is designed for small businesses, including MSMEs, to simplify tax compliance by allowing them to declare income at a prescribed rate (8% of turnover or 6% for digital transactions) without maintaining detailed books of accounts. It applies to eligible taxpayers whose total turnover or gross receipts do not exceed INR 2 crores in a financial year. The scheme reduces the burden of audit and record-keeping while promoting ease of taxation for small enterprises.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; small businesses; self-employed individuals; partnership firms
eligibility: The scheme is available to resident individuals, Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs), and partnership firms (excluding Limited Liability Partnerships) who are engaged in eligible business. The total turnover or gross receipts from the business must not exceed INR 2 crores in the financial year. Professionals (as defined under Section 44AA) are not eligible. The business must not be involved in agency, brokerage, or commission-based activities.
benefits: Taxpayers opting for Section 44AD are exempt from maintaining books of account as required under Section 44AA and are not required to get their accounts audited under Section 44AB. Income is computed presumptively at 8% of turnover (or 6% for turnover received through digital modes). This reduces compliance costs and simplifies return filing. The scheme also allows advance tax to be paid in a single installment by March 15 instead of quarterly installments.
financial_support: Under Section 44AD, the income is deemed to be 8% of the total turnover or gross receipts for the financial year (6% if received through account payee cheque, bank draft, or electronic clearing system). No actual expenses are allowed for deduction. The taxpayer must declare this presumed income in their income tax return and pay tax accordingly. There is no direct financial outlay or subsidy; the benefit is in reduced tax liability due to simplified computation and exemption from audit.
application_process: 1. Compute presumptive income at 8% of turnover (6% for digital receipts) under Section 44AD. 2. Ensure total turnover does not exceed INR 2 crores. 3. File Income Tax Return (ITR-4 Sugam) declaring the presumed income. 4. No need to maintain books of accounts or undergo tax audit. 5. Pay advance tax in full by March 15 if applicable. 6. Submit the return before the due date (usually July 31 for non-audit cases).
deadlines: Income Tax Return (ITR-4) must be filed by July 31 of the assessment year for non-audit cases. Advance tax, if applicable, must be paid in full by March 15.
implementing_agency: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
contact_details: Email: admin@cbdtdomain.gov.in (generic CBDT contact as per evidence) | Helpline: 1800-180-1961 (standard Income Tax Department helpline)

overview: Agri Stack is a digital infrastructure initiative by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, designed to create a federated database of farmers and farmland to improve access to credit, inputs, advice, and markets. It aims to enhance the delivery of government schemes by enabling presence-less farmer identification and authentication through a unique FarmerID linked to Aadhaar. The platform supports agri-tech innovation by providing secure, consent-based access to high-quality agricultural data via components like the Farmer Registry, Crop Sown Registry, Unified Farmer Service Interface (UFSI), Consent Manager, and Agri Stack Sandbox.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; agri-tech startups; private companies; public entities; state governments; central government
eligibility: Eligibility is not explicitly defined for direct beneficiary access in the evidence; the Farmer Registry is compiled by States according to common standards, and each farmer is assigned a unique FarmerID based on Aadhaar as per IndEA 2.0, with minimal demographic details to enable identification and eligibility determination for availing government scheme benefits.
benefits: Farmers gain easier access to cheaper credit, higher-quality farm inputs, localized and specific advice, and more informed and convenient access to markets. Governments can plan and implement farmer-focused benefit schemes more effectively. Agri-Tech startups and private companies benefit from secure, consent-based access to high-quality agricultural data via the Agri Stack Sandbox and UFSI to develop innovative products and services. The platform enables data-blind sharing of personal data only with explicit farmer consent through the Consent Manager, ensuring privacy and security.
financial_support: No direct financial support is provided to farmers or entities under Agri Stack; it is a digital infrastructure enabling access to services like credit, inputs, and advisory, which may be facilitated by banks, financial institutions, or service providers using the platform.
application_process: No specific application process for farmers or startups to access Agri Stack is detailed in the evidence; access is enabled through state-level Farmer Registry compilation and consent-based data sharing via the Consent Manager, with the Agri Stack Sandbox providing a simulated environment for authorized stakeholders to test products and services.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Implementation is ongoing as states form steering committees and provide APIs.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

overview: The Soil Health Card Scheme is a government initiative under the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, aimed at providing farmers with soil health cards to assess nutrient status and optimize fertilizer use. It empowers farmers with data-driven insights to improve yields, conserve resources, and promote sustainable agricultural practices. The scheme involves regular soil testing every three years and provides crop-specific fertilizer recommendations. It is implemented across India through state agricultural departments.
target_beneficiaries: farmers
eligibility: All farmers across India are eligible to receive a Soil Health Card under the scheme. The soil health card is provided for each farm holding, and farmers can get their soil tested at designated soil testing laboratories to receive the card.
benefits: Farmers receive a proper soil health record, become aware of soil management practices, and can plan future crops and land use accordingly. The card provides information on lacking nutrients, guiding farmers on which crops to invest in and which fertilizers to use, ultimately leading to increased crop yield. Regular updates are provided every three years to track changes in soil health over time.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support for soil testing, issuance of Soil Health Cards, and related activities such as capacity building of soil testing laboratories and training of agriculture students. Financial assistance is extended to states for setting up and strengthening soil testing laboratories, including village-level soil testing labs, and for conducting demonstrations under the scheme. The financial outlay is integrated under broader schemes like Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) and Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY).
application_process: 1. Visit the nearest soil testing laboratory or authorized collection center. 2. Collect soil sample from the farm as per guidelines (depth, location, etc.). 3. Submit the soil sample along with farmer details (name, address, land details). 4. Pay applicable fee (if any) for testing. 5. Laboratory analyzes the sample for nutrient status (N, P, K, organic carbon, pH, etc.). 6. Soil Health Card is generated based on test results. 7. Card is issued to the farmer with crop-specific fertilizer recommendations.
deadlines: Rolling basis — soil samples can be submitted throughout the year; cards are issued after testing.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

overview: The National Project on Organic Farming (NPOF) is a central sector scheme implemented by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. It aims to promote organic farming through financial assistance, capacity building, market development, and quality control mechanisms. The scheme supports the adoption of organic practices across the country by providing subsidies for inputs, certification, and infrastructure development.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; self-help groups; farmer producer organizations; state governments; agri-entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include individual farmers, groups of farmers, self-help groups (SHGs), farmer producer organizations (FPOs), state governments, and other entities engaged in organic farming or related activities, subject to guidelines issued by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare.
benefits: Financial assistance for setting up organic input production units, organic certification, residue testing, market development, training and capacity building, and support for organic farming clusters. The scheme also provides support for vermicompost units, bio-fertilizer and bio-pesticide production, and post-harvest management infrastructure.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as back-ended subsidies, typically ranging from 25% to 33% of the project cost, with upper limits varying by component. For example, assistance for setting up bio-fertilizer units is up to INR 40 lakhs, for vermicompost units up to INR 5 lakhs per unit, and for organic certification and residue testing up to INR 5 lakhs. The subsidy is released in installments based on verification of progress and utilization of funds.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant component under NPOF for which assistance is sought. 2. Prepare a detailed project report (DPR) as per the guidelines. 3. Submit the application along with required documents to the State Nodal Officer or the designated agency. 4. The application is scrutinized by the State Level Sanctioning Committee (SLSC). 5. Upon approval, the sanction is issued and funds are released in installments. 6. Beneficiaries must utilize the funds for the approved purpose and submit utilization certificates and progress reports.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and approval by the State Level Sanctioning Committee.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oils – Oil Palm (NMEO-OP)
overview: National Mission on Edible Oils – Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched by the Government of India to promote oil palm cultivation for achieving self-reliance in edible oils, with special focus on North-Eastern States and A&N Islands. The mission aims to bring an additional 6.5 lakh hectares under oil palm plantation by 2025-26, targeting 3.28 lakh ha in North-Eastern states and 3.22 lakh ha in the rest of India. It provides financial assistance for planting material, maintenance, drip irrigation, pump sets, bore-wells, vermi-compost units, machinery, and viability gap payments linked to assured procurement by industry.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers; Women; NE states beneficiaries
geographic_scope: Pan-India (20 states covering 284 districts including NE states and A&N Islands)
eligibility: Farmers in general states, North-Eastern states, and UTs including Andaman & Nicobar Islands are eligible. The scheme covers 20 states identified by ICAR-IIOPR Report 2020 as having potential for oil palm cultivation. Special focus is given to districts with more than 4000 to 5000 ha potential for oil palm area expansion and productivity enhancement. States must submit Annual Action Plans (AAPs) approved by State Level Sanctioning Committee (SLSC) headed by the Chief Secretary for fund allocation.
benefits: Financial assistance includes: 85% cost of planting material at Rs. 12,000/ha for entire land in first year; Rs. 10,000/ha/year for maintenance cost of new plantations and purchasing inputs for intercropping for four years during gestation period; installation of drip-irrigation systems as per PMSKY; 50% cost of diesel/electric pump-sets limited to Rs. 27,000/pump-set for SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women and NE states beneficiaries and Rs. 22,500/pump-set for other beneficiaries; 50% cost limited to Rs. 50,000/unit for bore-well and water harvesting structures/ponds (Rs. 1.50 lakh per unit in plain area and Rs. 1.80 lakh per unit in hilly areas); 50% cost limited to Rs. 15,000/unit for construction of vermi-compost units; 50% cost limited to Rs. 1500/- per oil palm cutter, Rs. 15,000/- per wire-mesh, Rs. 10,000/- per motorized chisel, Rs. 3000/- per unit for aluminium portable ladder, Rs. 20,000/- per unit for SC/ST/Small Farmers/Women/NE states and Rs. 16,000/- per unit for other beneficiaries as per SMAM norms; 40% of cost limited to Rs. 1.80 lakh for other beneficiaries and Rs. 2.25 lakh for SC/ST/Small Farmers/Women/NE states for small tractor of 20HP with trolley; in NE states, 50% of cost limited to Rs. 250.00 lakhs for setting up a new oil palm processing mill (5 MT per hour capacity); 50% of actual cost estimated by PWD/CPWD limited to 20% of total outlay of state under AAP for NFSM-Oil Palm for roads from oil palm field to nearest FFB collection/processing centre; Viability Gap Payment with central government compensating farmers if industry price is below viability price up to October 2037.
financial_support: Under NMEO-OP, the cost is shared as 60:40 between Central and State Government for General states and 90:10 for NE states and UT, with 100% for central agencies. Financial assistance is provided to farmers @ 85% cost of planting material (Rs. 12,000/ha) for entire land during first year for plantation and Rs. 10,000/ha/year for maintenance cost of new plantations and purchasing inputs for intercropping for four years during gestation period. Additional support includes 50% cost of drip-irrigation systems, pump-sets (Rs. 27,000 for SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women and NE states; Rs. 22,500 for others), bore-wells/water harvesting (Rs. 50,000 unit in plain, Rs. 1.50 lakh in hilly), vermi-compost units (Rs. 15,000 unit), and machinery/tools as per SMAM norms. Viability Gap Payment is provided with central government compensating farmers if industry price is below viability price up to October 2037.
grant_amount_per_entity: 85% cost of planting material @ Rs. 12,000/ha for first year plantation; Rs. 10,000/ha/year for maintenance and intercropping inputs for four years; 50% cost of pump-sets limited to Rs. 27,000 (SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women, NE states) and Rs. 22,500 (others); 50% cost of bore-well/water harvesting limited to Rs. 50,000 (plain) and Rs. 1.50 lakh (hilly); 50% cost of vermi-compost units limited to Rs. 15,000/unit; machinery/tools as per SMAM norms; Viability Gap Payment up to October 2037
application_process: 1. State Departments of Agriculture/Horticulture act as nodal agencies for area expansion under NMEO-OP in partnership with processors. 2. Processors submit oil palm area expansion target and component-wise Annual Action Plan (AAP) to the State for inclusion in the state AAP, approved by State Level Sanctioning Committee (SLSC). 3. The Department of Agriculture/Horticulture of State Governments undertakes the area expansion programme under NMEO-OP with close partnership with processors. 4. Funds are released to State Departments of Agriculture/Horticulture through respective State Governments using DBT for transfer to State/Agencies/Farmers/Processors/SAUs. 5. Private sector and NGOs can be involved through State Department of Agriculture, Horticulture & ICAR. 6. Government of India releases funds to agencies for 100% funded components/activities at Central level. 7. Release of Central and State share is through an escrow account mechanism; Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare authorized to release up to two instalments of 25% each to States without insisting on release of State’s share. 8. A Tripartite Agreement between Centre, State and the Bank is signed for this purpose (Annexure-XIV).
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

overview: The Dairy Entrepreneurship Development Scheme (DEDS) is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India. It aims to generate self-employment opportunities in the dairy sector by providing financial assistance for setting up small dairy farms and related activities. The scheme promotes the establishment of modern dairy farms, calf rearing units, vermicomposting, and other allied activities to enhance milk production and processing.
target_beneficiaries: individual entrepreneurs; self-help groups; dairy cooperative societies; milk unions; milk federations; NGOs; Panchayati Raj Institutions
eligibility: Individual entrepreneurs, self-help groups, dairy cooperative societies, milk unions, milk federations, NGOs, and Panchayati Raj Institutions are eligible to avail benefits under the scheme. The beneficiary must have a minimum of 2 milch animals (cows/buffaloes) for individual beneficiaries and 10 milch animals for SHGs/cooperatives. The unit must be located in a rural or peri-urban area and must not have availed similar benefits under any other central or state government scheme for the same component.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of back-ended subsidy is provided for various components such as establishment of small dairy farms with crossbred cows/indigenous descriptively graded buffaloes, rearing of heifer calves, vermicomposting, milk processing units, cold chain facilities, and transportation. The subsidy is linked with bank loans and is disbursed after successful verification of the unit. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, training, and monitoring support from implementing agencies.
financial_support: The scheme provides a back-ended subsidy ranging from 25% to 33.33% of the project cost, depending on the beneficiary category and component. For general category beneficiaries, the subsidy is 25% of the project cost, while for SC/ST and other special categories, it is 33.33%. The subsidy is released in installments after verification of the unit by the bank and NABARD. The maximum project cost eligible for subsidy varies by component, e.g., up to INR 5.00 lakhs for a small dairy farm with 10 animals and up to INR 20.00 lakhs for milk processing units.
application_process: 1. Identify the eligible component under DEDS (e.g., small dairy farm, calf rearing, vermicomposting, etc.). 2. Prepare a detailed project report including cost estimates, location details, and beneficiary information. 3. Approach a commercial bank, regional rural bank, or cooperative bank for loan sanction under the scheme. 4. Submit the project report and loan application to the bank along with required documents. 5. The bank forwards the proposal to NABARD for sanction and subsidy reservation. 6. After loan disbursement, set up the unit as per the approved plan. 7. Notify the bank upon completion for inspection and verification. 8. Upon successful verification, the subsidy amount is released by NABARD to the beneficiary's loan account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India

scheme_name: National Programme for Bovine Breeding & Dairy Dev (NPBBD)
overview: The National Programme for Bovine Breeding & Dairy Development (NPBBD) is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at enhancing milk production and productivity of bovines through genetic improvement, conservation of indigenous breeds, and development of dairy infrastructure. It focuses on strengthening semen stations, promoting artificial insemination, and supporting breed improvement programmes across the country. The scheme also supports the establishment of dairy cooperatives and milk processing units to ensure better returns for farmers.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; livestock rearers; dairy cooperatives; MSME
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include individual farmers, livestock rearers, dairy cooperative societies, self-help groups, NGOs, and state livestock development boards involved in bovine breeding and dairy development activities, subject to verification by the State Implementing Agency.
benefits: Financial assistance for setting up semen stations, strengthening existing semen stations, procurement of breeding bulls, implementation of progeny testing and pedigree selection programmes, establishment of embryo transfer technology (ETT) labs, training of technicians and farmers, and support for dairy cooperative infrastructure and milk processing units.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid and subsidies to eligible implementing agencies for various components such as semen station strengthening, breeding bull procurement, and dairy infrastructure development, with funding patterns varying by component and beneficiary type as per norms approved by the Government of India.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant component under NPBBD for which assistance is sought. 2. Prepare a detailed project proposal as per the guidelines issued by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 3. Submit the proposal to the State Implementing Agency (SIA) or State Livestock Development Board. 4. The SIA forwards the proposal to the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India for appraisal and approval. 5. Upon approval, funds are released in installments based on utilization and submission of progress reports.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and approval timelines.
implementing_agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying

scheme_name: Integrated Development of Small Ruminants & Rabbits
National Livestock Health & Disease Control Programme
Integrated Scheme for Development of Silk Industry (ISDSI)
National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm (NMOOP)
KVIC Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
overview: The Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is a credit-linked subsidy scheme implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) to generate employment opportunities through the establishment of micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector. It aims to support traditional artisans and unemployed youth by providing financial assistance for setting up new micro-enterprises. The scheme promotes self-employment and entrepreneurship across rural and urban areas of India.
target_beneficiaries: unemployed youth; traditional artisans; micro-entrepreneurs; individuals above 18 years
eligibility: Any individual above 18 years of age is eligible. For setting up of project costing above Rs. 10 lakh in the manufacturing sector and above Rs. 5 lakh in the business/service sector, the beneficiary should possess at least VIII standard pass educational qualification. There is no ceiling on income for assistance under the scheme. Existing units (under PMRY, REGP or any other scheme of Government of India or State Government) and units that have already availed government subsidy under any other scheme are not eligible.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of margin money subsidy and bank credit. The subsidy rate is 25% in urban areas and 35% in rural areas for beneficiaries belonging to special categories (including SC/ST/OBC/Minorities/Women, ex-servicemen, physically handicapped, NER, Hill and Border areas etc.). For general category beneficiaries, the subsidy is 15% in urban areas and 25% in rural areas. The maximum cost of project is Rs. 50 lakh in the manufacturing sector and Rs. 20 lakh in the business/service sector.
financial_support: The scheme provides margin money subsidy ranging from 15% to 35% of the project cost, with the balance being provided as term loan by banks. The maximum project cost allowed is Rs. 50 lakh for manufacturing sector and Rs. 20 lakh for business/service sector. The subsidy is disbursed through identified nodal banks which forward the margin money to KVIC/KVIB/DIC after sanction of the loan.
application_process: 1. The applicant submits the application form online through the PMEGP portal or offline to the concerned District Industries Centre (DIC) or KVIC/KVIB office. 2. The application is scrutinized by the Field Officer/Manager of the implementing agency. 3. Upon preliminary approval, the application is forwarded to the District Level Task Force Committee (DLTFC) for sanction. 4. After sanction by DLTFC, the application is sent to the nominated bank for sanction of term loan. 5. The bank sanctions the loan and disburses the amount. 6. The margin money subsidy is released by the implementing agency (KVIC/KVIB/DIC) to the bank after verification of utilization of loan amount.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)

scheme_name: Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) Equity Grant Fund
overview: The Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) Equity Grant Fund is a scheme under the Central Sector Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) implemented by the Small Farmers' Agri-Business Consortium (SFAC). It provides matching equity grants to Farmer Producer Companies (FPCs) to improve availability of working capital and support business development. The scheme aims to strengthen the equity base of FPOs and promote sustainable agribusiness through financial support and handholding.
target_beneficiaries: Farmer Producer Companies (FPCs); Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs); agri-startups
eligibility: Farmer Producer Companies (FPCs) registered under Part IXA of the Companies Act or under Co-operative Societies Act of the concerned States, formed for the purpose of leveraging collectives through economies of scale in production and marketing of agricultural and allied sector, and seeking equity grant for working capital and business development activities.
benefits: Financial support in the form of matching equity grant to strengthen the equity base of FPOs; non-financial benefits include handholding support from Cluster Based Business Organizations (CBBOs), capacity building, market linkages, credit linkages, and technical guidance for sustainable agribusiness development.
financial_support: The scheme provides matching equity grant subject to a maximum of Rs. 15.00 lakh per FPO in 3 tranches within a period of 3 Years. The grant is released based on the equity contribution made by the FPO shareholders and is intended to improve availability of working capital and development of business activities.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 15.00 lakh per FPO
application_process: 1. Application on prescribed form duly signed by two Board Members/Authorised Representative of FPC on each page. 2. Submit category wise allotment pattern of shares of FPC and proposed computation of allotment of shares out of Equity Grant as per Annexure-I. 3. Submit Resolution of the FPC Board/Governing Council to seek Equity Grant, issue of shares to shareholders against Equity Grant and transfer of shares in case of exit of any shareholder as per Annexure-II. 4. Submit Resolution to be ratified in the next AGM of the FPC as per Annexure-III. 5. Submit Resolution (No appointment letter required) for appointment of Chief Executive Officer of Company. 6. Submit Audited Financial Statements for last financial year. 7. Submit Photocopy of Bank Account Statement for last six months duly authenticated by the Branch Manager of the Bank. 8. Submit KYC documents of only those Representatives/Directors authorised by the Board of FPC for executing and signing documents with SFAC. 9. Submit Certificate of incorporation/commencement of business, Memorandum of Association/Articles of Association. 10. Submit Business plan for 18 months.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Small Farmers' Agri-Business Consortium (SFAC)

scheme_name: IFFCO Nano Urea Initiative for Agri Startups
overview: IFFCO Nano Urea Initiative for Agri Startups is a program by IFFCO to promote nano-based fertilizers like Nano Urea and Nano DAP, which are designed to improve nutrient use efficiency, reduce environmental impact, and support sustainable agriculture. The initiative includes the establishment of nano fertilizer production units at Aonla, Kalol, and Phulpur, with commercial production already underway.
