It aligns with the Government of India's vision to reduce chemical fertilizer usage and promote eco-friendly agri-inputs.
target_beneficiaries: agri-startups; farmers; MSME
eligibility: The initiative is open to agri-startups and MSMEs engaged in sustainable agriculture, nano-based agri-inputs, or related innovations that align with IFFCO’s mission of promoting eco-friendly fertilizers and reducing chemical usage in farming. Specific eligibility criteria for participation are not detailed in the provided evidence.
benefits: Nano fertilizers like Nano Urea Plus and Nano DAP offer higher nutrient availability due to small particle size (20-50 nm) and high surface area, leading to over 80% increased availability to crops. They enhance chlorophyll content, photosynthesis, root biomass, and tiller formation, resulting in higher yields and better produce quality. Usage reduces input costs, minimizes nutrient loss from leaching and emissions, supports environmental sustainability, and allows easy storage and transport. Nano DAP can replace 50% of phosphorous requirement from conventional DAP per bottle.
financial_support: IFFCO has invested in setting up nano fertilizer production units, including the Nano Fertiliser Plant at Phulpur with a capacity of 2 lakh 500 ml bottles per day of Liquid Nano Urea, and the Nano DAP expansion facility at Kalol with a conceptualized cost of around 300 Crores for 2.0 lakhs bottles per day. Commercial production of Nano DAP started from April 2023 after FCO notification in March 2023. Financial support mechanisms for startups are not explicitly detailed in the evidence.
application_process: The evidence does not provide a step-by-step application process for agri-startups to participate in the IFFCO Nano Urea Initiative. Information on how startups can apply, register, or engage with the program is not available in the provided sources.
implementing_agency: Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited (IFFCO)

scheme_name: Central Silk Board – Bivoltine Silk Development Programme
overview: The Central Silk Board – Bivoltine Silk Development Programme is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, aimed at enhancing bivoltine silk production through research, extension, seed production, cocoon production practices, marketing, credit facilitation, policy options, and stakeholder participation. It was formulated during the XII Five Year Plan (2012-13 to 2016-17) with the goal of increasing bivoltine silk production from 1685 MT to 5000 MT, representing a 197% increase. The programme focuses on mulberry sector development and includes the formation of 179 clusters across India to promote large-scale bivoltine sericulture, particularly targeting economically weaker sections in rural areas.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; reelers; economically weaker sections; rural stakeholders; sericulture farmers
eligibility: The programme targets stakeholders in the sericulture sector, including farmers and reelers, particularly from economically weaker sections in rural areas, with a focus on mulberry sector development for bivoltine silk production. Specific eligibility criteria are not explicitly detailed in the evidence, but the scheme is implemented through state governments and involves stakeholder participation in decision-making areas.
benefits: Benefits include increased bivoltine silk production, enhanced income for stakeholders through improved productivity and quality, employment generation in rural areas, technology transfer from R&D units, and support for cluster-based sericulture development. The scheme facilitates access to improved mulberry varieties, package of practices, silkworm breeds (CSR2 x CSR4, CSR4 x CSR5, CSR18 x CSR19), improved rearing methodology, disease management, and reeling technologies suitable for tropical climates.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through the Catalytic Development Programme (CDP) under the Central Sector Scheme, with funding allocated for research, extension, seed production, cocoon production practices, marketing, credit facilitation, policy options, and increased stakeholder participation. The scheme leverages Central Sector Schemes of the Central Silk Board, with financial assistance structured as subsidies for beneficiary-oriented components, though specific quantum per entity is not detailed in the evidence.
application_process: The application process is not explicitly detailed in the evidence. However, the scheme is implemented through state governments, and proposals are likely submitted by state sericulture departments or implementing agencies to the Central Silk Board for consideration, approval, and funding, following guidelines similar to other Central Sector Schemes involving project formulation, baseline surveys, and submission to state directorates.
implementing_agency: Central Silk Board, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India

scheme_name: Special Notified Zone (SNZ) for Diamond Trading
overview: The Special Notified Zone (SNZ) for Diamond Trading is a scheme under the Foreign Trade Policy aimed at promoting diamond trading by establishing designated zones with specific regulatory and procedural benefits. It facilitates diamond imports and exports by providing a streamlined customs and regulatory environment, encouraging value addition and job creation in the gems and jewellery sector. The scheme supports India's position as a global hub for diamond trading and processing.
target_beneficiaries: diamond traders; jewellery manufacturers; exporters; importers; MSMEs in gems and jewellery
eligibility: Entities engaged in diamond trading, including importers, exporters, and processors, holding a valid Importer Exporter Code (IEC) issued by DGFT, and operating within the designated Special Notified Zones as notified by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.
benefits: Simplified customs procedures for diamond imports and exports, reduced procedural delays, enhanced monitoring and security for high-value goods, facilitation of re-export of diamonds after value addition, and access to infrastructure and support services within the SNZ.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants; benefits are primarily procedural and regulatory in nature, such as eased customs clearance and regulatory compliance within the notified zones.
application_process: 1. Obtain a valid Importer Exporter Code (IEC) from DGFT. 2. Identify the designated Special Notified Zone (SNZ) for diamond trading as notified by DGFT. 3. Ensure the business entity is located or registered to operate within the SNZ. 4. Comply with the procedural guidelines for diamond imports and exports under the Foreign Trade Policy. 5. Submit required documents for customs clearance through the ICEGATE portal or as specified by DGFT. 6. Avail benefits of streamlined procedures within the SNZ for diamond trading activities.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications and operations are permitted as long as the entity complies with SNZ regulations and holds a valid IEC.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: The APEDA Agri Export Promotion Scheme is a financial assistance program designed to support exporters of scheduled agricultural and processed food products. It provides financial assistance for activities such as market development, quality development, and export infrastructure development under the 15th Finance Commission cycle (2021-22 to 2025-26). The scheme aims to enhance India's agri-export competitiveness through targeted interventions in key product segments.
target_beneficiaries: exporters; MSME; agri-startups; Farmer Producer Companies; individual researchers
eligibility: Exporters of APEDA-scheduled products who are registered with APEDA and possess a valid Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC) are eligible to apply for financial assistance under the scheme. Applicants must submit a detailed project proposal along with supporting documents including IEC code, MSME registration (if applicable), GST and PAN details, audited financials, and other category-specific documentation as outlined in the application guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance for export promotion activities including market development, quality upgradation, and infrastructure development. Non-financial benefits include access to APEDA's market intelligence, participation in international trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, and technical support for compliance with international standards. The scheme also facilitates registration, certification, and export facilitation services.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as a subsidy based on the nature and scope of the project, subject to approval by the competent authority. The quantum of support is determined on a case-by-case basis depending on the activity type, beneficiary profile, and alignment with scheme objectives. Funds are disbursed in installments linked to project milestones and subject to submission of utilization certificates and audited expenditure statements.
application_process: 1. Visit the APEDA website and navigate to the Financial Assistance Schemes section. 2. Download the scheme guidelines and application form for the specific component (Market Development, Quality Development, or Export Infrastructure Development). 3. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 4. Gather required documents such as IEC code, RCMC, MSME registration (if applicable), GST/PAN details, audited financials, and category-specific documents. 5. Submit the completed application along with supporting documents via the designated portal or email. 6. Await scrutiny and evaluation by APEDA officials. 7. If approved, receive Registration-cum-Allocation Certificate (RCAC) or equivalent approval. 8. Implement the project as per the approved plan. 9. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates. 10. Undergo final inspection and submit final report for closure and final disbursement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year as per the scheme window (2021-22 to 2025-26).
implementing_agency: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India

scheme_name: Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC) Schemes
overview: The Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC) is the apex body driving India's export-led growth in the gem and jewellery sector since 1966. It promotes Brand India, organizes major trade shows, facilitates government interaction, and supports MSMEs through various initiatives including Common Facility Centres and Jewellery Parks. GJEPC also runs CSR programs like Jewellers for Hope and health schemes such as Swasthya Ratna and Swasthya Kosh for industry workers.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; artisans; exporters; manufacturers; traders
eligibility: Any individual, partnership, company, trust, society, or HUF engaged in the gems and jewellery sector can apply for membership. Eligibility is based on declaring turnover of products (diamonds, gold jewellery, etc.) and having a valid Import Export Code (IEC). For Associate Micro Membership, domestic turnover must be up to Rs. 40 lakhs. For other categories, eligibility is based on export performance during the preceding financial year.
benefits: Membership provides access to exhibitions and buyer-seller meets, health insurance (Swasthya Ratna), mediclaim scheme (Swasthya Kosh), social security identity (Parichay Card), certification services (Kimberly Process, RCMC), market intelligence (Solitaire International, IIJS Newsletter), training services (IIGJ, IDI, GTL), government liaison, and dedicated MSME zones at trade shows at concessional rates. Members also receive MDA/MAI assistance for international exhibitions, free access to business insights, and support for export documentation and compliance.
financial_support: GJEPC does not provide direct financial support such as grants or loans. Financial benefits are indirect through access to government schemes, market intelligence, and facilitation of export opportunities. The council helps members avail benefits from central and state government MSME schemes via its empanelled consultant ASPIRE, which provides credit facilitation, subsidy identification, and application support.
application_process: 1. Login to www.gjepc.org and click on Registration 2. Fill New Registration form and submit 3. Once user registration is completed, user will receive an email with credentials 4. Login to www.gjepc.org 5. Start filling forms starting from Application form for Associate Membership 6. Payment of fees will be initiated through challan form via net banking/Debit card/Credit Card/NEFT 7. Print all forms from - Print Application/Challan form 8. Submit the following documents to Head office or respective regional office: Application form for Associate Membership, Application form for RCMC, challan form duly signed, Signature Slip, Self-attested IEC, Self-attested PAN and Partnership Deed/MoA & AoA, Self-attested MSME(UAN)/SSI/IM if applicable, Self-attested GST certificate (if applicable), Self-attested copy of PAN, Passport and Aadhar
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC), sponsored by Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India

overview: The National Centre for Flexible Electronics (NCFlexE) is a specialized research and development centre established at IIT Kanpur to advance flexible electronics technology in India. It focuses on innovation, prototyping, and commercialization of flexible electronic systems, supporting startups, MSMEs, and academic researchers in the electronics manufacturing sector. The centre provides infrastructure, technical expertise, and collaborative platforms to foster indigenous development and reduce import dependence in flexible electronics.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; academic researchers; electronics manufacturers
eligibility: Startups, MSMEs, academic institutions, and research organizations working in the field of flexible electronics, wearable technology, bendable sensors, and related domains are eligible to collaborate with NCFlexE. Entities must demonstrate innovative potential and alignment with the centre’s technological focus areas.
benefits: Access to state-of-the-art flexible electronics fabrication and characterization facilities, technical mentorship from IIT Kanpur experts, collaborative R&D opportunities, prototyping support, testing and validation services, training programs, and assistance in scaling lab-scale innovations to pilot production.
financial_support: NCFlexE provides subsidized access to its infrastructure and facilities on a cost-recovery basis. Financial support is primarily in the form of reduced user charges for equipment and lab usage, with potential for joint funding in collaborative projects. Specific grant or loan amounts are not detailed in the available evidence.
application_process: 1. Identify collaboration opportunity aligned with NCFlexE’s focus areas. 2. Submit a collaboration proposal detailing objectives, expected outcomes, and resource requirements. 3. Proposal reviewed by NCFlexE technical committee. 4. Upon approval, sign MoU or collaboration agreement. 5. Commence joint work with access to facilities and technical support as per agreement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of resources and alignment with centre’s priorities.
implementing_agency: Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur (IIT Kanpur)
contact_details: Email: info@ncflexe.iitk.ac.in | Phone: +91-512-259-XXXX (as per website contact section)

scheme_name: India International Jewellery Show (IIJS) Participation Support
overview: The India International Jewellery Show (IIJS) Participation Support scheme, administered by the Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC), provides financial and logistical assistance to GJEPC members for participation in IIJS Bharat shows, including IIJS Bharat - Premiere, Signature, and Tritiya. The scheme aims to enhance export opportunities, ensure long-term business planning, and offer preferential benefits such as rate locks, discounted participation fees, and exclusive facilities for committed exhibitors across multiple financial years.
target_beneficiaries: GJEPC members; exporters; MSME
eligibility: Eligibility is restricted to GJEPC members who have completed membership registration or renewal and possess valid login credentials. Applicants must submit space application forms and advance payment on or before the specified deadline (30th April 2026 for IIJS Prime Assure Scheme and IIJS Bharat – Premiere 2026 single show) to retain preference for space allotment. Non-submission or incomplete submission by the deadline results in automatic rejection and loss of preference status.
benefits: Benefits include rate lock for participation rates across IIJS Bharat – Premiere, Signature, and Tritiya for two years (2026–28), discounted rates under the IIJS Prime Assure Scheme compared to single show applications, no security deposit for two years, early show entry (30 minutes prior to official opening), access to IIJS Prime+ Lounge for owner exhibitors, discounted Networking Evening Pass, 25% discount on Innov8 Launchpad booking slots, hotel booking priority (one-day early access), priority access to sponsorship opportunities with 5% discount, special Prime Assure listing in the Digital Exhibitor Directory, and parking facility at Bombay Exhibition Centre (BEC) for booths 27 sqm and above. Exclusive benefits at IIJS Bharat - Tritiya for Prime Assure exhibitors include complimentary hotel room (3 nights) and food coupons: ₹7,500 for 18–27 sqm (1 room), ₹17,500 for 36–72 sqm (2 rooms), and ₹22,500 for 108 sqm (3 rooms).
financial_support: The scheme offers discounted participation rates for members who commit to multiple shows over two financial years (2026–28) under the IIJS Prime Assure Scheme. While specific subsidy amounts or percentages are not detailed in the evidence, the primary financial benefit is the reduction in effective cost per square meter through bundled pricing and the elimination of security deposits. Payment is processed via challan form through net banking, debit card, credit card, or NEFT after login at https://registration.gjepc.org/login.php.
application_process: 1. Visit https://registration.gjepc.org/login.php and log in using existing username and password (same as used for membership registration/renewal). New members must register first. 2. Fill out the space application form for either IIJS Prime Assure Scheme (6 shows) or IIJS Bharat – Premiere 2026 (single show). 3. Submit the application form along with advance payment on or before 30th April 2026 to avail the Discount Benefit Offer and retain preference status. 4. Failure to submit or incomplete submission by 30th April 2026 results in automatic rejection without notice and loss of preference for space allotment at IIJS Bharat - Premiere 2026 (single show) or for the IIJS Prime Assure Scheme across IIJS Bharat - Premiere 2026 & 2027, IIJS Bharat - Signature 2027 & 2028, and IIJS Bharat - Tritiya 2027 & 2028.
deadlines: The space application for all 6 IIJS Bharat shows for the year 2026–28 opens on 13th April 2026. Applications must be submitted on or before 30th April 2026 to avail the Discount Benefit Offer and preference status. Late or incomplete submissions after this date result in automatic rejection.
implementing_agency: Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC)

scheme_name: IN-SPACe Authorization for Private Space Launch
overview: IN-SPACe Authorization for Private Space Launch is a regulatory framework established by the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center (IN-SPACe) to enable private sector participation in space activities. It provides authorization for private entities to conduct space launches, establish space infrastructure, and operate space-based services in India. The scheme aims to promote private investment and innovation in the space sector by streamlining regulatory processes and ensuring compliance with national and international space laws.
target_beneficiaries: private space companies; startups; MSMEs; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Private entities including companies, startups, and MSMEs registered under Indian law, seeking to undertake space activities such as launch vehicle operations, satellite manufacturing, ground station establishment, or space-based services. Applicants must demonstrate technical capability, financial viability, and adherence to safety and regulatory norms as specified by IN-SPACe.
benefits: Authorization to conduct space launches and operations in India, access to ISRO infrastructure and technical support, regulatory clarity and single-window clearance, facilitation of technology transfer and collaboration with ISRO, and recognition as a authorized non-governmental entity (NGE) in the space sector.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or subsidies. Financial support is indirect through access to ISRO facilities on cost-sharing basis, potential for private investment, and opportunities for commercial contracts. No specific fund corpus or per-entity grant amount is allocated under this authorization framework.
application_process: 1. Visit the IN-SPACe official website at https://www.inspaceindia.org 2. Review the authorization guidelines and eligibility criteria 3. Prepare the required documentation including project report, technical details, safety plan, and company registration 4. Submit the application online through the IN-SPACe portal 5. Await preliminary review and feedback from IN-SPACe 6. Address any queries or modifications as required 7. Receive final authorization upon compliance with all regulatory requirements.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year with no fixed deadline.
implementing_agency: Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center (IN-SPACe), Department of Space

scheme_name: Gems & Jewellery Sector PLI – Design Innovation Grant
overview: The Gems & Jewellery Sector PLI – Design Innovation Grant is a scheme under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) framework aimed at boosting design innovation in the gems and jewellery sector. It provides financial incentives to manufacturers based on incremental sales of value-added products, encouraging domestic value addition and reducing import dependence. The scheme supports the development of a competitive domestic supply chain and promotes innovation-driven manufacturing in the sector.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers; MSME; startups
eligibility: Manufacturers of gems and jewellery products who are registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or as a partnership firm, and who undertake incremental investment in eligible product categories with a focus on design innovation and value addition, are eligible to apply under the scheme.
benefits: Financial incentives based on incremental sales of eligible products, support for design innovation, technical assistance for upgrading manufacturing capabilities, and facilitation of market access for value-added gems and jewellery products.
financial_support: The scheme provides a subsidy of 4–6% on incremental sales of eligible gems and jewellery products over a base year, as part of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) mechanism, to encourage investment in design-led manufacturing and value addition.
application_process: 1. Register on the official PLI portal for the Gems & Jewellery sector. 2. Submit application with details of incremental investment and production capacity. 3. Provide documentation including Certificate of Incorporation, GST details, and product specifications. 4. Await evaluation by the Project Management Agency. 5. Upon approval, sign agreement and begin production to claim incentives based on incremental sales.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: PLI for Mobile Phones & Specified Electronic Components
overview: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Mobile Phones & Specified Electronic Components is a government initiative aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing in the electronics sector. It provides financial incentives to eligible companies based on incremental sales of goods manufactured in India over a period of five years. The scheme seeks to attract large investments, enhance value addition, and generate employment in the electronics manufacturing value chain.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; large enterprises; electronics manufacturers
eligibility: Eligible applicants include companies engaged in the manufacturing of mobile phones and specified electronic components in India, with a minimum threshold of investment and incremental sales as defined in the scheme guidelines. Both domestic and foreign companies setting up new manufacturing units or expanding existing ones in India are eligible to apply.
benefits: Financial incentives in the form of production-linked incentives based on incremental sales over the base year; support for setting up manufacturing units; encouragement for technological upgradation; access to a growing domestic market; and potential for export promotion.
financial_support: The scheme provides incentives ranging from 4% to 6% on incremental sales of goods manufactured in India over a period of five years, depending on the product category and achievement of threshold investment and sales targets. The incentive is disbursed annually based on verified sales and investment claims.
application_process: 1. Review the scheme guidelines and eligibility criteria available on the MeitY website. 2. Prepare the required documentation including investment details, sales data, and manufacturing plans. 3. Submit the application through the designated online portal or as specified in the guidelines. 4. Application is evaluated by the Project Management Agency (PMA). 5. Upon approval, enter into an agreement with the government. 6. Commence production and submit periodic claims for incentives based on incremental sales. 7. Claims are verified and incentives are disbursed after validation.
deadlines: Applications were invited within a specified window as per the scheme notification; currently, the scheme is under implementation with disbursement ongoing for approved applicants.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

scheme_name: Indian National Space Promotion & Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) Seed Fund
overview: The Indian National Space Promotion & Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) Seed Fund is a financial support initiative aimed at nurturing early-stage space startups in India. It provides seed funding to innovative ventures engaged in space technology, applications, and services. The fund is designed to promote private sector participation in the Indian space economy by supporting proof-of-concept, prototype development, and early commercialization efforts. IN-SPACe, as the regulatory and promotional body under the Department of Space, administers this scheme to bridge the funding gap for emerging space entrepreneurs.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Indian-incorporated startups recognized by DPIIT or registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or LLP Act, 2008, working on innovative space technologies, applications, or services. The startup must be engaged in activities related to launch vehicles, satellites, ground systems, space-based applications, or allied domains. Preference is given to entities with a clear roadmap for technology development and market deployment within 18–24 months.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grant-in-aid for eligible expenses such as R&D, prototyping, testing, and technology development. Non-financial benefits include access to ISRO facilities and technical mentorship, regulatory guidance from IN-SPACe, networking opportunities with industry and academia, and support in intellectual property rights (IPR) facilitation. Selected startups also gain visibility through IN-SPACe’s ecosystem platforms and investor connect events.
financial_support: The Seed Fund provides grant-based financial assistance of up to INR 1 Crore per eligible startup. The grant is disbursed in milestones tied to project progress, subject to technical and financial review by IN-SPACe. Funds can be utilized for approved expenses including personnel costs, material procurement, software/tools, testing, and prototyping, as per the approved project plan. The support is non-dilutive and does not require equity sharing.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 1 Crore
application_process: 1. Visit the official IN-SPACe website and navigate to the Seed Fund section. 2. Review the eligibility criteria and guidelines document. 3. Prepare a detailed project proposal including technical approach, budget, timeline, and team credentials. 4. Submit the application online through the designated portal with all required documents. 5. Applications are screened for eligibility and technical merit by an expert committee. 6. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for a presentation or interview. 7. Final selection is based on innovation, feasibility, impact, and alignment with national space goals. 8. Selected startups receive a sanction letter and undergo due diligence before fund disbursement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds
implementing_agency: Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe), Department of Space, Government of India

overview: The ISRO Technology Transfer Programme facilitates the transfer of ISRO-developed technologies to Indian industries, startups, and academic institutions for commercialization and societal benefit. It aims to bridge the gap between space research and industrial application by enabling access to ISRO's intellectual property, know-how, and technical expertise. The programme supports innovation in sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, telecommunications, and manufacturing through licensing, joint development, and technical collaboration.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; academic institutions; industries
eligibility: Indian industries, startups, MSMEs, academic institutions, and R&D organizations are eligible to apply for technology transfer under the programme. Applicants must demonstrate the capability to absorb, develop, and commercialize the transferred technology for end-user applications.
benefits: Access to ISRO's patented technologies, technical know-how, and expertise; support for prototype development and testing; assistance in regulatory compliance and certification; opportunities for joint development and co-branding; potential for scaling up production with ISRO's technical guidance.
financial_support: Financial terms, including licensing fees, royalties, and revenue-sharing models, are negotiated on a case-by-case basis depending on the technology, scope of transfer, and commercialization plan. ISRO does not provide grants or subsidies under this programme; financial arrangements are based on mutual agreement between ISRO and the recipient.
application_process: 1. Identify the desired technology from ISRO's Technology Transfer Portal. 2. Submit a formal application expressing interest in technology transfer. 3. Provide details of the applicant organization, intended use, and commercialization plan. 4. ISRO evaluates the application based on technical merit, capability, and alignment with programme goals. 5. Upon approval, negotiate terms of transfer including licensing, royalties, and support. 6. Execute a Technology Transfer Agreement (TTA) and proceed with implementation.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Department of Space, Government of India

overview: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing is a Government of India initiative aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing and exports in the electronics sector. It provides financial incentives to eligible companies based on incremental sales of goods manufactured in India over a period of five years. The scheme targets large-scale electronics manufacturing units to enhance India's position in global electronics value chains.
target_beneficiaries: large-scale electronics manufacturers; domestic companies; foreign companies with manufacturing units in India
eligibility: Eligible applicants include companies engaged in manufacturing of specified electronic goods in India, with a minimum threshold of investment and incremental sales as defined under the scheme guidelines. Both domestic and foreign companies setting up new manufacturing units or expanding existing ones in India are eligible to apply.
benefits: Financial incentives in the form of production-linked incentives on incremental sales of manufactured goods over the base year. Non-financial benefits include facilitation of clearances, single-window approvals, and support for setting up manufacturing units through coordination with central and state agencies.
financial_support: The scheme provides incentives ranging from 4% to 6% on incremental sales (over base year) of goods manufactured in India, for a period of five years. The incentive is disbursed annually based on verified sales and investment claims submitted by the approved applicants.
application_process: 1. Submit application online through the designated portal 2. Provide details of proposed investment, manufacturing capacity, and employment generation 3. Upload required documents including incorporation certificates, project reports, and bank details 4. Application reviewed by the Project Management Agency (PMA) 5. Shortlisted applicants invited for presentation before the Empowered Committee 6. Final approval granted by the Empowered Committee based on evaluation criteria 7. Signing of approval letter and commencement of production 8. Annual submission of claims for incentive based on verified incremental sales
deadlines: Application window varies by component; specific timelines are notified through official circulars on the MeitY website.

overview: The Geospatial Data Liberalisation – NGIS Policy is a policy initiative by the Department of Science and Technology (DST) aimed at liberalizing access to geospatial data in India. The policy seeks to deregulate the acquisition and use of geospatial data, promote innovation in the geospatial sector, and encourage private sector participation in mapping and geospatial services. It aims to democratize access to high-resolution geospatial data for startups, industries, and researchers, fostering innovation in sectors like urban planning, agriculture, disaster management, and infrastructure development.
target_beneficiaries: startups; private sector; researchers; industries; startups in geospatial technology
eligibility: The policy applies to all Indian entities, including startups, private companies, research institutions, and individuals, who wish to access, use, or generate geospatial data. There are no prior approval or licensing requirements for the acquisition, generation, preparation, dissemination, distribution, dissemination, publication, or updating of digital geospatial data and maps within the territory of India.
benefits: The policy removes the need for prior approvals, security clearances, licenses, and other restrictions on the collection, generation, preparation, dissemination, distribution, dissemination, publication, or updating of digital geospatial data and maps within India. It enables free access to geospatial data for startups, industries, and researchers, fostering innovation in sectors such as agriculture, urban planning, disaster management, and infrastructure. It supports the growth of the Indian geospatial industry and aligns with the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision by promoting self-reliance in geospatial technologies.
financial_support: The policy does not provide direct financial support, grants, loans, or subsidies. It is a policy liberalization initiative that removes regulatory barriers to enable private sector investment and innovation in the geospatial sector. Financial support for geospatial initiatives may be accessed through other DST schemes such as the Research, Development, and Innovation (RDI) Scheme or the Fund of Funds for Startups, but these are not part of the Geospatial Data Liberalisation – NGIS Policy itself.
application_process:
1. No prior approval or license is required for the acquisition, generation, preparation, dissemination, distribution, publication, or updating of digital geospatial data and maps within India.
2. Entities can directly access geospatial data from government sources such as the Survey of India, National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), and other authorized agencies.
3. Private entities can generate their own geospatial data using drones, satellites, or other technologies without seeking prior permission.
4. Data can be used, shared, published, or commercialized freely for any lawful purpose.
5. Entities must comply with applicable laws related to national security, privacy, and data protection, but no separate geospatial licensing is required.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. The policy is in effect and applications or data access requests can be made at any time.
implementing_agency: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology

scheme_name: Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC) Data Access for Startups
overview: Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC) India is a Joint Industry Body founded by stakeholder bodies representing Broadcasters, Advertisers, and Advertising and Media Agencies. It provides transparent, accurate, and inclusive TV audience measurement data to power efficient media spends and content decisions in India's broadcasting sector. BARC India operates the world's largest television audience measurement system, covering approximately 257,000+ individuals across 58,000+ households. The scheme offers data access for startups through its products and insights, though no specific startup-focused grant or financial support program is detailed in the evidence.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: BARC India serves Broadcasters, Advertisers, and Advertising and Media Agencies as its primary stakeholders. Access to data and products is governed by its policies and compliance framework, though specific eligibility criteria for startups to access BARC data are not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence.
benefits: Access to currency data (TV viewership estimates), insight products for media spends and content decisions, YUMI Analytics software for data reporting and analysis, SpotTrek for next-day spot monitoring, BI Study research from 3 lakh households, and transparent audience measurement system that powers efficient media planning.
financial_support: No specific financial support, grants, loans, or subsidies for startups are mentioned in the evidence. BARC India operates as a self-regulated, not-for-profit Joint Industry Body funded by its stakeholder bodies (IBDF 60%, ISA 20%, AAAI 20%) and generates revenue through data and insight product sales to clients.
application_process: No specific application process for startups to access BARC data is detailed in the evidence. General access to products and data likely involves contacting BARC India through its official channels for inquiries about data access, product subscriptions, or partnership opportunities.
deadlines: No specific deadlines for startup data access applications are mentioned in the evidence.
implementing_agency: Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC) India

overview: NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) Technology Transfer scheme facilitates the transfer of ISRO-developed technologies to Indian industries, academia, and government organizations through formal agreements, handholding events, and technical support. The scheme aims to enhance industrial capabilities, promote self-reliance in space technologies, and support the growth of India's space economy by enabling industry access to ISRO's intellectual property. NSIL acts as the nodal agency under the Department of Space to manage technology transfer activities, including evaluation, agreement signing, fee remittance, and handholding by ISRO units. The scheme covers a wide range of technologies across domains such as antennas, communication & navigation, RF & electronics, remote sensing, materials, mechanical systems, optics, and software.
target_beneficiaries: entrepreneurs; industry; academia; State and Central Government organization
eligibility: Department of Space has authorised NSIL to enter into Technology Transfer Agreement with suitable entrepreneurs/Industry in India. Interested parties must submit a Technology Transfer (TT) Request through the IN-SPACe portal, followed by evaluation of company profile and technical capabilities by IN-SPACe, signing of TT Agreement with NSIL & IN-SPACe, remittance of TT Fee to NSIL, and handholding for technology transfer by ISRO.
benefits: Access to ISRO-developed technologies including antennas, communication & navigation systems, RF & electronics components, remote sensing algorithms, materials, mechanical systems, optics, and software. Benefits include handholding support from ISRO units during transfer, technology licensing opportunities, enhanced industrial capabilities, promotion of self-reliance in critical space technologies, and contribution to national development. The scheme enables industries to acquire knowhow for manufacturing and commercialization of space technologies.
financial_support: The scheme involves remittance of a Technology Transfer (TT) Fee to NSIL as part of the transfer process. However, the evidence does not specify the quantum, type, or mechanism of financial support beyond the requirement to pay the TT Fee. No details are provided on subsidies, grants, loans, or funding amounts associated with the technology transfer.
application_process: 1. Submission of Technology Transfer (TT) Request through IN-SPACe portal (link: https://www.inspace.gov.in/inspace?id=inspace_nge_proposal_page&sys_id=4e0bb01f87389150cc8310aabbbb352d). 2. Evaluation of company profile and technical capabilities by IN-SPACe. 3. Signing of TT Agreement with NSIL & IN-SPACe. 4. Remittance of TT Fee to NSIL. 5. Handholding for technology transfer by ISRO.
