The India Game Developer Conference (IGDC) Support scheme is a government initiative under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at supporting the growth of the game development industry in India. The scheme provides financial and non-financial support to game developers, startups, and MSMEs in the gaming sector to foster innovation, enhance competitiveness, and promote India as a global hub for game development. It includes financial assistance for participation in the India Game Developer Conference and related activities to strengthen the domestic gaming ecosystem.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; game developers; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Indian game developers, startups, and MSMEs engaged in game development, registered under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) as startups or with the Ministry of MSME as micro or small enterprises, incorporated in Indian territory, with annual revenue not exceeding INR 5 crores in any financial year since incorporation, and having raised funds not exceeding INR 10 crores.
benefits: Financial support for participation in the India Game Developer Conference (IGDC), including reimbursement of travel, accommodation, and conference fees; access to networking opportunities with global gaming industry stakeholders; exposure to international gaming trends and technologies; opportunities for business collaboration and investment; and recognition as part of India's growing gaming ecosystem.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance for participation in the India Game Developer Conference (IGDC), including reimbursement of travel, accommodation, and conference fees, subject to a maximum ceiling of INR 50 lakhs per entity for the scheme duration.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 50 Lakhs per entity
application_process: 1. Visit the online portal at https://tec.gov.in/tcrs 2. Register as an applicant (Start-up or MSE) 3. Fill in the application form with details of the applicant and the game development project 4. Upload required documents including Certificate of Incorporation, DPIIT/Udyam Registration, audited financial statements, test reports, product certificates, invoices, and undertakings 5. Submit the application online before the 20th of the last month of the quarter 6. Await screening by the Telecom Centres of Excellence (TCOE) 7. Upon clearance, the application is forwarded to the Technical Evaluation Committee for evaluation 8. After technical evaluation, the proposal is sent to the Administrative Committee for approval 9. Upon approval, funds are disbursed by the Telecom Centres of Excellence (TCOE) within 7 days of receipt from Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN)
deadlines: Applications can be submitted through the online portal on or before the 20th of the last month in the quarter.
implementing_agency: Telecom Centres of Excellence (TCOE)

overview: Startup India Climate Action Challenge is a program under the Startup India initiative aimed at supporting startups working on climate technology and green innovation. It provides a platform for startups to showcase solutions addressing climate change, with opportunities for funding, mentorship, and visibility. The challenge is part of broader efforts to promote sustainable entrepreneurship and align with national climate goals.
target_beneficiaries: startups; climate-tech startups; green-tech startups
eligibility: Startups must be DPIIT-recognised, working on innovative solutions in climate technology, green technology, or related sectors such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, waste management, or sustainable agriculture. The entity should be incorporated as a Private Limited Company, LLP, or partnership firm, with turnover not exceeding INR 200 crore (INR 300 crore for DeepTech) and within 10 years of incorporation (20 years for DeepTech).
benefits: Recognition under Startup India, access to funding schemes like Seed Fund Scheme and Fund of Funds, mentorship via MAARG, investor connect opportunities, tax benefits under Section 80-IAC, IPR fast-tracking with 80% rebate on patent filing, easier public procurement norms, and self-certification under labour and environmental laws.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through linked schemes such as the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) offering up to INR 20 lakhs as grant, and the Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) with a corpus of INR 10,000 crore, which invests in SEBI-registered AIFs that fund startups. Credit guarantee support is also available via CGSS for collateral-free debt up to INR 20 crore.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 20 Lakhs
application_process: 1. Register on the Startup India portal (startupindia.gov.in) 2. Apply for DPIIT recognition via the 'Get Recognised' section 3. Submit incorporation documents, PAN, and business description 4. Await recognition approval (typically 2-7 business days) 5. Once recognised, apply for the Climate Action Challenge through the Startup India Programs section 6. Submit proposal detailing climate innovation, impact, and scalability 7. Await evaluation and selection by the jury panel
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted year-round based on challenge cycles
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) Schemes
overview: The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) is a comprehensive framework launched by the Government of India to address climate change through eight national missions focusing on solar energy, enhanced energy efficiency, sustainable habitat, water, sustaining the Himalayan ecosystem, Green India, sustainable agriculture, and strategic knowledge for climate change. It aims to promote ecological sustainability while supporting economic development.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; agri-startups; women entrepreneurs; SC/ST
eligibility: The NAPCC is a policy framework and not a direct beneficiary scheme; its missions are implemented by various central ministries and state governments, with benefits flowing to sectors such as renewable energy, agriculture, water, forestry, and urban development through respective mission guidelines.
benefits: The NAPCC provides a coordinated approach to climate action, enabling access to financial and technical support under its eight missions, promoting renewable energy adoption, energy efficiency, sustainable agriculture, water conservation, afforestation, and climate-resilient infrastructure development across sectors.
financial_support: Financial support under NAPCC is channeled through its eight national missions, each with dedicated budget allocations; for example, the National Solar Mission and National Mission on Enhanced Energy Efficiency have specific funding mechanisms, while others rely on central and state budgetary provisions, external funding, and public-private partnerships.
application_process: As NAPCC is an overarching policy framework comprising multiple missions, there is no single application process; interested entities must apply to individual missions (e.g., Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission, National Mission for a Green India) through their respective implementing agencies and portals.
deadlines: Varies by mission; each of the eight national missions under NAPCC has its own timelines and application windows.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)

scheme_name: CERC Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM) for Startups
overview: The CERC Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM) for Startups is a market mechanism enabling startups to participate in renewable energy trading through term-ahead contracts. It facilitates price discovery and risk management for green power procurement. The scheme aims to promote renewable energy adoption among innovative enterprises by providing access to competitive, transparent bidding processes. Startups can bid for renewable power delivery over specified future periods, supporting India's clean energy transition goals.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups engaged in renewable energy projects or clean technology innovation that are registered under relevant government schemes and meet the technical and financial criteria specified in the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 and its amendments.
benefits: Access to transparent price discovery for renewable power, ability to hedge against price volatility in green energy markets, opportunity to secure long-term power purchase agreements at competitive rates, facilitation of market entry for innovative clean technology firms, and support for meeting renewable purchase obligations through market instruments.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants. Instead, it enables market-based transactions where startups can buy or sell renewable power through term-ahead contracts, with prices determined by competitive bidding. Financial support is indirect through reduced transaction costs and access to efficient price discovery mechanisms.
application_process: 1. Register as a participant in the Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM) through the power exchange platform approved by CERC. 2. Complete the necessary KYC and compliance requirements as per the exchange regulations. 3. Submit required documents including proof of startup registration, project details, and bank guarantees. 4. Participate in the bidding process for term-ahead renewable power contracts. 5. Upon successful bid, execute power purchase agreements and fulfill delivery obligations as per contract terms.
deadlines: Rolling basis — GTAM sessions are conducted regularly as per the power exchange calendar
implementing_agency: Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC)

scheme_name: National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) Innovation Fund
overview: The National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) Innovation Fund is a government initiative under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) aimed at supporting innovative solutions to combat air pollution in India. It focuses on fostering research, development, and deployment of clean technologies through financial and technical assistance. The fund encourages participation from startups, MSMEs, academic institutions, and research organizations to develop scalable and sustainable air quality improvement measures.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; academic institutions; research organizations
eligibility: Eligible applicants include startups, MSMEs, academic institutions, research organizations, and industry entities registered in India. Proposals must demonstrate innovation, technical feasibility, scalability, and potential for measurable impact on air quality improvement. Preference is given to solutions targeting particulate matter (PM2.5/PM10), nitrogen oxides, and other key pollutants in urban and industrial areas.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grants for prototype development, pilot testing, and scaling of clean air technologies. Non-financial benefits include technical mentorship, access to testing facilities, networking with policymakers and industry experts, and support for intellectual property rights (IPR) facilitation. Successful projects may also gain visibility for future funding and partnerships under national clean energy missions.
financial_support: The Innovation Fund provides grant-based financial support covering up to 70% of project costs for eligible entities, with the remaining 30% to be borne by the applicant. Funding is disbursed in milestones based on project progress review and approval by the designated technical committee. The exact quantum varies depending on the technology readiness level (TRL) and scope of the proposed intervention.
application_process: 1. Visit the official NCAP portal at https://cpcb.nic.in/ncap to access the Innovation Fund guidelines. 2. Review eligibility criteria and prepare a detailed project proposal including problem statement, objectives, methodology, budget, and expected outcomes. 3. Ensure all required documents are ready as per the checklist. 4. Submit the proposal online through the designated submission portal or via email to the specified address. 5. Await preliminary screening by the technical evaluation committee. 6. Shortlisted applicants may be invited for presentation or field validation. 7. Final selection is based on technical merit, innovation, and alignment with NCAP goals. 8. Selected projects receive sanction letters and enter into memorandum of understanding (MoU) before fund disbursement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and periodic review cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

scheme_name: Account Aggregator (AA) Framework for FinTech Startups
overview: The Account Aggregator (AA) Framework is an RBI-approved initiative that enables secure, consent-driven sharing of financial data between Financial Information Providers (FIPs) and Financial Information Users (FIUs) via Account Aggregators (AAs). It forms a foundational pillar of India's Digital Public Infrastructure, promoting financial inclusion and innovation across lending, insurance, investments, and personal finance. Sahamati acts as the collective body supporting the AA ecosystem through technical standards, certification, governance, and member services.
target_beneficiaries: startups; fintech companies; regulated entities; financial institutions; MSMEs
eligibility: Any registered and regulated entity under RBI, PFRDA, SEBI, IRDAI, or Department of Revenue (GSTN) can participate in the AA ecosystem as a Financial Information Provider (FIP), Financial Information User (FIU), Account Aggregator (AA), or Technology Service Provider (TSP), provided they obtain certification for their APIs as per Sahamati Certification Guidelines and are 'Live' or 'Ready to go Live' in the AA production environment.
benefits: Members gain access to Sahamati Central Registry (UAT and Production), Common Token Issuance Service, member dashboards (e.g., sAAns), technical health data via APIs, support application access, inter-member dispute resolution framework, implementation/specification assistance, participation in participatory governance forums (Committees and Councils on fair use, economic model, interoperability, fraud prevention), tech working groups, access to Governing Council minutes, advocacy and education benefits including member-driven workshops, on-demand sessions, themed events, and discussion forums.
financial_support: The Account Aggregator Framework does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies to participating entities. Instead, it enables indirect financial benefits by improving access to credit, reducing operational costs in lending and underwriting, and expanding market reach for financial services through consent-based data sharing. For example, AA has enabled loans worth ₹1.6 lakh crore across 1.8+ crore loan accounts as of February 2026.
application_process: 1. Get registered with a Financial Service Regulator (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, or GSTN). 2. Implement the required module (FIP/FIU/AA/TSP) using RBI-defined API specifications published by ReBIT. 3. Test the module in RBI-approved Account Aggregator Sandboxes. 4. Enrol the module in the UAT-Central Registry for testing in the development environment. 5. Obtain certification from a Sahamati-empanelled auditor for adherence to ReBIT Technical Standards. 6. Get details publicised by Sahamati in the Central Registry upon going live. 7. Launch services with customers.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Sahamati – Collective of Account Aggregator Ecosystem
contact_details: Email: membership@sahamati.org.in | For RE membership: memberservices@sahamati.org.in | For certification: services@sahamati.org.in | For Fair Use: fairuse@sahamati.org.in | For SaaNS access: memberservices@sahamati.org.in | For grievances: operations@sahamati.org.in

overview: The UPI Innovation Fund (NPCI) is a scheme under the National Payments Corporation of India aimed at fostering innovation in the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) ecosystem. It supports startups and innovators developing solutions that enhance UPI's functionality, security, and reach. The fund is part of NPCI's broader initiative to strengthen India's digital payments infrastructure through collaboration with fintech entities.
target_beneficiaries: startups; fintech companies; innovators
eligibility: Startups and innovators working on UPI-related technologies, including but not limited to payment gateways, UPI-enabled apps, security solutions, and value-added services on the UPI platform, are eligible to apply. Entities must be registered in India and demonstrate alignment with NPCI's vision for digital payments.
benefits: Selected beneficiaries receive financial support, technical mentorship from NPCI experts, access to UPI sandbox environments, potential integration with NPCI's product suite, and visibility through NPCI's innovation network. Non-financial benefits include guidance on compliance, scalability, and market readiness.
financial_support: The UPI Innovation Fund provides grant-based financial support to selected startups and innovators. The quantum of support is determined on a case-by-case basis depending on the innovation's scope, impact, and alignment with NPCI's strategic goals. Funds are disbursed in milestones tied to project deliverables.
application_process: 1. Visit the NPCI Partner Program or Developer Studio section on the NPCI website. 2. Review the UPI Innovation Fund guidelines and eligibility criteria. 3. Submit a detailed proposal outlining the innovation, its impact on UPI, and implementation plan. 4. Await evaluation by the NPCI innovation committee. 5. If shortlisted, participate in technical discussions and due diligence. 6. Receive approval and sign agreement for fund disbursement.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)

overview: The IRDAI Regulatory Sandbox for InsurTech is a framework established by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) to enable innovative insurance products, services, and business models to be tested in a controlled environment with regulatory relaxations. It aims to foster innovation in the insurance sector by allowing startups and insurers to experiment with new technologies under supervision. The sandbox provides a safe space for testing without immediately requiring full compliance with all regulatory norms, subject to safeguards and oversight.
target_beneficiaries: startups; insurers; InsurTech companies
eligibility: Entities eligible to apply include insurance companies registered with IRDAI, InsurTech startups, technology firms, and other organizations proposing innovative insurance-related products, services, or processes. Applicants must demonstrate novelty, technological innovation, and potential benefits to policyholders or the insurance ecosystem. Proposals must include a clear testing plan, risk mitigation measures, and exit strategy.
benefits: Participants receive regulatory relaxations tailored to their innovation, enabling testing without full compliance with certain provisions of the Insurance Act, 1938, and IRDAI regulations during the sandbox tenure. They gain access to regulatory guidance, mentorship, and a structured environment to validate their solutions. Successful testing may lead to smoother regulatory approval for wider market launch.
financial_support: The IRDAI Regulatory Sandbox does not provide direct financial support, grants, or funding to participating entities. Support is limited to regulatory facilitation, guidance, and waivers of specific compliance requirements during the testing period. Any financial investment or operational costs must be borne by the applicant.
application_process: 1. Submit an application to IRDAI with details of the innovative product, service, or technology to be tested. 2. Include a comprehensive testing plan, objectives, duration, resources, and risk mitigation framework. 3. Disclose customer protection measures, data privacy safeguards, and exit strategy. 4. Await evaluation by IRDAI’s Sandbox Evaluation Committee. 5. If approved, enter into a sandbox agreement outlining terms, conditions, and regulatory relaxations. 6. Conduct the test under IRDAI supervision. 7. Submit periodic reports and a final evaluation report upon completion.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year as per IRDAI notifications.
implementing_agency: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)

overview: PFRDA Innovation for PensionTech Startups is a scheme launched by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) to support startups innovating in the pension technology space. The initiative aims to foster innovation in pension services through regulatory sandbox frameworks and digital platforms. It encourages the development of solutions that enhance accessibility, efficiency, and user experience in pension systems. The scheme is part of PFRDA’s broader efforts to modernize pension delivery and promote financial inclusion.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups incorporated in India working on innovative pension technology solutions, including but not limited to digital onboarding, grievance redressal, pension analytics, and subscriber education platforms, are eligible to apply under the PFRDA Innovation for PensionTech Startups scheme.
benefits: Selected startups gain access to PFRDA’s regulatory sandbox environment, enabling live testing of innovations with real users under supervision. They receive mentorship from PFRDA officials, technical guidance, and potential pathways for scaling solutions across national pension schemes like NPS and APY. The scheme also offers visibility through PFRDA’s official channels and opportunities to collaborate with intermediaries such as CRAs, pension funds, and Points of Presence.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or funding to startups. Support is primarily non-financial, focusing on regulatory facilitation, sandbox access, and technical collaboration. Any financial engagement would be subject to separate agreements outside the scope of this innovation initiative.
application_process: 1. Visit the PFRDA official website and navigate to the Innovation or Regulatory Sandbox section. 2. Review the guidelines for the PensionTech Startups initiative. 3. Prepare a detailed proposal outlining the innovation, its relevance to pension systems, and testing requirements. 4. Submit the application through the designated portal or email as specified in the guidelines. 5. Await review by the PFRDA Innovation Committee. 6. If shortlisted, present the solution for evaluation. 7. Upon approval, enter the regulatory sandbox for testing and refinement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)

scheme_name: National Mission for a Green India (GIM)
overview: The National Mission for a Green India (GIM) is one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) aimed at protecting, restoring, and enhancing India's forest cover and responding to climate change through a combination of adaptation and mitigation measures. It focuses on increasing forest/tree cover on 5 million hectares of forest/non-forest lands and improving the quality of forest cover on another 5 million hectares. The mission emphasizes ecosystem services such as biodiversity, water, biomass, and carbon sequestration, while also supporting forest-dependent communities through livelihood improvement.
target_beneficiaries: forest-dependent communities; local communities; Panchayati Raj Institutions; Joint Forest Management Committees; NGOs; state forest departments
eligibility: The mission is implemented through State Forest Departments and other designated agencies. Funds are released to State Governments based on approved Annual Plans of Operations (APOs). Eligible implementing agencies include State Forest Departments, Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs), Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), NGOs, and other local institutions involved in afforestation, reforestation, and forest conservation activities. Activities must align with the mission’s objectives and be part of the State’s APO approved by the National Steering Committee.
benefits: Financial support for afforestation, reforestation, and forest conservation activities; technical guidance and monitoring; capacity building for local communities and institutions; improved access to non-timber forest products (NTFPs); enhanced watershed management; biodiversity conservation; carbon sequestration benefits; and livelihood generation for forest-dependent communities through sustainable forest management and value addition.
financial_support: The mission provides central financial assistance in the form of grants to State Governments for implementing approved Annual Plans of Operations (APOs). Funding is released in installments based on utilization certificates and progress reports. The financial support covers activities such as plantation, soil and moisture conservation, livelihood improvement, and monitoring and evaluation. The cost-sharing pattern is typically 90:10 (Centre:State) for Himalayan and Northeastern states, and 60:40 for other states.
application_process: 1. State Forest Departments prepare Annual Plans of Operations (APOs) based on the GIM guidelines and submit them to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). 2. The APOs are appraised by the National Mission Directorate and the National Steering Committee (NSC). 3. Upon approval, funds are released in installments to the State Governments. 4. States implement the projects through Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs), Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), and other local bodies. 5. Progress is monitored through periodic reporting, field visits, and third-party evaluations. 6. Utilization certificates and audited statements of expenditure are submitted for subsequent fund releases.
deadlines: Annual cycle — APOs are typically submitted by States before the start of the financial year (April), with mid-year reviews possible.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

scheme_name: GIFT City Financial Services Startup Support
overview: GIFT City Financial Services Startup Support is a program designed to foster innovation and growth in the financial technology and banking, financial services, and insurance (BFSI) sectors by providing startups with access to GIFT City's infrastructure, regulatory sandbox, and ecosystem benefits. The scheme aims to attract and nurture FinTech startups by offering them a conducive environment for development, testing, and scaling of financial products and services within India's first international financial services centre.
target_beneficiaries: startups; FinTech startups; BFSI startups
eligibility: Startups operating in the financial technology (FinTech), banking, financial services, and insurance (BFSI) sectors that are incorporated as private limited companies, LLPs, or partnerships and are working on innovative financial products, services, or processes. Preference may be given to entities seeking to leverage GIFT City's regulatory sandbox or international financial services platform.
benefits: Access to GIFT City's plug-and-play infrastructure, high-speed connectivity, and 24x7 operational support; eligibility to apply for the IBBI-regulated regulatory sandbox; facilitation in obtaining necessary approvals from financial regulators; networking opportunities with banks, financial institutions, and investors; tax benefits under the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Act; and support for international business setup and operations.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or subsidies. Instead, support is primarily non-financial, focusing on infrastructure access, regulatory facilitation, and ecosystem enablement. Startups may benefit indirectly through reduced operational costs, tax incentives under SEZ provisions, and access to funding networks within GIFT City.
application_process: 1. Visit the official GIFT City website or contact the GIFT City Council for startup engagement. 2. Submit an expression of interest detailing the startup’s FinTech/BFSI innovation and business model. 3. Undergo preliminary evaluation by GIFT City authorities. 4. If shortlisted, present the proposal to the relevant committee for approval. 5. Upon approval, complete registration formalities and allocate workspace allotment process. 6. Begin operations and access available support services including sandbox application if applicable.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on availability and evaluation cycles.
implementing_agency: GIFT City Council (GCC), under the aegis of the Government of Gujarat and Government of India

overview: The IFSCA FinTech Incentive Scheme (GIFT City) is designed to promote and support FinTech innovation within the International Financial Services Centre at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat. It aims to create a conducive ecosystem for FinTech startups and entities by providing regulatory support, access to infrastructure, and facilitation for setting up operations in the IFSC. The scheme encourages the development and testing of innovative financial products and services under a regulated environment, leveraging GIFT IFSC's status as India's maiden international financial services centre.
target_beneficiaries: startups; FinTech entities
eligibility: Entities interested in setting up FinTech operations in GIFT IFSC must engage with the IFSCA Development team for guidance on opportunities and the application process. All entities except Market Infrastructure Institutions, Foreign Universities, and Payment Service Providers are required to fill the Common Application Form (CAF) along with vertical-specific annexures. The application is submitted via the SWIT Portal (https://swit.ifsca.gov.in/).
benefits: Benefits include access to a unified regulatory framework, ease of doing business in a regulated IFSC environment, opportunity to operate in India's first international financial services centre, facilitation through the IFSCA Development team for information and presentations, access to networking and collaboration opportunities within the GIFT IFSC ecosystem, and support for regulatory compliance and approvals.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or subsidies. Support is primarily non-financial, focusing on regulatory facilitation, access to infrastructure, and ecosystem enablement. Any financial aspects related to setup or operations (such as fees for application, registration, or ongoing compliance) are to be borne by the applicant entity as per IFSCA's fee structure.
application_process: 1. Engage with the IFSCA Development team at development[at]ifsca[dot]gov[dot]in to seek information on opportunities and the process for setting up business in GIFT IFSC. 2. Request a presentation on your business plan if needed. 3. Once decided to apply, connect with the concerned regulatory team as per the relevant vertical (e.g., FinTech Sandbox) for queries on the regulatory framework or application process. 4. Fill the Common Application Form (CAF) and download vertical-specific annexures (for FinTech Sandbox: Preliminary Sandbox Application Form and Fintech Sandbox Application form). 5. Submit the final application via the SWIT Portal at https://swit.ifsca.gov.in/. 6. Await outreach from the regulatory team for any further queries within 7 working days of submission. 7. IFSCA will strive to take a final decision on all applications within 45 days.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA)
contact_details: Email: development[at]ifsca[dot]gov[dot]in | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

overview: EESL Energy Efficiency Innovation Support is a program by Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL) to facilitate business development through partnerships with technology service providers, channel partners, and strategic partners. It enables EESL to aggregate demand for consultancy services and energy efficiency projects across sectors like lighting, buildings, industry, electric mobility, smart metering, and agriculture. The program operates via registration processes where partners submit proposals, documents, and a refundable security deposit, and are evaluated for approval to collaborate on projects such as DEEP, Urja Bachat Sewa, and PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana in Odisha.
target_beneficiaries: technology service providers; channel partners; strategic partners; MSME; government departments; public sector undertakings
eligibility: Interested parties must register via the EESL website, submit a filled registration form along with requisite documents including GST Certificate, PAN Card, Demand Draft/NEFT/RTGS of Rupees One Lakh Only as refundable security deposit, To Whom It May Concern letter, Self-Declaration for Blacklisting, Contract Agreement copies, Non-Disclosure Agreement, PPP MII and Land Border Sharing Certificate, Compliance Matrix, EFT form, and Cancelled Cheque. Applicants must not have been blacklisted by any Central/State Government or Public Sector Undertaking.
benefits: Registered partners gain access to EESL's project pipeline, opportunity to generate leads and secure orders for energy efficiency projects, remuneration via success fees (4-5% of order value) or designated charges (5% of CFA & SFA per consumer), platform for promoting technology solutions, and collaboration with EESL on consultancy assignments. Benefits also include non-financial support such as technical guidance, project facilitation, and access to EESL's network of stakeholders including MSMEs, government bodies, and utilities.
financial_support: Financial support varies by partner type: Technology Solution Providers pay a one-time registration fee of INR 5,000 (including GST) and earn 5% of invoice value (excluding GST) as project facilitation fees, plus INR 25,000 per event for financial sponsorship. Channel Partners receive payments after deducting 5% of Central and State Financial Assistance per consumer as EESL charges for supervision and support. Strategic Partners earn success fees based on order value: 4% for orders between INR 0.10–10 Crores, 4.5% for INR 10–25 Crores, and 5% for orders above INR 25 Crores, payable upon receipt of payment from the end consumer. All partners must submit a refundable security deposit of INR 1 Lakh, returnable after 2 years and 3 months from contract execution.
application_process: 1. Visit EESL website and fill the registration form via the provided link (e.g., Registration of Technology Service Provider, Channel Partners, or Strategic Partners). 2. Submit the printed form along with all requisite documents in physical form as per EESL prescribed format. 3. Include a refundable security deposit of INR 1 Lakh via Demand Draft/NEFT/RTGS in favor of Energy Efficiency Services Limited. 4. Submit self-declaration for blacklisting on company letterhead. 5. Provide To Whom It May Concern letter, PPP MII and Land Border Sharing Certificate, Compliance Matrix, EFT form, and cancelled cheque. 6. Submit two copies of Contract/Definitive Agreement and Non-Disclosure Agreement on stamp paper after registration. 7. Send all documents via registered post to the specified address (e.g., GM (CDP) or Head (Cluster Contract) at EESL, Ikon Tower, Noida). 8. Await evaluation by EESL and approval by competent authority. 9. Receive Letter of Registration upon approval. 10. Execute Non-Disclosure Agreement within 7 days of registration letter issuance.
application_portal_url: https://eeslindia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Expression of Interest for Technical Solution Provider1.pdf
deadlines: Last Date for Submission of Application: 04th Mar 2026 at 23:00 Hrs (for TSP EOI issued 02nd Feb 2026); 15/01/2026 at 1100 Hrs (for Strategic Partner EOI issued 24.12.2025); 16/01/2026 (for Odisha Channel Partner EOI issued 16/01/2026)
implementing_agency: Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL)
contact_details: Email: info@eesl.co.in | Phone: 0120-6541601 (Corporate Office, Noida) | Address: 1 to 4th Floor, IKON Tower, FC-24C, Sector-16A, Film City, Noida-201301, U.P.

scheme_name: National Programme for Prevention & Control of Cancer (NPCC)
overview: The National Programme for Prevention & Control of Cancer (NPCC) is a public health initiative under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare aimed at reducing cancer incidence and mortality through prevention, early detection, diagnosis, treatment, and palliative care. It focuses on strengthening infrastructure, capacity building, and awareness generation across the country. The programme supports screening for common cancers such as cervical, breast, and oral cancer at various levels of the healthcare system.
target_beneficiaries: general public; women; elderly; rural populations; healthcare facilities
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component: individuals are eligible for screening based on age and risk factors (e.g., women aged 30-65 for cervical and breast cancer screening); healthcare institutions (government hospitals, CHCs, PHCs) are eligible for infrastructure and human resource support under the programme; NGOs and academic institutions may participate in awareness and training activities as per guidelines.
benefits: Financial support for setting up cancer diagnostic and treatment facilities; free or subsidized cancer screening services for eligible populations; training of healthcare workers in early detection and palliative care; strengthened referral linkages between primary, secondary, and tertiary care centers; availability of essential cancer medicines at reduced cost; public awareness campaigns on cancer prevention and early symptoms.
financial_support: Financial support is provided to states and union territories under the National Health Mission (NHM) framework for infrastructure development, procurement of equipment, training of manpower, and implementation of screening and treatment activities. Funds are allocated based on state-specific proposals and disease burden, with central government contributing a defined share and states providing the remaining portion as per NHM funding norms.
application_process: 1. States/UTs submit annual Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under the National Health Mission (NHM) for cancer-related activities under NPCC. 2. Proposals are appraised by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare based on norms, disease burden, and gap analysis. 3. Upon approval, funds are released in installments as per NHM financial management guidelines. 4. Implementation is monitored through regular reporting, field visits, and performance reviews. 5. Utilization certificates and audit reports are submitted by states for subsequent fund releases.
deadlines: Annual — aligned with the National Health Mission (NHM) planning cycle; proposals typically submitted during the financial year planning process.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

scheme_name: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) BharatPay
overview: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) BharatPay is a digital payments initiative by NPCI, an RBI-regulated entity, aimed at enabling seamless and secure digital transactions across India. It encompasses platforms like UPI, RuPay, BHIM, and NACH to promote financial inclusion and modernize retail payments. The scheme supports interoperable, real-time payments for individuals, merchants, and businesses through a robust, scalable infrastructure.
target_beneficiaries: individuals; merchants; businesses; banks; fintech companies
eligibility: Eligibility varies by product: For UPI, any individual with a bank account linked to a UPI-enabled app can participate; for RuPay, banks issuing cards must be NPCI members; for BHIM, users need a bank account and mobile number; for NACH, institutions must register as corporate or retail users with participating banks.
benefits: Benefits include instant 24x7 fund transfers, low transaction costs, wide acceptance across merchants and banks, interoperability, enhanced security via UPI PIN and biometric authentication, support for bill payments, merchant QR codes, international usage through UPI One World, and access to transaction history and complaint redressal mechanisms.
financial_support: NPCI BharatPay does not provide direct financial support such as grants or loans. It operates as a non-profit infrastructure provider facilitating digital transactions. Revenue is generated through transaction fees paid by member banks and participants, which are used to sustain operations and innovation.
application_process: 1. For UPI: Download a UPI-enabled bank app, register using mobile number linked to bank account, set UPI PIN, and link bank account. 2. For RuPay: Approach a member bank to issue a RuPay debit/credit card. 3. For BHIM: Download BHIM app, verify mobile number, link bank account, set UPI PIN. 4. For merchants: Register with a bank or payment gateway to accept UPI/QR payments. 5. For NACH: Corporates/institutions must register with their bank, submit mandate forms, and complete onboarding via NPCI’s NACH portal.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Users and entities can onboard anytime.
implementing_agency: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)

scheme_name: Sustainable Finance for Green MSMEs (SIDBI Green Finance)
overview: Sustainable Finance for Green MSMEs (SIDBI Green Finance) is a loan scheme aimed at supporting MSMEs in adopting green technologies and sustainable practices. It provides financial assistance for projects related to energy efficiency, renewable energy, pollution control, and other environmentally friendly initiatives. The scheme is part of SIDBI's broader efforts to promote sustainable development within the MSME sector through targeted lending and capacity building.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSME units in the manufacturing or services sector. Applicant unit should be in operation for at least three years and should have earned cash profit in the last two years of operation and should not be in default to any bank/FI. Proposal should be in the range of C1-C8. The unit should have undergone the process of Detailed Energy Audit (DEA) through a technical agency/consultant having BEE certified Energy Auditors. Further, the Detailed Project Report (DPR) prepared by the technical agency/consultant should have been vetted by EEC, SIDBI. The unit should not have availed Performance Linked Grant under the WB-GEF Project for the proposed EE Project. The unit should be in compliance with the Environment & Social Management Framework.
benefits: Financial products that enable climate and environment-friendly investments. Includes end-to-end digital processes, quick disbursement, collateral-free financing, and support for energy-saving measures. The scheme promotes investment in clean production and energy-efficient technologies under bilateral lines of credit from international agencies such as JICA, AFD, and KfW. It also enhances awareness of climate control benefits among MSE clusters.
financial_support: Upto 90% of the project cost with minimum loan amount of ₹10 lakh and maximum loan amount not to exceed ₹150 lakh per eligible borrower. The repayment period including initial moratorium period of up to 6 months shall not be more than 36 months for loans up to ₹50 lakh and 60 months for loans beyond ₹50 lakh. Minimum promoter's contribution of 10% of the project cost. Interest rate as per internal rating. Security includes hypothecation of assets created under the project, collateral security where necessary, and CGTMSE cover if available.
application_process: 1. After the Detailed Energy Audit, the prospective borrower shall submit the Detailed Project Report (DPR) to SIDBI for its vetting by EEC. 2. If required, the sample format of the DPR shall be made available by EEC. 3. The Borrower shall submit application to SIDBI BOs along with a copy of the DPR vetted by EEC. 4. Eligible amount of capital subsidy under CLCSS, TEQUP, etc. shall also be sanctioned along with the loan as per prevalent guidelines. 5. Disbursement shall be made after compliance of terms & conditions of the sanction stipulated in the LoI and documentation as per the extant guidelines for DCS.
implementing_agency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

scheme_name: Open Credit Enablement Network (OCEN) for Lenders
overview: Open Credit Enablement Network (OCEN) is a framework of application programming interfaces (APIs) designed to democratize credit access for MSMEs by enabling interaction between lenders, loan agents, collections and disbursement partners, derived data providers, and account aggregators. It aims to solve the MSME credit gap of ₹20-25 trillion by facilitating short-tenure, small-ticket loans through standardized, consent-based data sharing and specialized participant roles. OCEN 4.0 introduces product and participant registries maintained by SROs, enabling a cambrian explosion of customized cash-flow based lending products across sectors.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; lenders; loan agents; borrowers
eligibility: Participants must be regulated entities such as lenders (regulated by RBI), Loan Agents, Derived Data Partners, Collections Partners, Disbursement Partners, KYC Partners, or Account Aggregators. They must comply with OCEN 4.0 API specifications, security requirements (HTTPS, Two-way TLS, digital signatures), and onboard via the Participant Registry verified by SROs. Lenders create and own credit products; Loan Agents act as borrower agents to help select the best loan offer.
benefits: Enables access to formal, affordable credit for MSMEs; reduces loan processing costs at scale; provides easy access to new borrower segments; allows lenders to leverage new data sets (AA, GST, bank statements) for underwriting; supports specialized roles (Loan Agent, Collections Partner, Disbursement Partner, etc.) to enhance system efficiency; facilitates escrow-based repayments to mitigate collections risk; enables dispute resolution via SRO mediation; promotes financial inclusion through consent-based data sharing; unlocks value of data in India’s digital ecosystem for economic growth.
financial_support: OCEN does not provide direct financial support. It is a technical framework that enables lenders to offer loans. Loan amounts, tenures, and interest rates are determined by individual lenders based on borrower underwriting. The framework supports short-tenure (max 3 months) and small-ticket loans (as low as Rs.100). Revenue for participants comes from loan origination fees (Loan Agents), interest income (Lenders), and service fees (other partners).
application_process: 1. Onboard as a participant via the Participant Registry (managed by SROs) with role-specific verification. 2. Create or manage credit products via the Product Registry (Lenders) or Product Networks (Loan Agents). 3. Integrate with OCEN 4.0 standardized APIs using client credentials (client_id, client_secret) to generate access tokens. 4. Follow API design principles: asynchronous calls, idempotency via requestId, and security (HTTPS, Two-way TLS, digital signatures). 5. Participate in loan journeys: Loan Agents source borrowers, Lenders underwrite and disburse, Collections/Dispatch/KYC partners support as per product network. 6. Use registries to discover products, participants, and product networks for collaboration.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Onboarding and participation are open year-round.
implementing_agency: iSPIRT (in collaboration with RBI, Account Aggregator framework, and SROs)

scheme_name: SEBI FinTech Regulatory Framework for WealthTech
overview: The SEBI FinTech Regulatory Framework for WealthTech is a regulatory initiative by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) aimed at overseeing and guiding the growth of financial technology (FinTech) companies operating in the wealth management sector. It establishes guidelines and compliance requirements for entities providing digital wealth management services, including robo-advisory, digital portfolio management, and online investment platforms. The framework seeks to ensure investor protection, market integrity, and transparency while fostering innovation in the WealthTech space. It applies to intermediaries and platforms offering wealth-tech solutions under SEBI’s regulatory purview.
target_beneficiaries: wealth-tech startups; FinTech companies; digital wealth management platforms; robo-advisors
eligibility: Entities offering digital wealth management services, including robo-advisory platforms, online portfolio managers, and FinTech firms providing algorithm-based investment advice, must comply with SEBI’s regulatory framework if they fall under the definition of investment advisers or portfolio managers as per SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 or SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020.
benefits: Regulatory clarity for FinTech firms operating in wealth management; enhanced credibility and investor trust through SEBI compliance; access to a structured pathway for legal operation; protection against regulatory penalties; guidance on technology, governance, and disclosure standards; promotion of fair and ethical practices in digital wealth distribution.
financial_support: The SEBI FinTech Regulatory Framework for WealthTech does not provide direct financial support, grants, subsidies, or funding to beneficiaries. It is a regulatory guideline aimed at compliance and oversight rather than financial assistance.
application_process: 1. Determine if your wealth-tech platform falls under SEBI’s definition of an investment adviser or portfolio manager. 2. If applicable, register under SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 or SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020. 3. Ensure compliance with operational, governance, technology, and disclosure norms as outlined in the framework. 4. Implement robust cybersecurity, data protection, and audit mechanisms. 5. Submit required disclosures and reports to SEBI as per periodic reporting requirements. 6. Undergo inspections or audits as conducted by SEBI or its authorized agencies.
deadlines: Ongoing compliance — entities must adhere to the framework continuously; registration and reporting follow SEBI’s prescribed timelines under relevant regulations.
implementing_agency: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

Strengthening healthcare systems
Prioritising the well-being of every individual
Building a healthier society
application_process: Engage with the Ministry through its official website (mohfw.gov.in), explore departments such as Department of Health & Family Welfare and Department of Health Research, access services via Related Links, Help, Sitemap, Archives/Tenders, and Related Links sections, and engage via social media channels as available on the website.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India

overview: India MedTech Expo & Investment Support is a platform designed to showcase innovations in the medical technology sector, connect stakeholders, and promote investment opportunities in MedTech. The event facilitates networking between startups, investors, industry players, and government bodies to accelerate the growth of the MedTech ecosystem in India. It aims to highlight cutting-edge technologies, foster collaborations, and support the scaling of MedTech ventures through exposure and matchmaking.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; MedTech companies; innovators; investors
eligibility: Open to MedTech startups, MSMEs, innovators, and companies involved in healthcare technology, medical devices, diagnostics, and digital health solutions seeking to showcase their products or explore investment opportunities.
benefits: Opportunity to exhibit products and innovations at a national-level expo, access to potential investors and venture capitalists, networking with industry experts and healthcare institutions, visibility among policymakers and government officials, and support for business development and market access.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or subsidies; support is primarily through investment matchmaking, exhibition opportunities, and facilitation of funding connections rather than direct monetary assistance.
application_process: 1. Visit the official India MedTech Expo website or portal. 2. Register as an exhibitor, startup, or visitor based on your profile. 3. Submit company profile, product details, and innovation summary. 4. Await confirmation of participation from the organizing committee. 5. Prepare exhibit materials and attend the expo for showcasing and networking.
deadlines: Based on event schedule; specific dates announced annually for each edition of the expo.
implementing_agency: Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers

overview: The National Organ & Tissue Transplant Organisation (NOTTO) is a government initiative under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) that facilitates organ and tissue donation pledges through a national registry. It enables individuals aged 18 and above to voluntarily register as organ donors via Aadhaar-linked ABHA ID verification. The platform supports multilingual access and provides tools for verifying pledge certificates and viewing donation statistics across states and organs.
target_beneficiaries: general public; individuals aged 18 and above
eligibility: Any person not less than 18 years of age, who voluntarily authorizes the removal of any of his organ and/or tissue after death, can register as a donor. Registration requires Aadhaar number and mobile number linked to ABHA, with consent to share demographic information with the National Health Authority (NHA) for ABHA creation and use in the National Digital Health Ecosystem.
benefits: Individuals who register receive a verifiable pledge certificate that can be validated via QR code. The system allows donors to contribute to life-saving transplants, with one donor potentially saving up to 8 lives. Registered pledges are accessible to healthcare facilities and professionals within the NDHE for transplant coordination. The platform ensures data privacy and allows users to revoke consent at any time.
financial_support: NOTTO does not provide any financial support, grants, subsidies, or monetary benefits to registrants. The organ and tissue donation pledge is a purely voluntary, non-financial act of social contribution.
application_process: 1. Visit the NOTTO website at https://notto.abdm.gov.in/register 2. Select preferred language (English, Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu) 3. Enter Aadhaar number (12 digits) and mobile number linked to ABHA 4. Verify Aadhaar via OTP authentication with UIDAI 5. Read and accept the terms and conditions, including consent to share Aadhaar-demographic data with NHA for ABHA creation 6. Submit the Form 7 for Organ or Tissue Pledging as per THOTA 1994 and Rules 2014 7. Receive a downloadable pledge certificate with QR code for verification 8. Optionally verify certificate at https://notto.abdm.gov.in/verify-certificate by scanning the QR code
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Registrations are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: National Organ & Tissue Transplant Organisation (NOTTO), under the National Health Authority (NHA) and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)
contact_details: Address: 4th Floor, National Institute of Pathology, NIOP Building, Safdarjung Hospital Campus, New Delhi-110029 | Email: dir[at]notto[dot]nic[dot]in | Toll-Free Number: 1800-11-4770

scheme_name: National TB Elimination Programme – Digital Initiative
overview: The National TB Elimination Programme – Digital Initiative, known as Nikshay, is a web-enabled patient management system for TB control under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP). It is developed and maintained by the Central TB Division (CTD), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, in collaboration with the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and the World Health Organization Country office for India. Nikshay is used by health functionaries across the country in both public and private sectors to register TB cases, order tests, record treatment details, monitor adherence, and transfer cases between care providers. It also functions as the National TB Surveillance System and enables reporting of surveillance data to the Government of India.
target_beneficiaries: health functionaries; public and private healthcare providers; TB patients
eligibility: Health functionaries at various levels across the country, both in the public and private sector, who are involved in TB case management under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP).
benefits: Enables case registration, test ordering from labs, treatment recording, adherence monitoring, case transfer between providers, national TB surveillance, and reporting of surveillance data to the Government of India. The service is provided at no cost by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
financial_support: The Nikshay application is provided by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, at no cost to users. There is no financial support disbursed to beneficiaries under this digital initiative.
application_process: 1. Visit the Nikshay portal at https://nikshay.in 2. Click on 'Login' to access the system 3. For new users, register via 'New Health Facility Registration' or 'New Informant Registration' as applicable 4. Complete the required registration form with details such as state, district, block, facility, address, basic information, designation, contact number, email, and bank details (if applicable) 5. Create login credentials (username) 6. Submit the form for approval 7. Upon approval, use the login credentials to access the Nikshay dashboard 8. Navigate to relevant modules such as case registration, test ordering, treatment monitoring, etc.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Registrations are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Central TB Division (CTD TB Division (CTD), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

overview: The Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP) integrates academic learning with on-the-job training to enhance employability and bridge the skill gap. It is designed to provide students with a degree while gaining practical industry experience through apprenticeships. The programme aims to align education with industry needs and promote workforce readiness. It supports the Skill India Mission by combining formal education with structured training.
target_beneficiaries: students; youth; candidates
eligibility: Candidates must be enrolled in a recognized degree programme and meet the educational qualifications specified for the apprenticeship trade, including minimum 10+2 or equivalent as per the trade requirements.
benefits: Participants gain hands-on industry experience, earn a stipend during training, receive a degree upon completion, and improve job prospects through certified skills and NSQF alignment.
financial_support: Under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), the government reimburses 25% of the stipend paid to apprentices, capped at INR 1,500 per month per apprentice, for a maximum duration of the training period.
application_process: 1. Register as a candidate on the apprenticeshipindia.org portal. 2. Complete profile with educational and personal details. 3. Search for apprenticeship opportunities under AEDP or related schemes. 4. Apply to establishments offering embedded degree apprenticeships. 5. Upon selection, sign the apprenticeship contract. 6. Begin on-the-job training while pursuing academic studies. 7. Complete assessments and submit required documentation. 8. Receive degree and certification upon successful completion.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri National AIDS Control Programme
overview: The Pradhan Mantri National AIDS Control Programme (PMNACP) is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. It aims to prevent and control HIV/AIDS through targeted interventions, awareness campaigns, and provision of antiretroviral therapy (ART) and other healthcare services. The programme focuses on high-risk groups, general population awareness, and strengthening healthcare infrastructure for HIV management across the country.
target_beneficiaries: people living with HIV/AIDS; high-risk groups; general population; healthcare workers
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component: for ART services, individuals must be diagnosed HIV-positive and registered at designated ART centres; for targeted interventions, beneficiaries include female sex workers, men who have sex with men, transgender persons, injecting drug users, and migrants; for general awareness, the entire population is targeted; healthcare workers and institutions involved in HIV service delivery are also eligible for training and capacity-building support.
benefits: Benefits include free antiretroviral therapy (ART) for eligible HIV-positive individuals, diagnostic services (CD4 testing, viral load monitoring), treatment for opportunistic infections, psychosocial support, nutritional support in select cases, prevention of parent-to-child transmission (PPTCT) services, harm reduction measures for injecting drug users, behaviour change communication, condom promotion, and capacity building for healthcare providers.
financial_support: Financial support under PMNACP is primarily in the form of subsidized or free healthcare services rather than direct cash transfers. The Government of India provides grants-in-aid to State AIDS Control Societies (SACS) for programme implementation, including procurement of ART kits, diagnostics, consumables, and operational costs. The central government bears a significant portion of the costs, with states contributing a share as per the funding pattern.
application_process: 1. Individuals seeking ART must visit a designated ART centre with HIV-positive test report. 2. Registration is done at the ART centre after counselling and baseline investigations. 3. Eligibility for free ART is assessed based on clinical and immunological criteria. 4. Upon registration, monthly ART drug kits are dispensed free of cost. 5. Regular follow-up visits are scheduled for monitoring and adherence counselling. 6. For targeted interventions, high-risk groups access services through NGOs or TI sites after outreach and mobilization.
deadlines: Rolling basis — services are available throughout the year at designated centres.
implementing_agency: National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

overview: Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Vocational Training is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship to provide vocational skills to non-literate, neo-literate, and persons with rudimentary level of education up to 8th standard, with priority to women, SC, ST, minorities, and other disadvantaged groups. The scheme aims to enhance employability and promote self-employment through need-based, life-enriching, and income-generating vocational training programs delivered at the doorstep of beneficiaries.
target_beneficiaries: women; SC; ST; minorities; disadvantaged groups; neo-literates; semi-literates
eligibility: Beneficiaries must be non-literate, neo-literate, or persons with education level up to 8th standard, with priority given to women, SC, ST, minorities, and other disadvantaged groups. There is no upper age limit, but the focus is on adults and out-of-school youth. Training is conducted through registered Jan Shikshan Sansthans (JSSs) which are NGOs or voluntary organizations accredited by the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) or State Resource Centres (SRCs).
benefits: Beneficiaries receive free vocational training in market-relevant trades, life skills education, awareness on health, hygiene, and civic rights, and post-training placement or self-employment support. Training includes toolkits or raw material support where applicable. Successful trainees are awarded certificates jointly by JSS and NIOS or State Open Schools, enhancing employability and credibility in the job market.
financial_support: The scheme provides 100% financial assistance to Jan Shikshan Sansthans (JSSs) for conducting vocational training programs. The Government of India bears the full cost of training, including honorarium to trainers, raw materials, contingency, and administrative expenses. Funds are released in installments based on utilization certificates of utilization and performance. There is no direct financial transfer to beneficiaries; support is in-kind through free training and materials.
application_process: 1. NGOs/voluntary organizations apply to State Resource Centres (SRCs) or NIOS for accreditation as a Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS). 2. Upon accreditation, JSS submits annual action plan and budget to the State Directorate of Employment & Craftsmen Training or State Skill Development Mission. 3. After approval, funds are released in installments by the State Government based on utilization certificates. 4. JSS identifies beneficiaries, conducts training, and submits progress reports. 5. Central Ministry monitors performance through periodic reviews and third-party evaluations.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications for accreditation and funding are accepted throughout the year subject to budget availability and state-specific timelines.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of India

National Digital Library of India (NDLI) is a virtual repository of learning resources sponsored and mentored by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, through its National Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology (NMEICT). It provides a single-window access to learning resources across disciplines, academic levels, and languages, supporting learners from school to lifelong education. NDLI offers user group-specific services such as examination preparatory content, resources for researchers, and general learners, with interface support for 10 widely used Indian languages. It is developed, operated, and maintained from the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur.
target_beneficiaries: students; researchers; lifelong learners; job aspirants; educators
eligibility: Open to all learners, researchers, and educators across India with no restrictions based on age, educational background, or institutional affiliation. Access is free and available to anyone with internet connectivity.
benefits: Free access to a vast repository of learning resources including textbooks, lecture videos, question papers, journals, theses, manuscripts, and multimedia content. Services include examination preparatory materials, research support, multilingual interface, accessibility for differently-abled learners, and integration with various educational boards and levels. Users can explore content by subject, language, resource type, and provider.
financial_support: The NDLI project is sponsored and funded by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, through the National Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology (NMEICT). No direct financial support is provided to end-users; the platform is entirely free to access and use.
application_process: 1. Visit the NDLI portal at https://ndl.iitkgp.ac.in 2. Browse or search for resources using the search bar or explore by subject, language, or resource type 3. For institutional registration, set up an NDLI-Club via https://club.ndl.iitkgp.ac.in to obtain an Institutional Registration No. 4. Individual users can register for an account via https://ndl.iitkgp.ac.in/account/registration 5. Use the portal to access learning materials, prepare for exams, or conduct research without any fees.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Access and registration are available year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Education, Government of India, through its National Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology (NMEICT)

overview: The Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Scheme under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) aims to certify and upskill individuals with existing skills acquired through informal or non-formal learning. It provides formal recognition to such competencies, enhancing employability and livelihood opportunities. The scheme aligns with the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) and is implemented nationwide through accredited training partners and assessment agencies.
target_beneficiaries: individuals with prior learning; informal sector workers; youth; unskilled and semi-skilled workers
eligibility: Any individual possessing skills acquired through informal or non-formal learning channels, such as work experience, self-learning, or traditional training, is eligible to apply under the RPL component of PMKVY. There is no minimum educational qualification required, and the scheme is open to all Indian citizens.
benefits: Successful candidates receive a government-recognized certificate aligned with NSQF levels, a monetary reward of INR 500 upon assessment and certification, and improved access to job opportunities, wage progression, and formal skill upgrading pathways.
financial_support: Under the RPL scheme, a fixed monetary reward of INR 500 is disbursed to each candidate who successfully completes the assessment and certification process. This amount is transferred directly to the beneficiary's bank account via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 500
application_process: 1. Mobilization and counseling of potential candidates by training partners or implementing agencies. 2. Enrollment of eligible candidates at designated RPL centers. 3. Conduct of pre-assessment bridge training (if required) to address skill gaps. 4. Final assessment by empaneled assessment agencies as per NSQF-aligned qualification packs. 5. Certification and disbursement of reward money upon successful completion.
deadlines: Rolling basis — admissions and assessments are conducted throughout the year based on training partner schedules.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)

overview: The Impact Investors Council (IIC) India Fund is a social entrepreneurship initiative aimed at catalyzing impact investing in India by supporting enterprises that generate measurable social and environmental outcomes alongside financial returns. It functions as a platform to mobilize capital toward high-impact ventures, particularly in underserved sectors. The fund seeks to bridge the gap between traditional investment and social development by promoting scalable, innovative business models. It operates under the IIC’s broader mission to strengthen the impact investing ecosystem in India through collaboration, research, and capital deployment.
target_beneficiaries: social enterprises; impact-driven startups; MSMEs with social objectives
eligibility: Enterprises must demonstrate a clear intent to generate positive social or environmental impact alongside financial returns, operate within India, and have a scalable business model. Preference is given to ventures in sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, education, clean energy, and financial inclusion. Applicants must be legally registered entities, including private limited companies, LLPs, or Section 8 companies, with a minimum operational track record.
benefits: Access to patient capital from impact-focused investors, technical assistance in impact measurement and reporting, networking opportunities with global impact investors, capacity-building support, and potential follow-on funding. The fund also aids in enhancing credibility and visibility within the impact investing community.
financial_support: The IIC India Fund provides financial support through equity or quasi-equity investments in eligible enterprises, with investment sizes typically ranging from early-stage to growth-stage tickets. The fund emphasizes patient capital with flexible return expectations aligned to impact goals, though specific quantum per entity is not detailed in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Submit an expression of interest through the IIC India Fund portal or designated channel. 2. Undergo initial screening based on impact thesis, scalability, and team strength. 3. Submit detailed business and impact plans for due diligence. 4. Participate in impact assessment and investment committee review. 5. Receive term sheet and complete legal documentation upon approval. 6. Disbursement of funds post-closing.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Impact Investors Council (IIC)

scheme_name: NGO Darpan – CSR Fund Access Portal
overview: NGO Darpan – CSR Fund Access Portal is a digital platform operated by NITI Aayog that enables Non-Profit Organizations (NPOs) to obtain a unique Darpan ID through self-declared affidavit-based registration. The portal facilitates access to government grant applications by linking NPOs to official portals of various Ministries and Departments for submitting online grant applications. It does not issue physical certificates but provides a Darpan registration ID that allows NPOs to start applying for grants and exemptions after registration. The portal also includes important advisories regarding the prohibition of misuse of NITI Aayog's name, logo, or National Emblem.
target_beneficiaries: Non-Profit Organizations (NPOs); Trusts; Societies; Section 8 Companies
eligibility: Any Non-Profit Organization (NPO) including Trusts, Societies, and Section 8 Companies can register by creating an account, filling in organizational details, uploading necessary documents, and submitting for review to receive a Darpan Unique ID based on self-declared affidavit.
benefits: Registered NPOs receive a Darpan Unique ID that enables them to start applying for grants and exemptions through online portals of various Ministries and Departments. The portal provides access to official grant application links for sectors such as tourism, chemicals, higher education, North Eastern Region development, social justice, tribal affairs, biotechnology, handicrafts, minority affairs, MSME, legal literacy, chemical weapons convention, Atal Innovation Mission, solar energy, information broadcasting, economic affairs, skill development, housing, mines, pharmaceuticals, disability empowerment, health, water mission,MPLADS, and AYUSH.
financial_support: The portal itself does not provide direct financial support but serves as an access point to online grant application systems of various Government Ministries and Departments where NPOs can apply for financial assistance such as grants-in-aid, subsidies, or other funding schemes offered by those departments.
application_process: 1. Create an account on the NGO Darpan portal. 2. Fill in organizational details. 3. Upload necessary documents. 4. Review and submit the application. 5. Receive the Darpan Unique ID upon approval. 6. Start applying for grants and exemptions via the Online Grant Application Links provided for various Ministries and Departments.
deadlines: Rolling basis — registration and application for grants can be done year-round as there is no fixed deadline mentioned.
implementing_agency: NITI Aayog

overview: The Modular Employable Skills (MES) Scheme, under the Skill Development Initiative (SDI) scheme, was launched in 2007 by the erstwhile Directorate General of Employment and Training (DGE&T) to provide vocational training through Modular Employable Skills. It aimed to enhance employability by offering short-term, industry-relevant courses. The scheme was closed effective 31.03.2017.
target_beneficiaries: youth; unemployed; school dropouts; workers seeking skill upgradation
eligibility: Open to individuals seeking vocational training, particularly youth, school dropouts, and workers looking to upgrade skills; specific eligibility criteria varied by course and were defined under the Skill Development Initiative Scheme (SDIS) guidelines.
benefits: Participants received industry-relevant vocational training, certification upon completion, improved employability, and access to placement support. The scheme also facilitated self-employment and wage employment opportunities through skill certification.
financial_support: The scheme provided reimbursement of training costs to Vocational Training Providers (VTPs) based on norms fixed by the government, with advance payments against bank guarantees limited to 40% of the amount due per batch. Assessment fees were also managed through reimbursement mechanisms.
application_process: 1. Vocational Training Providers (VTPs) applied for registration through the prescribed procedure. 2. Applications were evaluated by the concerned authorities. 3. Upon approval, VTPs signed contracts with the government. 4. Registered VTPs could then enroll candidates for training. 5. Candidates were registered by VTPs. 6. Training was conducted as per the course structure. 7. Assessment was carried out by Assessing Bodies. 8. Post-assessment, certificates were issued. 9. Training cost reimbursement was claimed by VTPs after submission of required documents.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
