overview: The Coding for Kids Initiative – CBSE & MeitY is a government initiative aimed at introducing coding education to school students in collaboration with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). The initiative seeks to promote digital literacy and computational thinking among school-going children across India. It is part of MeitY's broader efforts to promote digital literacy and future-ready skills in the education sector.
target_beneficiaries: school students; schools; teachers
eligibility: The initiative is targeted at school students affiliated with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) across India. Specific eligibility criteria for participation are not detailed in the provided evidence.
benefits: The initiative aims to provide students with foundational coding skills, enhance digital literacy, and prepare them for future technology-driven careers through structured coding education in schools.

overview: The Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) was introduced by the Government of India in 1950 to ensure a steady flow of skilled workers in different trades for the domestic industry, to raise quantitatively and qualitatively the industrial production by systematic training, to reduce unemployment among the educated youth by providing them employable skills, and to cultivate and nurture a technical and industrial attitude in the minds of younger generation. The scheme operates through a vast network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) spread across various States and Union Territories. It aims to meet the existing and future manpower needs of industry by shaping craftsmen through vocational training.
target_beneficiaries: educated youth; trainees; students
eligibility: Age 14 years & above. Entry Criteria: 8th pass to 12th pass, most trades require 10th pass.
benefits: Training in 166 NSQF compliant trades with duration from 6 months to 2 years. Provides employable skills, certification through NCVT, and access to employment opportunities in industry. Includes employability skills training as part of the curriculum.
financial_support: The financial assistance was granted to State Governments/Union Territory administrations in the form of bulk grant in consultation with the erstwhile Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance. From 1st April 1969, the financial control of the Industrial Training Institutes in the States as well as in the Union Territories was transferred to the respective State Governments / Union Territory.
application_process: Admission to ITIs under CTS is managed by respective State Governments / Union Territory administrations. The process involves meeting eligibility criteria (age 14+, 8th to 12th pass depending on trade), applying through state-level admission procedures, and securing a seat in the desired trade at an ITI.
deadlines: Admission processes are managed by State Governments/UTs and vary by state; specific dates are not centrally defined in the evidence.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

overview: The National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) is a Government of India initiative under the Ministry of Education aimed at enhancing the employability of engineering and diploma graduates through structured on-the-job training. It provides apprenticeship opportunities in various industries and organizations, enabling fresh graduates to gain practical skills and industry exposure. The scheme facilitates a mutually beneficial arrangement where employers get trained manpower and graduates acquire hands-on experience relevant to their academic qualifications.
target_beneficiaries: engineering graduates; diploma holders; fresh graduates
eligibility: Engineering graduates (B.E./B.Tech) and diploma holders in engineering/technology disciplines who have passed their qualifying examination are eligible to apply for apprenticeship training under NATS. Candidates must register on the NATS portal and seek placement with participating establishments.
benefits: Apprentices receive a monthly stipend during the training period, with 50% of the stipend reimbursed to the employer by the Government of India. Upon successful completion, apprentices are awarded a Certificate of Proficiency by the Government of India, which is recognized for employment purposes across industries. The training helps in skill development and improves job readiness.
financial_support: The Government of India reimburses 50% of the monthly stipend paid to apprentices by the employer, subject to a maximum limit as prescribed. The stipend amount is determined based on the apprentice's qualification (engineering graduate or diploma holder) and is paid by the employer during the apprenticeship period, typically ranging from 6 months to 1 year.
application_process: 1. Eligible candidates (engineering/diploma graduates) must register on the NATS portal at https://mhrdnats.gov.in. 2. After registration, candidates can browse and apply for apprenticeship vacancies posted by participating establishments. 3. Upon selection by an employer, the candidate joins the organization for apprenticeship training. 4. The employer uploads the apprenticeship contract and monthly attendance/stipend details on the portal. 5. After verification, the government processes the 50% stipend reimbursement to the employer. 6. Upon successful completion of training, the apprentice receives a Certificate of Proficiency.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on vacancy notifications from employers.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Education, Government of India

overview: Social Alpha is a full-stack lab-to-market platform that supports science- and technology-led innovations addressing critical social, economic, and environmental challenges. It enables mission-driven entrepreneurs to de-risk, deploy, and scale deep-tech innovations across sectors such as energy, health, agriculture, and climate through incubation, seed funding, mentorship, market access, and deployment partnerships. Since 2016, Social Alpha has supported 450+ startups, awarded 200+ catalytic grants, made 100+ seed investments, and unlocked 150 million+ in follow-on capital, with impact reaching 3.5 million+ people across 400+ districts in 28 states and union territories.
target_beneficiaries: startups; science- and technology-led innovations; mission-driven entrepreneurs; deep-tech innovators
eligibility: An applying start-up should be a registered company in India, preferably be a DPIIT registered/applied start-up and should have completed a minimum of three months of association with Social Alpha in its resident or virtual incubation program. The start-up should have developed clarity on their Unique Selling Preposition (USP) through customer validation and a value proposition for its targeted customers. This support is not meant for Indian Subsidiaries of MNCs/foreign companies. Persons holding Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) would be considered as Indian citizens for the purpose of this scheme. The shareholding by Indian promoters in the start-up should be at least 51%. Preference will be given to start-ups who have not availed any funding from any Government of India /State Govt. body. The application should mandatorily include a declaration by the applying start-up that they have not received any NIDHI-seed support from any other DST supported Incubator.
benefits: Access to innovation labs for product development, design, iterations, and testing; real-world test beds and pilots; technical and regulatory support for compliance, regulatory support, guidance to help startups navigate compliance, certifications, and technical benchmarks; early risk capital through catalytic grants and seed investments; market access and procurement pathways to catalyze demand and connect with procurement channels; deployment partnerships for real-world deployment and follow-on investment; mentorship and knowledge services including bootcamps, masterclasses, and theme-based workshops; shared services for accounting, taxation, legal, IP, HR, and payroll; access to development sector partnerships with Tata Trusts and Government of India; opportunity to pitch for seed funding and access to follow-on capital from investor networks.
financial_support: Social Alpha provides catalytic grants and seed investments to de-risk innovations at the earliest stages. Under the NIDHI Seed Support Scheme hosted by Social Alpha, a seed fund with a corpus of INR 10 crores offers financial assistance for technology/product development, de-risking activities, testing and trials, marketing, mentoring, professional consultancy, IPR issues, and manpower for day-to-day operations. Financial support is disbursed based on milestones and monitored by the NIDHI-Seed Support Management Committee (NIDHI-SSMC). Startups can also access seed investment up to INR 50 lakh through the Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EIR) Fellowship and up to INR 1 crore through programs like the Namma Bengaluru Challenge. Grant support under Techtonic: Innovations for Sustainability includes up to INR 30 lakhs for R&D, INR 40 lakhs for Pilot, and INR 60 lakhs for Scale-Up tracks.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 60 lakhs (under Techtonic Scale-Up track)
application_process: 1. Visit the Social Alpha website and navigate to the relevant program page (e.g., Techtonic, NIDHI-SSS, EIR, or Namma Bengaluru Challenge). 2. Review eligibility criteria and program details. 3. Click on 'Apply Now' or 'View Details' to access the application form. 4. Fill in the application with details about your startup, including innovation focus, stage of development, team information, and financial needs. 5. Upload required documents such as Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, pitch deck, and declaration of no prior NIDHI-seed support from other DST incubators (if applicable). 6. Submit the application and await review by the respective selection committee (e.g., NIDHI-SSMC, SpIN Selection Committee, or Social Alpha portfolio team). 7. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for interviews, pitches, or due diligence. 8. Selected startups will receive formal communication and onboarding into the program.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round for most programs (e.g., EIR, NIDHI-SSS). Specific programs like Techtonic and Namma Bengaluru Challenge have defined cycles (e.g., quarterly reviews).
implementing_agency: Foundation for Innovation and Social Entrepreneurship (FISE)

overview: The National Water Awards (NWA) Innovation Support is a recognition-based scheme under the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, aimed at promoting innovation in water technology and management. It seeks to identify, encourage, and reward innovative solutions in water conservation, efficiency, and sustainability across sectors. The scheme supports grassroots innovators, startups, and organizations contributing to national water security goals through recognition and visibility.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; NGOs; research institutions; individual innovators
eligibility: Open to individuals, startups, MSMEs, NGOs, research institutions, and organizations across India that have developed innovative solutions in water conservation, efficiency, reuse, recycling, or management. Projects must demonstrate measurable impact, scalability, and sustainability. Preference is given to grassroots and community-driven innovations aligned with national water missions.
benefits: Recognition through national awards, certificate of appreciation, media coverage, inclusion in Ministry publications, opportunity to showcase innovations at national events like India International Water Week, and networking with policymakers, investors, and sector experts. Awardees may also gain visibility for potential funding, collaboration, and technology adoption by government or private entities.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support, grants, or subsidies. It is purely recognition-based, offering non-monetary benefits such as awards, certificates, and platform exposure to promote and scale innovative water solutions.
application_process: 1. Visit the National Water Awards portal at https://jalshakti-dowr.gov.in/nwa 2. Review eligibility criteria and innovation categories 3. Prepare a detailed proposal highlighting the innovation, impact, scalability, and sustainability 4. Submit the application online through the portal with required documents 5. Applications are evaluated by a technical committee 6. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for presentation or field verification 7. Final awardees are selected and announced at the National Water Awards ceremony.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year, with awards announced annually around World Water Day (March 22).
implementing_agency: Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti

overview: The Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Innovation Fund is a scheme under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs aimed at promoting CSR activities and innovation in corporate compliance. The scheme is part of the broader CSR framework governed by the Companies Act, 2013 and related circulars, encouraging companies to allocate funds toward social welfare and sustainable development initiatives.
target_beneficiaries: companies; corporations; NGOs; social enterprises
eligibility: Companies meeting the CSR applicability criteria under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 (net worth of ₹500 crore or more, or turnover of ₹1000 crore or more, or net profit of ₹5 crore or more during any financial year) are required to constitute a CSR Committee and spend at least 2% of their average net profits of the preceding three financial years on CSR activities.
benefits: Compliance with legal CSR obligations, enhanced brand reputation, contribution to sustainable development, access to government-recognized CSR projects, and potential tax benefits under applicable provisions of the Income Tax Act.
financial_support: Companies are required to spend at least 2% of their average net profits from the preceding three financial years on CSR activities. The funds are to be utilized through registered trusts, societies, or Section 8 companies engaged in CSR projects, or directly by the company for approved initiatives.
application_process: 1. Constitute a CSR Committee as per Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013. 2. Formulate a CSR policy and approve projects aligned with Schedule VII of the Act. 3. Ensure expenditure of at least 2% of average net profits on CSR. 4. Monitor and report CSR spending annually in the Board’s Report. 5. File CSR-related forms (e.g., CSR-2) on the MCA portal.
deadlines: Annual filing — CSR-2 form to be filed within 30 days from the close of the financial year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Corporate Affairs

scheme_name: PM CARES Fund CSR Project Support
overview: PM CARES Fund is a public charitable trust established on 27th March 2020 to provide relief and assistance during emergencies or distress situations, such as the COVID-19 pandemic. It supports relief efforts including healthcare infrastructure, research funding, and financial assistance to affected populations. The fund operates through voluntary contributions and qualifies for CSR expenditure under the Companies Act, 2013 and 80G tax benefits under the Income Tax Act, 1961.
target_beneficiaries: affected population; individuals; organizations
eligibility: Voluntary contributions from individuals/organizations and contributions as part of CSR from Companies/Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) are accepted. However, contributions flowing out of budgetary sources of the PSUs are not accepted.
benefits: Donations to PM CARES Fund qualify for 80G benefits for 100% exemption under the Income Tax Act, 1961. Contributions also qualify as Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) expenditure under the Companies Act, 2013. The fund is exempted from paying Income Tax as per Section 10(23)(c) of Income Tax Act, 1961. Donors can download formal donation receipts after successful transaction via the Print Receipt section on the portal.
financial_support: The fund consists entirely of voluntary contributions from individuals/organizations and does not get any budgetary support. The fund will be utilised in meeting the objectives as stated above. The Trustees have powers to formulate rules/criteria for carrying out any of the Objectives of the Trust.
application_process: 1. Visit the PM CARES Fund website (pmcares.gov.in) 2. Select the mode of donation (Net Banking, Card Payments, UPI, NEFT/RTGS, Cheque/DD, etc.) 3. Complete the transaction through the chosen channel 4. Go to the 'Print Receipt' section on the website 5. Select the channel used for donation 6. Enter mobile number and bank reference number 7. Enter Transaction Order Number/Merchant Order Number or Bank Reference Number 8. Click on Get OTP and enter the OTP received on mobile 9. Click on Submit to download the receipt
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Donations are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Prime Minister's Office (PMO)

overview: The Social Stock Exchange (SSE) is a platform established by SEBI to facilitate fundraising for social enterprises and voluntary organizations through the issuance of securities such as zero-coupon zero-principal instruments (ZCZPIs) and other innovative financial products. It aims to channel capital toward social welfare activities by enabling transparent, regulated, and efficient fundraising mechanisms. The SSE operates under SEBI's regulatory framework and is designed to support entities engaged in eligible social welfare activities as defined by SEBI.
target_beneficiaries: social enterprises; voluntary organizations; non-profit organizations
eligibility: Eligible entities include social enterprises and voluntary organizations engaged in eligible social welfare activities as defined under SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 and subsequent circulars. These entities must be registered under relevant Indian laws such as the Societies Registration Act, Trusts Act, or Section 8 of the Companies Act, and must comply with disclosure and governance norms specified by SEBI for SSE listing.
benefits: Access to a regulated capital market platform for raising funds; enhanced credibility and visibility through SEBI-regulated listing; ability to issue innovative instruments like ZCZPIs; transparency in fund utilization; potential tax benefits for donors/investors under applicable income tax provisions; and a structured exit mechanism for investors.
financial_support: The SSE does not provide direct financial support but enables eligible social enterprises to raise funds from investors through the issuance of securities such as equity, debt, or zero-coupon zero-principal instruments (ZCZPIs). The quantum of funds raised depends on market demand and investor participation, with no upper cap prescribed by SEBI. Funds are raised via public or private placement as per SEBI regulations.
application_process: 1. Determine eligibility as a social enterprise or voluntary organization under SEBI-defined social welfare activities. 2. Ensure registration under applicable Indian law (e.g., Societies Act, Trusts Act, Section 8 Company). 3. Prepare required disclosures including object clause, audited financials, and governance structure. 4. Appoint a merchant banker or lead manager registered with SEBI. 5. File draft offer document with SEBI for review. 6. Address SEBI observations and obtain final approval. 7. Issue securities and list on the Social Stock Exchange platform of a recognized stock exchange (e.g., BSE or NSE). 8. Comply with ongoing reporting and disclosure requirements post-listing.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year as per SEBI timetable for issue of capital.
implementing_agency: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

scheme_name: National Hydrology Project (NHP) Data Access for Startups
overview: The National Hydrology Project (NHP) Data Access for Startups initiative provides access to hydrological data and resources to support innovation in water technology. It aims to enable startups to leverage NHP's data infrastructure for developing solutions in water management, forecasting, and related domains. The program is part of the broader National Hydrology Project implemented by the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups registered in India working on water technology, hydrology, or related domains are eligible to access data under the National Hydrology Project. Specific eligibility criteria may include validation of the startup's focus on water-related innovation and compliance with data usage policies.
benefits: Access to hydrological datasets, hydro-meteorological data, water resources information systems, and related tools developed under the National Hydrology Project. Startups can utilize this data for research, product development, and validation of water technology solutions.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Support is primarily in the form of data access and technical resources.
application_process: 1. Visit the National Hydrology Project official website at https://nhp.gov.in 2. Navigate to the data access or startup engagement section 3. Review the data access policy and terms of use 4. Submit a request for data access detailing the startup's purpose and intended use 5. Await review and approval from the NHP data access committee 6. Upon approval, receive credentials or access links to the requested datasets
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications for data access are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti

scheme_name: PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) – Micro Irrigation
overview: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) – Micro Irrigation is a component of PMKSY focused on enhancing water use efficiency at farm level through micro irrigation technologies like drip and sprinkler systems. It aims to increase the area under micro irrigation, improve crop productivity and farmer income, and promote precision water management. The scheme is implemented by the Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare under the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; small and marginal farmers; other farmers
eligibility: Farmers can apply for the scheme either in MIS system (online) or in offline mode. Aadhaar details of the beneficiary are required to access the benefit of the programme. Aadhaar details need to be linked through a web based registration process. The subsidy payable to the beneficiary will be limited to an overall ceiling of 5 hectare per beneficiary. The subsidy payment will be limited to the unit costs specified in the scheme guidelines. 25% higher amounts have been taken into calculation of subsidy for the North Eastern and Himalayan states and 15% higher for states with low penetration of MI namely Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Union Territories.
benefits: The pattern of assistance payable under the micro irrigation scheme will be 55% for small and marginal farmers and 45% for other farmers which will be met by both Central Government and State Government in the ratio of 60:40 for all states except the North Eastern and Himalayan states. In the case of these states, ratio of sharing is 90:10. For the Union Territories, funding pattern is 100% grant by the Central Government. Subsidy is released to the beneficiary electronically through the mechanism of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Micro irrigation techniques not only help in water saving, but also in reducing fertilizer usage, labour expenses, and other inputs and input costs, besides sustaining soil health. Micro-irrigation systems deliver water savings of upto 40 per cent over conventional flood irrigation methods, along with appreciable crop productivity and income enhancement.
financial_support: The pattern of assistance payable under the micro irrigation scheme will be 55% for small and marginal farmers and 45% for other farmers which will be met by both Central Government and State Government in the ratio of 60:40 for all states except the North Eastern and Himalayan states. In the case of these states, ratio of sharing is 90:10. For the Union Territories, funding pattern is 100% grant by the Central Government. Subsidy is released to the beneficiary electronically through the mechanism of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). The subsidy payable to the beneficiary will be limited to an overall ceiling of 5 hectare per beneficiary. The subsidy payment will be limited to the unit costs specified in the scheme guidelines. 25% higher amounts have been taken into calculation of subsidy for the North Eastern and Himalayan states and 15% higher for states with low penetration of MI namely Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Union Territories.
application_process: Farmers may contact to nearest Office of Agricultural Department or District Agriculture Officer/ District Horticulture Officer for more information and obtaining benefits under PMKSY. Farmers can apply for the scheme either in MIS system (online) or in offline mode. Subsidy is released to the beneficiary electronically through the mechanism of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Aadhaar details of the beneficiary are required to access the benefit of the programme. Aadhaar details need to be linked through a web based registration process.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

overview: The National Rural Economic Transformation Project (NRETP) is a World Bank-assisted initiative under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at promoting rural enterprises, enhancing value chains, and supporting women’s collectives in farm and non-farm sectors. It focuses on scaling up successful livelihood interventions, strengthening producer enterprises, and facilitating access to finance and markets for rural poor households. The project operates across 13 high-poverty states and supports innovation, skill development, and digital inclusion in rural economies.
target_beneficiaries: rural poor households; women's collectives; self-help groups (SHGs); producer enterprises; rural entrepreneurs
eligibility: The project targets rural poor households, particularly women, belonging to Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations under DAY-NRLM. Benefits are extended to producer enterprises and collectives engaged in agricultural, livestock, handicrafts, and other non-farm activities. Implementation is focused on 13 high-priority states identified based on poverty and livelihood indicators.
benefits: Beneficiaries receive support for enterprise development, access to revolving funds and credit linkages, technical assistance for value chain development, training and capacity building, market access facilitation, and infrastructure support for rural enterprises. The project also promotes digital tools for SHG management and financial inclusion through convergence with banking and financial institutions.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through revolving funds, community investment funds, and matching grants to SHGs and their federations for livelihood activities and enterprise development. Funds are channeled via State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs) and disbursed based on micro-investment plans approved at the community level. The project leverages both grant and loan components to ensure sustainability and scalability of rural enterprises.
application_process: 1. Mobilization and formation of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) at the village level under DAY-NRLM. 2. Training and capacity building of SHGs on financial literacy, livelihood planning, and enterprise development. 3. Preparation of micro-investment plans (MIPs) by SHGs for livelihood activities. 4. Appraisal and approval of MIPs by Village Organizations (VOs) and Cluster Level Federations (CLFs). 5. Disbursement of revolving funds or community investment funds to SHGs based on approved plans. 6. Monitoring and hand-holding support by SRLMs and community resource persons. 7. Linkage with banks, markets, and value chains for enterprise growth and sustainability.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on community planning cycles
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) – Connectivity for Agri
overview: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 2000 to provide all-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations in rural areas, thereby improving access to markets, education, and healthcare. The scheme focuses on constructing and upgrading rural roads to ensure year-round connectivity, with a special emphasis on habitations with a population of 500+ in plain areas and 250+ in special category states (North-East, Himalayan, tribal and desert areas). PMGSY aims to boost rural economic growth by enhancing agricultural productivity and non-farm employment opportunities through improved infrastructure.
target_beneficiaries: rural habitations; farmers; rural communities
eligibility: Habitations with a population of 500 persons and above in plain areas, and 250 persons and above in special category states (North-Eastern States, Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Uttarakhand, tribal areas under Schedule V, and desert areas) as per Census 2001 are eligible for new connectivity. For upgradation, existing rural roads that form part of the core network and serve habitations of 1000 persons and above (500 and above in special category states) are eligible.
benefits: All-weather road connectivity ensures year-round access to markets, enabling farmers to transport agricultural produce efficiently and reduce post-harvest losses. Improved connectivity facilitates access to healthcare centers, educational institutions, and government services, thereby enhancing quality of life. The scheme stimulates local economic activity by promoting rural non-farm employment, agro-processing, and small-scale industries. Constructed roads are built to technical specifications (IRC:SP:20) ensuring durability and reduced maintenance costs. Community involvement in maintenance fosters ownership and long-term sustainability of rural infrastructure.
financial_support: The scheme is funded through central government grants, with the Ministry of Rural Development releasing funds to State Governments based on annual project proposals and utilization certificates. The funding pattern is 60:40 between Centre and State for plain areas, and 90:10 for special category states (North-East and Himalayan states). Funds are released in installments linked to physical progress, and the scheme operates through a decentralized implementation mechanism with State Rural Roads Development Agencies (SRRDA) and district-level units executing works via competitive bidding.
application_process: 1. State Governments identify eligible habitations and prepare Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for new connectivity and upgradation works. 2. DPRs are scrutinized by the State Level Standing Committee (SLSC) and forwarded to the Ministry of Rural Development for clearance. 3. Upon approval, the Ministry allocates funds and issues sanction orders. 4. State Rural Roads Development Agencies (SRRDA) invite tenders through e-procurement systems for civil works. 5. Contracts are awarded to qualified contractors following transparent bidding procedures. 6. Works are executed under technical supervision of SRRDA and National Quality Monitors (NQMs). 7. Completed roads undergo joint inspection before being handed over to Panchayati Raj Institutions for maintenance.
deadlines: Annual project proposals are submitted by States typically between October and December for the ensuing financial year; specific dates vary by State.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India

overview: The National Aquifer Mapping and Management and Management (NAQUIM) programme, initiated in 2012 under the Ground Water Management and Regulation Plan Scheme (XII plan), is one of the largest aquifer mapping endeavours globally. It aims to support effective groundwater management by delineating aquifers, characterizing their hydrogeological properties, assessing resource availability and quality, preparing aquifer maps, identifying issues, and developing sustainability strategies. The programme has completed mapping of 25 lakh km² mappable area out of 33 lakh km² total geographical area by 2023, with outputs disseminated via www.cgwb.gov.in and www.aims-cgwb.org.
target_beneficiaries: state government agencies; central ministries; district authorities; farmers; policy makers
eligibility: The NAQUIM programme is implemented by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) in coordination with state government counterparts and collaborates with organizations like GSI, NGRI, IMD, NRSC, IISc, IIT, etc. There is no direct application process for external beneficiaries; benefits are delivered through government channels and public dissemination of reports and maps.
benefits: Outputs support drinking water source finding and sustainability, site selection for artificial recharge, safe drinking water in arsenic-affected areas, assured irrigation in areas with adequate groundwater potential, implementation of water conservation and AR recommendations, ground water regulation based on NAQUIM recommendations, rejuvenation of springs, and integration into Atal Bhujal Yojana. Findings are used by state government agencies involved in groundwater management and water supply.
financial_support: The NAQUIM programme is a government-funded initiative under the Ground Water Management and Regulation Plan Scheme (XII plan). No specific financial support is provided to external entities; funding is utilized by CGWB for surveys, studies, and report generation. The master plan for artificial recharge estimates a total cost of Rs 1.34 lakh Cr for 141.75 Lakh structures, but this is not part of NAQUIM funding.
application_process: There is no application process for external beneficiaries. The programme is implemented by CGWB through field surveys by professional hydrogeologists from regional offices, data compilation, gap analysis, data generation and integration, aquifer map preparation, and management plan formulation. Outputs are shared via DO from Secretary (WR, RD & GR) to Chief Secretaries and Central Ministries, State Ground Water Coordination Committees (SGWCC), District Authorities (DM/DC), and Public Interaction Programmes (PIP) at grassroots level.
deadlines: Mapping of entire targeted area completed in 2023. Dissemination and implementation are ongoing.
implementing_agency: Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Ministry of Jal Shakti, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation

overview: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is a centrally sponsored scheme of the Government of India that provides financial assistance to the elderly, widows, and persons with disabilities in the form of social pensions. It aims to ensure minimum national standards for social assistance and supplement state-level efforts in providing social security to vulnerable groups. The programme includes components such as Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS).
target_beneficiaries: elderly; widows; persons with disabilities; BPL households
eligibility: Beneficiaries must be living below the poverty line (BPL) as per state-specific criteria. For IGNOAPS: age 60 years and above. For IGNWPS: widows aged 40-79 years. For IGNDPS: persons aged 18-79 years with severe or multiple disabilities. The applicant must not be receiving any other pension under any other scheme of the Government of India or State Government.
benefits: Monthly pension under IGNOAPS: ₹300 per month for ages 60-79 and ₹500 per month for age 80 and above. Under IGNWPS: ₹300 per month for widows aged 40-79. Under IGNDPS: ₹300 per month for persons with disabilities aged 18-79. Benefits are disbursed directly into bank/post office accounts via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as a monthly social pension through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the bank or post office accounts of eligible beneficiaries. The central government contributes a fixed amount, with states expected to supplement it. The pension is disbursed monthly and aims to provide a minimum level of income support.
application_process: 1. Check eligibility based on age, disability, widow status, and BPL criteria. 2. Obtain application form from the local Gram Panchayat, Municipality, or designated office. 3. Fill the form with required details and attach supporting documents. 4. Submit the application to the concerned local authority. 5. Application is verified by the local body and forwarded to the district level for sanction. 6. Upon approval, pension is disbursed monthly via DBT to the beneficiary's bank/post office account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India

scheme_name: Namami Gange – Ganga Rejuvenation Innovation Fund
overview: The Namami Gange – Ganga Rejuvenation Innovation Fund is a financial mechanism under the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) aimed at supporting innovative technologies and solutions for the rejuvenation of the Ganga River. It focuses on funding projects related to pollution abatement, water quality monitoring, and sustainable interventions along the river basin. The fund is part of the broader Namami Gange Programme, which integrates institutional development and infrastructure investments to achieve a clean and ecologically healthy Ganga.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; research institutions; NGOs; technology providers
geographic_scope: Pan-India (Ganga River Basin states: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal)
eligibility: Eligible entities include startups, MSMEs, research institutions, NGOs, and technology providers proposing innovative solutions for Ganga rejuvenation. Projects must align with the objectives of the Namami Gange Programme and demonstrate technical feasibility, environmental impact, and scalability. Preference is given to solutions addressing sewage treatment, industrial effluent control, solid waste management, and real-time water quality monitoring.
benefits: Financial support for project implementation, access to NMCG’s network of experts and institutions, technical guidance, pilot-scale testing opportunities, potential for scaling up successful models, and integration into national river conservation strategies. Non-financial benefits include visibility under the Namami Gange brand, collaboration with state SPMGs, and support for regulatory compliance.
financial_support: The fund provides grants and/or seed funding to selected innovative projects. The quantum of support is determined based on project scope, stage of development, and expected outcomes. Funding is disbursed in tranches linked to project milestones, subject to technical and financial appraisal by NMCG or its designated agencies.
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed project proposal through the NMCG portal or designated channel. 2. Proposal undergoes preliminary screening for eligibility and alignment with Namami Gange objectives. 3. Shortlisted applications are evaluated by a technical committee for innovation, feasibility, and impact. 4. Selected applicants are invited for presentation or detailed discussion. 5. Final approval is granted by the NMCG steering committee. 6. Funds are released in installments based on project progress and utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG), Ministry of Jal Shakti, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)
overview: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is a placement-linked skill training programme under the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, aimed at transforming rural poor youth into an economically independent and globally relevant workforce. The scheme focuses on enhancing employability through skill development in various sectors, ensuring job placements for trained candidates, and promoting sustainable livelihoods in rural areas.
target_beneficiaries: rural poor youth; SC/ST; women; minorities; persons with disabilities
eligibility: The scheme targets rural poor youth aged 15-35 years from families covered under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) or Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011, including SC/ST, women, minorities, and persons with disabilities, who are seeking skill training and wage employment opportunities.
benefits: Benefits include free skill training in industry-relevant trades, placement assistance with minimum wage guarantee, post-placement support for retention, accommodation and food during training, travel support, and certification recognized by the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT) or State Council for Vocational Training (SCVT).
financial_support: The scheme provides 100% financial support for training costs, including course fees, stipends, boarding, lodging, and travel, directly paid to the Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) based on norms and outcomes achieved, with no financial burden on the trainees.
application_process: 1. Identify eligible candidates from NRLM/SECC 2011 lists at the village level. 2. Mobilize and counsel youth to enroll in DDU-GKY training programmes. 3. Enroll candidates through registered Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs). 4. PIAs submit candidate details and training plans to the State Skill Development Mission (SSDM). 5. Obtain approval from SSDM and commence training as per approved under DDU-GKY norms. 6. Ensure placement of candidates post-training and report outcomes for reimbursement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on training cycles and PIA availability.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PM-FME)
overview: The Pradhan Mantri Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PM-FME) Scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) to provide financial, technical, and business support for the upgradation of existing micro food processing enterprises. It aims to enhance the competitiveness of individual micro enterprises, promote the 'One District One Product' (ODOP) approach, and support the formalization of the sector through credit-linked subsidies, seed capital, and capacity building. The scheme covers various components including individual micro enterprises, groups (FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives), and common infrastructure.
target_beneficiaries: Individual Micro Enterprises; Groups (FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives); Common Infrastructure
eligibility: Individual Micro Enterprises: Individuals, Proprietorship, Partnership, FPOs, NGOs, Cooperatives, SHGs, Pvt. Ltd. Co. would be provided credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of the eligible project cost with a maximum of Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit for upgradation or setting up of new units. Groups: The Groups - FPOs/FPCs/Cooperatives/SHG and its federation/Govt. Agencies - established or propose to establish food processing line along with common infrastructure/Value chain/incubation centers would be provided credit linked capital subsidy @35% of the eligible project cost with a maximum of Rs. 3.00 Crore. Seed Capital for SHGs: Seed capital @ Rs. 40,000/- per member of SHG for working capital and purchase of small tools maximum upto 4 Lakhs per SHG. Marketing & Branding: The scheme provides 50% financial grant for Branding and Marketing Support to groups of FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives or a SPV of micro food processing enterprises to promote their existing or proposed brands to market their processed food products under the scheme.
benefits: Financial benefits include credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of eligible project cost (max Rs. 10.0 lakhs for individual units, max Rs. 3.00 Crore for groups), seed capital @ Rs. 40,000/- per SHG member (max Rs. 4 Lakhs per SHG), and 50% financial grant for branding and marketing support for groups. Non-financial benefits include capacity building through training on Food Processing Entrepreneurship Development Programme, support under the One District One Product (ODOP) approach for value chain development and alignment of support infrastructure, and assistance in formalization of micro food processing enterprises.
financial_support: The scheme provides credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of the eligible project cost. For individual micro enterprises (Individual/Proprietorship/Partnership/FPOs/NGOs/Cooperatives/SHGs/Pvt. Ltd. Co.), the maximum subsidy is Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit. For groups (FPOs/FPCs/Cooperatives/SHG and its federation/Govt. Agencies), the maximum subsidy is Rs. 3.00 Crore. Seed capital for SHGs is provided as grant @ Rs. 40,000/- per member for working capital and purchase of small tools, maximum upto Rs. 4 Lakhs per SHG. The scheme also provides 50% financial grant for branding and marketing support to groups of FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives or a SPV of micro food processing enterprises.
application_process: The application process is not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence. However, based on the scheme structure, applicants would typically need to: 1. Identify eligibility under individual micro enterprise, group, or SHG components. 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) as per guidelines. 3. Apply through the designated portal or nodal agency. 4. Submit required documents including DPR, identity proof, bank details, etc. 5. Await sanction and disbursement of subsidy through credit-linked mechanism. 6. Utilize funds for project implementation as per approved DPR. 7. Submit utilization reports and comply with monitoring requirements.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI)

overview: The Technology Centre Systems Programme (TCSP) is a central sector scheme under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) aimed at establishing and upgrading Technology Centres (TCs) across India to provide technological support to MSMEs. The programme focuses on enhancing the competitiveness of MSMEs through access to advanced manufacturing technologies, skill development, testing, calibration, and advisory services. TCSP seeks to bridge the technology gap for MSMEs by creating world-class infrastructure and fostering innovation in manufacturing clusters.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; manufacturing units; startups in manufacturing; technical institutes
eligibility: MSMEs, manufacturing units, startups, technical institutions, and industry clusters located in proximity to Technology Centres can avail services. Eligibility for availing subsidized services is based on MSME classification as per MSMED Act, 2006, and specific service offerings of individual Technology Centres.
benefits: Access to advanced manufacturing technologies and machinery at subsidized rates, skill development training programs, testing and calibration facilities, technical consultancy, design and prototyping support, assistance in adopting Industry 4.0 technologies, and support for product development and process optimization.
financial_support: The scheme provides capital subsidy for setting up and upgrading Technology Centres. Financial support is extended to the implementing agencies (primarily Central and State Government PSUs) for creation of infrastructure and procurement of plant & machinery. MSMEs benefit through user charges for services rendered at TCs, which are offered at subsidized rates compared to market prices.
application_process: 1. Identify the nearest Technology Centre offering the required service. 2. Contact the TC to discuss service requirements and obtain a quotation. 3. Submit service request along with necessary documentation. 4. Avail the service upon approval and payment of subsidized user charges. 5. For long-term collaboration can be explored through MoUs or service agreements.
deadlines: Rolling basis — services are available throughout the year based on TC schedules and capacity.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

overview: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission (SPMRM) is a flagship initiative by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, aimed at developing 300 Rurban clusters across the country by provisioning economic, social, and physical infrastructure facilities. It seeks to stimulate local economic development, enhance basic services, and create well-planned Rurban clusters through convergence of various government schemes and Critical Gap Funding (CGF). The mission focuses on geographically contiguous villages with populations ranging from 5,000 to 50,000, depending on terrain, and aims to bridge the rural-urban divide while preserving rural community life with urban-like amenities.
target_beneficiaries: rural communities; gram panchayats; state governments; tribal and non-tribal areas
eligibility: The mission targets geographically contiguous villages forming clusters with a population of about 25,000 to 50,000 in plain and coastal areas, and 5,000 to 15,000 in desert, hilly, or tribal areas. Clusters must follow administrative convergence units of Gram Panchayats and be within a single block/tehsil. Selection is based on parameters such as decadal growth in rural population, non-farm work force participation, presence of economic clusters, tourism and pilgrimage significance, and proximity to transport corridors, with separate approaches for Tribal and Non-Tribal districts.
benefits: Benefits include provision of economic activities, skill development and local entrepreneurship training, infrastructure amenities such as piped water supply, sanitation, solid and liquid waste management, village streets and drains, street lights, inter-village road connectivity, public transport, LPG connections, digital literacy, Citizen Service Centres (CSCs), agro-processing, agri-services, storage and warehousing, fully equipped mobile health units, upgradation of school/higher education facilities, and digital literacy. Financial support is provided through Critical Gap Funding (CGF) to supplement convergence of scheme funds.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through Critical Gap Funding (CGF) under SPMRM, which supplements the shortfall in funding available through convergence of various Central Sector, Centrally Sponsored, and State Government schemes. For plain and coastal areas, CGF is up to 30% of the project cost or Rs. 30 crores per cluster, whichever is lesser. For desert, hilly, and tribal areas, CGF is up to 30% of the project cost or Rs. 15 crores per cluster, whichever is lesser. Funds are released in three instalments: 30%, 30%, and 40% of the total CGF approved, with the SNA transferring 35% of the CGF received as third instalment to the project and the balance 5% after completion of all project components.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 30 crores per cluster for plain areas and Rs. 15 crores per cluster for desert, hilly, and tribal areas, or 30% of project cost, whichever is lesser
application_process: 1. Identification of potential Rurban clusters by the Ministry and States based on demographic, economic, tourism, and transportation criteria. 2. Selection of clusters by State Governments within identified sub-districts, considering performance parameters like decadal rural population growth, rise in land values, non-farm work participation, girls' enrollment in secondary schools, bank account penetration under PMJDY, Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) performance, and good governance initiatives. 3. Preparation of Integrated Cluster Action Plan (ICAP) by State Nodal Agency (SNA) with support from State Technical Support Agencies (STSAs), covering baseline studies, required interventions, resource convergence, and CGF estimation. 4. Submission of ICAP to the Ministry for approval by the Empowered Committee. 5. Preparation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) for approved components. 6. Approval of DPR by State Level Empowered Committee (SLEC). 7. Release of funds in instalments as per financial concurrence. 8. Implementation of project components through convergence of schemes and CGF. 9. Operations and maintenance for ten years post-implementation. 10. Monitoring and evaluation through quarterly reports, utilization certificates, and site visits.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round as per the five-yearly iteration of ICAPs and fund release proposals.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
