overview: The Design Clinic Scheme for MSMEs is a government initiative aimed at enhancing the competitiveness of micro, small, and medium enterprises by providing access to professional design services. It supports product development, innovation, and value addition through expert design interventions. The scheme focuses on improving aesthetics, functionality, and market readiness of products manufactured by MSMEs.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) registered under the MSME Act, 2006 are eligible to apply for the Design Clinic Scheme. The enterprise must be engaged in manufacturing or production of goods and seek design intervention for product development or improvement.
benefits: MSMEs receive subsidized access to professional design services, including product conceptualization, design development, prototyping, and testing. The scheme covers a significant portion of the design consultancy fees, reducing the financial burden on MSMEs. Beneficiaries gain improved product design, enhanced market appeal, and increased potential for commercialization and export.
financial_support: Under the Design Clinic Scheme, the government provides a subsidy of up to 75% of the total project cost for design consultancy services, with the remaining 25% to be borne by the MSME. The maximum financial support per project is capped at INR 40,000 for micro enterprises and INR 60,000 for small and medium enterprises.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 60,000 per MSME (based on enterprise category)
application_process: 1. MSMEs must first register on the official Design Clinic Scheme portal at https://designclinic.in. 2. Submit an online application detailing the product requiring design intervention and the expected outcomes. 3. Upon preliminary screening, the application is forwarded to empaneled design institutes or professionals. 4. A design problem statement is formulated and agreed upon between the MSME and the design expert. 5. The design work is carried out as per the agreed scope and timelines. 6. Final designs and deliverables are submitted, and the subsidy is disbursed after verification and approval.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and empaneled design partners.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

overview: Mahatma Gandhi NREGA (MGNREGS) Convergence is a flagship rural employment guarantee scheme under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, which provides a legal entitlement to at least 100 days of wage employment per financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. The scheme aims to enhance livelihood security, create durable assets, strengthen natural resource management, and promote social inclusion through convergence with other government programs. It operates across rural India and integrates wage employment with infrastructure development, water conservation, and skill-building initiatives.
target_beneficiaries: rural households; unskilled manual workers; women; SC/ST; BPL families
eligibility: Every household residing in any rural area is entitled to a Job Card which contains the names and photographs of all adult members of the household so that they can demand and receive work. The adult member of every household residing in any rural area and willing to do unskilled manual work may submit their names, age and the address of the household to the Gram Panchayat at the village level in whose jurisdiction they reside for registration of their household for issuance of a job card.
benefits: Legal entitlement to wage employment within 15 days of demand, unemployment allowance if work not provided within 15 days, right to worksite facilities (drinking water, shade, first-aid), right to notified wage rate, right to receive wages within 15 days, right to conduct social audit, access to skill development and training programs, and creation of durable assets like water conservation structures, rural connectivity, and land development.
financial_support: Wages are paid directly into beneficiaries' bank/post office accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and Aadhaar Based Payment System (ABPS). The central government bears 100% of the cost of unskilled labor, 75% of material costs, and administrative expenses, while states bear 25% of material costs. Funds are released in tranches based on approved labor budgets and muster rolls.
application_process: 1. Apply for a Job Card at the Gram Panchayat office with household details. 2. Gram Panchayat verifies and issues Job Card within 15 days. 3. Submit application for work (written or oral) to Gram Panchayat/Programme Officer. 4. Work is allocated within 15 days of application. 5. Attend work site and mark attendance via muster roll. 6. Wages are paid within 15 days of work completion via DBT/ABPS.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications for work can be made throughout the year as per demand.
implementing_agency: Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
contact_details: Email: nicdrd@nic.in | Telephone No.: 011-23384338 | Website: https://nrega.nic.in/

overview: The National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP) is a scheme under the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises aimed at enhancing the competitiveness of the MSME sector through various interventions. It focuses on improving technology, quality, design, packaging, and market access for MSMEs. The programme supports clusters and individual enterprises in adopting modern practices to increase productivity and sustainability.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Manufacturing / Service sector MSMEs having valid Udyam Registration (UR) Certificate are eligible to avail benefits under the NMCP scheme components such as Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS), Design Clinic, Lean Manufacturing Competitiveness Scheme, etc., as per the specific guidelines of each sub-scheme.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of subsidies for various interventions: up to 80% subsidy on built-up space rent for trade fair participation (100% for SC/ST/Women/PH/Aspirational Districts), 80% financial assistance on one-time and annual recurring fees for Bar Code adoption (up to Rs. 50,650), financial assistance on annual membership/subscription fees for e-commerce platform adoption, capacity building support for clusters (up to Rs. 15 lakh per cluster), development of retail outlets (up to Rs. 30 lakh in Metro & A class cities and Rs. 20 lakh in other cities), and support for organizing national/international workshops and seminars (up to Rs. 5 lakh per event). Non-financial benefits include technology upgradation, skill development, market linkage creation, and access to common facility centres.
financial_support: Financial support under NMCP is provided as subsidies on a reimbursement basis. For trade fair participation, 80% subsidy on space rent (100% for special categories) and 100% contingency expenditure (up to Rs. 25,000) is available. For Bar Code adoption, 80% of one-time registration and annual recurring fees (for first three years) is reimbursed, subject to a maximum of Rs. 50,650. For e-commerce platform adoption, 75% of annual membership/subscription fee is supported, up to Rs. 25,000 per financial year. Capacity building interventions for clusters receive up to Rs. 15 lakh per cluster. Retail outlet development is supported up to Rs. 30 lakh in Metro & A class cities and Rs. 20 lakh in other cities, with 50% contribution required from the beneficiary. Workshop/seminar organization receives up to Rs. 5 lakh per event.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant NMCP component (e.g., PMS, Design Clinic, Lean Manufacturing) based on the required intervention. 2. Ensure the enterprise has a valid Udyam Registration Certificate. 3. Contact the concerned Implementing Agency (e.g., MSME Development Institute, NSIC, KVIC, Coir Board) or apply online through the designated portal. 4. Submit the application form along with required documents such as Udyam Registration, project report, quotations, and affidavits. 5. The Implementing Agency scrutinizes the application for eligibility and technical feasibility. 6. Upon approval, the beneficiary implements the approved activity. 7. Submit claim for reimbursement with supporting documents (bills, receipts, proof of participation) within the stipulated time (usually 30 days post-event or activity completion). 8. The Implementing Agency verifies the claim and processes the subsidy reimbursement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the year, subject to availability of funds and approval cycles of Implementing Agencies.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (Mo MSME)
contact_details: Email: pms[dot]division[at]dcmsme[dot]gov[dot]in | Phone: 011-23061198 (Head Quarters: Joint Director, O/o DC(MSME), Nirman Bhawan, New Delhi)

overview: The Common Facility Centre (CFC) under the MSE-CDP scheme aims to support the sustainability and growth of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) by addressing common issues such as technology, skills, quality, and market access. It focuses on creating or upgrading infrastructural facilities in industrial areas/clusters, setting up Common Facility Centres for testing, training, raw material depot, effluent treatment, and complementing production processes, and promoting green and sustainable manufacturing technology for clusters.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Existing Entrepreneurs [in form of a Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs)].
benefits: GoI Assistance: up to 80% of the maximum Project cost of Rs. 30 crores. Creation of, “Tangible Assets” such as Common Production / Processing Centre, Design Centers, Testing Facilities including Plug & Play Facilities.
financial_support: GoI Assistance: up to 80% of the maximum Project cost of Rs. 30 crores. The scheme provides financial assistance for setting up Common Facility Centres including Plug & Play Facilities, and support for Infrastructure Development Projects including Flatted Factory Complexes.
grant_amount_per_entity: up to 80% of the maximum Project cost of Rs. 30 crores
application_process: 1. Apply through the websites of MSME-DFOs, MSME-TC and other Implementing Agencies under MSE-CDP scheme. 2. The scheme link is https://cluster.dcmsme.gov.in
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

scheme_name: Infrastructure Development Scheme for MSME Clusters
overview: The Infrastructure Development Scheme for MSME Clusters aims to support the sustainability and growth of micro and small enterprises by addressing common issues such as technology, skills, quality, and market access. It focuses on creating and upgrading infrastructural facilities in industrial areas and clusters, setting up Common Facility Centres for testing, training, raw material depot, effluent treatment, and complementing production processes. The scheme promotes green and sustainable manufacturing technology and supports infrastructure development projects including flatted factory complexes.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Existing Entrepreneurs [in form of a Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs)].
benefits: GoI Assistance: up to 80% of the maximum Project cost of Rs. 30 crores. Creation of, “Tangible Assets” such as Common Production / Processing Centre, Design Centers, Testing Facilities including Plug & Play Facilities.
financial_support: GoI Assistance: up to 80% of the maximum Project cost of Rs. 30 crores. The scheme provides financial assistance for infrastructure development, common facility centres, and technology upgradation in MSME clusters.
application_process: 1. Identify the cluster and form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV). 2. Prepare a detailed project report including infrastructure needs, common facility requirements, and technology upgradation plans. 3. Submit the application through the Implementing Agency (State/Central Govt. organizations, NGOs) who need to provide land and 10% (5% in NER, J&K and Hill Areas) of Hard Intervention. 4. The Implementing Agency will forward the application to the Office of Development Commissioner (MSME) for scrutiny. 5. Upon approval, financial assistance of up to 80% (95% in NER, J&K and Hill Areas) of Hard Intervention cost, entire cost of Soft Intervention, Technical Agency fee and Implementing Agency fee is given by GoI.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Office of Development Commissioner (MSME)

scheme_name: Procurement and Marketing Support Scheme (PMS) for MSMEs
overview: The Procurement and Marketing Support Scheme (PMS) for MSMEs aims to enhance the marketability of products and services by supporting market access initiatives such as participation in national and international trade fairs, exhibitions, and buyer-seller meets. It provides financial assistance for adopting modern packaging techniques, bar codes, e-commerce platforms, and developing retail outlets. The scheme also includes capacity building, vendor development programs, and national workshops/seminars to educate MSMEs on business development, packaging, and export readiness.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Manufacturing/Service sector MSEs having valid Udyam Registration (UR) Certificate.
benefits: Financial assistance includes: 80% subsidy on built-up space rent for General category and 100% for SC/ST/Women/PH/Aspirational District units for trade fairs (Micro & Small Enterprises); 100% contingency expenditure for trade fairs; 80% financial assistance on one-time registration fee and annual recurring fee (first three years) for Bar Code adoption (Micro enterprises); financial assistance on annual membership/subscription fee/contingency expenses (photography, cataloguing, advertising) for selling products/services via e-commerce platform 'MSME Global Mart'; and support for developing retail outlets with infrastructure development up to Rs. 30 lakh max per outlet in Metro & A class cities and Rs. 20 lakh for other cities, subject to 50% contribution from the retailer.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of subsidies: 80% subsidy on built-up space rent for General category and 100% for SC/ST/Women/PH/Aspirational District units for trade fairs, with 100% contingency expenditure (subject to max Rs. 25,000 or actual, whichever is less). For Bar Code adoption, 80% of one-time registration fee and annual recurring fee (first three years) is provided, subject to a maximum of Rs. 50,650. For e-commerce platform adoption via 'MSME Global Mart', financial assistance of 75% of paid amount is provided, subject to a maximum of Rs. 25,000 per financial year. For retail outlet development, infrastructure support is up to Rs. 30 lakh max per outlet in Metro & A class cities and Rs. 20 lakh for other cities, with a limit of GIA (Grant-in-Aid) at Rs. 15.0 lakh for Class A & Metro cities and Rs. 10.0 lakh for other cities, subject to matching contribution from the retailer.
application_process: 1. Apply online through the URL: https://my.msme.gov.in/MyMsme/Reg/COM_ViewEvent.aspx 2. Submit claims for reimbursement to the respective Implementing Agency (MSME Development Institutes, NSIC, etc.) 3. For Bar Code reimbursement, apply to the Director/HOO of the regional MSME Development Institute with prescribed application form (Annexure - A) 4. For e-commerce platform claims, submit to NSIC for reimbursement 5. For retail outlet proposals, submit to MSME-Development Institutes (MSME-DIs) 6. Submit claims online or through system in place within 30 days from the date of conclusion of the event 7. Ensure submission of required documents including attested copies of payment receipts, licenses, UDYAM Registration, affidavit, and undertaking
deadlines: Applicant units shall have to submit their claim online (or system in place) in the prescribed format within 30 days from date of conclusion of the event.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME)
contact_details: Head Quarters: Joint Director, O/o DC(MSME), Nirman Bhawan, New Delhi. Tel: 011-23061198 Email: pms[dot]division[at]dcmsme[dot]gov[dot]in Field office: MSME-Development & Facilitation office (MSME-DFO) in the respective states.

overview: The Sikkim State Startup Policy is a state-level initiative aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship within Sikkim by providing support mechanisms for startups. It seeks to create a conducive ecosystem for new ventures through policy interventions, financial incentives, and institutional support. The policy targets early-stage enterprises and aims to promote sustainable economic growth by encouraging innovation-driven entrepreneurship across key sectors.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Startups incorporated in Sikkim, working on innovative products, services, or processes, with potential for scalability and job creation, and aligned with the state's priority sectors such as pharmaceuticals, eco-tourism, food processing, and organic farming.
benefits: Access to seed funding, mentorship, incubation support, market access assistance, regulatory facilitation, tax benefits, and linkages with investors and industry networks. The policy also offers support for intellectual property rights (IPR) filing and participation in national and international startup events.
financial_support: The policy provides financial support in the form of seed grants, equity-linked assistance, and interest-subsidized loans through designated financial institutions and government-backed funds. Specific quantum and disbursement mechanisms are defined under the policy's operational guidelines.
application_process: 1. Register the startup on the designated Sikkim State Startup Policy portal. 2. Submit the application form with details of the business model, innovation, and team. 3. Upload required documents including incorporation certificate, PAN, and pitch deck. 4. Await evaluation by the designated committee. 5. Receive approval and disbursement of benefits as per eligibility.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department of Commerce & Industries, Government of Sikkim

scheme_name: Bar Coding / Quality Certification Reimbursement Scheme
overview: The Bar Coding / Quality Certification Reimbursement Scheme provides financial assistance to micro enterprises for adopting bar codes and quality certification. It offers reimbursement of 80% of one-time registration fees and annual recurring fees for the first three years for bar code adoption, and financial assistance on annual membership or subscription fees for selling products via e-commerce platforms. The scheme aims to enhance market access and competitiveness of micro enterprises through standardized product identification and quality assurance.
target_beneficiaries: Micro enterprises
eligibility: Manufacturing / Service sector MSEs having valid Udyam Registration (UR) Certificate. Micro enterprises which have UDYAM Registration and also have registration with GS1 India for use of Bar Codes.
benefits: Financial assistance of 80% of one-time registration fee and annual recurring fee (for first three years) for adoption of Bar Code (Micro enterprises). Financial assistance on annual membership fee/subscription fee/contingency expenses (photography, cataloguing, advertising, etc.) for selling their products or services by Micro Enterprises. 80% subsidy on built up space rent paid for General & 100% for SC/ST/Women/PH/Aspirational District and 100% contingency expenditure for Trade fairs (Micro & Small Enterprises).
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance of 80% of one-time registration fee and annual recurring fee (for first three years) for adoption of Bar Code by micro enterprises, subject to a maximum of Rs. 50,650/-. For e-commerce platform adoption, financial assistance of 75% of paid amount by Micro Enterprises is provided, subject to a maximum of Rs. 25,000/- per financial year. For trade fairs, 80% subsidy on built up space rent is provided for General category and 100% for SC/ST/Women/PH/Aspirational District, along with 100% contingency expenditure (subject to maximum Rs. 25,000/-).
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 50,650/- for Bar Code registration (one-time and annual recurring fees for first three years)
application_process: 1. Confirm eligibility as a micro enterprise with valid Udyam Registration and GS1 India registration for Bar Code. 2. Obtain application form from the Director/HOO of the respective MSME Development Institute (MSME-DI). 3. Fill in the application form with details of the micro enterprise, amount paid for one-time and annual recurring fees to GS1 India. 4. Attach required documents: attested copy of cash receipt, license from GS1 India, pre-receipted bills in triplicate, copy of UDYAM Registration, affidavit, and undertaking. 5. Submit the application to the Director/HOO of the MSME-DI. 6. Await verification and reimbursement processing.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME)
contact_details: Head Quarters: Joint Director, O/o DC(MSME), Nirman Bhawan, New Delhi. Tel: 011-23061198 Email: pms[dot]division[at]dcmsme[dot]gov[dot]in

overview: The Mizoram State Startup Policy is a state-level initiative aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship within Mizoram. It seeks to create a conducive conditions by providing support mechanisms for startups through policy interventions, infrastructure development, and access to funding and mentorship. The policy targets early-stage ventures and aims to position Mizoram as an emerging hub for innovation in Northeast India.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Startups registered in Mizoram or founded by Mizoram domiciles, working on innovative products, services, or processes with potential for scalability and job creation.
benefits: Access to seed funding, mentorship, incubation facilities, networking opportunities, and policy support including single-window clearance and regulatory ease.
financial_support: The policy provides financial support through seed grants, equity-linked assistance, and access to state-backed funds, though specific quantum and disbursement mechanisms are not detailed in the available evidence.
application_process: 1. Register on the designated startup portal of Mizoram 2. Submit application with business profile and innovation details 3. Undergo screening by the State Startup Committee 4. Receive evaluation and feedback 5. Avail benefits upon approval.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department of Industries & Commerce, Government of Mizoram

overview: Meghalaya Startup Policy – MeghaStart is a state-level initiative launched by the Government of Meghalaya to foster innovation, support entrepreneurs, and build a robust startup ecosystem within the state. It aims to provide financial, infrastructural, and regulatory support to early-stage startups, particularly those led by youth, women, and marginalized communities. The policy emphasizes creating an enabling environment through incubation, mentorship, and access to funding. It aligns with national startup goals while addressing regional challenges and opportunities in Meghalaya.
target_beneficiaries: startups; women entrepreneurs; youth; SC/ST; MSME
eligibility: Startups registered in Meghalaya with a minimum of one founder domiciled in the state, incorporated as a Private Limited Company, LLP, or Partnership Firm, working on innovative products, services, or processes, and not older than 7 years from the date of incorporation. Preference is given to startups led by women, SC/ST communities, and those operating in priority sectors such as agriculture, tourism, handicrafts, and renewable energy.
benefits: Financial support in the form of seed grants, access to incubation facilities with infrastructure and internet, mentorship from industry experts and successful entrepreneurs, assistance in IPR filing and patenting, support for participation in national and international startup events, facilitation of market linkages and pilot projects, and guidance on compliance, taxation, and fundraising.
financial_support: The scheme provides seed funding of up to INR 10 lakhs per eligible startup as a non-repayable grant, disbursed in tranches based on milestone achievement. The funds are meant for product development, market validation, team building, and initial operational costs. The grant is administered through the State Innovation and Startup Fund, with disbursal managed by the Implementing Agency upon approval of the startup’s business plan and progress reports.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 10 Lakhs
application_process: 1. Visit the official Meghalaya Startup Policy portal or the designated nodal agency website. 2. Register as a startup and create a profile with basic details. 3. Fill out the online application form with information on the startup, innovation, team, and financial needs. 4. Upload required documents including Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, pitch deck, and founder details. 5. Submit the application for preliminary screening. 6. Shortlisted applicants will be invited for a pitch presentation before the Selection Committee. 7. Upon approval, sign the grant agreement and fulfill pre-disbursal compliance. 8. Receive the first tranche of funds and begin implementation. 9. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates for subsequent tranches.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Meghalaya Information Technology and Communication Department

overview: Mukhyamantri Swarozgar Yojana (MSY) is a state-level scheme in Uttarakhand aimed at generating maximum employment and subsidiary employment by providing loan facilities through nationalized/scheduled commercial banks, state cooperative banks, and regional rural banks for setting up enterprises, services, or businesses. It targets enterprising youth, returning migrants due to Covid-19, skilled/unskilled artisans, handicraftsmen, and educated urban/rural unemployed individuals. The scheme operates under guiding principles to encourage self-employment and industrial/business establishment in the state.
target_beneficiaries: youth; migrants returned due to Covid-19; skilled artisans; unskilled artisans; handicraftsmen; educated urban unemployed; educated rural unemployed
eligibility: Enterprising youth of the state, migrants of Uttarakhand who have returned due to Covid-19, skilled and unskilled artisans and handicraftsmen, and educated urban and rural unemployed individuals are eligible to establish their own industries/businesses under Mukhyamantri Swarozgar Yojana.
benefits: Loan facility through nationalized/scheduled commercial banks, state cooperative banks, and regional rural banks for setting up enterprise, service, or business; support for establishing own industries/businesses; encouragement of self-employment and entrepreneurship in Uttarakhand.
financial_support: The scheme provides loan facility through nationalized/scheduled commercial banks, state cooperative banks, and regional rural banks for setting up enterprise, service, or business. Specific quantum, interest rates, or repayment terms are not detailed in the evidence.
application_process: The evidence does not provide a numbered step-by-step application procedure for Mukhyamantri Swarozgar Yojana.
implementing_agency: Government of Uttarakhand

overview: The Delhi Industrial Policy 2021 is a state-level initiative aimed at promoting industrial development, attracting investment, and enhancing the competitiveness of industries in Delhi. It focuses on creating a conducive environment for manufacturing and service sectors through infrastructure development, skill enhancement, and policy support. The policy emphasizes sustainable and inclusive industrial growth aligned with national objectives like Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat.
target_beneficiaries: industries; manufacturing units; MSMEs; service sector enterprises
eligibility: Industrial units engaged in manufacturing or service activities within the National Capital Territory of Delhi, including MSMEs, large industries, and service enterprises, subject to compliance with zoning regulations, environmental norms, and other statutory requirements as per Delhi government policies.
benefits: Financial incentives such as capital subsidy, interest subsidy, and reimbursement of taxes; infrastructure support including land allocation and common facility centers; skill development and training programs; technology upgradation assistance; marketing and export promotion support; and facilitation of single-window clearance for approvals.
financial_support: The policy provides financial support in the form of capital subsidy (up to 30% of fixed capital investment), interest subsidy on term loans, reimbursement of SGST, and subsidies for technology adoption, quality certification, and patent registration, subject to ceilings and conditions specified under the policy.
application_process: 1. Identify eligibility under the Delhi Industrial Policy 2021. 2. Prepare project report and required documents. 3. Apply through the single-window clearance system of the Delhi government. 4. Submit application to the concerned department (e.g., DSIIDC or Industries Department). 5. Application undergoes scrutiny and site verification. 6. Approval is granted based on eligibility and availability of funds. 7. Disbursement of incentives follows post-implementation verification.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to fund availability and policy validity.
implementing_agency: Delhi State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (DSIIDC)

overview: The Nagaland Startup Policy – StartupNaga is a state-level initiative aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship in Nagaland. It seeks to create a supportive ecosystem for startups by providing financial, infrastructural, and mentorship support. The policy targets early-stage ventures and aims to promote sustainable economic growth through innovation-driven enterprises.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Startups registered in Nagaland with innovative ideas, scalable business models, and potential for job creation are eligible. Preference is given to ventures led by youth, women, and entrepreneurs from marginalized communities.
benefits: Benefits include seed funding, access to incubation centers, mentorship from industry experts, networking opportunities, assistance in regulatory compliance, and support for product development and market access.
financial_support: The policy provides financial support in the form of seed grants and soft loans to eligible startups, with disbursement based on project viability and milestones achieved. The exact quantum and mechanism are defined under the policy guidelines.
application_process: 1. Visit the official Nagaland Startup Policy portal or designated nodal agency. 2. Register as a startup and create a profile. 3. Submit the application form with business plan, pitch deck, and incorporation documents. 4. Undergo screening and evaluation by the selection committee. 5. Present the idea before the panel for final approval. 6. Upon selection, sign the agreement and receive disbursement of funds.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department of Industries & Commerce, Government of Nagaland

overview: The Arunachal Pradesh Industrial Investment Policy is a state-level initiative aimed at promoting industrial growth and investment within the state of Arunachal Pradesh. It seeks to create a conducive environment for industries by offering incentives, infrastructure support, and streamlined regulatory processes. The policy targets both new and existing industrial units to boost economic development, generate employment, and enhance the state's contribution to national manufacturing output.
target_beneficiaries: industries; MSME; manufacturing units; investors
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include new industrial units, expansion/diversification of existing units, and substantial investment in notified thrust sectors such as agro-processing, horticulture, handicrafts, tourism-related industries, mineral-based industries (subject to environmental clearances), and IT/ITES. Units must be registered under the Factories Act, 1948 or Shops and Establishments Act, and comply with all state and central environmental, labour, and safety norms. Priority is given to units employing local residents and utilizing locally available raw materials.
benefits: Benefits include capital investment subsidy, interest subsidy on term loans, reimbursement of state GST, power tariff concessions, stamp duty and registration fee exemptions, employment generation subsidy, quality certification assistance, patent registration support, and infrastructure development support. Non-financial benefits comprise single-window clearance, facilitation in land acquisition, skill development training, and marketing assistance through state participation in trade fairs.
financial_support: Financial support includes capital investment subsidy up to 30% of fixed capital investment (capped at INR 50 lakh), interest subsidy of 5% per annum on term loans for 5 years (capped at INR 10 lakh), reimbursement of net SGST paid for 7 years, and employment generation subsidy of INR 15,000 per local employee per year for 3 years. Power tariff concession is available at 20% for 5 years for industries in notified zones. All subsidies are disbursed through the Directorate of Industries after verification of claims and compliance with stipulated conditions.
application_process: 1. Submit application online via the Arunachal Pradesh State Portal or designated industrial investment portal. 2. Upload project report, incorporation documents, land ownership/lease details, and environmental clearances. 3. Application is scrutinized by the District Industries Centre (DIC) for preliminary eligibility. 4. Forwarded to the State Level Empowered Committee for final approval. 5. Upon approval, letter of intent is issued. 6. After commencement of commercial production, submit claim documents for subsidy disbursement. 7. Claims are verified by the Directorate of Industries before release of funds.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted throughout the year subject to budget availability.
implementing_agency: Directorate of Industries, Government of Arunachal Pradesh

overview: Mukhya Mantri Swavalamban Yojana (MMSY) is a state-level scheme by the Government of Himachal Pradesh aimed at promoting self-employment and entrepreneurship among the youth. It provides financial support in the form of capital and interest subsidies to eligible beneficiaries for setting up industrial, service, trade, or shop units. The scheme targets bonafide Himachali youth aged 18 to 45 years and supports projects in sectors like manufacturing, service, agriculture, animal husbandry, sericulture, and mining.
target_beneficiaries: youth; bonafide Himachali candidates; entrepreneurs; women (for higher subsidy)
eligibility: The scheme is exclusively for bonafide Himachali candidates. Applicants must be between 18 and 45 years of age at the time of application. They must possess a minimum level of education and have a viable business proposal. The unit must be set up in Himachal Pradesh and the applicant must not have engaged any private agency or middleman for aviling benefits under the scheme.
benefits: Beneficiaries are eligible for capital investment subsidy at 25% (30% for women) on plant & machinery and technical civil works, subject to a maximum investment ceiling of Rs. 40 lakh in plant & machinery and total project cost not exceeding Rs. 60 lakh. Additionally, interest subsidy at 5% per annum for 3 years is available on term loans up to Rs. 40 lakh sanctioned by financial institutions. Reimbursement of CGTMSE guarantee fee is also provided. Units must commence commercial production within 6 months (for service/trade/shop) or 1 year (for manufacturing).
financial_support: The scheme provides capital investment subsidy @ 25% (30% for women) on eligible investment in plant & machinery and technical civil works, with a maximum ceiling of Rs. 40 lakh in plant & machinery and total project cost not exceeding Rs. 60 lakh. Interest subsidy @ 5% per annum for 3 years is available on term loans up to Rs. 40 lakh sanctioned by financial institutions. Reimbursement of CGTMSE guarantee fee is also provided on a yearly basis. Subsidy is released after loan disbursement by the bank and verification by the District Industries Centre.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 40 lakh in plant & machinery (capital subsidy) and interest subsidy on loans up to Rs. 40 lakh
application_process: 1. Submit application online via the MMSY portal along with Aadhar Card, Bonafide Himachali certificate, and brief project profile including land details. 2. Obtain approval from the District Level Committee (DLC). 3. After approval, apply for loan from a financial institution. 4. Upon loan disbursement by the bank, apply for capital investment subsidy to the General Manager, District Industries Centre (DIC) with required documents. 5. Submit physical inspection report, undertaking, and engineer’s certificate. 6. After verification, the GM DIC issues sanction order for subsidy release. 7. Interest subsidy and CGTMSE fee reimbursement are applied for after commencement of commercial production.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline mentioned; applications are accepted subject to portal availability
implementing_agency: Department of Industries, Himachal Pradesh
contact_details: Helpdesk numbers available district-wise (e.g., Bilaspur: 01978-224248, Shimla: 0177-2628270); emails vary by district (e.g., gmdicblp-hp@nic.in for Bilaspur, gmdicsml-hp@nic.in for Shimla)

overview: The Punjab Skill Development Mission (PSDM) is a state-level initiative aimed at enhancing employability and entrepreneurship by providing skill training to youth across Punjab. It focuses on aligning training with industry demands and promoting self-employment through various vocational programs. The mission operates under the Department of Technical Education & Industrial Training, Punjab, and collaborates with training partners to deliver certified courses. It seeks to bridge the skill gap and support inclusive growth, particularly for marginalized and rural communities.
target_beneficiaries: youth; unemployed; rural populations; SC/ST; women; persons with disabilities
eligibility: Eligibility varies by course but generally includes Punjab residents aged 18–35 years, with preference given to unemployed youth, school dropouts, and individuals from SC/ST, women, and economically weaker sections. Specific educational qualifications depend on the trade or course selected.
benefits: Benefits include free or subsidized skill training, certification recognized by NCVT/SCVT, placement assistance, post-training support for self-employment, and stipends in certain schemes. Trainees also gain access to industry exposure, soft skills training, and entrepreneurship development modules where applicable.
financial_support: Financial support varies by course and partner, with many training programs offered free of cost or at highly subsidized rates. In some cases, stipends are provided during training, especially for disadvantaged groups. The mission does not typically offer direct loans or grants but facilitates access to government-sponsored skill schemes where financial aid may be available.
application_process: 1. Visit the official Punjab Skill Development Mission website or authorized training center. 2. Check available courses and eligibility criteria. 3. Register online or in person by filling the application form. 4. Submit required documents such as ID proof, residence proof, and educational certificates. 5. Attend counseling or selection process if applicable. 6. Enroll in the selected course and begin training.
deadlines: Rolling basis — admissions are open throughout the year depending on course availability and training partner schedules.

Eligibility criteria for AIR: Applicant must have completed at least one extramural funded project in India (with minimum project duration of 3 years & in the same research area of the project proposed), project must have been funded by Govt. funding agencies or Industry. Related Sanction order or funding note to be uploaded as a proof. Applicant must have authored one publication (indexed in Scopus/web of science) as first or lead author, or patents (filed) in the same research area of the project proposed for AIR. Applicant must upload the published paper or filing documents related to IP at the time of submission of application. Evidence of proof of principle (POP) and preliminary data, already gathered by the applicant, supporting the proposal is compulsory and must be submitted in the AIR application. Absence of which can result in disqualification of the proposal. Proposals involving agriculture should have viable product/technology as an outcome that can be considered for advanced trials by the industry/authorized national agencies. The final technical milestone of the AIR proposal should reflect technology/result that is near to industry readiness. Eligibility criteria for CRS: Evidence of proof of Concept (minimum TRL – 3) and validation ready data supporting the proposal is compulsory and must be submitted in the CRS application. Absence of which can result in disqualification of the proposal. Proposals that have received AIR funding should have the same industrial partner who collaborated for AIR project. Any deviation must be duly justified with clarity on IP governance. The CRS proposal should be accompanied by the Commitment Letter by the industrial partner to exercise the first right for monetizing the product/technology. Eligibility Criteria for Industry/LLP as collaborator: Minimum 51% of the shares of the Company should be held by Indian Citizens holding Indian passport (Indian Citizens do not include Person of Indian Origin (PIO) and Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) holders). Minimum half of the persons who subscribed their names to the LLP document as its Partners should be Indian citizens. The collaborating Company/LLP should have adequate in-house facility to address the project implementation or incubated with any of the recognized incubation facility.
benefits: Funding support (Grant): Total cost of the project must not exceed Rs. 50 lakhs (Non-recurring cost must not exceed 10% of the total cost). IP rights may be with academia alone, or jointly shared between academia and industry (if academia establishes PoC with industry) as per the understanding between the two partners. For CRS: Funding in the form of grant is provided to both academic as well as industrial partners. While funding is provided to the academia for In-House research which forms a part of validation of the Proof of Concept, funds are provided to the industrial partner for validation. There is no ceiling to the funding. IPR: Although the IP rights reside with the academia, the industry partner has first right of refusal for commercial exploitation of the New IP. The first right of refusal will be accompanied with an undertaking that its business strategy encompasses possibility of commercialization of the present technology under validation.
financial_support: Funding Support (Grant): Total cost of the project must not exceed Rs. 50 lakhs (Non-recurring cost must not exceed 10% of the total cost) for AIR. For CRS: Funding in the form of grant is provided to both academic as well as industrial partners. While funding is provided to the academia for In-House research which forms a part of validation of the Proof of Concept, funds are provided to the industrial partner for validation. There is no ceiling to the funding.
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 50 lakhs
application_process: 1. Log on the BIRAC website http://www.birac.nic.in/. 2. deadlines: There are three call for proposals in a year: 15th February – 31st March, 15th June – 31st July, 15th October – 30th November

It seeks to strengthen India's capabilities in deep technologies, promote technological self-reliance, and align with the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision. The mission operates through the Research, Development, and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, which provides long-term loans, equity infusion, and contributions to Deep-Tech Fund of Funds, excluding grants and short-term loans.

benefits: Financing can cover up to 50% of assessed project cost for transformative RDI projects at Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) 4 and above; exceptions may be approved by the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS). Funding modes include long-term loan at low or nil interest rates, equity infusion (especially for startups), and contributions to Deep-Tech Fund of Funds. The scheme promotes technological self-reliance, strengthens capabilities in strategic technologies, and supports private sector participation in high-impact R&D.
financial_support: Total Budget: ₹1 lakh crore. Modes of Financing: Long-term loan at low or nil interest rates. Equity infusion, especially in case of startups. Contributions to Deep-Tech Fund of Funds. Exclusions: Grants and short-term loans are not supported. application_process: Industry stakeholders seeking funding for projects under the RDI scheme are requested not to send proposals or emails directly to DST. scheme_name: National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations (NIDHI)
overview: National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations (NIDHI) is an umbrella programme conceived and developed by the Technology Translation and Innovation (TTI) Division, Department of Science & Technology, Government of India, for nurturing ideas and innovations (knowledge-based and technology-driven) into successful startups. The programme works in line with national priorities and goals, focusing on building an innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem with the objective of socio-economic development through wealth and job creation. It supports startups through scouting, supporting, and scaling of innovations via components like PRAYAS, EIR, TBI, Accelerator, Seed Support, and Centres of Excellence.
target_beneficiaries: startups; innovators; entrepreneurs; students; researchers
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component: For NIDHI-PRAYAS, innovators/startups can apply through NIDHI-PRAYAS Centres at selected TBIs; for NIDHI Seed Support Program, startups must be registered in India, preferably DPIIT-registered, with at least 3 months association with the incubator, clarity on USP, and at least 51% shareholding by Indian promoters; for NIDHI-EIR, applicants must be Indian citizens with minimum 4 years of formal education in science/engineering OR 3 years degree/diploma + 2 years work experience, committed to full-time entrepreneurial pursuit; for NIDHI-TBI, host institutions must be academic/technical/R&D or other entities with clear purpose to promote innovation, in existence for at least 3 years, and not-for-profit legal entities.
benefits: Benefits include financial support (grants up to INR 40 lakhs for prototyping under PRAYAS 2.0, up to INR 100 lakhs under Seed Support, up to INR 30,000/month under EIR), access to infrastructure (Fab Labs, incubation space), mentoring, technical and business guidance, IP and legal assistance, industry and investor connect opportunities, networking events, demo day exposure, and co-working spaces. Non-financial benefits also include training, prototype development support, and ecosystem integration.
financial_support: Financial support varies by component: NIDHI-PRAYAS 2.0 offers up to ₹20 lakhs per innovator for PRAYAS Centres and up to ₹40 lakhs for Advance PRAYAS Centres; NIDHI Seed Support Program provides up to INR 1000 lakh to incubators (released in phases) and up to INR 100 lakh per startup; NIDHI-EIR offers a monthly stipend of INR 10,000–30,000 for up to 18 months; NIDHI-Accelerator provides up to INR 40 lakh per cohort (INR 30 lakh for program, INR 10 lakh for demo day awards); NIDHI-CoE offers enhanced support of INR 50 crore over 5 years for selected incubators.
application_process: Application process varies by component: For NIDHI-PRAYAS 2.0, innovators apply to designated PRAYAS Centres/Advance PRAYAS Centres via the NIDHI PRAYAS Portal using a common application template; for NIDHI Seed Support Program, incubators apply once per year through an online portal (call announced annually), and startups apply to listed incubators/TBIs; for NIDHI-EIR, startups apply through NIDHI-EIR Centres at selected TBIs; for NIDHI-TBI, proposals are submitted to NSTEDB via their online portal with required enclosures; for NIDHI-Accelerator, TBIs apply through the department’s online portal http://onlinedst.gov.in.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round for most components; however, specific calls like NIDHI Seed Support Program are announced once per year, and Indo-German InnoXchange Programme had a deadline of 10th April, 2026.
implementing_agency: Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, through the National Science & Technology Entrepreneurship Development Board (NSTEDB) and Technology Translation and Innovation (TTI) Division

scheme_name: National Centre of Excellence for Green Port & Shipping (NCoEGPS)

scheme_name: Centre of Excellence for Drones & Counter Drone Systems
overview: The Centre of Excellence for Drones & Counter Drone Systems is a scheme under the Department of Science & Technology (DST) aimed at fostering innovation and development in drone technology and counter-drone systems. Approved projects receive sanction letters and fund disbursement begins as per milestones.

scheme_name: Coal India Ltd (CIL) Innovation & Startup Fund
overview: The Coal India Ltd (CIL) Innovation & Startup Fund is a dedicated initiative by Coal India Limited to support innovation and entrepreneurship in the coal and allied sectors. target_beneficiaries: startups

Preference is given to those aligned with CIL’s operational challenges and sustainability goals.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grants or equity-based funding, mentorship from CIL experts, access to CIL’s infrastructure and pilot testing facilities, technical guidance, and potential for long-term collaboration or procurement opportunities with Coal India Limited.

Shortlisted startups are invited for presentation and evaluation before a selection committee. 6. Final selection is based on innovation, feasibility, scalability, and alignment with CIL’s objectives. 7. Selected startups undergo due diligence before fund disbursement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to fund availability and review cycles.
implementing_agency: Coal India Limited (CIL)

scheme_name: IIT Hyderabad Deep Tech Startup Incubator

benefits: Mentorship, sitting space, basic business facilities, access to VC funding (in exchange for equity), financial support for prototype building and sustenance, technology licensing, consultancy participation, paid use of institute facilities, growth support on VC funding and revenue increase, professional working environment via rental space in the Technology Research Park (TRP), and reach-out points for queries or support related to innovation and entrepreneurship.

application_process: 1. For student startups: Register the startup at iTIC with oneself as (if pursuing internship in one's own startup). 2. For deferred placement: Opt out of regular placement season and register for a startup or enroll with an incubation centre.
deadlines: Rolling basis

scheme_name: ONGC Energy Centre (OEC) for Clean Energy Startups

deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.

overview: The MSME Assistance Programme Gujarat is an award-based recognition scheme for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Gujarat, administered by the Office of the MSME Commissionerate. It aims to identify and honor outstanding MSMEs across categories such as Women Entrepreneur, Young Entrepreneur, SC/ST Entrepreneur, and General through a formal application process involving documentation, verification, and committee evaluation. target_beneficiaries: MSME; women entrepreneurs; young entrepreneurs; SC/ST
eligibility: Applicants must be MSMEs registered under Udyam (Micro/Small/Medium) with valid registration, engaged in manufacturing or service activities, and have been in continuous production for the previous three years. Enterprises must have valid statutory clearances, no pending legal or tax liabilities, and must have paid all government dues. Applicants must be first-generation entrepreneurs (if applying under Young Entrepreneur category), belong to SC/ST/women/general category as applicable, and submit audited financials for 2021-22 to 2024-25. The unit must be owned by 51% or more women for Women Entrepreneur category, and applicants must be under 35 years for Young Entrepreneur category.
benefits: Recognition through state-level awards, trophy, certificate, and public acknowledgment. Awardees gain credibility and visibility, which may support business growth, market access, and networking opportunities. The award serves as a mark of excellence and can enhance reputation among customers, financial institutions, and government bodies.
financial_support: No direct financial support, grant, loan, or subsidy is provided under this scheme. The assistance is purely recognition-based in the form of awards, trophies, and certificates.
application_process: 1. Download the application form from the official MSME Commissionerate website. 2. Fill in entrepreneur and enterprise details including name, address, Udyam registration, constitution, and product details. 3. Attach required documents such as Udyam Udyam certificate, audited balance sheets, constitution proof, photographs, and category-specific documents. 4. Submit a write-up of up to 300 words justifying the enterprise’s achievements. 5. Obtain GM Certificate from District Industries Center verifying eligibility. 6. Submit the completed application in duplicate to the MSME Commissionerate before the deadline. 7. Await evaluation by the appointed committee. 8. If selected, receive award, trophy, and certificate.
deadlines: Last date for receipt of application is [date not specified in evidence]

scheme_name: CCAMP (Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms)
overview: CCAMP (Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms) is an initiative supported by the Department of Biotechnology, Government of India, established in 2009 to enable cutting-edge life science research and innovation. It serves as a catalyst for bioscience research and entrepreneurship by providing research, development, training, and services through state-of-the-art technology platforms. CCAMP promotes entrepreneurship and innovation through seed funding schemes, mentorship programs, and bio-incubation facilities, fostering an entrepreneur-friendly culture in academic and research environments.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; life science innovators; biotech startups; agri-startups; healthcare startups
eligibility: Eligibility varies across specific seed funding schemes but generally includes: Indian startups registered under Companies Act, 2013; at least 51% shareholding by Indian promoters (excluding OCI/PIO); turnover not exceeding specified limits (e.g., Rs 25 cr or Rs 100 cr depending on scheme); incorporation within 5-10 years; working on innovative, technology-driven products or services in life sciences, healthcare, agri-tech, or related sectors; product-oriented (not service-oriented); novel technology with IP generation potential; competent technical and business team; sound commercialization strategy and roadmap; clear understanding of end-user/customer and market size; sound business plan and company vision. Non-financial benefits encompass prototype generation, proof-of-concept studies, scaling-up support, patent analysis, market research, professional consultancy, enterprise building, IPR support, and guidance on regulatory pathways. financial_support: Financial support varies by scheme: BIRAC SEED offers equity-based investment up to INR 30 Lakhs; AIM Seed uses a co-investment model where CCAMP invests INR 12.5 Lakhs matched by private investors; LEAP Fund provides up to INR 1 crore per startup via equity or equity-linked instruments; NIDHI SEED Support Scheme offers INR 25 Lakhs (up to INR 100 Lakhs for exceptional cases) based on equity or equity-linked instruments; SISFS provides up to INR 20 Lakhs as grant for proof-of-concept/prototype/product trials and up to INR 50 Lakhs for market entry/commercialization/scaling via convertible debentures or debt; SIIP offers fellowship of INR 50,000/month and a kick-start grant of INR 5 Lakhs. application_process: 1. Identify the relevant seed funding scheme (e.g., BIRAC SEED, AIM Seed, LEAP, NIDHI SEED, SISFS, SIIP) based on eligibility and focus area. 2. Ensure compliance with scheme-specific eligibility criteria (e.g., incorporation, shareholding, turnover, innovation focus). 3. Prepare required documents including Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, business plan, pitch deck, details of technology/IP, team credentials, and financials. 4. Apply via the designated application portal (commonly https://www.ccamp.res.in/funding/content/application-form-seed-funding-schemes or scheme-specific URLs like https://www.birac.nic.in/desc_new.php?id=395 for SIIP). 5. Submit the application before the deadline (if applicable). 6. Undergo screening and evaluation by a panel of experts based on scientific strength, commercialization potential, societal impact, team strength, and implementation plan. 7. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for presentations or interviews. 8. Await final selection and funding disbursement upon agreement to terms (e.g., equity sharing, milestone reporting).
deadlines: Varies by scheme: NIDHI SEED Support Scheme open till 31st July 2026; LEAP Fund has rolling applications; AIM Seed has rolling applications; BIRAC SEED has rolling applications; SIIP has rolling applications; SISFS has rolling applications. Some schemes like TIDE 2.0 G2C have specific windows (e.g., 13th Nov to 20th Nov 2025). Many operate on a rolling basis with periodic review cycles.

benefits: Benefits include medical insurance coverage (IPD sum insured of Rs. 5 Lakhs per person, clubbable up to Rs. 10 Lakhs per family; OPD sum insured of Rs. 20 Thousand per member, clubbable up to Rs. 40 Thousand per family), corporate buffer of Rs. 1 Crore, bed/cabin charges based on pre-superannuation grade, coverage for pre-existing diseases without waiting period, domiciliary hospitalization, ambulance expenses up to Rs. 10,000, air ambulance in life-threatening situations, recipient and donor medical expenses (excluding organ cost), psychiatric/mental health coverage up to sum insured, AYUSH treatments, HIV/AIDS-related treatments, cancer treatments, physiotherapy, genetic disorders, and cashless facility through empanelled hospitals.
financial_support: The CPRMS-2026 scheme provides financial support via insurance coverage: IPD sum insured of Rs. 5 Lakhs per person (superannuated employee and/or spouse), with clubbing allowed between primary member and spouse up to a maximum of Rs. 10 Lakhs per family. scheme_name: Food Testing Infrastructure – NABL Accreditation Support
overview: NABL (National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories) provides voluntary accreditation services to testing laboratories, calibration laboratories, medical testing laboratories, proficiency testing providers, reference material producers, and biobanks in accordance with international standards such as ISO/IEC 17025, ISO 15189, ISO/IEC 17043, ISO 17034, and ISO 20387. The scheme ensures technical competence, international recognition, and facilitates acceptance of test/calibration results across borders through Mutual Recognition Arrangements (MRA with ILAC and APAC). NABL is self-financing and charges fees to conformity assessment bodies to cover operational costs.
target_beneficiaries: testing laboratories; calibration laboratories; medical testing laboratories; proficiency testing providers; reference material producers; biobanks
eligibility: Eligibility varies by CAB type: Testing laboratories must comply with ISO/IEC 17025, calibration laboratories with ISO/IEC 17025, medical testing laboratories with ISO 15189, proficiency testing providers with ISO/IEC 17043, reference material producers with ISO 17034, and biobanks with ISO 20387. Assessors for training must be aged 38-55 years, hold a Bachelor’s in Engineering/Technology or Master’s in Science (or relevant postgraduate/Ph.D. for medical), and have minimum ten years of experience in the relevant field, with five years at supervisory level or above.
benefits: Formal recognition of competence, international recognition, access to global markets, time and cost efficiency, enhanced customer confidence, robust quality management system, continual improvement, better operational control, assurance of accurate and reliable results, cost reduction, prevention of loss due to defects, eligibility to participate in tenders requiring independently verified laboratories, potential increase in business, and savings from reduced need for retesting.
financial_support: NABL is self-financing and charges fees to Conformity Assessment Bodies to cover operational costs and other expenditure. Fee details are available in NABL 100A 'General Information Brochure'. No direct financial support, grants, or subsidies are provided under this scheme.
application_process: 1. Determine the relevant discipline and standard for accreditation (e.g., ISO/IEC 17025 for testing/calibration labs). 2. Refer to NABL documents such as NABL 100B for accreditation process and procedure. 3. Prepare the application as per the relevant application form (e.g., NABL 180 for PTP, NABL 190 for RMP). 4. Submit the application online via the NABL portal. 5. NABL reviews the application and may conduct an on-site assessment. 6. Upon successful evaluation, accreditation is granted. 7. Maintain accreditation through periodic surveillance and re-assessment as per NABL 131.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL), under the Quality Council of India (QCI)

overview: The Cold Storage Infrastructure Subsidy (NHB) is a scheme under the National Horticulture Board aimed at supporting the development of cold storage infrastructure to reduce post-harvest losses in horticulture produce. It provides financial assistance for setting up cold storage facilities to enhance the shelf life and marketability of fruits and vegetables. The scheme is part of broader initiatives to strengthen the horticulture value chain and improve farmers' income through better storage and value addition.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; agri-startups; entrepreneurs; Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs); Cooperatives/Societies
eligibility: Entities eligible for consideration as Implementing Agencies (IAs) under this scheme should be legal entities excluding proprietorships or natural persons, including Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs/FPCs), Cooperatives/Societies, Partnership Firms, Companies, or combination thereof. The applicant entity must demonstrate a net worth at least equivalent to the equity contribution proposed, contribute a minimum of 20% of the IA’s Cost Component as equity, possess relevant experience in horticulture input supply, production, aggregation, trading, food processing, exporting, retailing, or logistics, have an annual turnover at least equal to the total project cost, secure a term loan from RBI-approved scheduled commercial banks constituting at least 20% of the IA’s Cost Component, and ensure the farmer component is minimum 40% of the total project cost.
benefits: Financial assistance for setting up cold storage infrastructure, reduction in post-harvest losses (20-44% range), enhanced shelf life and quality of horticulture produce, better price realization for farmers, improved market access and export potential, promotion of energy-efficient and sustainable cold chain technologies, support for value addition and processing activities, and contribution to doubling farmers' income through improved storage and market linkage.
financial_support: The scheme provides subsidy support for cold storage infrastructure under the Cluster Development Programme (CDP) and other NHB initiatives. Financial assistance is extended for setting up cold storage units as part of integrated horticulture projects. The subsidy is disbursed based on project appraisal and verification of milestones, with funding typically sourced from government allocations under schemes like Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) and Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF). The exact quantum varies based on project cost and appraisal, with beneficiary contribution and loan components as per eligibility norms.
application_process: 1. Submit Expression of Interest (EoI) online at https://cdp.nhb.gov.in for cluster-based projects including cold storage. 2. Await shortlisting based on concept note evaluation. 3. Submit Detailed Project Report (DPR) within the stipulated timeline after shortlisting. 4. DPR undergoes technical and financial appraisal by NHB or authorized agencies. 5. Upon approval, receive sanction letter and proceed with financial closure. 6. Implement the project as per approved DPR. 7. Submit utilization reports and completion certificates for subsidy disbursement in milestones.
deadlines: Rolling basis — subject to EoI cycles and DPR submission windows as notified

scheme_name: APEDA Export Facilitation for Organic Products
overview: APEDA Export Facilitation for Organic Products is a scheme under the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) aimed at promoting the export of organic products from India. It supports exporters through certification, market access, and participation in international trade fairs. The scheme focuses on enhancing the global competitiveness of Indian organic produce by providing technical and financial assistance.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; agri-startups; exporters; farmers
eligibility: Exporters of APEDA-scheduled organic products with valid Import-Export Code (IEC) and Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC) from APEDA are eligible. Farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), MSMEs, and agri-startups engaged in organic production and processing can apply. Applicants must comply with NPOP standards and have a valid organic certification.
benefits: Financial assistance for infrastructure development, quality certification, and market development. Support for participation in international trade fairs and buyer-seller meets. Assistance in obtaining organic certification and compliance with international standards. Access to APEDA’s market intelligence reports and export promotion services. Facilitation of RCMC and IEC registration. Support for branding, packaging, and traceability solutions.
financial_support: Under the Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS), APEDA provides grants for market development, quality development, and export infrastructure. The quantum of support varies based on the project proposal and is subject to availability of funds. Upon approval, submit bank guarantee and receive sanction letter. 8. Implement project and submit utilization report with expenditure details.

financial_support: The incubation program primarily provides infrastructural and technical support rather than direct financial grants. scheme_name: PM Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme (PM-FME)
overview: PM Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme (PM-FME) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries to provide financial, technical and business support for upgradation of existing micro food processing enterprises. The scheme aims to enhance the competitiveness of existing individual micro enterprises and support FPOs/SHGs/cooperatives through credit-linked subsidy, seed capital, and capacity building. It adopts the One District One Product (ODOP) approach to leverage economies of scale in procurement, services and marketing.
target_beneficiaries: Individual Micro Enterprises; FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives; Food Processing Units
eligibility: Individual Micro Enterprises: Individuals / Proprietorship / Partnership/ FPOs/ NGOs/ Cooperatives/ SHGs/ Pvt. Ltd. Co. would be provided credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of the eligible project cost - maximum of Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit for upgradation or setting up of new units. Groups: The Groups - FPOs/ FPCs/ Cooperatives/ SHG and its federation/ Govt. Agencies - established or propose to establish food processing line along with common infrastructure/ Value chain/ incubation centers would be provided credit linked capital subsidy @35% of the eligible project cost with a maximum of Rs. 3.00 Crore. Seed Capital for SHGs: Seed capital @ Rs. 40,000/- per member of SHG for working capital and purchase of small tools maximum upto 4 Lakhs per SHG. Seed Capital given as grant to the SHG Federation by SRLM/SULM through SNA for loan to the members of SHGs.
benefits: Credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of eligible project cost (max Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit for individuals, max Rs. 3.00 Crore for groups), Seed capital @ Rs. 40,000/- per SHG member (max Rs. 4 Lakhs per SHG), 50% financial grant for Branding and Marketing Support, Training on Food Processing Entrepreneurship Development Programme, Support for value chain development and alignment of support infrastructure through ODOP approach.
financial_support: The scheme provides credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of eligible project cost. For individual micro enterprises, the maximum subsidy is Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit. For groups (FPOs/FPCs/Cooperatives/SHG federation/Govt. Agencies) establishing common infrastructure, the maximum subsidy is Rs. 3.00 Crore. Seed capital is provided as grant to SHG Federation @ Rs. 40,000 per member (max Rs. 4 Lakhs per SHG) for working capital and small tools. Marketing and branding support is provided as 50% financial grant to groups of FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives or SPV of micro food processing enterprises.
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit for individual micro enterprises; Rs. 3.00 Crore for groups (FPOs/FPCs/Cooperatives/SHG federation/Govt. Agencies); Rs. 40,000 per SHG member (max Rs. 4 Lakhs per SHG); 50% grant for branding and marketing support to groups
application_process: 1. Visit the official PMFME portal at https://pmfme.mofpi.gov.in 2. Check eligibility under Individual Micro Enterprises or Group category (FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives) 3. Prepare project report with details of proposed food processing unit 4. Submit application through the portal with required documents 5. Application is scrutinized by State/Nodal Agency 6. Upon approval, subsidy is disbursed through linked bank loan 7. Implement project as per approved plan 8. Submit utilization reports and completion certificate
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Food Processing Industries

scheme_name: PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana – Har Khet Ko Pani
overview: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) was launched on 1st July, 2015 with the objective to achieve convergence of investments in irrigation at the field level, expand cultivable area under assured irrigation, improve on-farm water use efficiency, and promote precision irrigation and other water saving technologies. The scheme comprises four components: Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP), Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP), Per Drop More Crop (PDMC), and Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP). It aims to provide end-to-end solutions in the irrigation supply chain, including water resources, distribution network, farm-level applications, and extension activities.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; small and marginal farmers; other farmers
eligibility: Instead of incremental budgeting, PMKSY will adopt a dynamic annual fund allocation methodology that mandates States to allocate more funds to irrigation sectors for becoming eligible to access PMKSY funds. For this purpose: a) A State will become eligible to access PMKSY fund only if it has prepared the District Irrigation Plans (DIP) and State Irrigation Plan (SIP), excepting for the initial year, and the expenditure in water resource development for agriculture sector in the year under consideration is not less than baseline expenditure. The baseline expenditure will be the average of expenditure in irrigation sector irrespective of state departments (i.e. creation of water source, distribution, management and application from State plan schemes) in State Plan in three years prior to the year under consideration.
benefits: The scheme provides financial assistance through subsidy for micro irrigation systems (drip, sprinkler, rain-gun etc.), promotes efficient water conveyance and precision water application devices, supports micro level water storage structures, water lifting devices, secondary storage structures, extension activities for promotion of scientific moisture conservation and agronomic measures, capacity building, training and awareness campaigns, and ICT interventions for monitoring. The subsidy is released via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to beneficiaries' bank/postal accounts, preferably Aadhaar seeded.
financial_support: The pattern of assistance payable under the micro irrigation scheme will be 55% for small and marginal farmers and 45% for other farmers which will be met by both Central Government and State Government in the ratio of 60:40 for all states except the North Eastern and Himalayan states. In the case of these states, ratio of sharing is 90:10. For the Union Territories, funding pattern is 100% grant by the Central Government. The subsidy payable to the beneficiary will be limited to an overall ceiling of 5 hectare per beneficiary. The subsidy payment will be limited to the unit costs specified in the scheme guidelines. 25% higher amounts have been taken into calculation of subsidy for the North Eastern and Himalayan states and 15% higher for states with low penetration of MI namely Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Union Territories.
grant_amount_per_entity: Subsidy limited to an overall ceiling of 5 hectare per beneficiary
application_process: 1. Prepare District Irrigation Plans (DIPs) and State Irrigation Plan (SIP). 2. Ensure expenditure in water resource development for agriculture sector is not less than baseline expenditure (average of three prior years). 3. Submit DIPs and SIPs for approval. 4. Farmers can apply for the scheme either in MIS system (online) or in offline mode. 5. Subsidy is released to the beneficiary electronically through the mechanism of Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare (DAC&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
