Repair Renovation Restoration (RRR) of Water Bodies
overview: The Repair Renovation Restoration (RRR) of Water Bodies scheme is a centrally sponsored component under the Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY). It aims to restore and revive water bodies such as tanks, ponds, and lakes to enhance irrigation potential, improve water storage, recharge groundwater, and increase availability of drinking water. The scheme supports states in undertaking repair, renovation, and restoration of water bodies with central financial assistance, particularly focusing on special category areas and drought-prone regions.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; rural communities; farmers; water user associations
eligibility: State governments are eligible to propose projects under the RRR of Water Bodies scheme. Projects must focus on repair, renovation, and restoration of water bodies such as tanks, ponds, and lakes. Priority is given to special category areas including drought-prone (DPAP), tribal, flood-prone, Left-Wing extremist dominated areas (e.g., Koraput, Bolangir, Kalahandi districts of Odisha), Bundelkhand region of UP and MP, and Marathwada & Vidarbha region of Maharashtra. The scheme is implemented under the Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY).
benefits: Financial assistance from the central government for repair, renovation, and restoration of water bodies. Non-financial benefits include increased irrigation potential, improved groundwater recharge, enhanced drinking water availability, better water use efficiency, and stabilization of irrigation through revived water bodies. The scheme supports sustainable water management and contributes to drought resilience and climate adaptation in rural areas.
financial_support: Under the RRR of Water Bodies scheme, the Government of India provides central financial assistance to state governments for undertaking repair, renovation, and restoration of water bodies. The funding pattern is based on project categories and follows the guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY). Central assistance is released in instalments based on project progress and utilization certificates. The scheme operates as a centrally sponsored scheme with cost-sharing between the Centre and states as per PMKSY norms.
application_process: 1. State governments identify water bodies requiring repair, renovation, and restoration. 2. Project proposals are prepared with detailed project reports (DPRs) including scope, cost estimates, and expected benefits. 3. Proposals are submitted to the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation (DoWR, RD & GR) for appraisal. 4. The DoWR, RD & GR appraises the proposals for technical feasibility and alignment with scheme objectives. 5. Upon approval, central assistance is sanctioned and released in instalments. 6. State governments implement the projects through concerned departments or agencies. 7. Progress is monitored through periodic reporting and field inspections. 8. Utilization certificates and completion reports are submitted for final settlement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per the financial year cycle.
implementing_agency: Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation (DoWR, RD & GR), Ministry of Jal Shakti

scheme_name: PLI Scheme for Drones & Drone Components
overview: The PLI Scheme for Drones & Drone Components is a Production Linked Incentive scheme aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing of drones and drone components in India. It seeks to enhance India's position as a global drone manufacturing hub by providing financial incentives on incremental sales of eligible products. The scheme is part of the broader PLI initiative to promote self-reliance and reduce imports in strategic sectors.
target_beneficiaries: domestic manufacturers; MSME; startups
eligibility: Domestic manufacturers of drones and drone components who are registered in India and have commenced commercial production are eligible. Applicants must meet minimum investment thresholds and incremental sales criteria and commit to specific production targets as outlined in the scheme guidelines.
benefits: Financial incentives on incremental sales of eligible drone and drone component products manufactured in India. Non-financial benefits include facilitation of clearances, single-window support, and promotion of domestic value addition in the drone ecosystem.
financial_support: The scheme provides production linked incentives as a percentage of incremental sales of eligible products over a base year, disbursed annually based on verified sales and investment claims. The incentive rate varies by product category and is subject to annual caps.
application_process: 1. Register on the designated PLI portal for drones 2. Submit application with details of proposed investment and production plan 3. Provide documents including incorporation certificate, GST details, and project report 4. Application reviewed by the Project Management Agency 5. Upon approval, sign agreement with the government 6. Commence production and file quarterly claims for incentives 7. Claims verified and incentives disbursed annually
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: The National Aquifer Mapping and Management (NAQUIM) programme, initiated by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) in 2012 under the Ground Water Management and Regulation Plan Scheme (XII plan), aims to comprehensively map India's aquifers to support effective groundwater management. It involves delineation of aquifers in terms of horizontal and vertical extent, characterization of hydrogeological properties, assessment of resource availability and quality, preparation of aquifer maps, identification and quantification of issues, and development of management strategies for sustainability. The programme has completed mapping of the targeted 25 lakh km² area by 2023 and has expanded into NAQUIM 2.0 for higher granularity and issue-based scientific inputs.
target_beneficiaries: state government agencies; central government departments; policy makers; planners; water resource managers; farmers; industries
eligibility: The NAQUIM programme is implemented by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) in coordination with state government counterparts and collaborates with organizations/institutes like GSI, NGRI, IMD, NRSC, IISc, IIT etc. on specific topics. It is a government-led initiative and not a scheme open for external applications by individuals or entities.
benefits: NAQUIM outputs support drinking water source finding and source sustainability, site selection for Artificial Recharge, safe drinking water in Arsenic affected areas, assured irrigation through ground water in areas with adequate ground water potential, implementation of water conservation and AR recommendations, ground water regulation based on NAQUIM recommendations, rejuvenation of springs, and integration with Atal Bhujal Yojana. The programme has conducted 1300 Public Interaction Programmes (PIPs) at grassroots level with nearly 1 lakh participants, and disseminates findings through www.cgwb.gov.in, www.aims-cgwb.org, and India Water Resource Information System (India-WRIS).
financial_support: The NAQUIM programme is a government-funded initiative under the Ground Water Management and Regulation Plan Scheme (XII plan). No specific financial support mechanism for external beneficiaries is described in the evidence, as it is a mapping and management programme conducted by CGWB and its partners.
application_process: The NAQUIM programme is a government-implemented initiative and does not have an application process for external beneficiaries. It is carried out by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) in collaboration with state governments and technical partners.
deadlines: The mapping of the entire targeted area under NAQUIM was completed in the year 2023. The programme has evolved into NAQUIM 2.0 with ongoing activities.
implementing_agency: Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Ministry of Jal Shakti, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Government of India

overview: The DRDO – Drone Technology Development Fund, referred to as the Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme, supports the development of defence and dual-use systems, subsystems, components, or technologies for products that are Indian Designed, Developed and Manufactured (IDDM). It aims to promote Micro, Small, Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) including start-ups to develop innovative products for the armed forces under the 'Make in India' initiative. The scheme is implemented by DRDO to foster indigenous technological capabilities and self-reliance in defence technologies.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME
eligibility: Indian industries, specially MSMEs, including start-ups, are eligible for the Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme to undertake indigenisation of defence products, subsystems and components, or to develop new technologies as required by DRDO, Services and DPSUs.
benefits: Financial support for project development, access to DRDO's technological expertise, infrastructure, testing facilities, and support for technology transfer and commercialisation of defence technologies developed under the scheme.
financial_support: Under the Technology Development Fund (TDF) Scheme, a corpus fund of Rs. 100 Cr has been created to enable Indian industries, specially MSMEs, for indigenisation of defence products, subsystems and components. The fund may also be utilised for developing new technologies as required by DRDO, Services and DPSUs. The cost of each project under TDF can be up to Rs 10 Cr. The industry can get funding up to 90% of the project cost.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs 10 Cr per project (90% of project cost)
application_process: 1. Identify a defence technology requirement aligned with TDF objectives. 2. Prepare a project proposal detailing innovation, objectives, budget, and timeline. 3. Submit the proposal through the designated DRDO channel. 4. Proposal undergoes technical and financial evaluation by DRDO experts. 5. Upon approval, enter into a formal agreement with DRDO. 6. Receive funds in tranches based on project milestones. 7. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates. 8. Complete project and submit final report and financial statement.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), Ministry of Defence, Government of India

overview: The National Drone Policy 2021, implemented by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) under the Ministry of Civil Aviation, establishes a regulatory framework for the operation of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) in India. It aims to promote safe, secure, and sustainable drone operations while fostering innovation and growth in the drone ecosystem. The policy covers registration, certification, operational permissions, and safety standards for drones, including provisions for drone corridors, beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) operations, and drone training organizations. It applies to all categories of drones and stakeholders, including manufacturers, operators, and service providers.
target_beneficiaries: drone manufacturers; drone operators; drone service providers; startups; MSME
eligibility: Any person or entity intending to operate a drone in Indian airspace must comply with the National Drone Policy 2021. This includes obtaining a Unique Identification Number (UIN) for the drone, securing an Unmanned Aircraft Operator Permit (UAOP) for commercial operations, and adhering to operational limitations based on drone category (nano, micro, small, medium, large). Operators must ensure compliance with safety standards, no-drone zones, and height/restriction guidelines. Foreign nationals and entities may operate drones only through an Indian subsidiary or with specific DGCA approval.
benefits: The policy provides legal recognition for drone operations, enables access to regulated airspace, supports commercial drone services, facilitates participation in government tenders, encourages innovation through sandbox testing, and promotes skill development via approved drone training organizations. It also allows for conditional exemptions under certain rules (e.g., Rule 133A and Rule 160) for specific use cases like research, training, and surveillance.
financial_support: The National Drone Policy 2021 does not include direct financial support, grants, or subsidies. It is a regulatory framework focused on compliance, safety, and operational permissions. Financial incentives, if any, would be administered through separate schemes by other ministries (e.g., Ministry of Defence, Department of Science and Technology) and are not part of this policy.
application_process: 1. Determine the drone category based on weight (nano: ≤250g, micro: 250g–2kg, small: 2kg–25kg, medium: 25kg–150kg, large: >150kg). 2. Obtain a Unique Identification Number (UIN) via the Digital Sky platform by providing drone specifications and owner details. 3. For commercial operations, apply for an Unmanned Aircraft Operator Permit (UAOP) through the Digital Sky portal. 4. Ensure compliance with operational requirements such as pilot training, maintenance checks, and insurance. 5. Submit flight plans and obtain clearance for operations in controlled or restricted airspaces. 6. Adhere to no-drone zones, height limits (typically 400 ft AGL), and visual line-of-sight (VLOS) rules unless granted BVLOS approval. 7. Maintain operational logs and report incidents as required.
deadlines: Rolling basis — UIN and UAOP applications can be submitted at any time through the Digital Sky platform.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India

overview: The Drone Shakti Initiative (MoCA) is a government scheme launched by the Ministry of Civil Aviation to promote the drone and UAV ecosystem in India. It aims to foster innovation, support startups, and create employment opportunities in the drone sector through various initiatives including drone schools, pilot certification, and skill development programs. The initiative focuses on expanding drone applications across sectors such as agriculture, logistics, and surveillance, while ensuring regulatory compliance and safety standards. It also emphasizes skill development through partnerships with institutions like AASSC, IGRUA, and RGNAU to train certified pilots, trainers, and assessors.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; MSME; drone operators; certified pilots; drone schools; training partners
eligibility: The scheme is open to startups, MSMEs, drone operators, drone schools, training partners, and individuals seeking certification as drone pilots, trainers, or assessors. Entities must be registered in India and comply with the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) regulations under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024. Drone operators must hold valid Unique Identification Numbers (UIN) and Drone Authorization Numbers (DAN) as per DGCA guidelines. Training institutions must be affiliated with recognized bodies such as AASSC, IGRUA, or RGNAU.
benefits: The initiative provides financial and non-financial benefits including financial support for drone startups and MSMEs, skill development and certification programs for pilots, trainers, and assessors, facilitation of drone operations through simplified regulatory processes, support for drone applications in agriculture, logistics, and surveillance, promotion of indigenous drone manufacturing, and access to government-backed training and certification programs. It also facilitates ease of doing business through simplified compliance and access to government schemes and incentives.
financial_support: The initiative provides financial support to drone startups and MSMEs through various government schemes, including seed funding, seed loans, and credit guarantee schemes. Specific financial support mechanisms include the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS), Seed Fund Scheme, and Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) managed by SIDBI. The initiative also facilitates access to loans and credit through public sector banks and financial institutions under government-backed guarantee schemes.
application_process: 1. Identify eligibility under the Drone Shakti Initiative based on entity type (startup, MSME, drone operator, training partner, etc.). 2. Ensure compliance with DGCA regulations under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, including obtaining UIN and DAN where applicable. 3. For training partners, affiliate with recognized bodies such as AASSC, IGRUA, or RGNAU. 4. Apply for relevant government schemes such as the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS), Seed Fund Scheme, or Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) through the respective implementing agencies. 5. Submit required documents including incorporation certificates, PAN, business plan, compliance certificates, and training affiliation proofs. 6. Submit application via the respective scheme portal or through the Ministry of Civil Aviation's designated channels. 7. Await verification and approval from the concerned agency.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Civil Aviation

scheme_name: FAME India Phase II – EV Purchase Subsidy
overview: FAME India Phase II is a Government of India scheme launched to promote faster adoption and manufacturing of electric vehicles by providing upfront purchase incentives to consumers and supporting the development of charging infrastructure. The scheme focuses on incentivizing electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, four-wheelers, and buses through demand-side subsidies. It aims to reduce vehicular emissions and dependence on fossil fuels by making EVs more affordable.
target_beneficiaries: individual consumers; fleet operators; institutional buyers; public transport undertakings
eligibility: Electric vehicles that meet the technical specifications and localization criteria as defined under FAME India Phase II are eligible for incentives. The vehicle must be registered in India and purchased from an OEM that has been approved under the scheme. Incentives are available only for vehicles that are not used for commercial transport of goods or passengers unless specifically permitted under the scheme guidelines.
benefits: Upfront reduction in the purchase price of electric vehicles through direct subsidies to buyers. The incentive is claimed by the OEM and passed on to the consumer at the point of sale. The scheme also supports the installation of charging stations and promotes indigenization of EV components.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as a demand incentive directly proportional to the battery capacity of the electric vehicle, with higher subsidies for vehicles having greater kWh capacity. The subsidy amount is deducted from the ex-showroom price and reimbursed to the OEM by the government after verification of sales.
application_process: 1. OEMs must register on the FAME India portal and get their vehicle models approved under the scheme. 2. Consumers purchase eligible EV models from registered OEMs. 3. OEMs upload sales data and claim incentives on the FAME portal. 4. The Heavy Industries Ministry verifies the claims and disburses the subsidy amount to the OEMs. 5. The benefit is reflected as a reduced price for the end consumer.
deadlines: The scheme was valid until March 31, 2024, or until the exhaustion of funds, whichever occurred earlier.
implementing_agency: Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises

overview: The National Electric Mobility Mission Plan (NEMMP) 2020 is a comprehensive initiative launched by the Government of India to promote electric and hybrid vehicles, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, and address environmental concerns related to vehicular emissions. It aims to achieve national fuel security by encouraging the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and developing indigenous manufacturing capabilities for EV components and batteries. The plan sets a target of 6-7 million sales of hybrid and electric vehicles year on year from 2020 onwards and includes incentives for both manufacturers and consumers.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers; consumers; fleet operators; public transport agencies
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component: For manufacturers, eligibility includes domestic production of electric/hybrid vehicles, batteries, or key components with minimum localization requirements; for consumers, eligibility requires purchase of eligible electric or hybrid vehicles as defined under the Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles (FAME) India scheme, which operationalizes NEMMP; fleet operators and public transport agencies are eligible for subsidies on electric buses and commercial vehicles under specified conditions.
benefits: Financial incentives include upfront purchase subsidies for electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger cars, and buses; tax benefits under GST and income tax; exemptions from road tax and registration fees in select states; non-financial benefits include preferential treatment in government procurement, access to dedicated EV lanes (where available), and support for setting up charging infrastructure through public-private partnerships.
financial_support: Financial support is delivered primarily through the FAME India scheme, which offers demand incentives (upfront purchase subsidies) to consumers and institutional buyers, and supports charging infrastructure development. Under FAME II, incentives include INR 15,000 per kWh for electric two-wheelers (up to 40% of cost), INR 10,000 per kWh for electric three-wheelers and passenger cars (up to 40% of cost), and INR 20,000 per kWh for electric buses (up to 50% of cost), with additional incentives for advanced batteries and locally manufactured components.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to 50% of vehicle cost for electric buses, 40% for other EVs, capped at INR 20 lakhs for cars and proportionally lower for two/three-wheelers
application_process: 1. Identify eligible electric or hybrid vehicle models listed under FAME India; 2. Purchase the vehicle from a dealer registered with the FAME scheme; 3. The dealer uploads sale details and documents to the FAME portal; 4. The Department of Heavy Industry (DHI) verifies the claim; 5. Subsidy amount is transferred directly to the dealer, who passes on the benefit to the consumer as a discount.
deadlines: FAME II scheme is operational from April 1, 2019, to March 31, 2024, or until exhaustion of funds, whichever is earlier; applications are accepted on an ongoing basis during this period.
implementing_agency: Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises

scheme_name: UTM (Unmanned Traffic Management) Framework for Startups
overview: The UTM (Unmanned Traffic Management) Framework for Startups is a policy initiative by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) aimed at enabling safe and efficient integration of drones into Indian airspace. It supports startups in developing UTM technologies and services by providing regulatory guidance, testing infrastructure, and operational clearances. The framework encourages innovation in drone traffic management systems, including beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) operations, and aligns with national drone policy goals.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups incorporated in India working on unmanned traffic management (UTM) technologies, including drone navigation, surveillance, communication, and flight planning systems, are eligible to participate in the UTM Framework. Entities must comply with DGCA drone regulations and possess necessary technical capabilities for testing and validation.
benefits: Startups gain access to DGCA-regulated test environments, regulatory guidance on UTM operations, facilitation of flight clearances for testing, collaboration opportunities with aviation stakeholders, and recognition under DGCA’s innovation initiatives. The framework supports validation of UTM solutions in real-world scenarios and aids in scaling operations.
financial_support: The UTM Framework does not provide direct financial grants or funding. Support is primarily non-financial, focusing on regulatory enablement, access to test infrastructure, and operational clearances for drone traffic management systems developed by startups.
application_process: 1. Visit the DGCA website or eGCA portal to express interest in the UTM Framework. 2. Submit company profile and technical details of the UTM solution. 3. Await review by DGCA’s drone policy division. 4. Upon approval, engage in discussions for test environment access and regulatory guidance. 5. Conduct trials under DGCA supervision as per agreed parameters. 6. Submit test results and compliance reports for evaluation.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Ministry of Civil Aviation

scheme_name: PM E-Bus Sewa – Electric Bus Deployment
overview: PM-eBus Sewa is a scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) to promote electric bus deployment in Indian cities. The scheme aims to support the adoption of electric buses for public transport, reduce emissions, and improve urban mobility. It involves central assistance for procurement and operation of electric buses through a sanctioning and steering committee mechanism.
target_beneficiaries: Urban Local Bodies; State Transport Undertakings; Special Purpose Vehicles
eligibility: Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), State Transport Undertakings (STUs), and Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) formed by ULBs/STUs are eligible to apply under the PM-eBus Sewa scheme for deployment of electric buses in cities.
benefits: Financial support for procurement and operation of electric buses, reduction in operational costs due to lower energy and maintenance expenses, environmental benefits through zero tailpipe emissions, improved public transport quality and reliability, and contribution to national climate goals under India's EV mission.
financial_support: Central Assistance (CA) is provided under the scheme as a subsidy for procurement and operation of electric buses. The exact quantum and mechanism are detailed in the scheme guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for disbursement of central assistance, which are available for download from the scheme page.
application_process: 1. Visit the PM-eBus Sewa scheme page on the MoHUA website. 2. Download the scheme guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). 3. Prepare the proposal as per the guidelines. 4. Submit the application through the designated channel as specified in the guidelines. 5. Await review and approval by the Central Sanctioning & Steering Committee (CSSC).
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

scheme_name: Drone Didi Scheme for Women SHGs
overview: The Press Information Bureau (PIB) is the nodal agency of the Government of India under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. It serves as the interface between the government and media, disseminating information about government policies, programmes, and activities through press releases, features, backgrounders, and media outreach. PIB also provides accreditation to media persons, facilitates media facilitation, and offers feedback mechanisms to government departments based on media coverage.
target_beneficiaries: media persons; journalists; government departments; public sector organizations
eligibility: Eligibility for PIB accreditation varies by category: working journalists must be employed with a news organization in Delhi/NCR; freelance journalists require minimum 15 years of experience and 5 years of PIB association; veteran journalists must be 65+ years with 30 years of experience; digital news publishers must comply with IT Rules 2021, have a website active for at least one year, and have editorial team based in Delhi/NCR.
benefits: Accreditation provides easy access to government information, official press conferences, and government offices. It facilitates media outreach, feedback services, and access to PIB's dissemination network. Accredited journalists may also benefit from the Journalist Welfare Scheme (JWS) for financial assistance.
financial_support: Under the Journalist Welfare Scheme (JWS) by the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, financial assistance is provided to media persons in need, though specific quantum, type, and mechanism are not detailed in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Applicants must file their application online in the prescribed format available on the PIB website (https://www.pib.gov.in). 2. Applications for accreditation can be submitted any time. 3. Eligibility criteria, category, and relevant information are available in the Guidelines for Accreditation on PIB’s website. 4. Duly filled applications meeting all criteria are placed before the Central Media Accreditation Committee (CMAC) for consideration. 5. Accreditation is granted upon submission of supporting documents, completion of formalities, recommendation by CMAC, and police verification. 6. For queries, contact designated officers: Shri Abhishek Dayal, ADG (PF), Room No. 202, National Media Centre (Tel: 011-23488048, 23488041); Shri B.H. overview: The National Policy on Biofuels 2018 (Revised 2022) aims to promote the use of biofuels in India by setting indicative blending targets for ethanol and biodiesel, encouraging advanced biofuels, and supporting the development of a sustainable biofuel ecosystem through policy interventions, financial incentives, and institutional mechanisms.
target_beneficiaries: biofuel producers; ethanol manufacturers; biodiesel producers; agricultural farmers; MSMEs in bioenergy; startups in advanced biofuels
eligibility: Eligibility varies by biofuel type and production pathway. For ethanol: producers must comply with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) specifications, have valid licenses from excise authorities, and use approved feedstocks such as sugarcane, maize, damaged food grains, or surplus rice. For biodiesel: producers must use non-edible oils, used cooking oil, or animal fat, and meet BIS standards. Advanced biofuel projects require techno-economic clearance and adherence to sustainability criteria. All applicants must register with the concerned nodal agencies and obtain necessary environmental and statutory clearances.
benefits: Financial incentives include interest subvention, viability gap funding, and tax benefits under GST and excise duty schemes. Non-financial benefits encompass priority in government procurement, facilitation of land allocation, single-window clearances, and support for research and development through institutions like DBT, DST, and CSIR. The policy also enables blending obligations for oil marketing companies (OMCs), ensuring a guaranteed market for biofuel producers.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through mechanisms such as the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana for 2G ethanol, which offers financial assistance of up to ₹600 crores for setting up commercial projects and up to ₹50 crores for demonstration projects. Additional support includes interest subvention on loans, viability gap funding for first-of-its-kind projects, and concessional GST rates. Oil marketing companies are mandated to procure biofuels, ensuring off-take security for producers.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 600 Crores for commercial 2G ethanol projects under Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana
application_process: 1. Identify the appropriate scheme under the National Policy on Biofuels (e.g., Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana for 2G ethanol). 2. Prepare a detailed project report (DPR) including techno-economic analysis, feedstock availability, and environmental impact assessment. 3. Obtain necessary statutory clearances from pollution control boards, forest department, and other relevant agencies. 4. Apply through the designated nodal agency (e.g., Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency - IREDA for JI-VAN Yojana) via their online portal. 5. Submit the DPR along with required documents such as incorporation certificates, land documents, and promoter details. 6. Await technical and financial appraisal by the nodal agency. 7. Upon approval, sign the agreement and fulfill conditions for disbursement of financial support.
deadlines: Scheme-specific; Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana invites applications periodically as per notifications issued by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
implementing_agency: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
contact_details: Email: biofuelcell@petroleum.nic.in | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence

overview: Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana is a central sector scheme launched to provide financial support to integrated bioethanol projects using lignocellulosic biomass and other renewable feedstocks. The scheme aims to promote the production of second-generation (2G) ethanol from non-food biomass sources such as agricultural residues, waste, and grasses. It supports the establishment of commercial and demonstration projects to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
target_beneficiaries: companies; public sector undertakings; joint ventures; private enterprises
eligibility: Integrated bioethanol projects using lignocellulosic biomass and other renewable feedstocks are eligible. Projects must be for the production of second-generation (2G) ethanol and must be implemented by companies, public sector undertakings, joint ventures, or private enterprises registered in India. The project must have a minimum capacity as specified in the scheme guidelines and must use non-food biomass feedstocks.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grants for capital expenditure, interest subvention on loans, and reimbursement of certain operational costs. The scheme also provides support for project management, technical consultancy, and monitoring. Benefits include reduced production costs, improved viability of 2G ethanol projects, and contribution to national biofuel blending targets under the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support up to Rs. 100 crore per project for capital expenditure, interest subvention at the rate of 6% per annum for a period of 5 years on term loans, and reimbursement of expenses related to project management and technical consultancy. Support is disbursed in stages based on project milestones and verification by the implementing agency.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to Rs. 100 crore per project
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed project report (DPR) along with the application form to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. 2. The application is evaluated by a Technical Committee for technical feasibility and financial viability. 3. Upon approval, an in-principle sanction letter is issued. 4. The applicant must secure land, clearances, and financing as per the sanction. 5. After achieving financial closure, the final approval is granted. 6. Funds are released in installments based on verification of project progress and expenditure.
deadlines: The scheme was open for proposals during the specified window as per the official notification; currently, no active application window is indicated in the evidence.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

overview: The Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme 2024 (EMPS-2024) was a subscheme under the PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) Scheme, implemented from 1st April 2024 to 30th September 2024, aimed at promoting electric mobility through demand incentives for electric two-wheelers (e-2W) and three-wheelers (e-3W). It provided financial support based on battery capacity, with incentives of ₹5,000 per kWh for vehicles registered in FY 2024-25, subject to a cap of 15% of the ex-factory price. The scheme has been subsumed into the PM E-DRIVE Scheme, which runs from 1st October 2024 to 31st March 2026 with a total outlay of ₹10,900 crore.
target_beneficiaries: individual buyers; OEMs
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries for e-2W and e-3W include individuals purchasing privately or corporate-owned registered electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers. Vehicles must be manufactured and registered within the validity period of EMPS-2024/PM E-DRIVE certificate. For e-ambulances, eligibility is decided in consultation with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Incentives are not extended when EVs are purchased by Central or State Government departments or their agencies, as it constitutes passing funds between government heads.
benefits: Financial support in the form of upfront reduced purchase price for end-users, reimbursed to OEMs by the Ministry of Heavy Industries. Incentive rate: ₹5,000 per kWh for e-2W/e-3W registered in FY 2024-25, and ₹2,500 per kWh for those registered in FY 2025-26 under PM E-DRIVE. The incentive is capped at 15% of the ex-factory price, whichever is lower. Additional benefits include mandatory warranty requirements: 3 years or 20,000 km for e-2W, 3 years or 40,000 km for e-3W (e-rickshaw), and 3 years or 80,000 km for e-3W (L5).
financial_support: Demand incentives are provided at ₹5,000 per kWh for e-2W/e-3W registered in FY 2024-25 and ₹2,500 per kWh for FY 2025-26, subject to a cap of 15% of the ex-factory price. The incentive is reimbursed to OEMs after submission of claims. For e-buses, the incentive is ₹10,000 per kWh with size-based caps: standard bus (>10m & <=12m) up to ₹35,00,000, midi bus (>8m & <=10m) up to ₹25,00,000, and mini bus (>6m & <=8m) up to ₹20,00,000. Support for e-buses is released in four installments: 20% after supply order, 30% after commencement of commercial operation, 25% after 6 months, and 25% after 18 months of successful operation.
grant_amount_per_entity: 15% of ex-factory price or ₹5,000 per kWh (whichever is lower) for e-2W/e-3W; for e-buses: up to ₹35,00,000 for standard bus, ₹25,00,000 for midi bus, ₹20,00,000 for mini bus
application_process: 1. OEMs must apply for registration with the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) by submitting Annexure-I (Manufacturer Registration Form) along with required documents including Company Registration Certificate, GST Registration, PAN Card, Testing/Homologation Certificate, Pre-registration of EV model, MOA/AOA, sales/service network proof, and photographs of the vehicle. 2. Submit hard copy of the application to Deputy Secretary (E-Mobility), Udyog Bhavan, New Delhi-110011. 3. MHI processes the application and confirms registration if found in order. 4. OEMs upload production data of EVs for which they seek incentives. 5. After sale, OEMs submit reimbursement claims within 120 days, accompanied by an undertaking (Annexure-III), board resolution (Annexure-IV), and photo ID proof. 6. Claims are verified by MHI and reimbursed upon validation.
deadlines: The scheme was implemented from 1st April 2024 to 30th September 2024 and has been subsumed under PM E-DRIVE, which runs from 1st October 2024 to 31st March 2026.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Heavy Industries

overview: The SATAT Scheme (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) aims to promote Compressed Biogas (CBG) as a green transport fuel by setting up CBG plants and ensuring off-take by Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs). It supports entrepreneurs in establishing CBG production units using biomass and waste feedstock, contributing to waste-to-wealth initiatives and reducing dependence on fossil fuels. The scheme fosters a market-driven ecosystem for CBG production, procurement, and utilization in the transportation sector.
target_beneficiaries: entrepreneurs; MSME; farmers; waste management agencies; industrial units
eligibility: Any entrepreneur, MSME, cooperative society, self-help group, or industrial unit can apply to set up a CBG plant under the SATAT Scheme. The applicant must have access to suitable feedstock such as agricultural residue, cattle dung, sugarcane press mud, municipal solid waste, or sewage treatment plant waste. The plant must comply with technical standards and safety norms as specified by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) and other relevant authorities.
benefits: Benefits include assured off-take of CBG by OMCs at a fixed price for a period of 10 years, financial support through subsidies and incentives, technical guidance from implementing agencies, and facilitation in statutory clearances. The scheme promotes waste-to-wealth conversion, reduces greenhouse gas emissions, and provides additional income to farmers and waste generators through feedstock supply.
financial_support: Financial support includes a subsidy of INR 4 lakhs per tonne per day (TPD) of CBG production capacity, subject to a maximum of INR 2 crores per project. Additionally, OMCs provide an assured off-take agreement for CBG at a fixed price for 10 years, ensuring revenue stability. The subsidy is disbursed in stages linked to project milestones after verification by the implementing agency.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 2 crores per project
application_process: 1. Identify suitable feedstock and site for CBG plant setup. 2. Prepare Detailed Project Report (DPR) including technical, financial, and environmental aspects. 3. Apply online via the SATAT portal or through the concerned OMC. 4. Submit application along with DPR, land documents, feedstock agreement, and other required documents. 5. Application is reviewed by the OMC and forwarded to the Steering Committee for approval. 6. Upon approval, sign off-take agreement with OMC. 7. Install CBG plant as per approved DPR and technical standards. 8. Commission plant and commence CBG production for off-take by OMC.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

overview: The Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP) is a Government of India initiative aimed at reducing dependence on fossil fuels by blending ethanol with petrol. It seeks to promote the use of biofuels, support farmers through increased demand for sugarcane and other feedstocks, and contribute to environmental sustainability by lowering vehicular emissions. The programme mandates Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) to procure ethanol from domestic sources and blend it with petrol as per the notified blending targets.
target_beneficiaries: ethanol producers; sugarcane farmers; agri-based industries; MSMEs in biofuel sector
eligibility: Ethanol producers must be registered with the concerned State Excise Department and have a valid license for production and supply of ethanol. They must supply ethanol that meets the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) specification IS 15464:2004 (Fuel Ethanol for petrol blending). Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) are responsible for procurement and blending as per the EBP guidelines issued by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
benefits: Ethanol producers receive a guaranteed procurement mechanism through OMCs under the administered price mechanism. Farmers benefit from increased demand for sugarcane, maize, and other biomass, leading to better price realization. The programme supports rural employment, reduces greenhouse gas emissions, and enhances energy security. Financial incentives include interest subvention and financial assistance for setting up or expanding distillation capacity under related schemes.
financial_support: Financial support for ethanol projects is provided through the Interest Subvention Scheme for setting up 2G ethanol biorefineries and the Scheme for Extending Financial Assistance to Sugar Undertakings for setting up new molasses-based distilleries or expanding existing ones. Under these, interest subvention of 6% per annum or 50% of the interest charged by banks, whichever is lower, is provided for a period of 5 years on loans up to INR 150 Crore for setting up new distilleries or expanding existing ones.
application_process: 1. Ethanol producers must register with the respective State Excise Authority and obtain necessary clearances. 2. Ensure compliance with BIS standards for fuel ethanol (IS 15464:2004). 3. Enter into supply agreements with Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) through tender or nomination basis. 4. Submit quality and quantity documentation as required by OMCs for each consignment. 5. Receive payment from OMCs based on the notified ethanol price under the administered price mechanism.
deadlines: Rolling basis — ethanol supply and procurement occur throughout the year as per OMC requirements and notified blending targets.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

overview: The National Bamboo Mission (NBM) is a centrally sponsored scheme implemented by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. It aims to promote holistic growth of the bamboo sector through area-based, regionally differentiated strategies, focusing on increasing bamboo cultivation, improving post-harvest management, and developing product processing and value addition. The mission supports farmers, artisans, and entrepreneurs engaged in bamboo-based activities across India.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; artisans; entrepreneurs; MSME; self-help groups
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include individual farmers, farmer producer organizations (FPOs), self-help groups (SHGs), joint liability groups (JLGs), cooperatives, NGOs, and entrepreneurs engaged in bamboo cultivation, primary processing, value addition, and marketing activities. Beneficiaries must possess land or have legal rights to cultivate bamboo, and proposals must align with the mission's objectives and be submitted through the State Bamboo Mission or nodal department.
benefits: Financial assistance for bamboo plantation, establishment of nurseries, water harvesting structures, and pest management. Support for setting up primary processing units (e.g., slicing, splitting, treatment), product development units (e.g., handicrafts, furniture, bamboo shoots), and marketing infrastructure. Capacity building through training and exposure visits. Technical support for quality improvement and innovation. Subsidy-linked credit facilitation through banks.
financial_support: The scheme provides back-ended subsidies ranging from 50% to 100% of the project cost, depending on the beneficiary category and activity. For general category farmers, assistance is up to 50% of the cost; for SC/ST, women, and beneficiaries in Northeastern and Himalayan states, assistance can go up to 100%. Financial support is released in installments based on verification of field-level achievements and is routed through the State Bamboo Missions to the beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant activity under NBM (plantation, processing, value addition, etc.). 2. Prepare a detailed project report (DPR) including cost estimates, location, and expected outcomes. 3. Submit the proposal to the State Bamboo Mission or the nodal department of agriculture/horticulture in the respective state. 4. The proposal undergoes technical and financial appraisal by the State Level Committee. 5. Upon approval, administrative sanction is issued. 6. Beneficiary implements the project as per approved plan. 7. After verification of progress, subsidy is released in installments directly to the beneficiary's bank account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and state-specific announcements.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

overview: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) is a statutory body under the Ministry of Power, Government of India, established on 1st March 2002 under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001. Its primary mission is to reduce the energy intensity of the Indian economy by developing policies and strategies focused on self-regulation and market principles. BEE promotes energy efficiency across sectors through schemes like Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT), Standards & Labelling, and initiatives supporting electric vehicle charging infrastructure. It acts as the Central Nodal Agency for deploying public EV-charging infrastructure as per guidelines issued on 14th January 2022.
target_beneficiaries: industries; MSMEs; commercial buildings; residential consumers; state designated agencies; utilities
eligibility: Eligibility varies by scheme; for PAT scheme, designated consumers from energy-intensive sectors (Aluminum, Cement, Chlor-Alkali, Fertilizer, Iron & Steel, Paper & Pulp, Railways, Thermal Power, Textile) are notified based on specific energy consumption norms. For EV charging infrastructure, states must designate State Nodal Agencies (SNAs) to coordinate deployment. General eligibility for BEE programmes includes industries, commercial establishments, MSMEs, and government entities engaged in energy efficiency initiatives.
benefits: BEE provides financial assistance to institutions for promoting energy efficiency, promotes innovative financing of energy efficiency projects, develops testing and certification procedures, facilitates pilot and demonstration projects, promotes use of energy-efficient equipment and systems, encourages preferential treatment for energy-efficient appliances, prepares educational curricula on energy efficiency, and implements international cooperation programmes. It also enables energy savings certification, reduces GHG emissions, and lowers energy costs across sectors.
financial_support: BEE provides financial assistance to institutions for promoting efficient use of energy and its conservation. It promotes innovative financing mechanisms for energy efficiency projects. Specific financial details like fund size or per-entity grants are not explicitly mentioned in the evidence for the EV charging infrastructure scheme, but BEE leverages multi-lateral, bi-lateral and private sector support for programme implementation.
application_process: 1. States must designate a State Nodal Agency (SNA) to coordinate deployment of public EV-charging infrastructure as per MoP guidelines dated 14th January 2022. 2. SNAs oversee the installation and operation of EV charging stations in public areas. 3. BEE supports SNAs through policy measures, technical guidance, and coordination with central agencies. 4. Entities interested in setting up EV charging infrastructure can approach their respective SNA for approvals and guidelines. 5. Compliance with technical standards and safety norms is required for installation and operation.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, Government of India
contact_details: Email: dg-bee[at]nic[dot]in | Phone: 011-26766702 | Address: 4th Floor, Sewa Bhawan, R.K. Puram, New Delhi - 110066

overview: NITI Aayog serves as the apex public policy think tank of the Government of India, tasked with catalyzing economic development and fostering cooperative federalism through the involvement of State Governments in economic policymaking using a bottom-up approach. It provides strategic, functional, and technical inputs to the Prime Minister and Government at all levels, focusing on areas such as agriculture, social sectors, innovation, frontier technologies, manufacturing, services, smart urbanization, mobility, clean energy, improved governance, and aspirational districts. NITI Aayog also monitors and evaluates government programmes, promotes innovation and entrepreneurship through initiatives like Atal Innovation Mission, and fosters partnerships with stakeholders including academia, industry, and international think tanks.
target_beneficiaries: State Governments; Union Territories; Central Ministries; Academia; Industry; Startups; NGOs; Civil Society
eligibility: NITI Aayog serves as the apex public policy think tank of the Government of India, and the nodal agency tasked with catalysing economic development and fostering cooperative federalism through the involvement of State Governments in the economic policymaking process using a bottom-up approach.
benefits: NITI Aayog provides strategic, functional, and technical inputs to the Prime Minister and Government at all levels; fosters cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives with States; develops mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate them at higher levels of government; ensures national security interests are incorporated in economic strategy and policy; pays special attention to sections of society at risk of not benefiting adequately from economic progress; designs strategic and long-term policy and programme frameworks, monitors their progress and efficacy, and uses feedback for innovative improvements; provides advice and encourages partnerships between key stakeholders and national/international like-minded think tanks, educational and policy research institutions; creates a knowledge, innovation, and entrepreneurial support system through a collaborative community of national and international experts, practitioners, and other partners; offers a platform for resolution of inter-sectoral and inter-departmental issues to accelerate development agenda implementation; maintains a state-of-the-art resource centre as a repository of research on good governance and best practices in sustainable and equitable development, and helps disseminate findings to stakeholders; actively monitors and evaluates programme implementation, identifies needed resources to strengthen success probability and scope of delivery; focuses on technology upgradation and capacity building for programme implementation; and undertakes other activities necessary to further the execution of the national development agenda.
financial_support: NITI Aayog is supported by an attached office, Development Monitoring and Evaluation Organisation (DMEO), a flagship initiative, Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), and an autonomous body, National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development (NILERD). Its entire gamut of activities is divided into four main heads: Policy and Programme Framework, Cooperative Federalism, Monitoring and Evaluation, Think Tank, and Knowledge and Innovation Hub. The different divisions, cells, attached and autonomous bodies provide the requisite coordination and support framework needed to carry out its mandate.
implementing_agency: NITI Aayog, National Institution for Transforming India, Government of India

overview: The Alternate Fuels for Transportation (Hydrogen Mobility) scheme under the Department of Science & Technology (DST) aims to promote hydrogen as a clean fuel for transportation to reduce carbon emissions and support India's green mobility goals. It focuses on research, development, and deployment of hydrogen-based technologies in the transport sector, including fuel cell vehicles and refueling infrastructure. The scheme supports innovation through funding and collaboration with industry and research institutions to advance hydrogen mobility solutions.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; research institutions; industry
eligibility: Eligible Technology Entities engaged in developing RDI-intensive technology (TRL4 and above), including companies registered under the Companies Act 2013, partnerships under the Indian Partnership Act 1932, limited liability partnerships under the Limited Liability Partnership Act 2008, and startups as defined by DPIIT Notification G.S.R. 127(E) dated 19 February 2019, as may be modified from time to time.
benefits: Financial support through equity, debt, or a combination via Second Level Fund Managers (SLFMs); access to the Research Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF) under the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF); support for scale-up of hydrogen mobility technologies; facilitation of fund flow through Treasury Single Account (TSA) system; intellectual property rights vest with the Eligible Technology Entities.
financial_support: Funding is provided through the Research Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF) with a total outlay of ₹1 lakh crore. Modes of financing include long-term loans at low or nil interest rates, equity infusion (especially for startups), and contributions to Deep-Tech Fund of Funds. Financing can cover up to 50% of assessed project cost for transformative RDI projects at Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) 4 and above, with exceptions possible via the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS). Disbursements are routed exclusively through designated Second-Level Fund Managers (SLFMs).
application_process: 1. Industry stakeholders seeking funding must not send proposals directly to DST. 2. Disbursements are routed exclusively through designated Second-Level Fund Managers (SLFMs). 3. Interested SLFMs (Alternate Investment Funds, Development Finance Institutions, NBFCs, or Focused Research Organizations) must express interest by writing to Dr Jyoti Sharma, Head, RDI Cell at sharma[dot]jyoti[at]nic[dot]in. 4. Existing NBFCs planning to establish AIFs are encouraged to contact DST regarding potential participation. 5. Fund flow from RDIF to SLFMs occurs via Alternate Investment Fund (AIF) mechanisms or loans at low rates with extended tenors. 6. SLFMs prepare fund requirement showing estimated receipts from repayment or exit proceeds and forward to RDIF. 7. Upon receipt of demand, RDIF releases funds to the designated bank account of the SLFM within a specified time frame.
implementing_agency: Department of Science & Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology

scheme_name: EESL EV Aggregation Scheme for Bulk Procurement
overview: The EESL EV Aggregation Scheme for Bulk Procurement is a government initiative under the National Electric Mobility Mission Plan (NEMMP) 2020, aimed at accelerating the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) in India through bulk procurement by government departments and public sector undertakings. The scheme leverages EESL's innovative business model to aggregate demand, reduce costs, and deploy EVs and charging infrastructure at scale without upfront capital expenditure from beneficiary agencies. It supports India's goals of reducing carbon emissions, decreasing fossil fuel dependence, and promoting sustainable transportation.
target_beneficiaries: government departments; public sector undertakings; MSME
eligibility: Government departments, public sector undertakings, and other eligible entities seeking to procure electric vehicles and charging infrastructure through EESL's aggregation model are eligible to participate. Participation requires entering into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) or agreement with EESL for the supply, installation, and operation of EVs and related infrastructure under a service-based model.
benefits: Beneficiaries gain access to electric vehicles and charging infrastructure with zero upfront capital expenditure, pay only for usage (pay-as-you-save model), benefit from reduced operational and maintenance costs, contribute to national decarbonization goals, and receive end-to-end project management from EESL including procurement, installation, commissioning, and operations & maintenance. The scheme also enables compliance with government sustainability mandates and enhances green credentials.
financial_support: The scheme operates on a 'pay-as-you-save' or service model where EESL bears the upfront capital cost for EVs and charging infrastructure, and beneficiary agencies make payments based on actual usage or savings achieved. There is no direct subsidy or loan; instead, EESL recovers its investment through agreed-upon service charges over the contract period, typically tied to kilometers run or energy consumed, ensuring no financial burden on the beneficiary at the outset.
application_process: 1. Express interest via the EESL website or designated portal for the EV aggregation scheme. 2. Enter into discussions with EESL to assess vehicle and charging infrastructure requirements. 3. Sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) or agreement outlining scope, volume, and financial terms. 4. EESL procures EVs and charging equipment through competitive bidding. 5. EESL handles delivery, installation, and commissioning of vehicles and chargers. 6. Beneficiary agency begins usage and makes payments as per the agreed service model (e.g., per km or per kWh). 7. EESL provides operations and maintenance support throughout the contract period.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on demand aggregation cycles.
implementing_agency: Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL)

overview: BIRAC Industrial Biofoundry Support is a scheme under the Bioeconomy & Biofuels category aimed at providing infrastructure and technical support for scaling up bio-based innovations. It enables startups and SMEs to access advanced biofoundry facilities for strain engineering, fermentation, and downstream processing to accelerate product development and commercialization. The scheme supports the transition from lab-scale to pilot-scale operations, reducing the time and cost associated with scaling biotechnological processes. It is implemented through selected BioNEST incubators and partner institutions equipped with biofoundry capabilities.
target_beneficiaries: startups; SMEs; biotech entrepreneurs
eligibility: Indian startups and SMEs registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or LLP Act, 2008 with at least 51% shareholding by Indian citizens. The applicant must have a proof-of-concept (PoC) or validated prototype (TRL ≥ 4) in biotechnology domains such as healthcare, agri-tech, industrial biotech, or bio-IT. Preference is given to entities supported by BIRAC’s BioNEST program or other recognized incubators. The technology should have potential for scale-up and commercialization with clear IP ownership or freedom to operate.
benefits: Access to state-of-the-art biofoundry infrastructure including fermenters, downstream processing units, analytics, and automation. Technical support from domain experts in strain engineering, process optimization, and scale-up. Mentorship on regulatory compliance, IP management, and technology transfer. Opportunity to generate pilot-scale data for fundraising and regulatory submissions. No equity dilution as support is provided via grant-in-aid to host institutions. Networking with investors, industry partners, and potential off-takers.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support to startups. Instead, BIRAC provides grant-in-aid to selected BioNEST incubators and partner institutions to set up and operate biofoundry facilities. Startups access these facilities on a subsidized or fee-for-service basis, with costs determined by the host institution based on usage of equipment, consumables, and technical manpower. There is no fixed grant amount per entity; support is in-kind infrastructure access.
application_process: 1. Identify a BIRAC-supported BioNEST incubator or partner institution with biofoundry capabilities. 2. Discuss your technology and scale-up requirements with the facility manager. 3. Submit a formal application through the host institution detailing the project scope, objectives, timeline, and resource needs. 4. The institution evaluates the proposal based on technical readiness, scalability potential, and alignment with biofoundry capabilities. 5. If approved, sign a service agreement outlining access terms, timelines, and cost structure. 6. Begin work at the biofoundry facility with technical support from the host team. 7. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates as required. 8. Upon completion, receive a completion certificate and data package for further development or fundraising.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round subject to facility availability and host institution approval cycles.
implementing_agency: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), a Public Sector Enterprise set up by Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India

scheme_name: Design Linked Incentive (DLI) for Chip Design
overview: The Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme for Chip Design is a government initiative under the India Semiconductor Mission to provide financial incentives and infrastructure support to domestic companies, startups, and MSMEs engaged in the design of integrated circuits (ICs), chipsets, system on chips (SoCs), and related IP cores. The scheme aims to reduce dependency on imports, strengthen the domestic semiconductor design ecosystem, and promote innovation in chip design through fiscal support linked to sales turnover and deployment of semiconductor products.
target_beneficiaries: domestic companies; startups; MSMEs
eligibility: The applicant must be a company incorporated in India under the Companies Act, 2013 or earlier, or a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) registered under the LLP Act, 2008. The entity must be engaged in the design of integrated circuits (ICs), chipsets, system on chips (SoCs), semiconductor IP cores, or related designs. Startups and MSMEs are eligible provided they meet the design activity criteria. The design must be for deployment in electronic products, and the applicant must have a clear plan for fabrication and/or deployment of the designed semiconductor product.
benefits: Financial incentive of up to 50% of eligible expenditure on semiconductor design, including EDA tools, software licenses, IP procurement, manpower costs, and tape-out costs. Support for deployment-linked incentive of 4% to 6% of net sales turnover over 5 years for deployed semiconductor products. Access to government-approved EDA tools and design infrastructure through approved partners. Fiscal support is disbursed in stages linked to milestones such as design completion, tape-out, and product deployment.
financial_support: The scheme provides two components: (1) Product Design Linked Incentive (PDLI) of up to 50% of eligible design expenditure, capped at INR 15 Crore per applicant; and (2) Deployment Linked Incentive (DLI) of 4% to 6% of net sales turnover of the deployed semiconductor product over a period of 5 years from the date of deployment. The total financial support per applicant is subject to a ceiling of INR 30 Crore. Incentives are disbursed in stages based on achievement of pre-defined milestones verified by the Programme Management Agency (PMA).
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 30 Crore per applicant (combined PDLI and DLI)
application_process: 1. Eligible applicants must register on the India Semiconductor Mission portal. 2. Submit a detailed application including company profile, design proposal, bill of materials, fabrication plan, and deployment strategy. 3. Upload required documents such as Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, GST details, design specifications, and financial statements. 4. Application is reviewed by the Programme Management Agency (PMA) for technical and financial feasibility. 5. Upon approval, sign an agreement with the India Semiconductor Mission. 6. Incur eligible expenses and submit claims for reimbursement. 7. Claims are verified and incentives are disbursed in stages linked to milestones.
deadlines: Applications are accepted periodically as per notifications issued by the India Semiconductor Mission. Specific windows are announced on the portal; currently, there is no fixed rolling deadline but subject to periodic calls.
implementing_agency: India Semiconductor Mission, under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) Startup Support is a government initiative under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship in the semiconductor and display manufacturing sectors. It provides financial and non-financial support to startups engaged in semiconductor design, manufacturing, packaging, testing, and related advanced technologies. The scheme aims to strengthen India’s position in the global semiconductor value chain by nurturing early-stage ventures through incubation, mentorship, and funding linkages.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013 or as an LLP, working in semiconductor design, manufacturing, packaging, testing, or related advanced technologies, with a focus on innovation and technology development, and recognized by DPIIT or recommended by ISM-approved incubators.
benefits: Access to ISM-approved incubation centers, mentorship from industry experts, technical support for design and prototyping, facilitation of access to semiconductor fab and testing labs, support for IP filing and patenting, assistance in regulatory compliance, and linkages to investors and industry partners.
financial_support: Financial support includes seed funding of up to INR 50 Lakhs per startup through approved incubators, disbursed as grants or convertible notes based on milestone achievement, and support for accessing follow-on funding from government funds or private investors.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 50 Lakhs
application_process: 1. Apply through an ISM-approved incubation center 2. Submit startup profile, technology proposal, and team details 3. Undergo technical and business evaluation by the incubator 4. Receive recommendation from the incubator to ISM 5. ISM reviews and approves support package 6. Sign agreement and receive financial and non-financial support 7. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on availability of funds and incubator capacity.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

It is implemented through the Research, Development, and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, which was approved by the Union Cabinet on July 1, 2025, with a total outlay of ₹1 lakh crore. scheme_name: National Cyber Security Policy Implementation Fund
overview: The National Cyber Security Policy Implementation Fund is a financial mechanism established under India's National Cyber Security Policy to support cybersecurity initiatives, capacity building, and infrastructure development across government and critical sectors.
target_beneficiaries: government departments; critical information infrastructure sectors; public sector undertakings; academic institutions; startups in cybersecurity
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include central and state government ministries/departments, public sector undertakings, critical information infrastructure sectors (such as power, telecom, banking, finance, transport, etc.), academic and research institutions engaged in cybersecurity R&D, and recognized startups and MSMEs working in the cybersecurity domain, subject to approval by the empowered committee overseeing the fund.
benefits: Financial support for cybersecurity projects, access to advanced threat intelligence platforms, funding for setting up Security Operations Centres (SOCs), grants for cybersecurity research and innovation, support for participation in international cybersecurity exercises and collaborations, capacity building through specialized training programs, and assistance in achieving compliance with national and international cybersecurity standards.
financial_support: The fund provides financial assistance in the form of grants and subsidies for approved cybersecurity initiatives, with disbursement based on project milestones and outcomes. overview: Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) is Government of India's flagship initiative to create and promote a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship across the country. AIM's objective is to develop new programmes and policies for fostering innovation in different sectors of the economy, provide platforms and collaboration opportunities for different stakeholders, and create an umbrella structure to oversee the innovation & entrepreneurship ecosystem of the country. target_beneficiaries: students; startups; MSME; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligibility varies by sub-programme: For Atal Tinkering Labs (ATL), schools across India can apply; for Atal Incubation Centres (AIC), universities, institutions and corporates can apply; for Atal Community Innovation Centres (ACIC), applicants must be from unserved/underserved regions with a partnership model requiring equal or greater matching funding; for Atal New India Challenge (ANIC), Indian companies incorporated under Companies Act 1956/2013, primarily MSMEs or DPIIT-recognized startups with majority stake held in India and a working prototype of the proposed solution relevant to the challenge area can apply.
benefits: Benefits include access to 21st century tools and technologies (IoT, 3D printing, robotics, rapid prototyping), mentorship through Mentors of Change program, funding support, technical facilities, resource-based support, partnerships and networking, co-working spaces, lab facilities, training programs, curriculum integration, evaluation and monitoring systems, and opportunities to participate in national innovation challenges and marathons. Financial support varies by programme: ATLs receive grant-in-aid for establishment, AICs receive support for operationalization, ACICs receive up to Rs 2.5 crores grant subject to matching funding, and ANIC provides funding up to INR 1 crore for selected startups.
financial_support: Financial support varies across AIM programmes: Atal Tinkering Labs (ATL) receive grant-in-aid for establishment with schools expected to set up ATL within 3 months of fund receipt; Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) receive support for operationalization including technical facilities and mentorship; Atal Community Innovation Centres (ACICs) receive a grant of up to Rs 2.5 crores subject to a partner proving equal or greater matching funding; Atal New India Challenge (ANIC) provides funding up to INR 1 crore to selected startups for prototype to commercialization over 12-18 months along with associated support from the AIM innovation ecosystem.
application_process: 1. Visit the official AIM website at aim.gov.in 2. Navigate to the specific programme section (e.g., ATL, AIC, ACIC, ANIC) 3. Check if the application portal is open (as noted on the homepage: 'Important Dear Applicants, please note that the application portal for ATL, AIC and ACIC are not currently open') 4. If open, download guidelines and application forms from the respective programme page 5. Fill out the application with required details 6. Upload necessary documents 7. Submit the application through the designated portal 8. Await evaluation and selection as per the programme timeline 9. Upon selection, complete establishment or implementation as per guidelines 10. Submit utilization certificates and periodic reports via MyATL dashboard or equivalent systems.
deadlines: Application portal for ATL, AIC and ACIC are not currently open. Specific programmes like Youth Co:Lab have defined deadlines (e.g., Apply before midnight on 20th March 2026 for Youth Co:Lab National Innovation Challenge 2026). ATL Marathon and School Innovation Marathon have annual cycles with announcements made via AIM website.
