overview: The DSCI Cybersecurity Startup Programme is an initiative by the Data Security Council of India (DSCI) aimed at supporting cybersecurity startups through incubation, mentorship, and industry collaboration. It is part of DSCI's broader efforts to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in the cybersecurity domain via its Centres of Excellence such as N-CoE and CCoE. The programme focuses on nurturing early-stage ventures by providing access to DSCI's network, technical guidance, and market linkages.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: The programme is open to cybersecurity startups, particularly those emerging from DSCI's Centres of Excellence such as N-CoE and CCoE, with a focus on innovation in hardware security, software security, and privacy technologies. Preference is given to ventures led by women entrepreneurs and those from tier-II/III cities.
benefits: Startups benefit from mentorship by industry experts, access to DSCI's network of investors and corporates, participation in hackathons and innovation challenges, support for product development and commercialization, and opportunities to showcase at DSCI flagship events. They also gain visibility through thought leadership platforms and access to global cybersecurity markets.
financial_support: The programme does not provide direct financial grants or funding to startups. Instead, it facilitates access to investment networks and helps startups become investment-ready through mentorship, product validation, and market linkage support. Financial support, if any, is indirect and partner-driven.
application_process: 1. Identify eligibility under DSCI's incubation initiatives such as N-CoE or CCoE. 2. Apply through the respective Centre of Excellence portal or via DSCI's official channels. 3. Submit a detailed proposal including technology innovation, team profile, and market potential. 4. Undergo evaluation by DSCI and partner experts. 5. Selected startups are inducted into the incubation programme with access to labs, mentorship, and industry connect.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Data Security Council of India (DSCI)

overview: Information Security Education and Awareness (ISEA) is an initiative of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, aimed at generating human resources in Information Security and creating general awareness on Cyber Hygiene/Cyber Security among the masses. The project, started in 2005 and currently in its third phase since October 2023, focuses on four key verticals: generating highly skilled and certified cybersecurity professionals (CISOs), grooming students towards product and solution development, strengthening research and education in emerging areas of Information Security, and developing cyber-aware Digital Naagriks (mass awareness). It is implemented through 50 premier academic institutions in a hub-and-spoke model, supported by common infrastructure and shared resources via the ISEA Virtual Platform (IVP).
target_beneficiaries: students; faculty; government officials; police; MSME; entrepreneurs; senior citizens; women; NGOs; academic institutions
eligibility: Eligibility varies by vertical: For CISO training and certification, professionals seeking specialization in 13 domains of knowledge and skilling are eligible; for student grooming, students from 50 participating Lead & Co-Lead institutes and affiliated colleges can participate in Bootcamps, Hackathons, and Innovation Challenges; for research and education, faculty, professionals, Post-docs, MS/PhD scholars, and research personnel in niche areas of Information Security are eligible; for mass awareness, general users, students, teachers, government personnel, LEAs, parents, women, and senior citizens can participate in awareness programs, workshops, and online quiz competitions.
benefits: Participants gain access to training and certification programs (including CISO), skill development in 10 thematic areas of cybersecurity, opportunities to innovate through Bootcamps, Hackathons, and Innovation Challenges, access to standardized curricula, specialized M.Tech programs, MOOC courses, faculty development programs, internships, research support (Post-docs, SRF/JRF, etc.), domain-specific lab setup, paper publication and patent filing support, participation in national/international conferences and expert lectures, access to cybersecurity exercise platforms, sandboxing environments, IT-OT simulation platforms, and centralized data repositories via ISEA-Cloud and ISEA Virtual Platform (IVP), and mass awareness through awareness weeks, workshops, online quizzes, and multilingual awareness material (handbooks, newsletters, videos, posters, cartoon stories) disseminated through print, electronics, social media, and staysafeonline.in.
financial_support: The ISEA Project is funded by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India. ISEA Phase II was approved with an outlay of Rs. 96.08 crore for implementation over 5 years w.e.f. 01.04.2014. Financial support under the scheme includes funding for training programs, research manpower (Post-docs, MS by Research, SRF/JRF, RA, Young Fellows), setting up domain-specific labs, faculty build-up, research paper publications, patent filing, national and international conferences, expert lectures, development of standardized curriculum, specialized M.Tech programs, MOOC courses, faculty development programs, internships, and mass awareness activities including awareness weeks, workshops, online quiz competitions, and production and dissemination of multilingual awareness material.
application_process: 1. Visit the ISEA website at https://isea.gov.in 2. Navigate to the relevant vertical section (e.g., Grooming Students, Research & Education, CISO Training & Certification, or Mass Awareness) 3. Select the specific program of interest (e.g., Bootcamp, Hackathon, Innovation Challenge, MOOC, Internship, or Awareness Workshop) 4. Click on 'Register now' for the chosen program 5. Fill in the registration form with required details 6. Submit the form and await confirmation 7. Upon approval, access the program via the ISEA Virtual Platform (IVP) 8. Participate in the scheduled activities (online or at designated institutes) 9. Complete assessments or project work as required 10. Receive certification or recognition upon successful completion.
deadlines: Rolling basis — programs such as Bootcamps, Hackathons, Innovation Challenges, MOOCs, internships, and awareness workshops have specific start and end dates as per the event calendar; admissions are open until seats are filled or as per the schedule announced on the website.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India

overview: The MSME Industry 4.0 Adoption Scheme is designed to support micro, small, and medium enterprises in adopting advanced technologies under Industry 4.0, including automation, IoT, AI, and digital transformation, to enhance productivity, competitiveness, and sustainability. The scheme provides financial and technical assistance for technology upgradation, skill development, and integration of smart manufacturing systems. It aims to strengthen the MSME sector’s readiness for future industrial trends and global value chains.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises with valid Udyam Registration Certificate (URC) are eligible to apply. The enterprise must be engaged in manufacturing or service activities and demonstrate a viable project plan for technology adoption under Industry 4.0. Priority may be given to enterprises in aspirational districts, SC/ST/women-led units, and those showing potential for scalability and employment generation.
benefits: Financial subsidy for technology acquisition and implementation, technical guidance for digital transformation, access to expert consultation and training programs, support for pilot projects and proof-of-concept development, assistance in integrating IoT, AI, and automation systems, and facilitation of market linkages through technology-enabled platforms.
financial_support: The scheme provides a capital subsidy of up to 50% of the project cost for eligible technology adoption initiatives, with a maximum ceiling of INR 25 lakhs per enterprise. The remaining 50% of the project cost is to be borne by the beneficiary. Funds are disbursed in installments based on project milestones and verification of implementation.

Locate the MSME Industry 4.0 Adoption Scheme and click on 'Apply Now'. 3. Register on the portal using Udyam Registration Number and create a login profile. 4. Fill in the online application form with enterprise details, project proposal, and technology adoption plan. 5. Shortlisted applications will undergo technical evaluation by the empowered committee. 8. deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.

target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; academic institutions; government agencies; private sector enterprises

Provide supporting documents such as incorporation certificates, technical expertise proof, and past project details. 5. Await evaluation by the NCCC technical committee. 6. overview: The National Data and Analytics Platform (NDAP) is an initiative by NITI Aayog to facilitate and improve access to Indian government data. It allows users to search, merge, visualize, and download datasets from across India's administrative landscape. The platform hosts datasets from various sectors and ministries, enabling data-driven decision-making and research.
target_beneficiaries: researchers; policy makers; academics; journalists; developers; civil society
eligibility: The platform is accessible to all users without restriction; no specific eligibility criteria are mentioned for accessing NDAP.
benefits: Users can access thousands of government datasets, search and filter data, merge multiple datasets, visualize key indicators and trends, and download data for analysis. The platform supports data accessibility for people with disabilities through WCAG 2.0 AA compliance.
financial_support: No financial support is provided under NDAP as it is a data access platform, not a funding scheme.
application_process: 1. Visit the NDAP website at https://ndap.niti.gov.in 2. Use the search function to find datasets by sector, ministry, or keyword 3. Apply filters such as time period, frequency, and granularity 4. Preview dataset details including columns and last updated date 5. Merge multiple datasets if needed 6. Visualize data using built-in tools 7. Download datasets in usable formats
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. The platform is accessible year-round.
implementing_agency: NITI Aayog

scheme_name: MeitY AI CoE – Farming, Healthcare & Smart Cities
overview: The MeitY AI CoE – Farming, Healthcare & Smart Cities is part of the IndiaAI Mission, which aims to build a comprehensive AI ecosystem by democratizing computing access, enhancing data quality, developing indigenous AI capabilities, attracting top AI talent, enabling industry collaboration, providing startup risk capital, ensuring socially impactful AI projects, and promoting ethical AI. The initiative focuses on establishing Centers of Excellence in AI for key sectors including farming, healthcare, and smart cities to drive innovation and socio-economic transformation.
target_beneficiaries: startups; researchers; academic institutions; MSME; agri-startups
eligibility: Eligible organizations include academic & research institutions, startups and companies, and non-profit and civil society organizations that demonstrate relevant expertise, data capabilities, and domain competence. Only institutional entities are eligible to contribute datasets or AI artefacts to the AIKosh platform; individual submissions are not permitted.
benefits: Improved dataset quality through community engagement and collaborative data cleaning; versioning features enabling continuous refinement of datasets and models; wider adoption and impact as hosted datasets can be utilized by public and private sectors to build real-world AI applications; ease of AI development via user-friendly tools that simplify dataset integration into AI models; community engagement and recognition through challenges and hackathons on contributed datasets, attracting top talent for innovative solutions.
financial_support: The IndiaAI Mission provides startup risk capital through streamlined access to funding for innovative AI projects under the IndiaAI Startup Financing pillar. However, specific financial support details for the MeitY AI CoE – Farming, Healthcare & Smart Cities are not explicitly mentioned in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Register on the AIKosh platform using the designated onboarding process for private entities. 2. Designate at least one authorized representative (Administrative SPOC) responsible for managing submissions. 3. Ensure compliance with DPDPA, NDSAP, and other applicable Indian data sharing, privacy, and security laws. 4. Comply with AIKosh Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. 5. Submit complete and accurate metadata, specify licensing terms, and adhere to data governance policies. 6. Upload non-personal, India-specific datasets or AI artefacts (models and use cases) ensuring metadata completeness and compliance with platform guidelines. 7. Submit datasets undergo backend validation for quality and compliance before final approval and publication. 8. For support, contact official support at support@indiaai.gov.in.
deadlines: Rolling basis — submissions are accepted on a rolling basis with periodic reviews for compliance.
implementing_agency: IndiaAI, an Independent Business Division (IBD) under the Digital India Corporation, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

scheme_name: AI for Agriculture – ICAR-ICRISAT Partnership Grant
overview: The AI for Agriculture – ICAR-ICRISAT Partnership Grant is a collaborative initiative between the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT) aimed at leveraging artificial intelligence and data analytics to enhance agricultural productivity, sustainability, and farmer livelihoods. The scheme supports research and innovation in AI-driven solutions for crop improvement, precision farming, and climate-resilient agriculture, particularly focusing on semi-arid regions. It seeks to bridge the gap between advanced AI technologies and on-ground agricultural challenges through joint research projects, capacity building, and technology transfer.
target_beneficiaries: researchers; scientists; agri-startups; farmers; ICAR institutes; ICRISAT scientists
eligibility: Eligible applicants include scientists and researchers from ICAR institutes, ICRISAT, State Agricultural Universities, and recognized agri-tech startups working on AI-driven agricultural solutions. Preference is given to projects focusing on semi-arid tropics, smallholder farmers, and scalable technologies with clear pathways for field validation and adoption.
benefits: Financial support for research and development, access to ICAR and ICRISAT research facilities and datasets, technical mentorship from domain experts, opportunities for field trials and pilot testing, potential for technology scaling and commercialization, joint publication and intellectual property rights as per agreement, and networking with national and international agricultural research communities.
financial_support: The grant provides financial support for research projects, including funding for personnel, equipment, data acquisition, software tools, and field validation activities. The exact quantum and disbursement mechanism are determined based on project scope and mutual agreement between ICAR and ICRISAT, with funds released in tranches upon milestone achievement.
application_process: 1. Identify a collaborative research problem aligned with AI in agriculture and semi-arid tropics. 2. Develop a joint project proposal between ICAR and ICRISAT scientists or affiliated institutions. 3. Submit the proposal through the designated ICAR-ICRISAT coordination cell. 4. Proposal undergoes technical review by a joint expert committee. 5. Shortlisted proposals are presented for final approval. 6. Upon approval, a memorandum of understanding (MoU) is signed. 7. Funds are released in installments based on project milestones. 8. Progress is monitored through quarterly reports and annual reviews.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year subject to review cycles.
implementing_agency: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
contact_details: Email: dkma@icar.org.in | Phone: +91-11-25843600 (Directorate of Knowledge Management in Agriculture, ICAR)

overview: The LIFE Programme (Lifestyle for Environment) is a national initiative launched by the Government of India to promote sustainable living and environmental conservation through individual and community actions. It encourages citizens to adopt eco-friendly lifestyles by making simple, mindful choices in daily life that collectively contribute to climate change mitigation and environmental protection. The programme aims to create a mass movement for environmental stewardship by leveraging behavioural change and public participation across diverse sectors of society.
target_beneficiaries: general public; students; communities; institutions
eligibility: The LIFE Programme is open to all Indian citizens, institutions, schools, colleges, NGOs, and community groups who wish to participate in promoting sustainable living practices. There are no specific eligibility restrictions based on age, income, or background; participation is voluntary and based on commitment to environmental stewardship.
benefits: Participants gain awareness about sustainable practices, contribute to national environmental goals, receive recognition for eco-friendly actions, and help build a culture of environmental responsibility. The programme fosters behavioural change that leads to long-term ecological benefits, including reduced pollution, conservation of natural resources, and improved public health outcomes.
financial_support: The LIFE Programme primarily focuses on awareness, behavioural change, and voluntary action rather than direct financial support to individuals or entities. Financial assistance, if any, is channelled through partner organisations or government schemes aligned with LIFE objectives, but the programme itself does not provide grants, loans, or subsidies to beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Visit the official LIFE Programme website at https://www.missionlife-india.com 2. Explore the themes and suggested actions under the LIFE initiative 3. Adopt sustainable practices in daily life such as saving energy, reducing waste, using public transport, and conserving water 4. Share your actions on social media using the hashtag #MissionLife 5. Encourage others in your community to join the movement 6. Participate in organised events, campaigns, or challenges launched under the programme
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Participation is encouraged continuously throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India

overview: The ResponsibleAI Startup Grants (NASSCOM & MeitY) is a scheme aimed at supporting startups in the AI & Data sector, particularly focusing on responsible AI development. It is part of NASSCOM's initiatives to foster innovation and responsible AI adoption in India, often in collaboration with government bodies like MeitY. The scheme provides financial and non-financial support to eligible startups working on responsible AI solutions.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups must be focused on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), have a Minimum Viable Product (MVP), demonstrate market traction with at least one paying client or three paid Proof of Concepts (POCs), be less than 10 years old since incorporation, and be legally incorporated in India.
benefits: Selected startups receive Free HPAIC Access (A100: 6-months or 1000 GPU hours), Domain Expertise & Research Know-How, Access to Data & Platforms, Fundraising Readiness Program, Curated Investor Connect, Support to build Responsible AI-Compliant Solutions, Technology Mentoring, Bootcamps on GTM Strategy and Growth Strategy, Collaborations & Partnerships, Global Access, and Office Hours.
financial_support: The scheme provides non-financial support such as free high-performance AI computing access, mentorship, and investor connect. No direct monetary grant amount is specified in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Check eligibility criteria focusing on GenAI focus, MVP, client engagement, company age, and Indian incorporation. 2. Prepare documentation including proof of MVP, client engagement details, incorporation certificate, and team information. 3. Apply through the official NASSCOM GenAI Foundry portal or designated application channel. 4. Submit application for review by the selection panel. 5. Await intimation of selection and subsequent contracting if selected.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: NASSCOM in collaboration with MeitY (Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology)

overview: The India AI Startup Fellowship Programme is part of the IndiaAI Mission's Startup Financing pillar, which supports and accelerates deep-tech AI startups by providing streamlined access to funding for innovative AI projects. target_beneficiaries: startups

benefits: Streamlined access to funding for innovative AI projects, support for deep-tech AI startups, contribution to AIKosh platform as a central repository for AI innovation and research in India, visibility and recognition through the IndiaAI portal, access to datasets, models, AI sandbox and more via AIKosh Platform, opportunities to participate in AI initiatives and events, collaboration with government and industry stakeholders.
financial_support: The IndiaAI Mission provides startup risk capital as part of its seven pillars, though specific quantum, type, and mechanism of financial support for the Startup Fellowship Programme are not detailed in the evidence.

Register on AIKosh platform using the designated onboarding process for private entities including startups, companies, MSMEs, academic institutions, research organizations, thinktanks, non-profits, etc. 2. Ensure valid and verifiable legal status (Registered Society, Corporate Body, Statutory Body, Registered Company, etc.). 3. Designate at least one authorized representative (Administrative SPOC) responsible for managing dataset submissions, metadata maintenance, and contributor management on AIKosh. 4. Ensure data or dataset shared with AIKosh complies with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), National Data Sharing and Accessibility Policy (NDSAP), and all other applicable laws, regulations, and policies of the Government of India governing data sharing, privacy, and security. 5. Ensure compliance with AIKosh Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. 6. Include complete and accurate metadata, specify licensing terms, and adhere to applicable data governance policies. 7. implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

overview: The National Mission for Himalayan Studies (NMHS) is a central sector scheme aimed at supporting research, knowledge generation, and capacity building in the Indian Himalayan Region (IHR). It focuses on sustainable development, climate change adaptation, biodiversity conservation, and livelihood improvement in the Himalayan states. The mission promotes interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary research to address region-specific challenges through scientific and traditional knowledge systems.
target_beneficiaries: researchers; academic institutions; NGOs; state government departments; local communities
eligibility: Eligible applicants include universities, colleges, research institutions, NGOs, state government departments, and individuals working in the Indian Himalayan Region. Proposals must align with the thematic priority areas of NMHS and demonstrate relevance to sustainable development, climate resilience, biodiversity conservation, or livelihood improvement in the IHR.
benefits: Financial support for research projects, fellowships, and capacity-building programs; access to research networks and collaborative platforms; opportunities for knowledge dissemination and policy engagement; support for fieldwork, data collection, and publication; integration of traditional knowledge with scientific research.
financial_support: NMHS provides financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid for research projects, fellowships, and thematic programs. The quantum of support varies based on the scope and duration of the project, with funding typically covering personnel, equipment, travel, consumables, and overheads. Grants are disbursed in installments based on project milestones and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Identify a research theme aligned with NMHS priority areas. 2. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, methodology, budget, and expected outcomes. 3. Submit the proposal through the designated nodal officer or online portal as specified in the annual call. 4. Proposals undergo peer review and evaluation by expert committees. 5. Selected projects are sanctioned and funds are released upon submission of required documents. 6. Implement the project and submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates.
deadlines: Based on annual call for proposals; specific dates vary each year
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)

overview: The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) Grants are part of a national mechanism established under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 to manage funds collected for compensatory afforestation in lieu of forest land diverted for non-forest purposes. The scheme aims to promote afforestation and regeneration activities as a way of compensating for forest land diversion. Funds are utilized by State/UT CAMPAs for plantation, conservation, protection and management of forests and wildlife.
target_beneficiaries: State Governments; Union Territory Administrations; State/UT CAMPAs
eligibility: State Governments and Union Territory Administrations are eligible to receive funds from the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund under the CAMPA scheme. The funds are released to State/UT CAMPAs based on approved Annual Plans of Operations (APOs) for undertaking afforestation and conservation activities.
benefits: Financial support for afforestation, reforestation, forest conservation, protection and management activities. Includes support for plantation, assisted natural regeneration, pest and disease control, forest fire prevention, soil and moisture conservation, wildlife habitat improvement, protected area management, capacity building, monitoring and evaluation, and forest-related infrastructure development.
financial_support: Funds are released from the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund (NCAF) to State/UT CAMPAs based on their approved Annual Plans of Operations (APOs). The quantum of support depends on the funds collected from user agencies for compensatory afforestation and the approved APOs. There is no fixed per-entity grant amount; support is project-based and subject to availability of funds in the NCAF.
application_process: 1. State/UT CAMPAs prepare Annual Plans of Operations (APOs) detailing proposed afforestation and conservation activities. 2. APOs are submitted to the National Authority, CAMPA for approval. 3. Upon approval, funds are released from the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund (NCAF) to the respective State/UT CAMPAs. 4. State/UT CAMPAs implement the approved activities and submit utilization certificates and progress reports. 5. The National Authority monitors utilization and may conduct audits.
deadlines: Annual Plans of Operations (APOs) are typically submitted yearly for approval, with funds released upon sanction. Specific dates vary by state and are not fixed nationally.
implementing_agency: National Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (National Authority, CAMPA), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

scheme_name: AI & ML Research Grant – DST SERB

Foreign nationals (including OCI and NRI) are also eligible to apply provided they fulfil the eligibility criteria notified. The applicant(s) must hold a Ph.D. degree in Sciences, Mathematics and Engineering. Applicants with Master’s Degree in medicine, surgery, or dental sciences (M.D. / M.S. / M.D.S. / M.V.Sc.) can apply two years after obtaining degree. Under Quantitative Social Sciences area, PI and Co-Investigator(s) should hold Ph.D. degree in Science, Mathematics, Engineering, M.D. / M.S. / M.D.S. / M.V.Sc. degree or Ph.D degree in any Social Sciences area. The applicant(s) (PIs and Co-PIs) must hold a regular position in a recognized academic institution or National Research Laboratory or in any other recognized research organization in India. A research professor or Professor of Practice may be a Co-PI. Private Academic institutions with valid UGC / AICTE / PCI approval, Private R&D Institutions with valid DSIR-SIRO recognition and Voluntary and Non-Governmental Organizations registered under NITI-AAYOG Darpan portal are eligible to host a project. NGOs must have a valid DARPAN portal registration, and DSIR SIRO recognition to receive direct grant-in-aid under the program. The term 'Regular' in the context of ARG refers to applicants who are appointed against a sanctioned post or on a tenure-track post of an Institute/University, and are likely to be renewed after the end of the tenure. Research Associates, Post-doctoral fellows, Ad-hoc faculties, Guest Faculties, Visiting Scientists, Consultants, Project Fellows, Faculty members/researchers whose contract is renewed every year are not eligible to apply. INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship, Ramanujan Fellowship, and Ramalingaswamy Fellowship holders are also eligible to apply as PI or Co-PI subject to fulfilling the service criteria as indicated below. Service Duration: In general, PI should have at least 'the duration of the proposed project plus one year' of official service remaining at the time of submission of proposals (for purposes of computation, the last date for submission of proposals will be taken). PI who will be superannuating during the duration of the project or already superannuated are also eligible to apply. In such cases, a Faculty/Scientist from the host institute who has at least the duration of the proposed project plus one year of official service remaining should be associated as a Co-PI. Under no condition will ANRF projects be allowed to continue with a PI or Co-PI aged 70. Such individual’s host institution should ensure the transfer of PI responsibilities to Co-PI. Investigators can hold a maximum of two ANRF (or erstwhile SERB) projects at any point of time. In one project, they may be a PI and in another Co-PI; or, they could be Co-PIs in two projects. If an individual has hit or crossed this limit, they may not apply in this cycle of ARG. This limitation, however, does not apply to PIs involved in IRG/EMEQ schemes or PIs / Co-PIs in mission-mode programs (ANRF MAHA, ATRI, PAIR programs or other similar Mission programs of ANRF). Investigators become eligible to apply for another project within six months from the date of completion of the ongoing project. Application for another project more than six months prior to the completion will not be considered. In respect of cases that are not mentioned above, ANRF reserves the right to determine eligibility.
benefits: Funding support for projects for a maximum period of five years. For a project beyond three-year duration, support beyond the initial three-year period will be provided in a phased manner (i.e. 3+1 for 4 years and 3+1+1 for five years), contingent upon demonstrated research progress, impact and outcomes, in addition to publications and patents. ANRF will introduce an impact assessment scorecard with a real time dashboard per project and expect regular project updates post award. All data generated from project must be shared in appropriate depositories and managed. All publication pre-prints funded by the project must be shared in the public domain. Budget: The upper limit for project funding under the ARG Program is ₹ 5 Crores. The research grant will be provided under two budget heads: Recurring [Research personnel, Consumables, Travel, Field Work Costs, Contingencies, other costs (to cover Cloud Compute Credits, Software Licenses, Publication Costs, Analytical / Facility Access charges) and Overheads] Non-Recurring (Equipment, Software Purchased, Long-term purchase of cloud or remote facility access). No reallocation of funds will be permissible from Non-recurring to Recurring heads or vice-versa. Operational flexibility is provided to utilize funds under Recurring head (i.e. all sub-heads of Recurring) subject to the following conditions: Research Personnel: Operational flexibility is provided for engaging research personnel in the project. The norms for emoluments, and general terms and conditions of research personnel engaged in the project will be as per ANRF norms, informed through Office Memoranda viz., ANRF/OM/N/01/2024 and SB/S9/Z-06/2019 and updated from time to time. All personnel, including Research Personnel engaged under the project, for the full/part duration of the project, are to be treated as temporary employees and governed by administrative rules/service conditions (for leave, TA/DA etc.) of the host institute. They shall not to be treated as employees of the ANRF or Government of India nor permanent employees of the host institute. Travel: Budget of up to Rs. 5 Lakhs will be provided for a project to undertake travel related to the project. International travel for project-related work is also permitted within this travel head. Contingency: Contingency funds of up to Rs. 5 Lakhs will be provided for a project. They can also be utilized for registration charges for international conferences. The PI shall ensure that the total funds sanctioned under the recurring head is not exceeded in any case. Publication and patent filing charges: Expenditure towards open access publications in top journals of any discipline is permitted, as long as they are publications resulting from this project. Funds under the recurring head can also be utilized for patent filing charges. Equipment: The change of approved or sanctioned equipment is generally not permitted and may only be considered on a case-by-case basis, provided it is within the sanctioned budget for equipment/s. The PI must obtain prior approval from ANRF to change the approved or sanctioned equipment. [Refer ANRF OM ANRF/OM/N-01/2024 for details on overheads, travel and contingency. Optionally, PIs are encouraged to invite cost-sharing from industry or international partners. An LoI from industry or international partner can be added in full proposal stage. Industry, institutional or international co-funding is NOT mandatory, but is encouraged, and should be declared. Emerging academic research institutions are defined as any State University OR lower NIRF ranked research active public or private academic institution, i.e. those institutions having > 50 NIRF overall ranking. Note: National Research Laboratories, R&D Organizations and Deemed Universities under any Ministries/Departments except Department of Higher Education are not considered as emerging academic research institutions.

application_process: 1. Visit the website 'www.anrfonline.in' for the Call for Proposals (CFP) notification. 2. Ensure eligibility as per criteria including Ph.D. in Sciences/Mathematics/Engineering or equivalent, regular position in recognized institution, and service duration requirements. 3. Prepare a pre-proposal in the prescribed format and submit it through 'www.anrfonline.in' by the deadline. 4. If shortlisted, submit a full proposal via the same portal. 5. overview: The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is a dedicated source of climate finance aimed at limiting or reducing greenhouse gas emissions and supporting climate change adaptation in developing countries. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) has been designated as India's National Designated Authority (NDA) for the GCF, with its Climate Change Division serving as the focal point. The GCF Toolkit has been developed by India's NDA to guide national stakeholders in engaging with the fund, covering policies, governance, stakeholder roles, accreditation processes, and proposal development support.
target_beneficiaries: government entities; accredited entities; national stakeholders
eligibility: The Green Climate Fund Toolkit does not specify eligibility criteria for beneficiaries, as it is a guidance document intended for National Designated Authorities and national stakeholders to understand and engage with the GCF. Eligibility for GCF funding is determined by the GCF Board based on project proposals submitted by Accredited Entities.
benefits: The toolkit provides comprehensive guidance on engaging with the Green Climate Fund, including understanding GCF investment criteria, navigating the accreditation process for Direct Access Entities, developing funding proposals, accessing readiness and preparatory support, and aligning projects with national climate change policies and GCF priorities. It supports national stakeholders in effectively accessing GCF resources for climate action.
financial_support: The Green Climate Fund Toolkit itself does not provide financial support. It is a guidance document that assists stakeholders in accessing financial support from the Green Climate Fund, which provides grants, concessional loans, guarantees, and equity investments for climate mitigation and adaptation projects in developing countries.
application_process: The Green Climate Fund Toolkit does not outline an application process for the scheme itself, as it is a guidance resource. For accessing GCF funds, the process involves: 1. Identifying a project aligned with national climate priorities and GCF investment criteria; 2. Engaging with the National Designated Authority (MoEFCC Climate Change Division) for no-objection and support; 3. Applying through an Accredited Entity (international or national) or seeking accreditation as a Direct Access Entity; 4. Developing a funding proposal with support from the GCF's readiness and preparatory programs; 5. Submitting the proposal to the GCF Secretariat for review and approval by the GCF Board.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications to the Green Climate Fund are accepted throughout the year via Accredited Entities.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)

scheme_name: National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC)
overview: The National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC) is a central sector scheme established to support concrete adaptation activities that mitigate the adverse effects of climate change. It provides financial assistance to state governments and union territories for implementing climate change adaptation projects in sectors such as agriculture, water, forestry, and disaster management. The fund aims to enhance resilience and reduce vulnerability to climate change impacts across India.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; union territories
eligibility: State governments and union territories are eligible to apply for financial assistance under NAFCC for implementing climate change adaptation projects. Projects must be aligned with the State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC) and focus on sectors vulnerable to climate change impacts.
benefits: Financial support for project implementation, technical guidance, monitoring and evaluation, and capacity building for climate change adaptation initiatives.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-based financial support to state governments and union territories for implementing agencies adaptation activities under NAFCC is ₹364 crore for the period 2015-16 to 2019-20, with funds released in installments based on project progress and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. State governments/UTs prepare project proposals aligned with SAPCC 2. Submit proposals to MoEF&CC for appraisal 3. Obtain approval from the Steering Committee on Climate Change 4. Sign Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with MoEF&CC 5. Implement project activities 6. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates 7. Receive subsequent installments based on satisfactory progress
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and appraisal cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC)

scheme_name: Special Accelerated Road Development Programme for NE (SARDP-NE)
overview: The Special Accelerated Road Development Programme for NE (SARDP-NE) is a government initiative aimed at accelerating road infrastructure development in the North Eastern region of India. It focuses on improving connectivity, enhancing road networks, and supporting socio-economic development in the region through targeted investments in highways and bridges. The programme is implemented by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and involves upgrading existing roads, constructing new links, and improving infrastructure to integrate the North East with the rest of the country.
target_beneficiaries: residents of North Eastern States; state governments of NE region; commuters and transporters
eligibility: Projects under SARDP-NE are sanctioned for implementation in the North Eastern States including Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura. Eligibility is based on project proposals submitted by the respective state governments or central agencies like NHIDCL, subject to technical feasibility, alignment with national highway network, availability of funds.
benefits: Improved road connectivity leading to better access to markets, healthcare, and education; reduced vehicle operating costs and travel time; enhanced safety due to better road design and maintenance; boost to local economies through increased trade and tourism; creation of employment during construction and maintenance; strengthened disaster resilience and emergency response capabilities.
financial_support: Financial support under SARDP-NE is provided as central grants to state governments and central agencies like NHIDCL for the development and upgradation of national highways, state roads, and bridges in the North Eastern region. The funding pattern typically involves 90% central grant and 10% state share for most NE states, with 100% central funding for certain special category states or specific components. Funds are released in phases based on project milestones and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. State governments or implementing agencies prepare Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for road projects in the NE region. 2. DPRs are submitted to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) for appraisal. 3. MoRTH evaluates the proposals based on technical feasibility, alignment with SARDP-NE objectives, and cost-effectiveness. 4. Approved projects are sanctioned with financial and technical approvals. 5. Funds are released in installments based on progress and submission of utilization certificates. 6. Projects are monitored through regular site visits and progress reviews by MoRTH and regional offices.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year subject to fund availability and appraisal cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)

overview: The National Wetlands Conservation Programme (NWCP) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) to conserve and manage wetlands across India. It aims to prevent further degradation of wetlands, promote their wise use, and support biodiversity conservation and livelihood security of dependent communities. The programme provides financial assistance to state governments and implementing agencies for wetland conservation activities, including survey, demarcation, fencing, desilting, catchment area treatment, and community participation initiatives.
target_beneficiaries: state governments; implementing agencies; local communities; NGOs
eligibility: State governments, union territory administrations, and their designated implementing agencies (such as Forest Departments, Pollution Control Boards, and other relevant departments) are eligible to apply for financial assistance under the NWCP. Non-governmental organizations (NGOs), research institutions, and community-based organizations may also be considered as implementing partners in collaboration with state agencies.
benefits: Financial support for wetland conservation activities including survey and demarcation, fencing, desilting, catchment area treatment, biodiversity conservation, community participation, awareness generation, and institutional strengthening. The scheme also supports livelihood improvement initiatives for wetland-dependent communities and promotes wise use of wetland resources.
financial_support: The NWCP provides central financial assistance to state governments and implementing agencies on a cost-sharing basis. The central government typically bears 70% of the project cost for general category states and 90% for special category states (North-Eastern and Himalayan states), with the remaining share borne by the state government. Funds are released in installments based on project progress and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. State government or implementing agency identifies a wetland for conservation and prepares a detailed project report (DPR). 2. The DPR is submitted to the concerned Regional Office of MoEFCC or the Wetlands Division in New Delhi. 3. The proposal is reviewed by the Wetlands Division and, if found suitable, forwarded for approval. 4. Upon approval, a sanction order is issued specifying the quantum of central assistance. 5. Funds are released in installments against submission of utilization certificates and progress reports. 6. The implementing agency undertakes the conservation activities as per the approved plan. 7. Monitoring and evaluation are conducted by MoEFCC through field visits and reports.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and approval cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)

overview: The Bamboo Mission for North East is a centrally sponsored scheme under the National Bamboo Mission aimed at promoting holistic growth of the bamboo sector in the North Eastern Region. It focuses on increasing the area under bamboo cultivation, improving post-harvest management, and developing value-added bamboo products. The mission supports farmers, artisans, entrepreneurs, and self-help groups through training, infrastructure development, and market linkages. It aims to enhance income and livelihood opportunities in the region by leveraging bamboo as a sustainable resource.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; artisans; entrepreneurs; self-help groups; MSME
eligibility: Individual farmers, farmer producer organizations (FPOs), self-help groups (SHGs), non-governmental organizations (NGOs), cooperatives, and entrepreneurs engaged in bamboo cultivation, processing, or value addition in the North Eastern States are eligible to avail benefits under the scheme. Priority is given to small and marginal farmers, women, and SC/ST communities.
benefits: Financial assistance for bamboo plantation, establishment of nurseries, and tissue culture units. Subsidy for setting up primary processing and value addition units. Support for creation of bamboo bazaars, retail outlets, and export promotion. Training and capacity building programs on bamboo cultivation, treatment, and craftsmanship. Assistance for research and development in bamboo technology. Market development support including participation in trade fairs and buyer-seller meets.
financial_support: The scheme provides back-ended subsidies ranging from 50% to 100% of the project cost depending on the component and beneficiary category. For plantation, farmers receive assistance up to INR 24,000 per hectare over three years. For primary processing units, subsidy is up to 50% of the cost, limited to INR 25 lakhs. For value addition units, subsidy extends up to 50% of the cost with a ceiling of INR 50 lakhs. Assistance is released in installments upon verification of progress and utilization of previous installments.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant component under the Bamboo Mission (e.g., plantation, processing, value addition). 2. Prepare a detailed project report including cost estimates, land details, and implementation timeline. 3. Submit the application along with required documents to the State Bamboo Mission Office or designated nodal agency. 4. Application undergoes technical and financial appraisal by the State Level Committee. 5. Upon approval, receive administrative sanction and proceed with implementation. 6. Submit utilization certificates and progress reports for release of subsequent installments of subsidy.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Mission Directorate of National Bamboo Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

scheme_name: PM Van Mitra Scheme – Urban Forestry
overview: The PM Van Mitra Scheme – Urban Forestry is a government initiative under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change aimed at promoting urban forestry and green cover in cities. It focuses on increasing tree plantation in urban areas to combat pollution, enhance biodiversity, and improve the quality of life for urban residents. The scheme encourages community participation, including citizens, NGOs, and local bodies, in developing and maintaining urban forests. It aligns with national goals of environmental sustainability and climate resilience.
target_beneficiaries: citizens; NGOs; local bodies; urban communities
eligibility: The scheme is open to citizens, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), resident welfare associations, municipal corporations, urban local bodies, and other community groups interested in undertaking urban forestry projects. Applicants must propose viable tree plantation and maintenance plans in urban areas, with preference given to projects involving native species and community engagement.
benefits: Financial assistance for tree plantation and maintenance, technical guidance on species selection and plantation techniques, recognition for outstanding contributions to urban greening, capacity building through training and workshops, and support for long-term sustainability of urban green spaces.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support in the form of subsidies for tree plantation, including costs for saplings, planting materials, and maintenance for a specified period. The exact quantum and mechanism of support are determined based on project proposals and availability of funds under the scheme.
application_process: 1. Identify a suitable urban area for tree plantation. 2. Prepare a project proposal detailing the plantation plan, species selection, maintenance strategy, and community involvement. 3. Submit the proposal to the designated nodal officer or through the official portal of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. 4. Await review and approval by the concerned authorities. 5. Upon approval, receive financial and technical support to implement the project. 6. Execute the plantation and maintenance activities as per the approved plan. 7. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year subject to fund availability.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

overview: The Holistic Development of Islands (Andaman & Lakshadweep) scheme aims to promote sustainable and inclusive development in the islands of Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep through infrastructure development, livelihood generation, tourism promotion, and environmental conservation. It focuses on improving basic amenities, enhancing economic opportunities, and preserving the unique ecological and cultural heritage of the islands.
target_beneficiaries: local communities; fishermen; artisans; tourism units; MSMEs
eligibility: Beneficiaries include local residents, self-help groups, cooperatives, NGOs, and private enterprises operating in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep, subject to project viability and alignment with scheme guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance for infrastructure projects, livelihood support through skill training and market linkages, promotion of eco-friendly tourism, conservation of natural resources, improved access to basic services, and capacity building for local institutions.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support in the form of grants and subsidies for approved projects, with funding patterns varying by component and implementing agency, subject to budgetary allocations and utilization norms.
application_process: 1. Identify project proposal aligned with scheme objectives 2. Prepare detailed project report (DPR) 3. Submit application to the nodal department or implementing agency 4. Undergo technical and financial appraisal 5. Obtain approval from the competent authority 6. Execute project upon fund release 7. Submit utilization certificates and progress reports.
implementing_agency: NITI Aayog Aayog in coordination with the Ministry of Home Affairs and respective Union Territory administrations

scheme_name: Schemes under Ministry of DoNER (North East)
overview: The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) implements various schemes for the socio-economic development of the North Eastern Region of India. These include infrastructure development, livelihood generation, and bridging sectoral gaps through initiatives like PM-DevINE, NESIDS, and Special Development Packages. The Ministry coordinates with central ministries, state governments, and implementing agencies to ensure effective execution of development projects.
target_beneficiaries: North Eastern States; State Governments; Implementing Agencies; NGOs; Citizens of North-Eastern Region
geographic_scope: North Eastern Region (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura)
eligibility: State Governments of the eight North-Eastern States, Implementing Agencies/NGOs working on MDoNER-supported programmes, and Central Ministries/Departments are eligible to submit proposals under various schemes such as NESIDS, PM-DevINE, Special Development Packages, and Schemes of NEC. Proposals must be submitted in prescribed format with all supporting documents and clearances through the Purvottar Vikas Setu Portal.
benefits: Financial support for infrastructure projects, livelihood generation, and social development; technical assistance and capacity building; monitoring and evaluation mechanisms; grievance redressal; timely disbursement of funds; and support for project formulation and implementation through guidelines and portal-based submission.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets and general grants-in-aid to State Governments and implementing agencies. Funds are released after approval by the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) or Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region, following submission of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) and concept notes. Disbursement is linked to utilization certificates and progress reports as per scheme guidelines.
application_process: 1. Prepare complete proposal in prescribed format with required documents as per scheme guidelines (NESIDS, PM-DevINE, Special Development Packages, or Schemes of NEC). 2. Submit the proposal by the State Government through the Purvottar Vikas Setu Portal. 3. Undergo preliminary examination and circulation for comments (15 days). 4. Receive comments on Concept Note from Line Ministries/NITI Aayog (15 days). 5. Receive comments on Detailed Project Report (DPR) from Line Ministries/NITI Aayog (30 days). 6. Submit proposal for Expenditure Finance Committee (EIMC) consideration after inter-ministerial consultation (30 days). 7. Receive Minutes of EIMC meeting after conduct (15 days). 8. Obtain Administrative Approval and Financial Sanction (AFS) after all approvals and clearances (15 days). 9. Proceed with implementation by the implementing agency or State Government.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year as per scheme guidelines and availability of funds.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region
contact_details: Email: secydoner@nic.in | Phone: 011-21411140 | Address: Jodhpur Officers Hostel, Pandara Road, New Delhi-110003

scheme_name: North East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme (NESIDS)
overview: The North East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme (NESIDS), launched in 2017, provides full central funding to North Eastern States for vital infrastructure in water, power, connectivity, tourism, education, and health. Roads projects are handled by the North Eastern Council (NEC), while other infrastructure falls under the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER). The scheme aims to accelerate socio-economic development in the North Eastern Region by addressing critical infrastructure gaps.
target_beneficiaries: North Eastern States
eligibility: North Eastern States are eligible for funding under NESIDS for infrastructure projects in water, power, connectivity, tourism, education, and health sectors. Roads projects are implemented by NEC, while other infrastructure projects are implemented by MDoNER.
benefits: Full central funding for infrastructure projects, implementation support through NEC for roads and MDoNER for other infrastructure, focus on vital sectors including water, power, connectivity, tourism, education, and health, and contribution to socio-economic development and growth parity with the rest of India.
financial_support: NESIDS offers full central funding (100% Government of India funding) for approved infrastructure projects in the North Eastern States. The financial support is provided as grants for creation of capital assets, with specific budget allocations detailed in the Detailed Demands for Grants documents.
application_process: The evidence does not provide a specific step-by-step application process for NESIDS. Proposals are likely submitted through state governments to the respective implementing agencies (NEC for roads, MDoNER for other infrastructure) as part of the annual budget planning process.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) and North Eastern Council (NEC)

overview: The North East Rural Livelihood Project (NERLP) is a World Bank-assisted initiative aimed at improving rural livelihoods in the North Eastern states of India. It focuses on empowering rural poor, especially women, through the promotion of self-help groups (SHGs), capacity building, and access to microfinance and livelihood opportunities. The project operates in Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura, supporting sustainable economic development through community-driven interventions.
target_beneficiaries: rural poor; women; self-help groups (SHGs); marginalized communities
eligibility: The project targets rural poor households, particularly women, in the participating North Eastern states. Beneficiaries are identified through participatory rural appraisal and are typically members of self-help groups (SHGs) or community-based organizations. Priority is given to marginalized groups including Scheduled Tribes, Scheduled Castes, and economically weaker sections.
benefits: Beneficiaries receive capacity building and training, access to microcredit through SHGs, support for livelihood activities such as agriculture, horticulture, livestock, and non-farm enterprises, infrastructure support like rural roads and market sheds, and social empowerment initiatives. The project also facilitates convergence with other government schemes and provides technical assistance for sustainable resource management.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through a community-driven development approach where self-help groups (SHGs) access revolving funds and microcredit from project-supported financial intermediaries. The project promotes savings and internal lending within SHGs, and facilitates bank linkage for larger loans. Grants are also provided for community infrastructure and skill training, while livelihood investments are often made through matching grants or subsidized loans.
application_process: 1. Community mobilization and formation of self-help groups (SHGs) at the village level. 2. Training of SHG members in group management, bookkeeping, and livelihood planning. 3. Preparation of micro-investment plans (MIPs) by SHGs for livelihood activities. 4. Appraisal and approval of MIPs by village-level committees and project facilitators. 5. Disbursement of funds as revolving fund, grant, or loan based on the MIP. 6. Monitoring and support for implementation of livelihood activities. 7. Repayment and recycling of funds within the SHG system.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the project period based on community readiness and village-level planning cycles.
implementing_agency: North Eastern Council (NEC), Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER)

scheme_name: PM DevINE – PM Development Initiative for NE Region
overview: PM-DevINE, a Central Sector scheme launched in Union Budget 2022-23 with ₹6,600 crore outlay (2022-26), aims to accelerate sustainable development in the North-East through infrastructure, social projects, livelihood generation, and bridging sectoral gaps.
target_beneficiaries: North Eastern States; State Governments; Implementing agencies
eligibility: State Governments of the eight North-Eastern States submit complete and accurate project proposals in the prescribed formats with all supporting documents and clearances through the Purvottar Vikas Setu Portal.
benefits: Full central funding for approved projects, financial support for infrastructure and social development, livelihood generation, and bridging sectoral gaps in the North Eastern Region.
financial_support: The scheme provides grants for creation of capital assets and grants-in-aid-general to State Governments and implementing agencies for projects under PM-DevINE, with funds released after approval by the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) and issue of Administrative Approval and Financial Sanction (AFS).
application_process: 1. Submission of complete proposal in prescribed format with documents as per guidelines of PM-DevINE. 2. Projects are submitted by State Government through Purvottar Vikas Setu Portal. 3. State Government (SLEC) -> MDoNER -> Comments of Line Ministries/Departments - MDoNER(EIMC) -> AFS issue -> Implementation by Implementing agency/State Govt. 4. (i) Preliminary examination and circulation of the complete proposal for comments: 15 days. (ii) Comments on Concept Note from Line Ministries/ NITI Aayog: 15 days. (iii) Comments on DPR from Line Ministries/ NITI Aayog: 30 days. (iv) Submission of the proposal for EIMC consideration after completion of inter-ministerial consultation: 30 days. (v) Issue of Minutes of the EIMC meeting after conduct of the meeting: 15 days. (vi) Issue of AFS after all approvals and clearances are in place: 15 days.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region
contact_details: Shri S.D. Meena, Director, PM-DevINE, Tel: 011-21410599, Email: meena.sd@nic.in

scheme_name: Integrated Basin Development & Livelihoods Programme (IBDLP) – Meghalaya
overview: The Integrated Basin Development & Livelihoods Programme (IBDLP) – Meghalaya is a North East Special scheme aimed at holistic development of river basins in Meghalaya through sustainable livelihood generation, natural resource management, and infrastructure development. It focuses on integrating basin planning with community participation to enhance resilience and economic opportunities in rural areas. The programme targets watershed management, agro-forestry, eco-tourism, and skill development to uplift local communities. It is implemented under the Community & Rural Development Department of the Government of Meghalaya.
target_beneficiaries: rural communities; self-help groups; farmers; artisans; youth
eligibility: The scheme is open to rural communities, self-help groups, NGOs, and local institutions operating in the identified river basins of Meghalaya. Beneficiaries must be residents of Meghalaya and engaged in or willing to undertake livelihood activities aligned with basin development goals such as agriculture, horticulture, fisheries, handicrafts, or eco-tourism. Priority is given to marginalized groups including women, youth, and economically weaker sections.
benefits: Financial support for livelihood projects, technical guidance and training in sustainable practices, assistance in forming producer groups and cooperatives, infrastructure development support (e.g., check dams, irrigation channels), market access facilitation, and convergence with other government schemes for holistic development. Non-financial benefits include capacity building, exposure visits, and handholding for project implementation.
financial_support: The programme provides grant-based financial support to eligible beneficiaries for undertaking approved livelihood and natural resource management activities. Funds are disbursed through implementing agencies in a phased manner based on project milestones and utilization certificates. The quantum of support varies according to the nature and scale of the project, with a focus on cost-sharing and community contribution.
application_process: 1. Identify a viable livelihood or basin development project aligned with IBDLP objectives. 2. Form a self-help group or community organization if not already existing. 3. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 4. Submit the proposal to the concerned Block Development Officer or District Rural Development Agency. 5. Undergo technical and financial appraisal by the reviewing committee. 6. Upon approval, enter into an agreement with the implementing agency. 7. Begin project implementation after receiving the first installment of funds. 8. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates for subsequent fund releases. 9. Complete the project and submit final report for closure and impact assessment.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Community & Rural Development Department, Government of Meghalaya

overview: The Lakshadweep Development Corporation Limited (LDCL) is a key implementing agency under the Administration of Lakshadweep, responsible for executing development schemes and managing public utilities in the Union Territory. It functions as a government-owned corporation under the administrative control of the Lakshadweep Administration, with its Managing Director appointed from the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) cadre. LDCL oversees infrastructure, industrial, and socio-economic development initiatives across the islands, including fisheries, tourism, power, and cooperative sectors. The corporation operates under the guidance of the Secretary (Finance, Planning Statistics & Taxation) who also serves as its Chairman cum Managing Director.
target_beneficiaries: residents of Lakshadweep; local entrepreneurs; fishermen; cooperative societies; MSMEs
eligibility: Eligibility varies depending on the specific scheme implemented by LDCL; generally open to residents of Lakshadweep, registered cooperative societies, self-help groups, local entrepreneurs, and MSMEs engaged in permissible economic activities within the UT, subject to scheme-specific criteria such as project viability, local employment generation, and compliance with environmental and regulatory norms.
benefits: Benefits include access to financial support, technical guidance, infrastructure development, market linkages, subsidies on inputs, training and capacity building, and implementation of government welfare and livelihood schemes. LDCL also facilitates access to central and state government schemes, promotes entrepreneurship, and supports the development of key sectors like fisheries, tourism, and handicrafts through targeted interventions.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through various mechanisms including grants, loans, subsidies, and equity participation, depending on the scheme. LDCL implements centrally sponsored schemes and UT-specific programs, disbursing funds as per guidelines from the Ministry of Home Affairs, NITI Aayog, or other central agencies. The quantum and terms of support are scheme-specific and outlined in respective guidelines.
application_process: Application processes vary by scheme. Generally, applicants must submit proposals through the concerned department or LDCL office, accompanied by required documents such as project reports, identity proof, land documents (if applicable), bank details, and scheme-specific forms. Applications are reviewed by LDCL or the relevant administrative department for technical and financial feasibility before approval.
implementing_agency: Lakshadweep Development Corporation Limited (LDCL)

scheme_name: NITI Aayog Island Development Agency Scheme
overview: NITI Aayog serves as the apex public policy think tank of the Government of India, tasked with catalyzing economic development and fostering cooperative federalism through the involvement of State Governments in economic policymaking using a bottom-up approach. It provides strategic, functional, and technical inputs to the Prime Minister and government at all levels, focusing on areas such as agriculture, social sectors, innovation, frontier technologies, manufacturing, services, smart urbanization, mobility, clean energy, improved governance, and development of aspirational districts.
target_beneficiaries: States; Union Territories; Central Ministries; State Governments
eligibility: NITI Aayog serves as the apex public policy think tank of the Government of India, and the nodal agency tasked with catalysing economic development and fostering cooperative federalism through the involvement of State Governments in the economic policymaking process using a bottom-up approach.
benefits: NITI Aayog provides specialized inputs - strategic, functional and technical to Prime Minister and the Government at all levels (Centre as well as States). The policy interventions include but are not limited to agriculture, social sectors (including nutrition, health, education and social upliftment), innovation, frontier technologies, manufacturing & services sectors, smart urbanization, mobility, clean energy, improved governance, development of aspirational districts and so on. It also offers a platform for resolution of inter-sectoral and inter-departmental issues, maintains a state-of-the-art resource centre, and actively monitors and evaluates programmes and initiatives.
financial_support: NITI Aayog is funded by the Government of India as the National Institution for Transforming India. Specific financial allocations for its various initiatives are detailed in documents such as the State Support Mission, which has an approved outlay of Rs. 237.5 crore for the period 2022-23 to 2024-25.
application_process: NITI Aayog does not have a direct application process for beneficiaries as it is a policy think tank. Engagement occurs through structured support initiatives, consultations, and collaborations with States, Central Ministries, and other stakeholders as per specific programme guidelines.
deadlines: NITI Aayog operates as a standing institution with ongoing activities. Specific initiatives under it may have their own timelines, but the organization itself does not have application deadlines.
implementing_agency: NITI Aayog, National Institution for Transforming India, under the Ministry of Planning, Government of India
