scheme_name: Seekho aur Kamao (Learn & Earn) for Minorities
overview: Seekho aur Kamao (Learn & Earn) for Minorities is a skill development scheme aimed at enhancing the employability of minority youth through training in various sectors. The scheme focuses on providing placement-linked skill training to school dropouts and educated unemployed youth from notified minority communities. It is implemented through Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) selected by the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
target_beneficiaries: minority youth; school dropouts; educated unemployed youth
eligibility: Youth belonging to notified minority communities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains) in the age group of 14–45 years, with minimum educational qualification varying by course, and preference given to school dropouts and educated unemployed youth.
benefits: Free skill training, stipend during training, placement assistance, post-placement support, and certification upon successful completion. The scheme also provides soft skills and entrepreneurship development training.
financial_support: The scheme provides 100% funding for training costs and a stipend of Rs. 1,000 per month per trainee during the training period. Financial assistance is released to Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) in installments based on milestones such as enrollment, training completion, and placement.
application_process: 1. Identify and mobilize eligible minority youth. 2. Enroll candidates in approved training courses through Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs). 3. Provide skill training along with stipend. 4. Conduct assessments and certification. 5. Facilitate placement of trained youth. 6. Submit claims for reimbursement to the Ministry of Minority Affairs with required documents.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Minority Affairs

overview: The NMDFC Concessional Loan Schemes are implemented by the National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation (NMDFC), a Government of India undertaking under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, to provide concessional finance to notified minority communities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains) for self-employment and income generation activities. Preference is given to artisans and women. The schemes are implemented through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) and cover various loan types including Term Loan, Education Loan, Virasat (for artisans), and Micro Finance, with benefits extended across Pan-India.
target_beneficiaries: minorities; artisans; women
eligibility: Beneficiaries must belong to notified minority communities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains as per National Commission for Minorities Act 1992, with Jains added in January 2014). Annual family income determines credit line eligibility: Credit Line-1 for income up to ₹3.00 lakh per annum, Credit Line-2 for income up to ₹8.00 lakh per annum. Preference is given to artisans and women. Applications are routed through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) nominated by state governments.
benefits: Concessional interest rates varying by scheme and beneficiary category: Term Loan at 6-8% per annum (with 2% rebate for women under Credit Line-2), Education Loan at 3-8% per annum (with 3% rebate for women under Credit Line-2), Micro Finance at 7-10% per annum (with 2% rebate for women under Credit Line-2), and Virasat scheme at 5-6% per annum (with 1% rebate for women artisans). Loan tenures range from 3 to 5 years with moratorium periods of 3-6 months. Financial assistance is provided via State Channelizing Agencies. Additional benefits include marketing assistance schemes and promotional support for artisans.
financial_support: Loan quantum varies by scheme and credit line: Term Loan up to ₹20 lakh under Credit Line-1 and ₹30 lakh under Credit Line-2; Education Loan up to ₹20 lakh for domestic courses and ₹30 lakh for foreign courses under both credit lines; Micro Finance up to ₹1 lakh per SHG member under Credit Line-1 and ₹1.5 lakh under Credit Line-2; Virasat scheme up to ₹10 lakh under both credit lines. Interest rates are concessional: 6-8% for Term Loan, 3-8% for Education Loan, 7-10% for Micro Finance, and 5-6% for Virasat, with additional rebates for women beneficiaries. Repayment periods range from 3 to 5 years, with moratorium periods of 3-6 months depending on the scheme.
application_process: 1. Identify the appropriate scheme (Term Loan, Education Loan, Virasat, or Micro Finance) based on activity and eligibility. 2. Confirm eligibility based on minority status and annual family income (Credit Line-1: ≤₹3 lakh; Credit Line-2: ≤₹8 lakh). 3. Approach the designated State Channelizing Agency (SCA) for your state/UT. 4. Submit application form along with required documents: self-attested income certificate, residence proof (Aadhaar/ration card/voter ID/passport/phone/electricity bill), religious certificate (if loan > ₹1 lakh), and brief project report. 5. Provide security as per loan amount: self-guarantee & post-dated cheques (loans up to ₹1 lakh); guarantee of one govt./PSU/bank employee or income tax payer + PDCs (₹1-5 lakh); guarantee of two govt./PSU/bank employees or two income tax payers/public representatives or collateral (₹5-10 lakh). 6. Await sanction and disbursement through the SCA.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation (NMDFC)
contact_details: Email: abha[dot]111796[dot]cbdt[at]nic[dot]in | cmd[dot]nmdfc[at]gmail[dot]com | Phone: +91-11-22441635 | Toll Free Helpline: 14402

overview: The Garib Nawaz Employment Scheme is a financial assistance program under the National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation (NMDFC) aimed at providing concessional loans to minority communities for self-employment and income generation activities. The scheme targets economically backward sections among minorities, with preference given to artisans and women. It operates through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) and offers term loans, education loans, microfinance, and the Virasat scheme for craftspersons. The scheme is implemented nationwide and focuses on uplifting minorities through accessible credit at subsidized interest rates.
target_beneficiaries: minorities; artisans; women; economically backward sections
eligibility: Beneficiaries must belong to one of the minority communities notified under Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains added in 2014). Annual family income must be up to ₹3.00 lakh for Credit Line-1 and up to ₹8.00 lakh for Credit Line-2. Preference is given to artisans and women. Applicants must submit self-attested income certificate, residence proof (Aadhaar, ration card, voter ID, etc.), religious certificate (for loans over ₹1 lakh), and a brief project report. Security requirements vary by loan amount: self-guarantee and post-dated cheques for loans up to ₹1 lakh; guarantee of one government/PSU/bank employee or income tax payer for loans between ₹1–5 lakhs; and guarantee of two such entities or collateral for loans between ₹5–10 lakhs.
benefits: Financial benefits include concessional loans at subsidized interest rates (6–8% per annum for term loans, 3–8% for education loans, 5–6% for Virasat scheme). Non-financial benefits include implementation through State Channelizing Agencies, preference for artisans and women, no collateral required for loans up to ₹1 lakh, and support for income-generating activities. The scheme also offers refinancing through Canara Bank and marketing assistance for artisans via exhibitions and buyer-seller meets.
financial_support: Under the Term Loan scheme, loans up to ₹20 lakh are available for Credit Line-1 (annual income ≤ ₹3 lakh) and up to ₹30 lakh for Credit Line-2 (annual income ≤ ₹8 lakh), at interest rates of 6% and 8% per annum respectively, with a 2% rebate for women beneficiaries under Credit Line-2. Education loans offer up to ₹20 lakh for domestic courses and ₹30 lakh for overseas courses at 3–8% per annum, with a 3% rebate for women under Credit Line-2. Microfinance provides up to ₹1 lakh per SHG member under Credit Line-1 and ₹1.5 lakh under Credit Line-2 at 7% and 10% per annum, with a 2% rebate for women under Credit Line-2. The Virasat scheme offers up to ₹10 lakh for working and fixed capital at 5% per annum for Credit Line-1 and 6% for Credit Line-2, with a 1% rebate for women artisans. All loans have a 6-month moratorium and repayment periods of 3–5 years depending on the scheme.
application_process: 1. Identify the nearest State Channelizing Agency (SCA) from the list of 39 operational partners across states and UTs. 2. Obtain the loan application form from the SCA or download it from the NMDFC website. 3. Fill in the application form with personal, financial, and project details. 4. Attach required documents: self-attested income certificate, residence proof (Aadhaar/ration card/voter ID/passport/phone/electricity bill), religious certificate (if loan > ₹1 lakh), and a brief project report. 5. Arrange for security as per loan amount: self-guarantee & post-dated cheques (≤₹1 lakh); one guarantor from govt/PSU/bank or income tax payer (₹1–5 lakhs); two guarantors or collateral (₹5–10 lakhs). 6. Submit the completed application and documents to the SCA. 7. The SCA verifies documents and forwards the proposal to NMDFC for approval. 8. Upon approval, the loan is disbursed through the SCA to the beneficiary.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation (NMDFC)
contact_details: Email: abha[dot]111796[dot]cbdt[at]nic[dot]in, cmd[dot]nmdfc[at]gmail[dot]com | Phone: +91-11-22441635 | Toll-free helpline: 14402

overview: Hamari Dharohar – Cultural Heritage Preservation is a sub-scheme under the Ministry of Minority Affairs aimed at preserving the rich cultural heritage of minority communities in India. It focuses on safeguarding traditions, artifacts, and historical sites of notified minority communities such as Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains. The scheme supports documentation, conservation, and promotion of cultural expressions to ensure intergenerational transmission and national recognition of minority heritage.
target_beneficiaries: minority communities; cultural institutions; heritage organizations
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include registered societies, trusts, NGOs, and institutions working in the field of cultural heritage preservation, particularly those representing notified minority communities under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992. Organizations must have a proven track record in heritage-related activities and must not be blacklisted by any government ministry or department.
benefits: Financial assistance for conservation projects, documentation of heritage, training programs, exhibitions, and publication of cultural materials. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, networking opportunities, and recognition for contributing to national cultural diversity.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-in-aid for approved projects, with funding typically covering up to 90% of project costs, subject to ceiling limits. Disbursement is made in installments based on milestone achievement and submission of utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Identify a heritage conservation project aligned with scheme objectives. 2. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 3. Ensure organizational eligibility and registration on NITI Aayog Darpan portal. 4. Submit the proposal through the designated channel of the Ministry of Minority Affairs. 5. Await scrutiny and approval by the concerned division. 6. Upon approval, enter into a memorandum of understanding and receive first installment. 7. Implement the project and submit progress reports. 8. Submit final report, utilization certificate, and audited statement of expenditure for final settlement.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Minority Affairs

scheme_name: Venture Capital Fund for SCs (VCFSC) – IFCI
overview: The Venture Capital Fund for SCs (VCFSC) – IFCI is a government initiative aimed at promoting entrepreneurship among Scheduled Castes by providing financial support through venture capital. The fund is managed by IFCI Limited and focuses on investing in SC-owned enterprises to foster inclusive economic growth. It operates under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and supports early and growth-stage ventures across various sectors.
target_beneficiaries: SC entrepreneurs; SC-owned enterprises
eligibility: The scheme is open to enterprises promoted and managed by Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs. The business must be legally registered in India and operate in sectors permitted under the fund’s investment policy. Preference is given to innovative, high-growth potential ventures with scalable business models.
benefits: Financial support in the form of venture capital equity or debt investments. Non-financial benefits include mentorship, business guidance, and access to IFCI’s network and expertise in enterprise development.
financial_support: The fund provides financial assistance through equity participation or debt instruments, depending on the stage and needs of the enterprise. Investment decisions are made based on due diligence and growth potential, with flexible structuring to suit entrepreneurial requirements.
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed business plan and proposal to IFCI Venture Capital Funds Ltd. 2. Undergo preliminary screening for eligibility and viability. 3. Present the business case to the investment committee. 4. Complete due diligence process including financial, legal, and technical assessment. 5. Receive term sheet and negotiate investment terms. 6. Finalize legal documentation and disbursement of funds.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: IFCI Limited (formerly Industrial Finance Corporation of India)

overview: The Assistance to Disabled Persons (ADIP) Scheme is a central government initiative under the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, aimed at providing aids and assistive devices to persons with disabilities to promote their physical, social, and psychological rehabilitation. The scheme focuses on reducing the effects of disabilities and enhancing the economic potential of beneficiaries through the provision of modern, scientifically manufactured aids and appliances. It supports individuals with various disabilities as defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, and operates across India through implementing agencies such as NGOs, national institutes, and state governments.
target_beneficiaries: persons with disabilities; divyangjan
eligibility: The scheme covers persons with disabilities of any age who are Indian citizens, hold a disability certificate indicating at least 40% disability, and have a monthly income not exceeding Rs. 20,000. In case of dependents, the income of parents/guardians is considered. Beneficiaries must not have received similar assistance under any other government scheme during the last 3 years (for children under 12 years, this period is 1 year).
benefits: The scheme provides financial assistance for the procurement of aids and assistive devices such as hearing aids, wheelchairs, crutches, braces, artificial limbs, spectacles, and other devices necessary for mobility, communication, and daily living. The assistance includes cost of the device, fitting, and post-fitting follow-up. Devices are provided free of cost to beneficiaries with monthly income up to Rs. 15,000 and at 50% subsidy for those with income between Rs. 15,001 and Rs. 20,000.
financial_support: Financial support under the ADIP Scheme is provided as a subsidy for the purchase of aids and appliances. The central government releases funds to implementing agencies (NGOs, national institutes, state governments) based on proposals and beneficiary lists. The subsidy covers up to 100% of the device cost for beneficiaries with monthly income up to Rs. 15,000 and 50% for those with income between Rs. 15,001 and Rs. 20,000. The assistance includes the cost of the aid, fitting, and post-fitting services.
application_process: 1. Identify the nearest implementing agency (NGO, national institute, or state government department) authorized under the ADIP Scheme. 2. Obtain the application form from the agency or download it from the DEPwD website. 3. Fill in the application form with personal, disability, and income details. 4. Attach required documents including disability certificate, income proof, identity proof, and residence proof. 5. Submit the completed application to the implementing agency. 6. The agency verifies eligibility and processes the request for aid. 7. Upon approval, the aid is procured and distributed to the beneficiary, followed by fitting and follow-up.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and aids.
implementing_agency: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

overview: The OBC Pre-Matric & Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme is designed to provide financial assistance to students belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for their education at pre-matric and post-matric levels. The scheme aims to reduce dropout rates and promote educational attainment among OBC students by covering expenses such as tuition fees, maintenance allowances, and other incidental costs. It is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and is part of the broader welfare initiatives for socially and educationally backward classes.
target_beneficiaries: OBC
eligibility: Students belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBC) as per the central list of OBCs, studying in classes I to X (pre-matric) or XI to PhD level (post-matric) in recognized institutions, with family income not exceeding a specified threshold (as per scheme guidelines), and not receiving any other central government scholarship.
benefits: Financial assistance includes reimbursement of tuition fees, maintenance allowance, and other incidental charges such as books, stationery, and equipment. For pre-matric students, benefits may include admission fees, tuition fees, and maintenance allowance. For post-matric students, benefits cover course fees, maintenance allowance, and other non-refundable charges. The scholarship is disbursed via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support in the form of grants covering tuition fees, maintenance allowance, and other incidental expenses. The exact quantum varies by course level and institution type, with payments made annually through DBT. The maintenance allowance is disbursed in monthly or annual installments as per the level of study.
application_process: 1. Visit the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) at https://scholarships.gov.in. 2. Register or log in using your credentials. 3. Complete One-Time Registration (OTR) if not already done. 4. Fill in the application form for the OBC Pre-Matric & Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme. 5. Upload required documents such as income certificate, caste certificate, bonafide certificate, and previous year's mark sheet. 6. Submit the application before the deadline. 7. Track application status via the NSP dashboard.
deadlines: Application window typically opens in June and closes in October for the academic year, subject to annual notification. For Academic Year 2026-27, the portal is open from 1st June 2026 onwards, with student application closing on 31-10-2026.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Department of Social Justice & Empowerment (Backward Classes)
contact_details: Email: helpdesk@nsp.gov.in | Helpline: 0120-6619540 (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on all days, except government holidays) | Toll Free: 1800 118 111

scheme_name: National Backward Classes Finance & Dev Corp (NBCFDC) Loans
overview: The National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation (NBCFDC) provides concessional financial assistance to members of Backward Classes whose annual family income is up to Rs. 5.00 Lakh through Channel Partners (State Channelising Agencies/Banks). The loans are intended for income generating activities that have potential to provide sustainable income generation for the beneficiary or group of beneficiaries. The Corporation operates under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and implements its schemes via nominated Channel Partners across India.
target_beneficiaries: Backward Classes; OBC; Self Help Groups (SHGs); individual beneficiaries
eligibility: Members of Backward Classes as notified by Central/State Govt. from time to time. Applicant's annual family income should be upto Rs. 5.00 Lakh. For Group Loan Scheme, at least 60% members of SHG must belong to Backward Classes, with other members from weaker sections (SC/ST/Minorities/PwD). For skill training under PM DAKSH, eligibility includes belonging to OBC/EBC/De-notified Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribe/Sr. Citizen/Beggars/Transgender.
benefits: Concessional financial assistance through Channel Partners; loans for income generating activities, education, and skill development; timely payment rebate of 1% per annum equally shared between Channel Partners and Beneficiaries; finance up to 85-90% of project cost via NBCFDC, with remaining share from Channel Partner/Beneficiary; support for agriculture, small business/artisan, technical/professional trades, transport and service sectors; skill development training under PM DAKSH; marketing linkages for artisans; awareness camps and publicity grants to Channel Partners.
financial_support: NBCFDC provides loans covering 85% (Individual Loan Scheme) or 90% (Group Loan Scheme) of project cost, with Channel Partner/Beneficiary contributing 15% or 10% respectively. Maximum loan limit is Rs. 25.00 Lakh per beneficiary under Individual Loan Scheme and per SHG under Group Loan Scheme (with per beneficiary limit of Rs. 1.25 Lakh in SHG). Education loans up to Rs. 25.00 Lakh available at 8% p.a. for 10 years (inclusive of 5 year moratorium). Rate of Interest: 4-5% p.a. from NBCFDC to Channel Partner, 7-8% p.a. from Channel Partner to Beneficiary (varies by loan amount and scheme). Repayment Period: 3-7 years for income generating activities, max 10 years for education loans. Moratorium period: 1 quarter for all loans except education loans (5 years). All schemes carry timely payment rebate @1% per annum, equally shared between Channel Partners and Beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Prospective eligible beneficiaries should apply on prescribed form (available with Channel Partners) to District Office of Channel Partners where they normally reside. 2. Applicant should clearly mention felt needs, choice of vocation, and training requirements in application form. 3. Applicant must fulfil eligibility criteria (belong to Backward Class and have annual family income upto Rs. 3.00 lakh as per 'How & Where to Apply' page, though other pages state Rs. 5.00 Lakh - using Rs. 3.00 lakh as specified in application guidelines). 4. Submit documents as proof such as Caste and Income Certificate issued by Competent Authority (Tehsildar/Sub Divisional Magistrate/District Collector). 5. Self-certified annual family income certificate duly endorsed by gazetted officers of State Government or Branch Manager of Bank giving the loan are admissible. 6. Eligible persons can apply online at registration portal on NBCFDC website; requests received will be forwarded to concerned Channel Partners (SCAs/Banks) under intimation to applicant. 7. For more details, contact concerned Channel Partner (State Channelizing Agency/RRB/PSB).
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation (NBCFDC), a Govt. of India Undertaking under the aegis of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
contact_details: Email: nf-obc@nbcfdc.gov.in | Contact No. 011-45854421 (for NFOBC scheme; general contact not explicitly stated in evidence)

scheme_name: Scheme for Implementation of Persons with Disabilities Act (SIPDA)
overview: The Scheme for Implementation of Persons with Disabilities Act (SIPDA) is a central sector scheme aimed at empowering persons with disabilities through various interventions including rehabilitation, education, skill development, and accessibility initiatives. It supports the implementation of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 across India by providing financial assistance to states, NGOs, and institutions for disability-inclusive programs.
target_beneficiaries: persons with disabilities; NGOs; state governments; educational institutions; rehabilitation centers
eligibility: State governments, union territory administrations, local bodies, institutions established by central or state governments, NGOs registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 or Indian Trusts Act, 1882, and other organizations working in the field of disability rehabilitation and empowerment are eligible to apply for financial assistance under SIPDA, subject to fulfilling scheme-specific guidelines and submission of required documents.
benefits: Financial assistance for setting up and running rehabilitation centers, special schools, vocational training units, and accessible infrastructure; support for assistive devices, scholarships, and skill development programs; funding for awareness campaigns, early intervention services, and community-based rehabilitation; grants for organizing national events, workshops, and training programs; assistance for research and development in disability sector.
financial_support: Under SIPDA, grants-in-aid are provided to eligible organizations for specific projects, with funding patterns varying by component — typically 90% central assistance for northeastern and hill states, and 60% for other states, subject to upper ceilings and utilization certificates. The scheme operates through annual proposals submitted by states and institutions, which are appraised and sanctioned by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD).
application_process: 1. Eligible organizations prepare project proposals as per SIPDA guidelines. 2. Proposals are submitted through the respective state government or directly to DEPwD, depending on the component. 3. State governments forward recommendations for NGO/institution proposals. 4. DEPwD appraises proposals technically and financially. 5. Approved proposals are sanctioned with specific terms and conditions. 6. Funds are released in installments based on progress and utilization certificates. 7. Beneficiaries must submit audited accounts and performance reports for continued funding.
deadlines: Annual basis — proposals are invited once a year, typically aligned with the financial year cycle.
implementing_agency: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

scheme_name: Nai Manzil – Education & Skill Development for Minorities
overview: Nai Manzil – Education & Skill Development for Minorities is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Ministry of Minority Affairs to provide education and skill development to minority youth. It targets school dropouts and those educated in community education institutions like madrasas, offering them formal education (up to Class VIII or X) and skill training in market-relevant trades. The scheme aims to enhance employability and socio-economic upliftment of minority communities through integrated education and vocational training.
target_beneficiaries: minority youth; school dropouts; madrasa students
eligibility: The scheme targets minority youth in the age group of 17-35 years who are school dropouts or educated in community education institutions such as madrasas, and belong to notified minority communities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, and Jains).
benefits: Beneficiaries receive free formal education (up to Class VIII or X) and skill training in market-relevant trades, along with a stipend during training, post-placement support, and certification recognized by NCVT or equivalent bodies. The scheme also provides placement assistance and tracking for sustainable livelihoods.
financial_support: The scheme provides 100% financial assistance from the Ministry of Minority Affairs, covering education, skill training, stipend to trainees, and placement support. Funds are disbursed through implementing agencies following General Financial Rules (GFRs).
application_process: 1. Identify eligible minority youth through community mobilization and outreach. 2. Mobilize and counsel target beneficiaries for enrollment. 3. Enroll candidates in designated education and skill training centers. 4. Provide integrated education and vocational training as per NCVT norms. 5. Conduct assessments and issue certifications. 6. Facilitate placement and post-placement tracking for sustainable livelihoods.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Minority Affairs

scheme_name: National Trust Scheme for Persons with Autism etc.
Senior Care Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) – Startup Support
overview: The Senior Care Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) – Startup Support is a Government of India initiative under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment aimed at promoting innovation and entrepreneurship in the senior care sector. It supports startups developing products, services, and solutions for the elderly and Divyangjan (persons with disabilities) through financial assistance, mentorship, and market linkage. The scheme encourages the development of affordable, accessible, and scalable solutions for ageing populations. It operates as a pan-India program to foster inclusive growth in the senior care ecosystem.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups registered in India as a Private Limited Company, Limited Liability Partnership (LLP), or Registered Partnership Firm, working on innovative products, services, or solutions for senior citizens and/or Divyangjan, with a focus on healthcare, assisted living, mobility, mental wellness, or age-friendly technologies.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grants, mentorship from experts in ageing and social sectors, incubation support, access to testing and validation facilities, market linkage opportunities, and visibility through government platforms and events.
financial_support: Selected startups receive a grant of up to INR 50 lakhs for product development, pilot testing, and market deployment, disbursed in milestones based on project progress and utilization of funds.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 50 lakhs
application_process: 1. Visit the SAGE portal at https://social.nic.in/sage 2. Register as a startup on the portal 3. Fill out the online application form with details of the innovation, team, and impact 4. Upload required documents including incorporation certificate, PAN, and project proposal 5. Submit the application for review 6. Await evaluation by the expert committee 7. If selected, sign the grant agreement and receive funds in tranches.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

scheme_name: Dr. Ambedkar Post-Matric Scholarship for EBC
overview: Dr. Ambedkar Post-Matric Scholarship for EBC is a welfare-based scholarships belonging to the Economically Backward Classes (EBC) category, providing financial assistance to pursue post-matriculation or post-secondary studies. The scheme is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and aims to support students from economically weaker sections in continuing their education beyond the matriculation level.
target_beneficiaries: EBC
eligibility: The candidate should be from the Economically Backward Classes (EBC) category. Family income from all sources should not be more than Rs. 1 lakh per annum during the financial year of the application. The candidate should be currently studying in a recognized educational institution at the post-matriculation or post-secondary level. The candidate should not be in receipt of any other central government, state government, or AICTE-sponsored scholarship.
benefits: The scholarship provides financial assistance for payment of college fee, purchase of computer, stationeries, books, equipment, software, etc. No other additional grant will be payable in lieu of hostel charges and medical charges. The scholarship is disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode on an annual basis. Aadhaar card and Aadhaar-seeded bank account in the name of the candidate are mandatory for submitting the online application.
financial_support: The scholarship amount is Rs. 50,000 per annum for every year of study, with a maximum duration of 4 years for first-year admitted degree students and 3 years for diploma students. For students currently studying in the 2nd/3rd/4th year at degree level, the duration is reduced to 3/2/1 year respectively. Similarly, for diploma students in the 2nd/3rd year, the duration is reduced to 2/1 year respectively. The amount is provided as a lump sum towards payment of college fee, purchase of computer, stationeries, books, equipment, software, etc.
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 50,000 per annum
application_process: 1. Visit the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) at https://scholarships.gov.in/. 2. Register or log in using your OTR (One Time Registration) number. 3. Fill in the online application form with accurate personal, academic, and financial details. 4. Upload the required documents, including income certificate, bonafide certificate, category certificate, and mark sheets. 5. Submit the application before the deadline. 6. Await verification and approval from the concerned authorities.
deadlines: Student Application Open till: 31-10-2026
implementing_agency: Department of Social Justice & Empowerment(Backward Classes)
contact_details: Email: helpdesk[at]nsp[dot]gov[dot]in | Helpline: 0120 - 6619540 (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on all days, except government holidays)

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Top Class Education for SC Students
overview: The Central Sector Scheme for Top Class Education for SC Students is a merit-based scholarship scheme implemented by the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment to support SC students pursuing higher education in top-class institutions. The scheme provides financial assistance for tuition fees, living expenses, books, and computers to eligible students. It aims to promote educational empowerment and reduce dropout rates among SC students in professional and technical courses.
target_beneficiaries: SC/ST
eligibility: The student must belong to a Scheduled Caste (SC) community. The annual family income should not exceed Rs. 4.5 lakh. The student must have secured admission in a notified institute for pursuing a full-time course. The student must not be in receipt of any other scholarship or stipend. The student must be pursuing a course at the graduate or postgraduate level in engineering, medicine, law, management, or other notified professional courses.
benefits: The scheme provides full tuition fee reimbursement, living expenses of Rs. 2,200 per month, annual book grant of Rs. 3,000, and a one-time computer grant of Rs. 45,000. The benefits are disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the student's Aadhaar-seeded bank account. The scholarship is renewable annually subject to satisfactory academic performance and promotion to the next year of study.
financial_support: Financial support includes reimbursement of actual tuition fees (subject to a ceiling), monthly living allowance of Rs. 2,200, annual book allowance of Rs. 3,000, and a one-time computer allowance of Rs. 45,000. The total financial support varies based on the course and institution but is designed to cover major educational expenses. Disbursement is made through DBT via PFMS to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account.
application_process: 1. Visit the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) at https://scholarships.gov.in. 2. Register and generate a One-Time Registration (OTR) number. 3. Log in using OTR credentials. 4. Select the 'Central Sector Scheme for Top Class Education for SC Students' from the list of available schemes. 5. Fill in the online application form with personal, academic, and bank details. 6. Upload required documents including caste certificate, income certificate, admission proof, and bank details. 7. Submit the application before the deadline. 8. Await verification by the institute and nodal officer. 9. Upon approval, the scholarship amount will be disbursed via DBT.
deadlines: Student Application Open till: 31-10-2026
implementing_agency: Department of Social Justice & Empowerment

overview: The PM Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat) is a nationwide initiative aimed at achieving universal accessibility for persons with disabilities and senior citizens by creating an enabling and barrier-free environment. It focuses on three verticals: built environment, transportation, and information and communication ecosystem. The campaign seeks to enhance accessibility in public facilities, transport systems, and digital platforms to promote inclusion and independent living.
target_beneficiaries: persons with disabilities; senior citizens
eligibility: The scheme is intended for persons with disabilities and senior citizens across India. Implementation involves various central and state government ministries, departments, and local authorities responsible for public infrastructure, transport, and digital services.
benefits: Benefits include improved physical access to government buildings, public spaces, and transport facilities; enhanced accessibility of websites and digital platforms; availability of assistive technologies; and greater independence and mobility for persons with disabilities and senior citizens through barrier-free environments.
financial_support: The campaign involves convergence of existing schemes and programs of various ministries and departments. Financial support is provided through budgetary allocations of participating ministries for specific accessibility audits, retrofitting, and creation of accessible infrastructure under their respective schemes.
application_process: The application process varies by vertical and implementing agency. For built environment accessibility, concerned departments conduct accessibility audits of public buildings and submit proposals for retrofitting. For transportation, ministries like Railways, Road Transport, and Civil Aviation implement accessibility features in vehicles and infrastructure. For ICT, ministries ensure compliance with accessibility standards in websites and mobile applications. There is no centralized application portal for beneficiaries; implementation is carried out by designated nodal agencies.
deadlines: Rolling basis — initiatives are implemented as part of ongoing government projects and schemes.
implementing_agency: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

scheme_name: Canteen Stores Department MSME Procurement Scheme
overview: The Canteen Stores Department (CSD) MSME Procurement Scheme aims to support ex-servicemen by facilitating procurement from MSMEs owned or operated by them. The scheme is designed to promote economic rehabilitation and self-reliance among ex-servicemen through increased market access via CSD's procurement network.
target_beneficiaries: ex-servicemen; MSME
eligibility: MSMEs that are owned, operated, or controlled by ex-servicemen are eligible to participate in the CSD MSME Procurement Scheme. The enterprise must be duly registered as an MSME and provide proof of ex-servicemen ownership or control.
benefits: Benefits include access to CSD's extensive procurement network across India, guaranteed purchase orders from CSD canteens, timely payment settlement, and support in product listing and vendor registration. The scheme also provides marketing exposure through CSD's customer base of defence personnel and their families.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or loans. Instead, it facilitates market access and procurement opportunities, enabling ex-servicemen-owned MSMEs to generate revenue through supply contracts with the Canteen Stores Department.
application_process: 1. Register the MSME on the CSD vendor portal. 2. Submit proof of MSME ownership/servicemen. 3. Await verification and approval by CSD. 4. Upon approval, list products on the CSD portal for procurement consideration.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Canteen Stores Department, Ministry of Defence

overview: The Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS) is a cashless and capless health scheme launched on April 1, 2003, by the Ministry of Defence to provide comprehensive medical facilities to retired armed forces personnel and their dependents. It operates through a network of ECHS Polyclinics and empanelled civil hospitals, offering indoor/outdoor treatment, tests, and medicines without monetary ceiling on treatment. The scheme is financed by the Government of India and aims to deliver quality healthcare by leveraging existing Armed Forces infrastructure and empanelling civil healthcare providers.
target_beneficiaries: ex-servicemen; dependents of ex-servicemen; retired armed forces personnel; spouse and eligible dependents
eligibility: Retired Armed Forces personnel till 2002 could avail medical facilities only for specific high cost surgery/treatment for a limited number of diseases covered under the Army Group Insurance(Medical Branch Scheme) (AGI(MBS)) and Armed Forces Group Insurance Scheme(Management Information System) (AFGIS (MIS)) schemes. Based on the noble aim of establishing a medicare system for retirees, ECHS was authorised vide Government of India, Ministry of Defence letter No 22(i) 01/US/D(Res) dated 30 Dec 2002 and launched with effect from 01 Apr 2003. Ex-servicemen pensioners and their dependants who were only entitled for treatment in service hospital are now authorised treatment in service hospitals and in civil/private hospitals specifically empanelled with the ECHS.
benefits: No age or medical condition bar for becoming a member. Life time contribution ranges from Rs 30,000/- to Rs 1,20,000/- (depending upon Grade Pay). Provision for re-imbursement at CGHS rates in case of treatment under Emergency in a non-empanelled facility. No monetary ceiling on treatment. Indoor/outdoor treatment, tests and medicines. Familiar environment and sense of belongingness. Covers spouse and all eligible dependents.
financial_support: The Scheme is financed by Govt of India. The existing infrastructure includes command and control structure, spare capacity of Service Medical facilities (Hospitals and MI Rooms), procurement organisations for medical and non medical equipment, defence land and buildings etc. In order to ensure minimal disruption of the Scheme during war/training and availability of ECHS services in non military areas, resources are supplemented by establishing new Armed Forces Polyclinics in Non Military areas, augmenting existing medical facilities/clinics in selected military stations, empanelling civil hospitals and diagnostic centres, and providing finances.
application_process: 1. Retired Armed Forces personnel and their dependents become eligible for ECHS membership upon retirement. 2. Members must make a one-time contribution based on their Grade Pay at the time of retirement, ranging from Rs 30,000/- to Rs 1,20,000/-. 3. Upon payment, members receive an ECHS card enabling access to empanelled facilities. 4. For treatment, beneficiaries visit ECHS Polyclinics or empanelled hospitals. 5. In emergencies, treatment can be sought at non-empanelled facilities with reimbursement at CGHS rates. 6. Annual validation of dependents above 18 years is required (excluding spouse) as per CO ECHS letter No B/49711-NSC/AG/ECHS/Gen Corrs dt 10 Jun 25. 7. Beneficiaries must carry out Annual Validation as per directives; in case of issues, contact jditechs1[at]echs[dot]gov[dot]in. 8. For card-related issues, email echs-card[at]echs[dot]gov[dot]in or call Toll Free No: 1800 114 115. 9. For general issues, contact via echs[at]sourceinfosys[dot]com or WhatsApp on +91-7703818578 / 7701976194 / 8448086480 / 8448086481.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Defence, Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare (DoESW)
contact_details: Email: echs[at]sourceinfosys[dot]com | WhatsApp: +91-7703818578 / 7701976194 / 8448086480 / 8448086481 | Toll Free No: 1800 114 115 | Card-related issues: echs-card[at]echs[dot]gov[dot]in | Annual validation queries: jditechs1[at]echs[dot]gov[dot]in

scheme_name: National Fellowship for Students with Disabilities
overview: The National Fellowship for Students with Disabilities is a welfare-based scholarship scheme under the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, aimed at providing financial support to students with disabilities for pursuing higher education. It is part of the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) ecosystem and requires One Time Registration (OTR) for application. The scheme supports students with disabilities in accessing technical and professional education through direct benefit transfer (DBT).
target_beneficiaries: students with disabilities
eligibility: The candidate should be admitted to First year of Diploma level course OR Second year of Diploma level course through lateral entry in any of the AICTE approved Institution of respective year. Specially-abled student, having disability of not less than 40%. Family income from all sources should not be more than Rs. 8 lakh per annum during the current financial year. A valid income certificate issued by State/UT Government needs to be enclosed. The candidate should NOT be recipient of any of the Central Govt./State Govt./AICTE Sponsored scholarships.
benefits: Rs. 50,000/- per annum for every year of study i.e. maximum 3 years for first year admitted students and maximum 2 years for second year admitted students through lateral entry as lump sum amount towards payment of college fee, purchase of computer, stationeries, books, equipments, softwares etc. No other additional grant will be payable in lieu of hostel charges and medical charges etc. Scholarship will be disbursed only through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in the bank account of the student by AICTE. Student must have General Saving Account in his/her name (FRILL/Minor/Joint account will not be accepted). Aadhaar card and Aadhaar seeded bank account in the name of candidate is mandatory for submitting online application.
financial_support: Rs. 50,000 per annum for every year of study i.e. maximum 3 years for first year admitted students and maximum 2 years for second year admitted students through lateral entry as lump sum amount towards payment of college fee, purchase of computer, stationeries, books, equipments, softwares etc. No other additional grant will be payable in lieu of hostel charges and medical charges etc. After selection, the awardee will be paid scholarship through DBT mode on annual basis.
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 50,000.00 per annum
application_process: 1. Visit the NSP Portal using the link: https://scholarships.gov.in/ 2. Select the “Institutions” option 3. Click on the “Registration Form” option to proceed further 4. The User will be redirected to the “Scholarship Institute KYC Registration” page, wherein detailed instructions regarding Institute Registration will be displayed. The User will be required to click on “Continue to Registration” to proceed further 5. Upon cl icking “Continue to Registration”, the user will be redirected to the “Registration” page. 6. The user is required to enter the Institute details under the “Fill Registration Form” section 7. The user must enter the Institute’s UDISE+ Code, enter the CAPTCHA code displayed on the screen, and click Next 8. After successful verification of the UDISE+ Code, the system validates the institute details. If the verification is successful, a confirmation pop-up message will be displayed 9. After successful verification, the Institute Details page will be displayed. The following fields will be auto-populated based on the UDISE+ data: UDISE+ Code, Institute Name, State, District. The user must complete the remaining fields: Institute Address, State for Affiliated University, Affiliated University/Board, Institute Management Type/Nature, Institute Website URL. After entering all required details, user must click Next 10. Upon clicking “Next”, the user is redirected to the “Nodal Officer” page, where the details of the Institute Nodal Officer (INO) for Aadhaar authentication are displayed. The user is required to enter: Mobile Number (linked with Aadhaar), Aadhaar Number, Name as in Aadhaar, Date of Birth, Gender, Designation, Official Mail ID, Alternate Contact Number, INO Identity Proof Upload 11. The user must then enter the mobile number linked with Aadhaar and click on Validate Mobile Number. An OTP is sent to the registered mobile number. Enter the OTP received on the mobile device and click on Verify. After successful OTP verification, the system will display a confirmation message indicating that the mobile number has been verified successfully 12. Next, select the consent declaration checkbox authorizing NSP to authenticate Aadhaar details through UIDAI and click on Next to proceed. The system then verifies the details of INO details as entered by the user 13. Upon successful verification of the INO, the user is redirected to the “Institute Head” page. The user is required to enter: Mobile Number (linked with Aadhaar), Aadhaar Number, Name as in Aadhaar, Date of Birth, Gender, Designation, Official Mail ID, Alternate Contact Number 14. HoI is required to enter the mobile number linked with Aadhaar and click on “Validate Mobile Number”. Subsequently, the HoI must enter the OTP received on the registered mobile number and click on “Verify”. After successful OTP verification, the Aadhaar-linked details are displayed. The user must: Verify all details carefully, Select the consent declaration checkbox, Click Submit 15. After successful submission of HOI details, the system verifies the details and displays a confirmation message 16. Upon successful completion of the registration process, the system generates a unique KYC Registration Reference ID. The user is advised to note the reference number for future use. The registration process under Fill Registration Form is marked as completed. The page also displays instructions regarding printing, attestation, and submission of the KYC Registration Form 17. After successful biometric authentication, the INO can proceed to the “Print & Upload Registration Form” section. The system will display the current KYC status and will provide the option to “Go to Print & Upload”. Upon selecting the “Go to Print & Upload”, the INO is required to: Enter the KYC Registration Reference Number, Click on Send OTP & Print, Complete the OTP verification, Download or print the KYC Registration Form. After printing the KYC form, INO must: Affix the latest passport-size photograph, Get the form duly attested/signed by the Head of Institute, Scan the attested KYC Registration Form, Upload the scanned document in PDF or JPEG format. Note: Upload Requirements: File Format: PDF/JPEG, File Size: 50 KB to 500 KB 18. Before accessing the Approval by Head of Institute (HoI) module, the user must verify the institute details. Enter the institute's UDISE+ Code, Enter the CAPTCHA code displayed on the screen, Click Next 19. The Head of Institute must access the HoI approval module by entering the institute UDISE+ Code and CAPTCHA. The system will then display the current KYC Registration status indicating that: KYC Form has been filled by the INO, Face Authentication of both INO and HoI has been completed, The attested KYC Form has been uploaded, Approval by HoI is pending. Click Go to HoI KYC to continue. The Head of Institute must review the following information: Institute Details (having parameters KYC Registration Form ID, UDISE+ Code, Institute Name, Address, State, District, Affiliated University, Institute Nature, Website URL), Head of Institute Information (having parameters Aadhaar Details, Name, Date of Birth, Gender, Mobile Number, Official Mail ID, Designation, Contact Information, Photograph), Institute Nodal Officer Information (having parameters Aadhaar Details, Name, Date of Birth, Gender, Mobile Number, Official Mail ID, Designation, Contact Information, Photograph). HoI must click on “View Attested KYC Form” and review the uploaded KYC Registration Form carefully. HoI then must select the declaration checkbox and click on “Approve”. After reviewing the KYC Registration Form, verifying the institute details, and approving the registration request, the Head of Institute (HoI) completes the approval process. To finalize the request, HoI must: Enter the institute's UDISE+ Code, Enter the CAPTCHA code displayed on the screen, Click Next. The system validates the entered details and updates the KYC registration status. Upon successful validation, the KYC registration request is forwarded to the concerned Ministry/Department for final review and approval. 20. After approval by the Head of Institute, the KYC Registration request is forwarded to the concerned Ministry/Department for final verification and approval. The Ministry/Department reviews: Institute details, Aadhaar authentication status, Biometric authentication status, Uploaded attested KYC Registration Form, HoI approval status. Upon successful verification, the institute KYC registration is approved and activated on NSP.
