implementing_agency: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities

overview: Agmark Certification for Agricultural Products is a quality certification scheme administered by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI) under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. It ensures that agricultural commodities meet specified grade standards for quality, purity, and hygiene. The certification is voluntary and applies to a wide range of agricultural and allied products, promoting fair trade practices and consumer confidence.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; processors; traders; exporters; MSME
eligibility: Any person, firm, company, cooperative society, or other entity engaged in the production, processing, or trading of agricultural commodities covered under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937, is eligible to apply for Agmark certification. The product must conform to the grade standards prescribed under the Act.
benefits: Agmark certification provides legal recognition of product quality, enhances marketability and consumer trust, facilitates access to premium markets and exports, enables better price realization, and serves as a proof of compliance with food safety and quality standards. It also helps in reducing post-harvest losses and supports implementation of quality control systems.
financial_support: The Agmark certification scheme does not provide direct financial support, subsidies, or grants to applicants. It is a fee-based quality certification service where applicants bear the cost of testing, inspection, and certification as per the prescribed fee structure.
application_process: 1. Identify the applicable Agmark standard for the product from the Gazette of India or DMI website. 2. Ensure the product and processing unit meet the prescribed grade and hygiene requirements. 3. Apply online through the Agmark portal (agmark.gov.in) or submit a physical application to the nearest Regional Agmark Laboratory. 4. Submit required documents including product details, processing unit information, and quality control plan. 5. Pay the applicable fee for sample testing and certification. 6. Undergo inspection and sampling by DMI officials. 7. Laboratory testing of samples for quality parameters. 8. Grant of Agmark certificate upon compliance, valid for a specific period subject to renewal and surveillance.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

scheme_name: National Accreditation Board for Testing & Calibration Labs (NABL)
overview: The National Accreditation Board for Testing & Calibration Laboratories (NABL) is an autonomous body under the Quality Council of India (QCI) that provides voluntary accreditation services to testing laboratories, calibration laboratories, medical testing laboratories, proficiency testing providers (PTP), reference material producers (RMP), and biobanks in accordance with international standards such as ISO/IEC 17025, ISO 15189, ISO/IEC 17043, ISO 17034, and ISO 20387. NABL ensures technical competence and impartiality of conformity assessment bodies through third-party assessment and maintains international recognition via ILAC and APAC Mutual Recognition Arrangements (MRAs). It operates as a self-financing entity, charging fees to accredited bodies for operational sustainability.
target_beneficiaries: testing laboratories; calibration laboratories; medical testing laboratories; proficiency testing providers (PTP); reference material producers (RMP); biobanks
eligibility: Accreditation is voluntary and accessible to all testing including medical and calibration laboratories, proficiency testing providers, and reference material producers in India and other countries in the region, regardless of the size of the applicant conformity assessment body (CAB) or its membership in any association or group, or the number of CABs already accredited by NABL. For assessor training, candidates must be aged 38-55 years, hold a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering/Technology or Master’s in Science (or postgraduate/Ph.D. in relevant medical fields for medical testing), and have a minimum of ten years of experience in the relevant field, including five years at supervisory level or above.
benefits: Formal recognition of competence by NABL in accordance with international standards provides international recognition, access to global markets, time and cost efficiency, enhanced customer confidence and satisfaction, robust quality management systems, continual improvement, better operational control, assurance of accurate and reliable results, cost reduction, prevention of losses due to defects, eligibility to participate in tenders requiring independently verified laboratories, potential increase in business, and savings from reduced or eliminated need for retesting in another country. Accredited laboratories' results are used by regulators for public benefit in areas such as environmental protection, food safety, clean water, energy, health, and social care.
financial_support: NABL is self-financing and charges fees to conformity assessment bodies to cover operational costs and other expenditure. Accreditation involves payment of fees by applicants, which vary based on the type and scope of accreditation sought. Detailed fee structures are available in NABL 100A 'General Information Brochure'.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant accreditation standard and scope (e.g., ISO/IEC 17025 for testing/calibration labs, ISO 15189 for medical labs). 2. Refer to the appropriate NABL document (e.g., NABL 100B for accreditation process, NABL 120 for product group classification). 3. Prepare the application as per the specific criteria document (e.g., NABL 112A for medical labs, NABL 180 for PTP, NABL 190 for RMP). 4. Submit the application online via the NABL portal (hard copies not accepted). 5. Await selection and communication from NABL post-evaluation. 6. Upon selection, submit required documents and course/material details as communicated. 7. Undergo on-site assessment by NABL-empanelled assessors. 8. Address any non-conformities. 9. Receive accreditation decision and certificate upon compliance.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: National Accreditation Board for Testing & Calibration Laboratories (NABL), Constituent Board of Quality Council of India (QCI)
contact_details: Email: Not explicitly stated in evidence | Helpline: Not explicitly stated in evidence

overview: The Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS) for Ex-Servicemen (ESM) is a welfare initiative by the Kendriya Sainik Board (KSB) under the Ministry of Defence, aimed at providing financial assistance to the wards of Ex-Servicemen and Ex-Coast Guard personnel for pursuing professional degree courses. The scheme supports education through scholarships disbursed in installments based on academic performance and renewal criteria.
target_beneficiaries: wards of Ex-Servicemen; wards of Ex-Coast Guard personnel
eligibility: The applicant must be a ward (son/daughter) of an Ex-Serviceman or Ex-Coast Guard personnel who has been released/discharged/retired after 01 July 1987 and is in receipt of pension. The student must have secured admission in the first year of an approved professional course between 01 April to 15 November (except lateral entry/integrated courses), possess a valid PPO number, Aadhaar card, bank account (SBI/PNB), and meet the minimum educational qualification (MEQ) for the course. The applicant must score at least 50% aggregate marks in each semester/academic year to continue receiving the scholarship.
benefits: Financial assistance of INR 30,000 per annum for boys and INR 36,000 per annum for girls, disbursed in installments upon successful renewal. Non-financial benefits include access to the KSB online portal for application and renewal, document verification support, and helpline assistance for technical and scheme-related queries.
financial_support: The scholarship provides INR 30,000 per year for male students and INR 36,000 per year for female students. The amount is disbursed in installments: the first installment is paid upon selection in the merit list, and subsequent installments are released annually upon submission of renewal application with original mark sheets showing at least 50% aggregate marks in each semester/academic year. Payments are made directly to the student's bank account after verification of documents.
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 30,000 per annum for boys and INR 36,000 per annum for girls
application_process: 1. Visit KSB website www.online.ksb.gov.in and register by providing ESM/widow/orphan details including photograph, PPO number, bank account (SBI/PNB), ESM I/Card, Aadhaar, mobile, email, and dates of birth, enrollment, discharge, and death (if applicable). 2. After registration, login using credentials sent to email and activate account via activation link. 3. Log in to the portal, select 'PMSS New Application' from the dashboard. 4. Fill in Part-1 (ESM details: Army No, Rank, Name, PPO, Category) and Part-2 (Student details: Aadhaar, mobile, email, MEQ, marks, course details, bank details). 5. Fill in Part-3: select regulatory body, confirm Aadhaar-bank linkage, provide student name as bank account holder, select bank (SBI/PNB), provide correct account number. 6. Upload scanned original documents: photograph, ESM/Ex-Coast Guard certificate (Annexure-1), Bonafide Certificate (Annexure-2), Bank Manager's certificate (Annexure-3), 10th mark sheet, MEQ mark sheets, first page of bank passbook/cancelled cheque, category-supporting certificate, Aadhaar card, and affidavit if applicable. 7. Click 'Save and Forward' to submit the application. 8. For renewal, visit the portal, login, select 'Renewal Application', enter Selection Serial Number, click 'Get Details', fill renewal form, upload required documents (bonafide, exam passing, bank manager's certificate, mark sheets, bank passbook, Aadhaar), and submit.
deadlines: Admission must be taken between 01 April to 15 November (except lateral entry/integrated courses). Renewal application must be submitted within one year of declaration of result of each academic year.
implementing_agency: Kendriya Sainik Board, Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare, Ministry of Defence

scheme_name: National Organic Farming Research Institute (NOFRI) Certification
overview: The National Organic Farming Research Institute (NOFRI) Certification scheme, based at https://nofri.org.in, provides organic certification services for agricultural producers and processors. It operates under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and focuses on verifying compliance with national organic standards. The institute supports the growth of organic farming through technical guidance, training, and certification for domestic and export markets.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; processors; agri-entrepreneurs; MSME
eligibility: Farmers, producer groups, processors, traders, and exporters engaged in organic agriculture or processing who wish to certify their products under NPOP standards are eligible to apply for certification through NOFRI.
benefits: Certification enables access to premium organic markets, eligibility for export under NPOP, consumer trust through recognized quality label, and compliance with domestic and international organic regulations. Certified entities can use the 'India Organic' logo on their products.
financial_support: NOFRI Certification does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. It is a fee-based certification service where applicants pay forfeit costs as per the fee structure defined by the institute based on farm size, processing unit capacity, and scope of certification.
application_process:
1. Submit application form available on NOFRI website or through regional centers
2. Provide farm/unit details including land records, input usage, and processing facilities
3. Undergo initial review of application and documents
4. Schedule and undergo on-site inspection by NOFRI-certified inspectors
5. Submit inspection report for review by certification committee
6. Receive certification decision; if approved, issuance of certificate valid for one year
7. Undergo annual surveillance and renewal inspection for continued certification
deadlines: Applications are accepted throughout the year on a rolling basis; there is no fixed annual deadline.
implementing_agency: National Organic Farming Research Institute (NOFRI), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

scheme_name: Quality Council of India (QCI) Certification Support for MSMEs
overview: Quality Council of India (QCI) Certification Support for MSMEs is a recognition scheme aimed at enhancing the quality and competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises through certification under various QCI boards such as NABL, NABH, NABCB, NABET, and NBQP. The scheme supports MSMEs in adopting quality standards, improving service delivery, and gaining national and international acceptance of their products and services. It is implemented through QCI’s constituent boards and divisions, with DPIIT serving as the nodal ministry. The initiative aligns with national goals like Viksit Bharat 2047 and Zero Defect, Zero Effect manufacturing vision.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSMEs engaged in manufacturing or services seeking third-party assessment of their products, services, or processes for quality compliance under QCI’s constituent boards such as NABL (testing/calibration labs), NABH (hospitals/healthcare), NABCB (certification bodies), NABET (education/training), or NBQP (quality promotion). Eligibility is based on the specific criteria of the respective accreditation or certification scheme under which the MSME applies.
benefits: Enhanced credibility and trust among customers, regulators, and global partners; transparent and consistent processes aligned with international best practices; national and international recognition of certifications; improved market access and competitiveness; eligibility for government tenders and procurement; access to QCI’s training and capacity-building programmes; inclusion in QCI’s directory of accredited entities; support for export readiness and quality-led growth.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Instead, it offers non-financial benefits through certification and recognition. Any costs associated with assessment, application, or accreditation fees are borne by the applying MSME, though rationalised fee structures (e.g., for NABH Entry Level Ayush Hospitals) may apply based on scale and scope.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant QCI board or scheme based on the MSME’s sector (e.g., NABL for labs, NABH for healthcare, NABCB for certification bodies). 2. Visit the respective board’s website or QCI’s accreditation portal to review eligibility and documentation requirements. 3. Submit the application online via the designated portal (e.g., nabh.co for NABH, nabl-india.org for NABL). 4. Upload required documents such as legal registration, quality manuals, test reports, and operational records. 5. Pay the applicable assessment fee as per the fee structure. 6. Undergo document review and/or on-site assessment by QCI-appointed assessors. 7. Address any non-conformities raised during assessment. 8. Upon successful compliance, receive accreditation/certification from the respective QCI board. 9. Maintain compliance through periodic surveillance and re-certification as per scheme validity (typically 2–3 years).
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on the specific scheme and board schedules.
implementing_agency: Quality Council of India (QCI), operating under the nodal oversight of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry

scheme_name: India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) – MSME Banking
overview: India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) – MSME Banking is a specialized banking service offered by India Post Payments Bank to support Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) with digital banking solutions, including current and savings accounts, digital payments, and access to credit through partnerships. The scheme aims to enhance financial inclusion for MSMEs by leveraging IPPB’s extensive network of over 155,000 banking access points across India, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas. It provides MSMEs with easy access to formal banking services, enabling them to manage transactions, receive payments, and build credit history.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSMEs registered under the MSME Act, 2006, including proprietorships, partnerships, private limited companies, and other entities engaged in manufacturing or service activities, are eligible to open current or savings accounts with India Post Payments Bank for business purposes.
benefits: MSME customers gain access to zero-balance savings accounts, low-cost current accounts, UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, bill payments, mobile banking, doorstep banking services, and integration with government schemes. Through partnerships, they may also access working capital loans, term loans, and overdraft facilities. The service helps MSMEs build financial credibility and improve cash flow management.
financial_support: IPPB does not directly lend to MSMEs but facilitates access to credit through strategic partnerships with banks, NBFCs, and financial institutions. Loan products such as working capital finance, term loans, and overdrafts are offered by partner lenders, with IPPB enabling account verification, transaction history sharing, and digital onboarding to support credit assessment.
application_process: 1. Visit the nearest India Post Payments Bank access point or use the IPPB mobile app. 2. Provide MSME registration details (Udyam Registration Number) and business information. 3. Submit KYC documents of the business and authorized signatory. 4. Complete in-person or video KYC verification. 5. Receive account details and start using digital banking services immediately.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications

overview: Postal Life Insurance (PLI) for MSMEs is a government-backed life insurance scheme offered through India Post, designed to provide affordable insurance coverage to micro, small, and medium enterprises and their employees. It offers various insurance plans with competitive premiums and benefits, aiming to enhance financial security and social welfare within the MSME sector. The scheme leverages the extensive postal network to ensure wide accessibility, especially in semi-urban and rural areas.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; employees of MSMEs
eligibility: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as defined under the MSMED Act, 2006, and their employees (including proprietors, partners, and directors) are eligible to enroll in Postal Life Insurance (PLI) schemes. The scheme is also available to individuals employed in government and semi-government organizations, but under this context, MSME-specific enrollment is facilitated through employer or self-enrollment routes where applicable.
benefits: Financial benefits include life cover on death, maturity benefits, surrender value, and loan facility against policy. Non-financial benefits include tax relief under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, bonus accruals, and peace of mind through risk coverage. Policies offer flexible premium payment options and are backed by the Government of India, ensuring high claim settlement reliability.
financial_support: Postal Life Insurance provides financial support in the form of life insurance proceeds upon death or maturity, surrender value after a minimum lock-in period, and the ability to avail loans up to 80-90% of the surrender value. Premiums are subsidized compared to private market rates, and bonuses are declared periodically by the Government of India, enhancing returns. The exact quantum depends on the plan, sum assured, age, and policy term.
application_process: 1. Visit the nearest post office or access the PLI India portal (pliindia.gov.in). 2. Obtain and fill out the relevant PLI proposal form based on the desired plan (e.g., Whole Life, Endowment, etc.). 3. Submit proof of age, identity, and employment, and address verification documents. 4. Undergo a medical examination if required based on age and sum assured. 5. Pay the initial premium via cash, cheque, or digital mode at the post office. 6. Receive the policy document upon acceptance and premium realization.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications

scheme_name: Kendriya Sainik Board Startup & Entrepreneurship Fund
overview: The Kendriya Sainik Board Startup & Entrepreneurship Fund is a scheme aimed at supporting ex-servicemen (ESM) in establishing startups and entrepreneurial ventures. It provides financial and non-financial assistance to eligible ESMs to promote self-employment and economic rehabilitation. The scheme is implemented under the Armed Forces Flag Day Fund (AFFDF) and targets ex-servicemen, widows, and dependents seeking to launch business initiatives.
target_beneficiaries: ex-servicemen; widows of ex-servicemen; dependents
eligibility: Ex-servicemen (ESM) released/discharged/retired after 01 July 1987 who are in receipt of pension, along with their widows and dependents, are eligible to apply. Applicants must register on the KSB website and provide PPO number, ESM identity card, bank account details linked with Aadhaar, and other required documents as per category.
benefits: Financial support for startup ventures, assistance in business setup, access to entrepreneurial training and mentorship, linkage with government schemes for MSMEs, and support under the Armed Forces Flag Day Fund (AFFDF) for welfare and resettlement.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-based financial support to eligible ex-servicemen for startup and entrepreneurship activities under the Armed Forces Flag Day Fund (AFFDF). The exact quantum, disbursement mechanism, and per-entity limits are not specified in the available evidence.
application_process: 1. Register on the KSB website www.online.ksb.gov.in to obtain login credentials. 2. Log in to the portal using registered email and password. 3. Navigate to the PMSS section and select 'New Application' or 'Startup & Entrepreneurship Fund' as applicable. 4. Fill in the application form with personal, educational, and business details. 5. Upload required documents including ESM/Ex-Coast Guard Certificate, Bonafide Certificate, Bank Manager’s certificate for Aadhaar seeding, mark sheets, bank passbook, and Aadhaar card. 6. Submit the application and save & forward it for processing. 7. Await verification by Zila Sainik Board (ZSB), Rajya Sainik Board (RSB), and Kendriya Sainik Board (KSB) for approval and disbursement.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Kendriya Sainik Board, Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare, Ministry of Defence

scheme_name: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) Hallmarking Scheme
India Post Logistics – e-Commerce Integration Scheme
overview: India Post Logistics – e-Commerce Integration Scheme is a government initiative under the Department of Posts aimed at integrating India Post's extensive logistics network with e-commerce platforms to enhance last-mile delivery, improve supply chain efficiency, and support small and medium enterprises in accessing national and international markets through postal infrastructure.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; e-commerce sellers; startups; rural entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include MSMEs, e-commerce sellers, startups, and rural entrepreneurs engaged in online retail or logistics services who wish to utilize India Post's network for shipping, delivery, and fulfillment services across India.
benefits: Benefits include access to India Post's extensive postal network for reliable and cost-effective shipping, integration with e-commerce platforms for automated order processing, real-time tracking of shipments, cash-on-delivery services, reverse logistics support, warehousing facilities at select post offices, and assistance with customs documentation for international shipments.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial subsidies or grants; instead, it offers logistics services at competitive rates through India Post's existing infrastructure, with pricing based on weight, distance, and service type (e.g., Speed Post, Parcel, Logistics Post).
application_process: 1. Visit the India Post official website or visit a designated post office offering e-commerce logistics services. 2. Register as a business user on the India Post Logistics portal or through the concerned post office. 3. Submit required documents including business registration, GSTIN, PAN, and KYC details. 4. Sign a service agreement outlining terms, rates, and service levels. 5. Integrate your e-commerce platform with India Post's API or use manual booking via portal/post office. 6. Begin shipping orders using India Post's logistics network.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications

scheme_name: Interest Subsidy Scheme for Housing (CLSS under PMAY)
overview: The Interest Subsidy Scheme for Housing (CLSS under PMAY) is a component of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) aimed at providing interest subsidies on home loans to eligible urban beneficiaries. It targets Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Low Income Groups (LIG), and Middle Income Groups (MIG) to facilitate affordable housing through reduced EMI burden. The scheme is implemented via nodal agencies and primary lending institutions (PLIs) across India. Beneficiaries can avail subsidies on loans for purchase, construction, or enhancement of residential properties.
target_beneficiaries: EWS; LIG; MIG; urban beneficiaries
eligibility: Beneficiary families belonging to Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Low Income Groups (LIG), or Middle Income Groups (MIG) as defined under PMAY(U) are eligible. The family should not own a pucca house anywhere in India. The loan must be taken from a PLI for purchase, construction, or enhancement of a house. The beneficiary must not have availed central assistance under any other housing scheme. The property must be located within statutory towns as per Census 2011 or notified planning areas.
benefits: Interest subsidy on home loans up to a maximum tenure of 20 years or loan tenure, whichever is lower. Subsidy is credited upfront to the loan account, reducing EMI burden. Financial support varies by income category: EWS/LIG get 6.5% subsidy on loans up to ₹6 lakh; MIG-I gets 4% on loans up to ₹9 lakh; MIG-II gets 3% on loans up to ₹12 lakh. Subsidy is calculated at net present value (NPV) at a discount rate of 9%. Beneficiaries also gain access to formal credit and improved housing conditions.
financial_support: The scheme provides an interest subsidy credited upfront to the home loan account through Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs). The subsidy amount is calculated as the present value of future interest payments at a discount rate of 9%. For EWS/LIG: 6.5% subsidy on loans up to ₹6,00,000. For MIG-I: 4% subsidy on loans up to ₹9,00,000. For MIG-II: 3% subsidy on loans up to ₹12,00,000. The subsidy is released by the Central Nodal Agency (CNA) to PLIs upon verification of eligible claims. There is no direct cash transfer to beneficiaries; benefit is realized via reduced EMI.
application_process: 1. Identify eligibility based on income category (EWS/LIG/MIG-I/MIG-II) and property location. 2. Approach a Primary Lending Institution (PLI) such as a bank or housing finance company. 3. Submit loan application along with required documents. 4. PLI verifies eligibility and uploads application to the CLSS portal. 5. Central Nodal Agency (CNA) processes the claim and releases subsidy to PLI. 6. PLI credits the subsidy amount to the beneficiary's loan account, reducing the outstanding principal and EMI.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted throughout the year subject to fund availability and scheme guidelines.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

scheme_name: Credit Risk Guarantee Fund Trust for Low Income Housing
overview: The Credit Risk Guarantee Fund Trust for Low Income Housing (CRGFTLIH) is a scheme under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) designed to provide credit guarantee support to lending institutions for extending housing loans to low-income households. It aims to facilitate access to formal credit for economically weaker sections by reducing the risk perceived by banks and financial institutions. The trust operates by offering a guarantee cover on housing loans, thereby encouraging lenders to sanction loans to beneficiaries who may lack conventional collateral or credit history.
target_beneficiaries: low-income households; economically weaker sections
eligibility: The scheme benefits lending institutions (such as banks, housing finance companies, and microfinance institutions) that extend housing loans to individuals belonging to the economically weaker sections (EWS) and low-income groups (LIG) as defined under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban). Beneficiaries must have a valid income certificate, proof of identity, and property documents as per the lending institution's norms and the guidelines of the scheme. Loans must be for housing purposes including construction, purchase, or improvement of a dwelling unit.
benefits: The scheme provides credit guarantee cover to lending institutions, reducing their risk exposure on housing loans to low-income borrowers. This enables lenders to offer collateral-free or low-collateral loans, thereby increasing credit access for underserved populations. The guarantee enhances lenders' confidence to sanction loans to first-time borrowers and those without formal credit history, supporting financial inclusion in the housing sector.
financial_support: The Credit Risk Guarantee Fund Trust for Low Income Housing provides a guarantee cover on housing loans sanctioned by lending institutions to eligible beneficiaries. The guarantee is typically a percentage of the loan amount, covering a portion of the default risk, and is activated upon classification of the loan as a non-performing asset (NPA). The exact guarantee percentage and loan coverage limits are determined by the trust's operational guidelines and are subject to periodic review.
application_process: 1. Lending institutions identify eligible beneficiaries under EWS/LIG categories as per PMAY(U) guidelines. 2. Sanction housing loans for construction, purchase, or improvement of dwelling units. 3. Submit loan details to the Credit Risk Guarantee Fund Trust for Low Income Housing for guarantee coverage. 4. The trust evaluates the loan proposal based on beneficiary eligibility and loan-to-value ratio. 5. Upon approval, the trust issues a guarantee cover certificate to the lending institution. 6. The lending institution disburses the loan to the beneficiary. 7. In case of default, the lending institution can invoke the guarantee by submitting a claim to the trust with required documentation. 8. The trust processes the claim and reimburses the lending institution as per the guarantee terms.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

overview: The National Intellectual Property Awareness Mission (NIPAM) is a flagship program launched by the Government of India to promote intellectual property (IP) awareness and education across the country. It aims to inculcate the spirit of creativity and innovation among students, faculty, and innovators in higher educational institutions and schools. The mission provides training and capacity-building programs on various aspects of IP rights, including patents, trademarks, copyrights, and designs. NIPAM is implemented by the Intellectual Property Office, India under the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM).
target_beneficiaries: students; faculty; innovators; educational institutions
eligibility: Students, faculty members, and innovators from recognized higher educational institutions (universities, colleges) and schools across India are eligible to participate in NIPAM training programs. Institutions must register to host or participate in the awareness sessions conducted under the mission.
benefits: Participants gain foundational knowledge of intellectual property rights, including patents, trademarks, copyrights, and designs. The program enhances awareness about the importance of IP in innovation, entrepreneurship, and economic development. It provides training on IP processes, procedures, and benefits, helping individuals and institutions protect their innovations. NIPAM also encourages a culture of creativity and supports the national goal of strengthening India’s IP ecosystem.
financial_support: NIPAM does not provide direct financial support, grants, or subsidies to beneficiaries. The program is focused on awareness, training, and capacity building in the field of intellectual property rights. All training sessions and educational resources are provided free of cost to eligible participants and institutions.
application_process: 1. Educational institutions interested in participating in NIPAM must register on the official NIPAM portal. 2. After registration, institutions can schedule IP awareness sessions for their students and faculty. 3. Sessions are conducted by trained resource persons or IP officials either virtually or in person, as per mutual convenience. 4. Participants attend the training sessions covering various aspects of IPR. 5. Upon completion, participants may receive certificates of participation issued by the Intellectual Property Office, India.
deadlines: Rolling basis — institutions can apply throughout the year based on availability of resource persons and scheduling convenience.
implementing_agency: Intellectual Property Office, India, Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: DigiGaon – Rural Digital Hub via Post Offices
overview: DigiGaon – Rural Digital Hub via Post Offices is a scheme under the Department of Posts that leverages India Post's extensive rural network to establish digital hubs in villages, providing access to digital services, e-governance, financial inclusion, and skill development through post offices transformed into common service centers.
target_beneficiaries: rural citizens; villagers; MSME; entrepreneurs
eligibility: The scheme is implemented through selected post offices in rural areas; specific eligibility criteria for beneficiaries are not detailed in the provided evidence.
benefits: Access to digital services, e-governance, banking, insurance, skill development, and entrepreneurship support via post office networks; promotes financial inclusion and rural development.
financial_support: The evidence does not specify financial support mechanisms, quantum, or funding details for the DigiGaon scheme.
application_process: The evidence does not provide a step-by-step application process for the DigiGaon scheme.
implementing_agency: Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications

scheme_name: HUDCO Loan Scheme for Affordable Housing Projects
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS-MIG)
overview: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS-MIG) is a component of the PMAY-Urban mission aimed at providing interest subsidies on home loans to Middle Income Group (MIG) beneficiaries for the acquisition or construction of houses. It targets MIG-I and MIG-II categories with annual household incomes between ₹6 lakh and ₹18 lakh. The scheme offers an interest subsidy on home loans taken from banks, housing finance companies, and other such institutions. The subsidy is credited upfront to the loan account, reducing the effective loan burden and EMI outflow for the beneficiary.
target_beneficiaries: Middle Income Group (MIG); MIG-I; MIG-II
eligibility: Beneficiaries belonging to Middle Income Group (MIG) with annual household income between ₹6,00,001 and ₹12,00,000 (MIG-I) or between ₹12,00,001 and ₹18,00,000 (MIG-II). The beneficiary family should not own a pucca house (an all-weather dwelling unit) in any part of India. The scheme applies to first-time homebuyers. The house being purchased or constructed must be located in a statutory town as per Census 2011 or in a planning area notified with respect to such towns.
benefits: Interest subsidy on home loans at the rate of 4% for MIG-I (loan amount up to ₹9 lakh) and 3% for MIG-II (loan amount up to ₹12 lakh). The subsidy is calculated on the net present value (NPV) basis and credited upfront to the loan account. Maximum subsidy amount is ₹2.35 lakh for MIG-I and ₹2.30 lakh for MIG-II. The benefit reduces the effective loan amount and EMI burden. The scheme is implemented through nodal agencies and primary lending institutions (PLIs) such as banks and HFCs.
financial_support: The scheme provides an interest subsidy rather than a direct loan or grant. For MIG-I, 4% interest subsidy on loan amounts up to ₹9 lakh; for MIG-II, 3% interest subsidy on loan amounts up to ₹12 lakh. The subsidy is computed as the net present value (NPV) of future interest payments discounted at 9% and credited upfront to the loan account. The maximum subsidy amount is capped at ₹2.35 lakh for MIG-I and ₹2.30 lakh for MIG-II. The actual loan amount can exceed these limits, but subsidy is calculated only on the specified cap. The subsidy is released to the primary lending institution (PLI) which then credits it to the beneficiary’s loan account.
application_process: 1. Identify a primary lending institution (PLI) such as a bank or housing finance company participating in CLSS under PMAY-U. 2. Apply for a home loan with the PLI for the purchase or construction of a house. 3. Submit required documents including income proof, identity proof, address proof, and property details. 4. The PLI checks eligibility under CLSS-MIG based on income and other criteria. 5. If eligible, the PLI includes the subsidy claim in the loan application and forwards it to the nodal agency (e.g., HUDCO, NHB). 6. Upon approval, the nodal agency releases the subsidy amount to the PLI. 7. The PLI credits the subsidy upfront to the beneficiary’s loan account, reducing the outstanding principal. 8. The beneficiary repays the loan based on the reduced principal amount.
deadlines: The scheme was operational till March 31, 2021, for MIG-I and MIG-II categories under PMAY-U. No further extensions have been announced in the provided evidence. Applications are no longer being accepted under this vertical as of the cutoff date.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

overview: The APEDA HACCP & Organic Certification Support scheme provides financial and technical assistance to exporters and processors for obtaining HACCP and organic certifications to enhance export competitiveness and compliance with international standards. The scheme supports quality development initiatives under APEDA's Financial Assistance Schemes (FAS) for the 15th Finance Commission cycle (2021-22 to 2025-26). It aims to improve product safety, traceability, and market access for agricultural and processed food products.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; exporters; processors; agri-startups
eligibility: Exporters and processors of APEDA-scheduled products who are registered with APEDA and possess a valid Import-Export Code (IEC) are eligible to apply for financial assistance under the scheme for HACCP and organic certification.
benefits: Financial support for certification costs, technical guidance on compliance requirements, improved market access for certified products, enhanced brand reputation, and facilitation of export promotion activities.
financial_support: Under the Financial Assistance Schemes (FAS), APEDA provides subsidy support for certification expenses, including HACCP and organic certification, as part of its Quality Development initiative. The exact quantum and mechanism are detailed in the FAS guidelines for the 15th Finance Commission cycle (2021-22 to 2025-26).
application_process: 1. Register as an exporter with APEDA to obtain Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC). 2. Ensure possession of valid Import-Export Code (IEC) from DGFT. 3. Apply for financial assistance under APEDA's Financial Assistance Schemes (FAS) for Quality Development. 4. Submit required documents including CA-certified financials, IEC, RCMC, and project proposal for certification. 5. Await approval and disbursement of subsidy upon successful certification.
deadlines: As per the Financial Assistance Schemes (FAS) guidelines for the 15th Finance Commission cycle (2021-22 to 2025-26); specific dates are announced periodically.
implementing_agency: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: MSME SAMADHAAN is a Delayed Payment Monitoring System designed to help Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) track and resolve delayed payments from buyers, including government departments and public sector undertakings. The system enables MSMEs to file complaints online regarding delayed payments and facilitates conciliation and arbitration through the Arbitration & Conciliation Centre for MSMEs. It aims to ensure timely payment realization and reduce financial stress on MSMEs by providing a digital platform for grievance redressal.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Any Micro, Small, or Medium Enterprise (MSME) registered under the MSME Act, 2006, facing delayed payments from buyers including central government departments, state governments, public sector undertakings, or private companies, is eligible to file a complaint through the SAMADHAAN portal.
benefits: Online filing of delayed payment complaints, tracking of complaint status, facilitation of conciliation and arbitration processes, access to the Arbitration & Conciliation Centre for MSMEs, and support in realizing delayed payments through a structured grievance redressal mechanism.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Instead, it offers procedural and institutional support to help MSMEs recover delayed payments through legal and administrative channels, including conciliation and arbitration.
application_process: 1. Visit the SAMADHAAN portal at https://samadhaan.msme.gov.in 2. Register as an MSME by providing Udyam Registration details 3. Log in to the portal using credentials 4. File a complaint by entering buyer details, invoice information, and amount due 5. Submit the complaint for processing 6. Track the status of the complaint through the portal 7. Await conciliation or arbitration proceedings as initiated by the Arbitration & Conciliation Centre for MSMEs.
deadlines: Rolling basis — complaints can be filed at any time as there is no fixed deadline.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

scheme_name: NHB Refinance Schemes for Housing Finance Companies
overview: The NHB Refinance Schemes for Housing Finance Companies provide financial support to primary lending institutions (PLIs) by extending refinance against eligible housing loans extended to individual borrowers. The scheme aims to augment resources for the housing finance sector and make housing credit more affordable. It operates under various sub-schemes including the Affordable Housing Fund (AHF), Special Refinance Facility (SRF), and Regular Refinance facilities. The Bank also provides direct finance to public housing agencies for large-scale integrated housing projects.
target_beneficiaries: Housing Finance Companies (HFCs); Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs); Public housing agencies
eligibility: Primary lending institutions (PLIs) in respect of eligible housing loans extended by them to individual borrowers. Public housing agencies such as State Level Housing Boards and Area Development Authorities for large scale integrated housing. The scheme operates under various sub-schemes with specific eligibility criteria for each.
benefits: Provides refinance and direct finance to lending institutions. Augments resources for the housing finance sector. Makes housing credit more affordable. Supports promotion of a sound and viable housing finance system. Enables supervision of HFCs. Facilitates public agency participation in housing finance.
financial_support: NHB extends financial support through refinance and direct finance to a large set of lending institutions. Refinance is provided under various schemes including Affordable Housing Fund (AHF), Special Refinance Facility (SRF), and Regular Refinance facilities. During FY 2024-25, under AHF scheme, refinance assistance of ₹5,790.90 crore was extended to PLIs for individual housing loans to 36,300 households. During FY 2024-25, ₹2,055 crore was disbursed under Fixed Rate Refinance. As of June 2025, the outstanding refinance portfolio stood at ₹1,07,913 crore.
application_process: 1. Primary lending institutions (PLIs) extend eligible housing loans to individual borrowers. 2. PLIs approach NHB for refinance against these eligible housing loans. 3. NHB verifies the eligibility of loans and the lending institution. 4. NHB sanctions refinance amount based on the scheme guidelines. 5. Disbursement of refinance funds to the PLI's account. 6. PLI utilizes the funds for further lending to individual borrowers.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: National Housing Bank (NHB)

scheme_name: Startup Legal Facilitation – Virtual Courts for IP Disputes
overview: The Scheme of Action Research and Studies on Judicial Reforms is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice, Government of India. It provides financial assistance in the form of grants to universities, law schools, research institutions, and other eligible entities for undertaking research projects on judicial reforms, access to justice, ease of doing business, and related themes. The scheme aims to generate evidence-based policy inputs for judicial reforms and strengthen the research ecosystem in the legal domain.
target_beneficiaries: universities; law schools; research institutions; NGOs; individual researchers
eligibility: Universities, law schools, research institutions, NGOs, and individual researchers based in India are eligible to apply for grants under the Scheme of Action Research and Studies on Judicial Reforms, subject to the terms of the agreement and approval by the Department of Justice.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grants-in-aid for approved research projects, disbursed in instalments based on project milestones, with funding typically covering up to 100% of the sanctioned project cost.
financial_support: Grants are released in instalments (e.g., 20%, 40%, 30% or similar tranches) based on project progress and submission of utilization certificates, as per the terms of the agreement signed with the implementing agency, with payments made through e-payment to the beneficiary's account.
application_process: 1. Submit a research proposal under the Scheme of Action Research and Studies on Judicial Reforms to the Department of Justice. 2. Obtain approval of the proposal from the Competent Authority. 3. Sign an agreement with the Department of Justice outlining terms, budget, and timeline. 4. Receive instalments of the sanctioned grant upon completion of milestones and submission of required documents. 5. Submit utilization certificates and progress reports as per the agreement.
implementing_agency: Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice, Government of India

scheme_name: IP India – Patent Filing Fee Reduction for Startups
overview: The IP India – Patent Filing Fee Reduction for Startups scheme provides a 50% reduction in patent filing fees for startups and small entities under Section 54 of the Patents Act, 1970, as part of the government's effort to promote innovation and reduce the cost of intellectual property protection for early-stage ventures. The scheme is administered by the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM) under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Eligible applicants include startups, small entities, educational institutions, and natural persons filing patent applications in India. The fee reduction applies to various stages of the patent process, including application filing, request for examination, and renewal, with specific fee structures outlined in the First Schedule of the Patents Rules, 2003.
target_beneficiaries: startups; small entity; educational institution; natural person
eligibility: Eligible applicants include natural persons, startups, small entities, or educational institutions filing patent applications in India. The fee reduction under Section 54 of the Patents Act, 1970 applies when the applicant is a natural person, startup, small entity, or educational institution, either alone or in combination with others. The applicant must specify their category in Form 1 under 'Category of Applicant' by ticking the appropriate box (Natural Person, Startup, Small Entity, Educational Institution).
benefits: The primary benefit is a 50% reduction in statutory fees for various patent-related procedures as specified in the First Schedule of the Patents Rules, 2003. This includes reduced fees for filing a patent application (Form 1), request for examination (Form 18), request for expedited examination (Form 18A), patent renewal, and other procedural steps. For example, the fee for filing a patent application is reduced from ₹1600 to ₹800 for natural persons/startups/small entities/educational institutions, and from ₹8000 to ₹4000 for others. Similar reductions apply to examination requests (₹4000 to ₹2000), renewal fees, and other formalities, significantly lowering the overall cost of obtaining and maintaining a patent in India.
financial_support: The scheme provides a 50% fee concession on statutory payments under the Patents Rules, 2003 for eligible applicants. The reduction is applied directly at the time of fee payment via the e-filing portal or physical submission, with no intermediary disbursement. The applicant pays the reduced fee as per the First Schedule, which outlines separate fee structures for 'Natural person or startup or small entity or educational institution' versus 'Other(s)'. For instance, the base fee for filing a patent application (Form 1) is ₹800 for eligible entities versus ₹1600 for others, and the request for examination (Form 18) is ₹2000 versus ₹4000. The concession is automatic upon correct categorization in the application form and does not require separate approval or funding allocation.
application_process: 1. Determine eligibility as a natural person, startup, small entity, or educational institution under the Patents Act, 1970. 2. Complete Form 1 (Application for Grant of Patent) and tick the appropriate category under 'Category of Applicant'. 3. Prepare and attach required documents including Form 2 (Provisional/Complete Specification), Form 3 (Statement and Undertaking under Section 8), Form 5 (Declaration as to Inventorship), and others as applicable. 4. Calculate the reduced fee based on the First Schedule of the Patents Rules, 2003 for the selected category. 5. File the application online via the IP India e-filing portal (https://ipindia.gov.in) or submit physically at the appropriate patent office. 6. Pay the prescribed reduced fee through online banking, UPI, cheque, demand draft, or cash, or demand draft. 7. Submit the application and await acknowledgment and further processing by the Patent Office.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
contact_details: Email: cgoffice[dot]in[at]gov[dot]in | Phone: 011-28034302 (Director, Administration and Establishment) | Helpdesk: Available via IP India portal

overview: The Fast-Track Trademark Registration for Startups is a scheme under the Intellectual Property India portal that provides expedited trademark registration services specifically for startups. The scheme is part of the broader Startup India initiative and aims to reduce the time and cost associated with trademark registration for early-stage ventures. It leverages the e-filing system and offers facilitation through registered trademark agents and facilitators under the SIPP scheme.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: The scheme is available to startups recognized by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Startup India initiative. Eligible entities must be incorporated as a private limited company, registered partnership firm, or limited liability partnership (LLP), have been in existence for less than 10 years, and have an annual turnover not exceeding INR 100 crore in any preceding financial year.
benefits: Startups benefit from expedited examination of trademark applications, reduced official fees for trademark filing (as per the First Schedule of the Patents Rules, 2003, which provides fee concessions for natural persons, startups, small entities, and educational institutions), access to free facilitation services under the SIPP (Scheme for Facilitating Startups Intellectual Property Protection), and guidance through the trademark application workflow via the IP India portal. The scheme also provides access to e-filing facilities, tracking of application status, and support for responding to examination reports.
financial_support: Under the SIPP scheme, the government bears the fees of the facilitator, and the startup only needs to pay the statutory government fees for trademark filing. For startups, the official fee for filing a trademark application (Form TM-A) is reduced: INR 4,500 for e-filing and INR 5,000 for physical filing, as opposed to the standard fee of INR 9,000 (e-filing) and INR 10,000 (physical filing) for other applicants. This represents a 50% fee concession.
application_process: 1. Ensure the startup is recognized by DPIIT under the Startup India initiative. 2. Access the IP India portal at https://ipindia.gov.in. 3. Conduct a trademark search using the 'Search Existing Trademarks' tool. 4. Prepare the trademark application (Form TM-A) with details of the mark, goods/services (classified under Nice Classification), and applicant information. 5. Login to the e-filing portal via the 'Comprehensive e-Filing Services' section. 6. Upload the completed Form TM-A and supporting documents (such as user affidavit, if applicable, and power of attorney if filed through an agent). 7. Pay the prescribed fee online (INR 4,500 for startups for e-filing). 8. Submit the application and track its status using the 'Track Application Status' facility. 9. Respond to any examination reports or objections within the stipulated time. 10. Upon acceptance, the trademark will be published in the Trade Marks Journal for opposition. 11. If no opposition is filed within 4 months, the trademark proceeds to registration and a registration certificate is issued.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) 2.0 is a government scheme aimed at incentivizing employers to generate new employment by paying the employer's contribution to the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) for new employees. The scheme encourages job creation in the formal sector by reducing the financial burden on employers for social security contributions. It targets establishments registered with EPFO and ESIC that hire new workers earning up to a specified wage ceiling.
target_beneficiaries: employers; establishments; new employees
eligibility: Employers/establishments registered with EPFO and ESIC are eligible if they hire new employees with a monthly wage of up to INR 15,000. The new employee must not have been employed in any EPFO-registered establishment prior to 1st April 2021, and the employer must have remitted EPFO and ESIC contributions for the new employee for the first three months.
benefits: The government pays the employer's contribution of 12% towards EPFO and 3.25% towards ESIC (total 15.25%) for a period of three years from the date of registration of the new employee. This reduces the employer's outlay on statutory social security contributions. Employees gain access to social security benefits including provident fund, pension, and medical coverage.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support by reimbursing the employer's share of EPFO (12%) and ESIC (3.25%) contributions, amounting to 15.25% of the monthly wage (capped at INR 15,000) for each eligible new employee for a duration of three years. The support is disbursed directly to the employer's EPFO account after verification of contribution remittance.
application_process: 1. Register the establishment on the EPFO portal if not already registered. 2. Ensure the new employee is registered with EPFO and ESIC and has a Universal Account Number (UAN). 3. Remit the employer's and employee's contributions to EPFO and ESIC for the first three months. 4. Apply for reimbursement through the EPFO employer portal by submitting the required details of the new employee and contribution proof. 5. The EPFO verifies the eligibility and credits the government's share of the employer's contribution to the employer's EPFO account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted as long as the employee remains eligible under the scheme conditions.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Labour and Employment

overview: The Copyright Societies Support Scheme is a framework under the Copyright Act, 1957 for the registration, regulation, and support of copyright societies in India. It enables collective administration of copyright by societies formed by authors and other owners of rights to manage licensing, fee collection, and royalty distribution. The scheme ensures transparency, accountability, and fair distribution of royalties while promoting the interests of creators and users of copyrighted works.
target_beneficiaries: authors; other owners of rights; copyright societies; right holders
eligibility: A copyright society is formed by authors and other owners of rights. The minimum membership required for registration of a society is seven. Ordinarily, only one society is registered to do business in respect of the same class of work. The registration is granted for a period of five years and may be renewed subject to continued collective control by authors and owners of rights.
benefits: Copyright societies can issue or grant licences, collect fees, and distribute royalties after deducting administrative expenses (not exceeding 15%). They can enter into agreements with foreign societies for cross-border royalty collection. Members receive regular, full, and detailed information about activities. Royalties are distributed in proportion to actual use of works. Societies are subject to collective control by authors and owners of rights regarding fee collection, distribution, and utilisation.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support or grants to copyright societies. Financial operations are self-sustained through licensing fees and royalty collections. Administrative expenses are capped at 15% of collections. No government fund size or per-entity grant amount is specified in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Form a society with authors and other owners of rights (minimum seven members). 2. Prepare application for registration under Section 33 of the Copyright Act, 1957. 3. Submit application to the Registrar of Copyrights. 4. Await examination and potential objections from the Copyright Office. 5. If approved, receive registration certificate valid for five years. 6. For renewal, submit application before expiry with report from Registrar of Copyrights. 7. Maintain required registers and file annual returns. 8. Adhere to tariff and distribution schemes as per Copyright Rules, 2013.
deadlines: Registration is valid for five years and must be renewed before expiry. Renewal applications must be submitted in prescribed form before the end of every five-year period. Annual returns must be filed within one month from the date of conclusion of each annual General Body meeting.
implementing_agency: Copyright Office, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (ABVKY) is a welfare measure for employees covered under Section 2(9) of ESI Act, 1948, providing relief payment up to 90 days once in a lifetime. Introduced on a pilot basis from 01-07-2018, the scheme has been extended up to 30 June 2024, with enhanced benefits including unemployment relief at 50% of wages (up from 25%) and relaxed eligibility conditions. Claims can be submitted online at www.esic.gov.in along with physical submission of affidavit, Aadhaar copy, and bank details to the designated ESIC Branch Office/DCBO.
target_beneficiaries: employees covered under Section 2(9) of ESI Act, 1948
eligibility: The Insured Person should have been in insurable employment for a minimum period of one year immediately before her/his unemployment and should have contributed for not less than 78 days in the completed contribution period in 12 months immediately prior to unemployment.
benefits: Relief payment up to 90 days once in a lifetime at 50% of wages (enhanced from 25%), relief becomes due for payment after 30 days from date of unemployment, claim can be submitted online at www.esic.gov.in along with physical submission of affidavit, photocopy of Aadhaar Card and Bank Account details to the designated ESIC Branch Office/DCBO by post or in person.
financial_support: The scheme provides relief payment at the rate of 50% of wages for a maximum period of 90 days once in a lifetime. The enhanced benefit and relaxed conditions are applicable up to 30 June 2024.
application_process: 1. Make claim online at the website www.esic.gov.in 2. Submit physical claim with an affidavit, photocopy of Aadhaar Card and Bank Account details 3. Submit to the designated ESIC Branch Office / DCBO by post or in person.
deadlines: The enhanced benefit and relaxed conditions are applicable upto 30 th June, 2024.
implementing_agency: Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC)

scheme_name: ESIC Health Insurance Scheme for MSME Workers
overview: The Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) Health Insurance Scheme for MSME Workers provides comprehensive social security benefits to insured persons and their families under the ESI Act, 1948. It offers medical, sickness, maternity, disablement, dependents, and other benefits including funeral expenses and vocational rehabilitation. The scheme is a self-financing health insurance program funded by contributions from employees and employers.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; workers; employees; insured persons
eligibility: The ESI Act is applicable to all non-seasonal factories employing 10 or more persons. State Governments have extended coverage to shops, hotels, restaurants, cinemas, road-motor transport, newspaper establishments, private medical institutions, educational institutions, and contract/casual employees of Municipal Corporations employing 10 or more persons. The Central Government has extended coverage to shops, hotels, restaurants, road motor transport, cinemas, newspaper establishments, insurance business establishments, non-banking financial companies, port trust, airport authorities, and warehousing establishments employing 20 or more persons. The existing wage limit for coverage under the Act, effective from 01.01.2017, is Rs.21,000/- per month (Rs.25,000/- per month for persons with disability). Employees earning up to Rs.176/- per day are exempted from payment of their share of contribution.
benefits: Medical Benefit: Full medical care with no ceiling on expenditure. Sickness Benefit: Cash compensation at 70% of wages for up to 91 days/year (extendable to two years for 34 malignant diseases at 80% wages). Enhanced Sickness Benefit: Full wage for sterilization (7 days vasectomy, 14 days tubectomy). Maternity Benefit: Full wage for 26 weeks extendable by one month. Temporary Disablement Benefit: 90% of wage during disability. Permanent Disablement Benefit: 90% of wage as monthly payment. Dependants Benefit: 90% of wage as monthly payment. Funeral Expenses: Rs.15,000/-. Confinement Expenses: For insured women or IP's wife when medical facilities unavailable. Vocational Rehabilitation: For permanently disabled insured persons. Physical Rehabilitation: For physical disablement due to employment injury. Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana: Unemployment allowance at 50% of wage for up to two years, medical care, vocational training. Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana: Relief payment up to 90 days, once in a lifetime, enhanced to 50% of wages with one-year insurable employment and 78 days contribution in 12 months prior to unemployment, claim after 30 days of unemployment.
financial_support: ESI Scheme is a self-financing health insurance scheme. Contributions are raised from covered employees and employers as a fixed percentage of wages. Employees contribute 0.75% of wages, employers contribute 3.25% of wages. Employees earning up to Rs.176/- per day are exempted from employee contribution, but employers still contribute their share. State Governments contribute 1/8th of medical benefit expenditure within a per capita ceiling of Rs.1500/- per insured person per annum. Additional expenditure by State Governments over the ceiling is borne by them.
application_process: 1. Employer registers online via ESIC portal without physical documents. 2. Employer submits information in online screens; code number generated automatically. 3. Registration letter (C-11) sent to employer's email along with user credentials. 4. Employer logs in to ESIC website using credentials. 5. For manpower suppliers, security agencies, contractors: pay advance contribution for six months calculated as (number of employees earning up to Rs.21000/month) × minimum wages × 6 × 6.5%. 6. Advance contribution paid online; registration documents sent after bank confirmation (1 day for SBI, 2 days for other banks).
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Employees' State Insurance Corporation, Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India
contact_details: Email: ITCare[at]esic[dot]nic[dot]in or help-shramsuvidha[at]gov[dot]in | Phone: 011-27552237 (IT), 011-23354722 (Shram Suvidha), 1800113839 (Medical), 1800112526 (General) | Grievances: pg-hqrs[at]esic[dot]nic[dot]in

overview: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme launched by the Government of India for old age protection and social security of unorganized workers. It provides an assured monthly pension of Rs. 3000/- after attaining the age of 60 years, with matching contributions from the government. The scheme also includes a National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed persons with similar benefits.
target_beneficiaries: unorganized workers; self-employed persons; traders; street vendors; home-based workers; agricultural workers; construction workers
eligibility: For Unorganized Workers (UW): Entry age between 18 to 40 years, monthly income up to Rs 15000/-, should not be engaged in organized sector (member of EPFO/NPS/ESIC), should not be an income tax payer, must possess Aadhaar card and savings bank account/Jana Dhan account with IFSC. For self-employed shop owners, retail owners and other vyaparis: Entry age between 18 to 40 years, annual turnover should not exceed Rs 1.5 crore, should not be covered under any National Pension Scheme contributed by the Central Government or member of EPFO/NPS/ESIC, must be an income tax payer, enrolled under PM-SYM or PM-Kisan Maandhan, and possess Aadhaar card and savings bank account with IFSC.
benefits: Assured monthly pension of Rs. 3000/- after attaining age 60; family pension of 50% of the pension amount to spouse upon beneficiary's death; voluntary and contributory pension scheme with matching contribution by the Government of India; no administrative cost to beneficiary; nomination facility available; option to continue scheme by spouse in case of beneficiary's death before pension start; refund of member's contribution with interest if spouse opts out.
financial_support: The scheme is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme where beneficiaries make monthly contributions ranging from Rs 55 to Rs 200 based on entry age, and the Government of India provides an equal matching contribution. The total monthly contribution (beneficiary + government) ranges from Rs 110 to Rs 400 as per the contribution chart. The pension amount of Rs. 3000/- per month is paid from the accumulated corpus after age 60.
application_process: 1. Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or access the online portal. 2. Provide Aadhaar card and savings bank account/Jana Dhan account details with IFSC. 3. Self-certify eligibility regarding age, income, and non-coverage under statutory social security schemes. 4. Fill out the enrollment form and provide consent for auto-debit facility. 5. Make the first contribution in cash at the CSC. 6. Subsequent contributions can be made via auto-debit, quarterly, half-yearly, or yearly modes. 7. Upon successful enrollment, receive a laminated colour scheme-card and acknowledgment receipt.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Labour & Employment
