scheme_name: Fixed Term Employment (FTE) Scheme for MSMEs
overview: The Fixed Term Employment (FTE) Scheme for MSMEs is a policy initiative under the Ministry of Labour & Employment aimed at providing flexibility in hiring for micro, small, and medium enterprises by allowing them to employ workers on a fixed-term basis without the obligation of permanent employment. The scheme seeks to enhance employment opportunities while ensuring certain protections for fixed-term workers, including parity in wages, working conditions, and statutory benefits with regular employees performing similar work. It is designed to support MSMEs in managing fluctuating demand and seasonal operations while promoting formalization of labor contracts.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: The scheme applies to all MSMEs as defined under the MSMED Act, 2006, engaged in manufacturing or service activities. Fixed-term employees under this scheme must be engaged for a specific duration or project, and their employment terms must not be less favorable than those of regular employees performing similar work in terms of wages, working hours, allowances, and statutory benefits such as EPFO, ESIC, and gratuity eligibility.
benefits: Fixed-term employees under the scheme are entitled to equal pay for equal work, same working hours, allowances, and statutory benefits including Employees' Provident Fund (EPFO), Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), and eligibility for gratuity after five years of continuous service. Employers benefit from reduced long-term liability, flexibility in workforce management, and compliance with labor laws through formal contracts. The scheme also promotes social security coverage for workers who might otherwise be in informal arrangements.
financial_support: The Fixed Term Employment Scheme does not involve direct financial subsidies or grants to employers or employees. Instead, it provides regulatory flexibility by allowing fixed-term contracts under labor laws, thereby reducing indirect costs associated with permanent hiring, such as long-term liabilities and complex termination procedures. Financial obligations such as wages, EPFO, and ESIC contributions remain the responsibility of the employer as per standard labor regulations.
application_process: 1. MSMEs must identify the need for fixed-term employment based on project or seasonal requirements. 2. Employers must draft a fixed-term employment contract specifying duration, role, remuneration, and benefits in compliance with the scheme guidelines. 3. The contract must ensure parity in wages and benefits with regular employees performing similar work. 4. Employers must register the fixed-term employee with EPFO and ESIC as applicable. 5. Maintain records of employment, wages, and contributions for inspection. 6. Ensure compliance with labor inspections and audits under the Ministry of Labour & Employment.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications or contract registrations can be made throughout the year as per business needs.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Labour and Employment

scheme_name: GST Composition Scheme for Small Businesses
overview: The GST Composition Scheme is a simplified tax scheme under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime designed for small businesses to reduce compliance burden. It allows eligible taxpayers to pay GST at a fixed rate on their turnover instead of the normal GST rates, with simplified return filing and record-keeping requirements. The scheme aims to support small traders, manufacturers, and service providers by lowering their tax liability and procedural complexities.
target_beneficiaries: small businesses; traders; manufacturers; service providers; MSME
eligibility: Taxpayers whose aggregate annual turnover in the preceding financial year did not exceed Rs. 1.5 crore (Rs. 75 lakh for special category states) are eligible. The scheme is available to manufacturers, traders, and restaurants (not serving alcohol). Service providers (except restaurant services) are not eligible unless their service component is part of mixed supply and does not exceed specified limits. Taxpayers must not be engaged in inter-state supply, e-commerce operations, or supply of non-taxable goods.
benefits: Lower tax rates (1% for manufacturers and traders, 5% for restaurants, 6% for service providers under special provisions), quarterly return filing (GSTR-4) instead of monthly, simplified compliance, reduced need for detailed invoicing and input tax credit tracking, and exemption from maintaining elaborate records. Tax is paid at a fixed rate on turnover without the complexity of input tax credit reversal.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support but offers indirect financial benefit through reduced tax outflow. Tax is calculated as a fixed percentage of turnover (1% for traders and manufacturers, 5% for restaurants, 6% for certain service providers), which is generally lower than the effective GST rate under normal scheme, resulting in cash flow improvement for small businesses.
application_process: 1. Log in to the GST portal (https://www.gst.gov.in). 2. Navigate to Services > Registration > Application for Composition Scheme. 3. Fill in Form CMP-02 to opt for the composition scheme. 4. Provide details such as business type, turnover, and bank account information. 5. Submit the application electronically. 6. Upon approval, the taxpayer can start paying tax under the composition scheme from the beginning of the next quarter.
deadlines: Applications can be filed at the beginning of each financial year or within 30 days of obtaining GST registration. Once opted, the scheme continues until voluntarily withdrawn or until eligibility criteria are violated.
implementing_agency: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) under the guidance of the GST Council and Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)

scheme_name: National Career Service (NCS) Portal – MSME Hiring
overview: National Career Service (NCS) Portal – one-stop destination that provides a one-stop destination that provides a host of career-related services such as dynamic job matching, career-related services such as dynamic job matching, career counselling, job notifications, vocational guidance, information on skill development courses, internships and alike. A national portal (www.ncs.gov.in) is operational and provides a nation-wide platform to connect job seekers and employers.
target_beneficiaries: jobseekers; employers; MSME
eligibility: Any Jobseeker can register itself on NCS Portal by following the below mentioned steps: Visit www.ncs.gov.in, The Home Page will be displayed - Click on New User? Sign Up button on right side of the Home Page. - Select the Jobseeker option from the “Register As” drop-down. This displays the employer user registration screen. - Fill the complete Registration Form basic details along with Unique Identification Number (either of Pan card, Voter’s Identity Card, Passport, Driving License, or UAN Number) - After successful registration, an OTP will be sent to the registered mobile number. Use the same OTP for successful verification - After entering the OTP, Click on Submit button and the account will been created successfully.
benefits: NCS offers two kinds of profiles for Jobseekers (i) Detailed Profile: For Jobseekers with qualification above class 12th (ii) Short Profile: For Jobseekers with qualification below class 12th. Once registered on NCS Portal, the Job seeker should update profile to get Job recommendations and noticed by Employers for relevant openings. - Click on “View/Update NCS Profile” in left navigation panel and update profile (i) Detailed Profile - Personal information, Physical Attributes, Communication, Education and Training, Experience, Other Skills, My references, Preferences all the tabs need to be updated (ii) Short Profile - Only needs to update Personal Information and Communication Tabs - Upload relevant documents under each tab using “DigiLocker connect” Link. Jobseekers who are already registered on DigiLocker , can sign in using existing credentials and those who do not have DigiLocker account can sign up using Mobile no. or Aadhaar no. - Once successfully registered on DigiLocker, NCS will take consent to share certificates with NCS reg
application_process: 1. Visit www.ncs.gov.in, The Home Page will be displayed 2. Click on New User? Sign Up button on right side of the Home Page. 3. Select the Jobseeker option from the “Register As” drop-down. This displays the employer user registration screen. 4. Fill the complete Registration Form basic details along with Unique Identification Number (either of Pan card, Voter’s Identity Card, Passport, Driving License, or UAN Number) 5. After successful registration, an OTP will be sent to the registered mobile number. Use the same OTP for successful verification 6. After entering the OTP, Click on Submit button and the account will been created successfully.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Employment, MINISTRY OF LABOUR

scheme_name: Input Tax Credit (ITC) Automation for MSMEs
overview: Input Tax Credit (ITC) Automation for MSMEs is a GST initiative aimed at streamlining the ITC claim process for micro, small, and medium enterprises through automation and digital tools. The scheme seeks to reduce manual intervention, minimize errors, and accelerate ITC processing by leveraging technology on the GST portal. It supports MSMEs in improving cash flow by ensuring timely and accurate ITC utilization. The initiative is part of broader GST reforms to enhance compliance and ease of doing business.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSMEs registered under the GST Act with valid GSTIN and engaged in the supply of goods or services, subject to compliance with ITC rules under Section 16 of the CGST Act, including possession of tax invoices, receipt of goods/services, and payment of tax to the government.
benefits: Faster ITC processing, reduced compliance burden, improved accuracy in ITC claims, enhanced transparency in credit utilization, better working capital management, and integration with GSTN systems for seamless return filing.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support but facilitates indirect financial benefits by enabling quicker and more accurate utilization of Input Tax Credit, thereby improving liquidity and reducing working capital strain for MSMEs.
application_process: 1. Ensure GST registration and valid GSTIN. 2. Maintain proper tax invoices and supporting documents for inward supplies. 3. File GSTR-3B and GSTR-2A/GSTR-2B returns regularly. 4. Reconcile ITC claimed in GSTR-3B with auto-populated ITC from GSTR-2B. 5. Utilize the ITC ledger on the GST portal for payment of output tax liability. 6. Use offline tools or APIs for bulk ITC reconciliation if required. 7. Monitor ITC availability and expiry through the GST portal dashboard.
deadlines: Rolling basis — ITC must be claimed within the stipulated time under Section 16(4) of the CGST Act, i.e., by the due date of filing GSTR-3B for the month of September following the end of the financial year or filing of annual return, whichever is earlier.
implementing_agency: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) under the guidance of the GST Council and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)

scheme_name: GST Sahay – Working Capital Loans via GST Data
overview: GST Sahay is a working capital loan scheme that leverages GST data to provide financial support to businesses. It aims to improve access to credit for MSMEs and other enterprises by using their GST compliance and transaction history as a basis for lending decisions. The scheme is designed to enhance liquidity and support business continuity through data-driven lending.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Businesses registered under GST with compliant return filing history and verifiable transaction data through GSTN are eligible to apply for loans under GST Sahay.
benefits: Access to working capital loans based on GST data, faster loan processing due to digital verification, reduced reliance on traditional collateral, improved creditworthiness assessment through transaction history, and support for business expansion and operational needs.
financial_support: Working capital loans are extended based on the analysis of GST returns and transaction data, with loan quantum determined by the business's turnover, compliance history, and financial health as reflected in GSTN records. The mechanism involves fintech or NBFC partners using GSTN APIs to assess creditworthiness.
application_process: 1. Ensure GST registration and regular filing of returns 2. Approach participating lenders (banks/NBFCs) offering GST Sahay loans 3. Share GSTN consent for data access 4. Lender verifies GST data and assesses creditworthiness 5. Loan amount is sanctioned based on eligibility 6. Funds are disbursed to the borrower's account
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN)

scheme_name: Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme (Tax Dispute Resolution)
overview: The Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme (Tax Dispute Resolution) was launched to reduce litigation and provide a mechanism for settlement of pending tax disputes. It allows taxpayers to settle disputed tax, It allows taxpayers to settle disputed tax, settle disputed tax, interest, and penalty by paying a specified amount, thereby avoiding prolonged litigation. The scheme aims to provide certainty and reduce the burden on the tax administration and taxpayers.
target_beneficiaries: taxpayers
eligibility: Taxpayers having pending tax demands before any appellate forum as on a specified cutoff date are eligible to opt for the scheme.
benefits: Waiver of interest and penalty on payment of disputed tax amount; immunity from prosecution and penalty under certain provisions; withdrawal of pending appeals, revisions, references; no further proceedings under the Income-tax Act after settlement.
financial_support: Taxpayers pay a percentage of the disputed tax amount as settlement amount, with reduced rates if paid without interest; no interest or penalty is charged on the settlement amount if paid within the specified time.
application_process: 1. Eligible taxpayer identifies pending tax disputes as on cutoff date. 2. Computes settlement amount as per scheme provisions. 3. Files declaration in prescribed form online. 4. Pays the settlement amount. 5. Receives certificate of settlement and withdrawal of pending proceedings.
deadlines: The scheme was open for a limited window; currently closed as per evidence.
implementing_agency: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

scheme_name: Jawaharlal Nehru Aluminium Research & Design Centre (JNARDDC)
overview: Jawaharlal Nehru Aluminium Research & Design Centre (JNARDDC) is a premier research and development institute under the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, focused on aluminium and allied materials. It provides scientific and technical support to the aluminium industry through research, testing, design, and consultancy services. The centre aims to enhance the competitiveness of the Indian aluminium sector by promoting innovation, quality improvement, and sustainable practices. JNARDDC also offers training and skill development programmes for industry personnel and students.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; industries; researchers; startups
eligibility: Industries, MSMEs, startups, research institutions, and individuals seeking technical support in aluminium and allied materials can avail of JNARDDC's services. There are no specific restrictions based on entity type or size, but services are primarily aimed at those engaged in aluminium production, processing, or application.
benefits: Access to advanced research facilities, expert technical guidance, testing and characterization services, product design and development support, process optimization consultancy, failure analysis, material selection advice, training programmes, and customized solutions to improve quality, productivity, and competitiveness in the aluminium sector.
financial_support: JNARDDC provides services on a consultancy and fee-based model; financial support in the form of grants or subsidies is not a primary feature of the centre. Users are required to pay for the services availed based on the nature and scope of the work undertaken.
application_process: 1. Identify the specific technical or research requirement related to aluminium or allied materials. 2. Contact JNARDDC via email, phone, or through the official website to discuss the requirement. 3. Submit a formal request detailing the scope of work, objectives, and expected outcomes. 4. JNARDDC evaluates the request and prepares a proposal with scope, timeline, and cost estimate. 5. Upon acceptance of the proposal and payment of advance fee (if applicable), the work is initiated. 6. Regular progress updates are provided during the execution phase. 7. Final report, test results, or deliverables are submitted upon completion. 8. Payment of balance dues, if any, is made as per the agreed terms.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on service availability and project scheduling.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Mines, Government of India

scheme_name: National Steel Policy Raw Material Security for MSMEs
overview: The National Steel Policy Raw Material Security for MSMEs is a scheme under the Ministry of Steel aimed at ensuring the availability of critical raw materials like iron ore and coking coal for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the steel sector. It involves coordination with multiple government ministries to address raw material security challenges, including diversifying import sources, enhancing domestic production, and optimizing resource use. The scheme supports MSMEs by improving access to essential inputs for sustained growth in the iron and steel industry.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSMEs in the steel sector engaged in production or processing activities requiring raw materials such as iron ore, coking coal, or related inputs, as determined by the Ministry of Steel in coordination with Ministry of Mines, Ministry of Coal, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Logistic Ministries, and concerned State Governments.
benefits: Enhanced availability of domestic coking coal through allocation of coking coal blocks, auction of coking coal, and MoU for coking coal linkage; reduced import dependence on coking coal; improved access to iron ore and non-critical raw material; support for MSMEs in securing raw materials through policy coordination and logistics facilitation.
financial_support: The scheme does not involve direct financial disbursement to MSMEs. Instead, it focuses on policy interventions, coordination between ministries (Steel, Mines, Coal, Environment, etc.), and logistical measures such as allocation of coking coal blocks, auction mechanisms, and setting up of washeries to enhance domestic raw material availability and reduce import burden.
application_process: 1. Identify raw material requirements as an MSME in the steel sector. 2. Engage with Ministry of Steel or designated nodal agency for raw material security facilitation. 3. Submit request for support in accessing domestic raw materials or import facilitation. 4. Ministry coordinates with Ministry of Mines, Ministry of Coal, and State Governments for allocation or linkage. 5. Benefit from MoUs, block allocations, or auction outcomes for coking coal and iron ore access.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round based on availability and coordination cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Steel
contact_details: Email: secy-steel@nic.in | Tele No.: 24673489 24673912 (as per Citizens’ Charter 2025)

overview: The MSME Steel Processing Cluster Scheme is a government initiative under the Ministry of Steel aimed at supporting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the steel processing sector. The scheme focuses on enhancing the competitiveness and productivity of MSME steel processors through financial and technical assistance. It aims to promote cluster-based development, technology upgradation, and value addition in steel processing activities. The scheme is part of broader efforts to strengthen the domestic steel industry and support self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat).
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) engaged in steel processing activities as per the MSME Act, 2006 are eligible to apply under the scheme. The enterprises must be registered with the appropriate authorities and possess valid UDYAM registration. The scheme applies to units involved in processing activities such as cutting, bending, coating, fabrication, and value addition of steel products. Both new and existing MSME units are eligible, subject to meeting the scheme-specific criteria outlined in the guidelines.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of subsidies for setting up or upgrading steel processing infrastructure, including plant and machinery. Technical support for technology adoption, process optimization, and quality improvement. Access to common facility centers (CFCs) within steel processing clusters for shared resources like testing labs, training centers, and logistics support. Market linkage assistance and participation in trade fairs and buyer-seller meets. Skill development programs for workers and supervisors. Support for obtaining certifications and compliance with quality standards. Guidance on energy efficiency and waste reduction practices.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support in the form of subsidies for capital expenditure on plant and machinery, technical civil works, and other eligible components. The subsidy is typically a percentage of the project cost, subject to upper limits as per the scheme guidelines. Funds are disbursed in installments based on project milestones and verification. The exact quantum and mechanism are defined in the scheme's operational guidelines, which are issued by the Ministry of Steel from time to time.
application_process: 1. Check eligibility and ensure UDYAM registration is valid. 2. Prepare a detailed project report (DPR) outlining the proposed steel processing cluster or unit upgradation. 3. Submit the application online through the designated portal of the Ministry of Steel or its authorized agency. 4. Upload required documents including UDYAM certificate, project report, cost estimates, and land/building documents. 5. Application is scrutinized by the technical committee or project approval body. 6. Site verification may be conducted if required. 7. Upon approval, sanction letter is issued and funds are released in installments. 8. Submit utilization certificates and progress reports as per schedule. 9. Final settlement is made after project completion and verification.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Steel

scheme_name: Faceless Assessment & Appeal Scheme for MSMEs
overview: The Faceless Assessment & Appeal Scheme for MSMEs is a tax administration initiative by the Income Tax Department of India aimed at providing a transparent, efficient, and technology-driven assessment and appeal process for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). It eliminates physical interface between taxpayers and tax authorities by conducting proceedings electronically through a centralized system. The scheme enhances compliance, reduces litigation, and ensures timely resolution of tax matters for MSMEs under the Income Tax Act, 2025 and related rules.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: All Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as defined under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, who are assessees under the Income Tax Act, 1961 or Income Tax Act, 2025, and whose assessment or appeal proceedings are selected for faceless proceedings under the scheme notified by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT).
benefits: Elimination of physical interface with tax authorities, reduced compliance burden, transparent and standardized assessment process, timely disposal of cases, access to centralized facilitation centers, reduced scope for harassment or discretion, and enhanced trust in tax administration through technology-driven proceedings.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support, grants, subsidies, or loan benefits. It is a procedural and administrative reform aimed at improving the efficiency and fairness of tax assessment and appeal processes for MSMEs without any monetary disbursement.
application_process: 1. The Income Tax Department initiates faceless assessment or appeal proceedings based on risk management criteria and assigns a unique document identification number (DIN). 2. Notices are served electronically through the registered email ID of the MSME assessee or their authorized representative. 3. The assessee must respond within the stipulated time by uploading required documents and submissions on the designated e-filing portal (incometaxindia.gov.in). 4. All communications, including notices, responses, and orders, are exchanged electronically via the faceless assessment and appeal platform. 5. The assessment or appeal is decided by a designated Faceless Assessment Unit or Faceless Appeal Unit located anywhere in India. 6. Final orders are communicated electronically to the assessee through the e-filing portal.
deadlines: As per the timelines specified in the individual notice or communication issued under the Faceless Assessment & Appeal Scheme; responses must be submitted within the stipulated date mentioned in the electronic notice.

scheme_name: OIDB – Oil Industry Development Board Grants
overview: The Oil Industry Development Board (OIDB) provides financial assistance in the form of grants and loans to support research and development, techno-economic studies, manpower development, and other activities related to the petroleum sector. The scheme aims to promote indigenous technology development, improve refining and marketing operations, and enhance safety and environmental standards in the oil and gas industry. Financial support is extended to entities including public sector undertakings, research institutions, and private companies engaged in petroleum-related activities.
target_beneficiaries: public sector undertakings; research institutions; private companies; MSME
eligibility: Eligible entities include public sector undertakings under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, recognized research and development institutions, educational institutions offering petroleum-related courses, and private companies engaged in petroleum exploration, production, refining, marketing, or related activities. Proposals must align with national energy security goals and demonstrate technical feasibility and economic viability.
benefits: Financial support for R&D projects, techno-economic studies, manpower development programs, pilot plant demonstrations, and safety and environmental improvement initiatives. Assistance may cover partial or full project costs depending on the nature and beneficiary type. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, access to OIDB expertise, and collaboration opportunities with industry stakeholders.
financial_support: OIDB provides grants and loans based on the nature of the project and beneficiary. Grants are typically offered for R&D, studies, and manpower development to academic and research institutions, while loans are extended to commercial entities such as PSUs and private companies at concessional interest rates. The quantum of support is determined on a case-by-case basis after technical and financial appraisal.
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed project proposal to the Oil Industry Development Board (OIDB) outlining objectives, methodology, budget, and expected outcomes. 2. Proposal undergoes preliminary screening for alignment with OIDB priorities. 3. Technical appraisal by subject matter experts to assess feasibility and innovation. 4. Financial appraisal to evaluate cost-effectiveness and funding requirements. 5. Approval by the OIDB Governing Body based on recommendations. 6. Signing of agreement detailing terms and conditions of support. 7. Disbursement of funds in installments tied to project milestones. 8. Submission of progress reports and utilization certificates during project implementation. 9. Final evaluation and submission of project completion report.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year.

overview: TReDS (Trade Receivables Discounting System) is an RBI-regulated digital platform that enables MSMEs to unlock working capital by converting their approved receivables into immediate cash through competitive bidding by financiers. RXIL (Receivables Exchange of India Limited), established in December 2014 as a joint venture of SIDBI and NSE, is India's first TReDS platform. It facilitates invoice discounting without collateral or debt, providing funds within 24 hours of invoice approval, and supports MSME liquidity by bridging the payment gap between buyers and sellers.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSMEs engaged for at least 1 year since registration can register on TReDS. Eligibility factors include: GST compliance history, business turnover, buyer credit profile, invoice age, payment history, financial stability. A strong buyer profile often improves financing approval chances. MSMEs must be classified as per the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act).
benefits: Faster access to working capital (funds within 24 hours), reduced payment delays, lower borrowing costs compared to loans, no added debt on books, competitive bidding in auction models, seamless digital experience, ERP integration, enhanced procurement terms, strengthened supplier relationships, quicker payments, access to multiple financiers, without recourse borrowing, lower cost of funds, priority sector lending benefits, low risk of default, access to quality customers, automated reconciliation.
financial_support: Funds are disbursed through competitive bidding by multiple authorised banks and NBFCs on approved invoices. MSMEs receive early payment based on the best bid, often within 24 hours, while repayment responsibility rests with the corporate buyer on the invoice due date. The mechanism allows MSMEs to convert receivables into working capital without taking on traditional short-term debt or providing collateral. RXIL has facilitated invoice financing exceeding ₹2 lakh crore, with over 51,500 MSMEs registered across 1,160+ cities and participation from 70+ banks and NBFCs.

Any revision/correction/modification in such ECR shall not be allowed for claiming any enhanced benefits at any future date. 7. The ECR for any wage month for claiming the benefits under the Scheme has to be filed by eligible establishment not later than 60 days of the close of that wage month. 8. In case such ECR for any wage month is filed beyond the due date specified in Para 38 of the EPF Scheme, 1952 but within 60 days of close of the wage month, the liability of interest due u/s 7Q of the EPF& MP Act, 1952 on such belated remittances shall be borne by the employer. 9. Since the Central Government is paying the employee’s share of EPF contributions for new employees eligible under the Scheme, the employer shall not make any deduction towards employee’s share of EPF contribution from the monthly wages of any new employee and disburse the wages without such deduction to the new employee concerned and file declaration in regard to above with the ECR. 10. Any violation of this condition will be treated as breach of trust and render the employer liable for appropriate legal action as per law apart from recovery of such amount. 11. Once ECR is uploaded by an employer eligible for benefits, then the challan will separately show the amount of employees’ and employers’ contribution in respect of new employees due from Central Government under the Scheme and the amount payable by the employer. 12. The employer has to remit the payment due from him as reflected in Challan as noted above and complete the process of ECR filing. 13. The Central Government benefit due under the Scheme in respect of new eligible employees will be credited upfront in the Aadhaar seeded UAN of new employees by the EPFO from funds allocated by the Central Government. 14. Wherever employer has filed ECR for wage month of October and November 2020 prior to deployment of facility for registration under the Scheme, benefits due under the Scheme which is already remitted through ECR be reimbursed to employer for employers’ share by way of future adjustments against employer’s share of contribution. 15. The employee’s share of benefit of the respective new eligible employee will also be adjusted in their UANs. 16. Employers and Establishments shall be responsible for the correctness of all particulars submitted for claiming any benefit under the Scheme. 17. Any amount claimed through incorrect or false declaration shall be recoverable besides other action under appropriate provisions of law for making such false declaration. 18. Along with ECR to claim subsidy for any wage month, the employer shall be required to electronically upload a certificate / declaration in format appended below: CERTIFICATE/ DECLARATION OF EMPLOYER That I have read the Scheme Guidelines and declare that my establishment satisfies all the eligibility conditions for receiving benefit from the Central Government for creating new employment . I certify that no deductions towards either employees’ EPF contributions or employers’ EPF/EPS contributions have been made from wages of eligible new employees. That I have neither suppressed any material information nor omitted any particulars and submitted correct information in ECR filed with this declaration to avail the subsidy of employer’s and or employees’ share of contributions in respect of new eligible employees from the Central Government. I undertake that the subsidy received from Central Government under the Scheme shall not booked as expenditure incurred by the establishment or employer for claiming or receiving any benefit / exemption / rebate/ concessions under any law. I understand that the employer is liable to refund the benefit amount and is also liable for any penal action for submitting any incorrect or false information/declaration to avail the Central Government assistance.
deadlines: The Scheme stands commenced from 1st October 2020 and shall remain open for registration of eligible employers and new employees up to 30th June, 2021. The Central Government on 30.06.2021 approved for extension of last date of registration for eligible employers and new employees under the scheme from 30.06.2021 to 31.03.2022. The benefit shall be available for a period of twenty-four months from date of registration of new employee, not later than 31/03/2024 in any case.
implementing_agency: Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)

overview: The MRO (Maintenance, Repair & Overhaul) Policy 2021 is a policy initiative by the Ministry of Civil Aviation aimed at promoting India as a global hub for aircraft maintenance, repair, and overhaul services. It seeks to attract investment, create employment, and reduce dependence on foreign MRO facilities by offering incentives and streamlining regulatory processes. The policy focuses on developing infrastructure, providing fiscal incentives, and simplifying procedures to encourage both domestic and foreign investment in the MRO sector.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; entrepreneurs; domestic and foreign investors; aircraft maintenance companies
eligibility: Entities engaged in or planning to undertake aircraft maintenance, repair, and overhaul activities, including domestic and foreign companies, joint ventures, and special purpose vehicles, provided they meet the regulatory requirements set by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) and other relevant authorities under the Aircraft Act, 1934 and Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024.
benefits: The policy offers fiscal incentives such as tax holidays, customs duty exemptions on import of tools, equipment, and spare parts, and simplified customs procedures. Non-financial benefits include single-window clearance, infrastructure support through land allocation at airports, and facilitation of skill development programs. It also encourages public-private partnerships and provides a conducive regulatory environment for MRO operations.
financial_support: The policy provides fiscal incentives including customs duty exemptions on import of tools, test equipment, spare parts, and components required for MRO activities, along with possible tax holidays or concessions as per applicable government schemes. However, the policy does not specify direct financial grants or subsidies; support is primarily regulatory and fiscal in nature.
application_process: 1. Identify a suitable location for setting up an MRO facility, preferably at or near an airport. 2. Ensure compliance with DGCA regulations under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 and Aircraft Act, 1934. 3. Apply for necessary security clearances from the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS). 4. Obtain necessary clearances from the Airports Authority of India (AAI) or airport operator for land and infrastructure use. 5. Apply for customs duty exemptions and other fiscal benefits through the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) or customs authorities. 6. Obtain DGCA approval for the MRO facility and its operations. 7. Commence operations after obtaining all required approvals and clearances.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Civil Aviation
contact_details: Email: moca@nic.in | Helpline: 1800-11-5565 (Ministry of Civil Aviation helpline)

scheme_name: DGCA Regulatory Sandbox for eVTOL & AAM
overview: The DGCA Regulatory Sandbox for eVTOL & AAM is an initiative by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to support innovation in electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) and Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) technologies. It provides a controlled environment for testing and validating new aviation technologies under regulatory supervision. The sandbox aims to accelerate the development and certification of emerging aerial mobility solutions while ensuring safety and compliance with civil aviation norms.
target_beneficiaries: startups; technology developers; aviation innovators
eligibility: Eligible participants include startups, technology developers, and aviation innovators working on eVTOL, AAM, or related emerging aviation technologies that require regulatory testing under real-world conditions but within the sandbox frameworks
benefits: Access to regulatory guidance and support from DGCA during testing phases; opportunity to conduct flight trials under supervised conditions; assistance in navigating certification pathways; potential for fast-tracked evaluation of innovative technologies; collaboration with aviation experts and regulatory bodies.
financial_support: The evidence does not specify any direct financial support, grants, loans, or subsidies under the DGCA Regulatory Sandbox for eVTOL & AAM. The scheme focuses on regulatory facilitation rather than financial assistance.
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed proposal outlining the eVTOL or AAM technology to be tested. 2. Define the scope, objectives, and safety parameters of the proposed testing. 3. Provide technical specifications, risk assessments, and mitigation plans. 4. Await review by DGCA sandbox evaluation committee. 5. Upon approval, receive regulatory clearance to conduct tests under defined conditions. 6. Conduct tests and submit periodic progress and safety reports. 7. Final evaluation and feedback on compliance and performance.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India

overview: The National Aviation Security Fund is a financial mechanism established to support aviation security initiatives in India. It is managed by the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) under the Ministry of Civil Aviation. The fund is utilized for strengthening security infrastructure, procuring security equipment, and implementing security measures at airports and civil enclaves across the country.
target_beneficiaries: airport operators; airlines; civil aviation stakeholders
eligibility: Eligibility for utilization of the National Aviation Security Fund is restricted to government entities and authorized agencies involved in civil aviation security, including the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS), Airports Authority of India (AAI), and other central or state government departments engaged in aviation security functions, as per guidelines issued by the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
benefits: Financial support for procurement of security equipment, upgradation of security systems, funding for security training and capacity building, and implementation of national aviation security plans. Non-financial benefits include enhanced security coordination, standardized security protocols, and improved threat detection and response capabilities across the civil aviation sector.
financial_support: The National Aviation Security Fund provides financial assistance in the form of grants or direct funding for approved aviation security projects. The quantum of support is determined based on project proposals submitted by eligible agencies and approved by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, subject to availability of funds and adherence to security priorities.
application_process: 1. Identify aviation security project requiring funding 2. Prepare detailed project proposal with budget and timelines 3. Submit proposal to the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) 4. BCAS evaluates proposal for technical feasibility and security impact 5. Forward approved proposals to Ministry of Civil Aviation for final sanction 6. Receive fund allocation and implement project 7. Submit utilization certificates and progress reports as required
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals can be submitted throughout the year subject to fund availability and ministry review cycles.
implementing_agency: Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS), Ministry of Civil Aviation

scheme_name: CSIR-NAL Technology Transfer for Aerospace MSMEs
overview: CSIR-NAL Technology Transfer for Aerospace MSMEs is a program under the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - National Aerospace Laboratories (CSIR-NAL) aimed at transferring aerospace technologies developed by CSIR-NAL to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the aerospace sector. The scheme supports technology commercialization, industry collaboration, and innovation by enabling MSMEs to access CSIR-NAL's patented technologies, technical expertise, and R&D facilities. It focuses on strengthening the aerospace MSME ecosystem through technology licensing, joint development, and incubation support.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) engaged in aerospace, aviation, or allied sectors, with valid Udyam registration, capable of absorbing and commercializing transferred technologies, and meeting technical and financial criteria as defined in the technology transfer agreement.
benefits: Access to CSIR-NAL's patented aerospace technologies, technical know-how, and R&D facilities; support for prototype development and testing; assistance in regulatory compliance and certification; opportunities for joint development projects; incubation and mentorship support; potential for revenue sharing or licensing agreements; and enhanced market readiness through technology validation.
financial_support: Financial support is structured on a case-by-case basis through technology transfer agreements, which may include upfront licensing fees, royalty-based models, or joint investment mechanisms. Specific quantum or standardized financial assistance is not detailed in the evidence; support is negotiated based on the technology, scope, and commercialization plan.
application_process: 1. Identify relevant CSIR-NAL technology for transfer via the CSIR-NAL technology portfolio or outreach. 2. Express interest through CSIR-NAL's Business Development or Industry Incubation division. 3. Submit a formal application detailing the MSME's profile, intended use, and commercialization plan. 4. Undergo technical and commercial evaluation by CSIR-NAL experts. 5. Negotiate and sign a technology transfer agreement (TTA) outlining terms, royalties, and milestones. 6. Access technology documentation, know-how, and facility support as per agreement. 7. Proceed with prototype development, testing, and scaling under CSIR-NAL guidance.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - National Aerospace Laboratories (CSIR-NAL)

scheme_name: Common Facility Centre for Gems & Jewellery Clusters
overview: The Common Facility Centre for Gems & Jewellery Clusters is a scheme under the Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP) of the Ministry of MSME, Government of India. It aims to support the sustainability and growth of micro and small enterprises by addressing common issues such as improvement of technology, skills, quality, and market access. The scheme facilitates the creation of Common Facility Centres (CFCs) that provide shared infrastructure like production/processing centres, design centres, testing facilities, effluent treatment, and raw material depots to clusters of MSMEs in the gems and jewellery sector.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Existing Entrepreneurs [in form of a Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs)].
benefits: Creation of Common Facility Centres providing shared infrastructure such as Common Production / Processing Centre, Design Centers, Testing Facilities including Plug & Play Facilities. GoI Assistance: up to 80% of the maximum Project cost of Rs. 30 crores.
financial_support: GoI Assistance: up to 80% of the maximum Project cost of Rs. 30 crores. The balance amount of the total project cost is to be contributed by the SPV/cluster members and/or financial institutions.
application_process: 1. Identify the cluster and form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) of existing entrepreneurs. 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Common Facility Centre. 3. Submit the application through the MSME Cluster Development Programme portal. 4. Application is appraised by the Technical Agency and forwarded to the Ministry of MSME. 5. Upon approval, GoI releases funds in installments based on project milestones. 6. The SPV implements the project and utilizes the CFC for shared services.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (M/o MSME), Government of India

overview: India International Jewellery Week (IIJW) Support is a scheme by the Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC) to promote participation in the IIJW trade show. It provides benefits such as rate locks, discounted rates, no security deposit, and exclusive benefits like complimentary hotel rooms and food coupons for members who opt into the IIJS Prime Assure Scheme for multiple financial years. The scheme aims to facilitate long-term business planning and ensure economy of participation for GJEPC members in international jewellery exhibitions.
target_beneficiaries: GJEPC members; exporters; manufacturers; traders
eligibility: GJEPC members who have completed membership registration/renewal and possess valid login credentials are eligible to apply for the IIJS Prime Assure Scheme or single show application for IIJS Bharat – Premiere 2026. Applicants must be verified members of recognized trade associations.
benefits: Rate Lock: Same participation rates for IIJS Bharat – Premiere, IIJS Bharat – Signature and IIJS Bharat – Tritiya for a period of two years (2026-28). Discount Benefit Offer: Discounted rates for IIJS Prime Assure Scheme (6 shows) over single show application. No Security Deposit: No security deposits for 2 years. Exclusive Benefits at IIJS Bharat - Tritiya for Prime Assure Exhibitor: Complimentary Hotel Room (3 Nights) Complimentary Food Coupons 18 – 27 sqm: 1 Room 18 – 27 sqm: ₹7,500 36 – 72 sqm: 2 Rooms 36 – 72 sqm: ₹17,500 108 sqm: 3 Rooms 108 sqm: ₹22,500. Facilities and benefits: Early Show Entry: Access to the exhibition 30 minutes prior to the official opening hours. IIJS Prime+ Lounge: Access to Prime+ Badge (Owner Exhibitors) in the IIJS Prime+ Lounge. Networking Evening Pass: Available at discounted rates. Innov8 Launchpad: 25% discount on booking slots. Hotel Booking Priority: One-day early access to hotel room bookings for participating exhibitors. Sponsorship Opportunities: Priority access along with a 5% discount. Priority Listing: Special Prime Assure listing in the Digital Exhibitor Directory. Parking Facility: – 27 sqm and above: Parking at Bombay Exhibition Centre (BEC) – 9 sqm to 18 sqm: Parking at Lodha MCGM
financial_support: The scheme provides financial benefits through discounted participation rates, elimination of security deposits, and complimentary services such as hotel rooms and food coupons. The discount benefit offer ensures reduced costs for members opting for the multi-show Prime Assure Scheme compared to single show applications. Specific financial values include complimentary food coupons worth ₹7,500 for 18–27 sqm, ₹17,500 for 36–72 sqm, and ₹22,500 for 108 sqm stall sizes at IIJS Bharat - Tritiya.
application_process: 1. Visit the IIJS Bharat Shows space application portal. 2. Log in using existing username and password (same as used for membership registration/renewal) at https://registration.gjepc.org/login.php. 3. New members must register on the same portal. 4. Fill out the space application form for IIJS Prime Assure Scheme (6 show) or IIJS Bharat – Premiere 2026 (single show). 5. Submit the application form along with advance payment on or before 30th April 2026 to avail the exclusive Discount Benefit Offer of IIJS Prime Assure. 6. Ensure submission is completed by the deadline to retain preference status for space allotment.
deadlines: The space application for all 6 IIJS Bharat shows for the year 2026–28 will open on 13th April 2026. Applications must be submitted on or before 30th April 2026 to avail the exclusive Discount Benefit Offer of IIJS Prime Assure and continue with the preference status offered to different categories.
implementing_agency: Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC)

overview: The Civil Aviation Research Organisation (CARO) Grants scheme is a research funding initiative under the Ministry of Civil Aviation aimed at promoting research and innovation in civil aviation. The scheme supports research projects related to aviation safety, technology, infrastructure, and operations. It provides financial assistance to eligible institutions and researchers to undertake civil aviation research projects.
target_beneficiaries: research institutions; academic institutions; researchers; startups
eligibility: Eligible applicants include recognized research institutions, academic institutions, universities, and startups engaged in civil aviation research. Applicants must be Indian entities with relevant expertise in aviation domain. Projects must align with national aviation priorities and demonstrate clear outcomes.
benefits: Financial support for research projects, access to ministry data and facilities, collaboration opportunities with aviation stakeholders, technical guidance from ministry experts, and potential for technology transfer and commercialization of research outcomes.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as grants-in-aid for approved research projects. The quantum of support varies based on project scope and duration, typically covering equipment, consumables, personnel, and travel expenses. Funds are disbursed in installments based on project milestones and utilization certificates.
application_process:
1. Identify research topic aligned with civil aviation priorities
2. Prepare detailed project proposal with objectives, methodology, budget, and timeline
3. Submit application through the Ministry of Civil Aviation's official portal
4. Application undergoes technical review by expert committee
5. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for presentation/interview
6. Final selection and sanction order issued by the Ministry
7. Funds released in installments upon submission of utilization certificates and progress reports
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted throughout the year subject to budget availability
implementing_agency: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India
contact_details: Email: moca@nic.in | Helpline: Not specified in evidence

scheme_name: Indian Footwear, Leather & Accessories Development Programme (IFLADP)
overview: The Indian Footwear, Leather & Accessories Development Programme (IFLDP) is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India, with a total outlay of Rs.1700 Crores for the period 2021-2026. It consists of six sub-schemes: Sustainable Technology and Environmental Promotion (STEP), Integrated Development of Leather Sector (IDLS), Brand Promotion of Indian Brands in Leather and Footwear Sector, Development of Design Studios in Leather and Footwear Sector, Mega Leather, Footwear and Accessories Cluster Development (MLFACD), and Establishment of Institutional Facilities (EIF). The scheme aims to provide grant-based financial assistance to eligible units for modernization, technology upgradation, cluster development, and institutional support in the leather and footwear sector.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; industry units; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligible units must submit proposals/applications through the online NSWS portal (https://www.nsws.gov.in) for availing grant assistance under the respective sub-schemes. Assistance is subject to appraisal by PIUs (FDDI and CLRI for IDLS), recommendations by the Steering Committee, and final approval by DPIIT. Mere submission of an application does not entitle an applicant to GoI assistance.
benefits: Financial grant assistance for project implementation under the six sub-schemes. Non-financial benefits include technical appraisal by PIUs, guidance on project formulation, and access to institutional support for modernization, cluster development, brand promotion, design studio development, and environmental sustainability initiatives.
financial_support: Grant-based financial assistance is provided under the six sub-schemes of IFLDP. The assistance is disbursed to applicant units after due appraisal by PIUs (FDDI and CLRI for IDLS), forwarding to DPIIT, and approval by the Steering Committee. The quantum of support varies by sub-scheme and project proposal, subject to availability of funds and scheme guidelines.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant sub-scheme under IFLDP (STEP, IDLS, Brand Promotion, Design Studios, MLFACD, or EIF). 2. Prepare the project proposal as per the guidelines of the respective sub-scheme. 3. Submit the application through the online NSWS portal (https://www.nsws.gov.in) for availing grant. 4. For IDLS sub-scheme, applications are submitted to PIUs (FDDI and CLRI) via the NSWS portal. 5. After due appraisal by PIUs, applications are forwarded to DPIIT for consideration by the Steering Committee. 6. Upon approval by the Steering Committee, grant is disbursed to the applicant unit. 7. Note: Mere submission does not entitle assistance; approval is subject to appraisal and recommendations.
deadlines: For IDLS sub-scheme: applications must be submitted on or before 10th July 2025 (15-day window from 25th June 2025). For all other sub-schemes: NSWS portal is closed with immediate effect from 25th June 2025. The scheme period is till 31st March 2026 or till further review, whichever is earlier.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India

scheme_name: PLI Scheme for Leather & Footwear Products
overview: The PLI Scheme for Leather & Footwear Products is a Production Linked Incentive scheme aimed at boosting domestic manufacturing, enhancing exports, and attracting investment in the leather and footwear sector. It provides financial incentives based on incremental sales to eligible manufacturers. The scheme is part of the broader PLI initiatives under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) to make India a global manufacturing hub.
target_beneficiaries: manufacturers; MSME; large enterprises
eligibility: Eligible applicants include companies engaged in manufacturing of leather and footwear products, with a minimum threshold of investment and turnover as specified in the scheme guidelines. Applicants must be registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or equivalent, and must commit to incremental sales growth over the base year to qualify for incentives.
benefits: Financial incentives in the form of a percentage of incremental sales over the base year, tax benefits under relevant provisions, support for technology upgradation, and facilitation of access to credit and markets. The scheme also provides non-financial support such as guidance on compliance, quality standards, and export promotion.
financial_support: The scheme provides production-linked incentives calculated as a percentage of incremental sales (over the base year) incurred by eligible manufacturers. The incentive rate varies by product category and is disbursed annually based on verified sales and investment claims. The financial support is directly tied to performance and incremental growth in manufacturing and sales.
application_process: 1. Register on the designated PLI portal for Leather & Footwear Products. 2. Submit the application form with details of existing investment, production capacity, and base year sales. 3. Upload required documents including Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, GST details, audited financial statements, and details of plant and machinery. 4. Provide a commitment letter for achieving targeted incremental sales. 5. Await evaluation by the Project Management Agency (PMA) and approval by the Empowered Committee. 6. Upon approval, sign the agreement and begin operations to claim incentives based on verified incremental sales.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted periodically as per notifications issued by DPIIT.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: The National Leather Development Programme (NLDP) is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India, with a total outlay of Rs.1700 Crores during the period 2021-2026 till 31st March 2026 or till further review, whichever is earlier. The scheme consists of six sub-schemes: Sustainable Technology and Environmental Promotion (STEP), Integrated Development of Leather Sector (IDLS), Brand Promotion of Indian Brands in Leather and Footwear Sector, Development of Design Studios in Leather and Footwear Sector, Mega Leather, Footwear and Accessories Cluster Development (MLFACD), and Establishment of Institutional Facilities (EIF). Proposals/applications under the scheme (except IDLS) are submitted through the online National Single Window System (NSWS) portal, which has been closed with immediate effect for all sub-schemes except IDLS, which has a 15-day window for application submission until 10th July 2025.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; industry associations; entrepreneurs; manufacturers
eligibility: Eligible units under the IDLS sub-scheme submit applications through the online NSWS portal to PIUs (FDDI and CLRI). After due appraisal, applications are forwarded to DPIIT for consideration by the Steering Committee, and after approval by the Steering Committee, the grant is disbursed to the applicant units. Mere submission of an application does not entitle an applicant to GOI assistance; assistance is subject to appraisal and recommendations by the PIUs and final approval by the Steering Committee.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of grants for availing benefits under the six sub-schemes of IFLDP (NLDP), subject to appraisal by PIUs and approval by the Steering Committee. Non-financial benefits include technical support, institutional development, brand promotion, design studio development, cluster development, and environmental protection initiatives.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-based financial support under its six sub-schemes, with a total outlay of Rs.1700 Crores for the period 2021-2026. Assistance is disbursed after appraisal by PIUs (FDDI and CLRI) and approval by the Steering Committee of DPIIT. Mere submission of an application does not guarantee assistance; it is subject to technical appraisal and final approval.
application_process: 1. Submit proposals/applications through the online NSWS portal (https://www.nsws.gov.in) for availing of the grant under IFLDP (NLDP). 2. For IDLS sub-scheme, applications are submitted by eligible units to PIUs (FDDI and CLRI) through the online NSWS portal. 3. After due appraisal by PIUs, applications are forwarded to DPIIT for consideration by the Steering Committee. 4. After approval by the Steering Committee, the grant is disbursed to the applicant units. 5. Note: The NSWS portal for IFLDP 2021-26 is closed with immediate effect for all sub-schemes except IDLS, which has a 15-day window for application submission until 10th July 2025.
deadlines: For IDLS sub-scheme, a 15-day window is being provided and the portal will be closed within 15 days from the date of issuance of the letter (25th June 2025), i.e., by 10th July 2025 (Thursday). No applications will be accepted beyond 10th July 2025. For all other sub-schemes, the NSWS portal is closed with immediate effect.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Govt of India

overview: The Mega Leather, Footwear & Accessories Cluster (MLFAC) is a sub-scheme under the Indian Footwear & Leather Development Programme (IFLDP) 2021-26, implemented by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India. It aims to develop mega clusters for leather, footwear, and accessories manufacturing with infrastructure support, including industrial plots for allotment. The scheme is part of a central sector initiative with a total outlay of Rs.1700 Crores for all six sub-schemes under IFLDP during 2021-2026.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; manufacturers; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligible units must be registered with the Council for Leather Exports (CLE) or relevant authorities, possess valid Udyam Registration, and be engaged in leather, footwear, or accessories manufacturing. Applications were required to be submitted through the National Single Window System (NSWS) portal (https://www.nsws.gov.in) for consideration under the IFLDP 2021-26 scheme, subject to appraisal by PIUs (FDDI and CLRI) and final approval by the Steering Committee.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of grants for cluster development, infrastructure support including access to industrial plots, technical guidance, and facilitation of linkages with suppliers, markets, and institutions. Benefits also include access to common facilities, skill development, and convergence with other government schemes for holistic cluster growth.
financial_support: Under the IFLDP 2021-26, the Mega Leather, Footwear and Accessories Cluster Development (MLFACD) sub-scheme is one of six components with a total allocation of Rs.1700 Crores for all sub-schemes combined during 2021-2026. Financial support is provided as grants for infrastructure development, with disbursement subject to appraisal by Project Implementation Units (PIUs) and approval by the Steering Committee. Mere submission of an application does not guarantee assistance; final approval is based on technical and financial viability.
application_process: 1. Visit the National Single Window System (NSWS) portal at https://www.nsws.gov.in 2. Register or log in to the portal 3. Select the Indian Footwear & Leather Development Programme (IFLDP) 2021-26 4. Choose the Mega Leather, Footwear and Accessories Cluster Development (MLFACD) sub-scheme 5. Fill in the application form with project details 6. Upload required documents including Udyam Registration, project report, and bank details 7. Submit the application online 8. Await appraisal by PIUs (FDDI or CLRI) 9. Receive recommendation from PIUs to the Steering Committee 10. Await final approval and grant disbursement upon clearance.
deadlines: The NSWS portal for IFLDP 2021-26 was closed with immediate effect from 25th June 2025 for all sub-schemes except IDLS. For IDLS, a 15-day window was provided, closing by 10th July 2025. As of the notice dated 25th June 2025, no further applications are being accepted under MLFACD via NSWS.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India

overview: The Technology Upgradation of Leather Sector (TULS) is a sub-scheme under the Indian Footwear & Leather Development Programme (IFLDP) 2021-26, implemented by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India. It aims to support the modernization and technological upgradation of leather sector units through financial assistance. The scheme is part of a central sector initiative with a total outlay of Rs.1700 Crores for the period 2021-2026, targeting eligible units in the leather and footwear industry for grant-based support.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; leather sector units; footwear sector units
eligibility: Eligible units must be engaged in the leather and footwear sector and submit proposals through the online NSWS portal (https://www.nsws.gov.in) for availing grant assistance under the IFLDP 2021-26. Applications are subject to appraisal by PIUs (FDDI and CLRI) and final approval by the Steering Committee of DPIIT. Mere submission of an application does not entitle an applicant to Government of India assistance; assistance is subject to appraisal and recommendations by the PIUs and final approval by the Steering Committee.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of grants for technology upgradation, subject to appraisal and approval by the Steering Committee. Support includes funding for sustainable technology adoption, environmental protection measures, and modernization of production units. Non-financial benefits include technical guidance, monitoring, and verification through PIUs and Steering Committee oversight.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as grants under the IFLDP 2021-26, with a total outlay of Rs.1700 Crores allocated across six sub-schemes including TULS. The quantum of support per entity is determined based on project appraisal and Steering Committee approval. scheme_name: CLFA (Council for Leather Exports) Marketing Support
overview: The Council for Leather Exports (CLE) Marketing Support scheme under the CLFA (Council for Leather Exports) provides marketing and export promotion assistance to leather and footwear industry stakeholders. It facilitates participation in international trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, and market development activities to enhance global market access and export competitiveness. The scheme supports MSMEs and industry associations in leveraging government-backed export promotion initiatives.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; exporters; industry associations
eligibility: Eligible organisations include Ministry of MSME and organizations under the Ministry; State/Central Government Organisations/Institutions; and Registered Industry/Enterprise Associations. The applicant organization should be suitably registered under the relevant Act with the primary objective of promotion and development of MSMEs. The applicant organization should have regular audited accounts for the past 3 years. Events for which financial support is sought must be from the list of approved exhibitions/events/buyer-seller meets finalized by the Ministry of MSME each financial year. Financial assistance to one applicant organisation would normally be restricted to three events in a financial year. The applicant organisation must ensure that one MSME unit does not participate in more than 2 events in a financial year under the scheme. Adequate representation would be given to SC/ST/Women/NER entrepreneurs in such events. While selecting entrepreneurs as well as representative(s) of the participating units, priority should be given to persons who have not participated in such events earlier with Government grant.
benefits: Financial assistance for participation of MSME delegations in international exhibitions, trade fairs and buyer-seller meets in foreign countries (physical mode): 100% of space rent subject to a maximum of Rs.3.00 lakh per MSME unit; 100% of economy class airfare subject to a maximum of a maximum of Rs.1.50 lakh per MSME unit; duty allowance of USD 150 per day for office bearer; actual freight charges subject to maximum of Rs.50,000/- per MSME unit (Rs.75,000/- for Latin American Countries); advertisement and publicity charges up to Rs.2.50 lakh for delegation size up to 14 MSME units (Rs.5.00 lakh for 15 or more units); registration fee up to Rs.5,000/- per MSME unit. For organizing international conferences/summits/workshops/seminars in India: maximum of Rs.10.00 lakh for charges and Rs.5.00 lakh for economy class airfare for foreign speakers/experts. For organizing mega international exhibitions/fairs/buyer-seller meets, conferences/summits/workshops/seminars abroad: no expenditure ceiling. For Ministry of MSME led industrial delegations to international exhibitions/fairs/conferences: 10% of the budget allocated for the scheme shall be spent under this head. For virtual mode participation: maximum of Rs.1.5 lakh for space/stall charges; maximum of Rs.2.5 lakh for advertisement and publicity charges for delegation size up to 14 MSME units (Rs.5.00 lakh for 15 or more units). For organizing international conferences/summits/workshops/seminars in virtual mode: maximum of Rs.2.00 lakh for virtual space/platform/license fee/rent; maximum of Rs.5.00 lakh for publicity cost; maximum of Rs.1.00 lakh for translation and interpretation charges. The maximum ceiling of financial assistance for participation in one international event to be held abroad is Rs.2.00 crore (physical mode) and Rs.1.00 crore (virtual mode).
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as reimbursement of eligible expenditure incurred by applicant organisations for organizing or participating in international trade promotion activities. The assistance is supplemental in nature to the contribution of the organizer. The quantum of assistance is worked out on the basis of the budget estimate of the expenditure on the proposed event and in accordance with the criteria/scale mentioned in the guidelines, further at the discretion of the Screening Committee. The maximum ceiling of financial assistance for participation in one international event to be held abroad is Rs.2.00 crore (physical mode) and Rs.1.00 crore (virtual mode). For relaxation of the ceiling, Secretary (MSME) is the competent authority.
application_process: 1. The applicant organisation will submit an online application for financial assistance, along with the relevant documents and the budget estimate of the expenditure on the proposed event in the proforma online giving full details of expenditure. 2. The admissible financial assistance would be worked out on the basis of this budget estimate and in accordance with the criteria/scale mentioned in paragraph 3.2 and further at the discretion of the Screening Committee. 3. The applicant organisation must satisfy itself regarding eligibility before proposing the name of MSME unit in the delegation and any discrepancy, if noticed later, shall be the sole responsibility of the applicant organization. 4. While selecting entrepreneurs/participants, the applicant organization should ensure that one MSME unit must not participate in more than 2 events in a financial year under the scheme. 5. Adequate representation would be given to SC/ST/Women/NER entrepreneurs in such events. 7. While selecting entrepreneurs as well as representative(s) of the participating units, priority should be given to persons who have not participated in such events earlier with Government grant.

scheme_name: National Forest Policy for Paper Industry
overview: The National Forest Policy for Paper Industry is a scheme under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) aimed at promoting sustainable forest management and supporting the paper industry through policy guidelines and financial assistance. Preference is given to units located in ecologically sensitive zones with approved farm forestry models.
benefits: Benefits include financial assistance for setting up farm forestry units, subsidies on saplings and planting material, technical support for sustainable harvesting and processing, access to government nurseries for quality planting stock, training programs on agro-forestry best practices, facilitation of market linkages for non-wood forest products, and support for obtaining certifications like FSC or PEFC. financial_support: Financial support is provided in the form of subsidies and grants for establishing farm forestry plantations, with cost-sharing between the government and beneficiaries. The scheme covers up to 50% of the cost for planting material, land preparation, and initial maintenance for agro-forestry models. For paper industry units, support is extended for pollution control equipment, wastewater treatment systems, and energy-efficient machinery under technology upgradation components. Funds are disbursed through nodal agencies after verification of project milestones and utilization certificates.

overview: PM Awas Yojana – Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC) is a component of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) aimed at providing financial assistance to eligible urban poor families for the construction or enhancement of their houses. Under this scheme, beneficiaries who own land can construct their houses with central government support. The scheme focuses on enabling self-driven house construction through direct benefit transfer to the bank accounts of eligible beneficiaries.
target_beneficiaries: urban poor; slum dwellers; low-income groups; economically weaker sections
eligibility: Beneficiary families must not own a pucca house (either in their name or that of any family member) in any part of India. The family should include husband, wife, and unmarried children. The beneficiary must own a plot of land or have legal rights to the land. The annual household income should not exceed INR 3 lakhs for EWS and INR 6 lakhs for LIG categories. The scheme is applicable only in statutory towns as per Census 2011.
benefits: Financial assistance of INR 1.5 lakh per house for construction or enhancement. The amount is transferred in installments directly to the beneficiary's bank account linked to Aadhaar. The scheme promotes ownership of pucca houses with basic amenities like water, electricity, and sanitation. It supports inclusive urban development and reduces housing shortage in cities.

The funds are released in 2-3 installments based on construction progress, verified through geo-tagged photographs and uploaded on the PMAY(U) MIS. The transfer is made directly to the beneficiary's bank account via DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer).
grant_amount_per_entity: 1.5 lakh
application_process: 1. Identify eligible beneficiaries through ULB-led surveys using SECC data or voluntary submission. 2. Validate land ownership and income eligibility. 3. Obtain beneficiary consent and Aadhaar linkage. 4. Upload beneficiary details on PMAY(U) MIS. 5. Obtain administrative approval from State Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (SLSMC). 6. Release first installment of funds to beneficiary's bank account. 7. Monitor construction progress via geo-tagged photos. 8. Release subsequent installments upon verification. 9. Certify house completion and close the project.
deadlines: Rolling basis — subject to annual budget allocation and project sanction cycles
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
