scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA)
overview: Saubhagya – Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana was launched on 25th September 2017 to achieve universal household electrification by providing last mile connectivity and free electricity connections to all willing households in rural areas and poor families in urban areas. The scheme targets un-electrified households identified via SECC 2011 data, with non-eligible households able to obtain connections for a payment of Rs. 500. It aims to electrify approximately 4 crore households, including 300 lakh under the scheme (250 lakh rural, 50 lakh urban).
target_beneficiaries: willing households in rural areas; poor families in urban areas
eligibility: Under Saubhagya scheme, the government will provide all willing households in rural areas and poor families in urban areas free electricity connections identified using Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) data 2011 having at least one deprivation. The households not found eligible as per SECC data would also be provided electricity connection on payment of Rs. 500 per household which shall be recovered by respective Discom/ Power Departments as per the scheme.
benefits: Free electricity connections including service line cable, energy meter (including pre-paid/smart meter), single point wiring, LED lamp, and associated accessories. Last mile connectivity includes erection of poles, conductors, etc. For remote areas, solar photo voltaic (SPV) based standalone systems with 200-300 Watt power packs, battery backup, up to 5 LED lights, 1 DC fan, 1 DC power plug, and 5 years of repair and maintenance are provided. Access to electricity reduces indoor pollution by substituting kerosene, improves health, education, safety, and economic activities, especially for women.
financial_support: The cost of the Saubhagya scheme is Rs. 16,320 crore, which is over and above the investment under DDUGJY. Free connections are provided to eligible households; non-eligible households pay Rs. 500 per connection, recoverable in 10 instalments of Rs. 50 each along with the electricity bill. There is no provision for free power consumption—consumers must pay for electricity usage as per prevailing DISCOM tariffs.
grant_amount_per_entity: Free electricity connection (value not specified in monetary terms); Rs. 500 for non-SECC households
application_process: 1. Camps are organised in villages or clusters using mobile app/web portal for beneficiary identification. 2. Applications for electricity connections are registered electronically at camps. 3. Required documentation including applicant photograph, identity card copy, mobile number, Aadhar number, and bank account details are completed on spot. 4. Gram Panchayat/public institutions may collect applications, complete documentation, and handle billing and revenue collection. 5. Connections are released at the earliest after documentation completion.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline mentioned; implementation is time-bound but applications processed via camps and electronic registration as per scheme rollout.
implementing_agency: Rural Electrification Corporation Limited (REC)

scheme_name: Green Building Rating System (GRIHA) Certification Support
overview: GRIHA (Green Rating for Integrated Habitat Assessment) is India’s national rating system for green buildings, developed by TERI and adopted by the Government of India in 2007. It evaluates buildings based on nationally acceptable benchmarks for energy, water, waste, and sustainability. The GRIHA Council, an autonomous not-for-profit society, promotes and administers the rating system to advance sustainable habitats in India.
target_beneficiaries: developers; builders; architects; engineers; MSME; government projects; private sector
eligibility: Eligibility varies by GRIHA variant: For GRIHA Rating, residential projects require >5,000 sq.m built-up area with ≥80% residential use; non-residential requires >2,500 sq.more than 2,500 sq.m. For SVAGRIHA, residential projects range from 100–5,000 sq.m and non-residential from 100–2,500 sq.m. GRIHA for Existing Buildings (EB) requires operational buildings with >1 year of continuous operations data. GRIHA for Affordable Housing aligns with PMAY norms. All projects must exclude parking, basements, and service rooms from built-up area calculations.
benefits: Benefits include reduced energy and water consumption, lower operational costs, enhanced asset value, faster government approvals, eligibility for incentives like extra FAR and tax rebates, improved marketability, recognition in government tenders, access to GRIHA Product Catalogue, networking opportunities, and contribution to national sustainability goals. Certified projects gain visibility on GRIHA website, endorsement to use GRIHA logo, and inclusion in quarterly newsletters.
financial_support: GRIHA is a rating and certification system, not a direct financial subsidy scheme. Financial support comes indirectly through government incentives such as additional FAR (Floor Area Ratio), fast-track approvals, and tax rebates offered by state and central authorities for GRIHA-rated projects. For example, Punjab provides up to 10% additional FAR free of cost for 5-star GRIHA-rated buildings, along with 100% exemption from building scrutiny fees. Maharashtra and other states have similar policies. The GRIHA Council does not disburse grants or loans but enables access to fiscal benefits via certification.
application_process: 1. Register the project on the GRIHA website and select the appropriate rating variant. 2. Pay the registration fee (varies by project type and size). 3. Attend an orientation workshop (optional but recommended). 4. Submit required documents including design drawings, compliance reports, and calculations. 5. Undergo preliminary evaluation by GRIHA Council. 6. Conduct mandatory site visit(s). 7. Submit final documentation. 8. Undergo final evaluation. 9. Receive award of rating upon successful compliance. 10. Optionally appeal for re-evaluation if needed.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: GRIHA Council (an autonomous, not for profit society)

application_process: 1. Visit the specific program page on NSRCEL website (e.g., https://nsrcel.org/launchpad/, https://nsrcel.org/campus-founders/). 2. Click 'Register Your Interest' or 'Apply Now' to access the application form. 3. Fill out the online application form with venture details, pitch deck, and required documents. 4. Submit the form for initial screening. 5. Undergo eligibility check and telephonic interview (if applicable). 6. Present pitch to mentor panel for evaluation. 7. Final assessment and onboarding into the program upon selection.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round for most programs, with specific cohorts announced periodically.
implementing_agency: NSRCEL (National Startup Resource and Collaboration Centre for Entrepreneurship and Leadership), Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB)
contact_details: Email: nsrcel.socialmedia@iimb.ac.in | For escalations: escalations@nsrcel.iimb.ac.in | Program-specific contacts: healthcare@nsrcel.iimb.ac.in, velocity@nsrcel.iimb.ac.in, sustainabilityincubationprogram@iimb.ac.in, nsrcel.mobility@iimb.ac.in, wspqueries@iimb.ac.in, nsrcel.social@nsrcel.iimb.ac.in

overview: IIM Calcutta Innovation Park (IIMCIP) is a national, leading social-impact incubator established in 2014 under the aegis of IIM Calcutta. It is committed to building an inclusive and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem across India, with a focus on underserved regions, rural women entrepreneurs, and social impact-driven ventures. IIMCIP offers a range of programs including incubation, pre-incubation, acceleration, and specialized initiatives like MeitY TIDE 2.0, NIDHI-EIR, and Prakriti Incubation, providing mentorship, seed funding, market access, and networking opportunities to early-stage startups.
target_beneficiaries: startups; early-stage startups; women entrepreneurs; social enterprises; cleantech startups; sustainability startups; North Eastern Region startups; technology-driven ventures
geographic_scope: Pan-India with special focus on East, North-East, and underserved regions
eligibility: Eligibility varies by program. Generally, applicants must be Indian citizens with a startup registered in India or having an office in India. For specific programs: MeitY TIDE 2.0 requires ICT-enabled ideas solving national priority concerns; Prakriti Incubation targets early-stage, early-revenue, MVP startups from the North East Region in sustainability and circular economy; NIDHI-EIR requires applicants to be Indian citizens with minimum 4 years of formal education, first-generation innovators willing to work full-time on a technology business idea; Maruti Suzuki NURTURE welcomes early-stage startups with prototype/MVP in mobility, manufacturing, and social impact domains; Pragati Accelerator targets early revenue stage innovative technology-enabled social ventures from East & North-east India with scalable models.
benefits: Benefits include mentorship from industry experts and IIM Calcutta faculty/alumni, access to fully-furnished workspace at IIM Calcutta campus (free of charge), seed capital and investor connect opportunities, legal/secretarial/IT/HR support at preferential rates, capacity-building workshops, market access and networking opportunities, participation in demo days and pitch events, fellowship grants (e.g., Rs 4-7 lakhs for MeitY TIDE 2.0, Rs 15 lakhs reward grant for Prakriti top performers), equity consideration (up to 5% by IIMCIP), and access to corporate and government partnerships. Some programs offer cash rewards (e.g., Rs 13 lakhs in Maruti Suzuki NURTURE) and opportunities for paid Proof of Concept projects.
financial_support: Financial support varies across programs. IIMCIP provides seed capital through equity or debt instruments for early-stage ventures. Specific programs offer: MeitY TIDE 2.0 Entrepreneur-in-Residence: Rs 4 lakhs grant for validation and development; MeitY TIDE 2.0 Grant: Rs 7 lakhs for MVP development from PoC; NIDHI-EIR: Rs 30,000 per month fellowship for 12 months; Prakriti Incubation: Fellowship grant plus reward grant up to Rs 15 lakhs for top performers; Maruti Suzuki NURTURE: Cash rewards worth INR 13 lakhs and paid PoC opportunities; Pragati Accelerator: Upto Rs 10 lakhs award to top 3-5 startups; DST NIDHI-SSS: Average seed fund of Rs 25 lakhs, up to Rs 100 lakhs per startup via loan, equity, or equity-linked instruments at 2-3% interest. IIMCIP has till date provided seed funding support amounting to Rs.26 crores and facilitated follow-on funding of Rs.1,946 crores for incubated startups.
application_process: 1. Submit a formal application including business plan and expression of interest in joining the portfolio. 2. Application undergoes initial screening by IIMCIP management team. 3. Shortlisted candidates proceed to final review by an independent investment committee. 4. Upon approval, sign an incubation agreement with IIMCIP (requires registration as a for-profit company before signing). 5. Gain access to IIMCIP facilities and resources. 6. Work closely with assigned mentors through regular interactions. 7. Submit monthly progress updates and detailed quarterly reports for monitoring. 8. Graduate upon achieving self-sustainability, securing expansion funding, completing an acquisition, or reaching end of incubation term (standard period: 24 months). 9. IIMCIP may take up to 5% equity as consideration for incubation support.
deadlines: Varies by program: Maruti Suzuki NURTURE Cohort 4 deadline is June 30, 2026; Prakriti Incubation Cohort 2 last date extended to July 31, 2026; MeitY TIDE 2.0 EiR: Last date for applications August 25, 2025; MeitY TIDE 2.0 Grant: Last date for applications January 5, 2026; NIDHI-EIR: Last date for applications August 10, 2024; Pragati Accelerator (2022): Last date for applications July 10, 2022; Balmer Lawrie National Level Startup Hunt: Last date for applications May 20, 2023. Some programs operate on rolling basis.
implementing_agency: IIM Calcutta Innovation Park (IIMCIP), a Section 8 company set up under the aegis of the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta
contact_details: Email: contact@iimcip.org | Phone: 33******13 (as per MGT-7 filing) | Address: IIM Calcutta, Joka, Diamond Harbour Road, Kolkata 700104

overview: ISERD (Israel-Europe R&D Directorate) facilitates Israeli participation in Horizon Europe, the European Union's flagship research and innovation programme running from 2021 to 2027 with a budget of €95.5 billion. It supports Israeli organizations, including startups, SMEs, academia, and public sector entities, in accessing Horizon Europe funding through partner search, proposal writing workshops, and technology transfer opportunities. ISERD also provides information on financial support mechanisms such as reimbursement of proposal expenses via the Israel Innovation Authority and highlights success stories of Israeli entities securing Horizon Europe grants.
target_beneficiaries: startups; SMEs; academia and research institutes; large companies; public sector and NGOs
eligibility: Organizations registered in Israel, including SMEs, large companies, academia and research institutes, public sector entities, and NGOs, are eligible to participate in Horizon Europe as associated country members and benefit from ISERD support.
benefits: Access to Horizon Europe funding opportunities, partner search and consortium building support, proposal writing workshops (e.g., for MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships), technology transfer and business development opportunities, reimbursement of proposal expenses via the Israel Innovation Authority, and guidance on EU funding programmes.
financial_support: Israeli organizations submitting Horizon Europe proposals as part of a consortium are entitled to reimbursement of expenses from the Israel Innovation Authority. Additionally, Israeli startups have secured funding through Horizon Europe-related programmes such as the EIC Accelerator, which offers a grant of up to €2.5 million and equity investment of up to €15 million.
application_process: 1. Identify a Horizon Europe call matching your idea or technology via ISERD resources. 2. Use ISERD partner search tools and attend webinars (e.g., 'Call Identified, Consortium Needed') to find consortium partners. 3. Participate in ISERD proposal writing workshops (e.g., MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026) to structure applications. 4. Leverage ISERD technology transfer webinars to explore business development opportunities. 5. Submit proposals through the Horizon Europe portal. 6. Apply for reimbursement of proposal expenses via the Israel Innovation Authority if part of a consortium.
deadlines: Based on Horizon Europe call timelines; ISERD offers weekly sessions (e.g., 'Sunday Morning with Horizon Europe') to help applicants stay updated on open calls.
implementing_agency: Israel-Europe R&D Directorate (ISERD)

overview: The India-US Strategic Clean Energy Partnership (SCEP) is a bilateral initiative between India and the United States to advance clean energy cooperation, focusing on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and emerging technologies. It aims to strengthen collaboration in areas such as solar, wind, hydrogen, and grid modernization through joint research, policy dialogue, and technology deployment. The partnership supports India's clean energy transition and climate goals while promoting U.S. engagement in India's energy sector. SCEP operates under the framework of the U.S.-India Strategic Energy Partnership and is co-led by the U.S. Department of Energy and Indian government agencies.
target_beneficiaries: government agencies; research institutions; private sector; energy companies
eligibility: Eligibility is open to entities from India and the United States, including government agencies, national laboratories, research institutions, private companies, and non-profit organizations engaged in clean energy innovation, deployment, or policy development under the SCEP framework.
benefits: Benefits include access to joint funding opportunities, technical collaboration with U.S. national laboratories and Indian research institutions, participation in bilateral working groups, technology transfer, pilot project demonstration projects in solar, wind, hydrogen, and grid technologies, and support for clean energy entrepreneurship and workforce development.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through competitive funding opportunities announced by the U.S. Department of Energy, including grants, cooperative agreements, and technical assistance, with specific amounts varying by opportunity (e.g., up to $11 million for SolWEB2, up to $12.5 million for Circular Supply Chains Accelerator). Funding is subject to Congressional appropriations and awarded via merit-based selection.
application_process: 1. Identify relevant funding opportunity on the U.S. Department of Energy website under SCEP or related offices (e.g., CMEI, EERE, GDO). 2. Review eligibility, deadlines, and required documents in the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO). 3. Submit a concept paper (if required) by the specified date via EERE Exchange. 4. Upon concept paper approval, submit a full application through EERE Exchange before the deadline. 5. Applications undergo merit review; selected applicants are notified for award negotiations.
deadlines: Varies by opportunity; examples include concept paper deadlines of February 14, 2025 (SolWEB2) and March 31, 2025 (Circular Supply Chains Accelerator), with full application deadlines ranging from May 2, 2025 to July 18, 2025.
implementing_agency: U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), in coordination with the Government of India
contact_details: For NOFO-specific support: solarwildlife@ee.doe.gov (SolWEB2), Circularity.NOFO.FY25@ee.doe.gov (Circular Supply Chains Accelerator); general inquiries: DOENews@hq.doe.gov

scheme_name: IARI – Indian Agricultural Research Institute Startup Grants
overview: The Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) offers various startup and entrepreneurship development programs through its Pusa Krishi Incubator, including Agripreneurship Development Programs on Spirulina cultivation, Smart Snacks with Millets, and Entrepreneurship Development in Biofertilizers and Microbial Solutions. These programs aim to foster agri-startups and innovation in sustainable agriculture through training, skill development, and exposure to commercial ventures.
target_beneficiaries: agri-startups; entrepreneurs; young scientists; farmers
eligibility: Eligibility varies by program: For the Dual PhD program with WSU, applicants must be doctoral students enrolled during 2022-23 or 2023-24 academic sessions. For Agripreneurship Development Programs, eligibility is open to interested candidates seeking training in Spirulina cultivation, millet-based snacks, or biofertilizers. For Young Professional-I (YP-I) positions under DMRC-funded projects, candidates must have a B.Sc. in Horticulture, Agriculture, Botany, Forestry, or Life Sciences from a recognized university.
benefits: Participants gain practical skills in research proposal writing, access to expert guidance from retired scientists and research leaders, exposure to national and international funding opportunities, training in interdisciplinary and impact-oriented research, skill development in GIS mapping, technical reporting, and field surveys, certification upon completion, and enhanced employability in agri-tech and research sectors. Some programs offer stipends, fee waivers, and research grants (e.g., AU$35,000 tuition waiver and AU$4,000 annual research grant in the WSU dual PhD program).
financial_support: Financial support varies across programs: The IARI-WSU Dual PhD program offers a full tuition fee waiver of AU$35,000 and a pro-rata annual research grant of AU$4,000 for 18–24 months. Other programs like Agripreneurship Development and YP-I positions provide stipends (e.g., ₹30,000 consolidated per month for YP-I) but do not mention direct grant funding for startups. No specific grant amount or fund corpus for startup grants is mentioned in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Submit Expression of Interest (EoI) along with a research proposal to the Office of International Affairs, IARI, within 30 days of notification (for Dual PhD program). 2. For training programs like Agripreneurship Development, apply via announcements on the IARI website or through designated coordinators. 3. For contractual positions (e.g., YP-I, SRF, JRF), submit applications via email to the specified address with self-attested documents. 4. Attend walk-in interviews or online/offline selection processes as announced. 5. Selected candidates must submit original documents for verification before offer letter issuance.
deadlines: Rolling basis for some training programs; specific deadlines apply (e.g., 30 days for Dual PhD program EoI submission, 14.07.2026 for YP-I interview).
implementing_agency: Indian Council of Agricultural Research - Indian Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR-IARI)
contact_details: Email: tkdutta@iari.res.in (for SRF positions), drajaitiwari@gmail.com (for YP-I positions), ashish.pathology@gmail.com (for JRF positions); Helpline: IARI Helpline Numbers for Farmers - Farmer WhatsApp Helpline: 9560297502, Pusa Helpline: 011-25841670 / 25841039

overview: India-UK PRISM (Prosperity & Resilience through Innovation) is a bilateral initiative under Innovate UK aimed at fostering innovation collaboration between India and the UK. The scheme supports deep tech businesses and innovation-driven enterprises in priority sectors through funding, knowledge exchange, and joint research initiatives. It is part of the UK’s broader innovation agency activities under UK Research and Innovation, focusing on strengthening international partnerships in science and technology.
target_beneficiaries: startups; deep tech businesses; innovation-driven enterprises
eligibility: The scheme targets innovative deep tech businesses in the UK’s priority sectors that are engaged in or seeking collaboration with Indian partners. Specific eligibility criteria are not detailed in the provided evidence, but participation is linked to Innovate UK’s innovation support programmes.
benefits: Access to funding, collaboration opportunities with Indian innovation entities, participation in joint research and development projects, and support through Innovate UK’s innovation programmes. The scheme facilitates international partnerships that enhance innovation capacity and market access.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through Innovate UK’s innovation funding mechanisms, including grants and collaborative funding streams. The exact quantum, type, and mechanism are not specified in the evidence, but support aligns with Innovate UK’s role in backing innovative businesses via grants and innovation loans.
application_process: The application process is not detailed in the provided evidence. Interested entities are likely required to engage through Innovate UK’s official channels, potentially involving proposal submission, partnership validation, and alignment with priority sectors, but no numbered steps are available.
implementing_agency: Innovate UK, part of UK Research and Innovation

overview: The EU-India Innovation Cooperation is part of the European Innovation Council (EIC), which supports breakthrough innovation across Europe through grants, equity investments, and business acceleration services. The EIC funds deep tech startups and SMEs via schemes like Pathfinder, Transition, Accelerator, and STEP Scale Up, offering grants up to EUR 4 million and investments up to EUR 30 million. It also provides access to coaching, mentoring, networking, and global partner connections through its Business Acceleration Services.
target_beneficiaries: startups; SMEs; research teams; deep-tech innovators
geographic_scope: EU Member States and Horizon Europe associated countries
eligibility: Applicants must be from EU Member States or countries associated to Horizon Europe. For EIC Pathfinder: research teams, consortia of at least 3 different independent legal entities from different countries, or single applicants for Pathfinder Challenges only. For EIC Transition: SMEs, start-ups, spin-offs, research organisations, universities as single applicants, or consortia of 2-5 legal entities. For EIC Accelerator: start-ups and SMEs, individuals intending to launch an SME, small mid-caps (up to 499 employees). For STEP Scale Up: single SME or small mid-cap (<500 employees) in EU Member States or eligible Associated Countries (excluding UK), or investors submitting on behalf of eligible companies. All proposals must be submitted via the Funding and Tenders Opportunities Portal.
benefits: Grants of up to EUR 4 million (Pathfinder), EUR 2.5 million (Transition), or below EUR 2.5 million (Accelerator grant component); equity investments of EUR 0.5M–€10M (Accelerator) or EUR 10M–€30M (STEP Scale Up); access to Business Acceleration Services including coaching, mentoring, training, networking, global partner access, innovation ecosystem connections, and venture-building support; Seal of Excellence for unsuccessful but high-quality applicants to facilitate alternative funding; pre-financing payments and milestone-based funding disbursement.
financial_support: Financial support varies by scheme: EIC Pathfinder offers grants up to EUR 4 million plus booster grants of EUR 50,000; EIC Transition provides grants up to EUR 2.5 million and booster grants up to EUR 50,000; EIC Accelerator offers a grant component below EUR 2.5 million and an investment component of €1–€10 million (higher under STEP Scale Up); STEP Scale Up provides equity-only investments of EUR 10–30 million; EIC Pre-Accelerator offers individual grants between €300K–€500K (2025 call) or €500K–€1M (2027 call). The EIC Fund manages equity investments with a long-term horizon (7–10 years, max 15) and follows a blended finance model combining grants and quasi-equity instruments.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to EUR 4 million for EIC Pathfinder, EUR 2.5 million for EIC Transition, below EUR 2.5 million for EIC Accelerator grant component
application_process: 1. Write your proposal (short or full depending on scheme) 2. Submit via the Funding and Tenders Opportunities Portal before the deadline 3. Proposal undergoes remote evaluation by expert evaluators 4. If successful, invited to interview with EIC Jury 5. Interview conducted online or in person 6. Final funding decision communicated post-interview 7. Sign grant agreement and receive pre-financing 8. For investment component, due diligence conducted by EIC Fund and external advisors 9. Investment tranches released based on milestones 10. Receive access to Business Acceleration Services throughout the project lifecycle.
deadlines: Multiple batching dates per year: EIC Accelerator Open/Challenges: 7.01.2026, 04.03.2026, 06.05.2026, 08.07.2026, 02.09.2026, 04.11.2026; EIC Pathfinder Open: 12 May 2026; EIC Pathfinder Challenges: 28 October 2026; EIC Transition: 16/09/2026; STEP Scale Up: 6. May 2026, 9 September 2026, 25 November 2026; STEP Scale Up Defence: Apply by 28 October 2026; EIC Pre-Accelerator: 18 November 2027.
implementing_agency: European Innovation Council (EIC) established by the European Commission under the Horizon Europe programme (2021-2027), managed by the European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA)
contact_details: National Contact Points (NCPs) in each EU Member State and Associated Country; Enterprise Europe Network (https://een.ec.europa.eu/)

overview: The India-Canada Industrial R&D Programme (IC-IMPACTS) is a bilateral initiative fostering collaborative research and development between Indian and Canadian entities, focusing on innovation in sectors such as water, health, and energy. It supports joint projects that address mutual challenges through technology development and knowledge exchange. The programme encourages industry-academia partnerships and aims to commercialize R&D outcomes for socio-economic impact.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; research institutions; industry partners
eligibility: Indian entities including startups, MSMEs, academic institutions, and research organizations are eligible to apply in partnership with Canadian counterparts. Projects must involve joint R&D activities with clear technology development goals and potential for commercialization. Each project requires a minimum of one Indian and one Canadian partner, with balanced contribution and shared intellectual property rights.
benefits: Financial support for joint R&D projects, access to international expertise and infrastructure, opportunities for technology validation and scaling, enhanced market access in both countries, and support for intellectual property management and commercialization pathways.
financial_support: The programme provides grant-based financial support to cover eligible project costs such as personnel, materials, travel, and prototyping. Funding is typically cost-shared between the Indian and Canadian partners, with each side contributing resources as per bilateral agreement. The exact quantum varies per project based on scope and budget, subject to approval by the respective national funding agencies.
application_process: 1. Identify a suitable Canadian partner and develop a joint project proposal aligned with programme priorities. 2. Prepare a detailed project plan including objectives, methodology, budget, timelines, and expected outcomes. 3. Ensure compliance with eligibility criteria and intellectual property guidelines. 4. Submit the joint application through the designated national agency in India (as per current implementing arrangement). 5. Undergo bilateral review by experts from both countries. 6. Receive funding decision and sign collaborative agreement upon approval. 7. Implement the project with periodic reporting and final evaluation.
implementing_agency: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India

overview: The Indo-German Science & Technology Centre (IGSTC) is a joint initiative by the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India and the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), Government of Germany. It was established to facilitate Indo-German R&D networking through substantive interactions among government, academia/research system and industries, thus fostering innovation for overall economic and societal developments in both the countries. IGSTC supports various programmes including 2+2 Projects, Industrial Fellowships, WISER, PECFAR, SING, and IGSTC-CONNECT Plus to promote bilateral collaboration in science and technology.
target_beneficiaries: researchers; academics; industry professionals; PhD students; Postdoctoral researchers; women researchers
eligibility: Eligibility varies by programme. For 2+2 Projects: at least one research/academic institution and one industry from both India and Germany are required, with a maximum of six partners (three from each country). Indian academic partners must be public/private non-profit research organisations/institutions of higher education/universities with valid accreditation. Indian industry partners must be companies registered under Indian Companies Act 2013 or LLP Act 2008 or MSME Act 2006 with at least 51% Indian shareholding, R&D setup in India, and in existence for at least three years. German academic partners must be higher education institutions or research organisations providing R&D contributions. German industry partners must be companies in the commercial sector, especially SMEs, with a branch in Germany. For Industrial Fellowships: PhD Industrial Exposure Fellowship (PIEF) – PhD students (science/engineering) enrolled in any research institution/university in India with at least one year of PhD completed, age limit 28 years. Post Doctoral Industrial Fellowship (PDIF) – Postdoctoral researchers/fresh PhDs awarded PhD in science/engineering within 2 years of application deadline, age limit 35 years. For WISER: women researchers/entrepreneurs holding a regular position with minimum 5 years experience in academic/research institutions/industry in India and Germany, no age limit, active employment contract/fellowship valid for more than 4 years from application deadline. For PECFAR: Early Career Researchers with Master’s in Science/Bachelors in Engineering (4 years), regular positions or job contract in academia/research institution/industry, or employment contract with parent organisation while enrolled for PhD, age limit up to 40 years as on application deadline.
benefits: Financial support in the form of grants-in-aid, travel support, fellowship amounts, health insurance, airfare, visa fees, and access to collaborative research networks. Non-financial benefits include access to joint research platforms, technology transfer opportunities, capacity building, networking with academia and industry from both countries, mentorship, and support for commercialization of research outcomes. Specific benefits vary by programme: 2+2 Projects provide grant-in-aid up to Rs. 350 lakhs for Indian partners and Euro 500,000 for German partners over three years. Industrial Fellowships provide €1500/month for PIEF and €2500/month for PDIF, plus round-trip airfare up to €1000 and health insurance up to €100/month. WISER provides travel support for 2-3 visits, research stay of 30-90 days over 24-36 months, and basic project assistance. PECFAR provides fellowship of €2300 per month per fellow (pro rata), travel of €1500 for both Indian and German awardees, and basic project assistance.
financial_support: Financial support varies by programme. For 2+2 Projects: grant-in-aid to Indian partners up to Rs. 350 lakhs and to German partners up to Euro 500,000 for a three-year period. Funding is released yearly as per approved budget and milestones. Indian academic/research partners receive 100% grant-in-aid; Indian industry partners receive up to Rs. 150 lakhs grant-in-aid subject to matching contribution from own resources. German academic/research partners receive 100% of eligible costs in grant form; German industry partners (SMEs) receive grant based on De-Minimis or AGVO rules. For Industrial Fellowships: PhD Industrial Exposure Fellowship: €1500 per month; Post Doctoral Industrial Fellowship: €2500 per month; single round-trip economy class airfare including visa fees and travel insurance up to €1000; health insurance as per actuals with maximum €100/month. For WISER: grant includes travel support for 2-3 visits, research stay of 30-90 days, and basic project assistance (research staff, consumables, minor equipment, overheads, contingency). For PECFAR: fellowship of €2300 per month per fellow (pro rata), travel of €1500 for both Indian and German awardees (single round-trip economy class airfare, visa fees, medical/health/travel insurance, airport transfer, cost of travel for networking visits), and basic project assistance.
application_process: 1. Register on the IGSTC application portal using email addresses. 2. The applicant who starts the application first from the pair is known as the Primary applicant. 3. Primary applicant adds the paired applicant’s details in the application. 4. Paired applicant receives notification and logs in to complete their part. 5. Both applicants jointly access and complete the ‘Paired Project Details’ section. 6. Complete all required sections including financial overview, budget table, activity plan, and upload required documents. 7. Final submission is done by the Primary applicant after all sections are completed by both applicants. 8. Applications must be submitted online via the Application Portal; submissions by other means are not accepted.
deadlines: Varies by programme: WISER and PECFAR have application window from 1st February 2026 to 31st March 2026 (extended to 2nd April 2026, 12:00 Noon IST/CET). Industrial Fellowships: Application Submission – 1st February 2026 to 31st March 2026 (extended to 2nd April 2026, 12:00 Noon IST). Open Call for Workshops: deadlines twice a year – 31st January and 31st July. 2+2 Projects: annual call for proposals (specific dates vary by year).
implementing_agency: Indo-German Science & Technology Centre (IGSTC), a joint initiative by the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India and the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR), Government of Germany
contact_details: Phone: +91-011-26543500 | Email: industrial.fellowship@igstc.org (for Industrial Fellowships), wiser@igstc.org (for WISER), pecfar@igstc.org (for PECFAR) | Mailing Address: Indo-German Science & Technology Centre, Ground Floor, Block – II, Technology Bhavan, New Mehrauli Road, New Delhi – 110016, India

overview: The National Crop Insurance Programme (NCIP) is a government initiative aimed at providing financial support to farmers in the event of crop failure due to natural calamities, pests, or diseases. It seeks to stabilize farm income and encourage the adoption of progressive farming practices and technology. The programme operates through various component schemes and is implemented across India to mitigate risks associated with agriculture.
target_beneficiaries: farmers
eligibility: All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing notified crops in notified areas are eligible for coverage under the National Crop Insurance Programme (NCIP).
benefits: Financial compensation for crop loss due to defined perils such as drought, flood, hailstorm, landslide, pest attack, and disease. The scheme helps maintain creditworthiness of farmers and supports investment in agriculture by reducing risk exposure.
financial_support: Claims are paid based on the extent of crop loss as determined by weather data, remote sensing, or crop cutting experiments. The sum insured is pre-declared and linked to the scale of finance for the crop. Premium is subsidized by the government, with farmers paying a nominal share.
application_process: 1. Farmers enroll for the scheme through designated agencies such as banks, insurance companies, or Common Service Centres (CSCs). 2. Provide land records and sowing details as per the notified crop and area. 3. Pay the applicable premium (after government subsidy). 4. In case of crop loss, notify the concerned authority within the stipulated time. 5. Submit required documents for claim assessment. 6. Claim is processed and paid upon verification of loss.
deadlines: Enrollment is seasonal and aligned with the sowing periods of notified crops. Specific cut-off dates are declared before each season (Kharif/Rabi).
implementing_agency: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

overview: The India-Japan Startup Hub Initiative is a collaborative program under the Startup India initiative aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship by connecting Indian startups with Japanese counterparts. It facilitates cross-border collaboration, knowledge sharing, and market access for startups from both countries. The initiative supports startups through mentorship, networking opportunities, and access to funding and incubation resources in Japan and India.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups must be DPIIT recognised under the Startup India initiative to be eligible for the India-Japan Startup Hub Initiative. The startup should be working towards innovation, development or improvement of products or processes or services, or be a scalable business model with high potential for employment generation or wealth creation. The entity should not have been formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business.
benefits: Startups gain access to mentorship from seasoned experts and successful founders via the MAARG National Mentorship Platform, opportunities to participate in global market linkage programs, handholding support, and exclusive access to international startup events and challenges. They also benefit from representation in mega startup events for greater visibility and business development, and access to private funding networks and venture capital connections.
financial_support: The initiative does not provide direct financial support but facilitates access to funding through connected programs such as the Fund of Funds for Startups, Startup India Seed Fund Scheme, and Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups. Startups can leverage the hub to connect with investors and funding opportunities in Japan and India.
application_process: 1. Register on the Startup India portal at https://www.startupindia.gov.in 2. Complete the BHASKAR registration form with details such as first name, last name, email ID, and nationality to generate a BHASKAR ID 3. Log in to the Startup India Portal using credentials 4. Navigate to the 'Get Recognised' section to apply for DPIIT recognition 5. Fill out the application form detailing the startup’s uniqueness and innovation 6. Upload necessary documents including Certificate of Incorporation, PAN, pitch deck, and business description 7. Submit the form for review 8. Upon recognition, access the India-Japan Startup Hub Initiative through the Startup India portal's programs and challenges section
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: IRDAI Motor Third Party Pooling for EV Startups
overview: The IRDAI Motor Third Party Pooling for EV Startups is a regulatory framework established by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) to facilitate third-party liability insurance coverage for electric vehicle (EV) startups through a pooling mechanism. This scheme aims to address the challenges faced by EV startups in obtaining affordable and accessible motor third-party insurance by spreading risk across insurers. It supports the growth of the EV ecosystem by ensuring compliance with mandatory insurance requirements under the Motor Vehicles Act.
target_beneficiaries: EV startups

It focuses on sectors like textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, agriculture, and services, and includes provisions for market access, investment promotion, skill development, and non-tariff barrier reduction. The scheme operates under bilateral and regional trade agreements signed with countries such as the UK, EU, New Zealand, Oman, and Kenya, with implementation coordinated through the Department of Commerce.

benefits: Beneficiaries gain access to zero-duty or preferential market access in partner countries, enhanced market access in labour-intensive and high-value sectors, opportunities for skill development and training under initiatives like ITEC and 'Study in India', access to investment commitments (e.g., USD 20 billion from New Zealand), support for innovation and technology transfer, facilitation of market entry through faster regulatory approvals (e.g., pharma and medical devices via GMP/GCP recognition), promotion of traditional medicine and AYUSH systems globally, support for Geographical Indications (GI) protection, access to Centres of Excellence for agricultural productivity (e.g., apples, kiwifruit, honey), enhanced mobility for professionals through visa commitments (e.g., 5,000 skilled visas to New Zealand), and support for MSMEs through export readiness programmes, trade-related information linkages, and integration into global value chains.
financial_support: Financial support under the BTPA Export Grants scheme is delivered indirectly through bilateral trade agreements that unlock market access and investment opportunities rather than direct cash grants. Key financial mechanisms include investment commitments from partner countries (e.g., New Zealand’s commitment to facilitate USD 20 billion in investment into India), support for setting up Centres of Excellence in agriculture and technology, facilitation of collateral-free loans under initiatives like #GeMSahay, and support for export credit through ECGC schemes such as Collateral-Free Cover for MSEs up to Rs.10 crore and enhanced cover up to Rs.50 crore 50 crore. The scheme also enables access to government procurement platforms like GeM and supports export promotion through Market Access Initiative (MAI) and Interest Equalisation Scheme (IES).
application_process: 1. Identify relevant bilateral trade agreement (FTA/CEPA) under which your sector or product qualifies for benefits. 2. Avail skill development or training programmes under ITEC or 'Study in India' for skill enhancement. 10. Engage with Indian missions abroad or Export Promotion Councils for business matchmaking and participation in international exhibitions (e.g., Autoexpo Kenya, The Big 5 Construct Kenya).

overview: Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (WBCIS) aims to mitigate the hardship of insured farmers against financial loss from anticipated crop loss due to adverse weather conditions such as rainfall, temperature, wind, and humidity. It uses weather parameters as a proxy for crop yields to compensate cultivators for deemed crop losses. The scheme operates on an 'Area Approach' basis and is implemented through the National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP). WBCIS is part of the broader Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) framework and is administered by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India.
target_beneficiaries: farmers
eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in a notified area during the season who have insurable interest in the crop are eligible. Compulsory coverage applies to loanee farmers (those with Crop Loan/KCC account) and voluntary coverage is available for non-loanee farmers with insurable interest.
benefits: Financial support for crop loss due to weather perils; premium subsidy shared equally by Centre and State; use of technology for yield estimation and claim settlement; access to National Crop Insurance Portal for application and grievance redressal; coverage for prevented sowing, post-harvest losses, localized calamities, and yield losses; claim settlement based on actual weather data from notified Reference Weather Stations.
financial_support: The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged by the Implementing Agency. The rate of insurance charges payable by farmers is: 2% of Sum Insured for Kharif foodgrain and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi foodgrain and oilseed crops, and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops, whichever is less than the actuarial rate. The difference between the actuarial premium rate and the farmer's share is treated as normal premium subsidy, shared equally by Centre and State. Claims are settled based on actual weather data from Reference Weather Stations, with payouts calculated as per term sheets triggered by weather deviations.
application_process: 1. Visit the National Crop Insurance Portal (https://pmfby.gov.in). 2. Click on 'Farmer Corner' and select 'Apply for Crop Insurance by yourself'. 3. Enroll as a new user by selecting stakeholder type (e.g., Farmer). 4. Provide required details and upload necessary documents. 5. Submit the application and note the application ID for tracking. 6. Pay the applicable premium as per the notified rates. 7. Await confirmation and policy issuance.
deadlines: Cut-off date for receipt of proposals: 31st July for Kharif season and 31st December for Rabi season. Declarations from loanee farmers must be submitted within 15 working days after cut-off date, and for non-loanee farmers within seven working days after cut-off date.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India

scheme_name: PMFBY – Crop Insurance for Agri Startups
overview: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is a flagship crop insurance scheme launched by the Government of India in Kharif 2016 to provide affordable and comprehensive crop insurance to farmers against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest stage. The scheme aims to stabilize farmers' income, encourage adoption of innovative agricultural practices, ensure credit flow to the agriculture sector, and protect farmers from production risks. It operates on an 'Area Approach' basis and is implemented through a multi-agency framework involving insurance companies, financial institutions, and government agencies under the guidance of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; loanee farmers; non-loanee farmers; agri-startups
eligibility: All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing the notified crops in the notified areas are eligible for coverage. Compulsory coverage applies to loanee farmers (those availing Crop Loan/KCC account for notified crops during the crop season). Voluntary coverage is available for other farmers not covered under compulsory component who have insurable interest in the crop. Farmers must possess insurable interest in the cultivation of the notified crop in the notified area.
benefits: Financial support for crop loss due to non-preventable risks (natural fire, lightning, storm, hailstorm, cyclone, typhoon, tempest, hurricane, tornado, flood, inundation, landslide, drought, dry spells, pests/diseases), prevented sowing (up to 25% of sum-insured), post-harvest losses (up to 14 days from harvesting for cut & spread crops), localized calamities (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, farm basis of indemnity levels of 80%, 90%) based on threshold, premium subsidy shared equally by Centre and State, technology-enabled claim settlement via mobile apps, remote sensing, YES-TECH, WINDS, and electronic credit to insured bank account.
financial_support: The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged by the Implementing Agency (IA). The rate of Insurance Charges payable by the farmer is: 2.0% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate (whichever is less) for Kharif foodgrain and oilseeds crops; 1.5% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate (whichever is less) for Rabi foodgrain and oilseeds crops; 5% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate (whichever is less) for Kharif and Rabi annual commercial/horticultural crops. The difference between the actuarial premium rate and the farmer's charge is treated as Normal Premium Subsidy, shared equally by the Centre and State. Premium subsidy is paid by the Government to provide full insured amount to farmers against crop loss on account of natural calamities, with no upper limit on Government subsidy.
application_process: 1. Visit the PMFBY portal (https://pmfby.gov.in) or use the Farmer App, WhatsApp Chatbot, or Krishi Rakshak Portal & Helpline (KRPH). 2. Select 'Farmer Corner' and click 'Enroll Now' to apply for crop insurance. 3. Choose stakeholder category (farmer) and user category. 4. Provide required details including mobile number for OTP verification. 5. Upload necessary documents (land records, sowing details, etc.). 6. Pay the applicable premium (2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi, 5% for commercial/horticultural). 7. Submit application and receive acknowledgment. 8. Track application status via 'Application Status' tab using policy ID. 9. For grievances or crop loss reporting, contact KRPH Helpline at 14447 or use WhatsApp Chatbot at 7065514447.
deadlines: Cut-off date for receipt of proposals: 31st July for Kharif season, 31st December for Rabi season. Cut-off date for receipt of declarations of loanee farmers: within 15 working days after cut-off date. Cut-off date for receipt of declarations of non-loanee farmers: within seven working days after cut-off date. Cut-off date for receipt of declarations from designated insurance agents: within two working days after receiving declaration/premium.

benefits: Participants gain practical knowledge in food processing, packaging, marketing, and quality standards; develop business planning and financial literacy skills; strengthen linkages with key departments, technical experts, and financial institutions; improve livelihoods and household incomes; and are empowered as change agents for sustainable rural development through enterprise management training and exposure to food processing facilities and agri-business incubators.
financial_support: The program facilitates access to funding opportunities for agribusiness startups through public-private partnerships and explores financing options including government schemes. It includes a role-play exercise for pitching to investors and provides guidance on commercialization pathways, licensing, partnerships, and spin-offs.
application_process: 1. Create a login to apply for the course and furnish all requisite information. 2. Submit the application online and download the submitted application form. 3. Take a printout of the submitted application form and get appropriate signatures at all signature placeholders including English proficiency certificate, medical report, candidate undertaking form, and employer nomination form. 4. Scan the complete application document and submit physical copies to the Indian High Commission in your country. 5. Email the scanned copy of the executed application form to icrisat-ipfc@icrisat.org with copy to vishwambhar.duche@icrisat.org and babu.potta@icrisat.org.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round for various training programs, with specific deadlines varying per course (e.g., 12 January 2026 for Agri-Entrepreneurship Training for Women and Youth).

scheme_name: ICAR – National Fund for Basic, Strategic and Frontier Application Research
overview: The ICAR – National Fund for Basic, Strategic and Frontier Application Research (NFBSFARA) is a scheme under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) aimed at supporting basic, strategic, and frontier application research in agriculture and allied sectors. The scheme focuses on funding high-impact, innovative research projects that address national agricultural challenges and promote technological advancement in the sector. It supports research initiatives that are fundamental, strategic, and frontier in nature, contributing to long-term agricultural development and innovation.
target_beneficiaries: researchers; scientists; agri-startups; agricultural researchers; agricultural scientists
eligibility: Researchers, scientists, and institutions under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) system, including ICAR institutes, agricultural universities, and recognized research organizations engaged in agricultural research and education, are eligible to apply for funding under the NFBSFARA scheme.
benefits: Financial support for research projects, access to research infrastructure and facilities, opportunities for collaboration with national and international research institutions, capacity building for researchers, and contribution to national agricultural development through innovative research outcomes.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support in the form of grants for approved research projects. The quantum of funding is determined based on the scope, duration, and requirements of the proposed research project, as evaluated by the expert review committee. Funds are disbursed in installments based on project milestones and progress reports.
application_process: 1. Identify a research proposal aligned with the objectives of NFBSFARA. 2. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, methodology, budget, and expected outcomes. 3. Submit the proposal through the designated ICAR portal or nodal office. 4. The proposal undergoes technical and financial review by an expert committee. 5. Upon approval, funds are sanctioned and disbursed in phases. 6. Progress reports and utilization certificates are submitted periodically. 7. Final submission of project completion report and audited utilization certificate.
implementing_agency: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

scheme_name: NABI – National Agri-Food Biotechnology Institute Incubation
overview: The National Agri-Food Biotechnology Institute (NABI), formerly known as National Agri-Food and Biomanufacturing Institute, is an autonomous institute under the Department of Biotechnology, Government of India. Established in 2010, NABI focuses on research and innovation in agricultural biotechnology, food and nutritional biotechnology, human resource development, and technology transfer. The institute aims to catalyze transformation in the agri-food sector through value-added products, skilled human resource development, and translational science.
target_beneficiaries: startups; agri-startups; researchers; scientists; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Outstanding scientists working abroad who are interested in applying under the Prime Minister's Research Fellowship (PMRF) Scheme 2026 in the Young Research Fellows, Senior Fellows and Research Chairs categories, with an outstanding track record of high-impact publications, patents, technology development, or product innovation in areas aligned with BRIC-NABI's research mandate.
benefits: Opportunity to work on translational research, biofortification, designer crops, and functional foods aimed at enhancing nutritional security and promoting sustainable food systems; access to NABI's research infrastructure and facilities; collaboration with national and international organizations; potential for technology transfer and outreach programs.
financial_support: The evidence does not specify financial support details such as quantum, type, or mechanism of financial support for the incubation scheme.
application_process: 1. Interested candidates are requested to submit a research proposal (maximum 3 pages) along with their detailed curriculum vitae to edoffice@nabi.res.in on or before 2 July 2026. 2. For detailed information on the PMRF Scheme 2026, please visit: https://pmrc.education.gov.in/. 3. Applications are invited under the Prime Minister's Research Fellowship (PMRC) scheme 2026.
deadlines: on or before 2 July 2026
implementing_agency: Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science & Technology, Govt. of India

scheme_name: Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) Incubation Scheme
overview: The Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) Incubation Scheme supports HealthTech startups by providing access to CDRI's research infrastructure, expertise, and facilities for drug discovery and development. The scheme aims to foster innovation in the pharmaceutical sector by enabling startups to leverage CDRI's capabilities in formulation development, pharmacokinetics, toxicity screening, and analytical services. It is designed to bridge the gap between academic research and commercialization, particularly for MSMEs and startups in the pharmaceutical domain.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME
eligibility: The scheme is open to MSMEs and startups operating in the pharmaceutical sector that require support in formulation development, analytical method validation, pharmacokinetics, toxicity screening, or access to specialized instruments such as SAIF, X-ray crystallography, or Biolayer Interferometry. Applicants must be engaged in drug discovery or development activities aligned with national health priorities.
benefits: Startups and MSMEs gain access to CDRI's state-of-the-art facilities including the Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facility (SAIF), Biological Screening units, Toxicity and Safety testing (GLP-compliant), Formulation Development and Pharmacokinetics suite, X-Ray Crystallography, National Laboratory Animal Center, and Biolayer Interferometry. These services support end-to-end drug development from early screening to preclinical validation. The collaboration is funded jointly by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) and the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR).
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or funding to startups. Instead, it offers access to CDRI's research infrastructure and technical expertise on a collaborative or service basis, with costs potentially subsidized or shared under the DSIR-CSIR joint funding model. Specific fee structures or waivers are not detailed in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Visit the CDRI CRTDH portal at https://cdri.res.in/crtdh-home 2. Review the available services and facilities under the CRTDH initiative 3. Initiate collaboration by contacting CDRI through the provided contact channels 4. Submit a proposal outlining the required support (e.g., formulation development, analytical testing, pharmacokinetics) 5. Undergo technical evaluation by CDRI experts 6. Execute a collaboration agreement or service contract 7. Access the agreed-upon facilities and expertise 8. Receive progress reports and final deliverables as per the agreement
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) - Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow
contact_details: Email: recruit.cdri@csir.res.in (as referenced in recruitment notices; general inquiries may be directed via the CDRI website)

overview: The DBT–BIRAC BIONEST scheme supports the establishment and scaling of bio-incubators across India to foster biotech innovation and entrepreneurship. It provides grant-in-aid funding for capital and operational expenses to academic institutions, research organizations, and state government bodies to create incubation facilities that offer startups access to infrastructure, mentorship, IP management, and networking opportunities. The program aims to bridge the gap in early-stage support for biotech startups by enabling incubators to nurture ventures from ideation to commercialization.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; biotech startups; life science startups
eligibility: Indian institutions including Universities/ Research Institutes/ Colleges/ Management Institutes/ Business Schools/ Business Incubators/Biotech-Parks/State government S & T bodies/ Biotech State Councils/Research Hospitals. Incorporation of an Indian legal entity* is recommended for Bioincubators, however it is not a must for the new applicants especially from Indian Institutions including Universities/ Research Institutes/Colleges/ Management Institutes/ Business Schools etc. *Private Company/ Not for profit Section 8 company/Trust/Society - The legal entities under the relevant Law of India having at least 51% Indian (Citizen) stakeholders (owners/partners/trustees/members/associates/directors etc. as applicable).
benefits: Incubation space for startups and entrepreneurs, access to high-end infrastructure and specialized equipment, business mentorship, IP and technology management support for Technology management, legal and regulatory guidance, resource mobilization, networking platform, technical and business mentorship, access to specialized services for IP and Technology management, legal support, certifications, validation, regulatory requirements.
financial_support: The BIRAC funding for the BIRAC BioNEST Centres will be done in alignment with the Government’s umbrella scheme ‘Biotechnology Research Innovation and Entrepreneurship Development’ (Bio-RIDE). The funding support from BIRAC will be in the form of grant in aid for both Capital and Operational expenses and will be based on the need and scope of the project as adjudged by the BioNEST committee. Private entities/Institutions - Minimum contribution of 30% will be required for the total project cost by the applicant. Funding to Government entities shall be done as per the following categories: Government Academic Institutions (Centre/State -owned): Support shall be provided as Grant-in-aid; Central Government owned Section -8 company (ies): Support shall be provided as Grant-in-aid; State Government -Owned Section -8 company(ies) /Councils: Minimum contribution of 50% from the applicant is required (for applications under Category 4).
