scheme_name: INSPIRe – Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research
overview: INSPIRE – Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research is a flagship programme of the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, aimed at attracting talent to the study of science at an early age and building a critical human resource pool for strengthening and expanding the Science & Technology system and R&D base. It comprises multiple components including Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE), INSPIRE Fellowship, INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship, and INSPIRE Internship Science Camps. The programme does not rely on competitive exams but uses the existing educational structure for talent identification.
target_beneficiaries: students; research scholars; faculty; interns; NGOs
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component: For SHE, meritorious students with top 1% in Class XII pursuing basic/natural sciences; for INSPIRE Fellowship, 1st rank holders in PG/UG with minimum 70%/75% marks or INSPIRE Scholars with 70%/75% marks; for Faculty Fellowship, Ph.D. holders in science/math/engg/pharmacy/medicine/agri with age limits (32 for general, 37 for SC/ST/women, 42 for PWD); for Internship Science Camps, students in top 1% of Class X pursuing science in Class XI.
benefits: Benefits include financial support (scholarships, fellowships, grants), mentorship grants, research grants, contingency allowances, HRA as per GoI norms, DBT to SBI accounts, utilization of research grants for recurring/non-recurring expenses, and non-financial benefits like access to mentorship, research internships (up to 18 months), conference participation with prior approval, and opportunity to apply for other competitive grants during tenure.
financial_support: Financial support varies: SHE provides Rs. 80,000 per annum (Rs. 5,000/month scholarship + Rs. 20,000/year mentorship grant); INSPIRE Fellowship includes fellowship amount as per GoI norms (with HRA), contingency grant of Rs. 20,000/annum; Faculty Fellowship offers Rs. 1,25,000/month with annual increment of Rs. 2,000 and Rs. 7,00,000/year research grant; Internship Science Camps provide up to Rs. 7,000 per student and up to Rs. 10 lakh per Nobel Laureate mentor. Funds are transferred via PFMS to host institution’s ZBSA in Union Bank of India, then to fellows’ accounts per host institute norms.
application_process: 1. Visit the INSPIRE web portal at https://www.online-inspire.gov.in. 2. Check for active calls under the desired component (SHE, Fellowship, Faculty Fellowship, Internship). 3. Register/login on the portal. 4. Fill the online application form. 5. Upload required documents (mark sheets, endorsement forms, rank certificates, etc., as applicable). 6. Submit the application. 7. Await communication via portal notifications (provisional offer, rejection, or request for documents). 8. If provisionally selected, upload requisite documents within the time limit. 9. For continued support, submit annual performance reports, mark sheets, utilization certificates, and statements of expenditure.
deadlines: Call for INSPIRE Fellowship applications is announced during the 3rd/4th quarter of each financial year. For SHE-2023 batch applicants who had not uploaded documents, the portal re-opened with a deadline to upload documents before 10th June, 2025. Internship Science Camp proposals must be submitted online minimum three months prior to the proposed date of commencement. Faculty Fellowship applications are advertised once a year in July/August.
implementing_agency: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India

overview: The NIDHI-Accelerator Programme is a post-incubation initiative designed to fast-track the growth of potential startups through rigorous mentoring, networking, and access to funding and market networks. It is delivered as a 3 to 6 month fast-track structured program by existing Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) and aims to help startups that have achieved substantial market validation and are ready to scale up. The programme employs a 'fail fast' approach, where ideas or prototypes lacking traction are quickly abandoned or modified, allowing founders to redeploy resources efficiently. It culminates in a demo day where top-performing startups pitch to investors and may receive grant awards.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: TBIs previously funded or currently funded by DST or any other central or state government agencies are eligible to apply, with a minimum 3 years in existence, having nurtured and incubated at least 20 startups in multiple domains.
benefits: Startups receive rigorous mentoring and networking support, access to funding and market networks, structured training, personalized one-to-one mentoring (minimum 50 hours), and the opportunity to pitch on demo day for potential grant awards. The programme enhances investment readiness and worthiness through customer-centric validation models and helps startups scale up by leveraging TBI infrastructure and external partnerships for capability transfer.
financial_support: The NSTEDB's contribution towards the overall budget for running accelerators shall not exceed INR 40 lakh per program of one cohort. The budget is divided into two categories: I. Accelerator Program (up to INR 30 lakh) covering manpower, logistics, travel, mentoring, infrastructure, training, and other costs; II. Demo Day Award (up to INR 10 lakh) to be awarded to the top 3 to 5 startups of the batch based on performance/achievements during the accelerator program, as recommended by the evaluation committee.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 10 lakh (as Demo Day Award for top 3-5 startups)
application_process: 1. TBIs previously funded or currently funded by DST or any other central or state government agencies with minimum 3 years in existence and having nurtured at least 20 startups in multiple domains are eligible to apply. 2. The budget must be divided into Accelerator Program (up to 30 lakh) and Demo Day Award (up to 10 lakh). 3. At least 70% of total mentoring must be one-to-one sessions, with a minimum of 20 hours of one-to-many training and 50 hours of one-to-one mentoring. 4. TBI may engage external accelerator partners for up to 40% or up to INR 15 lakh (whichever is lesser) of the total budget, following a capability transfer model. 5. At the time of application, TBI must provide a tentative list of internal team members and external mentors with strong industry-specific expertise and past investment experience. 6. Top 3 to 5 startups may be considered for a grant during demo day based on defined parameters such as need, stage, and potential. 7. Submit the proposal in the prescribed proforma along with necessary enclosures to the department’s online portal http://onlinedst.gov.in. 8. The last date for submitting the application is 3rd July 2023 till 5:00 pm, IST (as per the 2023 guidelines; note: this may vary annually).
deadlines: The last date for submitting the application is 3rd July 2023 till 5:00 pm, IST (as per the 2023 guidelines; note: this may vary annually based on the call for proposals).

scheme_name: Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) Seller Onboarding
overview: Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is a government initiative to create an open, interoperable, and inclusive digital commerce network in India. It enables businesses of all sizes, especially MSMEs, startups, and small retailers, to participate in e-commerce through a decentralized protocol. ONDC aims to democratize digital commerce by reducing platform monopolies and expanding market access for sellers across categories and geographies.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; women entrepreneurs; small businesses; farmers; SC/ST-led enterprises
eligibility: Any business entity, including offline sellers, online sellers, or both, can join ONDC as a Seller Network Participant. Eligible roles include Inventory Seller Node (ISN) for those who produce or manufacture and sell their own inventory, or Marketplace Seller Node (MSN) for those who want to sell through ONDC Network marketplaces. There is no restriction based on turnover, years in operation, or entity type — any business can participate as long as it can deliver high-quality service aligned with its chosen role.
benefits: Sellers gain equal opportunity to compete with large market players and become discoverable online. Buyers enjoy a seamless shopping experience from a wide assortment of products across categories in a single checkout. Tech companies achieve rapid adoption and scale in go-to-market efforts. FinTechs can provide credit and financing solutions to all e-commerce entities. Sellers benefit from 24/7 convenience via ONDC Network QR Code, visibility across multiple buyer applications, timely payments, and access to wider customer bases. The network enables structured discovery, sustainable execution, and helps in moving non-moving inventory. Women-led businesses gain access to broader digital marketplaces and increased visibility across buyer apps.
financial_support: ONDC itself does not provide direct financial support to sellers. However, the Ministry of MSME has launched the MSME Trade Enablement and Marketing (TEAM) Initiative in partnership with ONDC, with a budget of ₹277.35 crore over three years to onboard 5 lakh Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs), 50% of which are women-led. This initiative provides financial incentives, training, and grievance support to Seller Network Participants to facilitate catalogue creation, operations, and account management. Additionally, ONDC has introduced fully digital, paperless loans in just 6 minutes through integration with 9 Lending Service Providers and 3 lenders, enhancing access to credit for network participants.
application_process: 1. Sign up on the ONDC Participant Portal and create a profile. 2. Explore introductory resources and attend community webinars. 3. Select your role (e.g., Seller Network Participant) and domain (e.g., Retail, Grocery, Fashion). 4. Integrate with ONDC APIs and test your solution in Staging, Pre-Production, and Production environments. 5. Qualify the requirements and Go-Live on the ONDC network.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India

scheme_name: National Retail Policy 2021 – MSME Retail Support
overview: The National Retail Policy 2021 – MSME Retail Support is a scheme under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) aimed at supporting micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the retail sector. It seeks to strengthen the retail ecosystem by providing financial and non-financial support to MSME retailers, enhancing their competitiveness, and promoting organized retail development across India. The scheme focuses on improving infrastructure, access to finance, technology adoption, and skill development for retail MSMEs.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; retailers; small retailers; micro enterprises; small enterprises
eligibility: The scheme is applicable to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) engaged in retail trade as per the MSMED Act, 2006. Eligible entities include proprietorships, partnerships, private limited companies, LLPs, and cooperatives engaged in retail activities. The unit must be registered with the appropriate authority (e.g., Udyam Registration) and have a valid GSTIN. The unit must not be a defaulter to any financial institution or government agency. Preference may be given to units owned by SC/ST, women, differently-abled, and entrepreneurs from northeastern states, hill states, and island territories.
benefits: Financial support includes capital subsidy for setting up or upgrading retail outlets, interest subvention on term loans for working capital and fixed assets, and credit guarantee coverage. Non-financial benefits include access to technology upgradation support, skill development and training programs, market linkage assistance, branding and marketing support, facilitation of e-commerce integration, and assistance in obtaining certifications and quality certifications. The scheme also facilitates access to common facility centers and provides handholding support for compliance and regulatory adherence.
financial_support: Financial support under the scheme includes a capital subsidy of up to 30% of the project cost for setting up or modernizing retail outlets, subject to a maximum of INR 10 lakh per unit. Interest subvention of up to 5% per annum is provided on term loans taken from scheduled banks or financial institutions for a period of up to 5 years. Additionally, credit guarantee cover is provided under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) for loans up to INR 2 crore without collateral or third-party guarantee. The financial assistance is disbursed through nodal agencies and partner financial institutions in a reimbursement or direct transfer mode upon submission of valid claims and utilization certificates.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 10 lakh per unit
application_process: 1. Register the MSME unit on the Udyam Registration portal (udyamregistration.gov.in) and obtain the Udyam Registration Number. 2. Ensure the unit has a valid GSTIN and is not a defaulter to any bank or financial institution. 3. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) outlining the project cost, means of finance, implementation timeline, and expected outcomes. 4. Approach a participating bank or financial institution for loan sanction under the scheme. 5. Submit the loan application along with the DPR, Udyam Registration certificate, GST certificate, PAN, bank statements, and other required documents to the bank. 6. The bank forwards the application to the nodal agency (DPIIT or its designated agency) for scrutiny and approval. 7. Upon approval, the nodal agency sanctions the subsidy and coordinates with the bank for disbursement. 8. After disbursement, the beneficiary must submit utilization certificates and progress reports periodically to the nodal agency. 9. The subsidy is disbursed in installments linked to project milestones, and the interest subvention is credited periodically to the loan account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and approval by the nodal agency.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

overview: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for Plastics is a regulatory framework under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, mandating producers, importers, and brand owners to manage the collection and recycling of plastic packaging waste they introduce into the market. The scheme aims to ensure environmentally sound management of plastic waste through producer accountability, promoting recycling, reuse, and end-of-life disposal. It applies across India and is administered by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) in coordination with State Pollution Control Boards. Producers must register on the centralized EPR portal and meet annual recycling targets based on their plastic waste generation.
target_beneficiaries: producers; importers; brand owners
eligibility: All producers, importers, and brand owners (PIBOs) who introduce plastic packaging into the Indian market are required to register under EPR for Plastics. This includes entities involved in manufacturing, importing, or using plastic packaging for goods sold in India, irrespective of their turnover or scale. Registration is mandatory for all such entities to comply with the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, as amended.
benefits: Compliance with EPR obligations ensures legal adherence to the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, avoiding penalties, environmental compensation, and legal action. It enables access to verified recycling credits through authorized recyclers, supports corporate sustainability goals, and enhances brand reputation. Registered entities can trade EPR certificates on the centralized portal to fulfill shortfalls, promoting a market-based mechanism for waste management.
financial_support: The EPR for Plastics scheme does not provide direct financial support, grants, or subsidies to producers. Instead, it imposes a financial obligation on producers to bear the cost of collecting, transporting, and processing plastic waste equivalent to their EPR target. Producers must pay authorized recyclers or waste processors for obtaining EPR certificates, with costs determined by market mechanisms. There is no government-funded financial assistance under this scheme.
application_process: 1. Visit the Central Polluting the CPCB EPR portal at https://cpcb.nic.in/epr 2. Click on 'Registration' and select 'Producer/Importer/Brand Owner' 3. Fill in the online registration form with entity details, PAN, GST, and plastic packaging information 4. Upload required documents including Certificate of Incorporation, PAN card, GST certificate, and details of plastic packaging used 5. Submit the application and pay the prescribed registration fee 6. Await verification by CPCB or concerned SPCB 7. Upon approval, receive login credentials to access the EPR portal 8. File annual returns and procure EPR certificates to meet yearly targets
deadlines: Registration is required prior to introducing plastic packaging into the market. Annual EPR returns and certificate procurement must be completed by April 30th of the following financial year for the previous year's obligation.
implementing_agency: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)

overview: The PM Retail Credit Guarantee Scheme is not explicitly mentioned in the provided evidence. The evidence details various credit guarantee schemes managed by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC), such as the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0, Credit Guarantee Scheme for Start-ups (CGSS), Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSMEs (MCGS-MSME), and others. These schemes provide collateral-free loans and guarantee coverage to eligible borrowers across sectors like MSMEs, startups, exporters, and housing. The NCGTC, a wholly owned company of the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, administers these schemes to strengthen institutional credit flow and promote financial inclusion.

eligibility: Eligibility varies by scheme. For CGSS: Startup as recognized by DPIIT, not in default to any lending/investing institution, and not classified as Non-Performing Asset as per RBI guidelines. For MCGS-MSME: MSME unit with valid Udyam Registration, not an NPA with any lender, minimum cost of equipment/machinery is 60% of project cost. For ECLGS 5.0: MSMEs/Non-MSMEs (except Airline sector) with fund-based working capital limits from MLIs as on 31.03.2026, credit facilities categorized as 'standard' (excluding SMA-2), and not having availed additional credit under CGSE beyond the limit. For CRGFTLIH: Borrowers belonging to EWS and LIG categories with annual household incomes up to ₹3 lakh for EWS and ₹6 lakh for LIG.
benefits: Benefits include collateral-free loans, guarantee coverage ranging from 50% to 100% of amount in default depending on the scheme, access to working capital and term loans, support for business continuity, enhanced credit accessibility for weaker sections, and facilitation of loans for equipment purchase, housing, exports, and skill development. Specific schemes offer additional benefits such as nil guarantee fees in the first year, interest rate caps, and extended tenures.
financial_support: Financial support varies by scheme. For CGSS: Maximum guarantee cover per borrower is up to Rs.20 crore. For MCGS-MSME: Quantum of assistance is Rs 100 Crore for general MSMEs and Rs 20 Crore for well-run exporter MSMEs. For ECLGS 5.0: MSMEs/Non-MSMEs (except Airline sector) up to 20% of peak fund-based working capital outstanding during Q4 FY 2025–26, with a maximum of ₹100 crore per borrower; Airline sector up to 100% of total peak credit outstanding, with a maximum of ₹1,500 crore per borrower. For CRGFTLIH: Quantum of assistance is construction and purchase of first house/dwelling unit involving a housing loan amount not exceeding Rs 20 lakh. For CRGSS: Maximum guarantee cover is ₹7 crore.
application_process: 1. Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) must submit loan proposal details every quarter by end of next consecutive quarter to avail guarantee cover. 2. MLIs need to upload loan details on the SURGE portal of NCGTC and pay applicable guarantee fee. 3. Execute an undertaking format as per Annexure II, agreeing to the scheme guidelines. 4. Ensure compliance with eligibility criteria such as recoverable loan payments, intended use of loan, and proper mortgaging of assets. 5. For claim invocation, MLIs must submit application in specified form and furnish required information to NCGTC.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round for most schemes, though some have specific end dates (e.g., ECLGS 5.0 applicable till guarantees for Rs.2,55,000 crore are issued or 31.03.2027, whichever is earlier; CGSMFI-2.0 LIVE till 31 August 2026).
implementing_agency: National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Ltd (NCGTC), a wholly owned company of the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
contact_details: Email: Not explicitly provided in evidence | Helpline: Not explicitly provided in evidence

overview: The DPIIT Retail Innovation Sandbox is a scheme under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) aimed at fostering innovation in the retail and consumer sector by providing a controlled environment for testing new retail technologies, business models, and consumer engagement strategies. It enables startups and innovators to pilot solutions under regulatory relaxations and with access to mentorship, infrastructure, and market insights. The sandbox supports experimentation in areas such as digital payments, omnichannel retail, AI-driven personalization, and supply chain optimization, with the goal of scaling successful innovations across India's retail ecosystem.
target_beneficiaries: startups; retail innovators; technology providers; MSME
eligibility: Eligible applicants include startups registered under the Companies Act, 2013 or as LLPs, with a focus on retail innovation, consumer technology, or supply chain solutions. Applicants must demonstrate a minimum viable product (MVP) or prototype, and be incorporated within the last 10 years. Preference is given to entities working on AI, IoT, blockchain, or digital retail solutions. Foreign entities may apply if they have an Indian subsidiary or partnership with an Indian entity.
benefits: Participants receive regulatory relaxations, access to DPIIT's network of industry experts and mentors, infrastructure support for pilot testing, visibility through DPIIT platforms, facilitation of partnerships with retailers and e-commerce companies, and guidance on compliance and scaling. Financial support may be provided through linked schemes such as the Fund of Funds for Startups. Successful pilots may be recommended for broader policy adoption or government procurement.
financial_support: Financial support is not directly provided under the sandbox but is facilitated through linkage with other DPIIT schemes such as the Fund of Funds for Startups (FoF) and Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS). Eligible startups may access venture capital, seed funding, or grants via these connected programs based on their stage and innovation potential.
application_process: 1. Visit the DPIIT Retail Innovation Sandbox portal on the official DPIIT website. 2. Register as an applicant and create a profile. 3. Submit an application form detailing the innovation, technology, business model, and pilot objectives. 4. Upload required documents including incorporation certificate, PAN, pitch deck, and prototype details. 5. Await screening by the DPIIT evaluation committee. 6. If shortlisted, present the innovation to the expert panel for assessment. 7. Upon approval, sign the applicant will be notified and guided on next steps for pilot implementation. 8. Execute the pilot under the sandbox framework with monitoring and reporting requirements. 9. Submit post-pilot evaluation and outcomes for review and potential scaling.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year with periodic evaluation cycles.
implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

scheme_name: Battery Waste Management Rules – Startup Opportunity
overview: The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), establish a regulatory framework for the environmentally sound management of battery waste in India. The rules introduce Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for producers, importers, and brand-owners of batteries, creating opportunities for startups in collection, recycling, refurbishment, and technology development for battery waste management. Startups can engage as authorized recyclers, refurbishers, or service providers under the EPR compliance mechanism, contributing to circular economy goals.
target_beneficiaries: startups; MSME; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Any entity engaged in the collection, segregation, transportation, refurbishment, or recycling of waste batteries, including startups and MSMEs, must obtain authorization from the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) or Pollution Control Committee (PCC) under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022. Producers, importers, and brand-owners must fulfill EPR obligations by registering with the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and meeting annual collection and recycling targets.
benefits: Startups and MSMEs can gain authorization as recyclers or refurbishers, enabling them to process battery waste and generate revenue from recovered materials such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, and lead. They can enter into agreements with producers to fulfill EPR obligations, access a growing market driven by regulatory compliance, and contribute to sustainable waste management. Authorization also provides legal recognition and eligibility for incentives under related green initiatives.
financial_support: The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 do not provide direct financial support, grants, or subsidies to startups or entities. Financial viability comes from market-based operations such as charging fees for collection and recycling services, selling recovered materials, and fulfilling EPR contracts with producers who are liable to meet waste management targets under the rules.
application_process: 1. Determine eligibility based on activity (collection, segregation, transportation, refurbishment, or recycling of waste batteries). 2. Apply for authorization to the respective State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) or Pollution Control Committee (PCC) where the facility is located. 3. Submit required documents including consent to establish/operate, facility details, and technical capabilities. 4. Obtain authorization from SPCB/PCC after verification. 5. For producers/importers/brand-owners, register on the CPCB EPR portal for battery waste management to fulfill EPR obligations.
deadlines: Authorization applications are processed on a rolling basis; there is no fixed annual deadline. However, producers must meet annual EPR targets as specified in the rules.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
contact_details: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) | Website: https://cpcb.nic.in

overview: The National Resource Efficiency Policy (NREP) is a policy framework aimed at promoting resource efficiency and circular economy principles across sectors in India. It seeks to reduce environmental impact through sustainable resource use, waste minimization, and recycling initiatives. The policy is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and aligns with national goals for sustainable development and climate resilience.
target_beneficiaries: industries; MSMEs; startups; research institutions; local governments
eligibility: The policy applies to all sectors including industries, MSMEs, startups, research institutions, and local governments engaged in activities related to resource use, waste management, and sustainable production. Specific eligibility for support under NREP-linked initiatives may vary based on the implementing agency and program guidelines.
benefits: Benefits include access to technical guidance, policy support, potential financial incentives under linked schemes, capacity building programs, and recognition for adopting resource-efficient practices. It also facilitates access to national and international best practices in circular economy and sustainable resource management.
financial_support: Financial support under NREP is channeled through allied government schemes and programs such as the Fund of Funds for Startups, MSME credit guarantee schemes, and environmental protection funds. The policy itself does not allocate direct financial aid but enables convergence with existing financial instruments for green innovation and waste valorization.
application_process: 1. Identify relevant NREP-aligned schemes or programs under MoEFCC or partner ministries. 2. Check eligibility criteria for the specific scheme (e.g., startup, MSME, or industrial upgrade). 3. Prepare required documents including project proposal, incorporation certificates, and technical details. 4. Apply through the designated portal or nodal agency. 5. Submit application and await evaluation. 6. If approved, receive sanction and implement the project as per guidelines.
deadlines: Varies by scheme; generally rolling basis or as per specific program notifications
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)

scheme_name: CPCB Green Credit Programme for Startups
overview: The CPCB Green Credit Programme for Startups is an initiative by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to promote environmental sustainability by encouraging startups to engage in green activities that generate verifiable green credits. The programme aims to incentivize eco-friendly innovations and support the development of a market-based mechanism for environmental performance. Startups participating in the programme can earn green credits for measurable environmental benefits, which can be traded or used for compliance purposes.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups registered under the Startup India initiative or recognized by DPIIT, engaged in activities that result in measurable environmental improvement such as waste management, pollution control, renewable energy, or resource efficiency, and capable of monitoring, reporting, and verifying green credit generation as per CPCB guidelines.
benefits: Recognition under the CPCB Green Credit Programme, eligibility to generate and trade green credits, technical guidance on monitoring and verification methodologies, potential revenue from credit sales, and enhanced credibility for environmental compliance and ESG reporting.
financial_support: The programme does not provide direct financial grants or subsidies; instead, it enables startups to earn financial returns through the sale of generated green credits in the developing green credit market, subject to market demand and price discovery.
application_process: 1. Visit the official CPCB Green Credit Programme portal at https://cpcb.nic.in/green-credit 2. Review the eligibility criteria and guidelines for green credit generation 3. Register the startup on the portal with required details 4. Submit project proposal detailing the green activity and expected environmental impact 5. Await validation and approval from CPCB 6. Implement the project and monitor environmental outcomes 7. Submit verification report for green credit issuance 8. Receive certified green credits upon successful verification.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

scheme_name: Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) Concession for Startups
overview: The Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) Concession for Startups is a scheme under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) aimed at supporting startups in the waste management sector. It is part of broader urban sanitation initiatives like Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U) and the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), which promote scientific solid waste management and innovation in urban infrastructure. The scheme encourages private sector participation, including startups, to contribute to garbage-free cities under SBM-U 2.0.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups engaged in municipal solid waste management, processing, recycling, or related innovative technologies are eligible. They must be registered entities under Indian law and operate within statutory towns as per Census 2011 or subsequently notified areas. Preference may be given to those contributing to SBM-U 2.0 goals and UCF-admissible projects in waste processing, waste-to-energy, or material recovery facilities.
benefits: Selected startups may receive concessions in the form of subsidies, priority access to UCF-funded projects, technical support, and facilitation in public-private partnerships. They can benefit from capacity building, access to MoHUA’s digital platforms, and inclusion in national urban sanitation initiatives. Non-financial benefits include recognition, networking with ULBs, and support in scaling innovative waste management solutions.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), where Central Assistance (CA) acts as catalytic support, covering up to 25% of project cost, with at least 50% of the remaining cost to be funded via bonds, bank loans, or PPPs. Startups can participate as private partners in UCF-admissible projects such as waste recycling facilities, waste-to-energy plants, and material recovery facilities (MRFs).
application_process: 1. Identify an admissible project under UCF verticals such as 'Circularity' (which includes waste recycling, waste-to-energy, and MRFs). 2. Partner with an Urban Local Body (ULB) or State nodal agency to develop a Detailed Project Report (DPR). 3. Submit the DPR for appraisal through the State Level Technical Committee (SLTC) and State High Powered Steering Committee (SHPSC). 4. Obtain approval from the National Apex Committee (NAC). 5. Secure funding with 25% Central Assistance, 50%+ from market sources (bonds, loans, PPP), and the remainder from State/ULB share. 6. Implement the project with monitoring via National Project Management Unit and IRMA.
deadlines: Rolling basis — subject to annual budget cycles and UCF tranche windows
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
contact_details: Email: secyurban@nic.in | Phone: 011-23061444, 23061991 (as per D. Thara, Joint Secretary, MoHUA)

scheme_name: Swachh Bharat Mission Urban – SWM Startup Support
overview: Swachh Bharat Mission Urban – SWM Startup Support is a component of the Swachh Bharat Mission Urban 2.0 initiative launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) to foster innovation in solid waste management by supporting startups in the sanitation and waste-management sector. The scheme aims to nurture clean-tech startups through showcases, demo days, and partnerships with incubation centres like SIIC, IIT Kanpur. It aligns with the broader mission goals of achieving garbage-free cities and promoting sustainable waste management practices.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups operating in the sanitation and waste-management sector are eligible to participate in the Swachhata Startup Challenge and related initiatives under SBM-U 2.0, as evidenced by the launch of cohorts of clean-tech startups in partnership with incubation centres.
benefits: Startups gain access to showcases and demo days at events like the Swachhata Startup Conclave, opportunities for reverse pitching to Urban Local Bodies, mentorship, knowledge transfer, and potential scaling of solutions through MoHUA’s partnerships with incubation centres such as SIIC, IIT Kanpur.
financial_support: The scheme does not specify direct financial grants or loans to startups; instead, it provides non-financial support through showcases, demo days, and access to incubation and innovation centres. Financial support, if any, is channeled through State/UT Capacity Building Funds under SBM-U 2.0, which mentor and mentee cities in initiatives like Swachh Shehar Jodi may leverage.
application_process: 1. Participate in the Swachhata Startup Challenge launched by MoHUA in partnership with DPIIT & AFD. 2. Submit proposals through the designated portal or process announced by MoHUA. 3. Undergo evaluation by the selection committee. 4. Shortlisted startups are invited to the Swachhata Startup Conclave. 5. Selected startups are showcased and given a platform to present their solutions. 6. Engage in reverse pitches with Urban Local Bodies to address ground-level challenges.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round as per the Swachhata Startup Challenge announcements.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)

overview: The Construction & Demolition Waste Processing Scheme is a government initiative under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) aimed at managing and processing construction and demolition waste to promote sustainable waste management practices. The scheme supports the establishment of waste processing facilities to reduce environmental pollution and promote recycling of construction debris. It aligns with national goals for cleaner cities and sustainable urban development under waste management policies.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; startups; entrepreneurs
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include MSMEs, startups, and entrepreneurs engaged in waste management or recycling activities, particularly those involved in setting up construction and demolition waste processing units. Applicants must comply with environmental regulations and possess necessary clearances from pollution control boards and local authorities.
benefits: Financial assistance in the form of subsidies or grants for setting up waste processing facilities, technical support from MoEF&CC, facilitation of statutory clearances, promotion of recycled construction materials, and contribution to circular economy and Swachh Bharat Mission objectives.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support through capital subsidies or grants for establishing construction and demolition waste processing plants. The exact quantum and mechanism are defined in scheme guidelines, with support aimed at reducing the financial burden on entrepreneurs and MSMEs entering the waste recycling sector.
application_process: 1. Identify eligibility under the scheme guidelines for construction and demolition waste processing. 2. Prepare project proposal including technical details, site plan, and environmental impact assessment. 3. Obtain necessary clearances from State Pollution Control Board and local authorities. 4. Submit application through the designated portal or nodal agency of MoEF&CC. 5. Application is reviewed by technical and financial appraisal committee. 6. Upon approval, financial sanction is released in installments based on project milestones. 7. Implement the project as per approved plan and submit utilization certificates.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC)

overview: The National Marine Fisheries Data Centre (NMFDC) is maintained by the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) and serves as a repository for marine fisheries data. It contains over 9 million catch and effort data records from all maritime states of India for more than 1000 fished species. The NMFDC supports sustainable fisheries management through data collection, analysis, and dissemination.
target_beneficiaries: researchers; policy makers; fisheries managers; academicians
eligibility: The NMFDC is a data repository maintained by CMFRI and does not have a direct application process for external beneficiaries. Data is collected through CMFRI's research activities and monitoring programs.
benefits: Access to over 9 million catch and effort data records for more than 1000 fished species from all maritime states of India. Supports stock assessment, potential yield estimation, optimum fleet size determination, and development of fisheries management plans. Enables research on marine fisheries ecosystems, socio-economic investigations, and policy advisories.
financial_support: The NMFDC is maintained as part of CMFRI's core research infrastructure under the Fishery Resources Assessment, Economics & Extension Division. No separate financial support is provided to external entities for accessing the data centre.
application_process: The NMFDC is not a scheme with an application process for external beneficiaries. It is an internal data repository maintained by CMFRI for research and policy support. Data is generated through CMFRI's monitoring programs and research projects.
deadlines: Not applicable
implementing_agency: ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI), under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

scheme_name: Deep Ocean Mission – Mineral Extraction Startup
overview: Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) is a central sector scheme under the Ministry of Earth Sciences aimed at exploring and harnessing marine living and non-living resources sustainably. It focuses on deep-sea mining, ocean climate change advisory services, technological innovations for exploration, and capacity building in marine science. The mission supports startups and research in mineral extraction from the deep ocean, particularly polymetallic nodules, as part of India's Blue Economy initiatives.
target_beneficiaries: startups; researchers; MSME
eligibility: Startups, MSMEs, research institutions, and organizations engaged in deep-sea exploration, mineral extraction, ocean technology development, and related Blue Economy activities are eligible to participate under the Deep Ocean Mission, subject to project proposals aligning with mission objectives and guidelines issued by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
benefits: Financial support for R&D projects, access to deep-sea data and samples, technical collaboration with MoES-affiliated institutions (NIOT, NCPOR, INCOIS, IITM), infrastructure support for testing and validation, policy and regulatory guidance, and recognition under national Blue Economy frameworks.
financial_support: Funding is provided through competitive grant-based mechanisms for approved projects under the Deep Ocean Mission, with financial assistance sanctioned as per the Detailed Demands for Grants and annual budget allocations of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, subject to project appraisal and approval by the competent authority.
application_process: 1. Identify project area aligned with Deep Ocean Mission objectives such as mineral exploration, ocean technology, or marine resource assessment. 2. Prepare a detailed project proposal including technical feasibility, budget, timeline, and expected outcomes. 3. Submit the proposal through the designated channel of the Ministry of Earth Sciences. 4. Proposal undergoes technical and financial appraisal by expert committees. 5. Upon approval, enter into a memorandum of understanding or agreement with MoES. 6. Receive funds in installments as per project milestones. 7. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates. 8. Final project completion report and asset disclosure upon conclusion.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted throughout the year subject to budget availability and review cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Earth Sciences

overview: The National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) is a nodal agency under the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, established to promote sustainable development of fisheries and aquaculture in India. It implements various schemes and programs aimed at enhancing fish production, productivity, and value addition across the fisheries value chain, including capture fisheries, aquaculture, post-harvest operations, and marketing. NFDB provides financial and technical assistance to stakeholders such as fishers, fish farmers, cooperatives, entrepreneurs, and state governments to strengthen the fisheries sector and support livelihoods in coastal and inland areas.
target_beneficiaries: fishers; fish farmers; cooperatives; entrepreneurs; state governments
eligibility: Eligibility varies across specific schemes implemented by NFDB but generally includes fishers, fish farmers, fisheries cooperatives, self-help groups, entrepreneurs, NGOs, and state governments involved in fisheries and aquaculture activities. Applicants must be engaged in eligible fisheries-related activities as per the guidelines of individual schemes.
benefits: NFDB schemes offer financial assistance in the form of grants, subsidies, or loans for activities such as construction of ponds, tanks, and raceways; installation of aerators and feed mills; procurement of fishing vessels and gears; development of hatcheries and nurseries; establishment of feed mills and processing units; and implementation of disease surveillance and quality control measures. Technical support, training, and capacity building are also provided to enhance skills and adoption of best practices.
financial_support: Financial support under NFDB schemes is provided as per the specific guidelines of each program, which may include capital subsidies, interest subsidies, or grant-in-aid. The quantum of assistance varies depending on the activity, beneficiary category, and scheme norms, with funding typically released in installments based on achievement of milestones or submission of utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Identify the relevant NFDB scheme based on the proposed activity and beneficiary category. 2. Obtain the scheme guidelines and application form from the NFDB website or concerned office. 3. Prepare the project proposal as per the prescribed format, including technical and financial details. 4. Submit the completed application along with required documents to the NFDB headquarters or designated state-level office. 5. Application undergoes technical and financial appraisal by NFDB officials. 6. Upon approval, sanction letter is issued and funds are released in stages as per scheme provisions.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and scheme-specific timelines.
implementing_agency: National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying

scheme_name: Coastal Aquaculture Authority (CAA) Licensing for Startups
overview: The Coastal Aquaculture Authority (CAA) Licensing for Startups scheme regulates coastal aquaculture activities in India, ensuring environmental protection and responsible farming practices. It mandates registration of coastal aquaculture farms and hatcheries, issues certificates of compliance for antibiotic-free inputs, and promotes sustainable aquaculture through guidelines and monitoring. The scheme applies to all coastal areas across India.
target_beneficiaries: startups; farmers; hatchery operators; aquaculture input manufacturers
eligibility: Any person carrying on coastal aquaculture shall register their farm with the Coastal Aquaculture Authority. Application must be made in Form-I with documents as per Schedule-II of CAA Rules, 2024, along with the prescribed processing fee. For hatcheries, Form-II is required with documents as per Schedule-II and payment of registration fee of rupees ten thousand. For antibiotic-free aquaculture inputs, Form-III is required with documents as per Schedule-III and a non-refundable processing fee of ten thousand rupees.
benefits: Registration provides legal authorization to operate coastal aquaculture farms and hatcheries. Certificate of Compliance for Antibiotic-Free Aquaculture Inputs allows manufacturers to market certified inputs. The scheme ensures biosecurity, disease-free broodstock, and sustainable practices. It supports access to certified inputs, promotes exports, and protects coastal livelihoods.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. Financial obligations include payment of processing fees: rupees ten thousand for hatchery and live feed unit registration, and a non-refundable processing fee of ten thousand rupees for renewal of Certificate of Compliance for Aquaculture Inputs. No fund size or grant amount per entity is specified.
application_process: 1. Identify the appropriate form based on activity: Form-I for farm registration/renewal, Form-II for hatchery/NRH/Live Feed Unit registration, Form-III for Certificate of Compliance for Aquaculture Inputs. 2. Prepare documents as per the respective Schedule (I, II, or III) of CAA Rules, 2024. 3. Pay the required fee: Rs. 10,000 for Form-I and Form-II applications; Rs. 10,000 non-refundable processing fee for Form-III renewal. 4. Submit the application with documents and fee to the Coastal Aquaculture Authority, Chennai, or through the designated Sub-Divisional Level Committee (SDLC) or District Level Committee (DLC). 5. Await inspection and approval by the Authority as per the laid-down procedure in rules 9, 10, and 11 of CAA Rules, 2024.
deadlines: Renewal of farm registration shall be made within 60 days before expiry of registration. Renewal of Certificate of Compliance for Aquaculture Inputs must be submitted three months before expiry. No fixed deadline for new applications; processed on receipt basis.
implementing_agency: Coastal Aquaculture Authority, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India
contact_details: Email: caaheadoffice[at]caa[dot]gov[dot]in | Phone: 044-2435 3502 / 044-2435 3784 | Address: Secretary, Coastal Aquaculture Authority, 5th Floor, Integrated Office Complex for Animal Husbandry and Fisheries Department, Fanepet, Nandanam, Chennai-600 035, Tamilnadu, India.

overview: The National Smart Grid Mission (NSGM) is a Government of India initiative under the Ministry of Power aimed at planning and monitoring the implementation of smart grid-related activities in the power distribution sector. It focuses on modernizing the electricity grid through advanced technologies to improve efficiency, reliability, efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of power supply across the country.
target_beneficiaries: power distribution utilities; state governments; public sector undertakings; private sector entities involved in power distribution
eligibility: Power distribution utilities (both public and private), state governments, and their designated agencies involved in electricity distribution are eligible to participate in NSGM-supported projects. Projects must align with the smart grid framework and contribute to grid modernization goals.
benefits: Financial support for smart grid projects, technical guidance and monitoring, capacity building and training programs, standardization of smart grid technologies, improved grid reliability and efficiency, reduction in AT&C losses, better integration of renewable energy, and enhanced consumer engagement through smart metering.
financial_support: NSGM provides financial support in the form of grants to eligible projects, covering a portion of the project cost. The quantum of support is determined based on project specifics and adherence to mission guidelines, with funds disbursed through the implementing agency after project approval and milestone verification.
application_process: 1. Identify and formulate a smart grid project aligned with NSGM objectives. 2. Prepare a detailed project report (DPR) including technical, financial, and implementation details. 3. Submit the proposal to the designated nodal agency or utility. 4. The proposal is reviewed by the NSGM Secretariat for technical and financial appraisal. 5. Upon approval, a memorandum of understanding (MoU) is signed. 6. Funds are released in tranches based on project milestones. 7. Project implementation is monitored and evaluated by NSGM.
deadlines: Rolling basis — proposals are accepted and reviewed periodically as per NSGM notification cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Power, Government of India

scheme_name: Seaweed Mission – National Mission for Seaweed Cultivation
overview: The Seaweed Mission – National Mission for Seaweed Cultivation is a strategic initiative under the Blue Economy category aimed at promoting seaweed farming as a sustainable and high-value aquaculture practice. It seeks to enhance livelihoods, create employment opportunities, and support coastal economic development through scientific innovations and improved production practices. The mission includes the establishment of a Centre of Excellence for Seaweed Farming and Research at ICAR-CMFRI, Mandapam, and focuses on cluster development in identified regions such as Lakshadweep and Madurai. It aligns with broader fisheries sector goals of sustainability, income diversification, and climate resilience.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; entrepreneurs; women; youth; marginal farmers; coastal communities
eligibility: The evidence does not specify explicit eligibility criteria for the Seaweed Mission. However, based on the context of cluster development and Centre of Excellence establishment, beneficiaries likely include fishers, fish farmers, entrepreneurs, women self-help groups, and coastal communities engaged in or interested in seaweed cultivation and mariculture activities.
benefits: The Seaweed Mission is expected to benefit approximately 20,000 farmers and create around 5,000 employment opportunities. It supports livelihood diversification, coastal economic development, and entrepreneurship among women, youth, and marginal farmers through activities like seaweed cultivation. The mission strengthens the aquaculture sector through scientific innovations, improved production practices, and the establishment of a Centre of Excellence for Seaweed Farming and Research at ICAR-CMFRI, Mandapam. It contributes to ocean health by absorbing excess nutrients and carbon dioxide, and aligns with climate resilience and sustainable blue economy goals.
financial_support: The evidence does not specify direct financial support mechanisms such as grants, subsidies, or loans under the Seaweed Mission. Financial support is implied through broader departmental initiatives like the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), Blue Revolution Scheme, and Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), which have funded mariculture and seaweed-related activities. However, no specific financial allocation or support mechanism is detailed for the Seaweed Mission itself in the provided evidence.
application_process: The evidence does not provide a step-by-step application process for the Seaweed Mission. No application procedure, portal, or registration steps are described in the documents.
implementing_agency: Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India

scheme_name: Housing & Urban Development Corporation (HUDCO) Tech Scheme
overview: HUDCO Tech Scheme is a technology-focused initiative by the Housing and Urban Development Corporation (HUDCO) aimed at promoting innovation and sustainable development in urban infrastructure and housing sectors. The scheme supports the adoption of advanced technologies, green building practices, and smart city solutions through financial and technical assistance. It targets stakeholders involved in urban development projects seeking to integrate modern technological interventions for improved efficiency and environmental sustainability.
target_beneficiaries: urban local bodies; state governments; public sector undertakings; private developers; housing boards
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include central/state government agencies, urban local bodies, public sector undertakings, housing boards, and private sector entities engaged in housing and urban infrastructure projects. Projects must demonstrate technological innovation, sustainability, and compliance with HUDCO’s lending norms. Priority is given to projects aligned with national missions such as Smart Cities, AMRUT, and Housing for All.
benefits: Benefits include concessional interest rates on loans, extended repayment tenors, technical advisory support for technology selection and implementation, assistance in accessing international best practices, and support for monitoring and evaluation of technology performance. The scheme also facilitates capacity building and knowledge sharing among stakeholders.
financial_support: HUDCO provides term loans covering up to 75% of the project cost for technology adoption in eligible projects. The financial support is structured as a rupee-term loan with interest rates linked to HUDCO’s benchmark rates, offering concessions for projects with high sustainability and innovation quotients. Repayment tenors can extend up to 15 years, including a moratorium period, based on project cash flows.
application_process: 1. Submit a detailed project proposal outlining the technology intervention, expected outcomes, and sustainability benefits. 2. Include project cost estimates, financing plan, and implementation timeline. 3. Provide clearances and approvals from relevant statutory authorities, if applicable. 4. Submit organizational and financial documents of the applicant entity. 5. HUDCO undertakes technical and financial appraisal of the proposal. 6. Upon approval, a loan sanction letter is issued with terms and conditions. 7. Disbursement occurs in stages based on project milestones and verification.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to fund availability and appraisal timelines.
implementing_agency: Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited (HUDCO)

scheme_name: Smart Cities Labs – Urban Innovation Challenge
Smart Metering National Programme Startup Empanelment
overview: The Smart Metering National Programme Startup Empanelment is a subsumed under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (as a Reforms-based and Results-linked Scheme with an outlay of Rs.3,03,758 crore over a period of five years from FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 with the objective to Empanel Startups is an initiative under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) that aims to empanel startups to provide smart metering solutions for distribution utilities. The scheme is part of the Ministry of Power's broader effort to modernize India's power distribution infrastructure through smart metering, leveraging startup innovation for deployment and integration of smart meters across the country. It supports the national goal of reducing AT&C losses and improving the financial sustainability of DISCOMs by enabling prepaid smart metering and data-driven energy accounting.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups must be empaneled under the Smart Metering National Programme as part of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme. Eligibility is determined by the implementing agency based on technical capability, financial viability, and compliance with the scheme's guidelines for smart metering deployment and integration with DISCOM operations.
benefits: Empanelled startups gain recognition to participate in smart metering projects under RDSS, access to deployment opportunities across DISCOMs, involvement in PPP-based prepaid smart metering implementation, and the ability to leverage AI for data analytics from smart meters. They contribute to loss reduction, demand forecasting, ToD tariff implementation, RE integration, and improved consumer services through monthly energy accounting reports.
financial_support: Financial support is provided under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme, which has an outlay of Rs.3,03,758 crore over five years (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26). The scheme provides financial assistance for prepaid smart metering, system metering, and distribution infrastructure works, subject to meeting pre-qualifying criteria and achieving basic minimum benchmarks by DISCOMs. Funds are disbursed based on action plans and performance against agreed trajectories including AT&C losses, ACS-ARR gaps, and infrastructure upgrades.
application_process: 1. Startups must apply for empanelment under the Smart Metering National Programme as part of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme. 2. Applications are evaluated based on technical and financial qualifications. 3. Empanelled startups are eligible to bid for smart metering projects through competitive bidding processes conducted by DISCOMs or designated agencies. 4. Selected startups enter into agreements to deploy smart metering systems in PPP mode. 5. Implementation includes installation of smart meters, integration with IT/OT systems, and monthly energy accounting reporting. 6. Performance is monitored against predefined trajectories for funding eligibility.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Power, Government of India

overview: The Desalination Technology for Coastal MSMEs (CSIR-CSMCRI) scheme focuses on providing desalination technology solutions to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in coastal regions. It aims to support sustainable water purification and resource utilization through indigenous membrane-based technologies developed by CSIR-CSMCRI. The scheme facilitates technology transfer, technical collaboration, and capacity building for MSMEs engaged in water treatment, desalination, and related industrial applications.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: MSMEs operating in coastal regions seeking desalination, water purification, or brine treatment technologies; must be engaged in industrial or commercial activities related to water treatment, desalination, or value recovery from saline waste streams; eligibility is subject to technical feasibility and alignment with CSIR-CSMCRI’s technology portfolio.
benefits: Access to indigenously developed reverse osmosis (RO), ultrafiltration (UF), nanofiltration, and electrodialysis technologies; technical support for plant design, installation, and operation; training on membrane maintenance and fouling mitigation; assistance in achieving zero liquid discharge (ZLD); recovery of valuable by-products like potash, magnesia, and bromine from brine; compliance with environmental standards for wastewater treatment.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through consultancy, sponsored projects, or technology transfer agreements on a case-by-case basis; costs are determined based on project scope, technology complexity, and scale of deployment; payment terms follow CSIR Guidelines for technology transfer and utilization of knowledgebase; no fixed grant or subsidy amount is specified in the evidence.
application_process: 1. Identify relevant desalination or water purification technology from CSIR-CSMCRI’s portfolio. 2. Initiate contact via the Business Development & Information Management Division. 3. Submit a formal collaboration request outlining intended application and scale. 4. Undergo technical feasibility assessment by CSIR-CSMCRI experts. 5. Negotiate terms of technology transfer, consultancy, sponsored project. 6. Execute agreement and proceed with technology deployment, if applicable.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year based on project feasibility and mutual agreement.
implementing_agency: Central Salt & Marine Chemicals Research Institute (CSIR-CSMCRI), Bhavnagar

overview: The Urban Innovation Challenge (UIC) – MoHUA is a scheme under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) that aims to catalyse a paradigm shift in urban development by encouraging cities to transition towards market-based financing and integrated regional development. It positions cities as a bankable asset class through targeted reforms, strengthened institutional capacity, improved governance and planning frameworks, and the development of sustainable revenue-generating urban infrastructure. The scheme supports urban transformation through three verticals: 'Cities as Growth Hubs', 'Creative Redevelopment of Cities', and 'Water and Sanitation'.
target_beneficiaries: Urban Local Bodies (ULBs); States; Union Territories (UTs)
eligibility: All States and UTs are eligible to participate in UCF with a specific focus on strengthening Tier II and Tier III cities. The following categories of cities shall be covered under UCF: All cities with a projected 2025 population of 10 lakh or more; Capital cities of State/UT not included in the first category; Major industrial cities (Manufacturing & Services) with a projected 2025 population of 1,00,000 or more; All Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) in Hilly States/UTs, Northeastern States; and ULBs with population below 1,00,000 in other States/UTs. As per above, all ULBs are eligible to participate in UCF.
benefits: Central Assistance (CA) acts as catalytic support to leverage market-based financing, enable structured project implementation, and ensure timely execution of financially viable and reform-linked urban infrastructure investments. The fund supports projects across three verticals: Digital Governance, Development of Trunk Infrastructure, Circularity, Projects for decongestion, Last mile connectivity infrastructure, Revitalisation of old city areas, Redevelopment of old markets, Non-motorised transport infrastructure, Transit Hub upgradation, TOD infrastructure development, Projects for prevention of urban flooding, Integrated waste processing, Green field/ Semi Greenfield City infrastructure, Development of road infrastructure and flyovers, Riverfront development, and Projects required for implementation of reforms.
financial_support: The Urban Challenge Fund provides a total Central Assistance (CA) of ₹1,00,000 crore over the Mission period. The Central Assistance (CA) is designed as a catalytic instrument to leverage significantly larger investments from market-based sources. The CA for projects is limited to 25 percent of the cost of bankable projects with a stipulation that at least 50 percent of the project cost is funded from bonds, bank loans, and PPPs. The Central Assistance for UCF is structured as: Projects: ₹90,000 crore; Project Preparation and Capacity Building at National, State/UT, and City levels: ₹5,000 crore; and Credit Repayment Guarantee Sub-Scheme (CRGSS): ₹5,000 crore.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
