DST Inspire Faculty Award & Research Grant
overview: The DST Inspire Faculty Award & Research Grant is a component of the INSPIRE programme sponsored by the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, aimed at attracting talent to science and strengthening the Science & Technology system and R&D base. It offers contractual research fellowships to young achievers with Ph.D. degrees for independent research, with the goal of emerging as future leaders in science & technology. The scheme includes a monthly fellowship amount and an annual research grant, and is tenable for a maximum period of five years.
target_beneficiaries: young achievers; Ph.D. holders; Indian citizens; people of Indian origin including NRI/PIO
eligibility: Indian citizens and people of Indian origin including NRI/PIO status with Ph.D. (in Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Pharmacy, Medicine, and Agriculture related subjects) from any recognized university in the world. Those applicants who apply by choosing the new subject area ‘Translational Research in S&T’ need to have at least two patents filed or one patent granted to their credit. Those who have submitted their Ph.D. thesis and are awaiting award of the degree are also eligible. However, the Fellowship will be conveyed only after confirmation of award of the Ph.D. degree.
benefits: Faculty fellowship amount is Rs. 1,25,000/- per month with an annual increment of Rs. 2000/- and Research Grant of Rs. 7,00,000/- per year for 5 years’ period. The fellowship amount is consolidated (all inclusive). No break-up will be provided by DST. Selected fellow must submit two undertakings: a) Duly signed 'Undertaking by INSPIRE Faculty Fellow' and b) Undertaking duly signed by both the competent authority from the chosen Host institution and the INSPIRE Faculty Fellow. Bank account detail of the Host Institute, Joining Report, and Budget breakup on usage of Research Grant are required for receiving the first instalment grant.
financial_support: Faculty fellowship amount is Rs. 1,25,000/- per month with an annual increment of Rs. 2000/- and Research Grant of Rs. 7,00,000/- per year for 5 years’ period. The Research Grant of Rs.7.0 lakh per year can be utilized for expenditures under recurring and non-recurring budget subheads flexibly. The fellow has inter-operational flexibility to use the research grant in other budget subheads other than the subhead of Travel, Contingency and overhead. However, Expenditure under Travel and Contingencies subheads will be limited to 10% each (Rs. 70,000/- per year) and Overhead 5% (Rs. 35,  per year). As per the new fund flow mechanism initiated by the government w.e.f. 2024-2025 i.e. Hybrid-TSA Model grant provided to INSPIRE Faculty Fellows should be utilized within the same financial year in which it has been released. There is no provision of carry forwarding of unspent Research Grant to next financial year.
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 1,25,000/- per month with an annual increment of Rs. 2000/- and Research Grant of Rs. 7,00,000/- per year
application_process: 1. Call for applications are advertised once in a year in the month of July/Aug on the online portal. 2. One can apply for the Faculty Fellowship through online portal only. 3. To apply online, please follow the link https://www.online-inspire.gov.in. 4. Selected candidates should avail the INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship within 3 months of issue of offer letter. 5. Selected fellow must submit two undertakings: a) Duly signed 'Undertaking by INSPIRE Faculty Fellow' and b) Undertaking duly signed by both the competent authority from the chosen Host institution and the INSPIRE Faculty Fellow. 6. Bank account detail of the Host Institute, Joining Report, and Budget breakup on usage of Research Grant are required for receiving the first instalment grant.
deadlines: Call for applications are advertised once in a year in the month of July/Aug on the online portal.
implementing_agency: Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India

overview: The National Mission for Protein Supplements (NMPS) is a sub-scheme under the National Livestock Mission (NLM) aimed at promoting protein-rich fodder production and enhancing livestock productivity through the distribution of certified seeds and planting material for fodder crops. It focuses on increasing the availability of high-quality protein supplements for livestock, particularly in regions with fodder deficits. The scheme supports farmers and livestock rearers by providing subsidized inputs to improve animal nutrition and milk/meat yield.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; livestock rearers; agri-entrepreneurs; self-help groups; cooperatives
eligibility: Farmers, livestock rearers, self-help groups, cooperatives, and agri-entrepreneurs engaged in fodder cultivation or livestock rearing are eligible to benefit from the scheme, subject to state-specific implementation guidelines and verification of landholding or livestock units.
benefits: Subsidized distribution of certified seeds of fodder crops such as maize, sorghum, bajra, napier, stylo, and legumes; technical guidance on fodder cultivation and utilization; improved animal health and productivity; reduced input costs for fodder production; promotion of perennial and annual fodder varieties suitable for different agro-climatic zones.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided in the form of back-ended subsidy on the cost of certified seeds and planting material for fodder crops, with subsidy rates varying by crop type and beneficiary category, typically ranging from 25% to 50% of the seed cost, disbursed through state implementing agencies after verification of purchase and planting.
application_process: 1. Approach the State Implementing Agency (SIA) or designated nodal office under the State Animal Husbandry Department. 2. Submit application along with required documents. 3. Undergo verification of eligibility and land/livestock details. 4. Receive approval and subsidy sanction order. 5. Purchase certified seeds from authorized dealers. 6. Submit proof of purchase and planting. 7. Receive subsidy disbursement directly into bank account.
deadlines: Rolling basis — subject to annual budget allocation and state-wise implementation schedules
implementing_agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying

overview: Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG) Expansion Round is the flagship programme of BIRAC which supports young startups by providing early-stage funding support of INR 50 Lakhs as grant-in-aid for a period of 18 months to translate innovative ideas into Proof of Concept. The purpose of the BIG Scheme is to foster generation of ideas with commercialisation potential, upscale and validate proof of concept, encourage researchers to take technology closer to market through a startup, and stimulate enterprise formation. The scheme is currently managed through 8 BIG Partners across the country who provide mentoring, monitoring, networking, and other business development related activities to Ignition grantees (BIG Innovators).
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: The Company/LLP should be registered under the Indian Companies Act, 1956/2013. The incorporation date of the Company/LLP should not be earlier than 5 years from the date of launch of a particular BIG call. A company is considered as 'owned' by resident Indian citizen(s) if minimum 51% of the capital is beneficially owned by resident Indian citizen(s) and/or Indian companies, which are ultimately owned and controlled by resident Indian citizens. Company/LLP’s application should be represented by a Project Leader. The Company/LLP must have its own in-house R&D facility that is functional and adequate to execute the project. If the Company/LLP does not have a functional and adequate laboratory of its own then it should be incubated at an incubator (This shall be verified and confirmed by BIG Partner). If an applicant company, in which any promoter holding more than or equal to 20% of the shares, is a co-promoter of another ineligible company or a partner in another ineligible LLP, then the applicant will not be eligible. The only exception to this shall be a situation wherein the latter ineligible company/LLP is operating in a non-biotech domain. Companies that are in default of loan repayment to BIRAC, as well as their promoters, shall be deemed ineligible to apply under the scheme.
benefits: Financial support of up to INR 50 lakhs as grant-in-aid for a period of 18 months. Entrepreneurial support including technical mentoring, IP support, legal support, networking and outreach, trainings, regulatory advice, business mentoring, and connect with investors. Milestone-based fund disbursement in 3-4 installments: INR 20.00 lakhs upon signing of the Grant Agreement, one to two instalments each of up to INR 20.00 lakhs based on satisfactory progress of project milestones and funding requirement, and up to INR 5.00 lakhs upon successful completion of the project and submission of the Final Technical Report. Continuous mentoring support from BIRAC and BIG Partners.
financial_support: The funding support under BIG is in the form of a grant-in-aid. Extent of funding is up to INR 50 lakhs. The fund allocation under BIG is milestone based and released in 3-4 installments as detailed below: 1. INR 20.00 lakhs upon signing of the Grant Agreement. 2. One to two instalments, each of up to INR 20.00 lakhs to be released based on satisfactory progress of project milestones and funding requirement. 3. Up to INR 5.00 lakhs upon successful completion of the project and submission of the Final Technical Report. Note: The final tranche shall be released as reimbursement upon submission and acceptance of the final Utilization Certificate (UC), Statement of Expenditure (SoE), and the Project Completion Report. Total fund not exceeding INR 50 lakhs. The funding is provided for a period of up to 18 months. The project is implemented in a milestone-based manner.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 50 lakhs
application_process: 1. BIRAC issues a national call inviting applications under BIG at least twice a year (typically on 1st of January & 1st of July). 2. The Call for Proposals is advertised through one or more means that may include BIRAC website, newspapers, journals and magazines. 3. The Call for Proposals is typically open for a period of 30 days. 4. The BIG Scheme is implemented across the country through BIRAC’s BIG Partners. The Call will mention the names of BIG Partners for the particular call. Names of the BIG Partners and their responsibilities are mentioned in Annexure 1. 5. Application for BIG needs to be submitted online ONLY through BIRAC website www.birac.nic.in. 6. Applicants are advised to fill-up and submit their applications early without waiting for the last date in order to avoid last-minute rush. Please note that the online system will stop accepting applications automatically at the specific date and time mentioned in the Call details. 7. Applicants are advised to provide sufficient details in their applications to allow for an informed and fair evaluation/review. 8. Requests for changes in a proposal once submitted will not be entertained. 9. Providing incorrect information intentionally is viewed adversely and may lead to disqualification.
deadlines: Call announcement calendar: The call for proposal is announced twice a year, i.e. on 1st January and 1st July. Call for proposals typically remains open for about 45 days.
implementing_agency: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), a Public Sector Enterprise, set up by Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India

scheme_name: Science & Engineering Research Board (SERB) CRG Grant
overview: The Science & Engineering Research Board (SERB) CRG Grant is part of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) framework, established under the ANRF Act, 2023, to support investigator-driven research in natural sciences, engineering, technology, and interdisciplinary domains. It aims to strengthen India’s R&D ecosystem, promote high-impact and transformative research, and align with national goals like Viksit Bharat 2047. The grant supports fundamental frontier research, use-inspired basic research, and applied/translational research with emphasis on outcomes, impact, and collaboration across academia, industry, and government.
target_beneficiaries: researchers; academicians; scientists; faculty members; post-doctoral fellows; research scholars
eligibility: Applicants (Principal Investigator and Co-Principal Investigator(s)) must be Indian citizens; foreign nationals (including OCI and NRI) are eligible if they meet notified criteria. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Sciences, Mathematics, and Engineering, or M.D./M.S./M.D.S./M.V.Sc. with two years post-degree experience. Under Quantitative Social Sciences, PI/Co-PI must hold Ph.D. in Science, Mathematics, Engineering, M.D./M.S./M.D.S./M.V.Sc., or Ph.D. in any Social Sciences. Applicants must hold a regular position in a recognized academic institution, National Research Laboratory, or recognized research organization in India. Private academic institutions with UGC/AICTE/PCI approval, private R&D institutions with DSIR-SIRO recognition, and NGOs registered under NITI-AAYOG Darpan portal with DSIR SIRO recognition are eligible to host projects. Research Associates, Post-doctoral fellows, Ad-hoc/Guest faculties, Visiting Scientists, Consultants, Project Fellows, and those with annually renewed contracts are not eligible. INSPIRE, Ramanujan, and Ramalingaswamy Fellowship holders are eligible as PI/Co-PI if meeting service criteria. PI must have at least 'project duration plus one year' of service remaining; superannuating PIs may apply if a Co-PI with sufficient service is associated. Investigators cannot hold more than two ANRF (or erstwhile SERB) projects simultaneously. Eligibility for another project arises six months after completion of ongoing project.
benefits: Financial support for project execution; flexibility in utilizing funds under recurring head for research personnel, consumables, travel, field work, contingencies, cloud compute credits, software licenses, publication costs, and analytical/facility access charges; support for non-recurring heads including equipment, software, and long-term cloud/remote facility access; travel budget up to Rs. 5 Lakhs; contingency funds up to Rs. 5 Lakhs (usable for international conference registration); permission for open access publication and patent filing charges from recurring head; industry/international collaboration encouraged with cost-sharing optional; administrative responsibility with host institution, technical responsibility with PI; funding disbursed to PI’s institution and up to two additional institutions; impact assessment scorecard with real-time dashboard; requirement to share data in appropriate depositories and pre-prints in public domain.
financial_support: The upper limit for project funding under the ARG Program is ₹ 5 Crores. The research grant is provided under two budget heads: Recurring (research personnel, consumables, travel, field work, contingencies, cloud compute credits, software licenses, publication costs, analytical/facility access charges) and Non-Recurring (equipment, software purchases, long-term cloud/remote facility access). No reallocation of funds between recurring and non-recurring heads is permissible. Operational flexibility is available under recurring head subject to norms. Travel budget: up to Rs. 5 Lakhs. Contingency: up to Rs. 5 Lakhs. Publication and patent filing charges permitted from recurring head. Equipment changes require prior ANRF approval. For projects over ₹1 Cr, Co-PI from PI’s institution is mandatory. Funding is disbursed to the PI’s institution and up to two additional institutions.
grant_amount_per_entity: ₹ 5 Crores
application_process: 1. Visit www.anrfonline.in to access the proposal submission portal. 2. Register as a new user if not already registered (PI/Co-PI/Mentor/Referee). 3. Fill registration form with required details and submit. 4. Click verification link sent to email to complete registration. 5. Log in and fill mandatory fields under User Profile (bio data, photo, institute address, etc.). 6. Prepare proposal with Project Title (max 500 chars), Project summary (max 3000 chars), Keywords (max 6), Objectives (max 1500 chars), Expected output/outcome (max 1500 chars), and Budget (Research Personnel, Consumables, Travel, Equipment, Contingency, Overheads). 7. Upload technical document (TD) as single PDF ≤10 MB. 8. Submit pre-proposal by deadline via www.anrfonline.in. 9. If shortlisted, submit full proposal. 10. Proposals undergo review by subject matter experts; PIs may be called for presentation. 11. Larger proposals (>₹1 Cr) undergo third-level evaluation by Empowered Technical Committee focusing on impact and collaboration depth.
deadlines: Call for Proposals notified via www.anrfonline.in; specific windows vary by program (e.g., ARG: May 15–Jun 10, 2026; MAHA Water: Jun 1–Jul 10, 2026; Ramanujan Fellowship: Jan 1–Dec 31, 2026). Applications must be submitted within announced windows; no rolling basis mentioned for ARG in this evidence.
implementing_agency: Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)

scheme_name: Horticulture Development Programme for NE and Himalayan States
overview: The Horticulture Development Programme for NE and Himalayan States is a sub-scheme of the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), implemented by State Horticulture Missions (SHM) in the North Eastern States and Himalayan States. It aims to promote holistic growth of the horticulture sector, including bamboo and coconut, through regionally differentiated strategies covering research, technology promotion, extension, post-harvest management, processing, and marketing. The scheme encourages farmer aggregation into groups like FIGs/FPOs/FPCs to achieve economies of scale, enhances production and farmers' income, strengthens nutritional security, improves productivity via quality germplasm and micro-irrigation, and supports skill development and employment generation for rural youth in horticulture and post-harvest management, especially in the cold chain sector.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; beneficiaries; rural youth; farmer groups like FIGs/FPOs/FPCs
geographic_scope: North Eastern States and Himalayan States
eligibility: Farmers / beneficiaries should contact the Horticulture Officer of concerned district to avail benefits and assistance under the scheme. Operational Guidelines, cost norms of different interventions being promoted under the mission, contact details of Mission Directors etc. are available on HMNEH web site.
benefits: Benefits include access to subsidies for horticulture development interventions such as planting material, micro-irrigation, protected cultivation, post-harvest management, processing, marketing, beekeeping, horticulture mechanization, training of farmers, nurseries, rejuvenation, area coverage, water resources, market infrastructures, and cold chain infrastructure. Financial assistance is provided based on cost norms for various interventions, with technical and administrative support from State Horticulture Missions (SHM).
financial_support: Under MIDH, Government of India (GOI) contributes 100% of total outlay for developmental programmes in the North Eastern States and Himalayan States. Financial assistance is provided as subsidies based on approved cost norms for various horticulture interventions, released through State Horticulture Missions (SHM) to eligible farmers and beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Farmers / beneficiaries should contact the Horticulture Officer of the concerned district. 2. Submit necessary data via online forms at the Hortnet Portal. 3. Data is verified at the Block Level to ensure it fits the criteria for the programs. 4. The District Horticulture Officer makes a decision regarding approval of the block horticulture project. 5. The project is forwarded to the state-level agricultural or horticultural department. 6. If the project meets the necessary criteria, it may receive approval at the ministry level.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

scheme_name: IISc MRDG Research Seed Grant for Startups
overview: The IISc MRDG Research Seed Grant for Startups is an innovation grant scheme offered by the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) to support early-stage startups with research-oriented projects. It aims to foster innovation by providing seed funding to startups that are aligned with IISc's research domains and have potential for technological impact. The grant is designed to bridge the gap between academic research and commercialization, particularly for startups emerging from IISc's ecosystem or collaborating with its faculty and labs.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups must be registered entities (Private Limited Company, LLP, or Partnership) with a clear linkage to IISc — either through IISc faculty, alumni, or research conducted at IISc. The startup must be working on an innovative product, service, or process grounded in scientific research. Preference is given to startups that are incubated at IISc or have ongoing collaboration with IISc departments or centres. The startup should be in the early stage (typically less than 5 years old) and not have received more than a specified limit in prior funding.
benefits: Financial support in the form of a seed grant, access to IISc's research laboratories and equipment, mentorship from IISc faculty, networking opportunities with investors and industry partners, and potential for follow-on funding through IISc's innovation ecosystem.
financial_support: The scheme provides a one-time seed grant of up to INR 10 lakhs to selected startups. The grant is non-repayable and is disbursed in tranches based on milestone achievement. Funds are intended for prototyping, proof-of-concept development, and early-stage validation activities.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to INR 10 Lakhs
application_process: 1. Identify a potential IISc faculty mentor or research collaborator. 2. Develop a project proposal aligned with IISc's research domains. 3. Submit the application through the IISc MRDG portal with startup registration details, team profile, and project plan. 4. Upload supporting documents including incorporation certificate, PAN, and brief technical description. 5. Application is reviewed by the MRDG committee. 6. Shortlisted startups are invited for a presentation or interview. 7. Final selection is made based on innovation, feasibility, and IISc alignment. 8. Grant is awarded upon approval and disbursement begins post-agreement signing.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year, subject to availability of funds and review cycles.
implementing_agency: Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru

overview: PM Garib Kalyan Rozgar Abhiyan (PMGKRA) is a rural public works scheme launched to provide employment and livelihood opportunities to migrant workers and rural citizens affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. It focuses on creating durable rural infrastructure through 25 types of works across sectors like water conservation, plantation, and rural housing. The scheme was implemented in a mission mode for 125 days across 116 districts in six states.
target_beneficiaries: migrant workers; rural citizens; returning migrants
geographic_scope: 116 districts across six states (Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh)
eligibility: The scheme targeted returning migrant workers and rural citizens in the identified 116 districts across six states who were in need of wage employment opportunities during the post-lockdown period.
benefits: Wage employment under the scheme, creation of durable rural assets such as water conservation structures, plantation, rural housing, and rural connectivity works, skill development through engagement in various works, and livelihood support for vulnerable households.
financial_support: The scheme provided wage employment at prevailing MGNREGA rates. Financial support was channeled through the convergence of various central and state schemes, with funds released to states for implementation of the 25 types of works. The total financial outlay was INR 50,000 crore.
application_process: 1. Identify eligible beneficiaries (returning migrant workers and rural citizens) in the 116 identified districts. 2. Verify eligibility through local authorities and Gram Panchayats. 3. Allocate work under the 25 permissible categories based on local needs and infrastructure gaps. 4. Deploy workers to worksites with adherence to social distancing and safety norms. 5. Monitor work progress and ensure timely wage payment through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). 6. Conduct periodic reviews and asset verification.
deadlines: The scheme was implemented for a fixed duration of 125 days from launch, after which it concluded.
implementing_agency: Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development

CSIR Research Associateship for Industry Projects
overview: The CSIR Research Associateship for Industry Projects is a scheme under the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), Ministry of Science & Technology, Government of India, aimed at promoting industry-oriented research and innovation through research associateships. It supports individuals engaged in industry-linked R&D projects, fostering collaboration between CSIR laboratories and industrial partners. The scheme focuses on translating scientific research into practical applications and enhancing technological capabilities in industries.
target_beneficiaries: researchers; scientists; industry professionals
eligibility: The eligibility criteria are not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence text.
benefits: The benefits include financial support for research associates engaged in industry projects, opportunities to work on applied R&D in CSIR laboratories, and contribution to technology development and industrial innovation.
financial_support: The financial support details, including quantum, type, and mechanism, are not specified in the provided evidence text.
application_process: The step-by-step application procedure is not described in the provided evidence text.

overview: The Oil Palm Area Expansion (OPAE) Scheme is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) launched by the Government of India to promote oil palm cultivation and enhance domestic edible oil availability. The scheme aims to increase oil palm area from 3.5 lakh hectares to 10 lakh hectares by 2025-26, with a focus on North-Eastern States and Andaman & Nicobar Islands. It provides financial assistance for planting material, maintenance, drip irrigation, bore-wells, vermi-compost units, machinery, and small tractors, with viability gap payment for Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFBs) linked to industry procurement. The scheme is implemented through State Departments of Agriculture/Horticulture in coordination with processors and other stakeholders.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers; Women; NE states beneficiaries
geographic_scope: Pan-India (20 states covering 284 districts including NE states and Andaman & Nicobar Islands)
eligibility: Farmers (including SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women, and NE states beneficiaries) in 20 states covering 284 districts identified by ICAR-IIOPR as suitable for oil palm cultivation, including NE states and Andaman & Nicobar Islands. State Governments will develop long-term agreements between farmers, processors and states through the Oil Palm Act or any other mechanism prevalent in the state. Processors, ICAR, KVKs, SAUs, CAUs, CDDs, and other stakeholders are involved in formulation, prioritization of activities, and identification of beneficiaries at grass root level. No area restriction is applicable for individual farmers for availing subsidy/intervention.
benefits: Financial assistance for planting material @ 85% cost of Rs. 12,000/ha for entire land during first year for plantation and Rs. 10,000/ha/year for maintenance cost of new plantations and purchasing inputs for intercropping for four years during gestation period for entire land. Installation of drip-irrigation systems as per PMSKY. 50% of the cost limited to Rs. 27,000/pump-set for diesel/electric pump-sets for SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women and NE states beneficiaries and Rs. 22,500/pump-set for other beneficiaries. 50% cost limited to Rs. 50,000/unit for bore-well and water harvesting structures/ponds; 50% cost limited to Rs. 1.50 lakh per unit in plain area and Rs. 1.80 lakh per unit in hilly areas. For construction of vermi-compost units: 50% of the cost limited to Rs. 15,000/unit. For purchase of machinery & tools: 50% of the cost limited to Rs. 1500/- per oil palm cutter, Rs. 15,000/- per wire-mesh, Rs. 10,000/- per motorized chisel, Rs. 3000/- per unit for aluminium portable ladder, Rs. 20,000/- per unit for SC/ST/Small Farmers/Women/NE states and Rs. 16,000/- per unit for other beneficiaries as per SMAM norms. 40% of the cost limited to Rs. 1.80 lakh for other beneficiary and Rs. 2.25 lakh for SC/ST/Small Farmers/Women/NE states for small tractor of 20HP with trolley. In case of North Eastern States, 50% of the cost limited to Rs. 250.00 lakhs is provided to the State Government for setting up a new oil palm processing mill with capacity of 5 MT per hour. 50% of the actual cost estimated by PWD/CPWD limited to 20% of the total outlay of the state under AAP for NFSM-Oil Palm for roads from oil palm field to nearest FFB collection/processing centre. Viability Gap payment: Central government compensates farmers if price paid by industry is below viability price up to October 2037.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as subsidy for various components: planting material (85% of Rs. 12,000/ha), maintenance (Rs. 10,000/ha/year for 4 years), drip irrigation (as per PMSKY), pump-sets (50% cost up to Rs. 27,000 for SC/ST/Women/NE and Rs. 22,500 for others), bore-wells/water harvesting (50% cost up to Rs. 50,000/unit, with higher limits in hilly areas), vermi-compost units (50% cost up to Rs. 15,000/unit), machinery & tools (50% cost up to specified limits), and small tractors (40% cost up to Rs. 1.80 lakh for others and Rs. 2.25 lakh for SC/ST/Women/NE). In NE States, 50% cost up to Rs. 250 lakhs for State Government to set up oil palm processing mills and 50% of actual cost for roads limited to 20% of state AAP outlay. Viability Gap funding: ₹1163 crore (₹1144 crore for Rest of India and ₹19.00 crore for NE states and Andaman & Nicobar Islands till 2025-26). The total estimated cost of NMEO (Oil Palm) is ₹8844 crore (GOI share ₹2196 crore, state share, and total ₹11,040 crore). Fund flow is through DBT and escrow account mechanism. For UTs and central agencies, funding is 100% GOI share. For general states: 60:40 (GOI:State); for NE states: 90:10 (GOI:State) in all components except R&D, seed gardens, nurseries, and viability gap payment (100% GOI share).
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

scheme_name: PM POSHAN – National Programme for Mid Day Meals Vendor Scheme
MSME Performance and Credit Rating Scheme
overview: The MSME Performance and Credit Rating Scheme aims to enhance the creditworthiness and market perception of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) by providing independent credit ratings and performance assessments. The scheme facilitates easier access to credit at favorable terms by certifying the financial health and operational capabilities of participating enterprises. It supports MSMEs in building credibility with lenders, investors, and business partners through standardized evaluation mechanisms.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Manufacturing or service sector MSMEs with valid Udyam Registration (UR) Certificate are eligible to apply under the scheme. Enterprises must be operational and engaged in legitimate business activities as per MSME classification criteria.
benefits: Benefits include improved access to credit at preferential interest rates, enhanced credibility with financial institutions and buyers, better negotiation power for loan terms, increased visibility in government procurement and trade platforms, and support for market expansion through certified performance ratings.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of a subsidy for the cost of obtaining credit rating and performance assessment from accredited agencies. The subsidy covers a significant portion of the rating fee, reducing the financial burden on MSMEs seeking certification.
application_process: 1. Obtain valid Udyam Registration (UR) Certificate. 2. Select an accredited credit rating agency empaneled under the scheme. 3. Submit application through the designated MSME portal or implementing agency. 4. Provide required documents including Udyam Registration, financial statements, and business details. 5. Undergo evaluation by the rating agency. 6. Receive credit rating and performance certificate. 7. Claim reimbursement of eligible expenses as per subsidy norms.
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises

overview: Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETI) is an initiative of the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD) to provide dedicated infrastructure in each district for training and skill upgradation of rural youth geared towards entrepreneurship development. RSETIs are managed by banks with active cooperation from the Government of India and State Governments. The program targets unemployed youth aged 18 to 45 years, offering free residential training with free food and accommodation, along with hand-holding support for credit linkage and enterprise sustainability for at least two years.
target_beneficiaries: rural youth; unemployed youth; BPL youth; women; men
eligibility: Unemployed youth aged 18 to 45 years from rural areas, including both men and women, with priority given to BPL (Below Poverty Line) youth. Training is provided based on individual aptitude and interest in various self-employment courses.
benefits: Free training, free food, free accommodation, free tool kits, free uniforms, hand-holding support for bank credit linkage, escort services for at least two years to ensure enterprise sustainability, practical and theory-based training, industrial visits, activity-based EDP training, personalized teaching, and performance monitoring.
financial_support: While the training itself is free, RSETIs facilitate credit linkage with banks for trainees to establish micro enterprises. The program does not provide direct grants or subsidies but supports access to bank loans through assured credit linkage and hand-holding support during the initial phase of enterprise setup.
application_process: 1. Visit the RSETI website or contact the nearest RSETI institute. 2. Provide personal details through the online application or contact form. 3. A representative from the institute will contact the applicant via phone to provide further information. 4. Attend selection and counselling based on aptitude and interest. 5. Enroll in the chosen training course. 6. Complete the residential training programme with free food and accommodation. 7. Receive post-training support for credit linkage and enterprise setup.
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD)

scheme_name: National Livelihood Mission – Digital Financial Inclusion
Quality Management Standards & Quality Tech Tools (QMS/QTT)
overview: The Quality Management Standards & Quality Tech Tools (QMS/QTT) scheme under the Ministry of MSME aims to enhance the competitiveness of micro and small enterprises by promoting the adoption of quality management systems and modern quality tools. It supports MSMEs in achieving international standards, improving product quality, and gaining market access through financial assistance for certification and technology upgradation. The scheme focuses on building quality consciousness among MSMEs and enabling them to meet global benchmarks.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Manufacturing/Service sector MSMEs having valid Udyam Registration (UR) Certificate.
benefits: Financial assistance for adoption of Quality Management Standards and Quality Tech Tools, including subsidies for certification fees, implementation costs, and technology upgradation. The scheme supports MSMEs in achieving national and international quality benchmarks, thereby improving product acceptance, reducing defects, and enhancing export readiness.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial assistance in the form of subsidies for Quality Management Systems (QMS) and Quality Tech Tools (QTT) implementation. Specific subsidy percentages and monetary limits are not detailed in the provided evidence, but support is extended to eligible MSMEs for certification and quality enhancement activities.
application_process: Through online, URL: https://my.msme.gov.in/MyMsme/Reg/COM_ViewEvent.aspx
deadlines: Rolling basis
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME)

overview: India Stack Developer Access Programme is a vision for financial and social inclusion through a collection of open APIs and digital public goods that unlock economic primitives of identity, data, and payments at population scale. It enables developers to build applications using Aadhaar-based identity verification, UPI payments, eSign, Digilocker, and Account Aggregator frameworks. The programme aims to empower individuals and businesses with secure, consent-based data sharing and interoperable digital infrastructure.
target_beneficiaries: developers; startups; fintechs; MSMEs; businesses
eligibility: Developers, startups, fintechs, and businesses interested in building on India Stack can access APIs, sandboxes, and documentation through intermediaries like Digio, Karza, Signzy, OnGrid, or by volunteering with iSPIRT. Access is granted by respective government agencies or institutions owning each component (e.g., UIDAI for Aadhaar, NPCI for UPI, MeitY for Digilocker, RBI for Account Aggregators).
benefits: Access to open APIs for Aadhaar authentication, e-KYC, eSign, Digilocker, UPI payments, and Account Aggregator framework. Enables paperless KYC, legally valid digital signatures, secure document storage, real-time bank-to-bank transfers, and consent-based data sharing. Reduces cost of identity verification, eliminates paper documentation, and supports innovation in financial inclusion, healthcare, and credit access.
financial_support: India Stack Developer Access Programme does not provide direct financial support, grants, loans, or subsidies. It offers free access to open APIs, technical documentation, sandboxes, and developer resources. Financial benefits are indirect, such as reduced operational costs for identity verification and payment processing through UPI and e-KYC.
application_process: 1. Identify the India Stack component of interest (e.g., Aadhaar, UPI, eSign, Digilocker, Account Aggregator). 2. Visit the respective agency website (UIDAI, NPCI, MeitY, RBI) or intermediary platforms like Digio, Karza, Signzy, OnGrid. 3. Register as a developer or Application Service Provider (ASP). 4. Submit required documents for KYC verification and eligibility. 5. Agree to terms of service and obtain API access. 6. Integrate APIs in testing/pre-production environment. 7. Complete audit and compliance checks. 8. Receive production access to deploy applications.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Multiple agencies: Unique ID Authority of India (UIDAI) for Aadhaar, National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) for UPI, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) for Digilocker and eSign, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for Account Aggregator framework
contact_details: Email: info@indiastack.org | Volunteer with iSPIRT at ispirt.in

scheme_name: Grievance Against Payment Delay (MSME SAMADHAAN Plus)
overview: MSME SAMADHAAN Plus is a grievance redressal mechanism designed to address delayed payments to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). It enables MSMEs to file complaints against buyers who fail to make payments within the stipulated time as per the MSMED Act, 2006. The system facilitates monitoring, reconciliation, and resolution of payment disputes through an online portal. It aims to ensure timely realization of dues for MSMEs and strengthen their financial sustainability.
target_beneficiaries: MSME
eligibility: Any Micro, Small, or Medium Enterprise registered under the MSMED Act, 2006, having a valid Udyam Registration Number, can file a grievance against any buyer (including government departments, CPSEs, or private entities) for delayed payment of goods or services supplied, where the payment is due beyond 45 days from the date of acceptance or deemed acceptance of goods/services.
benefits: Online filing and tracking of payment delay grievances; automatic generation of acknowledgment and case ID; facilitation of conciliation through the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council (MSEFC); legal backing under Section 18 of the MSMED Act, 2006; potential recovery of compound interest at three times the bank rate on delayed amounts; access to status updates and reports on pending cases; multilingual support for wider accessibility.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial assistance or grants. However, it enables MSMEs to claim the delayed payment amount along with compound interest (at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India) as per Section 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006, upon successful resolution of the grievance through the facilitation council.
application_process: 1. Visit the official MSME SAMADHAAN portal at https://samadhaan.msme.gov.in. 2. Click on 'File Grievance' or 'Register Complaint' option. 3. Enter Udyam Registration Number and validate the enterprise details. 4. Fill in the grievance form with details of the buyer, invoice particulars, amount due, and date of supply. 5. Upload supporting documents such as invoices, delivery challans, and communication records. 6. Submit the grievance and note the generated Case ID for future reference. 7. Track the status of the complaint through the portal using the Case ID. 8. Await action by the concerned Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council (MSEFC) for conciliation and resolution.
deadlines: Rolling basis — grievances can be filed at any time; there is no fixed deadline for submission.
implementing_agency: Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

overview: The Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) is a flagship initiative launched by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India, to provide assured, comprehensive, and quality antenatal care free of cost to all pregnant women on the 9th of every month. The program targets pregnant women in their 2nd or 3rd trimester and aims to improve antenatal care coverage and quality, detect and manage high-risk pregnancies, and reduce maternal and neonatal mortality. It engages private sector healthcare providers on a voluntary basis to supplement government efforts at designated public health facilities.
target_beneficiaries: pregnant women
eligibility: All pregnant women in their 2nd or 3rd trimester of pregnancy are eligible to receive services under PMSMA at designated government health facilities on the 9th of every month. There are no exclusions based on socioeconomic status, geography, or prior registration status. The program universally covers all pregnant women across India seeking antenatal care during the specified trimester.
benefits: Pregnant women receive a minimum package of antenatal care services including all applicable diagnostic services (e.g., hemoglobin, urine albumin and sugar, malaria, VDRL/HIV/blood sugar, blood grouping, GDM screening), essential drugs (IFA supplements, calcium supplements, tetanus toxoid, etc.), and one ultrasound during the 2nd trimester. High-risk pregnant women (HRPs) receive additional benefits: Rs. 100/- per visit for transportation costs (up to three visits) and Rs. 500/- upon achieving a healthy outcome for mother and baby at 45 days post-delivery. ASHAs receive Rs. 100/- per HRP for mobilization (up to three follow-ups) and Rs. 500/- for healthy outcomes. Volunteers (private sector doctors) receive recognition through awards, virtual 'Hall of Fame', and social media acknowledgment.
financial_support: Financial support under PMSMA is primarily in the form of case-based incentives for high-risk pregnancies (HRPs) and ASHAs. For HRPs: Rs. 100/- per visit for transportation (max three visits) and Rs. 500/- for healthy maternal and neonatal outcomes at 45 days post-delivery. For ASHAs: Rs. 100/- per HRP for mobilization (max three follow-ups) and Rs. 500/- for healthy outcomes. These funds are sourced from the National Health Mission (NHM) annual programme implementation plans under RCH/NHM flexible pool, JSSK, and Free Diagnostics Initiative. Districts receive Rs. 50,000–200,000/year and states receive Rs. 3–5 lakhs/year for sensitization, meetings, and IEC campaigns under E-PMSMA.
application_process: 1. Visit the PMSMA portal at https://pmsma.mohfw.gov.in 2. Click on 'Register Now' or 'Join Us' 3. Select your role: Obstetrician/Radiologist/Physician, Government Organization, Professional Association, or Pregnant Woman 4. Fill in the required details (name, contact, profession, etc.) 5. Submit the registration form 6. Alternatively, register via SMS by sending 'PMSMA <space> your name' to 5616115 7. Call the toll-free number 1800-180-1104 for assistance 8. Download the mobile app from Play Store or iOS App Store for volunteer engagement 9. Upon registration, volunteers are matched with government health facilities for service on the 9th of each month 10. After service, volunteers submit monthly data via the portal for credit and recognition
deadlines: Rolling basis — services are provided on the 9th of every month; volunteer registration is open year-round with no fixed deadline.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India
contact_details: Email: drpawan[dot]mohfw[at]gmail[dot]com | Toll Free Number: 1800-180-1104 | SMS: PMSMA <space> Name to 5616115

scheme_name: DigiLocker API Integration for Fintech KYC
overview: DigiLocker is a flagship initiative of the Ministry of Electronics & IT (MeitY) under the Digital India programme. It provides a secure cloud-based platform for storage, sharing, and verification of digital documents and certificates. DigiLocker aims at 'Digital Empowerment' of citizens by enabling access to authentic digital documents anytime, anywhere, with legal validity at par with original physical documents as per IT Rules 2016.
target_beneficiaries: citizens; organizations; government agencies; financial institutions; educational institutions
eligibility: To access the DigiLocker platform, users must register using a valid Indian mobile number, Driving License, PAN or Aadhaar. Registration may require verification via an OTP. Users are using Aadhaar voluntarily.
benefits: For Citizens: Access Anytime, Anywhere; Legally Valid, Widely Trusted Digital documents; Effortless Sharing with explicit consent; Accelerate Services for jobs, government benefits, banking, healthcare, and education. For Agencies: Reduced Administrative Overhead; Digital Transformation; Trusted issued documents fetched in real-time; Secure Document Gateway; Real Time Verification enabling government agencies to verify data directly from issuers after obtaining user consent.
financial_support: No financial support is provided under DigiLocker as it is a free digital document wallet service. The platform does not charge fees for access to issued documents through DigiLocker.
application_process: 1. Register yourself using a valid Indian mobile number, Driving License, PAN or Aadhaar. 2. Verify yourself via OTP sent to your mobile number. 3. Fetch your documents from linked issuers. 4. Share your documents with consent. 5. Become a DigiLocker Partner Organization by getting registered as a DigiLocker Issuer or Requester.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Registration is accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics & IT (MeitY), Government of India
contact_details: Email: support@digilocker.gov.in | Address: National e-Governance Division (NeGD), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, New Delhi, India

scheme_name: National Urban Sanitation Policy Innovation Challenge
overview: The National Urban Sanitation Policy Innovation Challenge is a scheme under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs aimed at fostering innovation in urban sanitation and waste management. It encourages stakeholders to develop and implement novel solutions for improving sanitation infrastructure and services in urban areas. The initiative supports the broader goals of the Swachh Bharat Mission and sustainable urban development by promoting technological and behavioral innovations.
target_beneficiaries: startups; entrepreneurs; MSME; urban local bodies
eligibility: Open to startups, entrepreneurs, MSMEs, urban local bodies, and other entities working on innovative solutions in urban sanitation, waste management, and related sectors. Applicants must demonstrate novelty, feasibility, and potential for scale in their proposed innovations.
benefits: Selected innovators receive recognition, mentorship, pilot implementation support, and potential scaling opportunities. The scheme facilitates access to funding networks, technical guidance, and visibility through MoHUA platforms. Non-financial benefits include capacity building, networking with policymakers, and integration into national urban missions.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through grants or seed funding for pilot projects, with amounts determined based on project scope and viability. The fund is leveraged to attract additional investment from private and public sources. Disbursement is linked to milestone achievement and project progress.
application_process: 1. Visit the official MoHUA website or designated portal for the Innovation Challenge. 2. Register and create a profile on the application portal. 3. Submit a detailed proposal outlining the innovation, objectives, methodology, and expected impact. 4. Upload supporting documents such as team details, prototypes, and pilot results. 5. Submit the application for review by the expert committee. 6. Await evaluation and notification of results.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

scheme_name: Open Finance Framework for Embedded Lending Startups
overview: The Open Finance Framework for Embedded Lending Startups is a regulatory initiative by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) aimed at enabling startups in the FinTech and BFSI sectors to offer embedded lending services through standardized, secure, and interoperable financial data sharing mechanisms. It seeks to foster innovation in credit delivery by leveraging account aggregator ecosystems and consent-based data sharing, thereby reducing information asymmetry and improving access to credit for underserved segments. The framework supports the development of plug-and-play lending solutions that integrate with digital platforms, enhancing financial inclusion and efficiency in lending processes.
target_beneficiaries: startups; FinTech companies; embedded lending platforms
eligibility: Startups and FinTech entities operating in India that wish to offer embedded lending services by leveraging account aggregator frameworks, provided they comply with RBI guidelines on data privacy, security, and consumer protection, and are registered as regulated entities under relevant RBI statutes.
benefits: Access to standardized APIs for seamless integration with account aggregators; regulatory clarity on data usage for lending; enhanced credibility through RBI-recognized framework; ability to offer instant credit at point-of-sale or within digital platforms; reduced customer acquisition and underwriting costs; support for innovation in credit scoring and risk modeling using consented financial data.
financial_support: The framework does not provide direct financial support such as grants or loans. Instead, it enables startups to access financial opportunities by reducing barriers to entry in the lending space through regulatory facilitation and infrastructure support for data sharing.
application_process: 1. Review the Open Finance Framework guidelines published by RBI on its official website. 2. Ensure compliance with data protection, security, and consumer protection norms as outlined in the framework. 3. Integrate with RBI-recognized Account Aggregators (AAs) for consent-based financial data retrieval. 4. Implement secure and auditable data handling practices as per RBI standards. 5. Submit details of the embedded lending model and compliance framework to RBI for review, if required under specific notifications. 6. Obtain necessary approvals or registrations as per applicable RBI directions (e.g., as a lending platform or technology provider). 7. Launch services post-compliance validation and monitor adherence to ongoing reporting and audit requirements.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications or notifications can be submitted as per ongoing regulatory guidelines.
implementing_agency: Reserve Bank of India

scheme_name: National Action Plan on Marine Litter (NAPML) Innovation Grant
overview: The National Action Plan on Marine Litter (NAPML) Innovation Grant is a scheme under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) aimed at addressing marine litter through innovation and research. It supports projects focused on prevention, reduction, and management of marine litter, particularly plastic waste, in India's coastal and marine environments. The grant encourages technological and behavioral innovations to mitigate marine pollution and aligns with national and international commitments on ocean health.
target_beneficiaries: startups; research institutions; NGOs; MSME
eligibility: Eligible applicants include startups, MSMEs, research institutions, NGOs, and other organizations with expertise in environmental science, waste management, or related fields. Applicants must demonstrate technical capability, innovation potential, and alignment with NAPML objectives. Preference is given to entities with prior experience in marine or coastal projects and those proposing scalable, sustainable solutions.
benefits: Financial support for innovative projects, technical guidance from MoEFCC experts, opportunities for pilot testing and scaling, networking with national and international stakeholders, and recognition under national marine litter initiatives. Successful projects may also gain visibility for future funding and policy integration.
financial_support: The scheme provides grant-based financial support to selected projects. The quantum of support is determined based on project scope, innovation level, and implementation plan. Funds are disbursed in tranches linked to project milestones, subject to progress review and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Visit the MoEFCC official website or designated portal for scheme details. 2. Review eligibility criteria and guidelines for the NAPML Innovation Grant. 3. Prepare a detailed project proposal including objectives, methodology, budget, and expected outcomes. 4. Submit the application online via the specified portal with all required documents. 5. Applications are screened by a technical committee for eligibility and merit. 6. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for presentation or interview. 7. Final selection is made by the approval committee. 8. Selected applicants receive sanction letters and undergo agreement signing. 9. Funds are released in installments based on project progress. 10. Submit periodic reports and utilization certificates as per guidelines.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)

scheme_name: National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture – Climate Change Adaptation
overview: The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) is a centrally sponsored scheme under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) aimed at enhancing agricultural productivity, sustainability, and climate change adaptation measures. It focuses on integrated farming, water use of natural resources like soil and water, promote integrated farming systems, and build climate resilience in agriculture through location-specific interventions. It converges with other schemes like MGNREGS, IWMP, RKVY, and NFSM to promote sustainable agricultural practices across India.
target_beneficiaries: farmers; agri-entrepreneurs; self-help groups; NGOs; state governments
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component and implementing agency; generally includes farmers, self-help groups, NGOs, state government departments, and institutions involved in sustainable agriculture practices. Specific eligibility for sub-components like Soil Health Management (SHM), Rainfed Area Development (RAD), On Farm Water Management (OFWM), and Climate Change and Sustainable Agriculture: Monitoring, Modeling and Networking (CCSAMMN) is defined in the Operational Guidelines, with implementation led by State Governments, National Centre of Organic Farming (NCOF), Central Fertilizer Quality Control & Training Institute (CFQC&TI), and Soil and Land Use Survey of India (SLUSI).
benefits: Benefits include financial assistance for adopting sustainable agricultural practices, capacity building and training, creation of asset base (e.g., soil health cards, water harvesting structures), promotion of integrated farming systems, climate resilience, improved soil health, enhanced water use efficiency, livelihood diversification, and convergence with other central and state schemes for holistic development. Non-financial benefits include technical support, knowledge sharing, monitoring and evaluation, and institutional strengthening.
financial_support: Financial support is provided as subsidies or grants-in-aid to state governments and implementing agencies based on approved Annual Action Plans (AAPs). The funding pattern is 60:40 between Centre and State for general states, 90:10 for North Eastern and Himalayan states, and 100% central funding for Union Territories and National Level Agencies. Funds are released in installments upon submission of Utilization Certificates and progress reports. The mission operates through a structured fund flow mechanism from the Government of India to State Governments and then to district-level implementing agencies.
application_process: 1. State Governments prepare Annual Action Plans (AAPs) based on district-level proposals and fund availability. 2. AAPs are submitted to the Department of Agriculture & Cooperation (DAC&FW) for approval by the Project Sanctioning Committee (PSC). 3. Upon approval, funds are released in installments to states. 4. States implement components through designated agencies (e.g., Agriculture Departments, NGOs, ICAR institutes). 5. Implementation is monitored via Physical and Financial Progress Reports. 6. Utilization Certificates and audited statements are submitted for subsequent fund releases. 7. Unspent balances may be revalidated for use in the next financial year subject to conditions.
deadlines: Annual Action Plans (AAPs) are to be prepared yearly; submission timelines are communicated via circulars (e.g., for FY 2021-22, allocation was communicated on March 3, 2021). The scheme operates on an annual planning cycle with fund releases tied to AAP approval and utilization.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Cooperation (DAC), Ministry of Agriculture, Government of India

scheme_name: National Language Translation Mission (NLTM) – Bhashini Startup Integration
overview: The National Language Translation Mission (NLTM) – Bhashini Startup Integration is a Government of India initiative under the Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) that empowers startups to co-create innovative AI-driven multilingual solutions by integrating Bhashini’s language translation APIs. It fosters technological inclusivity, enabling startups to build products that break linguistic barriers and ensure seamless digital communication across India’s diverse language ecosystem. The program supports hackathons, innovation challenges, and collaborative development to advance scalable and inclusive AI language solutions.
target_beneficiaries: startups
eligibility: Startups can join the Bhashini ecosystem by integrating Bhashini’s language translation APIs to co-create and build new, innovative products that break linguistic barriers, ensuring seamless digital communication across India’s diverse language ecosystem.
benefits: Access to Bhashini’s multilingual APIs for integration into products and services, participation in hackathons and innovation challenges, opportunities for collaboration and recognition, support for building scalable and inclusive AI language solutions, and empowerment to develop multilingual solutions that connect a billion voices.
financial_support: The scheme does not provide direct financial grants or funding to startups. Instead, it offers non-financial support such as API access, mentorship, collaboration opportunities, and participation in hackathons and challenges to foster innovation and product development.
application_process: 1. Join the Bhashini ecosystem by integrating Bhashini’s language translation APIs into your products and services. 2. Participate in hackathons and innovation challenges organized by Bhashini to build multilingual solutions. 3. Collaborate with Bhashini to co-create innovative AI-driven multilingual solutions. 4. Leverage Bhashini’s resources such as models, datasets, and tools for development. 5. Scale your solutions while ensuring digital services are accessible to a broader audience across India’s linguistic diversity.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), an Independent Business Division under Digital India Corporation (DIC)

scheme_name: Zero Defect Zero Effect (ZED) Green Certification
overview: The Zero Defect Zero Effect (ZED) Green Certification is a Ministry of MSME initiative to create awareness among MSMEs about ZED practices, motivate them to adopt zero-defect and zero-environmental-impact manufacturing, and incentivize certification through financial subsidies and recognition. The scheme aims to enhance MSME competitiveness, sustainability, and global market readiness by promoting quality, productivity, energy efficiency, and environmental consciousness. It operates in two phases: Phase 1 for manufacturing MSMEs with UDYAM registration, and Phase 2 for service sector MSMEs. benefits: Benefits include Joining reward of Rs. 10,000/- for ZED Certification, free MSME KAWACH (WASH Certification) for ZED registered MSMEs, financial assistance/subsidy for certification cost (80% for Micro, 60% for Small, 50% for Medium Enterprises), additional 10% subsidy for Women/SC/ST Entrepreneurs or MSMEs in NER/Himalayan/LWE/Island territories/aspirational districts, additional 5% subsidy for MSMEs part of SFURTI or MSE-CDP, subsidy for surveillance assessment (Silver: Rs. 10,000, Gold: Rs. 20,000) at same subsidy rates, handholding support up to Rs. 5 Lakhs (Rs. 2 Lakhs for consultancy, Rs. 3 Lakhs for technology upgradation) with subsidies as per MSME size, and financial assistance for Testing/System/Product Certification up to 75% of cost with ceiling of Rs. 50,000/-.
financial_support: Financial assistance includes: Joining reward of Rs. 10,000/- (deductible from certification cost); subsidy on certification cost: Micro Enterprises 80%, Small Enterprises 60%, Medium Enterprises 50%; additional 10% subsidy for Women/SC/ST Entrepreneurs or MSMEs in NER/Himalayan/LWE/Island territories/aspirational districts; additional 5% subsidy for MSMEs in SFURTI or MSE-CDP; 100% subsidy for Women-owned MSMEs (as per Addendum 2023); subsidy for surveillance assessment (Silver: Rs. 10,000, Gold: Rs. 20,000) at same MSME-size-based rates; handholding support up to Rs. 5 Lakhs (Rs. 2 Lakhs for consultancy, Rs. 3 Lakhs for technology upgradation) with subsidies as per MSME size; and financial assistance for Testing/System/Product Certification up to 75% of cost with maximum ceiling of Rs. 50,000/- per certification.
application_process: 1. Visit the official ZED portal at https://zed.msme.gov.in/ 2. Enter valid Udyam Registration Number and associated mobile number for validation 3. Opt to avail Joining Reward of Rs. 10,000/- (deducted from certification cost) 11. Select payment option and make online payment for MSME contribution 12. Capture MSME Representative Selfie and Site Exterior Photographs 13. Upload Basic Information and Documents 14. Submit for assessment 15. Assessor verifies information and documents 16. Address any non-conformances raised within stipulated time 17. Upon successful verification, certificate and report are issued via email and dashboard.

scheme_name: CESL Convergence EV Charging Startup Programme
overview: The CESL Convergence EV Charging Startup Programme is an initiative by Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL) to support startups in the electric vehicle (EV) charging ecosystem. scheme_name: Digital Sky Platform – NPNT Drone Certification
overview: The Digital Sky Platform – NPNT Drone Certification is a government initiative under the Ministry of Civil Aviation and DGCA to enable the No Permission – No Takeoff (NPNT) compliance for drones operating in Indian airspace. It provides a centralized digital regulatory ecosystem for drone registration, flight permission, airspace zone management (Green, Yellow, Red zones), and remote pilot certification. The platform supports safe and compliant drone operations by integrating airspace mapping, flight planning, and real-time approvals through the DigitalSky engine and associated UTM framework.
target_beneficiaries: drone operators; remote pilots; drone manufacturers; UTMSPs; government agencies
eligibility: Any individual or organization operating a nano or micro drone (up to 250 grams) in Green Zone airspace does not require prior permission. For operations in Yellow Zone (above 400 ft in Green Zone or between 8-12 km from airport perimeter up to 200 ft), permission from Air Traffic Control is required. For Red Zone operations (near strategic installations, ports, or beyond territorial waters), Central Government permission is mandatory. All drone operators must register on the DigitalSky Platform and obtain a Unique Identification Number (UIN) or Drone Acknowledgement Number (DAN) for drones exceeding nano category. Remote pilots must hold a valid Remote Pilot Certificate from an authorized training organization.
benefits: Enables legal drone operations in Indian airspace through NPNT compliance; provides real-time flight plan approvals; offers access to airspace zone maps (Green, Yellow, Red); facilitates registration of drones and issuance of UIN/DAN; supports remote pilot certification and licensing; allows government agencies to manage airspace constraints; provides APIs for UTM service providers and supplementary service providers; ensures integration with Air Traffic Control and Air Defence for flight clearance; maintains flight logs and operational records for safety and compliance.
financial_support: The Digital Sky Platform – NPNT Drone Certification does not provide direct financial support, grants, subsidies, or loans to beneficiaries. It is a regulatory and operational platform for compliance, registration, and permission management. Financial incentives for drone manufacturing are available under separate schemes such as the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) for drones and drone components, which offers up to 20% incentive on eligible value addition in India with a total outlay of INR 120 Crore over three years.
application_process: 1. Visit the DigitalSky platform at https://digitalsky.dgca.gov.in 2. Register as a user by providing personal and organizational details 3. Complete Basic & Entity Info, Address Details, and Login Credentials sections 4. Upload required documents such as proof of identity, address, and authorization 5. Submit the registration request for administrator approval 6. Upon approval, log in to the platform 7. For drone registration, submit details of the drone (make, model, serial number) to obtain UIN/DAN 8. For flight operations, create a flight plan by filling in flight details 9. Submit the flight plan request for review 10. Await approval from the concerned authority (Air Traffic Control for Yellow Zone, Central Government for Red Zone) 11. Once approved, conduct the drone flight in the authorized airspace 12. Post-flight, log flight details if required for compliance
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications for registration, flight plans, and zone management are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India

scheme_name: AI Pravega – AI Research Grants via IIT Consortium
overview: AI Pravega – AI Research Grants via IIT Consortium is a scheme under the IndiaAI Mission's Startup Financing pillar that supports deep-tech AI startups by providing streamlined access to funding for innovative AI projects. The scheme is implemented through a consortium of IITs and aims to accelerate AI innovation by offering research grants to eligible entities. It focuses on fostering indigenous AI capabilities and enabling industry collaboration.
target_beneficiaries: startups; deep-tech AI startups
eligibility: Deep-tech AI startups and innovative AI projects are eligible for funding under the IndiaAI Startup Financing pillar. The scheme supports startups and companies working on AI innovation, with a focus on streamlining access to funding for AI-driven solutions.
benefits: Streamlined access to funding for innovative AI projects, support for deep-tech AI startups, facilitation of industry collaboration, promotion of ethical and responsible AI development, and contribution to building a robust domestic AI ecosystem.

overview: The Chip-to-Startup (C2S) Programme – VLSI Design Education is a MeitY initiative aimed at fostering VLSI design education and innovation by providing academic and industry collaboration opportunities. It focuses on building capacity in semiconductor design through training, mentorship, and access to EDA tools for students and startups. The programme supports the development of indigenous semiconductor ecosystem by enabling prototype development and productization. It targets academic institutions and startups engaged in VLSI design and related domains.
target_beneficiaries: startups; students; academic institutions
eligibility: The programme is open to startups, academic institutions, and students engaged in VLSI design, semiconductor research, or related electronics domains. Applicants must be registered entities in India with a focus on innovation in chip design and must demonstrate potential for technology development or commercialization.
benefits: Participants gain access to licensed EDA tools, technical mentorship from industry experts, design review support, prototyping facilities, and opportunities for collaboration with semiconductor companies. scheme_name: Amrita University – Ammachi Labs Social Innovation Fund
overview: Amrita University – Ammachi Labs Social Innovation Fund is a research initiative focused on social innovation, women's empowerment, and community development through technology-driven solutions. It operates as part of Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham's AMMACHI Labs and the Center for Women’s Empowerment & Gender Equality (CWEGE), which are thematic research centers in Kerala, India. The fund supports projects in skill development, rural technologies, water and sanitation, and gender equality, often in collaboration with government and international organizations.
target_beneficiaries: women entrepreneurs; rural communities; self-help groups; transgender individuals; youth
eligibility: Eligibility varies by specific project; for PhD programs, candidates require a Master of Social Work (MSW) or related social science discipline, strong interest in gender justice, community resilience, and rural development, readiness for field-based research, and Kannada language proficiency is preferred. For skill development programs, eligibility includes women from socio-economically underserved communities, particularly in rural areas.
benefits: Benefits include vocational training in trades such as plumbing, carpentry, tailoring, beekeeping, seaweed cultivation, and two-wheeler repair; life skills and entrepreneurship training; access to microcredit loans and insurance; support for forming Self-Help Groups (SHGs); community-led sanitation initiatives; menstrual health and hygiene management through reusable pads; water quality monitoring training; and participation in government scheme awareness and access programs.
financial_support: Financial support includes start-up capital, marketing assistance, and access to microcredit loans from government-regulated banks and affordable insurance plans. The AmritaSREE program has provided $14.2 million in support for 2021 and 2022, and $1,200 each to widows of fishermen. Funding sources include United Nations Development Programme (UNDEP), Government of India, World Bank, and other international partners.
application_process: 1. Identify the specific program or initiative (e.g., PhD admissions, skill training, sanitation project). 2. Check eligibility criteria for the respective program. 3. Apply through the designated portal (e.g., Amrita SSBS PhD Admissions Process for research roles). 4. Submit required documents such as academic qualifications, statement of purpose, and language proficiency proof. 5. Await selection based on merit and alignment with program goals. 6. For community programs, engage through local outreach and field participation.
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round for most programs.
implementing_agency: Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham (University) through AMMACHI Labs and the Center for Women’s Empowerment & Gender Equality (CWEGE)

scheme_name: World Bank MSME Development Programme India
overview: The World Bank MSME Development Programme India is part of the World Bank Group's Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for India FY2026-2031, which aims to support India's aspiration to become an upper-middle-income economy and achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047. The programme focuses on fostering rural prosperity and resilience, driving urban transformation, empowering people through better skills and health, and building resilient infrastructure and boosting energy security, with a cross-cutting emphasis on private sector-led job creation and MSME growth and innovation.
target_beneficiaries: MSME; youth; women
eligibility: The evidence does not specify explicit eligibility criteria for the World Bank MSME Development Programme India. Eligibility is inferred to align with the CPF's focus on MSMEs, youth, and women, particularly in rural and urban areas benefiting from CPF interventions.
benefits: Benefits include access to improved agricultural/food market linkages or trade (AgriConnect) for 150 million people, improved access to finance for small producers especially women, support for high-potential agribusiness firms, modernization and climate-proofing of agriculture including irrigation, strengthening integrated water resources management, and enabling resilient infrastructure and energy security through private sector mobilization and global innovation leverage.
financial_support: The CPF aims to provide US$8–10 billion in financing annually from the World Bank Group to help unlock another US$20 billion annually from markets by the end of the CPF period. application_process: The evidence does not describe a numbered step-by-step application procedure for the World Bank MSME Development Programme India. Implementation occurs through the CPF's engagement with government, private sector, and development actors.
deadlines: The CPF period is FY2026-2031; specific application deadlines are not detailed in the evidence.
implementing_agency: World Bank Group
